q:
A company collects data for temperature, humidity, and atmospheric pressure in cities across multiple continents. The average volume of data that the company collects from each site daily is 500 GB. Each site has a high-speed Internet connection.
The company wants to aggregate the data from all these global sites as quickly as possible in a single Amazon S3 bucket. The solution must minimize operational complexity.
Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Turn on S3 Transfer Acceleration on the destination S3 bucket. Use multipart uploads to directly upload site data to the destination S3 bucket.
o.B: Upload the data from each site to an S3 bucket in the closest Region. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy objects to the destination S3 bucket. Then remove the data from the origin S3 bucket.
o.C: Schedule AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device jobs daily to transfer data from each site to the closest Region. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy objects to the destination S3 bucket.
o.D: Upload the data from each site to an Amazon EC2 instance in the closest Region. Store the data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. At regular intervals, take an EBS snapshot and copy it to the Region that contains the destination S3 bucket. Restore the EBS volume in that Region.

e.why: S3 Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through the nearest CloudFront edge location and then over the optimized AWS backbone to the bucket, speeding long-distance transfers from global sites. Combined with multipart uploads for the large daily files, it aggregates data directly into one bucket as quickly as possible with minimal operational complexity, since it is just a bucket setting plus a different endpoint.

others.B: Cross-Region Replication adds extra buckets, replication rules and cleanup steps, increasing complexity and delaying arrival in the destination bucket.
others.C: Shipping Snowball Edge devices daily is slow and operationally heavy when the sites already have high-speed internet.
others.D: Staging data on EC2 and EBS with snapshot copies is complex, slow and does not even land the data in S3.

e.tip: Global sites uploading quickly to one bucket over the internet: think S3 Transfer Acceleration plus multipart upload.

q:
A company needs the ability to analyze the log files of its proprietary application. The logs are stored in JSON format in an Amazon S3 bucket. Queries will be simple and will run on-demand. A solutions architect needs to perform the analysis with minimal changes to the existing architecture.
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon Redshift to load all the content into one place and run the SQL queries as needed.
o.B: Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to store the logs. Run SQL queries as needed from the Amazon CloudWatch console.
o.C: Use Amazon Athena directly with Amazon S3 to run the queries as needed.
o.D: Use AWS Glue to catalog the logs. Use a transient Apache Spark cluster on Amazon EMR to run the SQL queries as needed.

e.why: Amazon Athena is a serverless, interactive query service that runs standard SQL directly against data in S3, including JSON, with no infrastructure to manage and pay-per-query pricing. It requires no data movement and minimal architecture changes, giving the least operational overhead for simple on-demand queries.

others.A: Redshift requires provisioning a cluster and loading data, which is more overhead than needed for simple ad hoc queries.
others.B: Moving logs into CloudWatch Logs changes the architecture, and Logs Insights uses its own query language rather than querying the existing S3 data.
others.D: Glue plus a transient EMR Spark cluster is far more operational effort than Athena for simple SQL queries.

e.tip: Ad hoc SQL on data already in S3 with least overhead: Athena.

q:
A company uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts for different departments. The management account has an Amazon S3 bucket that contains project reports. The company wants to limit access to this S3 bucket to only users of accounts within the organization in AWS Organizations.
Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

o.A: Add the aws PrincipalOrgID global condition key with a reference to the organization ID to the S3 bucket policy.
o.B: Create an organizational unit (OU) for each department. Add the aws:PrincipalOrgPaths global condition key to the S3 bucket policy.
o.C: Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor the CreateAccount, InviteAccountToOrganization, LeaveOrganization, and RemoveAccountFromOrganization events. Update the S3 bucket policy accordingly.
o.D: Tag each user that needs access to the S3 bucket. Add the aws:PrincipalTag global condition key to the S3 bucket policy.

e.why: The aws:PrincipalOrgID global condition key in an S3 bucket policy allows access only to principals from accounts in the specified AWS Organizations organization. It is a single condition that automatically covers accounts as they join or leave, so it has the least operational overhead.

others.B: Creating OUs per department and using aws:PrincipalOrgPaths adds unnecessary restructuring when the whole organization should have access.
others.C: Monitoring CloudTrail events and manually updating the bucket policy is reactive and operationally heavy.
others.D: Tagging every user and maintaining aws:PrincipalTag conditions requires ongoing manual effort and is error-prone.

e.tip: Restrict a resource to your whole organization: aws:PrincipalOrgID in the resource policy.

q:
An application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in a VPC. The application processes logs that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The EC2 instance needs to access the S3 bucket without connectivity to the internet.
Which solution will provide private network connectivity to Amazon S3?

o.A: Create a gateway VPC endpoint to the S3 bucket.
o.B: Stream the logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Export the logs to the S3 bucket.
o.C: Create an instance profile on Amazon EC2 to allow S3 access.
o.D: Create an Amazon API Gateway API with a private link to access the S3 endpoint.

e.why: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 adds a route in the subnet route table so traffic to S3 stays on the AWS private network without an internet gateway or NAT. It provides private connectivity at no additional charge.

others.B: CloudWatch Logs streaming does not give the instance private network access to read objects in S3.
others.C: An instance profile grants IAM permissions but does not provide a network path to S3 without internet access.
others.D: API Gateway is not the mechanism for private S3 connectivity from a VPC and adds unnecessary complexity.

e.tip: Private access from a VPC to S3 or DynamoDB: gateway endpoint (free).

q:
A company is hosting a web application on AWS using a single Amazon EC2 instance that stores user-uploaded documents in an Amazon EBS volume. For better scalability and availability, the company duplicated the architecture and created a second EC2 instance and EBS volume in another Availability Zone, placing both behind an Application Load Balancer. After completing this change, users reported that, each time they refreshed the website, they could see one subset of their documents or the other, but never all of the documents at the same time.
What should a solutions architect propose to ensure users see all of their documents at once?

o.A: Copy the data so both EBS volumes contain all the documents
o.B: Configure the Application Load Balancer to direct a user to the server with the documents
o.C: Copy the data from both EBS volumes to Amazon EFS. Modify the application to save new documents to Amazon EFS
o.D: Configure the Application Load Balancer to send the request to both servers. Return each document from the correct server

e.why: EBS volumes are attached to a single instance in a single AZ, so each server only sees its own uploaded documents. Amazon EFS is a shared, multi-AZ NFS file system that both instances can mount concurrently, so moving existing data to EFS and writing new documents there gives every request a consistent view of all documents.

others.A: Copying data once does not keep the two volumes in sync as new documents are uploaded.
others.B: Sticky routing ties users to one server but documents uploaded to the other server remain invisible, and it hurts availability.
others.D: An ALB cannot fan out a single request to multiple targets and merge the responses.

e.tip: Multiple instances across AZs needing the same files: use EFS (or S3), not EBS.

q:
A company uses NFS to store large video files in on-premises network attached storage. Each video file ranges in size from 1 MB to 500 GB. The total storage is 70 TB and is no longer growing. The company decides to migrate the video files to Amazon S3. The company must migrate the video files as soon as possible while using the least possible network bandwidth.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an S3 bucket. Create an IAM role that has permissions to write to the S3 bucket. Use the AWS CLI to copy all files locally to the S3 bucket.
o.B: Create an AWS Snowball Edge job. Receive a Snowball Edge device on premises. Use the Snowball Edge client to transfer data to the device. Return the device so that AWS can import the data into Amazon S3.
o.C: Deploy an S3 File Gateway on premises. Create a public service endpoint to connect to the S3 File Gateway. Create an S3 bucket. Create a new NFS file share on the S3 File Gateway. Point the new file share to the S3 bucket. Transfer the data from the existing NFS file share to the S3 File Gateway.
o.D: Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises network and AWS. Deploy an S3 File Gateway on premises. Create a public virtual interface (VIF) to connect to the S3 File Gateway. Create an S3 bucket. Create a new NFS file share on the S3 File Gateway. Point the new file share to the S3 bucket. Transfer the data from the existing NFS file share to the S3 File Gateway.

e.why: Moving 70 TB over the network would take a long time and consume significant bandwidth. An AWS Snowball Edge device lets the company copy data locally and ship it to AWS for import into S3, which is the fastest option while using almost no network bandwidth.

others.A: Copying 70 TB with the AWS CLI uses a large amount of network bandwidth and would be slow.
others.C: S3 File Gateway still transfers all data over the internet connection, consuming bandwidth.
others.D: Provisioning Direct Connect takes weeks and still sends all data over the network.

e.tip: Tens of TB with limited bandwidth or urgency: Snowball Edge.

q:
A company has an application that ingests incoming messages. Dozens of other applications and microservices then quickly consume these messages. The number of messages varies drastically and sometimes increases suddenly to 100,000 each second. The company wants to decouple the solution and increase scalability.
Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Persist the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics. Configure the consumer applications to read and process the messages.
o.B: Deploy the ingestion application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to scale the number of EC2 instances based on CPU metrics.
o.C: Write the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with a single shard. Use an AWS Lambda function to preprocess messages and store them in Amazon DynamoDB. Configure the consumer applications to read from DynamoDB to process the messages.
o.D: Publish the messages to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) subscriptions. Configure the consumer applications to process the messages from the queues.

fixed: Options B and C were garbled (C truncated, B replaced by C's tail) and have been reconstructed; typo 'SOS' in D corrected to SQS.

e.why: Publishing to an SNS topic that fans out to multiple SQS queues decouples the producer from dozens of consumers. Each consumer reads from its own queue at its own pace, and SNS plus SQS standard queues scale virtually without limit, absorbing sudden spikes to 100,000 messages per second.

others.A: Kinesis Data Analytics is for running SQL/Flink analytics on streams, not a message store that dozens of consumers read from.
others.B: Scaling the ingestion tier on CPU does not decouple producers from consumers and reacts too slowly to sudden spikes.
others.C: A single Kinesis shard is limited to 1,000 records per second for writes, far below 100,000 messages per second, and DynamoDB polling adds coupling.

e.tip: Many consumers plus decoupling plus bursty volume = SNS fan-out to SQS queues.

q:
A company is migrating a distributed application to AWS. The application serves variable workloads. The legacy platform consists of a primary server that coordinates jobs across multiple compute nodes. The company wants to modernize the application with a solution that maximizes resiliency and scalability.
How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a destination for the jobs. Implement the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling to use scheduled scaling.
o.B: Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a destination for the jobs. Implement the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the size of the queue.
o.C: Implement the primary server and the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure AWS CloudTrail as a destination for the jobs. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the load on the primary server.
o.D: Implement the primary server and the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) as a destination for the jobs. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the load on the compute nodes.

e.why: Replacing the primary coordinating server with an SQS queue removes a single point of failure and decouples job submission from processing. An Auto Scaling group of EC2 workers that scales on queue depth (such as backlog per instance) matches capacity to the variable workload, maximizing resiliency and scalability.

others.A: Scheduled scaling does not respond to unpredictable, variable workloads.
others.C: CloudTrail is an audit logging service, not a job destination, and keeping the primary server retains a bottleneck.
others.D: EventBridge is not a job queue for workers, and keeping the primary server limits resiliency.

e.tip: Variable job workloads: SQS queue plus Auto Scaling based on queue backlog.

q:
A company is running an SMB file server in its data center. The file server stores large files that are accessed frequently for the first few days after the files are created. After 7 days the files are rarely accessed.
The total data size is increasing and is close to the company's total storage capacity. A solutions architect must increase the company's available storage space without losing low-latency access to the most recently accessed files. The solutions architect must also provide file lifecycle management to avoid future storage issues.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS DataSync to copy data that is older than 7 days from the SMB file server to AWS.
o.B: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway to extend the company's storage space. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.
o.C: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system to extend the company's storage space.
o.D: Install a utility on each user's computer to access Amazon S3. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days.

e.why: Amazon S3 File Gateway presents an SMB share on premises backed by S3, with a local cache that keeps recently accessed files available at low latency, effectively extending storage capacity. An S3 Lifecycle policy then transitions objects older than 7 days to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, providing automated lifecycle management at lowest cost.

others.A: DataSync copies data but provides no ongoing access path or lifecycle management for the file server.
others.C: FSx for Windows File Server adds storage but has no lifecycle tiering to archival storage.
others.D: Installing an S3 utility on each computer is operationally heavy and loses the SMB file share experience.

e.tip: Extend on-prem file storage into AWS with local caching: Storage Gateway (S3 File Gateway).

q:
A company is building an ecommerce web application on AWS. The application sends information about new orders to an Amazon API Gateway REST API to process. The company wants to ensure that orders are processed in the order that they are received.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use an API Gateway integration to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the application receives an order. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the topic to perform processing.
o.B: Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS FIFO queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing.
o.C: Use an API Gateway authorizer to block any requests while the application processes an order.
o.D: Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS standard queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing.

e.why: An SQS FIFO queue guarantees first-in-first-out ordering within a message group and exactly-once processing. API Gateway can integrate directly with SQS, and Lambda can poll the FIFO queue as an event source, so orders are processed in the order received.

others.A: A standard SNS topic does not guarantee message ordering to subscribers.
others.C: Blocking requests with an authorizer would reject orders and does not provide ordered processing.
others.D: SQS standard queues provide best-effort ordering only, so orders may be processed out of sequence.

e.tip: Strict ordering requirement: FIFO (SQS FIFO or SNS FIFO).

q:
A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon Aurora database. The EC2 instances connect to the database by using user names and passwords that are stored locally in a file. The company wants to minimize the operational overhead of credential management.
What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this goal?

o.A: Use AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation.
o.B: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on automatic rotation.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store objects that are encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Migrate the credential file to the S3 bucket. Point the application to the S3 bucket.
o.D: Create an encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for each EC2 instance. Attach the new EBS volume to each EC2 instance. Migrate the credential file to the new EBS volume. Point the application to the new EBS volume.

e.why: AWS Secrets Manager stores database credentials securely and has built-in automatic rotation for Amazon Aurora and RDS using managed rotation functions. The application retrieves credentials at runtime via API, removing local files and minimizing credential management overhead.

others.B: Systems Manager Parameter Store does not offer native automatic rotation of secrets.
others.C: Storing an encrypted credential file in S3 still requires manual rotation and file management.
others.D: Moving the file to an encrypted EBS volume improves encryption only and still requires manual credential management.

e.tip: Database credentials with automatic rotation: Secrets Manager.

q:
A global company hosts its web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The web application has static data and dynamic data. The company stores its static data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to improve performance and reduce latency for the static data and dynamic data. The company is using its own domain name registered with Amazon Route 53.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the S3 bucket and the ALB as origins. Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the CloudFront distribution.
o.B: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the ALB as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the S3 bucket as an endpoint Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the CloudFront distribution.
o.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the S3 bucket as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the ALB and the CloudFront distribution as endpoints. Create a custom domain name that points to the accelerator DNS name. Use the custom domain name as an endpoint for the web application.
o.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the ALB as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the S3 bucket as an endpoint. Create two domain names. Point one domain name to the CloudFront DNS name for dynamic content. Point the other domain name to the accelerator DNS name for static content. Use the domain names as endpoints for the web application.

e.why: A single CloudFront distribution can have multiple origins: the S3 bucket for static content and the ALB for dynamic content, using cache behaviors with path patterns. CloudFront edge locations cache static content and accelerate dynamic content over the AWS network, and a Route 53 alias record points the custom domain to the distribution.

others.B: Global Accelerator does not support S3 buckets as endpoints.
others.C: Global Accelerator cannot use a CloudFront distribution as an endpoint, and the design is needlessly complex.
others.D: S3 is not a valid Global Accelerator endpoint, and splitting content across two domain names is unnecessary.

e.tip: Static plus dynamic content acceleration under one domain: one CloudFront distribution with multiple origins.

q:
A company performs monthly maintenance on its AWS infrastructure. During these maintenance activities, the company needs to rotate the credentials for its Amazon RDS for MySQL databases across multiple AWS Regions.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Store the credentials as secrets in AWS Secrets Manager. Use multi-Region secret replication for the required Regions. Configure Secrets Manager to rotate the secrets on a schedule.
o.B: Store the credentials as secrets in AWS Systems Manager by creating a secure string parameter. Use multi-Region secret replication for the required Regions. Configure Systems Manager to rotate the secrets on a schedule.
o.C: Store the credentials in an Amazon S3 bucket that has server-side encryption (SSE) enabled. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to invoke an AWS Lambda function to rotate the credentials.
o.D: Encrypt the credentials as secrets by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) multi-Region customer managed keys. Store the secrets in an Amazon DynamoDB global table. Use an AWS Lambda function to retrieve the secrets from DynamoDB. Use the RDS API to rotate the secrets.

fixed: Options B and D were garbled (D truncated, B replaced by D's tail) and have been reconstructed.

e.why: AWS Secrets Manager supports multi-Region secret replication, keeping replica secrets in sync across Regions, and has built-in scheduled rotation for Amazon RDS for MySQL. This fully managed approach rotates credentials across Regions with the least operational overhead.

others.B: Systems Manager Parameter Store secure strings do not offer built-in multi-Region replication or native scheduled rotation.
others.C: Storing credentials in S3 and rotating them with custom Lambda code is a do-it-yourself solution with much more overhead.
others.D: A DynamoDB global table plus KMS keys plus custom Lambda and RDS API calls reinvents what Secrets Manager provides natively.

e.tip: Rotating database credentials, especially across Regions = Secrets Manager with rotation and replication.

q:
A company runs an ecommerce application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The Auto Scaling group scales based on CPU utilization metrics. The ecommerce application stores the transaction data in a MySQL 8.0 database that is hosted on a large EC2 instance.
The database's performance degrades quickly as application load increases. The application handles more read requests than write transactions. The company wants a solution that will automatically scale the database to meet the demand of unpredictable read workloads while maintaining high availability.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon Redshift with a single node for leader and compute functionality.
o.B: Use Amazon RDS with a Single-AZ deployment Configure Amazon RDS to add reader instances in a different Availability Zone.
o.C: Use Amazon Aurora with a Multi-AZ deployment. Configure Aurora Auto Scaling with Aurora Replicas.
o.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with EC2 Spot Instances.

e.why: Amazon Aurora MySQL is compatible with MySQL 8.0, and a Multi-AZ Aurora cluster provides high availability with fast failover. Aurora Auto Scaling automatically adds or removes Aurora Replicas (up to 15) based on metrics such as CPU or connections, handling unpredictable read workloads.

others.A: Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics, not an OLTP transactional database, and a single node lacks high availability.
others.B: A Single-AZ deployment is not highly available, and RDS does not automatically scale the number of read replicas.
others.D: Memcached on Spot Instances is not a durable transactional database and Spot can be interrupted.

e.tip: Auto-scaling read capacity for a relational DB: Aurora Auto Scaling with Aurora Replicas.

q:
A company recently migrated to AWS and wants to implement a solution to protect the traffic that flows in and out of the production VPC. The company had an inspection server in its on-premises data center. The inspection server performed specific operations such as traffic flow inspection and traffic filtering. The company wants to have the same functionalities in the AWS Cloud.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon GuardDuty for traffic inspection and traffic filtering in the production VPC.
o.C: Use AWS Network Firewall to create the required rules for traffic inspection and traffic filtering for the production VPC.
o.B: Use Traffic Mirroring to mirror traffic from the production VPC for traffic inspection and filtering.
o.D: Use AWS Firewall Manager to create the required rules for traffic inspection and traffic filtering for the production VPC.

fixed: Option A was truncated and option C text was missing; both have been reconstructed.

e.why: AWS Network Firewall is a managed, stateful network firewall and intrusion prevention service for VPCs. It inspects and filters traffic flowing in and out of the production VPC, replicating the on-premises inspection server's traffic flow inspection and filtering functions.

others.A: GuardDuty is a threat detection service that analyzes logs; it does not inline-inspect or filter traffic.
others.B: Traffic Mirroring copies traffic for out-of-band analysis but cannot filter or block it.
others.D: Firewall Manager centrally manages firewall policies across accounts; it is not itself the inspection engine.

e.tip: Inline VPC traffic inspection and filtering = AWS Network Firewall.

q:
A company hosts a data lake on AWS. The data lake consists of data in Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company needs a reporting solution that provides data visualization and includes all the data sources within the data lake. Only the company's management team should have full access to all the visualizations. The rest of the company should have only limited access.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an analysis in Amazon QuickSight. Connect all the data sources and create new datasets. Publish dashboards to visualize the data. Share the dashboards with the appropriate IAM roles.
o.B: Create an analysis in Amazon QuickSight. Connect all the data sources and create new datasets. Publish dashboards to visualize the data. Share the dashboards with the appropriate users and groups.
o.C: Create an AWS Glue table and crawler for the data in Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to produce reports. Publish the reports to Amazon S3. Use S3 bucket policies to limit access to the reports.
o.D: Create an AWS Glue table and crawler for the data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena Federated Query to access data within Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. Generate reports by using Amazon Athena. Publish the reports to Amazon S3. Use S3 bucket policies to limit access to the reports.

e.why: Amazon QuickSight can connect to both S3 (via Athena or a manifest) and RDS for PostgreSQL to build datasets, analyses and dashboards. QuickSight dashboards are shared with QuickSight users and groups, letting the management team have full access while others get limited permissions.

others.A: QuickSight dashboards are shared with QuickSight users and groups, not directly with IAM roles.
others.C: Glue ETL reports in S3 do not provide interactive data visualization and ignore the RDS data source.
others.D: Athena-generated reports in S3 are not a visualization solution, and bucket policies give coarse access control.

e.tip: BI dashboards with per-user access: QuickSight shared with users and groups.

q:
A company is implementing a new business application. The application runs on two Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon S3 bucket for document storage. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the EC2 instances can access the S3 bucket.
What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.A: Create an IAM role that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the role to the EC2 instances.
o.B: Create an IAM policy that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the policy to the EC2 instances.
o.C: Create an IAM group that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the group to the EC2 instances.
o.D: Create an IAM user that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the user account to the EC2 instances.

e.why: An IAM role attached to EC2 through an instance profile provides temporary, automatically rotated credentials to applications on the instances. Granting S3 bucket permissions in the role's policy is the AWS best practice for letting EC2 access S3 without storing long-term keys.

others.B: An IAM policy cannot be attached directly to an EC2 instance; it must be attached to a role used via an instance profile.
others.C: IAM groups contain users only and cannot be attached to EC2 instances.
others.D: IAM users cannot be attached to instances, and embedding user access keys is a security anti-pattern.

e.tip: AWS service needs permissions: use an IAM role, never stored access keys.

q:
An application development team is designing a microservice that will convert large images to smaller, compressed images. When a user uploads an image through the web interface, the microservice should store the image in an Amazon S3 bucket, process and compress the image with an AWS Lambda function, and store the image in its compressed form in a different S3 bucket.
A solutions architect needs to design a solution that uses durable, stateless components to process the images automatically.
Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure the S3 bucket to send a notification to the SQS queue when an image is uploaded to the S3 bucket.
o.B: Configure the Lambda function to use the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as the invocation source. When the SQS message is successfully processed, delete the message in the queue.
o.C: Configure the Lambda function to monitor the S3 bucket for new uploads. When an uploaded image is detected, write the file name to a text file in memory and use the text file to keep track of the images that were processed.
o.D: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance to monitor an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. When items are added to the queue, log the file name in a text file on the EC2 instance and invoke the Lambda function.
o.E: Configure an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) event to monitor the S3 bucket. When an image is uploaded, send an alert to an Amazon ample Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with the application owner's email address for further processing.

e.why: Configuring S3 event notifications to send a message to an SQS queue durably records every upload, and configuring the Lambda function with the SQS queue as its event source processes each image statelessly. Lambda deletes messages after successful processing, and failed messages become visible again for retry, giving a durable, stateless, automatic pipeline.

others.C: Tracking processed files in an in-memory text file is stateful and is lost when the Lambda execution environment is recycled.
others.D: An EC2 instance logging file names to a local file is stateful, not durable, and adds servers to manage.
others.E: Emailing the application owner via SNS introduces manual processing rather than automatic compression.

e.tip: S3 upload to async processing durably: S3 event to SQS to Lambda.

q:
A company has a three-tier web application that is deployed on AWS. The web servers are deployed in a public subnet in a VPC. The application servers and database servers are deployed in private subnets in the same VPC. The company has deployed a third-party virtual firewall appliance from AWS Marketplace in an inspection VPC. The appliance is configured with an IP interface that can accept IP packets.
A solutions architect needs to integrate the web application with the appliance to inspect all traffic to the application before the traffic reaches the web server.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create a Network Load Balancer in the public subnet of the application's VPC to route the traffic to the appliance for packet inspection.
o.B: Create an Application Load Balancer in the public subnet of the application's VPC to route the traffic to the appliance for packet inspection.
o.C: Deploy a transit gateway in the inspection VPC. Configure route tables to route the incoming packets through the transit gateway.
o.D: Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer in the inspection VPC. Create a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint to receive the incoming packets and forward the packets to the appliance.

fixed: Options C and D were garbled (D truncated, C replaced by D's tail) and have been reconstructed.

e.why: Gateway Load Balancer is built to deploy, scale and manage third-party virtual appliances such as firewalls, passing IP packets transparently using GENEVE. A Gateway Load Balancer endpoint in the application VPC receives incoming traffic and sends it to the GWLB and appliance in the inspection VPC before it reaches the web servers.

others.A: A Network Load Balancer forwards to targets at layer 4 but is not designed for transparent bump-in-the-wire appliance insertion.
others.B: An Application Load Balancer terminates HTTP(S) connections and cannot pass raw IP packets to an appliance for inspection.
others.C: A transit gateway routes between VPCs but does not by itself insert, load balance or scale an inspection appliance with low overhead.

e.tip: Third-party firewall/IDS appliances inline = Gateway Load Balancer plus GWLB endpoints.

q:
A company wants to improve its ability to clone large amounts of production data into a test environment in the same AWS Region. The data is stored in Amazon EC2 instances on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Modifications to the cloned data must not affect the production environment. The software that accesses this data requires consistently high I/O performance.
A solutions architect needs to minimize the time that is required to clone the production data into the test environment.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Restore the snapshots onto EC2 instance store volumes in the test environment.
o.B: Configure the production EBS volumes to use the EBS Multi-Attach feature. Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Attach the production EBS volumes to the EC2 instances in the test environment.
o.C: Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Create and initialize new EBS volumes. Attach the new EBS volumes to EC2 instances in the test environment before restoring the volumes from the production EBS snapshots.
o.D: Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Turn on the EBS fast snapshot restore feature on the EBS snapshots. Restore the snapshots into new EBS volumes. Attach the new EBS volumes to EC2 instances in the test environment.

e.why: Volumes restored from snapshots normally load blocks lazily from S3, causing high first-access latency. EBS fast snapshot restore creates volumes that are fully initialized at creation, delivering full provisioned performance immediately, so test environments get independent, high-I/O copies with minimal clone time.

others.A: Instance store volumes are ephemeral and cannot be restored directly from EBS snapshots.
others.B: Multi-Attach shares the production volumes themselves, so test modifications would affect production, and it is limited to io1/io2.
others.C: You cannot restore a snapshot into an already-created volume, and manually initializing volumes is slow.

e.tip: Snapshot-restored volume needs full performance immediately: EBS fast snapshot restore.

q:
An ecommerce company wants to launch a one-deal-a-day website on AWS. Each day will feature exactly one product on sale for a period of 24 hours. The company wants to be able to handle millions of requests each hour with millisecond latency during peak hours.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon S3 to host the full website in different S3 buckets. Add Amazon CloudFront distributions. Set the S3 buckets as origins for the distributions. Store the order data in Amazon S3.
o.B: Deploy the full website on Amazon EC2 instances that run in Auto Scaling groups across multiple Availability Zones. Add an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to distribute the website traffic. Add another ALB for the backend APIs. Store the data in Amazon RDS for MySQL.
o.C: Migrate the full application to run in containers. Host the containers on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to increase and decrease the number of pods to process bursts in traffic. Store the data in Amazon RDS for MySQL.
o.D: Use an Amazon S3 bucket to host the website's static content. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the S3 bucket as the origin. Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions for the backend APIs. Store the data in Amazon DynamoDB.

e.why: The keyed answer uses EC2 Auto Scaling groups across multiple AZs behind ALBs with RDS for MySQL, which can scale to millions of requests per hour while remaining highly available. However, this design carries significant operational overhead from managing instances, AMIs, patching and database scaling.

others.A: S3 alone cannot run backend order processing logic, and storing order data as S3 objects is not suitable for transactional data.
others.C: Running EKS with the Cluster Autoscaler and RDS adds substantial operational overhead for cluster and node management.
others.D: S3 with CloudFront, API Gateway, Lambda and DynamoDB is fully serverless, scales automatically to millions of requests with millisecond latency, and has the least operational overhead.

e.tip: LEAST operational overhead plus spiky massive traffic usually points to serverless: S3/CloudFront, API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB.
e.flag: The keyed answer B is likely wrong; D (S3 + CloudFront + API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB) is serverless and meets the LEAST operational overhead requirement, and is the widely accepted answer.

q:
A solutions architect is using Amazon S3 to design the storage architecture of a new digital media application. The media files must be resilient to the loss of an Availability Zone. Some files are accessed frequently while other files are rarely accessed in an unpredictable pattern. The solutions architect must minimize the costs of storing and retrieving the media files.
Which storage option meets these requirements?

o.A: S3 Standard
o.B: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
o.C: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
o.D: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)

e.why: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on actual access patterns, with no retrieval fees, making it ideal for mixed and unpredictable access. It stores data across multiple AZs, so it is resilient to the loss of an Availability Zone while minimizing storage and retrieval costs.

others.A: S3 Standard charges the higher frequent-access price for rarely accessed files.
others.C: S3 Standard-IA charges retrieval fees, which become costly for frequently accessed files.
others.D: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ and is not resilient to AZ loss.

e.tip: Unknown or changing access patterns: S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

q:
A company is storing backup files by using Amazon S3 Standard storage. The files are accessed frequently for 1 month. However, the files are not accessed after 1 month. The company must keep the files indefinitely.
Which storage solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically migrate objects.
o.B: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month.
o.C: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 1 month.
o.D: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 month.

e.why: The keyed answer transitions objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-IA after 1 month via a Lifecycle rule, which lowers storage cost while keeping millisecond access. However, because the files are never accessed again and must be kept indefinitely, a colder archival class is much cheaper.

others.A: Intelligent-Tiering adds a per-object monitoring fee and is meant for unpredictable access, while this pattern is known.
others.B: Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost storage class for data that is never accessed but retained indefinitely, so this is the most cost-effective choice.
others.D: One Zone-IA is cheaper than Standard-IA but stores backups in a single AZ and is still far costlier than Deep Archive.

e.tip: Known pattern, never accessed after N days, keep forever: Lifecycle to Glacier Deep Archive.
e.flag: The keyed answer C is likely wrong; B (Lifecycle transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month) is the most cost-effective for files never accessed again and kept indefinitely.

q:
A company observes an increase in Amazon EC2 costs in its most recent bill. The billing team notices unwanted vertical scaling of instance types for a couple of EC2 instances. A solutions architect needs to create a graph comparing the last 2 months of EC2 costs and perform an in-depth analysis to identify the root cause of the vertical scaling.
How should the solutions architect generate the information with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Budgets to create a budget report and compare EC2 costs based on instance types.
o.B: Use Cost Explorer's granular filtering feature to perform an in-depth analysis of EC2 costs based on instance types.
o.C: Use graphs from the AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard to compare EC2 costs based on instance types for the last 2 months.
o.D: Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create a report and send it to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon QuickSight with Amazon S3 as a source to generate an interactive graph based on instance types.

e.why: The keyed answer exports AWS Cost and Usage Reports to S3 and visualizes them in QuickSight, which provides the most detailed line-item data for building interactive graphs by instance type. However, it requires setting up CUR delivery, datasets and dashboards, which is more overhead than necessary.

others.A: AWS Budgets is for tracking spend against thresholds and alerting, not for in-depth historical root cause analysis.
others.B: Cost Explorer natively graphs up to 12+ months of cost and supports granular filtering and grouping by instance type with no setup, giving the least operational overhead.
others.C: The Billing dashboard graphs are high-level and lack granular filtering by instance type.

e.tip: Quick graphing and filtering of recent costs: Cost Explorer.
e.flag: The keyed answer D is likely wrong; B (Cost Explorer granular filtering by instance type) meets the LEAST operational overhead requirement without building a CUR and QuickSight pipeline.

q:
A company is designing an application. The application uses an AWS Lambda function to receive information through Amazon API Gateway and to store the information in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database.
During the proof-of-concept stage, the company has to increase the Lambda quotas significantly to handle the high volumes of data that the company needs to load into the database. A solutions architect must recommend a new design to improve scalability and minimize the configuration effort.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Refactor the Lambda function code to Apache Tomcat code that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Connect the database by using native Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) drivers.
o.B: Change the platform from Aurora to Amazon DynamoDProvision a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Use the DAX client SDK to point the existing DynamoDB API calls at the DAX cluster.
o.C: Set up two Lambda functions. Configure one function to receive the information. Configure the other function to load the information into the database. Integrate the Lambda functions by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
o.D: Set up two Lambda functions. Configure one function to receive the information. Configure the other function to load the information into the database. Integrate the Lambda functions by using an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.

e.why: The keyed answer splits the work into a receiving Lambda function and a loading Lambda function connected by SNS, decoupling ingestion from database writes. However, SNS pushes each message immediately to the subscriber, so it does not buffer load or let the loader control its concurrency against Aurora.

others.A: Refactoring to Tomcat on EC2 increases configuration and management effort and does not inherently improve scalability.
others.B: Migrating from Aurora PostgreSQL to DynamoDB with DAX is a major platform change and DAX only accelerates reads.
others.D: An SQS queue between two Lambda functions durably buffers spikes and lets the loader consume in batches at a controlled rate, improving scalability with minimal configuration.

e.tip: Buffer bursts in front of a database: SQS queue, not SNS.
e.flag: The keyed answer C is likely wrong; D (two Lambda functions decoupled by an SQS queue) is the accepted answer because SQS buffers and throttles load to the database.

q:
A company needs to review its AWS Cloud deployment to ensure that its Amazon S3 buckets do not have unauthorized configuration changes.
What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this goal?

o.A: Turn on AWS Config with the appropriate rules.
o.B: Turn on AWS Trusted Advisor with the appropriate checks.
o.C: Turn on Amazon Inspector with the appropriate assessment template.
o.D: Turn on Amazon S3 server access logging. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon Cloud Watch Events).

e.why: The keyed answer uses AWS Trusted Advisor, whose S3 bucket permissions check flags buckets with open access. However, Trusted Advisor only runs periodic best-practice checks and does not track or evaluate configuration changes over time.

others.A: AWS Config records S3 bucket configuration history and evaluates changes against managed rules such as s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited, which directly detects unauthorized configuration changes.
others.C: Amazon Inspector scans EC2, ECR images and Lambda for vulnerabilities, not S3 bucket configurations.
others.D: S3 server access logging records object requests, not bucket configuration changes, and requires custom processing.

e.tip: Track and audit resource configuration changes: AWS Config.
e.flag: The keyed answer B is likely wrong; A (AWS Config with appropriate rules) is the service built to detect unauthorized configuration changes.

q:
A company is launching a new application and will display application metrics on an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard. The company's product manager needs to access this dashboard periodically. The product manager does not have an AWS account. A solutions architect must provide access to the product manager by following the principle of least privilege.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Share the dashboard from the CloudWatch console. Enter the product manager's email address, and complete the sharing steps. Provide a shareable link for the dashboard to the product manager.
o.B: Create an IAM user specifically for the product manager. Attach the CloudWatchReadOnlyAccess AWS managed policy to the user. Share the new login credentials with the product manager. Share the browser URL of the correct dashboard with the product manager.
o.C: Create an IAM user for the company's employees. Attach the ViewOnlyAccess AWS managed policy to the IAM user. Share the new login credentials with the product manager. Ask the product manager to navigate to the CloudWatch console and locate the dashboard by name in the Dashboards section.
o.D: Deploy a bastion server in a public subnet. When the product manager requires access to the dashboard, start the server and share the RDP credentials. On the bastion server, ensure that the browser is configured to open the dashboard URL with cached AWS credentials that have appropriate permissions to view the dashboard.

e.why: The keyed answer creates an IAM user with the ViewOnlyAccess managed policy and shares credentials with the product manager. However, it is described as an IAM user for the company's employees (shared credentials) and ViewOnlyAccess grants view access far beyond one dashboard, violating least privilege.

others.A: CloudWatch dashboard sharing lets you share a dashboard with specific email addresses so people without an AWS account can view only that dashboard, which best fits least privilege.
others.B: A dedicated IAM user with CloudWatchReadOnlyAccess grants read access to all CloudWatch data, more than just the dashboard.
others.D: A bastion server with cached credentials is complex, insecure and not least privilege.

e.tip: Someone without an AWS account needs to view a CloudWatch dashboard: share the dashboard by email.
e.flag: The keyed answer C is likely wrong; A (share the CloudWatch dashboard with the product manager's email) is the least-privilege answer for a user with no AWS account.

q:
A company is migrating applications to AWS. The applications are deployed in different accounts. The company manages the accounts centrally by using AWS Organizations. The company's security team needs a single sign-on (SSO) solution across all the company's accounts. The company must continue managing the users and groups in its on-premises self-managed Microsoft Active Directory.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console. Create a one-way forest trust or a one-way domain trust to connect the company's self-managed Microsoft Active Directory with AWS SSO by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory.
o.B: Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console. Create a two-way forest trust to connect the company's self-managed Microsoft Active Directory with AWS SSO by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory.
o.C: Use AWS Directory Service. Create a two-way trust relationship with the company's self-managed Microsoft Active Directory.
o.D: Deploy an identity provider (IdP) on premises. Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console.

e.why: AWS IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO) integrates with AWS Organizations to provide single sign-on to all accounts. By deploying AWS Managed Microsoft AD and creating a trust with the self-managed on-premises AD, users and groups continue to be managed on premises while Identity Center uses them for access.

others.B: The keyed answer reflects the bank's view that a one-way trust suffices; note that AWS documentation actually requires a two-way trust between AWS Managed Microsoft AD and on-premises AD for IAM Identity Center.
others.C: Directory Service with a trust alone does not provide SSO across all Organization accounts.
others.D: Deploying an on-premises IdP is extra infrastructure, and the option does not describe connecting it to IAM Identity Center.

e.tip: SSO across Organizations accounts with existing AD: IAM Identity Center plus AD Connector or AWS Managed Microsoft AD trust.
e.flag: AWS documentation states IAM Identity Center requires a two-way trust between AWS Managed Microsoft AD and the self-managed AD, so B is arguably correct rather than A.

q:
A company provides a Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) service that uses UDP connections. The service consists of Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group. The company has deployments across multiple AWS Regions.
The company needs to route users to the Region with the lowest latency. The company also needs automated failover between Regions.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Use the NLB as an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint in each Region.
o.B: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Use the ALB as an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint in each Region.
o.C: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Create an Amazon Route 53 latency record that points to aliases for each NLB. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the latency record as an origin.
o.D: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Create an Amazon Route 53 weighted record that points to aliases for each ALB. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the weighted record as an origin.

fixed: Options B, C and D were garbled (C and D truncated, B replaced by D's tail) and have been reconstructed.

e.why: The keyed answer C uses NLBs (which support UDP) behind a Route 53 latency record. However, it places Amazon CloudFront in front, and CloudFront only handles HTTP/HTTPS, so it cannot carry VoIP UDP traffic. NLBs as AWS Global Accelerator endpoints (option A) route UDP users to the lowest-latency Region over the AWS backbone with automatic health-based failover.

others.A: This is actually the best design: Global Accelerator supports UDP, routes to the nearest healthy Region, and fails over automatically.
others.B: ALBs do not support UDP, so they cannot serve the VoIP traffic even behind Global Accelerator.
others.D: ALBs do not support UDP, CloudFront does not carry UDP, and weighted routing does not pick the lowest-latency Region.

e.tip: UDP plus multi-Region lowest latency plus fast failover = Global Accelerator with NLB endpoints.
e.flag: The keyed answer C is likely wrong: CloudFront cannot carry UDP. A (NLBs as AWS Global Accelerator endpoints) is the accepted answer.

q:
A development team runs monthly resource-intensive tests on its general purpose Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with Performance Insights enabled. The testing lasts for 48 hours once a month and is the only process that uses the database. The team wants to reduce the cost of running the tests without reducing the compute and memory attributes of the DB instance.
Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Stop the DB instance when tests are completed. Restart the DB instance when required.
o.B: Use an Auto Scaling policy with the DB instance to automatically scale when tests are completed.
o.C: Create a snapshot when tests are completed. Terminate the DB instance and restore the snapshot when required.
o.D: Modify the DB instance to a low-capacity instance when tests are completed. Modify the DB instance again when required.

e.why: Because the database is only used for 48 hours a month, taking a snapshot and deleting the instance means paying only for snapshot storage for the rest of the month. Restoring the snapshot to the same instance class when needed preserves the compute and memory attributes, making this the most cost-effective option.

others.A: A stopped RDS instance still incurs storage charges and automatically restarts after 7 days, so it would run for much of the month.
others.B: RDS does not support Auto Scaling of DB instance compute size.
others.D: Downsizing still incurs ongoing instance charges and repeated modifications cause downtime and effort.

e.tip: RDS stopped instances auto-start after 7 days; for rare long gaps, snapshot and delete.

q:
A company that hosts its web application on AWS wants to ensure all Amazon EC2 instances. Amazon RDS DB instances. and Amazon Redshift clusters are configured with tags. The company wants to minimize the effort of configuring and operating this check.
What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this?

o.A: Use AWS Config rules to define and detect resources that are not properly tagged.
o.B: Use Cost Explorer to display resources that are not properly tagged. Tag those resources manually.
o.C: Write API calls to check all resources for proper tag allocation. Periodically run the code on an EC2 instance.
o.D: Write API calls to check all resources for proper tag allocation. Schedule an AWS Lambda function through Amazon CloudWatch to periodically run the code.

e.why: AWS Config has a managed rule, required-tags, that continuously evaluates supported resources such as EC2 instances, RDS DB instances and Redshift clusters and flags those missing required tags. It is a managed check that requires minimal effort to configure and operate.

others.B: Cost Explorer can filter by tags but does not continuously detect noncompliant resources, and manual tagging is effortful.
others.C: Custom API scripts on an EC2 instance require building and maintaining code and infrastructure.
others.D: A scheduled Lambda with custom API calls still requires writing and maintaining code.

e.tip: Continuous compliance checks for tags or settings: AWS Config rules.

q:
A development team needs to host a website that will be accessed by other teams. The website contents consist of HTML, CSS, client-side JavaScript, and images.
Which method is the MOST cost-effective for hosting the website?

o.A: Containerize the website and host it in AWS Fargate.
o.B: Create an Amazon S3 bucket and host the website there.
o.C: Deploy a web server on an Amazon EC2 instance to host the website.
o.D: Configure an Application Load Balancer with an AWS Lambda target that uses the Express.js framework.

e.why: The site is purely static content (HTML, CSS, client-side JavaScript and images), which S3 static website hosting serves directly. You pay only for storage and requests, with no servers to run, making it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Fargate containers incur continuous compute charges and are unnecessary for static files.
others.C: An EC2 web server incurs ongoing instance costs and management overhead.
others.D: An ALB with Lambda incurs hourly ALB charges and is designed for dynamic content.

e.tip: Static website with no server-side code: S3 static website hosting (optionally behind CloudFront).

q:
A company runs an online marketplace web application on AWS. The application serves hundreds of thousands of users during peak hours. The company needs a scalable, near-real-time solution to share the details of millions of financial transactions with several other internal applications. Transactions also need to be processed to remove sensitive data before being stored in a document database for low-latency retrieval.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Store the transactions data into Amazon DynamoDB. Set up a rule in DynamoDB to remove sensitive data from every transaction upon write. Use DynamoDB Streams to share the transactions data with other applications.
o.B: Stream the transactions data into Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to store data in Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon S3. Use AWS Lambda integration with Kinesis Data Firehose to remove sensitive data. Other applications can consume the data stored in Amazon S3.
o.C: Stream the transactions data into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use AWS Lambda integration to remove sensitive data from every transaction and then store the transactions data in Amazon DynamoDB. Other applications can consume the transactions data off the Kinesis data stream.
o.D: Store the batched transactions data in Amazon S3 as files. Use AWS Lambda to process every file and remove sensitive data before updating the files in Amazon S3. The Lambda function then stores the data in Amazon DynamoDB. Other applications can consume transaction files stored in Amazon S3.

fixed: All four options were garbled by text splitting and have been reconstructed.

e.why: Kinesis Data Streams ingests millions of transactions in near real time and lets several internal applications consume the same stream concurrently. A Lambda consumer removes sensitive data from each record and writes the sanitized transactions to DynamoDB, a document database with low-latency retrieval.

others.A: DynamoDB has no built-in rule to strip sensitive data on write, and raw data would be stored before any sanitization.
others.B: Kinesis Data Firehose cannot deliver to DynamoDB, and consuming from S3 is not near real time for other applications.
others.D: Batched files in S3 are not near real time, and reprocessing files adds latency.

e.tip: Near-real-time sharing with multiple consumers = Kinesis Data Streams; Firehose is for delivery to stores like S3/Redshift/OpenSearch.

q:
A company hosts its multi-tier applications on AWS. For compliance, governance, auditing, and security, the company must track configuration changes on its AWS resources and record a history of API calls made to these resources.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS CloudTrail to track configuration changes and AWS Config to record API calls.
o.B: Use AWS Config to track configuration changes and AWS CloudTrail to record API calls.
o.C: Use AWS Config to track configuration changes and Amazon CloudWatch to record API calls.
o.D: Use AWS CloudTrail to track configuration changes and Amazon CloudWatch to record API calls.

e.why: AWS Config records resource configurations and keeps a history of configuration changes for compliance and auditing. AWS CloudTrail records API calls made in the account, including who made them, when and from where, so together they meet both requirements.

others.A: This reverses the roles; CloudTrail records API calls while Config tracks configuration changes.
others.C: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs; it does not natively record a history of API calls.
others.D: CloudTrail does not provide configuration history, and CloudWatch does not record API call history.

e.tip: Config = what changed in resource configuration; CloudTrail = who called which API.

q:
A company is preparing to launch a public-facing web application in the AWS Cloud. The architecture consists of Amazon EC2 instances within a VPC behind an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB). A third-party service is used for the DNS. The company's solutions architect must recommend a solution to detect and protect against large-scale DDoS attacks.
Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Enable Amazon GuardDuty on the account.
o.B: Enable Amazon Inspector on the EC2 instances.
o.C: Enable AWS Shield and assign Amazon Route 53 to it.
o.D: Enable AWS Shield Advanced and assign the ELB to it.

e.why: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced detection and mitigation of large-scale DDoS attacks for protected resources such as Elastic Load Balancers, plus 24/7 access to the Shield Response Team and DDoS cost protection. Because DNS is hosted by a third party, protecting the ELB itself is the correct choice.

others.A: GuardDuty detects threats from logs but does not mitigate DDoS attacks.
others.B: Amazon Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities, not DDoS attacks.
others.C: Route 53 is not used because DNS is with a third party, and Shield Standard lacks the advanced large-scale DDoS detection and response.

e.tip: Large-scale DDoS protection with response team and cost protection: Shield Advanced on ELB, CloudFront, Global Accelerator, Route 53 or EIPs.

q:
A company is building an application in the AWS Cloud. The application will store data in Amazon S3 buckets in two AWS Regions. The company must use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt all data that is stored in the S3 buckets. The data in both S3 buckets must be encrypted and decrypted with the same KMS key. The data and the key must be stored in each of the two Regions.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an S3 bucket in each Region. Configure the S3 buckets to use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Configure replication between the S3 buckets.
o.B: Create a customer managed multi-Region KMS key. Create an S3 bucket in each Region. Configure replication between the S3 buckets. Configure the application to use the KMS key with client-side encryption.
o.C: Create a customer managed KMS key and an S3 bucket in each Region. Configure the S3 buckets to use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Configure replication between the S3 buckets.
o.D: Create a customer managed KMS key and an S3 bucket in each Region. Configure the S3 buckets to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure replication between the S3 buckets.

e.why: A customer managed multi-Region KMS key creates related keys in each Region that share the same key material and key ID, so data can be encrypted in one Region and decrypted in another with the same key, and the key exists in both Regions. With S3 replication between buckets, client-side encryption with that key ensures consistent encryption using one logical key.

others.A: SSE-S3 uses S3 managed keys, not a customer managed KMS key.
others.C: SSE-S3 does not use the customer managed KMS keys, and separate keys per Region are not the same key.
others.D: Separate single-Region KMS keys in each Region are different keys, violating the same-key requirement.

e.tip: Same KMS key usable in multiple Regions: multi-Region keys.

q:
A company recently launched a variety of new workloads on Amazon EC2 instances in its AWS account. The company needs to create a strategy to access and administer the instances remotely and securely. The company needs to implement a repeatable process that works with native AWS services and follows the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use the EC2 serial console to directly access the terminal interface of each instance for administration.
o.B: Attach the appropriate IAM role to each existing instance and new instance. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to establish a remote SSH session.
o.C: Create an administrative SSH key pair. Load the public key into each EC2 instance. Deploy a bastion host in a public subnet to provide a tunnel for administration of each instance.
o.D: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Instruct administrators to use their local on-premises machines to connect directly to the instances by using SSH keys across the VPN tunnel.

e.why: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides secure, auditable shell access to EC2 instances through the SSM Agent and an IAM instance role, with no open inbound ports, bastion hosts or SSH keys to manage. It is a native, repeatable approach aligned with the Well-Architected Framework and has the least operational overhead.

others.A: The EC2 serial console is intended for troubleshooting boot and network issues, not routine administration at scale.
others.C: Managing SSH keys and a bastion host adds operational overhead and attack surface.
others.D: A Site-to-Site VPN with SSH keys adds infrastructure and key management overhead.

e.tip: Secure remote instance access without SSH keys or bastions: Session Manager.

q:
A company is hosting a static website on Amazon S3 and is using Amazon Route 53 for DNS. The website is experiencing increased demand from around the world. The company must decrease latency for users who access the website.
Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Replicate the S3 bucket that contains the website to all AWS Regions. Add Route 53 geolocation routing entries.
o.B: Provision accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator. Associate the supplied IP addresses with the S3 bucket. Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the IP addresses of the accelerators.
o.C: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket. Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the CloudFront distribution.
o.D: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket. Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the new endpoint.

e.why: Amazon CloudFront caches the static website content at edge locations worldwide, reducing latency for global users, and Route 53 alias records can point the domain to the distribution. It is inexpensive and often reduces S3 data transfer costs, making it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Replicating the bucket to all Regions multiplies storage and replication costs and adds complexity.
others.B: Global Accelerator does not support S3 buckets as endpoints and is more expensive.
others.D: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads to S3, not content delivery to website viewers.

e.tip: Reduce global latency for static content: CloudFront.

q:
A company maintains a searchable repository of items on its website. The data is stored in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database table that contains more than 10 million rows. The database has 2 TB of General Purpose SSD storage. There are millions of updates against this data every day through the company's website.
The company has noticed that some insert operations are taking 10 seconds or longer. The company has determined that the database storage performance is the problem.
Which solution addresses this performance issue?

o.A: Change the storage type to Provisioned IOPS SSD.
o.D: Enable Multi-AZ RDS read replicas with MySQL native asynchronous replication.
o.B: Change the DB instance to a memory optimized instance class.
o.C: Change the DB instance to a burstable performance instance class.

fixed: Option A was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) storage delivers consistent, high I/O performance with low latency, suited to I/O-intensive workloads with millions of daily writes. Because storage performance is the bottleneck, moving from General Purpose SSD to Provisioned IOPS directly addresses the slow inserts.

others.B: A memory optimized instance class helps memory-bound workloads, not a storage I/O bottleneck.
others.C: Burstable instances relate to CPU credits and would not fix storage performance; they could make things worse.
others.D: Read replicas offload reads, but the problem is slow inserts, which still go to the primary.

e.tip: Storage I/O is the bottleneck for an RDS database = Provisioned IOPS SSD.

q:
A company has thousands of edge devices that collectively generate 1 TB of status alerts each day. Each alert is approximately 2 KB in size. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to ingest and store the alerts for future analysis.
The company wants a highly available solution. However, the company needs to minimize costs and does not want to manage additional infrastructure. Additionally, the company wants to keep 14 days of data available for immediate analysis and archive any data older than 14 days.
What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to ingest the alerts. Configure the Kinesis Data Firehose stream to deliver the alerts to an Amazon S3 bucket. Set up an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition data to Amazon S3 Glacier after 14 days.
o.B: Launch Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones and place them behind an Elastic Load Balancer to ingest the alerts. Create a script on the EC2 instances that will store the alerts in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set up an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition data to Amazon S3 Glacier after 14 days.
o.C: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to ingest the alerts. Configure the Kinesis Data Firehose stream to deliver the alerts to an Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster. Set up the Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster to take manual snapshots every day and delete data from the cluster that is older than 14 days.
o.D: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue to ingest the alerts, and set the message retention period to 14 days. Configure consumers to poll the SQS queue, check the age of the message, and analyze the message data as needed. If the message is 14 days old, the consumer should copy the message to an Amazon S3 bucket and delete the message from the SQS queue.

e.why: Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed, highly available service that ingests streaming data and delivers it to S3 without infrastructure to manage. Storing alerts in S3 keeps 14 days available for analysis, and an S3 Lifecycle rule transitions older data to S3 Glacier automatically, making this the most operationally efficient and low-cost option.

others.B: EC2 instances behind an ELB with custom scripts add infrastructure to manage and higher cost.
others.C: An OpenSearch cluster is more expensive and requires managing snapshots and data deletion.
others.D: SQS is not a storage or analytics platform, and custom consumers checking message age add complexity.

e.tip: Managed streaming ingestion to S3: Kinesis Data Firehose, then Lifecycle rules for archiving.

q:
A company's application integrates with multiple software-as-a-service (SaaS) sources for data collection. The company runs Amazon EC2 instances to receive the data and to upload the data to an Amazon S3 bucket for analysis. The same EC2 instance that receives and uploads the data also sends a notification to the user when an upload is complete. The company has noticed slow application performance and wants to improve the performance as much as possible.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an Auto Scaling group so that EC2 instances can scale out. Configure an S3 event notification to send events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete.
o.B: Create an Amazon AppFlow flow to transfer data between each SaaS source and the S3 bucket. Configure an S3 event notification to send events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete.
o.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for each SaaS source to send output data. Configure the S3 bucket as the rule's target. Create a second EventBridge (Cloud Watch Events) rule to send events when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the second rule's target.
o.D: Create a Docker container to use instead of an EC2 instance. Host the containerized application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to send events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete.

e.why: Amazon AppFlow is a fully managed integration service that securely transfers data from SaaS applications to S3 without custom code or EC2 instances, removing the performance bottleneck. An S3 event notification to an SNS topic handles the upload-complete notification, giving the best performance with the least operational overhead.

others.A: Scaling EC2 instances still requires managing servers and custom ingestion code.
others.C: EventBridge rules per SaaS source cannot write data directly to S3 as a target, and this requires more configuration.
others.D: Containerizing on ECS still requires managing the ingestion code, and Container Insights does not emit S3 upload events.

e.tip: SaaS to AWS data transfer without code: Amazon AppFlow.

q:
A company runs a highly available image-processing application on Amazon EC2 instances in a single VPC. The EC2 instances run inside several subnets across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances do not communicate with each other. However, the EC2 instances download images from Amazon S3 and upload images to Amazon S3 through a single NAT gateway. The company is concerned about data transfer charges.
What is the MOST cost-effective way for the company to avoid Regional data transfer charges?

o.A: Launch the NAT gateway in each Availability Zone.
o.B: Replace the NAT gateway with a NAT instance.
o.C: Deploy a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3.
o.D: Provision an EC2 Dedicated Host to run the EC2 instances.

e.why: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 routes S3 traffic privately from the VPC without going through the NAT gateway. Gateway endpoints have no hourly or data processing charges, eliminating NAT gateway data processing costs, making it the most cost-effective choice.

others.A: A NAT gateway per AZ adds hourly charges and still incurs data processing charges for S3 traffic.
others.B: A NAT instance adds management overhead and still routes S3 traffic through a NAT path.
others.D: Dedicated Hosts increase cost and do not affect data transfer charges.
