e.tip: S3 or DynamoDB traffic through NAT is costly: add a free gateway endpoint.

q:
A company has an on-premises application that generates a large amount of time-sensitive data that is backed up to Amazon S3. The application has grown and there are user complaints about internet bandwidth limitations. A solutions architect needs to design a long-term solution that allows for both timely backups to Amazon S3 and with minimal impact on internet connectivity for internal users.
Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Establish AWS VPN connections and proxy all traffic through a VPC gateway endpoint.
o.B: Establish a new AWS Direct Connect connection and direct backup traffic through this new connection.
o.C: Order daily AWS Snowball devices. Load the data onto the Snowball devices and return the devices to AWS each day.
o.D: Submit a support ticket through the AWS Management Console. Request the removal of S3 service limits from the account.

e.why: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private network connection from on premises to AWS that does not consume the internet link. Routing backup traffic over Direct Connect gives consistent, timely backups to S3 as a long-term solution while freeing internet bandwidth for internal users.

others.A: A VPN still runs over the existing internet connection, so it does not relieve bandwidth, and gateway endpoints are not reachable from on premises this way.
others.C: Ordering Snowball devices daily is operationally heavy and too slow for time-sensitive data.
others.D: S3 service limits are not the cause of the internet bandwidth problem.

e.tip: Long-term, consistent bandwidth to AWS separate from internet: Direct Connect.

q:
A company has an Amazon S3 bucket that contains critical data. The company must protect the data from accidental deletion.
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Enable versioning on the S3 bucket.
o.B: Enable MFA Delete on the S3 bucket.
o.C: Create a bucket policy on the S3 bucket.
o.D: Enable default encryption on the S3 bucket.
o.E: Create a lifecycle policy for the objects in the S3 bucket.

e.why: S3 Versioning keeps prior versions of objects, so an accidental delete only adds a delete marker and the data can be recovered. MFA Delete requires multi-factor authentication to permanently delete object versions or change versioning state, adding a further safeguard against accidental deletion.

others.C: A bucket policy can restrict deletes but does not provide recovery if data is deleted by an authorized user.
others.D: Default encryption protects confidentiality, not against deletion.
others.E: Lifecycle policies manage transitions and expirations and could actually delete data.

e.tip: Protect from accidental deletion: Versioning plus MFA Delete (or Object Lock).

q:
A company has a data ingestion workflow that consists of the following:
• An Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for notifications about new data deliveries
• An AWS Lambda function to process the data and record metadata
The company observes that the ingestion workflow fails occasionally because of network connectivity issues. When such a failure occurs, the Lambda function does not ingest the corresponding data unless the company manually reruns the job.
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to ensure that the Lambda function ingests all data in the future? (Choose two.)

o.A: Deploy the Lambda function in multiple Availability Zones.
o.B: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue, and subscribe it to the SNS topic.
o.C: Increase the CPU and memory that are allocated to the Lambda function.
o.D: Increase provisioned throughput for the Lambda function.
o.E: Modify the Lambda function to read from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.

e.why: Subscribing an SQS queue to the SNS topic durably stores each notification, and having the Lambda function read from the queue means messages that fail processing become visible again and are retried automatically. This SNS to SQS to Lambda pattern ensures every delivery is eventually ingested without manual reruns.

others.A: Lambda already runs across multiple AZs automatically, and this does not address lost messages.
others.C: More CPU and memory do not fix transient network failures or add retries.
others.D: Lambda has no provisioned throughput setting, and provisioned concurrency would not add durability.

e.tip: Need retry durability for events: put an SQS queue in front of Lambda.

q:
A company has an application that provides marketing services to stores. The services are based on previous purchases by store customers. The stores upload transaction data to the company through SFTP, and the data is processed and analyzed to generate new marketing offers. Some of the files can exceed 200 GB in size.
Recently, the company discovered that some of the stores have uploaded files that contain personally identifiable information (PII) that should not have been included. The company wants administrators to be alerted if PII is shared again. The company also wants to automate remediation.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

o.A: Use an Amazon S3 bucket as a secure transfer point. Use Amazon Inspector to scan the objects in the bucket. If objects contain PII, trigger an S3 Lifecycle policy to remove the objects that contain PII.
o.B: Use an Amazon S3 bucket as a secure transfer point. Use Amazon Macie to scan the objects in the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to trigger a notification to the administrators to remove the objects that contain PII.
o.C: Implement custom scanning algorithms in an AWS Lambda function. Trigger the function when objects are loaded into the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to trigger a notification to the administrators to remove the objects that contain PII.
o.D: Implement custom scanning algorithms in an AWS Lambda function. Trigger the function when objects are loaded into the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to trigger a notification to the administrators and trigger an S3 Lifecycle policy to remove the meats that contain PII.

e.why: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover PII in S3 objects with no custom code. Macie findings can trigger notifications through EventBridge and SNS to alert administrators, giving the least development effort.

others.A: Amazon Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities, not PII in S3 objects, and Lifecycle policies cannot be triggered per finding.
others.C: Writing custom PII scanning algorithms in Lambda requires significant development effort.
others.D: Custom scanning in Lambda requires significant development, and Lifecycle policies cannot be triggered on demand per object.

e.tip: Detect PII or sensitive data in S3: Amazon Macie.

q:
A company needs guaranteed Amazon EC2 capacity in three specific Availability Zones in a specific AWS Region for an upcoming event that will last 1 week.
What should the company do to guarantee the EC2 capacity?

o.A: Purchase Reserved Instances that specify the Region needed.
o.B: Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies the Region needed.
o.C: Purchase Reserved Instances that specify the Region and three Availability Zones needed.
o.D: Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies the Region and three Availability Zones needed.

e.why: On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone for any duration, with no long-term commitment, and can be cancelled after the event. Creating reservations in each of the three required AZs guarantees capacity for the one-week event.

others.A: Reserved Instances require 1- or 3-year terms, and Regional RIs do not reserve capacity.
others.B: Capacity Reservations are AZ-specific; specifying only the Region does not guarantee capacity in the needed AZs.
others.C: Zonal Reserved Instances do reserve capacity, but they require a 1- or 3-year commitment, which is wasteful for a 1-week event.

e.tip: Short-term guaranteed capacity in specific AZs: On-Demand Capacity Reservations.

q:
A company's website uses an Amazon EC2 instance store for its catalog of items. The company wants to make sure that the catalog is highly available and that the catalog is stored in a durable location.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Move the catalog to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
o.B: Deploy a larger EC2 instance with a larger instance store.
o.C: Move the catalog from the instance store to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
o.D: Move the catalog to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.

e.why: Instance store is ephemeral and data is lost if the instance stops or fails. Amazon EFS is a durable, highly available file system that stores data redundantly across multiple AZs and can be mounted by multiple instances, meeting both requirements.

others.A: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, not a primary durable store for the catalog.
others.B: A larger instance store is still ephemeral and tied to a single instance.
others.C: Glacier Deep Archive has retrieval times of hours, unsuitable for a live website catalog.

e.tip: Instance store = ephemeral; for durable shared files, use EFS.

q:
A company stores call transcript files on a monthly basis. Users access the files randomly within 1 year of the call, but users access the files infrequently after 1 year. The company wants to optimize its solution by giving users the ability to query and retrieve files that are less than 1-year-old as quickly as possible. A delay in retrieving older files is acceptable.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Store individual files with tags in Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. Query the tags to retrieve the files from S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
o.B: Store individual files in Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year. Query and retrieve the files that are in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena. Query and retrieve the files that are in S3 Glacier by using S3 Glacier Select.
o.C: Store individual files with tags in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Store search metadata for each archive in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 year. Query and retrieve the files by searching for metadata from Amazon S3.
o.D: Store individual files in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Store search metadata in Amazon RDS. Query the files from Amazon RDS. Retrieve the files from S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

e.why: S3 Intelligent-Tiering optimizes cost for randomly accessed files in the first year while keeping millisecond access, and Athena can query data in S3 directly. A Lifecycle rule moves files older than 1 year to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, a cheaper class where the acceptable retrieval delay applies, and S3 Glacier Select can query archived data.

others.A: Keeping all files in Glacier Instant Retrieval is costly for randomly accessed recent files due to retrieval fees, and S3 tags cannot be queried for search.
others.C: Glacier Instant Retrieval is pricier than Flexible Retrieval for old files where delay is acceptable, and searching metadata in S3 is cumbersome.
others.D: Running an RDS database for search metadata adds cost and management overhead.

e.tip: Delay acceptable for old data: move to a colder Glacier tier with Lifecycle.

q:
A company has a production workload that runs on 1,000 Amazon EC2 Linux instances. The workload is powered by third-party software. The company needs to patch the third-party software on all EC2 instances as quickly as possible to remediate a critical security vulnerability.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
o.B: Configure AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
o.C: Schedule an AWS Systems Manager maintenance window to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
o.D: Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run a custom command that applies the patch to all EC2 instances.

e.why: Systems Manager Run Command executes a custom script across many managed instances at once with configurable concurrency and targeting by tags, so a third-party software patch can be applied to all 1,000 instances immediately. This is the fastest way to remediate the critical vulnerability.

others.A: Lambda cannot directly run commands on EC2 instances without additional tooling and custom code.
others.B: Patch Manager is focused on OS and supported package patches with baselines and may not handle this third-party software patch as quickly.
others.C: A maintenance window schedules work for later rather than applying the patch as quickly as possible.

e.tip: Run an ad hoc script on a fleet now: Systems Manager Run Command.

q:
A company is developing an application that provides order shipping statistics for retrieval by a REST API. The company wants to extract the shipping statistics, organize the data into an easy-to-read HTML format, and send the report to several email addresses at the same time every morning.
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Configure the application to send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
o.B: Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to format the data and to send the report by email.
o.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Glue job to query the application's API for the data.
o.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Lambda function to query the application's API for the data.
o.E: Store the application data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as an S3 event destination to send the report by email.

e.why: An EventBridge scheduled rule can invoke a Lambda function every morning to query the REST API for the shipping statistics. Amazon SES can send formatted HTML email to multiple recipients, so Lambda builds the HTML report and sends it through SES.

others.A: Kinesis Data Firehose is for streaming delivery, not generating scheduled email reports.
others.C: AWS Glue is an ETL service and is heavier than needed to call a REST API.
others.E: SNS email notifications are plain text and not suitable for formatted HTML reports.

e.tip: Scheduled job: EventBridge schedule plus Lambda; formatted email: SES, not SNS.

q:
A company wants to migrate its on-premises application to AWS. The application produces output files that vary in size from tens of gigabytes to hundreds of terabytes. The application data must be stored in a standard file system structure. The company wants a solution that scales automatically. is highly available, and requires minimum operational overhead.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate the application to run as containers on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Use Amazon S3 for storage.
o.B: Migrate the application to run as containers on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) for storage.
o.C: Migrate the application to Amazon EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for storage.
o.D: Migrate the application to Amazon EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) for storage.

e.why: Amazon EFS provides a standard POSIX file system that scales automatically to petabytes, is highly available across multiple AZs and is fully managed. EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group can share the EFS file system, meeting scalability, availability and minimal overhead requirements.

others.A: Amazon S3 is object storage, not a standard file system structure.
others.B: EBS volumes are AZ-bound, do not scale automatically, and are not shared across pods in multiple AZs.
others.D: EBS is tied to a single AZ and instance, does not scale automatically, and is not highly available across AZs.

e.tip: Shared, auto-scaling file system across AZs: EFS.

q:
A company needs to store its accounting records in Amazon S3. The records must be immediately accessible for 1 year and then must be archived for an additional 9 years. No one at the company, including administrative users and root users, can be able to delete the records during the entire 10-year period. The records must be stored with maximum resiliency.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Store the records in S3 Glacier for the entire 10-year period. Use an access control policy to deny deletion of the records for a period of 10 years.
o.B: Store the records by using S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use an IAM policy to deny deletion of the records. After 10 years, change the IAM policy to allow deletion.
o.C: Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for a period of 10 years.
o.D: Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode for a period of 10 years.

e.why: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode prevents any user, including the root user, from deleting or overwriting locked object versions until the retention period expires, satisfying the 10-year non-deletion requirement. A Lifecycle rule keeps records in S3 Standard for immediate access during year 1 and then moves them to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, which stores data across multiple AZs for maximum resiliency at the lowest cost.

others.A: Glacier for the full period does not give immediate access in year 1, and access policies can be changed by administrators or root.
others.B: IAM policies can be modified by administrators and do not restrict the root user.
others.D: Governance mode lets users with special permissions bypass retention, and One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, reducing resiliency.

e.tip: No one, not even root, can delete: Object Lock compliance mode.

q:
A company runs multiple Windows workloads on AWS. The company's employees use Windows file shares that are hosted on two Amazon EC2 instances. The file shares synchronize data between themselves and maintain duplicate copies. The company wants a highly available and durable storage solution that preserves how users currently access the files.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate all the data to Amazon S3. Set up IAM authentication for users to access files.
o.B: Set up an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Mount the S3 File Gateway on the existing EC2 instances.
o.C: Extend the file share environment to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to FSx for Windows File Server.
o.D: Extend the file share environment to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to Amazon EFS.

e.why: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed native Windows file shares over SMB with Active Directory integration, so users keep accessing files the same way. A Multi-AZ deployment replicates data synchronously across two AZs with automatic failover, giving high availability and durability.

others.A: S3 is object storage and would change how users access files, replacing SMB shares.
others.B: S3 File Gateway is designed for on-premises access to S3, not for replacing Windows file shares on EC2.
others.D: Amazon EFS uses NFS and does not support Windows SMB clients.

e.tip: Windows SMB file shares in AWS: FSx for Windows File Server (Multi-AZ for HA).

q:
A solutions architect is developing a VPC architecture that includes multiple subnets. The architecture will host applications that use Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS DB instances. The architecture consists of six subnets in two Availability Zones. Each Availability Zone includes a public subnet, a private subnet, and a dedicated subnet for databases. Only EC2 instances that run in the private subnets can have access to the RDS databases.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a new route table that excludes the route to the public subnets' CIDR blocks. Associate the route table with the database subnets.
o.B: Create a security group that denies inbound traffic from the security group that is assigned to instances in the public subnets. Attach the security group to the DB instances.
o.C: Create a security group that allows inbound traffic from the security group that is assigned to instances in the private subnets. Attach the security group to the DB instances.
o.D: Create a new peering connection between the public subnets and the private subnets. Create a different peering connection between the private subnets and the database subnets.

e.why: Security groups are stateful allow-only firewalls that can reference other security groups as sources. Attaching a security group to the DB instances that allows inbound database traffic only from the security group of the private subnet instances restricts access exactly as required.

others.A: Route tables cannot block traffic within a VPC because the local route always allows communication among subnets.
others.B: Security groups cannot contain deny rules; they only allow traffic.
others.D: VPC peering connects VPCs, not subnets within the same VPC.

e.tip: Security groups allow only (no deny); reference source security groups for tier-to-tier access.

q:
A company has registered its domain name with Amazon Route 53. The company uses Amazon API Gateway in the ca-central-1 Region as a public interface for its backend microservice APIs. Third-party services consume the APIs securely. The company wants to design its API Gateway URL with the company's domain name and corresponding certificate so that the third-party services can use HTTPS.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create stage variables in API Gateway with Name="Endpoint-URL" and Value="Company Domain Name" to overwrite the default URL. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).
o.B: Create Route 53 DNS records with the company's domain name. Point the alias record to the Regional API Gateway stage endpoint. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.
o.C: Create a Regional API Gateway endpoint. Associate the API Gateway endpoint with the company's domain name. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region. Attach the certificate to the API Gateway endpoint. Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the API Gateway endpoint.
o.D: Create a Regional API Gateway endpoint. Associate the API Gateway endpoint with the company's domain name. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region. Attach the certificate to the API Gateway APIs. Create Route 53 DNS records with the company's domain name. Point an A record to the company's domain name.

e.why: For a Regional API Gateway endpoint with a custom domain name, the ACM certificate must be in the same Region as the API, here ca-central-1. You create the custom domain name, attach the certificate, map it to the API and create a Route 53 alias record to the API Gateway domain, enabling HTTPS with the company's domain.

others.A: Stage variables cannot change the API's default URL or domain.
others.B: For a Regional endpoint the certificate must be in the API's Region, not us-east-1, and no custom domain name is configured.
others.D: us-east-1 certificates are required only for edge-optimized endpoints, and pointing an A record to the company's own domain is circular.

e.tip: ACM certificate Region: same Region for Regional endpoints and ALB; us-east-1 for CloudFront and edge-optimized APIs.

q:
A company is running a popular social media website. The website gives users the ability to upload images to share with other users. The company wants to make sure that the images do not contain inappropriate content. The company needs a solution that minimizes development effort.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon Comprehend to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
o.B: Use Amazon Rekognition to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
o.C: Use Amazon SageMaker to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.
o.D: Use AWS Fargate to deploy a custom machine learning model to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.

e.why: Amazon Rekognition Content Moderation detects inappropriate, unwanted or offensive content in images through a simple API, with no model training. Amazon Augmented AI can route low-confidence predictions to human reviewers, minimizing development effort.

others.A: Amazon Comprehend analyzes text, not images.
others.C: Building and training a custom model in SageMaker requires significant development effort.
others.D: Deploying a custom ML model on Fargate requires building, training and operating the model yourself.

e.tip: Image or video moderation: Rekognition; text NLP: Comprehend.

q:
A company wants to run its critical applications in containers to meet requirements for scalability and availability. The company prefers to focus on maintenance of the critical applications. The company does not want to be responsible for provisioning and managing the underlying infrastructure that runs the containerized workload.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon EC2 instances, and install Docker on the instances.
o.B: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2 worker nodes.
o.C: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
o.D: Use Amazon EC2 instances from an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)-optimized Amazon Machine Image (AMI).

e.why: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate runs containers without provisioning, patching or scaling EC2 instances, so the company manages only its applications. ECS services spread tasks across AZs and integrate with Application Auto Scaling for scalability and availability.

others.A: Running Docker on self-managed EC2 instances requires managing the infrastructure.
others.B: ECS on EC2 worker nodes still requires managing the underlying instances.
others.D: Using an ECS-optimized AMI still means managing EC2 instances.

e.tip: Containers without managing servers: Fargate.

q:
A company hosts more than 300 global websites and applications. The company requires a platform to analyze more than 30 TB of clickstream data each day.
What should a solutions architect do to transmit and process the clickstream data?

o.A: Design an AWS Data Pipeline to archive the data to an Amazon S3 bucket and run an Amazon EMR cluster with the data to generate analytics.
o.B: Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to process the data and send it to an Amazon S3 data lake for Amazon Redshift to use for analysis.
o.C: Cache the data to Amazon CloudFront. Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. When an object is added to the S3 bucket. run an AWS Lambda function to process the data for analysis.
o.D: Collect the data from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to transmit the data to an Amazon S3 data lake. Load the data in Amazon Redshift for analysis.

e.why: Kinesis Data Streams ingests massive volumes of real-time clickstream data from many sources, and Kinesis Data Firehose delivers the data reliably into an S3 data lake. The data can then be loaded into Amazon Redshift for scalable analytics, forming a standard clickstream pipeline at 30 TB per day.

others.A: AWS Data Pipeline is a legacy batch orchestration service and does not handle real-time ingestion from hundreds of sites.
others.B: An Auto Scaling group of EC2 processors requires custom ingestion code and management.
others.C: CloudFront is a content delivery network, not a data ingestion or caching layer for clickstream data.

e.tip: Clickstream ingestion at scale: Kinesis Data Streams/Firehose to S3, then Redshift or Athena.

q:
A company has a website hosted on AWS. The website is behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that is configured to handle HTTP and HTTPS separately. The company wants to forward all requests to the website so that the requests will use HTTPS.
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.A: Update the ALB's network ACL to accept only HTTPS traffic.
o.B: Create a rule that replaces the HTTP in the URL with HTTPS.
o.C: Create a listener rule on the ALB to redirect HTTP traffic to HTTPS.
o.D: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer configured to use Server Name Indication (SNI).

e.why: ALB listeners support redirect actions, so a rule on the HTTP:80 listener can return an HTTP 301 redirect to HTTPS:443. This forwards all requests to HTTPS natively without application changes.

others.A: Network ACLs apply to subnets, not to the ALB itself, and blocking HTTP would drop requests rather than redirect them.
others.B: ALB rules do not rewrite URL text; the correct mechanism is a redirect action.
others.D: An NLB does not perform HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects, and SNI is unrelated to redirection.

e.tip: HTTP to HTTPS redirect: ALB listener rule with redirect action (or CloudFront viewer protocol policy).

q:
A company is developing a two-tier web application on AWS. The company's developers have deployed the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that connects directly to a backend Amazon RDS database. The company must not hardcode database credentials in the application. The company must also implement a solution to automatically rotate the database credentials on a regular basis.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Store the database credentials in the instance metadata. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and instance metadata at the same time.
o.B: Store the database credentials in a configuration file in an encrypted Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and the credentials in the configuration file at the same time. Use S3 Versioning to ensure the ability to fall back to previous values.
o.C: Store the database credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation for the secret. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the secret.
o.D: Store the database credentials as encrypted parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on automatic rotation for the encrypted parameters. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the encrypted parameters.

e.why: AWS Secrets Manager stores the database credentials as a secret with built-in automatic rotation for Amazon RDS. Granting the EC2 instance role permission to read the secret lets the application retrieve current credentials at runtime without hardcoding, with the least operational overhead.

others.A: Instance metadata cannot store custom credentials, and custom Lambda rotation adds overhead.
others.B: Managing credentials in an S3 config file with custom Lambda rotation is operationally heavy.
others.D: Parameter Store SecureString parameters do not support native automatic rotation.

e.tip: Automatic database credential rotation: Secrets Manager.

q:
A company is deploying a new public web application to AWS. The application will run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application needs to be encrypted at the edge with an SSL/TLS certificate that is issued by an external certificate authority (CA). The certificate must be rotated each year before the certificate expires.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue an SSL/TLS certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.
o.B: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue an SSL/TLS certificate. Import the key material from the certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.
o.C: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Private Certificate Authority to issue an SSL/TLS certificate from the root CA. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.
o.D: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to import an SSL/TLS certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to send a notification when the certificate is nearing expiration. Rotate the certificate manually.

fixed: All four options were garbled by text splitting and have been reconstructed.

e.why: The certificate must come from an external CA, so it has to be imported into ACM and applied to the ALB. ACM does not auto-renew imported certificates, but it emits expiration events, so an EventBridge rule can notify the team to rotate the certificate manually each year.

others.A: A certificate issued by ACM comes from Amazon's CA, not the required external CA.
others.B: ACM-issued certificates come from Amazon's CA, and you cannot export or import their key material this way.
others.C: ACM Private CA issues private certificates that public browsers do not trust, and it is not the required external CA.

e.tip: External-CA certificate = import into ACM; imported certificates need manual renewal, so alert on expiry.

q:
A company runs its infrastructure on AWS and has a registered base of 700,000 users for its document management application. The company intends to create a product that converts large .pdf files to .jpg image files. The .pdf files average 5 MB in size. The company needs to store the original files and the converted files. A solutions architect must design a scalable solution to accommodate demand that will grow rapidly over time.
Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Save the .pdf files to Amazon S3. Configure an S3 PUT event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to convert the files to .jpg format and store them back in Amazon S3.
o.B: Save the .pdf files to Amazon DynamoDB. Use the DynamoDB Streams feature to invoke an AWS Lambda function to convert the files to .jpg format and store them back in DynamoDB.
o.C: Upload the .pdf files to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application that includes Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage, and an Auto Scaling group. Use a program in the EC2 instances to convert the files to .jpg format. Save the .pdf files and the .jpg files in the EBS store.
o.D: Upload the .pdf files to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application that includes Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) storage, and an Auto Scaling group. Use a program in the EC2 instances to convert the file to .jpg format. Save the .pdf files and the .jpg files in the EBS store.

fixed: Option B text was missing and has been reconstructed.

e.why: Storing the .pdf files in S3 and using an S3 PUT event notification to invoke a Lambda function that converts each file and writes the .jpg back to S3 is fully serverless. S3 scales storage automatically and Lambda scales with demand and charges only per use, making this the most cost-effective scalable design.

others.B: DynamoDB items are limited to 400 KB, so 5 MB files cannot be stored there, and it is costly for blob storage.
others.C: EC2 instances and EBS storage must be provisioned and managed, which costs more, and EBS is not shared across instances.
others.D: EC2 fleets cost more than serverless processing, and the option inconsistently stores files in EBS.

e.tip: Event-driven file processing at scale = S3 event notification plus Lambda.

q:
A company has more than 5 TB of file data on Windows file servers that run on premises. Users and applications interact with the data each day.
The company is moving its Windows workloads to AWS. As the company continues this process, the company requires access to AWS and on-premises file storage with minimum latency. The company needs a solution that minimizes operational overhead and requires no significant changes to the existing file access patterns. The company uses an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection for connectivity to AWS.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy and configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Move the on-premises file data to FSx for Windows File Server. Reconfigure the workloads to use FSx for Windows File Server on AWS.
o.B: Deploy and configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to the S3 File Gateway. Reconfigure the on-premises workloads and the cloud workloads to use the S3 File Gateway.
o.C: Deploy and configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to Amazon S3. Reconfigure the workloads to use either Amazon S3 directly or the S3 File Gateway. depending on each workload's location.
o.D: Deploy and configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Deploy and configure an Amazon FSx File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to the FSx File Gateway. Configure the cloud workloads to use FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Configure the on-premises workloads to use the FSx File Gateway.

e.why: FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed SMB file shares in AWS for cloud workloads. Amazon FSx File Gateway deployed on premises provides low-latency local caching of the FSx file shares for on-premises users, preserving existing Windows file access patterns over the VPN with minimal overhead.

others.A: Moving everything to FSx without a local cache forces on-premises users to access files over the VPN, increasing latency.
others.B: S3 File Gateway stores files as S3 objects, and cloud workloads would not access the gateway efficiently, changing access patterns.
others.C: Having workloads use S3 directly changes file access patterns from SMB to object APIs.

e.tip: Hybrid low-latency access to FSx for Windows: FSx File Gateway on premises.

q:
A hospital recently deployed a RESTful API with Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The hospital uses API Gateway and Lambda to upload reports that are in PDF format and JPEG format. The hospital needs to modify the Lambda code to identify protected health information (PHI) in the reports.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use existing Python libraries to extract the text from the reports and to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
o.B: Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon SageMaker to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
o.C: Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
o.D: Use Amazon Rekognition to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.

e.why: Amazon Textract extracts printed and handwritten text from PDF and JPEG documents with a managed API. Amazon Comprehend Medical is a HIPAA-eligible service that detects PHI in text, so combining them in the Lambda code requires no model building and has the least operational overhead.

others.A: Using and maintaining custom Python libraries to detect PHI requires more development and is less accurate.
others.B: Building a PHI detection model in SageMaker adds significant operational and development overhead.
others.D: Rekognition text detection is for short text in images and is not designed for document text extraction like Textract.

e.tip: Documents to text: Textract; PHI or medical entities in text: Comprehend Medical.

q:
A company has an application that generates a large number of files, each approximately 5 MB in size. The files are stored in Amazon S3. Company policy requires the files to be stored for 4 years before they can be deleted. Immediate accessibility is always required as the files contain critical business data that is not easy to reproduce. The files are frequently accessed in the first 30 days of the object creation but are rarely accessed after the first 30 days.
Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?

o.A: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
o.B: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
o.C: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
o.D: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Move the files to S3 Glacier 4 years after object creation.

e.why: S3 Standard-IA provides millisecond access and the same durability as S3 Standard at a lower storage price for rarely accessed data, fitting the always-immediate-access requirement after 30 days. A Lifecycle rule transitions files after 30 days and expires them after 4 years, as policy allows deletion then.

others.A: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval does not provide immediate access; retrieval takes minutes to hours.
others.B: One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, risking loss of critical data that is hard to reproduce.
others.D: Moving files to Glacier after 4 years keeps paying for storage when the files can simply be deleted.

e.tip: Infrequent but immediate access with high durability: Standard-IA (or Glacier Instant Retrieval).

q:
A company hosts an application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes messages from an Amazon SQS queue, writes to an Amazon RDS table, and deletes the message from the queue. Occasional duplicate records are found in the RDS table. The SQS queue does not contain any duplicate messages.
What should a solutions architect do to ensure messages are being processed once only?

o.A: Use the CreateQueue API call to create a new queue.
o.B: Use the AddPermission API call to add appropriate permissions.
o.C: Use the ReceiveMessage API call to set an appropriate wait time.
o.D: Use the ChangeMessageVisibility API call to increase the visibility timeout.

e.why: If processing takes longer than the queue's visibility timeout, the message becomes visible again and another instance receives and processes it, causing duplicate RDS records. Increasing the visibility timeout with ChangeMessageVisibility (or on the queue) ensures the message stays hidden until it is processed and deleted.

others.A: Creating a new queue does not change how long messages stay hidden during processing.
others.B: Permissions do not affect duplicate processing.
others.C: The ReceiveMessage wait time controls long polling, not message visibility during processing.

e.tip: Duplicate processing from SQS: visibility timeout shorter than processing time.

q:
A solutions architect is designing a new hybrid architecture to extend a company's on-premises infrastructure to AWS. The company requires a highly available connection with consistent low latency to an AWS Region. The company needs to minimize costs and is willing to accept slower traffic if the primary connection fails.
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a VPN connection as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
o.B: Provision a VPN tunnel connection to a Region for private connectivity. Provision a second VPN tunnel for private connectivity and as a backup if the primary VPN connection fails.
o.C: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a second Direct Connect connection to the same Region as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
o.D: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Use the Direct Connect failover attribute from the AWS CLI to automatically create a backup connection if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.

e.why: AWS Direct Connect provides a private connection with consistent low latency to the Region. A Site-to-Site VPN over the internet as a backup is inexpensive and provides failover with slower, less consistent performance, which the company accepts, minimizing cost.

others.B: VPN tunnels over the internet do not provide consistent low latency for the primary connection.
others.C: A second Direct Connect connection gives better resiliency but costs significantly more than a VPN backup.
others.D: There is no Direct Connect failover attribute that automatically creates a backup connection.

e.tip: Cost-effective Direct Connect backup when slower failover is acceptable: Site-to-Site VPN.

q:
A company is running a business-critical web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The application uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database that is deployed in a single Availability Zone. The company wants the application to be highly available with minimum downtime and minimum loss of data.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

o.A: Place the EC2 instances in different AWS Regions. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks to redirect traffic. Use Aurora PostgreSQL Cross-Region Replication.
o.B: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple Availability Zones. Configure the database as Multi-AZ. Configure an Amazon RDS Proxy instance for the database.
o.C: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use one Availability Zone. Generate hourly snapshots of the database. Recover the database from the snapshots in the event of a failure.
o.D: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple AWS Regions. Write the data from the application to Amazon S3. Use S3 Event Notifications to launch an AWS Lambda function to write the data to the database.

e.why: Spreading the Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs and making the Aurora database Multi-AZ (with an Aurora Replica in another AZ) provides automatic failover with minimal downtime and data loss. RDS Proxy pools connections and further reduces failover times, all with little operational effort.

others.A: A multi-Region design with cross-Region replication adds significant complexity and is beyond what high availability requires.
others.C: A single AZ is not highly available, and hourly snapshots risk up to an hour of data loss.
others.D: Writing through S3 and Lambda across Regions is complex and does not make the database highly available.

e.tip: HA within a Region: Multi-AZ for compute and database.

q:
A company's HTTP application is behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The NLB's target group is configured to use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with multiple EC2 instances that run the web service.
The company notices that the NLB is not detecting HTTP errors for the application. These errors require a manual restart of the EC2 instances that run the web service. The company needs to improve the application's availability without writing custom scripts or code.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Enable HTTP health checks on the NLB, supplying the URL of the company's application.
o.B: Add a cron job to the EC2 instances to check the local application's logs once each minute. If HTTP errors are detected, the application will restart.
o.C: Replace the NLB with an Application Load Balancer. Enable HTTP health checks by supplying the URL of the company's application. Configure an Auto Scaling action to replace unhealthy instances.
o.D: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors the UnhealthyHostCount metric for the NLB. Configure an Auto Scaling action to replace unhealthy instances when the alarm is in the ALARM state.

fixed: Options B and D were garbled (D truncated, B replaced by D's tail) and have been reconstructed.

e.why: An Application Load Balancer is built for HTTP applications, and its HTTP health checks against the application URL detect HTTP errors. With the Auto Scaling group using ELB health checks, unhealthy instances are replaced automatically, without custom scripts or code.

others.A: The NLB in this scenario is not detecting the application's HTTP errors, and health checks alone do not replace instances.
others.B: A cron job that parses logs and restarts the app is a custom script, which the requirement forbids.
others.D: The NLB's UnhealthyHostCount does not reflect the HTTP errors it fails to detect, and the alarm cannot identify which instances to replace.

e.tip: Replace instances on application-level errors = ALB HTTP health checks plus ELB health checks in the Auto Scaling group.

q:
A company runs a shopping application that uses Amazon DynamoDB to store customer information. In case of data corruption, a solutions architect needs to design a solution that meets a recovery point objective (RPO) of 15 minutes and a recovery time objective (RTO) of 1 hour.
What should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure DynamoDB global tables. For RPO recovery, point the application to a different AWS Region.
o.B: Configure DynamoDB point-in-time recovery. For RPO recovery, restore to the desired point in time.
o.C: Export the DynamoDB data to Amazon S3 Glacier on a daily basis. For RPO recovery, import the data from S3 Glacier to DynamoDB.
o.D: Schedule Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots for the DynamoDB table every 15 minutes. For RPO recovery, restore the DynamoDB table by using the EBS snapshot.

fixed: Option B text was missing and option C was truncated; both have been reconstructed.

e.why: DynamoDB point-in-time recovery continuously backs up the table and can restore to any second within the last 35 days. That easily meets a 15-minute RPO after data corruption, and restoring to a new table typically completes within the 1-hour RTO.

others.A: Global tables replicate corruption to every Region almost immediately, so they do not protect against bad data.
others.C: Daily exports give an RPO of up to 24 hours, and Glacier retrieval plus import would exceed the 1-hour RTO.
others.D: DynamoDB is a managed service that does not use EBS volumes, so EBS snapshots cannot back it up.

e.tip: Protection from data corruption in DynamoDB with minutes of RPO = point-in-time recovery.

q:
A company runs a photo processing application that needs to frequently upload and download pictures from Amazon S3 buckets that are located in the same AWS Region. A solutions architect has noticed an increased cost in data transfer fees and needs to implement a solution to reduce these costs.
How can the solutions architect meet this requirement?

o.A: Deploy Amazon API Gateway into a public subnet and adjust the route table to route S3 calls through it.
o.B: Deploy a NAT gateway into a public subnet and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.
o.C: Deploy the application into a public subnet and allow it to route through an internet gateway to access the S3 buckets.
o.D: Deploy an S3 VPC gateway endpoint into the VPC and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.

e.why: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint routes traffic from the VPC to S3 in the same Region over the AWS network without NAT gateway processing charges, and gateway endpoints are free. An endpoint policy can restrict access to the specific buckets, reducing data transfer costs.

others.A: API Gateway is not a routing target for S3 traffic and would add per-request charges.
others.B: NAT gateways charge per GB processed, which is the source of the increased cost, and endpoint policies do not apply to NAT gateways.
others.C: Moving the application to a public subnet reduces security and still does not offer the cost and privacy benefits of an endpoint.

e.tip: Same-Region S3 traffic cost via NAT: use a gateway endpoint.

q:
A company recently launched Linux-based application instances on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet and launched a Linux-based bastion host on an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet of a VPC. A solutions architect needs to connect from the on-premises network, through the company's internet connection, to the bastion host, and to the application servers. The solutions architect must make sure that the security groups of all the EC2 instances will allow that access.
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the application instances.
o.B: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the internal IP range for the company.
o.C: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the external IP range for the company.
o.D: Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the private IP address of the bastion host.
o.E: Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the public IP address of the bastion host.

e.why: The bastion host is reached from on premises over the internet, so its security group should allow SSH only from the company's external (public) IP range. The application instances in the private subnet should allow SSH only from the bastion host's private IP address, because traffic within the VPC uses private addresses.

others.A: Allowing inbound access only from the application instances would block administrators connecting from on premises.
others.B: Traffic from on premises over the internet arrives from the company's public IP addresses, not internal ranges.
others.E: Traffic from the bastion to private instances within the VPC uses the bastion's private IP, not its public IP.

e.tip: Bastion SG: allow company public IPs; private instances SG: allow bastion private IP or its SG.

q:
A solutions architect is designing a two-tier web application. The application consists of a public-facing web tier hosted on Amazon EC2 in public subnets. The database tier consists of Microsoft SQL Server running on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet. Security is a high priority for the company.
How should security groups be configured in this situation? (Choose two.)

o.A: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
o.B: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow outbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
o.C: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on port 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
o.D: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow outbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 to the security group for the web tier.
o.E: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 from the security group for the web tier.

e.why: The public web tier must accept HTTPS from anywhere, so its security group allows inbound port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. The database tier should allow inbound SQL Server traffic on port 1433 only from the web tier's security group, following least privilege.

others.B: Security groups allow all outbound traffic by default, and outbound rules do not have a source.
others.D: Security groups are stateful, so return traffic is allowed automatically; outbound rules to the web tier are unnecessary.
others.E: Opening port 443 on the database tier is unnecessary and violates least privilege.

e.tip: Security groups are stateful; define inbound rules and reference source security groups.

q:
A company wants to move a multi-tiered application from on premises to the AWS Cloud to improve the application's performance. The application consists of application tiers that communicate with each other by way of RESTful services. Transactions are dropped when one tier becomes overloaded. A solutions architect must design a solution that resolves these issues and modernizes the application.
Which solution meets these requirements and is the MOST operationally efficient?

o.A: Use Amazon API Gateway and direct transactions to the AWS Lambda functions as the application layer. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) as the communication layer between application services.
o.B: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to analyze the application performance history to determine the servers' peak utilization during the performance failures. Increase the size of the application server's Amazon EC2 instances to meet the peak requirements.
o.C: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to handle the messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SNS queue length and scale up and down as required.
o.D: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to handle the messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SQS queue length and scale up when communication failures are detected.

e.why: API Gateway with Lambda functions provides an automatically scaling serverless application layer, and SQS queues between services buffer requests so transactions are not dropped when a tier is overloaded. This modernizes the application with the most operational efficiency.

others.B: Vertically scaling EC2 instances does not decouple tiers or prevent drops during unexpected spikes, and keeps server management.
others.C: SNS does not have a queue length to monitor and does not buffer messages for later processing.
others.D: SQS with EC2 Auto Scaling works but still requires managing servers, and scaling only after failures is reactive.

e.tip: Modernize and decouple with least ops: API Gateway, Lambda, SQS.

q:
A company receives 10 TB of instrumentation data each day from several machines located at a single factory. The data consists of JSON files stored on a storage area network (SAN) in an on-premises data center located within the factory. The company wants to send this data to Amazon S3 where it can be accessed by several additional systems that provide critical near-real-time analytics. A secure transfer is important because the data is considered sensitive.
Which solution offers the MOST reliable data transfer?

o.A: AWS DataSync over public internet
o.B: AWS DataSync over AWS Direct Connect
o.C: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) over public internet
o.D: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) over AWS Direct Connect

e.why: AWS DataSync transfers file data from on-premises storage to S3 with encryption in transit, integrity validation and automatic retries. Running it over AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private connection with consistent bandwidth for the daily 10 TB, making this the most reliable and secure transfer.

others.A: DataSync over the public internet is secure but less reliable and consistent than a dedicated connection.
others.C: DMS is for database migration, not for transferring JSON files from a SAN.
others.D: DMS is not designed for file transfers, regardless of the network used.

e.tip: Recurring file transfer to S3: DataSync; reliability and consistency: Direct Connect.

q:
A company needs to configure a real-time data ingestion architecture for its application. The company needs an API, a process that transforms data as the data is streamed, and a storage solution for the data.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance to host an API that sends data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that uses the Kinesis data stream as a data source. Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to send the data to Amazon S3.
o.B: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance to host an API that sends data to AWS Glue. Stop source/destination checking on the EC2 instance. Use AWS Glue to transform the data and to send the data to Amazon S3.
o.C: Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to send data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that uses the Kinesis data stream as a data source. Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to send the data to Amazon S3.
o.D: Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to send data to AWS Glue. Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use AWS Glue to send the data to Amazon S3.

e.why: API Gateway provides a fully managed API that can send records directly to a Kinesis data stream. Kinesis Data Firehose reads from the stream, transforms records in flight using Lambda, and delivers them to S3, so every component is managed and the design has the least operational overhead.

others.A: Hosting the API on an EC2 instance adds server management overhead.
others.B: An EC2 instance adds overhead, Glue is not a streaming ingestion endpoint for an API, and source/destination checks are irrelevant.
others.D: AWS Glue is not a direct API Gateway integration target for real-time streaming ingestion.

e.tip: Managed real-time pipeline: API Gateway to Kinesis Data Streams to Firehose (Lambda transform) to S3.

q:
A company needs to keep user transaction data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company must retain the data for 7 years.
What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

o.A: Use DynamoDB point-in-time recovery to back up the table continuously.
o.B: Use AWS Backup to create backup schedules and retention policies for the table.
o.C: Create an on-demand backup of the table by using the DynamoDB console. Store the backup in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set an S3 Lifecycle configuration for the S3 bucket.
o.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to back up the table and to store the backup in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set an S3 Lifecycle configuration for the S3 bucket.

e.why: AWS Backup supports DynamoDB with centrally managed backup plans that define schedules, retention periods of years, and lifecycle transitions to cold storage. Setting a 7-year retention policy automates long-term backups with no custom code, making it the most operationally efficient.

others.A: Point-in-time recovery only retains continuous backups for up to 35 days.
others.C: Manual on-demand backups from the console do not scale operationally, and DynamoDB backups are not directly stored in your own S3 bucket.
others.D: A custom Lambda backup process requires writing and maintaining code.

e.tip: Long-term scheduled backups with retention: AWS Backup.

q:
A company is planning to use an Amazon DynamoDB table for data storage. The company is concerned about cost optimization. The table will not be used on most mornings. In the evenings, the read and write traffic will often be unpredictable. When traffic spikes occur, they will happen very quickly.
What should a solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Create a DynamoDB table in on-demand capacity mode.
o.B: Create a DynamoDB table with a global secondary index.
o.C: Create a DynamoDB table with provisioned capacity and auto scaling.
o.D: Create a DynamoDB table in provisioned capacity mode, and configure it as a global table.

e.why: DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode charges per request and instantly accommodates sudden, unpredictable traffic spikes without capacity planning. When the table is idle in the mornings, you pay nothing for throughput, making it cost-optimized for this pattern.

others.B: A global secondary index adds query flexibility, not cost optimization or spike handling.
others.C: Provisioned capacity with auto scaling reacts over minutes and may throttle on very fast spikes, and you pay for minimum provisioned capacity while idle.
others.D: Global tables replicate across Regions, increasing cost without addressing unpredictable traffic.

e.tip: Unpredictable or spiky DynamoDB traffic: on-demand mode.

q:
A company recently signed a contract with an AWS Managed Service Provider (MSP) Partner for help with an application migration initiative. A solutions architect needs ta share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from an existing AWS account with the MSP Partner's AWS account. The AMI is backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) and uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt EBS volume snapshots.
What is the MOST secure way for the solutions architect to share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account?

o.A: Make the encrypted AMI and snapshots publicly available. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.
o.B: Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.
o.C: Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to trust a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner for encryption.
o.D: Export the AMI from the source account to an Amazon S3 bucket in the MSP Partner's AWS account, Encrypt the S3 bucket with a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner. Copy and launch the AMI in the MSP Partner's AWS account.

e.why: Modifying the AMI's launchPermission to share it with only the MSP Partner's account limits exposure to that account. Because the snapshots are encrypted with a customer managed KMS key, the key policy must also allow the partner account to use the key, making this the most secure sharing method.

others.A: Making the AMI and snapshots public exposes them to everyone and is not secure; encrypted AMIs cannot be shared publicly anyway.
others.C: The partner needs permissions on the source key to use the encrypted snapshots; a key policy cannot trust another KMS key.
others.D: Exporting the AMI to S3 adds unnecessary steps and is not the standard secure sharing method.

e.tip: Share encrypted AMI: share with the account and grant access to the customer managed KMS key.

q:
A solutions architect is designing the cloud architecture for a new application being deployed on AWS. The process should run in parallel while adding and removing application nodes as needed based on the number of jobs to be processed. The processor application is stateless. The solutions architect must ensure that the application is loosely coupled and the job items are durably stored.
Which design should the solutions architect use?

o.A: Create an Amazon SNS topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch configuration that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch configuration. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on CPU usage.
o.B: Create an Amazon SQS queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch configuration that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch configuration. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on network usage.
o.C: Create an Amazon SQS queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch template that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch template. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on the number of items in the SQS queue.
o.D: Create an Amazon SNS topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch template that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch template. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on the number of messages published to the SNS topic.

e.why: An SQS queue durably stores job items and decouples producers from processors. An Auto Scaling group using a launch template scales stateless processor instances based on the number of messages in the queue, directly matching nodes to the number of jobs.

others.A: SNS does not durably store jobs for workers to pull, and CPU usage does not reflect job backlog.
others.B: Network usage is not a good proxy for job count, and launch configurations are deprecated in favor of launch templates.
others.D: SNS pushes messages and does not hold a backlog, so scaling on published messages does not reflect pending work.

e.tip: Scale workers on queue depth (backlog per instance).

q:
A company hosts its web applications in the AWS Cloud. The company configures Elastic Load Balancers to use certificates that are imported into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). The company's security team must be notified 30 days before the expiration of each certificate.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

o.A: Add a rule in ACM to publish a custom message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic every day, beginning 30 days before any certificate will expire.
o.B: Create an AWS Config rule that checks for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to invoke a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) when AWS Config reports a noncompliant resource.
o.C: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to check for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on Trusted Advisor metrics for check status changes. Configure the alarm to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
o.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to detect any certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

e.why: ACM emits daily 'ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration' events to EventBridge starting before expiration (the threshold is configurable). An EventBridge rule can match these events, filter for 30 days, and invoke a Lambda function that sends a custom alert through SNS.

others.A: ACM has no feature to add custom rules that publish messages on a schedule.
others.B: An AWS Config rule (acm-certificate-expiration-check) is also viable, but the option requires additional custom alert wiring and is not the keyed approach.
others.C: Trusted Advisor checks for expiring certificates are not designed for a precise 30-day custom alert workflow via CloudWatch metrics.

e.tip: ACM expiration events go to EventBridge; imported certificates are not auto-renewed.

q:
A company's dynamic website is hosted using on-premises servers in the United States. The company is launching its product in Europe, and it wants to optimize site loading times for new European users. The site's backend must remain in the United States. The product is being launched in a few days, and an immediate solution is needed.
What should the solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in us-east-1 and migrate the site to it.
o.B: Move the website to Amazon S3. Use Cross-Region Replication between Regions.
o.C: Use Amazon CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to the on-premises servers.
o.D: Use an Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing policy pointing to on-premises servers.

e.why: Amazon CloudFront can use a custom origin, including on-premises servers, and serves content through edge locations in Europe, caching static assets and accelerating dynamic requests over the AWS backbone. It can be set up within days while the backend stays in the United States.

others.A: Migrating to an EC2 instance in us-east-1 does not reduce latency for European users and takes time.
others.B: A dynamic website cannot be hosted on S3, and the backend must remain in the United States.
others.D: Geoproximity routing to the same on-premises servers does not reduce latency for European users.

e.tip: Speed up global access to an existing origin quickly: CloudFront with custom origin.

q:
A company wants to reduce the cost of its existing three-tier web architecture. The web, application, and database servers are running on Amazon EC2 instances for the development, test, and production environments. The EC2 instances average 30% CPU utilization during peak hours and 10% CPU utilization during non-peak hours.
The production EC2 instances run 24 hours a day. The development and test EC2 instances run for at least 8 hours each day. The company plans to implement automation to stop the development and test EC2 instances when they are not in use.
Which EC2 instance purchasing solution will meet the company's requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use Spot Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
o.B: Use Reserved Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
o.C: Use Spot blocks for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
o.D: Use On-Demand Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Spot blocks for the development and test EC2 instances.

e.why: Production instances run 24/7 with steady usage, so Reserved Instances (or Savings Plans) give the largest discount. Development and test instances run only part of each day and will be stopped by automation, so On-Demand pricing avoids paying for unused reserved hours.

others.A: Spot Instances can be interrupted, which is unacceptable for production, and RIs for part-time instances waste money.
others.C: Spot blocks are no longer offered and are unsuitable for 24/7 production; RIs for part-time instances are wasteful.
others.D: On-Demand for 24/7 production is more expensive than RIs, and Spot blocks are discontinued.

e.tip: Steady 24/7: Reserved Instances or Savings Plans; intermittent: On-Demand; interruptible: Spot.

q:
A company has a production web application in which users upload documents through a web interface or a mobile app. According to a new regulatory requirement. new documents cannot be modified or deleted after they are stored.
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.A: Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock enabled.
o.B: Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to archive the documents periodically.
o.C: Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Configure an ACL to restrict all access to read-only.
o.D: Store the uploaded documents on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Access the data by mounting the volume in read-only mode.

e.why: S3 Object Lock provides write-once-read-many (WORM) protection so object versions cannot be overwritten or deleted during the retention period, and it requires S3 Versioning to be enabled. This directly meets the regulatory requirement that stored documents cannot be modified or deleted.

others.B: Lifecycle archiving does not prevent modification or deletion.
others.C: ACLs can be changed by privileged users and read-only access would also block uploads.
others.D: Mounting EFS read-only on clients does not prevent deletion by other clients and is not a compliance control.

e.tip: WORM compliance in S3: Object Lock (requires Versioning).

q:
A company has several web servers that need to frequently access a common Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. The company wants a secure method for the web servers to connect to the database while meeting a security requirement to rotate user credentials frequently.
Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Store the database user credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to access AWS Secrets Manager.
o.B: Store the database user credentials in AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to access OpsCenter.
o.C: Store the database user credentials in a secure Amazon S3 bucket. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to retrieve credentials and access the database.
o.D: Store the database user credentials in files encrypted with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) on the web server file system. The web server should be able to decrypt the files and access the database.

e.why: AWS Secrets Manager stores database credentials securely and can rotate them automatically on a schedule for Amazon RDS MySQL. Web servers with IAM permissions retrieve current credentials at runtime, meeting the frequent rotation requirement securely.

others.B: Systems Manager OpsCenter is for managing operational issues (OpsItems), not storing credentials.
others.C: Storing credentials in S3 offers no automatic rotation.
others.D: KMS-encrypted local files require manual distribution and rotation across web servers.

e.tip: Frequent credential rotation: Secrets Manager.

q:
A company hosts an application on AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by an Amazon API Gateway API. The Lambda functions save customer data to an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Whenever the company upgrades the database, the Lambda functions fail to establish database connections until the upgrade is complete. The result is that customer data is not recorded for some of the event.
A solutions architect needs to design a solution that stores customer data that is created during database upgrades.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Provision an Amazon RDS proxy to sit between the Lambda functions and the database. Configure the Lambda functions to connect to the RDS proxy.
o.B: Increase the run time of the Lambda functions to the maximum. Create a retry mechanism in the code that stores the customer data in the database.
o.C: Persist the customer data to Lambda local storage. Configure new Lambda functions to scan the local storage to save the customer data to the database.
