o.D: Store the customer data in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Create a new Lambda function that polls the queue and stores the customer data in the database.

e.why: Writing customer data to an SQS FIFO queue durably stores it even while the database is unavailable during upgrades. A separate Lambda function polls the queue and writes the data to Aurora once the database is available, with failed messages retried, so no data is lost.

others.A: RDS Proxy pools connections and speeds failover but cannot accept writes while the database is down for an upgrade.
others.B: Lambda functions time out after at most 15 minutes, and in-code retries may still lose data during longer upgrades.
others.C: Lambda local storage (/tmp) is ephemeral and not shared across invocations or functions.

e.tip: Database temporarily unavailable: buffer writes in SQS.

q:
A survey company has gathered data for several years from areas in the United States. The company hosts the data in an Amazon S3 bucket that is 3 TB in size and growing. The company has started to share the data with a European marketing firm that has S3 buckets. The company wants to ensure that its data transfer costs remain as low as possible.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure the Requester Pays feature on the company's S3 bucket.
o.B: Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication from the company's S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm's S3 buckets.
o.C: Configure cross-account access for the marketing firm so that the marketing firm has access to the company's S3 bucket.
o.D: Configure the company's S3 bucket to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Sync the S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm's S3 buckets.

e.why: With S3 Requester Pays enabled, the requester (the marketing firm) pays the request and data transfer costs for downloading data from the bucket. The company pays only for storage, keeping its data transfer costs as low as possible.

others.B: Cross-Region Replication incurs inter-Region data transfer charges that the company pays.
others.C: Cross-account access alone still leaves the bucket owner paying for data transfer out.
others.D: Intelligent-Tiering optimizes storage cost, and syncing to another bucket still incurs transfer costs for the company.

e.tip: Shift download costs to consumers: S3 Requester Pays.

q:
A company uses Amazon S3 to store its confidential audit documents. The S3 bucket uses bucket policies to restrict access to audit team IAM user credentials according to the principle of least privilege. Company managers are worried about accidental deletion of documents in the S3 bucket and want a more secure solution.
What should a solutions architect do to secure the audit documents?

o.A: Enable the versioning and MFA Delete features on the S3 bucket.
o.B: Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the IAM user credentials for each audit team IAM user account.
o.C: Add an S3 Lifecycle policy to the audit team's IAM user accounts to deny the s3:DeleteObject action during audit dates.
o.D: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the S3 bucket and restrict audit team IAM user accounts from accessing the KMS key.

e.why: S3 Versioning preserves every object version so deleted documents can be recovered, and MFA Delete requires an MFA code from the bucket owner (root) to permanently delete versions or disable versioning. Together they protect the audit documents against accidental deletion.

others.B: MFA on sign-in protects credentials but does not stop an authenticated user from accidentally deleting objects.
others.C: Lifecycle policies apply to buckets, not IAM users, and cannot deny API actions.
others.D: Restricting KMS key access would block the audit team from reading documents and does not prevent deletion.

e.tip: Accidental deletion protection: Versioning plus MFA Delete.

q:
A company is using a SQL database to store movie data that is publicly accessible. The database runs on an Amazon RDS Single-AZ DB instance. A script runs queries at random intervals each day to record the number of new movies that have been added to the database. The script must report a final total during business hours.
The company's development team notices that the database performance is inadequate for development tasks when the script is running. A solutions architect must recommend a solution to resolve this issue.
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ deployment.
o.B: Create a read replica of the database. Configure the script to query only the read replica.
o.C: Instruct the development team to manually export the entries in the database at the end of each day.
o.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache to cache the common queries that the script runs against the database.

e.why: An RDS read replica offloads the script's read-only queries from the primary DB instance, so the development team's workload is no longer impacted. Creating a replica and pointing the script at its endpoint is quick with the least operational overhead.

others.A: The Multi-AZ standby (in the classic instance deployment) cannot serve reads, so it does not offload the script.
others.C: Manual daily exports add operational effort and do not provide reports during business hours.
others.D: ElastiCache requires application changes and cache management, and random counting queries may not benefit from caching.

e.tip: Offload read-heavy reporting from the primary: read replica.

q:
A company has applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. One of the applications needs to call the Amazon S3 API to store and read objects. According to the company's security regulations, no traffic from the applications is allowed to travel across the internet.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure an S3 gateway endpoint.
o.B: Create an S3 bucket in a private subnet.
o.C: Create an S3 bucket in the same AWS Region as the EC2 instances.
o.D: Configure a NAT gateway in the same subnet as the EC2 instances.

e.why: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint lets EC2 instances reach the S3 API through the AWS private network via a route table entry, so no traffic traverses the internet. It requires no NAT or internet gateway and is free.

others.B: S3 buckets are Regional services and cannot be placed in a subnet.
others.C: Placing the bucket in the same Region does not by itself keep traffic off the internet path.
others.D: A NAT gateway sends traffic to S3 public endpoints via the internet gateway, and it must be in a public subnet.

e.tip: No internet path to S3: gateway endpoint.

q:
A company is storing sensitive user information in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to provide secure access to this bucket from the application tier running on Amazon EC2 instances inside a VPC.
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to accomplish this? (Choose two.)

o.A: Configure a VPC gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 within the VPC.
o.C: Create a bucket policy that limits access to only the application tier running in the VPC.
o.B: Create a bucket policy to make the objects in the S3 bucket public.
o.D: Create an IAM user with an S3 access policy and copy the IAM credentials to the EC2 instance.
o.E: Create a NAT instance and have the EC2 instances use the NAT instance to access the S3 bucket.

fixed: Option A was truncated and option C text was missing; both have been reconstructed.

e.why: A VPC gateway endpoint for S3 keeps traffic between the EC2 application tier and the bucket on the AWS network. A bucket policy that only allows access from the application tier (for example via aws:SourceVpce or the application's IAM role) ensures nothing else can read the sensitive data.

others.B: Making the objects public exposes sensitive data to everyone.
others.D: Copying long-term IAM user credentials onto instances is insecure; use an instance role instead.
others.E: A NAT instance sends traffic over the internet path and adds management overhead without restricting bucket access.

e.tip: Private S3 access from a VPC = gateway endpoint plus a bucket policy scoped to that endpoint or role.

q:
A company runs an on-premises application that is powered by a MySQL database. The company is migrating the application to AWS to increase the application's elasticity and availability.
The current architecture shows heavy read activity on the database during times of normal operation. Every 4 hours, the company's development team pulls a full export of the production database to populate a database in the staging environment. During this period, users experience unacceptable application latency. The development team is unable to use the staging environment until the procedure completes.
A solutions architect must recommend replacement architecture that alleviates the application latency issue. The replacement architecture also must give the development team the ability to continue using the staging environment without delay.
Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas for production. Populate the staging database by implementing a backup and restore process that uses the mysqldump utility.
o.B: Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas for production. Use database cloning to create the staging database on-demand.
o.C: Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ deployment and read replicas for production. Use the standby instance for the staging database.
o.D: Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ deployment and read replicas for production. Populate the staging database by implementing a backup and restore process that uses the mysqldump utility.

e.why: Aurora MySQL with Aurora Replicas across AZs offloads heavy read activity and provides high availability. Aurora database cloning uses a copy-on-write protocol to create a staging copy in minutes without a full export, so production latency is unaffected and developers can use staging immediately.

others.A: mysqldump full exports still load the production database and take time, delaying staging.
others.C: The RDS Multi-AZ standby cannot be accessed or used as a staging database.
others.D: mysqldump backup and restore still causes latency and delays for staging.

e.tip: Fast copy of an Aurora database for test or staging: Aurora cloning.

q:
A company is designing an application where users upload small files into Amazon S3. After a user uploads a file, the file requires one-time simple processing to transform the data and save the data in JSON format for later analysis.
Each file must be processed as quickly as possible after it is uploaded. Demand will vary. On some days, users will upload a high number of files. On other days, users will upload a few files or no files.
Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Configure Amazon EMR to read text files from Amazon S3. Run processing scripts to transform the data. Store the resulting JSON file in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.
o.B: Configure Amazon S3 to send an event notification to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use Amazon EC2 instances to read from the queue and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in Amazon DynamoDB.
o.C: Configure Amazon S3 to send an event notification to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function to read from the queue and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in Amazon DynamoDB.
o.D: Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to send an event to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams when a new file is uploaded. Use an AWS Lambda function to consume the event from the stream and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.

fixed: Option B text was missing and option C was truncated; both have been reconstructed.

e.why: S3 event notifications to SQS durably capture each upload, and a Lambda function processes queue messages as soon as they arrive, scaling with demand and down to zero. Storing the resulting JSON in DynamoDB keeps everything fully managed, giving the least operational overhead.

others.A: An EMR cluster is heavy to operate for small one-time transformations and does not react immediately to each upload.
others.B: EC2 instances must be provisioned, patched and scaled, which adds overhead for spiky or idle demand.
others.D: Kinesis Data Streams needs shard management and Aurora needs a provisioned cluster, adding overhead over SQS and DynamoDB.

e.tip: Event-driven, variable volume, least overhead = S3 events to SQS to Lambda.

q:
An application allows users at a company's headquarters to access product data. The product data is stored in an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. The operations team has isolated an application performance slowdown and wants to separate read traffic from write traffic. A solutions architect needs to optimize the application's performance quickly.
What should the solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Change the existing database to a Multi-AZ deployment. Serve the read requests from the primary Availability Zone.
o.B: Change the existing database to a Multi-AZ deployment. Serve the read requests from the secondary Availability Zone.
o.C: Create read replicas for the database. Configure the read replicas with half of the compute and storage resources as the source database.
o.D: Create read replicas for the database. Configure the read replicas with the same compute and storage resources as the source database.

e.why: RDS read replicas separate read traffic from writes by serving reads from replica endpoints, which is a quick change. Replicas should have the same compute and storage as the source so they can keep up with replication and the read load.

others.A: In a Multi-AZ instance deployment, reads are already served from the primary, so it does not separate traffic.
others.B: The Multi-AZ standby in a classic deployment cannot serve read traffic.
others.C: Undersized replicas can suffer replication lag and poor read performance.

e.tip: Separate reads from writes in RDS: read replicas sized like the source.

o.A: Users can terminate an EC2 instance in any AWS Region except us-east-1.
o.B: Users can terminate an EC2 instance with the IP address 10.100.100.1 in the us-east-1 Region.
o.C: Users can terminate an EC2 instance in the us-east-1 Region when the user's source IP is 10.100.100.254.
o.D: Users cannot terminate an EC2 instance in the us-east-1 Region when the user's source IP is 10.100.100.254.

fixed: The IAM policy referenced by the question was missing and has been added from the original question.

e.why: The first statement allows ec2:TerminateInstances when the caller's source IP is in 10.100.100.0/24. The second statement explicitly denies all EC2 actions outside us-east-1. A user whose source IP is 10.100.100.254 is inside the allowed range, so the user can terminate instances in us-east-1 only.

others.A: The Deny statement blocks all EC2 actions in every Region except us-east-1, the opposite of this option.
others.B: aws:SourceIp refers to the caller's IP address, not the IP address of the instance being terminated.
others.D: 10.100.100.254 falls within 10.100.100.0/24, so the Allow applies and nothing denies the action in us-east-1.

e.tip: aws:SourceIp is the requester's IP; an explicit Deny always overrides an Allow.

q:
A company has a large Microsoft SharePoint deployment running on-premises that requires Microsoft Windows shared file storage. The company wants to migrate this workload to the AWS Cloud and is considering various storage options. The storage solution must be highly available and integrated with Active Directory for access control.
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

o.A: Configure Amazon EFS storage and set the Active Directory domain for authentication.
o.B: Create an SMB file share on an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway in two Availability Zones.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket and configure Microsoft Windows Server to mount it as a volume.
o.D: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system on AWS and set the Active Directory domain for authentication.

e.why: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed native SMB file shares that integrate with Microsoft Active Directory for access control. Multi-AZ deployments provide high availability, and it is the AWS-recommended storage for SharePoint workloads.

others.A: Amazon EFS uses NFS and does not support Windows SMB or Active Directory authentication.
others.B: Storage Gateway file gateways are for hybrid access to S3 and are not a highly available multi-AZ file share for SharePoint.
others.C: S3 is object storage and cannot be natively mounted as a Windows volume.

e.tip: Windows shared storage with AD: FSx for Windows File Server.

q:
An image-processing company has a web application that users use to upload images. The application uploads the images into an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has set up S3 event notifications to publish the object creation events to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue. The SQS queue serves as the event source for an AWS Lambda function that processes the images and sends the results to users through email.
Users report that they are receiving multiple email messages for every uploaded image. A solutions architect determines that SQS messages are invoking the Lambda function more than once, resulting in multiple email messages.
What should the solutions architect do to resolve this issue with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Set up long polling in the SQS queue by increasing the ReceiveMessage wait time to 30 seconds.
o.B: Change the SQS standard queue to an SQS FIFO queue. Use the message deduplication ID to discard duplicate messages.
o.C: Increase the visibility timeout in the SQS queue to a value that is greater than the total of the function timeout and the batch window timeout.
o.D: Modify the Lambda function to delete each message from the SQS queue immediately after the message is read before processing.

e.why: If the SQS visibility timeout is shorter than the time Lambda takes to process a batch, messages reappear and are processed again, causing duplicate emails. AWS recommends setting the visibility timeout to at least six times the function timeout plus the batching window, which fixes the issue with a simple configuration change.

others.A: Long polling reduces empty responses but does not stop messages from becoming visible again during processing.
others.B: S3 event notifications cannot target SQS FIFO queues, and migrating queues adds overhead.
others.D: Deleting messages before processing risks losing messages if processing fails.

e.tip: Duplicate Lambda invocations from SQS: increase visibility timeout beyond function timeout.

q:
A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in an on-premises data center. The company needs the ability to use Lustre clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed.
Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Create an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol. Connect the application server to the file share.
o.B: Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
o.C: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system, and configure it to support Lustre. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
o.D: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.

e.why: Amazon FSx for Lustre is a fully managed, high-performance file system that is accessed with the Lustre client. On-premises Lustre clients can mount it over Direct Connect or VPN, meeting the shared storage and fully managed requirements.

others.A: Storage Gateway file gateways support NFS and SMB, not the Lustre protocol.
others.B: A self-managed Windows file share is not fully managed and does not support Lustre clients.
others.C: Amazon EFS cannot be configured to support the Lustre protocol.

e.tip: Lustre or HPC file system needs: FSx for Lustre.

q:
A company's containerized application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. The application needs to download security certificates before it can communicate with other business applications. The company wants a highly secure solution to encrypt and decrypt the certificates in near real time. The solution also needs to store data in highly available storage after the data is encrypted.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create AWS Secrets Manager secrets for encrypted certificates. Manually update the certificates as needed. Control access to the data by using fine-grained IAM access.
o.B: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the Python cryptography library to receive and perform encryption operations. Store the function in an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.C: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Allow the EC2 role to use the KMS key for encryption operations. Store the encrypted data on Amazon S3.
o.D: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Allow the EC2 role to use the KMS key for encryption operations. Store the encrypted data on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes.

e.why: AWS KMS customer managed keys provide highly secure, managed encryption and decryption via fast API calls, and the EC2 role can be granted permissions to use the key. Storing the encrypted data in Amazon S3 provides highly available, durable storage across multiple AZs with no infrastructure to manage.

others.A: Manually updating secrets adds overhead, and Secrets Manager is not meant for near-real-time encryption of arbitrary data.
others.B: A custom Lambda encryption function adds development overhead, and functions are not stored in S3 to run.
others.D: EBS volumes reside in a single AZ and are less highly available than S3.

e.tip: Managed encryption: KMS; highly available storage: S3 (multi-AZ) over EBS (single AZ).

q:
A solutions architect is designing a VPC with public and private subnets. The VPC and subnets use IPv4 CIDR blocks. There is one public subnet and one private subnet in each of three Availability Zones (AZs) for high availability. An internet gateway is used to provide internet access for the public subnets. The private subnets require access to the internet to allow Amazon EC2 instances to download software updates.
What should the solutions architect do to enable Internet access for the private subnets?

o.A: Create three NAT gateways, one for each public subnet in each AZ. Create a private route table for each AZ that forwards non-VPC traffic to the NAT gateway in its AZ.
o.B: Create three NAT instances, one for each private subnet in each AZ. Create a private route table for each AZ that forwards non-VPC traffic to the NAT instance in its AZ.
o.C: Create a second internet gateway on one of the private subnets. Update the route table for the private subnets that forward non-VPC traffic to the private internet gateway.
o.D: Create an egress-only internet gateway on one of the public subnets. Update the route table for the private subnets that forward non-VPC traffic to the egress-only Internet gateway.

e.why: NAT gateways placed in each AZ's public subnet allow instances in private subnets to initiate outbound IPv4 internet connections. A private route table per AZ that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway in the same AZ avoids cross-AZ dependency, preserving high availability.

others.B: NAT instances must be in public subnets and require management; placing them in private subnets does not work.
others.C: A VPC can have only one internet gateway, and private subnets by definition do not route to it.
others.D: Egress-only internet gateways support only IPv6 traffic, not IPv4.

e.tip: IPv4 outbound for private subnets: NAT gateway per AZ; IPv6: egress-only internet gateway.

q:
A company wants to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The data center hosts an SFTP server that stores its data on an NFS-based file system. The server holds 200 GB of data that needs to be transferred. The server must be hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance that uses an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to automate this task? (Choose two.)

o.A: Launch the EC2 instance into the same Availability Zone as the EFS file system.
o.B: Install an AWS DataSync agent in the on-premises data center.
o.C: Create a secondary Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume on the EC2 instance for the data.
o.D: Manually use an operating system copy command to push the data to the EC2 instance.
o.E: Use AWS DataSync to create a suitable location configuration for the on-premises SFTP server.

e.why: AWS DataSync automates and accelerates transfers from on-premises NFS storage to Amazon EFS. Installing a DataSync agent in the data center and creating a source location for the on-premises server's file system lets DataSync copy the 200 GB directly to EFS.

others.A: EFS is accessible from all AZs in the Region, and AZ placement does not automate the transfer.
others.C: An extra EBS volume is unnecessary because the data must reside on EFS.
others.D: Manual copy commands are not automated.

e.tip: Automated on-prem NFS/SMB to EFS, FSx or S3: DataSync with an agent.

q:
A company has an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs every day at the same time. The job processes XML data that is in an Amazon S3 bucket. New data is added to the S3 bucket every day. A solutions architect notices that AWS Glue is processing all the data during each run.
What should the solutions architect do to prevent AWS Glue from reprocessing old data?

o.A: Edit the job to use job bookmarks.
o.B: Edit the job to delete data after the data is processed.
o.C: Edit the job by setting the NumberOfWorkers field to 1.
o.D: Use a FindMatches machine learning (ML) transform.

e.why: AWS Glue job bookmarks track state from previous runs so the job processes only new data added to the S3 source. Enabling bookmarks prevents reprocessing old data on each daily run.

others.B: Deleting source data after processing is destructive and unnecessary.
others.C: Reducing workers only slows the job and still reprocesses all data.
others.D: FindMatches is an ML transform for deduplicating or matching records, not for incremental processing.

e.tip: Glue incremental processing: job bookmarks.

q:
A solutions architect must design a highly available infrastructure for a website. The website is powered by Windows web servers that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The solutions architect must implement a solution that can mitigate a large-scale DDoS attack that originates from thousands of IP addresses. Downtime is not acceptable for the website.
Which actions should the solutions architect take to protect the website from such an attack? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use AWS Shield Advanced to stop the DDoS attack.
o.B: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to automatically block the attackers.
o.C: Configure the website to use Amazon CloudFront for both static and dynamic content.
o.D: Use an AWS Lambda function to automatically add attacker IP addresses to VPC network ACLs.
o.E: Use EC2 Spot Instances in an Auto Scaling group with a target tracking scaling policy that is set to 80% CPU utilization.

e.why: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced detection and automatic mitigation of large-scale DDoS attacks with 24/7 Shield Response Team support. Serving both static and dynamic content through Amazon CloudFront absorbs attack traffic across the global edge network, protecting the origin and keeping the site available.

others.B: GuardDuty detects threats but does not automatically block DDoS traffic.
others.D: Network ACLs have a limited number of rules and cannot handle thousands of attacker IPs.
others.E: Spot Instances can be interrupted, risking downtime, and scaling does not mitigate DDoS.

e.tip: DDoS protection: CloudFront (edge absorption) plus Shield Advanced, optionally with AWS WAF.

q:
A company is preparing to deploy a new serverless workload. A solutions architect must use the principle of least privilege to configure permissions that will be used to run an AWS Lambda function. An Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule will invoke the function.
Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Add an execution role to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and * as the principal.
o.B: Add an execution role to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and Service: lambda.amazonaws.com as the principal.
o.C: Add a resource-based policy to the function with lambda:* as the action and Service: events.amazonaws.com as the principal.
o.D: Add a resource-based policy to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and Service: events.amazonaws.com as the principal.

e.why: For EventBridge to invoke a Lambda function, the function's resource-based policy must grant lambda:InvokeFunction to the events.amazonaws.com service principal. Limiting the action to InvokeFunction (and optionally the rule ARN as source) follows least privilege.

others.A: Execution roles define what the function can do, not who can invoke it, and a wildcard principal is not least privilege.
others.B: Execution roles do not control invocation, and lambda.amazonaws.com is not the invoking service.
others.C: lambda:* grants far more permissions than needed.

e.tip: Who can invoke Lambda: resource-based policy; what Lambda can access: execution role.

q:
A company is preparing to store confidential data in Amazon S3. For compliance reasons, the data must be encrypted at rest. Encryption key usage must be logged for auditing purposes. Keys must be rotated every year.
Which solution meets these requirements and is the MOST operationally efficient?

o.A: Server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)
o.B: Server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3)
o.C: Server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) with manual rotation
o.D: Server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) with automatic rotation

e.why: SSE-KMS encrypts data at rest with KMS keys, and every key use is logged in AWS CloudTrail for auditing. Enabling automatic key rotation on a customer managed key rotates the key material every year by default, making it the most operationally efficient option.

others.A: SSE-C requires the customer to manage and rotate keys, and key usage is not logged by KMS.
others.B: SSE-S3 does not provide auditable key usage logs or customer control over rotation.
others.C: Manual rotation requires additional operational effort compared with automatic rotation.

e.tip: Auditable key usage plus yearly rotation: SSE-KMS with automatic rotation.

q:
A bicycle sharing company is developing a multi-tier architecture to track the location of its bicycles during peak operating hours. The company wants to use these data points in its existing analytics platform. A solutions architect must determine the most viable multi-tier option to support this architecture. The data points must be accessible from the REST API.
Which action meets these requirements for storing and retrieving location data?

o.A: Use Amazon Athena with Amazon S3.
o.B: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda.
o.C: Use Amazon QuickSight with Amazon Redshift.
o.D: Use Amazon API Gateway with Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics.

e.why: Amazon API Gateway provides the REST API for location updates, and Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics processes the streaming location data in real time, feeding results into the existing analytics platform. This multi-tier design handles streaming location data during peak hours.

others.A: Athena with S3 is for ad hoc querying and does not provide a REST API for real-time location data.
others.B: API Gateway with Lambda can provide the API, but by itself it offers no storage or streaming analytics for the location data.
others.C: QuickSight with Redshift is a visualization and warehouse solution, not a REST-accessible tier for location data.

e.tip: Real-time streaming analytics behind an API: API Gateway plus Kinesis.

q:
A company has an automobile sales website that stores its listings in a database on Amazon RDS. When an automobile is sold, the listing needs to be removed from the website and the data must be sent to multiple target systems.
Which design should a solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Create an AWS Lambda function triggered when the database on Amazon RDS is updated to send the information to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for the targets to consume.
o.B: Create an AWS Lambda function triggered when the database on Amazon RDS is updated to send the information to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue for the targets to consume.
o.C: Subscribe to an RDS event notification and send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue fanned out to multiple Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topics. Use AWS Lambda functions to update the targets.
o.D: Subscribe to an RDS event notification and send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic fanned out to multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use AWS Lambda functions to update the targets.

e.why: A Lambda function invoked when the database is updated (for example, from an Aurora or RDS trigger or application logic) can send the sold-listing data to an SQS queue for the target systems to consume. This decouples the website from downstream systems.

others.B: FIFO queues add throughput limits and ordering that are not required here.
others.C: SQS cannot fan out to multiple SNS topics; fan-out is SNS to SQS.
others.D: RDS event notifications report instance-level events such as failovers and backups, not data changes like a listing being sold.

e.tip: RDS event notifications are operational events, not row-level data changes.

q:
A company needs to store data in Amazon S3 and must prevent the data from being changed. The company wants new objects that are uploaded to Amazon S3 to remain unchangeable for a nonspecific amount of time until the company decides to modify the objects. Only specific users in the company's AWS account can have the ability 10 delete the objects.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an S3 Glacier vault. Apply a write-once, read-many (WORM) vault lock policy to the objects.
o.B: Create an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock enabled. Enable versioning. Set a retention period of 100 years. Use governance mode as the S3 bucket’s default retention mode for new objects.
o.C: Create an S3 bucket. Use AWS CloudTrail to track any S3 API events that modify the objects. Upon notification, restore the modified objects from any backup versions that the company has.
o.D: Create an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock enabled. Enable versioning. Add a legal hold to the objects. Add the s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission to the IAM policies of users who need to delete the objects.

e.why: S3 Object Lock legal holds prevent an object version from being overwritten or deleted with no expiration date, which matches 'unchangeable for a nonspecific amount of time'. Object Lock requires versioning, and only users granted s3:PutObjectLegalHold can remove the hold and then delete objects, limiting deletion to specific users.

others.A: S3 Glacier vault lock applies to archives in vaults, not S3 objects, and locked policies cannot be changed to allow specific users.
others.B: A fixed 100-year retention period is not a nonspecific duration, and governance mode bypass is managed with a different permission.
others.C: CloudTrail notifications with restores are reactive and do not prevent changes.

e.tip: Indefinite immutability: Object Lock legal hold; fixed period: retention mode (governance or compliance).

q:
A social media company allows users to upload images to its website. The website runs on Amazon EC2 instances. During upload requests, the website resizes the images to a standard size and stores the resized images in Amazon S3. Users are experiencing slow upload requests to the website.
The company needs to reduce coupling within the application and improve website performance. A solutions architect must design the most operationally efficient process for image uploads.
Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Configure the application to upload images to S3 Glacier.
o.B: Configure the web server to upload the original images to Amazon S3.
o.C: Configure the application to upload images directly from each user's browser to Amazon S3 through the use of a presigned URL
o.D: Configure S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function when an image is uploaded. Use the function to resize the image.
o.E: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function on a schedule to resize uploaded images.

e.why: Presigned URLs let users' browsers upload images directly to S3, offloading upload traffic from the web servers and speeding up requests. An S3 event notification invoking Lambda to resize each image decouples processing from the web tier in an operationally efficient, event-driven way.

others.A: S3 Glacier is for archival and is unsuitable for images that must be processed and served.
others.B: Uploading through the web server still makes the web tier a bottleneck.
others.E: A scheduled resize job introduces delay and is less efficient than event-driven processing.

e.tip: Offload uploads: S3 presigned URLs; process on upload: S3 event to Lambda.

q:
A company recently migrated a message processing system to AWS. The system receives messages into an ActiveMQ queue running on an Amazon EC2 instance. Messages are processed by a consumer application running on Amazon EC2. The consumer application processes the messages and writes results to a MySQL database running on Amazon EC2. The company wants this application to be highly available with low operational complexity.
Which architecture offers the HIGHEST availability?

o.A: Add a second ActiveMQ server to another Availability Zone. Add an additional consumer EC2 instance in another Availability Zone. Replicate the MySQL database to another Availability Zone.
o.B: Use Amazon MQ with active/standby brokers configured across two Availability Zones. Add an additional consumer EC2 instance in another Availability Zone. Replicate the MySQL database to another Availability Zone.
o.C: Use Amazon MQ with active/standby brokers configured across two Availability Zones. Add an additional consumer EC2 instance in another Availability Zone. Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi-AZ enabled.
o.D: Use Amazon MQ with active/standby brokers configured across two Availability Zones. Add an Auto Scaling group for the consumer EC2 instances across two Availability Zones. Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi-AZ enabled.

e.why: Amazon MQ with active/standby brokers across two AZs provides a managed, highly available ActiveMQ broker. An Auto Scaling group across two AZs keeps consumer instances healthy and replaces failures, and RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ provides managed synchronous standby with automatic failover, giving the highest availability with low complexity.

others.A: Self-managed ActiveMQ servers and MySQL replication on EC2 increase operational complexity and lack managed failover.
others.B: Self-managed MySQL replication on EC2 lacks automatic failover and adds complexity.
others.C: Without an Auto Scaling group, failed consumer instances are not automatically replaced.

e.tip: Highest availability with low ops: managed services in Multi-AZ plus Auto Scaling.

q:
A company hosts a containerized web application on a fleet of on-premises servers that process incoming requests. The number of requests is growing quickly. The on-premises servers cannot handle the increased number of requests. The company wants to move the application to AWS with minimum code changes and minimum development effort.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Fargate on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to run the containerized web application with Service Auto Scaling. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the incoming requests.
o.B: Use two Amazon EC2 instances to host the containerized web application. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the incoming requests.
o.C: Use AWS Lambda with a new code that uses one of the supported languages. Create multiple Lambda functions to support the load. Use Amazon API Gateway as an entry point to the Lambda functions.
o.D: Use a high performance computing (HPC) solution such as AWS ParallelCluster to establish an HPC cluster that can process the incoming requests at the appropriate scale.

e.why: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate runs the existing container images with no code changes and no servers to manage. ECS Service Auto Scaling adjusts task counts to handle growing requests, and an ALB distributes traffic, giving the least operational overhead.

others.B: Two fixed EC2 instances do not scale automatically and require server management.
others.C: Rewriting the application for Lambda requires significant code changes.
others.D: An HPC cluster is not intended for serving web requests and adds complexity.

e.tip: Lift existing containers with least ops: ECS on Fargate.

q:
A company uses 50 TB of data for reporting. The company wants to move this data from on premises to AWS. A custom application in the company’s data center runs a weekly data transformation job. The company plans to pause the application until the data transfer is complete and needs to begin the transfer process as soon as possible.
The data center does not have any available network bandwidth for additional workloads. A solutions architect must transfer the data and must configure the transformation job to continue to run in the AWS Cloud.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS DataSync to move the data. Create a custom transformation job by using AWS Glue.
o.B: Order an AWS Snowcone device to move the data. Deploy the transformation application to the device.
o.C: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Copy the data to the device. Create a custom transformation job by using AWS Glue.
o.D: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device that includes Amazon EC2 compute. Copy the data to the device. Create a new EC2 instance on AWS to run the transformation application.

e.why: With no available network bandwidth, a Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device is the fastest way to move 50 TB to AWS offline. Once the data is in S3, an AWS Glue ETL job replaces the custom transformation job as a serverless, managed service, minimizing operational overhead.

others.A: DataSync needs network bandwidth, which the data center does not have.
others.B: A Snowcone holds only 8 to 14 TB and running the transformation on the device is not a long-term cloud solution.
others.D: Running the transformation on a self-managed EC2 instance adds operational overhead, and EC2 compute on the device is unnecessary.

e.tip: No bandwidth and tens of TB: Snowball Edge; serverless ETL: AWS Glue.

q:
A company has created an image analysis application in which users can upload photos and add photo frames to their images. The users upload images and metadata to indicate which photo frames they want to add to their images. The application uses a single Amazon EC2 instance and Amazon DynamoDB to store the metadata.
The application is becoming more popular, and the number of users is increasing. The company expects the number of concurrent users to vary significantly depending on the time of day and day of week. The company must ensure that the application can scale to meet the needs of the growing user base.
Which solution meats these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Lambda to process the photos. Store the photos and metadata in DynamoDB.
o.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to process the photos and to store the photos and metadata.
o.C: Use AWS Lambda to process the photos. Store the photos in Amazon S3. Retain DynamoDB to store the metadata.
o.D: Increase the number of EC2 instances to three. Use Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to store the photos and metadata.

fixed: Option A was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: Lambda scales automatically with highly variable numbers of concurrent users to process photos. Storing photos in Amazon S3 gives virtually unlimited, durable object storage, and keeping DynamoDB for metadata retains a scalable, low-latency metadata store.

others.A: DynamoDB items are limited to 400 KB, so it is not suitable for storing photos.
others.B: Kinesis Data Firehose is a delivery service for streaming data; it does not process photos or act as a store.
others.D: A fixed three EC2 instances do not scale with demand, and EBS volumes are not shared object storage.

e.tip: Images and large objects go in S3; keep metadata in DynamoDB.

q:
A medical records company is hosting an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes customer data files that are stored on Amazon S3. The EC2 instances are hosted in public subnets. The EC2 instances access Amazon S3 over the internet, but they do not require any other network access.
A new requirement mandates that the network traffic for file transfers take a private route and not be sent over the internet.
Which change to the network architecture should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

o.A: Create a NAT gateway. Configure the route table for the public subnets to send traffic to Amazon S3 through the NAT gateway.
o.B: Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to restrict outbound traffic so that only traffic to the S3 prefix list is permitted.
o.C: Move the EC2 instances to private subnets. Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon S3, and link the endpoint to the route table for the private subnets.
o.D: Remove the internet gateway from the VPC. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection, and route traffic to Amazon S3 over the Direct Connect connection.

fixed: Options C and D were garbled (D truncated, C replaced by D's tail) and have been reconstructed.

e.why: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3, linked to the private subnets' route table, sends S3 traffic over the AWS private network instead of the internet. Moving the instances to private subnets removes internet access they do not need.

others.A: A NAT gateway still sends S3 traffic out to the public S3 endpoint over the internet path.
others.B: Security group rules restrict destinations but do not change the route; traffic still goes through the internet gateway.
others.D: Direct Connect links on-premises networks to AWS; it does not provide a private route from EC2 instances already in a VPC.

e.tip: EC2 to S3 without the internet = S3 gateway VPC endpoint.

q:
A company uses a popular content management system (CMS) for its corporate website. However, the required patching and maintenance are burdensome. The company is redesigning its website and wants anew solution. The website will be updated four times a year and does not need to have any dynamic content available. The solution must provide high scalability and enhanced security.
Which combination of changes will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

o.A: Configure Amazon CloudFront in front of the website to use HTTPS functionality.
o.B: Deploy an AWS WAF web ACL in front of the website to provide HTTPS functionality.
o.C: Create and deploy an AWS Lambda function to manage and serve the website content.
o.D: Create the new website and an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy the website on the S3 bucket with static website hosting enabled.
o.E: Create the new website. Deploy the website by using an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer.

e.why: A static website hosted on Amazon S3 needs no servers or CMS patching and scales automatically. Placing CloudFront in front provides HTTPS (S3 website endpoints do not support HTTPS), edge caching and enhanced security features such as origin access control and AWS WAF integration, with the least overhead.

others.B: AWS WAF filters web requests but does not provide HTTPS functionality.
others.C: Using Lambda to serve static content adds unnecessary code and management.
others.E: EC2 instances behind an ALB require patching and management, defeating the goal.

e.tip: Static site with HTTPS and low ops: S3 plus CloudFront.

q:
A company stores its application logs in an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. A new policy requires the company to store all application logs in Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) in near-real time.
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Configure a CloudWatch Logs subscription to stream the logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service).
o.B: Create an AWS Lambda function. Use the log group to invoke the function to write the logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service).
o.C: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the log group as the delivery streams sources. Configure Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) as the delivery stream's destination.
o.D: Install and configure Amazon Kinesis Agent on each application server to deliver the logs to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Configure Kinesis Data Streams to deliver the logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service).

e.why: CloudWatch Logs subscription filters can stream log data to Amazon OpenSearch Service in near real time; the console wizard sets this up (using a managed Lambda function behind the scenes) with minimal configuration. This meets the requirement with the least operational overhead.

others.B: Writing and maintaining a custom Lambda function adds overhead compared with the built-in subscription.
others.C: Firehose works as a subscription destination but adds another resource to configure and manage.
others.D: Installing Kinesis Agent on every server and managing Data Streams adds significant overhead.

e.tip: CloudWatch Logs to OpenSearch near real time: subscription filter.

q:
A company is building a web-based application running on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. The web application will provide access to a repository of text documents totaling about 900 TB in size. The company anticipates that the web application will experience periods of high demand. A solutions architect must ensure that the storage component for the text documents can scale to meet the demand of the application at all times. The company is concerned about the overall cost of the solution.
Which storage solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
o.B: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
o.C: Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service)
o.D: Amazon S3

e.why: Amazon S3 offers virtually unlimited scalable storage and automatically handles high request rates, so it scales to meet demand at all times. For 900 TB of documents, S3 is far cheaper per GB than EBS, EFS or OpenSearch, making it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: EBS volumes are tied to single instances and AZs, have size limits, and are expensive at this scale.
others.B: EFS is shared and scalable but costs much more per GB than S3.
others.C: OpenSearch Service is a search engine whose cluster storage is much more expensive than S3.

e.tip: Massive scalable storage at lowest cost: S3.

q:
A global company is using Amazon API Gateway to design REST APIs for its loyalty club users in the us-east-1 Region and the ap-southeast-2 Region. A solutions architect must design a solution to protect these API Gateway managed REST APIs across multiple accounts from SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of administrative effort?

o.A: Set up AWS WAF in both Regions. Associate Regional web ACLs with an API stage.
o.B: Set up AWS Firewall Manager in both Regions. Centrally configure AWS WAF rules.
o.C: Set up AWS Shield in bath Regions. Associate Regional web ACLs with an API stage.
o.D: Set up AWS Shield in one of the Regions. Associate Regional web ACLs with an API stage.

e.why: AWS Firewall Manager centrally configures and deploys AWS WAF rules, including SQL injection and cross-site scripting protections, across multiple accounts in AWS Organizations and automatically applies them to API Gateway stages. This gives the least administrative effort for protecting APIs in two Regions across accounts.

others.A: Configuring WAF separately in each account and Region requires more administrative effort.
others.C: AWS Shield protects against DDoS, not SQL injection or XSS.
others.D: AWS Shield in one Region does not protect against SQL injection or XSS, nor the other Region.

e.tip: WAF rules across many accounts: Firewall Manager.

q:
A company has implemented a self-managed DNS solution on three Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in the us-west-2 Region. Most of the company's users are located in the United States and Europe. The company wants to improve the performance and availability of the solution. The company launches and configures three EC2 instances in the eu-west-1 Region and adds the EC2 instances as targets for a new NLB.
Which solution can the company use to route traffic to all the EC2 instances?

o.A: Create an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to route requests to one of the two NLBs. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Use the Route 53 record as the distribution’s origin.
o.B: Create a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Create endpoint groups in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Add the two NLBs as endpoints for the endpoint groups.
o.C: Attach Elastic IP addresses to the six EC2 instances. Create an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to route requests to one of the six EC2 instances. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Use the Route 53 record as the distribution's origin.
o.D: Replace the two NLBs with two Application Load Balancers (ALBs). Create an Amazon Route 53 latency routing policy to route requests to one of the two ALBs. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Use the Route 53 record as the distribution’s origin.

e.why: AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs and routes users to the nearest healthy endpoint over the AWS backbone, with fast regional failover. NLBs (supporting UDP and TCP for DNS) can be added as endpoints in endpoint groups for us-west-2 and eu-west-1, improving performance and availability.

others.A: CloudFront does not support UDP-based DNS traffic, so it cannot front a DNS service.
others.C: CloudFront cannot proxy DNS traffic, and routing to individual instances removes load balancing.
others.D: ALBs do not support UDP DNS traffic, and CloudFront cannot front DNS.

e.tip: Non-HTTP (TCP/UDP) multi-Region acceleration and failover: Global Accelerator.

q:
A company is running an online transaction processing (OLTP) workload on AWS. This workload uses an unencrypted Amazon RDS DB instance in a Multi-AZ deployment. Daily database snapshots are taken from this instance.
What should a solutions architect do to ensure the database and snapshots are always encrypted moving forward?

o.A: Encrypt a copy of the latest DB snapshot. Replace existing DB instance by restoring the encrypted snapshot.
o.B: Create a new encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and copy the snapshots to it. Enable encryption on the DB instance.
o.C: Copy the snapshots and enable encryption using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) Restore encrypted snapshot to an existing DB instance.
o.D: Copy the snapshots to an Amazon S3 bucket that is encrypted using server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) managed keys (SSE-KMS).

e.why: An existing unencrypted RDS instance cannot be encrypted in place. Copying the latest snapshot with encryption enabled using a KMS key and restoring it creates a new encrypted DB instance, and all future snapshots of that instance are encrypted automatically.

others.B: RDS storage is not managed through user EBS volumes, and encryption cannot be enabled on an existing DB instance.
others.C: An encrypted snapshot cannot be restored onto an existing DB instance; restore always creates a new instance.
others.D: Copying snapshots to S3 does not encrypt the running database or its future snapshots.

e.tip: Encrypt an existing RDS DB: copy snapshot with encryption, restore a new instance.

q:
A company wants to build a scalable key management infrastructure to support developers who need to encrypt data in their applications.
What should a solutions architect do to reduce the operational burden?

o.A: Use multi-factor authentication (MFA) to protect the encryption keys.
o.B: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to protect the encryption keys.
o.C: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create, store, and assign the encryption keys.
o.D: Use an IAM policy to limit the scope of users who have access permissions to protect the encryption keys.

e.why: AWS KMS is a fully managed, scalable service for creating, storing, rotating and controlling the use of encryption keys, integrated with many AWS services and SDKs. Using KMS removes the operational burden of running your own key management infrastructure.

others.A: MFA protects authentication but is not a key management infrastructure.
others.C: ACM manages SSL/TLS certificates, not data encryption keys for applications.
others.D: IAM policies control access but do not provide key management.

e.tip: Managed encryption keys: KMS; TLS certificates: ACM.

q:
A company has a dynamic web application hosted on two Amazon EC2 instances. The company has its own SSL certificate, which is on each instance to perform SSL termination.
There has been an increase in traffic recently, and the operations team determined that SSL encryption and decryption is causing the compute capacity of the web servers to reach their maximum limit.
What should a solutions architect do to increase the application's performance?

o.A: Create a new SSL certificate using AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Install the ACM certificate on each instance.
o.B: Create an Amazon S3 bucket Migrate the SSL certificate to the S3 bucket. Configure the EC2 instances to reference the bucket for SSL termination.
o.C: Create another EC2 instance as a proxy server. Migrate the SSL certificate to the new instance and configure it to direct connections to the existing EC2 instances.
o.D: Import the SSL certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener that uses the SSL certificate from ACM.

e.why: Importing the company's existing SSL certificate into ACM and attaching it to an ALB HTTPS listener moves SSL termination to the load balancer. This offloads encryption and decryption from the EC2 instances, freeing their compute capacity and improving performance.

others.A: ACM public certificates cannot be installed on EC2 instances, and termination would still burden the instances.
others.B: S3 cannot perform SSL termination for EC2 instances.
others.C: A single proxy instance becomes a bottleneck and single point of failure and must be managed.

e.tip: Offload SSL/TLS: terminate at the ALB with an ACM certificate.

q:
A company has a highly dynamic batch processing job that uses many Amazon EC2 instances to complete it. The job is stateless in nature, can be started and stopped at any given time with no negative impact, and typically takes upwards of 60 minutes total to complete. The company has asked a solutions architect to design a scalable and cost-effective solution that meets the requirements of the job.
What should the solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Implement EC2 Spot Instances.
o.B: Purchase EC2 Reserved Instances.
o.C: Implement EC2 On-Demand Instances.
o.D: Implement the processing on AWS Lambda.

e.why: Spot Instances offer up to 90% discount over On-Demand for spare EC2 capacity. Because the batch job is stateless and can be stopped and restarted at any time, Spot interruptions are acceptable, making Spot the most scalable and cost-effective option.

others.B: Reserved Instances require 1- or 3-year commitments, which is not cost-effective for a dynamic batch job.
others.C: On-Demand Instances cost more than Spot for interruption-tolerant workloads.
others.D: Lambda has a 15-minute maximum execution time, which a 60-minute job exceeds.

e.tip: Fault-tolerant, interruptible workloads: Spot Instances.

q:
A company runs its two-tier ecommerce website on AWS. The web tier consists of a load balancer that sends traffic to Amazon EC2 instances. The database tier uses an Amazon RDS DB instance. The EC2 instances and the RDS DB instance should not be exposed to the public internet. The EC2 instances require internet access to complete payment processing of orders through a third-party web service. The application must be highly available.
Which combination of configuration options will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use an Auto Scaling group to launch the EC2 instances in private subnets. Deploy an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance in private subnets.
o.B: Configure a VPC with two private subnets and two NAT gateways across two Availability Zones. Deploy an Application Load Balancer in the private subnets.
o.C: Use an Auto Scaling group to launch the EC2 instances in public subnets across two Availability Zones. Deploy an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance in private subnets.
o.D: Configure a VPC with two public subnets, two private subnets, and two NAT gateways across two Availability Zones. Deploy an Application Load Balancer in the public subnets.

e.why: Placing EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group in private subnets and an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance in private subnets keeps both off the public internet while staying highly available. A VPC with public and private subnets in two AZs, a NAT gateway in each AZ for outbound payment calls, and an internet-facing ALB in the public subnets completes the design.

others.B: An ALB in private subnets cannot receive internet traffic, and NAT gateways must reside in public subnets.
others.C: Launching EC2 instances in public subnets exposes them to the internet.

e.tip: Classic HA web tier: public ALB and NAT per AZ, private app and DB subnets.

q:
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to reduce a company's storage costs. All the company's data is in the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. The company must keep all data for at least 25 years. Data from the most recent 2 years must be highly available and immediately retrievable.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately.
o.B: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.
o.C: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Activate the archiving option to ensure that data is archived in S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
o.D: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) immediately and to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.

e.why: The most recent 2 years of data must stay highly available and immediately retrievable, so it remains in S3 Standard. A Lifecycle rule transitions objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years, the lowest-cost class for long-term retention up to 25 years.

others.A: Transitioning immediately to Deep Archive makes recent data unavailable for immediate retrieval.
others.C: Intelligent-Tiering archive tiers move objects based on lack of access, not age, so recent but unaccessed data could be archived and not immediately retrievable.
others.D: One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ and is not highly available.

e.tip: Age-based tiering with known pattern: Lifecycle rules.

q:
A media company is evaluating the possibility of moving its systems to the AWS Cloud. The company needs at least 10 TB of storage with the maximum possible I/O performance for video processing, 300 TB of very durable storage for storing media content, and 900 TB of storage to meet requirements for archival media that is not in use anymore.
Which set of services should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Amazon EBS for maximum performance, Amazon S3 for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage
o.B: Amazon EBS for maximum performance, Amazon EFS for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage
o.C: Amazon EC2 instance store for maximum performance, Amazon EFS for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 for archival storage
o.D: Amazon EC2 instance store for maximum performance, Amazon S3 for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage

e.why: EC2 instance store provides the highest possible I/O performance because it is physically attached NVMe storage, suitable for temporary video processing. Amazon S3 provides 11 nines of durability for 300 TB of media content, and S3 Glacier is low-cost archival storage for 900 TB of unused media.

others.A: EBS offers high performance, but instance store provides higher maximum I/O performance.
others.B: EBS is not maximum performance, and EFS is more expensive than S3 for durable bulk storage.
others.C: EFS is costly for 300 TB of durable storage, and S3 Standard is more expensive than Glacier for archives.

e.tip: Max I/O, temporary: instance store; durable: S3; archive: Glacier.

q:
A company wants to run applications in containers in the AWS Cloud. These applications are stateless and can tolerate disruptions within the underlying infrastructure. The company needs a solution that minimizes cost and operational overhead.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Spot Instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to run the application containers.
o.B: Use Spot Instances in an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) managed node group.
o.C: Use On-Demand Instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to run the application containers.
o.D: Use On-Demand Instances in an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) managed node group.

e.why: Amazon EKS managed node groups handle provisioning and lifecycle of worker nodes and support Spot capacity, including automatic handling of Spot interruptions by draining nodes. Since the stateless containers tolerate disruptions, Spot Instances minimize cost while the managed node group minimizes operational overhead.

others.A: Running containers directly on EC2 Auto Scaling instances requires managing a container runtime and orchestration yourself.
others.C: On-Demand Instances cost more, and you still manage container orchestration yourself.
others.D: On-Demand Instances cost more than Spot for disruption-tolerant workloads.

e.tip: Disruption-tolerant containers at lowest cost: Spot capacity in managed node groups (or Fargate Spot).

q:
A company is running a multi-tier web application on premises. The web application is containerized and runs on a number of Linux hosts connected to a PostgreSQL database that contains user records. The operational overhead of maintaining the infrastructure and capacity planning is limiting the company's growth. A solutions architect must improve the application's infrastructure.
Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to accomplish this? (Choose two.)

o.A: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora.
o.B: Migrate the web application to be hosted on Amazon EC2 instances.
o.C: Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the web application content.
o.D: Set up Amazon ElastiCache between the web application and the PostgreSQL database.
o.E: Migrate the web application to be hosted on AWS Fargate with Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).

e.why: The pain point is operational overhead and capacity planning. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL is a managed, auto-scaling-storage, PostgreSQL-compatible database, and AWS Fargate with ECS runs the existing containers without managing hosts or cluster capacity. Together they remove infrastructure maintenance from both tiers.

others.B: EC2 instances still require patching, scaling and capacity planning, so overhead is not reduced.
others.C: CloudFront improves content delivery latency but does nothing about managing hosts or the database.
others.D: ElastiCache adds another component to operate and addresses read performance, not operational overhead.

e.tip: Containers + 'no servers to manage' = Fargate; PostgreSQL + managed + scalable = Aurora.

q:
An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zonas. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The application performs best when the CPU utilization of the EC2 instances is at or near 40%.
What should a solutions architect do to maintain the desired performance across all instances in the group?

o.A: Use a simple scaling policy to dynamically scale the Auto Scaling group.
o.B: Use a target tracking policy to dynamically scale the Auto Scaling group.
o.C: Use an AWS Lambda function ta update the desired Auto Scaling group capacity.
o.D: Use scheduled scaling actions to scale up and scale down the Auto Scaling group.

e.why: A target tracking scaling policy keeps a metric such as ASGAverageCPUUtilization at a set value (40%) by automatically adding or removing instances. It is purpose-built for 'keep metric at X' requirements and needs no step tuning.

others.A: Simple scaling reacts to alarm thresholds with fixed adjustments and cooldowns, so it does not hold CPU near a target.
others.C: A custom Lambda function reinvents what target tracking already does natively, adding overhead.
others.D: Scheduled scaling is time-based and cannot respond to actual CPU utilization.

e.tip: 'Keep metric at or near N%' = target tracking policy.

q:
A company is developing a file-sharing application that will use an Amazon S3 bucket for storage. The company wants to serve all the files through an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company does not want the files to be accessible through direct navigation to the S3 URL.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Write individual policies for each S3 bucket to grant read permission for only CloudFront access.
o.B: Create an IAM user. Grant the user read permission to objects in the S3 bucket. Assign the user to CloudFront.
o.C: Write an S3 bucket policy that assigns the CloudFront distribution ID as the Principal and assigns the target S3 bucket as the Amazon Resource Name (ARN).
o.D: Create an origin access identity (OAI). Assign the OAI to the CloudFront distribution. Configure the S3 bucket permissions so that only the OAI has read permission.

e.why: An origin access identity (OAI) lets CloudFront authenticate to S3, and a bucket policy granting read only to the OAI blocks direct S3 URL access. Today AWS recommends Origin Access Control (OAC), the successor to OAI, but the principle is the same.

others.A: Policies granting 'CloudFront access' generically are not possible without an OAI/OAC principal, and there is only one bucket.
others.B: CloudFront cannot be assigned an IAM user to sign requests to S3.
others.C: A distribution ID is not a valid principal; OAC uses the cloudfront.amazonaws.com service principal with a SourceArn condition.

e.tip: Restrict S3 to CloudFront only = OAI (legacy) or OAC (current).

q:
A company’s website provides users with downloadable historical performance reports. The website needs a solution that will scale to meet the company’s website demands globally. The solution should be cost-effective, limit the provisioning of infrastructure resources, and provide the fastest possible response time.
Which combination should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3
o.B: AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB
o.C: Application Load Balancer with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
o.D: Amazon Route 53 with internal Application Load Balancers

e.why: Static downloadable reports fit Amazon S3, which needs no provisioning and scales automatically, and CloudFront caches them at edge locations globally for the fastest response time at low cost.

others.B: Lambda and DynamoDB are for dynamic compute and data, not efficient global delivery of static files.
others.C: EC2 with ALB requires provisioning infrastructure and is regional, so it is costlier and slower globally.
others.D: Internal ALBs are not internet-facing and Route 53 adds no caching.

e.tip: Global static content, cheap and fast = S3 + CloudFront.

q:
A company runs an Oracle database on premises. As part of the company’s migration to AWS, the company wants to upgrade the database to the most recent available version. The company also wants to set up disaster recovery (DR) for the database. The company needs to minimize the operational overhead for normal operations and DR setup. The company also needs to maintain access to the database's underlying operating system.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate the Oracle database to an Amazon EC2 instance. Set up database replication to a different AWS Region.
o.B: Migrate the Oracle database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. Activate Cross-Region automated backups to replicate the snapshots to another AWS Region.
o.C: Migrate the Oracle database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle. Create a read replica for the database in another AWS Region.
o.D: Migrate the Oracle database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. Create a standby database in another Availability Zone.

e.why: RDS Custom for Oracle is a managed database that still grants access to the underlying OS and database host, which standard RDS does not. It supports cross-Region read replicas for DR, minimizing operational overhead compared with self-managed EC2.

others.A: Oracle on EC2 gives OS access but you must manage installation, upgrades and replication yourself, which is high overhead.
others.B: Standard RDS for Oracle does not allow access to the operating system.
others.D: Standard RDS gives no OS access, and a Multi-AZ standby in the same Region is high availability, not Regional DR.

e.tip: Managed database + OS access needed = RDS Custom (Oracle or SQL Server).

q:
A company wants to move its application to a serverless solution. The serverless solution needs to analyze existing and new data by using SL. The company stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data requires encryption and must be replicated to a different AWS Region.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create a new S3 bucket. Load the data into the new S3 bucket. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to replicate encrypted objects to an S3 bucket in another Region. Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS multi-Region kays (SSE-KMS). Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
o.B: Create a new S3 bucket. Load the data into the new S3 bucket. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to replicate encrypted objects to an S3 bucket in another Region. Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS multi-Region keys (SSE-KMS). Use Amazon RDS to query the data.
o.C: Load the data into the existing S3 bucket. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to replicate encrypted objects to an S3 bucket in another Region. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
o.D: Load the data into the existing S3 bucket. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to replicate encrypted objects to an S3 bucket in another Region. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Use Amazon RDS to query the data.

e.why: Using the existing bucket with Cross-Region Replication, SSE-S3 encryption, and Amazon Athena (serverless SQL directly on S3) gives the least operational overhead. SSE-S3 needs no key management and replicates without extra KMS configuration.

others.A: A new bucket and KMS multi-Region keys add migration and key-management work beyond what is required.
others.B: Amazon RDS is not serverless SQL over S3 data and requires loading data into a database.
others.D: RDS cannot query S3 objects in place and is not a serverless analytics service.

e.tip: Serverless SQL on S3 = Athena; simplest encryption = SSE-S3.

q:
A company runs workloads on AWS. The company needs to connect to a service from an external provider. The service is hosted in the provider's VPC. According to the company’s security team, the connectivity must be private and must be restricted to the target service. The connection must be initiated only from the company’s VPC.
Which solution will mast these requirements?

o.A: Create a VPC peering connection between the company's VPC and the provider's VPC. Update the route table to connect to the target service.
o.C: Create a NAT gateway in a public subnet of the company's VPC. Update the route table to connect to the target service.
o.B: Ask the provider to create a virtual private gateway in its VPC. Use AWS PrivateLink to connect to the target service.
o.D: Ask the provider to create a VPC endpoint for the target service. Use AWS PrivateLink to connect to the target service.

fixed: Options A, B and C were truncated or garbled and have been reconstructed.

e.why: With AWS PrivateLink, the provider exposes its service as a VPC endpoint service and the company creates an interface VPC endpoint to it. Traffic stays private, access is limited to that single service, and connections can only be initiated from the company's (consumer) VPC.

others.A: VPC peering opens routing between whole networks rather than just the target service, and either side can initiate traffic.
others.B: A virtual private gateway is for VPN or Direct Connect connectivity and is not how PrivateLink services are exposed.
others.C: A NAT gateway sends traffic over the internet, so the connection would not be private.

e.tip: Private, service-specific, consumer-initiated access to another VPC's service = AWS PrivateLink.

q:
A company is migrating its on-premises PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The on-premises database must remain online and accessible during the migration. The Aurora database must remain synchronized with the on-premises database.
Which combination of actions must a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create an ongoing replication task.
o.B: Create a database backup of the on-premises database.
o.C: Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication server.
o.D: Convert the database schema by using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT).
o.E: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to monitor the database synchronization.

e.why: AWS DMS needs a replication instance (server) and a task configured for full load plus ongoing replication (CDC). That keeps Aurora in sync while the on-premises source stays online.
