others.B: A backup is a point-in-time copy and cannot keep the target continuously synchronized.
others.D: SCT is unnecessary for a homogeneous PostgreSQL-to-Aurora PostgreSQL migration.
others.E: EventBridge does not monitor or provide database synchronization.

e.tip: Homogeneous migration needs no SCT; 'stay in sync' = DMS ongoing replication (CDC).

q:
A company uses AWS Organizations to create dedicated AWS accounts for each business unit to manage each business unit's account independently upon request. The root email recipient missed a notification that was sent to the root user email address of one account. The company wants to ensure that all future notifications are not missed. Future notifications must be limited to account administrators.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure the company’s email server to forward notification email messages that are sent to the AWS account root user email address to all users in the organization.
o.B: Configure all AWS account root user email addresses as distribution lists that go to a few administrators who can respond to alerts. Configure AWS account alternate contacts in the AWS Organizations console or programmatically.
o.C: Configure all AWS account root user email messages to be sent to one administrator who is responsible for monitoring alerts and forwarding those alerts to the appropriate groups.
o.D: Configure all existing AWS accounts and all newly created accounts to use the same root user email address. Configure AWS account alternate contacts in the AWS Organizations console or programmatically.

e.why: Making each root email a distribution list delivers notifications to several administrators, so none is missed, while still limiting recipients to admins. Configuring alternate contacts (billing, operations, security) through Organizations routes specific notifications to the right people.

others.A: Forwarding to all users in the organization violates the requirement to limit notifications to administrators.
others.C: A single administrator is still a single point of failure for missed alerts.
others.D: Each AWS account requires a unique root email address, so they cannot share one.

e.tip: Root email best practice = distribution list + alternate contacts.

q:
A company runs its ecommerce application on AWS. Every new order is published as a massage in a RabbitMQ queue that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in a single Availability Zone. These messages are processed by a different application that runs on a separate EC2 instance. This application stores the details in a PostgreSQL database on another EC2 instance. All the EC2 instances are in the same Availability Zone.
The company needs to redesign its architecture to provide the highest availability with the least operational overhead.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate the queue to a redundant pair (active/standby) of RabbitMQ instances on Amazon MQ. Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Create another Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the PostgreSQL database.
o.B: Migrate the queue to a redundant pair (active/standby) of RabbitMQ instances on Amazon MQ. Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Migrate the database to run on a Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL.
o.C: Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the RabbitMQ queue. Create another Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Migrate the database to run on a Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL.
o.D: Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the RabbitMQ queue. Create another Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Create a third Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the PostgreSQL database

e.why: Amazon MQ provides managed RabbitMQ with redundant brokers, a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group makes the application tier highly available, and RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ gives managed automatic failover. Every tier becomes highly available with minimal operational overhead.

others.A: Running PostgreSQL in an Auto Scaling group is self-managed and does not handle replication or failover correctly.
others.C: Self-managing RabbitMQ on EC2 adds operational overhead compared with Amazon MQ.
others.D: Self-managing both the queue and the database on EC2 maximizes operational overhead.

e.tip: RabbitMQ or ActiveMQ lift-and-shift = Amazon MQ.

q:
A reporting team receives files each day in an Amazon S3 bucket. The reporting team manually reviews and copies the files from this initial S3 bucket to an analysis S3 bucket each day at the same time to use with Amazon QuickSight. Additional teams are starting to send more files in larger sizes to the initial S3 bucket.
The reporting team wants to move the files automatically analysis S3 bucket as the files enter the initial S3 bucket. The reporting team also wants to use AWS Lambda functions to run pattern-matching code on the copied data. In addition, the reporting team wants to send the data files to a pipeline in Amazon SageMaker Pipelines.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create a Lambda function to copy the files to the analysis S3 bucket. Create an S3 event notification for the analysis S3 bucket. Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as destinations of the event notification. Configure s3:ObjectCreated:Put as the event type.
o.B: Create a Lambda function to copy the files to the analysis S3 bucket. Configure the analysis S3 bucket to send event notifications to Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events). Configure an ObjectCreated rule in EventBridge (CloudWatch Events). Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as targets for the rule.
o.C: Configure S3 replication between the S3 buckets. Create an S3 event notification for the analysis S3 bucket. Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as destinations of the event notification. Configure s3:ObjectCreated:Put as the event type.
o.D: Configure S3 replication between the S3 buckets. Configure the analysis S3 bucket to send event notifications to Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events). Configure an ObjectCreated rule in EventBridge (CloudWatch Events). Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as targets for the rule.

e.why: S3 replication copies new objects automatically without custom code. Sending the analysis bucket's events to Amazon EventBridge allows a rule to target multiple consumers, including Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines, which plain S3 event notifications cannot target.

others.A: A custom copy Lambda adds code to maintain, and S3 event notifications cannot target SageMaker Pipelines.
others.B: A custom copy Lambda adds overhead compared with native S3 replication.
others.C: S3 event notifications support only SNS, SQS and Lambda as destinations, not SageMaker Pipelines.

e.tip: S3 events to many targets or non-Lambda/SQS/SNS targets = EventBridge.

q:
A solutions architect needs to help a company optimize the cost of running an application on AWS. The application will use Amazon EC2 instances, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda for compute within the architecture.
The EC2 instances will run the data ingestion layer of the application. EC2 usage will be sporadic and unpredictable. Workloads that run on EC2 instances can be interrupted at any time. The application front end will run on Fargate, and Lambda will serve the API layer. The front-end utilization and API layer utilization will be predictable over the course of the next year.
Which combination of purchasing options will provide the MOST cost-effective solution for hosting this application? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use Spot Instances for the data ingestion layer
o.B: Use On-Demand Instances for the data ingestion layer
o.C: Purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan for the front end and API layer.
o.D: Purchase 1-year All Upfront Reserved instances for the data ingestion layer.
o.E: Purchase a 1-year EC2 instance Savings Plan for the front end and API layer.

e.why: Interruptible, sporadic EC2 workloads are ideal for Spot Instances, which offer the deepest discount. A Compute Savings Plan is the only Savings Plan that covers Fargate and Lambda, and it fits predictable one-year usage.

others.B: On-Demand is far more expensive than Spot for interruptible work.
others.D: Reserved Instances suit steady usage, not sporadic, unpredictable workloads.
others.E: EC2 Instance Savings Plans apply only to EC2, not Fargate or Lambda.

e.tip: Fargate or Lambda discounts = Compute Savings Plan.

q:
A company runs a web-based portal that provides users with global breaking news, local alerts, and weather updates. The portal delivers each user a personalized view by using mixture of static and dynamic content. Content is served over HTTPS through an API server running on an Amazon EC2 instance behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company wants the portal to provide this content to its users across the world as quickly as possible.
How should a solutions architect design the application to ensure the LEAST amount of latency for all users?

o.A: Deploy the application stack in a single AWS Region. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve all static and dynamic content by specifying the ALB as an origin.
o.B: Deploy the application stack in two AWS Regions. Use an Amazon Route 53 latency routing policy to serve all content from the ALB in the closest Region.
o.C: Deploy the application stack in a single AWS Region. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the static content. Serve the dynamic content directly from the ALB.
o.D: Deploy the application stack in two AWS Regions. Use an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to serve all content from the ALB in the closest Region.

fixed: Option B text was missing and option C was truncated; both have been reconstructed.

e.why: CloudFront accelerates both static and dynamic content: it caches static objects at edge locations and, for dynamic personalized requests, terminates TLS near users and uses persistent connections over the AWS backbone to the ALB origin. That gives the lowest latency for users worldwide from a single-Region stack.

others.B: Two Regions still leave many users far from an origin, and nothing is cached at the edge.
others.C: Serving dynamic content directly from the ALB gives distant users full round trips over the public internet.
others.D: Geolocation routing to two Regions without an edge network still leaves high latency for users far from both Regions.

e.tip: CloudFront helps dynamic content too, through edge TLS termination and backbone routing.

q:
A gaming company is designing a highly available architecture. The application runs on a modified Linux kernel and supports only UDP-based traffic. The company needs the front-end tier to provide the best possible user experience. That tier must have low latency, route traffic to the nearest edge location, and provide static IP addresses for entry into the application endpoints.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure Amazon Route 53 to forward requests to an Application Load Balancer. Use AWS Lambda for the application in AWS Application Auto Scaling.
o.B: Configure Amazon CloudFront to forward requests to a Network Load Balancer. Use AWS Lambda for the application in an AWS Application Auto Scaling group.
o.C: Configure AWS Global Accelerator to forward requests to a Network Load Balancer. Use Amazon EC2 instances for the application in an EC2 Auto Scaling group.
o.D: Configure Amazon API Gateway to forward requests to an Application Load Balancer. Use Amazon EC2 instances for the application in an EC2 Auto Scaling group.

e.why: AWS Global Accelerator provides two static anycast IP addresses, routes UDP or TCP traffic to the nearest edge location, and carries it over the AWS backbone. A Network Load Balancer supports UDP, and EC2 instances can run a modified Linux kernel.

others.A: ALB supports only HTTP/HTTPS, and Lambda cannot run a custom kernel.
others.B: CloudFront does not support arbitrary UDP traffic and has no static IPs, and Lambda cannot run a custom kernel.
others.D: API Gateway and ALB handle HTTP only, not UDP, and API Gateway has no static IPs.

e.tip: UDP + static IPs + edge routing = Global Accelerator + NLB.

q:
A company wants to migrate its existing on-premises monolithic application to AWS. The company wants to keep as much of the front-end code and the backend code as possible. However, the company wants to break the application into smaller applications. A different team will manage each application. The company needs a highly scalable solution that minimizes operational overhead.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Host the application on AWS Lambda. Integrate the application with Amazon API Gateway.
o.B: Host the application with AWS Amplify. Connect the application to an Amazon API Gateway API that is integrated with AWS Lambda.
o.C: Host the application on Amazon EC2 instances. Set up an Application Load Balancer with EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group as targets.
o.D: Host the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up an Application Load Balancer with Amazon ECS as the target.

e.why: Containerizing each smaller application on Amazon ECS keeps most of the existing code, lets each team own a separate service, and scales well. An ALB with path-based routing fronts the services, so this is the least-overhead microservices approach.

others.A: Lambda would require substantial rewriting of the monolith into functions.
others.B: Amplify with Lambda also requires rewriting the backend into serverless functions.
others.C: EC2 Auto Scaling groups do not easily separate the app into independently managed services and carry more host overhead.

e.tip: Break up a monolith while keeping code = containers on ECS or EKS.

q:
A company recently started using Amazon Aurora as the data store for its global ecommerce application. When large reports are run, developers report that the ecommerce application is performing poorly. After reviewing metrics in Amazon CloudWatch, a solutions architect finds that the ReadIOPS and CPUUtilizalion metrics are spiking when monthly reports run.
What is the MOST cost-effective solution?

o.A: Migrate the monthly reporting to Amazon Redshift.
o.B: Migrate the monthly reporting to an Aurora Replica.
o.C: Migrate the Aurora database to a larger instance class.
o.D: Increase the Provisioned IOPS on the Aurora instance.

e.why: Pointing the reporting workload at an Aurora Replica offloads the read-heavy queries from the writer instance using the shared storage volume. It needs no new service and is cheaper than scaling up or moving to Redshift.

others.A: Redshift adds a separate data warehouse and ETL pipeline, which costs more than a replica for monthly reports.
others.C: A larger instance runs at higher cost 24/7 to handle a monthly spike.
others.D: Aurora does not use Provisioned IOPS in the same way, and IOPS would not fix CPU contention.

e.tip: Reporting load slowing the primary = read replica.

q:
A company hosts a website analytics application on a single Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instance. The analytics software is written in PHP and uses a MySQL database. The analytics software, the web server that provides PHP, and the database server are all hosted on the EC2 instance. The application is showing signs of performance degradation during busy times and is presenting 5xx errors. The company needs to make the application scale seamlessly.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Create an AMI of the web application. Use the AMI to launch a second EC2 On-Demand Instance. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the load to each EC2 instance.
o.B: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Create an AMI of the web application. Use the AMI to launch a second EC2 On-Demand Instance. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted routing to distribute the load across the two EC2 instances.
o.C: Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instance. Create an AWS Lambda function to stop the EC2 instance and change the instance type. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke the Lambda function when CPU utilization surpasses 75%.
o.D: Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instance. Create an AMI of the web application. Apply the AMI to a launch template. Create an Auto Scaling group with the launch template Configure the launch template to use a Spot Fleet. Attach an Application Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.

e.why: Moving MySQL to Aurora separates the database tier, and an Auto Scaling group built from a launch template scales the web tier seamlessly behind an ALB. Using Spot capacity makes the scaling tier the most cost-effective option, since the web tier is stateless once the database is moved off.

others.A: A fixed second On-Demand instance does not scale seamlessly and costs more than Spot.
others.B: Route 53 weighted routing with two fixed instances provides no automatic scaling or health-based load balancing.
others.C: Stopping the instance to resize it causes downtime and is vertical scaling, not seamless scaling.

e.tip: 'Scale seamlessly' = Auto Scaling group + load balancer; 'most cost-effective' often signals Spot.

q:
A company runs a stateless web application in production on a group of Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application experiences heavy usage during an 8-hour period each business day. Application usage is moderate and steady overnight. Application usage is low during weekends.
The company wants to minimize its EC2 costs without affecting the availability of the application.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Spot Instances for the entire workload.
o.B: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use Spot instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
o.C: Use On-Demand Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use Spot Instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
o.D: Use Dedicated Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use On-Demand Instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.

e.why: The steady baseline running around the clock suits Reserved Instances (or Savings Plans) for the biggest committed discount. The extra daytime peak capacity can use Spot Instances, and because the app is stateless behind an ALB, interruptions are tolerated without affecting availability.

others.A: An all-Spot fleet risks losing baseline capacity when instances are reclaimed, harming availability.
others.C: On-Demand for the always-on baseline is more expensive than Reserved Instances.
others.D: Dedicated Instances cost more and are not needed, and On-Demand for peaks is pricier than Spot.

e.tip: Baseline = RIs or Savings Plans; spiky stateless extra = Spot.

q:
A company needs to retain application log files for a critical application for 10 years. The application team regularly accesses logs from the past month for troubleshooting, but logs older than 1 month are rarely accessed. The application generates more than 10 TB of logs per month.
Which storage option meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use AWS Backup to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
o.B: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
o.C: Store the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use AWS Backup to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
o.D: Store the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

e.why: Amazon S3 stores the logs cheaply, and an S3 Lifecycle rule automatically transitions objects older than 30 days to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, the cheapest class for rarely accessed 10-year retention. Lifecycle rules are native and cost nothing extra to configure.

others.A: AWS Backup does not transition S3 objects between storage classes; that is the job of Lifecycle policies.
others.C: CloudWatch Logs storage for over 10 TB per month is expensive, and AWS Backup cannot move it to Deep Archive.
others.D: S3 Lifecycle policies cannot act on CloudWatch Logs data.

e.tip: Age-based storage class transitions = S3 Lifecycle.

q:
A company has a data ingestion workflow that includes the following components:
An Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that receives notifications about new data deliveries
An AWS Lambda function that processes and stores the data
The ingestion workflow occasionally fails because of network connectivity issues. When failure occurs, the corresponding data is not ingested unless the company manually reruns the job.
What should a solutions architect do to ensure that all notifications are eventually processed?

o.A: Configure the Lambda function for deployment across multiple Availability Zones.
o.B: Modify the Lambda function's configuration to increase the CPU and memory allocations for the function.
o.C: Configure the SNS topic’s retry strategy to increase both the number of retries and the wait time between retries.
o.D: Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as the on-failure destination. Modify the Lambda function to process messages in the queue.

e.why: With asynchronous invocation from SNS, Lambda can send events that fail after its retries to an on-failure destination such as an SQS queue. The function (or a retry consumer) can then process the queued messages later, so every notification is eventually processed instead of being lost.

others.A: Lambda already runs across multiple AZs, and that does not fix transient network failures.
others.B: More CPU or memory does not address network connectivity failures.
others.C: SNS retry policies apply to delivery to the endpoint, not to failures inside the function's processing, and retries eventually run out.

e.tip: Never lose failed async events = SQS DLQ or on-failure destination.

q:
A company has a service that produces event data. The company wants to use AWS to process the event data as it is received. The data is written in a specific order that must be maintained throughout processing. The company wants to implement a solution that minimizes operational overhead.
How should a solutions architect accomplish this?

o.A: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue to hold messages. Set up an AWS Lambda function to process messages from the queue.
o.B: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to deliver notifications containing payloads to process. Configure an AWS Lambda function as a subscriber.
o.C: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue to hold messages. Set up an AWS Lambda function to process messages from the queue independently.
o.D: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to deliver notifications containing payloads to process. Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a subscriber.

e.why: An SQS FIFO queue preserves strict message order (within a message group) and offers exactly-once processing. Lambda can poll it natively, so the setup is fully managed with minimal operational overhead.

others.B: Standard SNS topics do not guarantee ordering.
others.C: SQS standard queues provide only best-effort ordering.
others.D: A standard SNS topic and queue do not guarantee order, and no processing compute is defined.

e.tip: Ordering required = FIFO (SQS FIFO or SNS FIFO).

q:
A company is migrating an application from on-premises servers to Amazon EC2 instances. As part of the migration design requirements, a solutions architect must implement infrastructure metric alarms. The company does not need to take action if CPU utilization increases to more than 50% for a short burst of time. However, if the CPU utilization increases to more than 50% and read IOPS on the disk are high at the same time, the company needs to act as soon as possible. The solutions architect also must reduce false alarms.
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create Amazon CloudWatch composite alarms where possible.
o.B: Create Amazon CloudWatch dashboards to visualize the metrics and react to issues quickly.
o.C: Create Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canaries to monitor the application and raise an alarm.
o.D: Create single Amazon CloudWatch metric alarms with multiple metric thresholds where possible.

e.why: CloudWatch composite alarms combine multiple alarms with AND/OR logic, so an alarm fires only when high CPU and high read IOPS occur together. That reduces false alarms from short CPU bursts.

others.B: Dashboards only visualize data and require humans to watch, so they cannot alert automatically.
others.C: Synthetics canaries test endpoints and user flows, not combined infrastructure metric conditions.
others.D: A single metric alarm evaluates one metric (or one math expression) and is not the intended way to require two independent alarm states.

e.tip: Alarm only when X AND Y = composite alarm.

q:
A company wants to migrate its on-premises data center to AWS. According to the company's compliance requirements, the company can use only the ap-northeast-3 Region. Company administrators are not permitted to connect VPCs to the internet.
Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use AWS Control Tower to implement data residency guardrails to deny internet access and deny access to all AWS Regions except ap-northeast-3.
o.B: Use rules in AWS WAF to prevent internet access. Deny access to all AWS Regions except ap-northeast-3 in the AWS account settings.
o.C: Use AWS Organizations to configure service control policies (SCPS) that prevent VPCs from gaining internet access. Deny access to all AWS Regions except ap-northeast-3.
o.D: Create an outbound rule for the network ACL in each VPC to deny all traffic from 0.0.0.0/0. Create an IAM policy for each user to prevent the use of any AWS Region other than ap-northeast-3.
o.E: Use AWS Config to activate managed rules to detect and alert for internet gateways and to detect and alert for new resources deployed outside of ap-northeast-3.

e.why: AWS Control Tower offers preventive guardrails (controls), including Region deny and controls that disallow internet access. Organizations SCPs can also deny actions such as creating internet gateways and deny all Regions except ap-northeast-3 across accounts. Both prevent the action instead of just detecting it.

others.B: AWS WAF filters HTTP requests and cannot block VPC internet connectivity, and there is no account setting that denies Regions.
others.D: NACLs can be changed by administrators, and per-user IAM policies are hard to maintain and easy to bypass compared with SCPs.
others.E: AWS Config is detective only; it alerts after the fact rather than preventing the action.

e.tip: Prevent across accounts = SCPs or Control Tower preventive controls; Config = detect.

q:
A company uses a three-tier web application to provide training to new employees. The application is accessed for only 12 hours every day. The company is using an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance to store information and wants to minimize costs.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure an IAM policy for AWS Systems Manager Session Manager. Create an IAM role for the policy. Update the trust relationship of the role. Set up automatic start and stop for the DB instance.
o.B: Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache cluster that gives users the ability to access the data from the cache when the DB instance is stopped. Invalidate the cache after the DB instance is started.
o.C: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Create an IAM role that grants access to Amazon RDS. Attach the role to the EC2 instance. Configure a cron job to start and stop the EC2 instance on the desired schedule.
o.D: Create AWS Lambda functions to start and stop the DB instance. Create Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled rules to invoke the Lambda functions. Configure the Lambda functions as event targets for the rules.

e.why: Scheduled EventBridge rules invoking Lambda functions that call StartDBInstance and StopDBInstance stop the RDS instance during the 12 unused hours, cutting instance-hour costs with serverless, near-zero-cost automation.

others.A: Session Manager provides shell access to instances and has nothing to do with scheduling RDS start or stop.
others.B: Adding ElastiCache increases cost, and serving data while the DB is stopped is not required.
others.C: A dedicated EC2 instance running cron adds cost and management overhead compared with Lambda.

e.tip: Scheduled start or stop = EventBridge Scheduler or rule + Lambda (or Instance Scheduler).

q:
A company sells ringtones created from clips of popular songs. The files containing the ringtones are stored in Amazon S3 Standard and are at least 128 KB in size. The company has millions of files, but downloads are infrequent for ringtones older than 90 days. The company needs to save money on storage while keeping the most accessed files readily available for its users.
Which action should the company take to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage for the initial storage tier of the objects.
o.B: Move the files to S3 Intelligent-Tiering and configure it to move objects to a less expensive storage tier after 90 days.
o.C: Configure S3 inventory to manage objects and move them to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-1A) after 90 days.
o.D: Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy that moves the objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-1A) after 90 days.

e.why: Access patterns are known (rarely downloaded after 90 days), so a simple S3 Lifecycle rule moving objects to S3 Standard-IA after 90 days is the cheapest option. The files are at least 128 KB, so the Standard-IA minimum billable size is not a penalty, and recent files stay in Standard.

others.A: Storing new popular files in Standard-IA incurs retrieval fees on frequent access.
others.B: Intelligent-Tiering adds a per-object monitoring fee across millions of objects and does not let you set a 90-day rule; it is best for unknown patterns.
others.C: S3 Inventory reports on objects and cannot transition them.

e.tip: Known access pattern = Lifecycle; unknown = Intelligent-Tiering.

q:
A company needs to save the results from a medical trial to an Amazon S3 repository. The repository must allow a few scientists to add new files and must restrict all other users to read-only access. No users can have the ability to modify or delete any files in the repository. The company must keep every file in the repository for a minimum of 1 year after its creation date.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode with a legal hold of 1 year.
o.B: Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a retention period of 365 days.
o.C: Use an IAM role to restrict all users from deleting or changing objects in the S3 bucket. Use an S3 bucket policy to only allow the IAM role.
o.D: Configure the S3 bucket to invoke an AWS Lambda function every time an object is added. Configure the function to track the hash of the saved object so that modified objects can be marked accordingly.

e.why: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode makes objects WORM: no user, including root, can overwrite or delete a version until the retention period (365 days) ends. IAM permissions then control who can add files and who has read-only access.

others.A: Governance mode can be bypassed by users with special permissions, and a legal hold has no fixed period.
others.C: IAM policies can be changed by administrators, so they do not guarantee immutability.
others.D: Hash tracking only detects modifications after they happen; it does not prevent them.

e.tip: Nobody can delete, not even root = Object Lock compliance mode.

q:
A large media company hosts a web application on AWS. The company wants to start caching confidential media files so that users around the world will have reliable access to the files. The content is stored in Amazon S3 buckets. The company must deliver the content quickly, regardless of where the requests originate geographically.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS DataSync to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.
o.B: Deploy AWS Global Accelerator to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.
o.C: Deploy Amazon CloudFront to connect the S3 buckets to CloudFront edge servers.
o.D: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.

e.why: Amazon CloudFront caches S3 content at edge locations worldwide for fast, reliable delivery regardless of user location. Confidential files can be protected with OAC plus signed URLs or signed cookies.

others.A: DataSync is a data transfer and migration service, not a content delivery or caching layer.
others.B: Global Accelerator does not cache content and does not support S3 buckets as endpoints.
others.D: SQS is a message queue and cannot deliver or cache files.

e.tip: Caching content globally = CloudFront.

q:
A company produces batch data that comes from different databases. The company also produces live stream data from network sensors and application APIs. The company needs to consolidate all the data into one place for business analytics. The company needs to process the incoming data and then stage the data in different Amazon S3 buckets. Teams will later run one-time queries and import the data into a business intelligence tool to show key performance indicators (KPIs).
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use Amazon Athena for one-time queries. Use Amazon QuickSight to create dashboards for KPIs.
o.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for one-time queries. Use Amazon QuickSight to create dashboards for KPIs.
o.C: Create custom AWS Lambda functions to move the individual records from the databases to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
o.D: Use an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the data into JSON format. Load the data into multiple Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) clusters.
o.E: Use blueprints in AWS Lake Formation to identify the data that can be ingested into a data lake. Use AWS Glue to crawl the source, extract the data, and load the data into Amazon S3 in Apache Parquet format.

e.why: Lake Formation blueprints with AWS Glue crawlers and ETL ingest batch database data into an S3 data lake as Parquet with little custom code. Athena then runs serverless one-time SQL queries on S3, and QuickSight builds KPI dashboards, all fully managed.

others.B: Kinesis Data Analytics is for continuous streaming analytics, not ad hoc one-time queries.
others.C: Custom record-by-record Lambda functions into Redshift add significant development and operational overhead.
others.D: Running multiple OpenSearch clusters is costly to operate and not the stated S3 staging approach.

e.tip: Data lake on S3 = Lake Formation + Glue; ad hoc SQL = Athena; BI = QuickSight.

q:
A company stores data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. The company must store all the data for 5 years and must delete all the data after 5 years. The company also must indefinitely keep audit logs of actions that are performed within the database. Currently, the company has automated backups configured for Aurora.

Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Take a manual snapshot of the DB cluster.
o.B: Create a lifecycle policy for the automated backups.
o.C: Configure automated backup retention for 5 years.
o.D: Configure an Amazon CloudWatch Logs export for the DB cluster.
o.E: Use AWS Backup to take the backups and to keep the backups for 5 years.

e.why: Aurora automated backups max out at 35 days, so AWS Backup with a 5-year retention rule (and automatic deletion) meets the data requirement. Exporting the Aurora PostgreSQL audit or database logs to CloudWatch Logs with never-expire retention keeps audit logs indefinitely.

others.A: A manual snapshot is a single point in time, never expires automatically, and does not delete data after 5 years.
others.B: Aurora automated backups do not support lifecycle policies.
others.C: Automated backup retention is limited to 35 days.

e.tip: RDS or Aurora backups beyond 35 days = AWS Backup or manual snapshots.

q:
A solutions architect is optimizing a website for an upcoming musical event. Videos of the performances will be streamed in real time and then will be available on demand. The event is expected to attract a global online audience.

Which service will improve the performance of both the real-time and on-demand streaming?

o.A: Amazon CloudFront
o.B: AWS Global Accelerator
o.C: Amazon Route 53
o.D: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration

e.why: CloudFront delivers both live streaming (for example HLS or DASH segments from MediaPackage or MediaLive) and on-demand video from edge locations close to the global audience, improving performance for both.

others.B: Global Accelerator improves TCP/UDP routing but does not cache video segments at the edge.
others.C: Route 53 is DNS and does not accelerate or cache content.
others.D: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads into S3, not streaming to viewers.

e.tip: Live or VOD streaming to a global audience = CloudFront.

q:
A company is running a publicly accessible serverless application that uses Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The application’s traffic recently spiked due to fraudulent requests from botnets.

Which steps should a solutions architect take to block requests from unauthorized users? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create a usage plan with an API key that is shared with genuine users only.
o.B: Integrate logic within the Lambda function to ignore the requests from fraudulent IP addresses.
o.C: Implement an AWS WAF rule to target malicious requests and trigger actions to filter them out.
o.D: Convert the existing public API to a private API. Update the DNS records to redirect users to the new API endpoint.
o.E: Create an IAM role for each user attempting to access the API. A user will assume the role when making the API call.

e.why: AWS WAF attached to API Gateway can block bot traffic using rate-based rules, IP reputation lists and Bot Control. A usage plan with API keys issued only to genuine users adds throttling and quota control to identify legitimate clients.

others.B: Filtering in Lambda still incurs invocations and costs, and maintaining IP lists in code is fragile.
others.D: A private API is reachable only from within VPCs, which would cut off legitimate public users.
others.E: Creating an IAM role per public user does not scale and is impractical.

e.tip: Block bots or malicious requests on API Gateway or ALB or CloudFront = AWS WAF.

q:
An ecommerce company hosts its analytics application in the AWS Cloud. The application generates about 300 MB of data each month. The data is stored in JSON format. The company is evaluating a disaster recovery solution to back up the data. The data must be accessible in milliseconds if it is needed, and the data must be kept for 30 days.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service)
o.B: Amazon S3 Glacier
o.C: Amazon S3 Standard
o.D: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL

e.why: Only about 300 MB per month for 30 days is tiny, and S3 Standard offers millisecond access with no retrieval fees or minimum duration penalties. That makes it the most cost-effective option for this backup.

others.A: OpenSearch Service requires running a cluster, which is far costlier for simple backup storage.
others.B: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval takes minutes to hours to retrieve, and its 90-day minimum exceeds the 30-day need.
others.D: Running an RDS instance to hold JSON backups is costly and unnecessary.

e.tip: Millisecond access + short retention + small data = S3 Standard.

q:
A company has a small Python application that processes JSON documents and outputs the results to an on-premises SQL database. The application runs thousands of times each day. The company wants to move the application to the AWS Cloud. The company needs a highly available solution that maximizes scalability and minimizes operational overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Place the JSON documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Run the Python code on multiple Amazon EC2 instances to process the documents. Store the results in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.
o.B: Place the JSON documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs the Python code to process the documents as they arrive in the S3 bucket. Store the results in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.
o.C: Place the JSON documents in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use the EBS Multi-Attach feature to attach the volume to multiple Amazon EC2 instances. Run the Python code on the EC2 instances to process the documents. Store the results on an Amazon RDS DB instance.
o.D: Place the JSON documents in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as messages. Deploy the Python code as a container on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that is configured with the Amazon EC2 launch type. Use the container to process the SQS messages. Store the results on an Amazon RDS DB instance.

e.why: S3 event notifications invoking Lambda process each JSON document as it arrives, with automatic scaling and built-in high availability and no servers to manage. Aurora provides a managed, highly available SQL database for the results.

others.A: Running EC2 instances requires managing scaling, patching and availability.
others.C: EBS Multi-Attach works only with io1/io2 in a single AZ and needs a cluster-aware file system, so it is not highly available.
others.D: ECS on the EC2 launch type still requires managing cluster instances, and SQS message size limits suit references rather than documents.

e.tip: Process files as they land in S3 = S3 event + Lambda.

q:
A company wants to use high performance computing (HPC) infrastructure on AWS for financial risk modeling. The company’s HPC workloads run on Linux. Each HPC workflow runs on hundreds of Amazon EC2 Spot Instances, is short-lived, and generates thousands of output files that are ultimately stored in persistent storage for analytics and long-term future use.

The company seeks a cloud storage solution that permits the copying of on-premises data to long-term persistent storage to make data available for processing by all EC2 instances. The solution should also be a high performance file system that is integrated with persistent storage to read and write datasets and output files.

Which combination of AWS services meets these requirements?

o.A: Amazon FSx for Lustre integrated with Amazon S3
o.B: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server integrated with Amazon S3
o.C: Amazon S3 Glacier integrated with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
o.D: Amazon S3 bucket with a VPC endpoint integrated with an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) General Purpose SSD (gp2) volume

e.why: Amazon FSx for Lustre is a high-performance parallel file system for Linux HPC. It natively links to an S3 bucket via a data repository association, lazy-loading datasets and exporting outputs back to S3 for durable long-term storage.

others.B: FSx for Windows File Server targets Windows SMB workloads, not Linux HPC, and has no native S3 linking.
others.C: Glacier is archival with slow retrieval and is not a file system for active processing.
others.D: An EBS gp2 volume is block storage attached to one instance and cannot be shared by hundreds of instances.

e.tip: HPC + Linux + S3 integration = FSx for Lustre.

q:
A company is building a containerized application on premises and decides to move the application to AWS. The application will have thousands of users soon after it is deployed. The company is unsure how to manage the deployment of containers at scale. The company needs to deploy the containerized application in a highly available architecture that minimizes operational overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Store container images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the AWS Fargate launch type to run the containers. Use target tracking to scale automatically based on demand.
o.B: Store container images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Amazon EC2 launch type to run the containers. Use target tracking to scale automatically based on demand.
o.C: Store container images in a repository that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Run the containers on EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Monitor the average CPU utilization in Amazon CloudWatch. Launch new EC2 instances as needed.
o.D: Create an Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that contains the container image. Launch EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to scale out EC2 instances when the average CPU utilization threshold is breached.

e.why: ECR stores the images, and ECS on AWS Fargate runs containers without any EC2 hosts to manage. Tasks are spread across AZs for high availability, and target tracking Service Auto Scaling handles demand. This minimizes operational overhead for a team new to container orchestration.

others.B: The EC2 launch type requires managing, patching and scaling the container instances.
others.C: Self-hosting a registry and manually launching instances is high operational overhead.
others.D: Baking containers into AMIs abandons container orchestration and requires managing instances.

e.tip: Containers + least overhead = ECS (or EKS) on Fargate.

q:
A company has two applications: a sender application that sends messages with payloads to be processed and a processing application intended to receive the messages with payloads. The company wants to implement an AWS service to handle messages between the two applications. The sender application can send about 1,000 messages each hour. The messages may take up to 2 days to be processed: If the messages fail to process, they must be retained so that they do not impact the processing of any remaining messages.

Which solution meets these requirements and is the MOST operationally efficient?

o.A: Set up an Amazon EC2 instance running a Redis database. Configure both applications to use the instance. Store, process, and delete the messages, respectively.
o.B: Use an Amazon Kinesis data stream to receive the messages from the sender application. Integrate the processing application with the Kinesis Client Library (KCL).
o.C: Integrate the sender and processor applications with an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure a dead-letter queue to collect the messages that failed to process.
o.D: Subscribe the processing application to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive notifications to process. Integrate the sender application to write to the SNS topic.

e.why: SQS decouples the applications, retains messages up to 14 days (well above the 2-day processing window), and scales easily for about 1,000 messages per hour. A dead-letter queue isolates messages that repeatedly fail so they do not block the rest, all fully managed.

others.A: A self-managed Redis on EC2 adds operational burden and is not a durable queue.
others.B: Kinesis is for high-throughput ordered streaming and has no built-in per-message dead-letter handling.
others.D: SNS is push-based with no message retention for long processing or failed-message isolation.

e.tip: Decouple + retain failures = SQS + DLQ.

q:
A solutions architect must design a solution that uses Amazon CloudFront with an Amazon S3 origin to store a static website. The company’s security policy requires that all website traffic be inspected by AWS WAF.

How should the solutions architect comply with these requirements?

o.A: Configure an S3 bucket policy to accept requests coming from the AWS WAF Amazon Resource Name (ARN) only.
o.B: Configure Amazon CloudFront to forward all incoming requests to AWS WAF before requesting content from the S3 origin.
o.C: Configure a security group that allows Amazon CloudFront IP addresses to access Amazon S3 only. Associate AWS WAF to CloudFront.
o.D: Configure Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3 to use an origin access identity (OAI) to restrict access to the S3 bucket. Enable AWS WAF on the distribution.

e.why: AWS WAF is associated directly with the CloudFront distribution, so every viewer request is inspected. An OAI (now OAC) restricts the S3 bucket so it can be reached only through CloudFront, preventing anyone from bypassing WAF via the S3 URL.

others.A: S3 bucket policies cannot reference a WAF ARN as a principal.
others.B: CloudFront does not forward requests to WAF; WAF is attached to the distribution as a web ACL.
others.C: Security groups cannot be applied to S3 buckets.

e.tip: WAF on CloudFront + OAC so the origin cannot be bypassed.

q:
Organizers for a global event want to put daily reports online as static HTML pages. The pages are expected to generate millions of views from users around the world. The files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. A solutions architect has been asked to design an efficient and effective solution.

Which action should the solutions architect take to accomplish this?

o.A: Generate presigned URLs for the files.
o.B: Use cross-Region replication to all Regions.
o.C: Use the geoproximity feature of Amazon Route 53.
o.D: Use Amazon CloudFront with the S3 bucket as its origin.

e.why: CloudFront with the S3 bucket as origin caches the static HTML at edge locations worldwide. It handles millions of views with low latency and reduces S3 request costs.

others.A: Presigned URLs grant temporary access to private objects but do nothing for global performance.
others.B: Replicating to every Region is costly and complex and still lacks edge caching.
others.C: Route 53 geoproximity routing needs multiple endpoints and provides no caching.

e.tip: Static content, global audience = CloudFront + S3.

q:
A company runs a production application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application reads the data from an Amazon SQS queue and processes the messages in parallel. The message volume is unpredictable and often has intermittent traffic. This application should continually process messages without any downtime.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use Spot Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
o.B: Use Reserved Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
o.C: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use Spot Instances to handle additional capacity.
o.D: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use On-Demand Instances to handle additional capacity.

e.why: Reserved Instances cover the steady baseline at a discount, while On-Demand Instances handle unpredictable extra capacity without interruption risk. This meets the 'continually process without downtime' requirement.

others.A: Spot-only capacity can be reclaimed at any time, risking downtime.
others.B: Reserving for maximum capacity wastes money during intermittent low traffic.
others.C: Spot for additional capacity is cheaper but can be interrupted, and the keyed answer prioritizes no downtime.

e.tip: Interruption must be avoided = On-Demand rather than Spot for burst capacity.
e.flag: SQS consumers are idempotent-friendly and interruptions just return messages to the queue, so many argue C (RIs + Spot) is more cost-effective without real downtime.

q:
A security team wants to limit access to specific services or actions in all of the team’s AWS accounts. All accounts belong to a large organization in AWS Organizations. The solution must be scalable and there must be a single point where permissions can be maintained.

What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this?

o.A: Create an ACL to provide access to the services or actions.
o.B: Create a security group to allow accounts and attach it to user groups.
o.C: Create cross-account roles in each account to deny access to the services or actions.
o.D: Create a service control policy in the root organizational unit to deny access to the services or actions.

e.why: A service control policy attached to the root OU applies to every account in the organization. It sets maximum permissions centrally, so denying specific services or actions there is scalable and maintained in one place.

others.A: Network ACLs control subnet traffic, not access to AWS services or API actions.
others.B: Security groups control network traffic to resources and cannot be attached to users or accounts.
others.C: Roles in each account are not a single point of maintenance and do not inherently restrict other principals.

e.tip: Restrict all accounts centrally = SCP.

q:
A company is concerned about the security of its public web application due to recent web attacks. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A solutions architect must reduce the risk of DDoS attacks against the application.

What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.A: Add an Amazon Inspector agent to the ALB.
o.B: Configure Amazon Macie to prevent attacks.
o.C: Enable AWS Shield Advanced to prevent attacks.
o.D: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor the ALB.

fixed: Option B contained answer text instead of option text, and options A and D were truncated; they have been reconstructed.

e.why: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS detection and mitigation for ALBs, CloudFront, Route 53 and Global Accelerator. It adds 24/7 Shield Response Team support, cost protection and automatic application-layer mitigation through AWS WAF.

others.A: Amazon Inspector scans EC2, containers and Lambda for vulnerabilities; it is not installed on an ALB and does not stop DDoS.
others.B: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in S3; it does not prevent attacks.
others.D: GuardDuty detects threats from logs but does not mitigate DDoS attacks.

e.tip: DDoS protection beyond the default = AWS Shield Advanced.

q:
A company’s web application is running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The company recently changed its policy, which now requires the application to be accessed from one specific country only.

Which configuration will meet this requirement?

o.A: Configure the security group for the EC2 instances.
o.B: Configure the security group on the Application Load Balancer.
o.C: Configure AWS WAF on the Application Load Balancer in a VPC.
o.D: Configure the network ACL for the subnet that contains the EC2 instances.

fixed: Option C text was missing and has been reconstructed.

e.why: AWS WAF on the ALB supports geographic match rules, so a web ACL can allow requests from the one approved country and block all others. Security groups and network ACLs work only on IP addresses and ports and cannot match by country.

others.A: Security groups cannot filter by country, and instances behind the ALB see the ALB as the source.
others.B: ALB security groups only allow IP ranges and ports, not geographic locations.
others.D: Network ACLs filter by IP and port only and would need an unmanageable list of country IP ranges.

e.tip: Allow or block by country = AWS WAF geo match (or CloudFront geo restriction).

q:
A company provides an API to its users that automates inquiries for tax computations based on item prices. The company experiences a larger number of inquiries during the holiday season only that cause slower response times. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that is scalable and elastic.

What should the solutions architect do to accomplish this?

o.A: Provide an API hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance performs the required computations when the API request is made.
o.B: Design a REST API using Amazon API Gateway that accepts the item names. API Gateway passes item names to AWS Lambda for tax computations.
o.C: Create an Application Load Balancer that has two Amazon EC2 instances behind it. The EC2 instances will compute the tax on the received item names.
o.D: Design a REST API using Amazon API Gateway that connects with an API hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance. API Gateway accepts and passes the item names to the EC2 instance for tax computations.

e.why: API Gateway with Lambda is serverless and scales automatically and elastically with the holiday spike. Capacity drops back when demand falls, and no instances need to be provisioned.

others.A: A single EC2 instance does not scale elastically and is a single point of failure.
others.C: Two fixed EC2 instances behind an ALB have no automatic scaling.
others.D: API Gateway in front of a single EC2 instance still bottlenecks on that instance.

e.tip: Elastic and scalable API with least management = API Gateway + Lambda.

q:
A solutions architect is creating a new Amazon CloudFront distribution for an application. Some of the information submitted by users is sensitive. The application uses HTTPS but needs another layer of security. The sensitive information should.be protected throughout the entire application stack, and access to the information should be restricted to certain applications.

Which action should the solutions architect take?

o.A: Configure a CloudFront signed URL.
o.B: Configure a CloudFront signed cookie.
o.C: Configure a CloudFront field-level encryption profile.
o.D: Configure CloudFront and set the Origin Protocol Policy setting to HTTPS Only for the Viewer Protocol Policy.

e.why: CloudFront field-level encryption encrypts specific sensitive POST fields at the edge with a public key. The data stays encrypted through the whole stack and only applications holding the private key can decrypt it, on top of HTTPS.

others.A: Signed URLs control who can access content, not protection of submitted data fields.
others.B: Signed cookies also control access to content and do not encrypt user-submitted data.
others.D: HTTPS-only protects data in transit between hops but not throughout the stack, and it is already in use.

e.tip: Protect specific sensitive form fields end to end = CloudFront field-level encryption.

q:
A gaming company hosts a browser-based application on AWS. The users of the application consume a large number of videos and images that are stored in Amazon S3. This content is the same for all users.

The application has increased in popularity, and millions of users worldwide accessing these media files. The company wants to provide the files to the users while reducing the load on the origin.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Deploy an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator in front of the web servers.
o.B: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront web distribution in front of the S3 bucket.
o.C: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis instance in front of the web servers.
o.D: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance in front of the web servers.

e.why: CloudFront caches the identical media files at edge locations globally, serving millions of users while greatly reducing origin requests. It is cost-effective because CloudFront data transfer out is often cheaper than direct S3 transfer.

others.A: Global Accelerator does not cache content, so origin load is not reduced.
others.C: ElastiCache for Redis is an in-memory cache for application data, not for global delivery of large media files.
others.D: Memcached has the same limitation and does not serve users at the edge.

e.tip: Reduce origin load for static media worldwide = CloudFront.

q:
A company has a multi-tier application that runs six front-end web servers in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A solutions architect needs to modify the infrastructure to be highly available without modifying the application.

Which architecture should the solutions architect choose that provides high availability?

o.A: Create an Auto Scaling group that uses three instances across each of two Regions.
o.B: Modify the Auto Scaling group to use three instances across each of two Availability Zones.
o.C: Create an Auto Scaling template that can be used to quickly create more instances in another Region.
o.D: Change the ALB in front of the Amazon EC2 instances in a round-robin configuration to balance traffic to the web tier.

e.why: Spreading the existing Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones (three instances in each) behind the same ALB survives an AZ failure. No application change is needed because ALB and Auto Scaling are natively multi-AZ.

others.A: An Auto Scaling group cannot span Regions, and multi-Region requires more redesign.
others.C: A template for manual launches in another Region is not automatic high availability.
others.D: Changing the routing algorithm does not remove the single-AZ point of failure.

e.tip: High availability within a Region = Multi-AZ.

q:
An ecommerce company has an order-processing application that uses Amazon API Gateway and an AWS Lambda function. The application stores data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database. During a recent sales event, a sudden surge in customer orders occurred. Some customers experienced timeouts, and the application did not process the orders of those customers.

A solutions architect determined that the CPU utilization and memory utilization were high on the database because of a large number of open connections. The solutions architect needs to prevent the timeout errors while making the least possible changes to the application.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function. Modify the database to be a global database in multiple AWS Regions.
o.B: Use Amazon RDS Proxy to create a proxy for the database. Modify the Lambda function to use the RDS Proxy endpoint instead of the database endpoint.
o.C: Create a read replica for the database in a different AWS Region. Use query string parameters in API Gateway to route traffic to the read replica.
o.D: Migrate the data from Aurora PostgreSQL to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Modify the Lambda function to use the DynamoDB table.

e.why: RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections, so a surge of Lambda invocations does not exhaust Aurora connections, CPU and memory. The only code change is pointing the function at the proxy endpoint.

others.A: Provisioned concurrency would create more connections, and a global database does not fix connection exhaustion.
others.C: Order processing involves writes, so a read replica does not help, and query-string routing requires application changes.
others.D: Migrating to DynamoDB is a major application rewrite.

e.tip: Lambda + RDS or Aurora 'too many connections' = RDS Proxy.

q:
An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. The application needs to access an Amazon DynamoDB table.

What is the MOST secure way to access the table while ensuring that the traffic does not leave the AWS network?

o.A: Use a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB.
o.B: Use a NAT gateway in a public subnet.
o.C: Use a NAT instance in a private subnet.
o.D: Use the internet gateway attached to the VPC.

fixed: Option C contained answer text instead of option text, and options A and D were truncated; they have been reconstructed.

e.why: A gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB keeps traffic from the private subnets on the AWS network without internet, NAT or public IP access. Endpoint policies can also restrict which tables are reachable, making it the most secure option at no extra charge.

others.B: A NAT gateway sends traffic to DynamoDB's public endpoint over the internet path.
others.C: A NAT instance still routes traffic to the public endpoint and is self-managed; it also cannot work from a private subnet.
others.D: Using the internet gateway sends traffic over the internet and requires public IPs.

e.tip: Private access to S3 or DynamoDB = gateway VPC endpoint.

q:
An entertainment company is using Amazon DynamoDB to store media metadata. The application is read intensive and experiencing delays. The company does not have staff to handle additional operational overhead and needs to improve the performance efficiency of DynamoDB without reconfiguring the application.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

o.A: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
o.B: Use Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
o.C: Replicate data by using DynamoDB global tables.
o.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with Auto Discovery enabled.

e.why: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, API-compatible in-memory cache for DynamoDB that delivers microsecond reads. The application keeps using DynamoDB API calls with minimal change and no cache logic to write.

others.A: ElastiCache for Redis requires application code to implement caching logic.
others.C: Global tables replicate across Regions for multi-Region availability, not read caching.
others.D: Memcached also requires application changes to manage the cache.

e.tip: Speed up DynamoDB reads without code changes = DAX.

q:
A company’s infrastructure consists of Amazon EC2 instances and an Amazon RDS DB instance in a single AWS Region. The company wants to back up its data in a separate Region.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Backup to copy EC2 backups and RDS backups to the separate Region.
o.B: Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to copy EC2 backups and RDS backups to the separate Region.
o.C: Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) of the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to the separate Region. Create a read replica for the RDS DB instance in the separate Region.
o.D: Create Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots. Copy the EBS snapshots to the separate Region. Create RDS snapshots. Export the RDS snapshots to Amazon S3. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to the separate Region.

e.why: AWS Backup centrally manages backups for both EC2 and RDS. A backup plan with a cross-Region copy rule automatically copies recovery points to another Region, giving the least operational overhead.

others.B: Data Lifecycle Manager handles EBS snapshots and AMIs but not RDS backups.
others.C: Manual AMI copying and running a read replica add effort and ongoing cost.
others.D: A multi-step snapshot, export and replication process has high operational overhead.

e.tip: Centralized, cross-Region backup for many services = AWS Backup.

q:
A solutions architect needs to securely store a database user name and password that an application uses to access an Amazon RDS DB instance. The application that accesses the database runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. The solutions architect wants to create a secure parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.

What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.A: Create an IAM role that has read access to the Parameter Store parameter. Allow Decrypt access to an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that is used to encrypt the parameter. Assign this IAM role to the EC2 instance.
o.B: Create an IAM policy that allows read access to the Parameter Store parameter. Allow Decrypt access to an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that is used to encrypt the parameter. Assign this IAM policy to the EC2 instance.
o.C: Create an IAM trust relationship between the Parameter Store parameter and the EC2 instance. Specify Amazon RDS as a principal in the trust policy.
o.D: Create an IAM trust relationship between the DB instance and the EC2 instance. Specify Systems Manager as a principal in the trust policy.

e.why: An IAM role attached to the EC2 instance (via an instance profile) supplies temporary credentials. The role needs ssm:GetParameter on the SecureString parameter and kms:Decrypt on the KMS key that encrypts it.

others.B: IAM policies cannot be attached directly to an EC2 instance; they must go through a role and instance profile.
others.C: Parameters are not principals for trust relationships, and RDS is not the caller.
others.D: A trust relationship between a DB instance and EC2 is not an IAM concept and grants no Parameter Store access.

e.tip: EC2 accessing AWS APIs = IAM role (instance profile), never keys.

q:
A company is designing a cloud communications platform that is driven by APIs. The application is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The company uses Amazon API Gateway to provide external users with access to the application through APIs. The company wants to protect the platform against web exploits like SQL injection and also wants to detect and mitigate large, sophisticated DDoS attacks.

Which combination of solutions provides the MOST protection? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use AWS WAF to protect the NLB.
o.B: Use AWS Shield Advanced with the NLB.
o.C: Use AWS WAF to protect Amazon API Gateway.
o.D: Use Amazon GuardDuty with AWS Shield Standard
o.E: Use AWS Shield Standard with Amazon API Gateway.

fixed: Option B text was missing and option A was truncated; both have been reconstructed.

e.why: AWS WAF on API Gateway blocks SQL injection and other web exploits at the API entry point. AWS Shield Advanced on the NLB adds detection and mitigation of large, sophisticated DDoS attacks, plus Shield Response Team support and cost protection.

others.A: AWS WAF cannot be associated with a Network Load Balancer.
others.D: GuardDuty detects threats but does not mitigate attacks, and Shield Standard only covers common infrastructure-layer DDoS.
others.E: Shield Standard is automatic and basic; it does not give advanced detection and mitigation of sophisticated DDoS attacks.

e.tip: SQL injection = AWS WAF; large sophisticated DDoS = Shield Advanced.

q:
A company has a legacy data processing application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Data is processed sequentially, but the order of results does not matter. The application uses a monolithic architecture. The only way that the company can scale the application to meet increased demand is to increase the size of the instances.

The company’s developers have decided to rewrite the application to use a microservices architecture on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).

What should a solutions architect recommend for communication between the microservices?

o.A: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Add code to the data producers, and send data to the queue. Add code to the data consumers to process data from the queue.
o.B: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Add code to the data producers, and publish notifications to the topic. Add code to the data consumers to subscribe to the topic.
o.C: Create an AWS Lambda function to pass messages. Add code to the data producers to call the Lambda function with a data object. Add code to the data consumers to receive a data object that is passed from the Lambda function.
o.D: Create an Amazon DynamoDB table. Enable DynamoDB Streams. Add code to the data producers to insert data into the table. Add code to the data consumers to use the DynamoDB Streams API to detect new table entries and retrieve the data.

e.why: An SQS queue decouples producers and consumers among microservices. Each message is processed by one consumer, consumers can scale horizontally on ECS, and ordering is not required, so a standard queue fits.

others.B: SNS fans out to every subscriber and does not buffer work for consumers to pull at their own pace.
others.C: A Lambda function used as a message relay is not a messaging service, offers no buffering, and couples the services.
others.D: DynamoDB Streams retain data only 24 hours and is a workaround, not a purpose-built work queue.

e.tip: Decouple producers and consumers, order not needed = SQS standard.

q:
A company wants to migrate its MySQL database from on premises to AWS. The company recently experienced a database outage that significantly impacted the business. To ensure this does not happen again, the company wants a reliable database solution on AWS that minimizes data loss and stores every transaction on at least two nodes.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance with synchronous replication to three nodes in three Availability Zones.
o.B: Create an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance with Multi-AZ functionality enabled to synchronously replicate the data.
o.C: Create an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance and then create a read replica in a separate AWS Region that synchronously replicates the data.
o.D: Create an Amazon EC2 instance with a MySQL engine installed that triggers an AWS Lambda function to synchronously replicate the data to an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance.

e.why: RDS MySQL Multi-AZ synchronously replicates every transaction to a standby in another AZ before acknowledging the commit, so each transaction exists on at least two nodes. Failover is automatic, which minimizes data loss.

others.A: Standard RDS does not offer synchronous replication to three nodes, and no engine is specified.
others.C: Read replicas use asynchronous replication.
others.D: A custom Lambda replication scheme is unreliable, complex and not truly synchronous.

e.tip: Synchronous replication = Multi-AZ; read replicas = asynchronous.

q:
A company is building a new dynamic ordering website. The company wants to minimize server maintenance and patching. The website must be highly available and must scale read and write capacity as quickly as possible to meet changes in user demand.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Host static content in Amazon S3. Host dynamic content by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Use Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity for the database. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver the website content.
o.B: Host static content in Amazon S3. Host dynamic content by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Use Amazon Aurora with Aurora Auto Scaling for the database. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver the website content.
o.C: Host all the website content on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group to scale the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Use Amazon DynamoDB with provisioned write capacity for the database.
o.D: Host all the website content on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group to scale the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Use Amazon Aurora with Aurora Auto Scaling for the database.

e.why: S3, CloudFront, API Gateway, Lambda and DynamoDB are all serverless, so there is no patching. DynamoDB on-demand capacity instantly scales both reads and writes, whereas Aurora Auto Scaling only adds read replicas.

others.B: Aurora Auto Scaling adds Aurora Replicas, which scale reads only, and replicas take minutes to add.
others.C: EC2 requires patching, and provisioned write capacity does not scale as quickly as on-demand.
others.D: EC2 requires server maintenance, and Aurora Auto Scaling does not scale write capacity.

e.tip: Scale both reads and writes instantly, serverless = DynamoDB on-demand.

q:
A company has an AWS account used for software engineering. The AWS account has access to the company’s on-premises data center through a pair of AWS Direct Connect connections. All non-VPC traffic routes to the virtual private gateway.

A development team recently created an AWS Lambda function through the console. The development team needs to allow the function to access a database that runs in a private subnet in the company’s data center.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure the Lambda function to run in the VPC with the appropriate security group.
o.B: Set up a VPN connection from AWS to the data center. Route the traffic from the Lambda function through the VPN.
o.C: Update the route tables in the VPC to allow the Lambda function to access the on-premises data center through Direct Connect.
o.D: Create an Elastic IP address. Configure the Lambda function to send traffic through the Elastic IP address without an elastic network interface.

e.why: A console-created Lambda function runs in the AWS-managed network with no route to on premises. Attaching it to the VPC (private subnets plus a security group) gives it ENIs in subnets whose routes already send traffic through the virtual private gateway and Direct Connect.

others.B: Direct Connect already provides connectivity, and the function cannot use it until it is attached to the VPC.
others.C: Route tables do not affect a Lambda function that is not attached to the VPC.
others.D: Lambda cannot be assigned an Elastic IP, and public IPs would not reach a private data center.

e.tip: Lambda reaching private resources (VPC or on premises) = configure Lambda VPC access.

q:
A company runs an application using Amazon ECS. The application creates resized versions of an original image and then makes Amazon S3 API calls to store the resized images in Amazon S3.

How can a solutions architect ensure that the application has permission to access Amazon S3?

o.A: Update the S3 role in AWS IAM to allow read/write access from Amazon ECS, and then relaunch the container.
o.B: Create an IAM role with S3 permissions, and then specify that role as the taskRoleArn in the task definition.
o.C: Create a security group that allows access from Amazon ECS to Amazon S3, and update the launch configuration used by the ECS cluster.
o.D: Create an IAM user with S3 permissions, and then relaunch the Amazon EC2 instances for the ECS cluster while logged in as this account.

e.why: ECS task IAM roles (taskRoleArn in the task definition) provide temporary credentials to the containers in that task. This grants least-privilege S3 access to just that application.

others.A: There is no generic 'S3 role' to update, and the role must be attached to the task.
others.C: Security groups control network traffic, not IAM authorization to S3 APIs, and launch configurations are deprecated.
others.D: IAM users with long-term credentials are not how ECS tasks are authorized.

e.tip: Container permissions = task role (taskRoleArn); the execution role is for pulling images and logs.

q:
A company has a Windows-based application that must be migrated to AWS. The application requires the use of a shared Windows file system attached to multiple Amazon EC2 Windows instances that are deployed across multiple Availability Zone:

What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.A: Configure AWS Storage Gateway in volume gateway mode. Mount the volume to each Windows instance.
o.B: Configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Mount the Amazon FSx file system to each Windows instance.
