o.C: Configure a file system by using Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS file system to each Windows instance.
o.D: Configure an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume with the required size. Attach each EC2 instance to the volume. Mount the file system within the volume to each Windows instance.

e.why: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides a fully managed native SMB file share with Active Directory integration. It supports Multi-AZ deployment, so many Windows instances across AZs can share it.

others.A: Volume gateway presents iSCSI block volumes for on-premises backup, not a shared multi-instance file system.
others.C: Amazon EFS uses NFS and is not supported on Windows instances.
others.D: EBS volumes are AZ-scoped, and Multi-Attach does not provide a shared Windows file system across AZs.

e.tip: Shared Windows SMB storage = FSx for Windows File Server; Linux NFS = EFS.

q:
A company is developing an ecommerce application that will consist of a load-balanced front end, a container-based application, and a relational database. A solutions architect needs to create a highly available solution that operates with as little manual intervention as possible.

Which solutions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance in Multi-AZ mode.
o.B: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance and one or more replicas in another Availability Zone.
o.C: Create an Amazon EC2 instance-based Docker cluster to handle the dynamic application load.
o.D: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with a Fargate launch type to handle the dynamic application load.
o.E: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an Amazon EC2 launch type to handle the dynamic application load.

e.why: RDS Multi-AZ gives automatic failover for the relational database without manual action. ECS on Fargate runs the containers across AZs without managing servers, so both tiers need minimal manual intervention.

others.B: Read replicas need manual promotion and are not an automatic HA mechanism.
others.C: A self-managed Docker cluster on EC2 needs significant manual operation.
others.E: The EC2 launch type requires managing container instances, so it is more manual than Fargate.

e.tip: HA database = Multi-AZ; least-management containers = Fargate.

q:
A company uses Amazon S3 as its data lake. The company has a new partner that must use SFTP to upload data files. A solutions architect needs to implement a highly available SFTP solution that minimizes operational overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Transfer Family to configure an SFTP-enabled server with a publicly accessible endpoint. Choose the S3 data lake as the destination.
o.B: Use Amazon S3 File Gateway as an SFTP server. Expose the S3 File Gateway endpoint URL to the new partner. Share the S3 File Gateway endpoint with the new partner.
o.C: Launch Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet in a VPC. Instruct the new partner to upload files to the EC2 instances by using a VPN. Run a cron job script on the EC2 instances to upload files to the S3 data lake.
o.D: Launch Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet in a VPC. Place a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the EC2 instances. Create an SFTP listener port for the NLB. Share the NLB hostname with the new partner. Run a cron job script on the EC2 instances to upload files to the S3 data lake.

fixed: Options B, C and D were garbled by text splitting and have been reconstructed.

e.why: AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed, highly available SFTP endpoint that writes uploaded files directly to an S3 bucket. There are no servers, scripts or load balancers to run, which minimizes operational overhead.

others.B: S3 File Gateway exposes NFS and SMB shares, not SFTP.
others.C: Self-managed EC2 instances, a VPN and cron scripts add a lot of operational overhead.
others.D: An NLB with EC2 SFTP servers and cron scripts works but has far more overhead than a managed service.

e.tip: Managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP into S3 or EFS = AWS Transfer Family.

q:
A company needs to store contract documents. A contract lasts for 5 years. During the 5-year period, the company must ensure that the documents cannot be overwritten or deleted. The company needs to encrypt the documents at rest and rotate the encryption keys automatically every year.

Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

o.A: Store the documents in Amazon S3. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode.
o.B: Store the documents in Amazon S3. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode.
o.C: Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Configure key rotation.
o.D: Use server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys. Configure key rotation.
o.E: Use server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer provided (imported) keys. Configure key rotation.

e.why: Object Lock in compliance mode prevents any overwrite or delete during the 5-year retention, even by root. SSE-KMS with a customer managed key supports automatic annual key rotation, which you can enable and control.

others.A: Governance mode can be bypassed by users with special permissions, so it does not guarantee immutability.
others.C: SSE-S3 keys are managed and rotated by AWS, and you cannot configure or audit a rotation schedule.
others.E: Imported key material cannot be rotated automatically; rotation must be done manually.

e.tip: Automatic yearly rotation you control = KMS customer managed key.

q:
A company has a web application that is based on Java and PHP. The company plans to move the application from on premises to AWS. The company needs the ability to test new site features frequently. The company also needs a highly available and managed solution that requires minimum operational overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable static web hosting on the S3 bucket. Upload the static content to the S3 bucket. Use AWS Lambda to process all dynamic content.
o.B: Deploy the web application to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment. Use URL swapping to switch between multiple Elastic Beanstalk environments for feature testing.
o.C: Deploy the web application to Amazon EC2 instances that are configured with Java and PHP. Use Auto Scaling groups and an Application Load Balancer to manage the website’s availability.
o.D: Containerize the web application. Deploy the web application to Amazon EC2 instances. Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to dynamically route traffic between containers that contain the new site features for testing.

e.why: Elastic Beanstalk is a managed platform for Java and PHP that handles provisioning, load balancing, Auto Scaling and Multi-AZ. Swapping environment URLs (CNAME swap) enables blue/green testing of new features with minimal operational overhead.

others.A: S3 static hosting plus Lambda requires rewriting the Java and PHP app.
others.C: Self-managed EC2 with Auto Scaling and an ALB involves more operational work and has no built-in feature-testing workflow.
others.D: The AWS Load Balancer Controller is for Kubernetes (EKS), and containerizing adds work.

e.tip: Managed web app platform with blue/green = Elastic Beanstalk URL swap.

q:
A company has an ordering application that stores customer information in Amazon RDS for MySQL. During regular business hours, employees run one-time queries for reporting purposes. Timeouts are occurring during order processing because the reporting queries are taking a long time to run. The company needs to eliminate the timeouts without preventing employees from performing queries.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a read replica. Move reporting queries to the read replica.
o.B: Create a read replica. Distribute the ordering application to the primary DB instance and the read replica.
o.C: Migrate the ordering application to Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
o.D: Schedule the reporting queries for non-peak hours.

e.why: A read replica offloads the long-running reporting queries from the primary, so order writes no longer time out while employees can still query current data at any time.

others.B: Ordering is write-heavy, and writes cannot go to a read replica.
others.C: Migrating to DynamoDB is a major rewrite and does not suit ad hoc SQL reporting.
others.D: Scheduling reports for off-peak hours prevents employees from running queries when they need them.

e.tip: Separate reporting from OLTP = read replica.

q:
A hospital wants to create digital copies for its large collection of historical written records. The hospital will continue to add hundreds of new documents each day. The hospital’s data team will scan the documents and will upload the documents to the AWS Cloud.

A solutions architect must implement a solution to analyze the documents, extract the medical information, and store the documents so that an application can run SQL queries on the data. The solution must maximize scalability and operational efficiency.

Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Write the document information to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs a MySQL database.
o.B: Write the document information to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
o.C: Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to run a custom application that processes the scanned files and extracts the medical information.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Rekognition to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Transcribe Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text.
o.E: Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Textract to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text.

e.why: Lambda triggered on upload uses Amazon Textract to extract text from scanned documents and Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify medical entities. The results go to S3 and Athena runs serverless SQL over them, making the solution scalable and operationally efficient.

others.A: MySQL on a single EC2 instance is not scalable and requires management.
others.C: A custom extraction app on EC2 Auto Scaling adds development and operations effort.
others.D: Rekognition targets images and video rather than document text, and Transcribe Medical converts speech, not text.

e.tip: Text from scans = Textract; medical entities = Comprehend Medical; audio = Transcribe.

q:
A company is running a batch application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application consists of a backend with multiple Amazon RDS databases. The application is causing a high number of reads on the databases. A solutions architect must reduce the number of database reads while ensuring high availability.

What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.A: Add Amazon RDS read replicas.
o.B: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
o.C: Use Amazon Route 53 DNS caching
o.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached.

e.why: The keyed answer adds RDS read replicas, which absorb read traffic away from the primary databases and can be promoted, supporting availability. This reduces the read load on each primary without application caching logic.

others.B: ElastiCache for Redis would cache results but requires application changes to implement caching (the keyed answer prefers replicas).
others.C: Route 53 DNS caching caches name resolution, not database query results.
others.D: Memcached has no replication or failover, so it does not ensure high availability.

e.tip: 'Reduce reads on the DB' often hints at caching; 'scale reads' hints at replicas.
e.flag: Read replicas spread reads rather than reduce them; ElastiCache for Redis (B) with Multi-AZ replication actually reduces database reads while staying highly available, so B is arguably correct (41% community vote).

q:
A company needs to run a critical application on AWS. The company needs to use Amazon EC2 for the application’s database. The database must be highly available and must fail over automatically if a disruptive event occurs.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Launch two EC2 instances, each in a different Availability Zone in the same AWS Region. Install the database on both EC2 instances. Configure the EC2 instances as a cluster. Set up database replication.
o.B: Launch an EC2 instance in an Availability Zone. Install the database on the EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) to back up the data. Use AWS CloudFormation to automate provisioning of the EC2 instance if a disruptive event occurs.
o.C: Launch two EC2 instances, each in a different AWS Region. Install the database on both EC2 instances. Set up database replication. Fail over the database to a second Region.
o.D: Launch an EC2 instance in an Availability Zone. Install the database on the EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) to back up the data. Use EC2 automatic recovery to recover the instance if a disruptive event occurs.

e.why: Two EC2 database instances in different AZs within one Region, configured as a cluster with replication, can fail over automatically to the surviving node during an AZ disruption. That gives high availability on EC2.

others.B: Re-provisioning from an AMI with CloudFormation is backup and restore, not automatic failover, and loses data.
others.C: Cross-Region replication adds latency and complexity and is DR rather than automatic HA.
others.D: EC2 auto recovery handles only underlying host failures in the same AZ and does not protect against AZ events.

e.tip: HA = multi-AZ within a Region; DR = multi-Region.

q:
A company’s order system sends requests from clients to Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances process the orders and then store the orders in a database on Amazon RDS. Users report that they must reprocess orders when the system fails. The company wants a resilient solution that can process orders automatically if a system outage occurs.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to target an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task.
o.B: Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Update the order system to send messages to the ALB endpoint.
o.C: Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group. Configure the order system to send messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure the EC2 instances to consume messages from the queue.
o.D: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Create an AWS Lambda function, and subscribe the function to the SNS topic. Configure the order system to send messages to the SNS topic. Send a command to the EC2 instances to process the messages by using AWS Systems Manager Run Command.

e.why: Placing an SQS queue between the order system and the EC2 workers (in an Auto Scaling group) makes orders durable. If instances fail, messages remain in the queue and are processed automatically after the visibility timeout or by replacement instances.

others.A: An EventBridge rule targeting ECS does not buffer orders or link to the existing processing.
others.B: An ALB distributes requests but does not persist them, so in-flight orders are lost when instances fail.
others.D: SNS, Lambda and Run Command is convoluted and has no durable buffering or retries for the EC2 processing.

e.tip: Do not lose work during outages = queue (SQS) between tiers.

q:
A company runs an application on a large fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application reads and writes entries into an Amazon DynamoDB table. The size of the DynamoDB table continuously grows, but the application needs only data from the last 30 days. The company needs a solution that minimizes cost and development effort.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Use an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the complete solution. Redeploy the CloudFormation stack every 30 days, and delete the original stack.
o.B: Use an EC2 instance that runs a monitoring application from AWS Marketplace. Configure the monitoring application to use Amazon DynamoDB Streams to store the timestamp when a new item is created in the table. Use a script that runs on the EC2 instance to delete items that have a timestamp that is older than 30 days.
o.C: Configure Amazon DynamoDB Streams to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a new item is created in the table. Configure the Lambda function to delete items in the table that are older than 30 days.
o.D: Extend the application to add an attribute that has a value of the current timestamp plus 30 days to each new item that is created in the table. Configure DynamoDB to use the attribute as the TTL attribute.

e.why: DynamoDB Time to Live automatically deletes items after the epoch timestamp in a designated attribute at no extra cost (TTL deletes consume no write capacity). The only development effort is adding a timestamp of now plus 30 days to new items.

others.A: Redeploying stacks would destroy the table and all data, which is disruptive and wrong.
others.B: A Marketplace monitoring app on EC2 with scripts adds cost and maintenance.
others.C: Lambda deletion logic consumes write capacity and invocation costs and requires custom code.

e.tip: Auto-expire DynamoDB items = TTL.

q:
A company has a Microsoft .NET application that runs on an on-premises Windows Server. The application stores data by using an Oracle Database Standard Edition server. The company is planning a migration to AWS and wants to minimize development changes while moving the application. The AWS application environment should be highly available.

Which combination of actions should the company take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Refactor the application as serverless with AWS Lambda functions running .NET Core.
o.B: Rehost the application in AWS Elastic Beanstalk with the .NET platform in a Multi-AZ deployment.
o.C: Replatform the application to run on Amazon EC2 with the Amazon Linux Amazon Machine Image (AMI).
o.D: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate from the Oracle database to Amazon DynamoDB in a Multi-AZ deployment.
o.E: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate from the Oracle database to Oracle on Amazon RDS in a Multi-AZ deployment.

e.why: Rehosting the .NET app on Elastic Beanstalk's Windows .NET platform across multiple AZs requires minimal code change and is highly available. Migrating Oracle to RDS for Oracle Multi-AZ with DMS keeps the same engine and provides automatic failover.

others.A: Refactoring to Lambda requires significant development changes.
others.C: A .NET Framework app built for Windows Server would need porting to run on Amazon Linux.
others.D: Moving from Oracle to DynamoDB requires a major data model and code rewrite.

e.tip: Minimize changes = keep the same engine and platform (rehost or replatform).

q:
A company runs a containerized application on a Kubernetes cluster in an on-premises data center. The company is using a MongoDB database for data storage. The company wants to migrate some of these environments to AWS, but no code changes or deployment method changes are possible at this time. The company needs a solution that minimizes operational overhead.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes for compute and MongoDB on EC2 for data storage.
o.B: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate for compute and Amazon DynamoDB for data storage
o.C: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes for compute and Amazon DynamoDB for data storage.
o.D: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate for compute and Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) for data storage.

e.why: Amazon EKS runs the existing Kubernetes manifests and deployment methods unchanged, and Fargate removes worker-node management. Amazon DocumentDB is MongoDB-compatible, so the application code does not change and operational overhead is minimal.

others.A: ECS changes the deployment method away from Kubernetes, and MongoDB on EC2 is self-managed.
others.B: ECS changes the deployment method, and DynamoDB would require code changes.
others.C: DynamoDB is not MongoDB-compatible, and EC2 worker nodes add management overhead.

e.tip: Kubernetes = EKS; MongoDB = DocumentDB.

q:
A telemarketing company is designing its customer call center functionality on AWS. The company needs a solution that provides multiple speaker recognition and generates transcript files. The company wants to query the transcript files to analyze the business patterns. The transcript files must be stored for 7 years for auditing purposes.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon Rekognition for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon S3. Use machine learning models for transcript file analysis.
o.B: Use Amazon Transcribe for multiple speaker recognition. Use Amazon Athena for transcript file analysis.
o.C: Use Amazon Translate for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon Redshift. Use SQL queries for transcript file analysis.
o.D: Use Amazon Rekognition for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Textract for transcript file analysis.

e.why: Amazon Transcribe converts call audio to text and supports speaker diarization (identifying multiple speakers). The transcripts are stored in S3, where Athena can query them with SQL, and S3 retention or Lifecycle rules keep them for 7 years.

others.A: Rekognition analyzes images and video, not speech, so it cannot recognize speakers in audio.
others.C: Translate converts text between languages and does not recognize speakers or transcribe audio.
others.D: Rekognition cannot transcribe audio, and Textract extracts text from documents rather than analyzing transcripts.

e.tip: Speech to text with speaker labels = Transcribe.

q:
A company hosts its application on AWS. The company uses Amazon Cognito to manage users. When users log in to the application, the application fetches required data from Amazon DynamoDB by using a REST API that is hosted in Amazon API Gateway. The company wants an AWS managed solution that will control access to the REST API to reduce development efforts.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Configure an AWS Lambda function to be an authorizer in API Gateway to validate which user made the request.
o.B: For each user, create and assign an API key that must be sent with each request. Validate the key by using an AWS Lambda function.
o.C: Send the user’s email address in the header with every request. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to validate that the user with that email address has proper access.
o.D: Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool authorizer in API Gateway to allow Amazon Cognito to validate each request.

e.why: API Gateway has a built-in Amazon Cognito user pool authorizer that validates the users' JWT tokens on each request. It is AWS managed and needs no custom code, so it has the least operational overhead.

others.A: A Lambda authorizer requires writing and maintaining custom validation code.
others.B: API keys are for usage plans and metering, not user authentication, and Lambda validation adds code.
others.C: Trusting an email header is insecure and requires custom Lambda logic.

e.tip: Cognito users + API Gateway = Cognito user pool authorizer.

q:
A company is developing a marketing communications service that targets mobile app users. The company needs to send confirmation messages with Short Message Service (SMS) to its users. The users must be able to reply to the SMS messages. The company must store the responses for a year for analysis.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon Connect contact flow to send the SMS messages. Use AWS Lambda to process the responses.
o.B: Build an Amazon Pinpoint journey. Configure Amazon Pinpoint to send events to an Amazon Kinesis data stream for analysis and archiving.
o.C: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to distribute the SMS messages. Use AWS Lambda to process the responses.
o.D: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) FIFO topic. Subscribe an Amazon Kinesis data stream to the SNS topic for analysis and archiving.

e.why: Amazon Pinpoint (now AWS End User Messaging for SMS) supports two-way SMS, so users can reply. Journeys handle the messaging, and event streaming to Kinesis lets responses be archived and analyzed for a year.

others.A: Amazon Connect is a contact center service, not the right tool for marketing SMS campaigns with stored responses.
others.C: SQS is a message queue and cannot send SMS to phones.
others.D: SNS FIFO topics do not deliver SMS, and SNS SMS does not natively capture two-way replies for analysis.

e.tip: Two-way SMS or marketing campaigns = Pinpoint or End User Messaging.

q:
A company is planning to move its data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data must be encrypted when it is stored in the S3 bucket. Additionally, the encryption key must be automatically rotated every year.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Move the data to the S3 bucket. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Use the built-in key rotation behavior of SSE-S3 encryption keys.
o.B: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Enable automatic key rotation. Set the S3 bucket’s default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Move the data to the S3 bucket.
o.C: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Set the S3 bucket’s default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Move the data to the S3 bucket. Manually rotate the KMS key every year.
o.D: Encrypt the data with customer key material before moving the data to the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key without key material. Import the customer key material into the KMS key. Enable automatic key rotation.

e.why: The keyed answer relies on SSE-S3, which encrypts all objects at rest with AWS managed keys that AWS rotates automatically. It needs no key creation or configuration, so it has the least operational overhead.

others.B: A KMS customer managed key with automatic rotation works but adds key management and KMS request costs.
others.C: Manual rotation adds operational overhead.
others.D: Imported key material cannot be rotated automatically and requires client-side encryption effort.

e.tip: SSE-S3 = zero management; KMS CMK = you control and audit rotation.
e.flag: AWS does not document a guaranteed yearly rotation for SSE-S3 keys, whereas a KMS customer managed key with automatic rotation verifiably rotates yearly, so B arguably meets the explicit requirement better.

q:
The customers of a finance company request appointments with financial advisors by sending text messages. A web application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances accepts the appointment requests. The text messages are published to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue through the web application. Another application that runs on EC2 instances then sends meeting invitations and meeting confirmation email messages to the customers. After successful scheduling, this application stores the meeting information in an Amazon DynamoDB database.

As the company expands, customers report that their meeting invitations are taking longer to arrive.

What should a solutions architect recommend to resolve this issue?

o.A: Add a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster in front of the DynamoDB database.
o.B: Add an Amazon API Gateway API in front of the web application that accepts the appointment requests.
o.C: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the origin as the web application that accepts the appointment requests.
o.D: Add an Auto Scaling group for the application that sends meeting invitations. Configure the Auto Scaling group to scale based on the depth of the SQS queue.

e.why: The bottleneck is the invitation-sending consumers falling behind on the SQS queue. An Auto Scaling group that scales on queue depth (ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible or backlog per instance) adds consumers as messages pile up, cutting delivery delay.

others.A: DAX speeds DynamoDB reads, but the delay is in processing the queue, not database reads.
others.B: API Gateway in front of the intake app does not speed up downstream processing.
others.C: CloudFront caching does not help the queue-consuming application process messages faster.

e.tip: SQS consumers lagging = scale workers on queue depth.

q:
An online retail company has more than 50 million active customers and receives more than 25,000 orders each day. The company collects purchase data for customers and stores this data in Amazon S3. Additional customer data is stored in Amazon RDS.

The company wants to make all the data available to various teams so that the teams can perform analytics. The solution must provide the ability to manage fine-grained permissions for the data and must minimize operational overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate the purchase data to write directly to Amazon RDS. Use RDS access controls to limit access.
o.B: Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically copy data from Amazon RDS to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue crawler. Use Amazon Athena to query the data. Use S3 policies to limit access.
o.C: Create a data lake by using AWS Lake Formation. Create an AWS Glue JDBC connection to Amazon RDS. Register the S3 bucket in Lake Formation. Use Lake Formation access controls to limit access.
o.D: Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically copy data from Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS to Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon Redshift access controls to limit access.

e.why: AWS Lake Formation builds a governed data lake over S3 and, via a Glue JDBC connection, the RDS data. It provides centralized fine-grained (database, table, column and row level) permissions for many teams with minimal operational overhead.

others.A: Moving purchase data into RDS does not scale for analytics and RDS access controls are coarse for analysts.
others.B: S3 bucket policies cannot provide table- or column-level permissions, and custom copy Lambdas add overhead.
others.D: A Redshift cluster with custom copy jobs adds cost and operational overhead.

e.tip: Fine-grained permissions on a data lake = Lake Formation.

q:
A company hosts a marketing website in an on-premises data center. The website consists of static documents and runs on a single server. An administrator updates the website content infrequently and uses an SFTP client to upload new documents.

The company decides to host its website on AWS and to use Amazon CloudFront. The company’s solutions architect creates a CloudFront distribution. The solutions architect must design the most cost-effective and resilient architecture for website hosting to serve as the CloudFront origin.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a virtual server by using Amazon Lightsail. Configure the web server in the Lightsail instance. Upload website content by using an SFTP client.
o.B: Create an AWS Auto Scaling group for Amazon EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer. Upload website content by using an SFTP client.
o.C: Create a private Amazon S3 bucket. Use an S3 bucket policy to allow access from a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI). Upload website content by using the AWS CLI.
o.D: Create a public Amazon S3 bucket. Configure AWS Transfer for SFTP. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting. Upload website content by using the SFTP client.

e.why: A private S3 bucket serving as the CloudFront origin, accessible only through an OAI (now OAC), is the cheapest and most resilient way to host static documents. S3 is durable and serverless, and infrequent updates via the AWS CLI cost nothing extra.

others.A: A single Lightsail instance is a single point of failure.
others.B: An EC2 Auto Scaling group and ALB are costly overkill for static content.
others.D: Transfer Family SFTP endpoints carry an hourly charge, and a public bucket is less secure.

e.tip: Static site behind CloudFront = private S3 + OAC.

q:
A company wants to manage Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). The company currently copies AMIs to the same AWS Region where the AMIs were created. The company needs to design an application that captures AWS API calls and sends alerts whenever the Amazon EC2 CreateImage API operation is called within the company’s account.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to query AWS CloudTrail logs and to send an alert when a CreateImage API call is detected.
o.B: Configure AWS CloudTrail with an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification that occurs when updated logs are sent to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to create a new table and to query on CreateImage when an API call is detected.
o.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for the CreateImage API call. Configure the target as an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an alert when a CreateImage API call is detected.
o.D: Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue as a target for AWS CloudTrail logs. Create an AWS Lambda function to send an alert to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when a CreateImage API call is detected.

e.why: EventBridge receives CloudTrail-recorded management events such as ec2:CreateImage in near real time. A rule matching that API call can target an SNS topic for alerts with no code, which is the least operational overhead.

others.A: A custom Lambda function polling CloudTrail logs adds code and delay.
others.B: Querying with Athena after log delivery is slow and needs manual or scheduled queries.
others.D: CloudTrail cannot target SQS directly, and custom Lambda logic adds overhead.

e.tip: React to a specific API call = EventBridge rule on CloudTrail events.

q:
A company owns an asynchronous API that is used to ingest user requests and, based on the request type, dispatch requests to the appropriate microservice for processing. The company is using Amazon API Gateway to deploy the API front end, and an AWS Lambda function that invokes Amazon DynamoDB to store user requests before dispatching them to the processing microservices.

The company provisioned as much DynamoDB throughput as its budget allows, but the company is still experiencing availability issues and is losing user requests.

What should a solutions architect do to address this issue without impacting existing users?

o.A: Add throttling on the API Gateway with server-side throttling limits.
o.B: Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.
o.C: Create a secondary index in DynamoDB for the table with the user requests.
o.D: Use the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.

fixed: Option B text was missing and option D was truncated; both have been reconstructed.

e.why: An SQS queue durably buffers incoming requests so bursts do not exceed DynamoDB's provisioned write throughput. Lambda then drains the queue at a controlled rate, so requests are no longer lost and existing users are not throttled.

others.A: Throttling at API Gateway would reject user requests, which impacts existing users.
others.B: DAX is a read cache; it does not buffer or absorb writes.
others.C: A secondary index adds write cost and does nothing to absorb write bursts.

e.tip: Protect a throughput-limited backend from bursts = put an SQS queue in front of it.

q:
A company needs to move data from an Amazon EC2 instance to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must ensure that no API calls and no data are routed through public internet routes. Only the EC2 instance can have access to upload data to the S3 bucket.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the subnet where the EC2 instance is located. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.
o.B: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the Availability Zone where the EC2 instance is located. Attach appropriate security groups to the endpoint. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.
o.C: Run the nslookup tool from inside the EC2 instance to obtain the private IP address of the S3 bucket’s service API endpoint. Create a route in the VPC route table to provide the EC2 instance with access to the S3 bucket. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.
o.D: Use the AWS provided, publicly available ip-ranges.json file to obtain the private IP address of the S3 bucket’s service API endpoint. Create a route in the VPC route table to provide the EC2 instance with access to the S3 bucket. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.

e.why: An interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) for S3 keeps API calls and data on private IPs within AWS. A bucket policy allowing only the EC2 instance's IAM role, optionally with an aws:SourceVpce condition, restricts upload access to that instance.

others.B: Gateway endpoints attach to route tables at the VPC level (not per AZ) and do not support security groups, so the option is technically wrong as written.
others.C: S3 endpoint IPs are public and change, and static routes do not provide private routing.
others.D: ip-ranges.json lists public IP ranges, and routing to them still traverses public routes.

e.tip: Gateway endpoint = route table, no SGs; interface endpoint = ENI with SGs.

q:
A solutions architect is designing the architecture of a new application being deployed to the AWS Cloud. The application will run on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances and will automatically scale across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances will scale up and down frequently throughout the day. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) will handle the load distribution. The architecture needs to support distributed session data management. The company is willing to make changes to code if needed.

What should the solutions architect do to ensure that the architecture supports distributed session data management?

o.A: Use Amazon ElastiCache to manage and store session data.
o.B: Use session affinity (sticky sessions) of the ALB to manage session data.
o.C: Use Session Manager from AWS Systems Manager to manage the session.
o.D: Use the GetSessionToken API operation in AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to manage the session.

e.why: With instances scaling in and out frequently, session state must live outside the instances. Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) provides a fast, shared, distributed session store that every instance can read.

others.B: Sticky sessions lose session data when an instance terminates during scale-in and are not distributed.
others.C: Systems Manager Session Manager provides shell access to instances, not application session storage.
others.D: STS GetSessionToken issues temporary AWS credentials and does not manage application sessions.

e.tip: Distributed session state = ElastiCache (or DynamoDB).

q:
A company offers a food delivery service that is growing rapidly. Because of the growth, the company’s order processing system is experiencing scaling problems during peak traffic hours. The current architecture includes the following:

• A group of Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to collect orders from the application
• Another group of EC2 instances that run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to fulfill orders

The order collection process occurs quickly, but the order fulfillment process can take longer. Data must not be lost because of a scaling event.

A solutions architect must ensure that the order collection process and the order fulfillment process can both scale properly during peak traffic hours. The solution must optimize utilization of the company’s AWS resources.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to monitor the CPU of each instance in the Auto Scaling groups. Configure each Auto Scaling group’s minimum capacity according to peak workload values.
o.B: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to monitor the CPU of each instance in the Auto Scaling groups. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to invoke an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that creates additional Auto Scaling groups on demand.
o.C: Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues: one for order collection and another for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queue. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on notifications that the queues send.
o.D: Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues: one for order collection and another for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queue. Create a metric based on a backlog per instance calculation. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on this metric.

e.why: SQS queues decouple order collection from fulfillment so data is not lost during scaling. Scaling each Auto Scaling group on a custom backlog-per-instance metric (queue depth divided by running instances) with target tracking matches capacity to the work and optimizes resource use.

others.A: Setting minimum capacity to peak values wastes resources off-peak.
others.B: Creating additional Auto Scaling groups on demand via SNS is not how scaling works, and CPU does not reflect queue backlog.
others.C: SQS does not send scaling notifications; scaling must be driven by CloudWatch metrics.

e.tip: AWS-recommended SQS scaling = backlog-per-instance target tracking.

q:
A company hosts multiple production applications. One of the applications consists of resources from Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, Amazon RDS, Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS), and Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) across multiple AWS Regions. All company resources are tagged with a tag name of “application” and a value that corresponds to each application. A solutions architect must provide the quickest solution for identifying all of the tagged components.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS CloudTrail to generate a list of resources with the application tag.
o.B: Use the AWS CLI to query each service across all Regions to report the tagged components.
o.C: Run a query in Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights to report on the components with the application tag.
o.D: Run a query with the AWS Resource Groups Tag Editor to report on the resources globally with the application tag.

e.why: The AWS Resource Groups Tag Editor searches resources by tag across multiple Regions and resource types in a single query. It is the quickest way to list every component tagged application=<value>.

others.A: CloudTrail records API activity and does not inventory resources by tag.
others.B: Querying each service in each Region with the CLI is slow and laborious.
others.C: CloudWatch Logs Insights queries log data, not resource tags.

e.tip: Find resources by tag across Regions = Tag Editor (or Resource Explorer).

q:
A company needs to export its database once a day to Amazon S3 for other teams to access. The exported object size varies between 2 GB and 5 GB. The S3 access pattern for the data is variable and changes rapidly. The data must be immediately available and must remain accessible for up to 3 months. The company needs the most cost-effective solution that will not increase retrieval time.

Which S3 storage class should the company use to meet these requirements?

o.A: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
o.B: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
o.C: S3 Standard
o.D: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)

e.why: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent, infrequent and archive instant access tiers based on changing access patterns. Its millisecond access tiers add no retrieval fees or latency, which suits variable, rapidly changing access to large objects.

others.B: Glacier Instant Retrieval has high retrieval fees and a 90-day minimum, so it is costly for frequent access.
others.C: S3 Standard is costlier when objects go unaccessed for long periods.
others.D: Standard-IA retrieval fees add up when access is unpredictable and sometimes heavy.

e.tip: Unknown or changing access patterns = Intelligent-Tiering.

q:
A company is developing a new mobile app. The company must implement proper traffic filtering to protect its Application Load Balancer (ALB) against common application-level attacks, such as cross-site scripting or SQL injection. The company has minimal infrastructure and operational staff. The company needs to reduce its share of the responsibility in managing, updating, and securing servers for its AWS environment.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure AWS WAF rules and associate them with the ALB.
o.B: Deploy the application using Amazon S3 with public hosting enabled.
o.C: Deploy AWS Shield Advanced and add the ALB as a protected resource.
o.D: Create a new ALB that directs traffic to an Amazon EC2 instance running a third-party firewall, which then passes the traffic to the current ALB.

fixed: Option B contained answer text instead of option text, and options A and D were truncated; they have been reconstructed.

e.why: AWS WAF is a managed web application firewall that attaches directly to an ALB. AWS managed rule groups block SQL injection and cross-site scripting with no servers to manage, reducing the company's share of responsibility.

others.B: S3 static hosting cannot run the application backend and does not provide traffic filtering.
others.C: Shield Advanced focuses on DDoS protection; filtering XSS and SQL injection is done by WAF rules.
others.D: A third-party firewall on EC2 adds servers to patch and manage, increasing the company's responsibility.

e.tip: XSS/SQL injection filtering on ALB, API Gateway or CloudFront = AWS WAF.

q:
A company’s reporting system delivers hundreds of .csv files to an Amazon S3 bucket each day. The company must convert these files to Apache Parquet format and must store the files in a transformed data bucket.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

o.A: Create an Amazon EMR cluster with Apache Spark installed. Write a Spark application to transform the data. Use EMR File System (EMRFS) to write files to the transformed data bucket.
o.B: Create an AWS Glue crawler to discover the data. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to transform the data. Specify the transformed data bucket in the output step.
o.C: Use AWS Batch to create a job definition with Bash syntax to transform the data and output the data to the transformed data bucket. Use the job definition to submit a job. Specify an array job as the job type.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda function to transform the data and output the data to the transformed data bucket. Configure an event notification for the S3 bucket. Specify the Lambda function as the destination for the event notification.

e.why: An AWS Glue crawler infers the CSV schema into the Data Catalog, and a Glue ETL job (which can be generated visually) converts CSV to Parquet and writes it to the target bucket. Glue is serverless with minimal code, so this is the least development effort.

others.A: An EMR cluster with a custom Spark app requires cluster management and coding.
others.C: AWS Batch with custom Bash conversion scripts requires significant development.
others.D: A Lambda function needs custom Parquet-conversion code and libraries, and it has runtime and memory limits.

e.tip: CSV to Parquet with least effort = Glue ETL.

q:
A company has 700 TB of backup data stored in network attached storage (NAS) in its data center. This backup data need to be accessible for infrequent regulatory requests and must be retained 7 years. The company has decided to migrate this backup data from its data center to AWS. The migration must be complete within 1 month. The company has 500 Mbps of dedicated bandwidth on its public internet connection available for data transfer.

What should a solutions architect do to migrate and store the data at the LOWEST cost?

o.A: Order AWS Snowball devices to transfer the data. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
o.B: Deploy a VPN connection between the data center and Amazon VPC. Use the AWS CLI to copy the data from on premises to Amazon S3 Glacier.
o.C: Provision a 500 Mbps AWS Direct Connect connection and transfer the data to Amazon S3. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
o.D: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data and deploy a DataSync agent on premises. Use the DataSync task to copy files from the on-premises NAS storage to Amazon S3 Glacier.

fixed: Option B was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: Transferring 700 TB at 500 Mbps would take about 130 days, far beyond the 1-month deadline, so offline AWS Snowball devices are required. A Lifecycle policy to S3 Glacier Deep Archive gives the cheapest storage for rarely accessed data kept for 7 years.

others.B: A VPN over the same 500 Mbps link is still far too slow for 700 TB in a month.
others.C: A 500 Mbps Direct Connect link has the same bandwidth limit, plus provisioning time and cost.
others.D: DataSync over 500 Mbps cannot move 700 TB in a month, and S3 Glacier costs more than Deep Archive.

e.tip: Compute transfer time: if the network cannot finish in time, use the Snow Family.

q:
A company has a serverless website with millions of objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uses the S3 bucket as the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company did not set encryption on the S3 bucket before the objects were loaded. A solutions architect needs to enable encryption for all existing objects and for all objects that are added to the S3 bucket in the future.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?

o.A: Create a new S3 bucket. Turn on the default encryption settings for the new S3 bucket. Download all existing objects to temporary local storage. Upload the objects to the new S3 bucket.
o.B: Turn on the default encryption settings for the S3 bucket. Use the S3 Inventory feature to create a .csv file that lists the unencrypted objects. Run an S3 Batch Operations job that uses the copy command to encrypt those objects.
o.C: Create a new encryption key by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Change the settings on the S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). Turn on versioning for the S3 bucket.
o.D: Navigate to Amazon S3 in the AWS Management Console. Browse the S3 bucket’s objects. Sort by the encryption field. Select each unencrypted object. Use the Modify button to apply default encryption settings to every unencrypted object in the S3 bucket.

e.why: Turning on default bucket encryption covers all future uploads (S3 now encrypts new objects with SSE-S3 by default anyway). S3 Inventory identifies the unencrypted existing objects, and an S3 Batch Operations copy job re-encrypts millions of objects in place with minimal effort.

others.A: Downloading and re-uploading millions of objects to a new bucket is slow and laborious, and the CloudFront origin would need changing.
others.C: Changing default encryption and enabling versioning does not encrypt objects that already exist.
others.D: Modifying millions of objects one by one in the console is impractical.

e.tip: Bulk action on existing S3 objects = S3 Inventory + Batch Operations.

q:
A company runs a global web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application stores data in Amazon Aurora. The company needs to create a disaster recovery solution and can tolerate up to 30 minutes of downtime and potential data loss. The solution does not need to handle the load when the primary infrastructure is healthy.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy the application with the required infrastructure elements in place. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora Replica in a second AWS Region.
o.B: Host a scaled-down deployment of the application in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Create an Aurora Replica in the second Region.
o.C: Replicate the primary infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Create an Aurora database that is restored from the latest snapshot.
o.D: Back up data with AWS Backup. Use the backup to create the required infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora second primary instance in the second Region.

e.why: Deploying the required infrastructure in a second Region (pilot light or warm standby) with a cross-Region Aurora Replica keeps data nearly current. A Route 53 active-passive failover record switches traffic only when the primary fails, which fits the 30-minute RTO and RPO and the requirement that the standby does not serve traffic normally.

others.B: Active-active sends production traffic to the second Region, which the requirement says is not needed.
others.C: Active-active is unnecessary, and restoring from the latest snapshot risks more data loss and time.
others.D: Building infrastructure from backups at failover time risks exceeding 30 minutes, and Aurora does not support a second writable primary in another Region this way.

e.tip: Standby that does not take traffic = active-passive (failover) routing.

q:
A company has a web server running on an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet with an Elastic IP address. The default security group is assigned to the EC2 instance. The default network ACL has been modified to block all traffic. A solutions architect needs to make the web server accessible from everywhere on port 443.

Which combination of steps will accomplish this task? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create a security group with a rule to allow TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0.
o.B: Create a security group with a rule to allow TCP port 443 to destination 0.0.0.0/0.
o.C: Update the network ACL to allow TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0.
o.D: Update the network ACL to allow inbound/outbound TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0 and to destination 0.0.0.0/0.
o.E: Update the network ACL to allow inbound TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0 and outbound TCP port 32768-65535 to destination 0.0.0.0/0.

e.why: Security groups are stateful, so an inbound rule for TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 is enough (the default SG does not allow it). Network ACLs are stateless, so they need inbound 443 plus outbound ephemeral ports (1024-65535, or 32768-65535 for Linux) for the return traffic.

others.B: An outbound rule to a destination does not allow inbound HTTPS connections, and SG return traffic is automatic.
others.C: Allowing only inbound 443 on the stateless NACL blocks response traffic.
others.D: Responses go to client ephemeral ports, not port 443, so outbound 443 does not permit return traffic.

e.tip: SG stateful (inbound rule only); NACL stateless (allow ephemeral ports outbound).

q:
A company’s application is having performance issues. The application is stateful and needs to complete in-memory tasks on Amazon EC2 instances. The company used AWS CloudFormation to deploy infrastructure and used the M5 EC2 instance family. As traffic increased, the application performance degraded. Users are reporting delays when the users attempt to access the application.

Which solution will resolve these issues in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.A: Replace the EC2 instances with T3 EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group. Make the changes by using the AWS Management Console.
o.B: Modify the CloudFormation templates to run the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Increase the desired capacity and the maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group manually when an increase is necessary.
o.C: Modify the CloudFormation templates. Replace the EC2 instances with R5 EC2 instances. Use Amazon CloudWatch built-in EC2 memory metrics to track the application performance for future capacity planning.
o.D: Modify the CloudFormation templates. Replace the EC2 instances with R5 EC2 instances. Deploy the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to generate custom application latency metrics for future capacity planning.

e.why: The workload is memory-bound, so memory-optimized R5 instances fit, and updating the CloudFormation template keeps infrastructure as code. EC2 does not publish memory metrics natively, so installing the CloudWatch agent is required to collect memory and custom latency metrics for capacity planning.

others.A: Burstable T3 instances are not suited to sustained memory-heavy work, and console changes cause drift from CloudFormation.
others.B: Manual capacity changes are not operationally efficient, and scaling out a stateful app does not fix memory pressure.
others.C: CloudWatch has no built-in EC2 memory metrics; the agent is required.

e.tip: Memory metrics on EC2 = CloudWatch agent.

q:
A solutions architect is designing a new API using Amazon API Gateway that will receive requests from users. The volume of requests is highly variable; several hours can pass without receiving a single request. The data processing will take place asynchronously, but should be completed within a few seconds after a request is made.

Which compute service should the solutions architect have the API invoke to deliver the requirements at the lowest cost?

o.A: An AWS Glue job
o.B: An AWS Lambda function
o.C: A containerized service hosted in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
o.D: A containerized service hosted in Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2

e.why: AWS Lambda bills only per request and duration with no idle cost, which is ideal when hours pass without traffic. It starts within milliseconds to seconds, meeting the 'within a few seconds' processing target at the lowest cost.

others.A: Glue jobs are for ETL and have startup times and minimum billing that are unsuitable for per-request API work.
others.C: An EKS cluster has control plane and node costs even while idle.
others.D: ECS on EC2 requires instances that cost money even when idle.

e.tip: Sporadic, short tasks at lowest cost = Lambda.

q:
A company runs an application on a group of Amazon Linux EC2 instances. For compliance reasons, the company must retain all application log files for 7 years. The log files will be analyzed by a reporting tool that must be able to access all the files concurrently.

Which storage solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
o.B: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
o.C: Amazon EC2 instance store
o.D: Amazon S3

e.why: Amazon S3 is the cheapest durable storage for 7-year log retention, and lifecycle tiering can reduce cost further. Many clients or tools can read all objects concurrently through the API, and analytics tools such as Athena integrate with it directly.

others.A: EBS volumes are attached to one instance (Multi-AZ sharing is limited) and cost more per GB.
others.B: EFS supports concurrent access but costs much more than S3 for long-term retention.
others.C: Instance store is ephemeral and loses data when the instance stops.

e.tip: Long-term, cheap, concurrently accessible = S3.

q:
A company has hired an external vendor to perform work in the company’s AWS account. The vendor uses an automated tool that is hosted in an AWS account that the vendor owns. The vendor does not have IAM access to the company’s AWS account.

How should a solutions architect grant this access to the vendor?

o.A: Create an IAM role in the company’s account to delegate access to the vendor’s IAM role. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the role for the permissions that the vendor requires.
o.B: Create an IAM user in the company’s account with a password that meets the password complexity requirements. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.
o.C: Create an IAM group in the company’s account. Add the tool’s IAM user from the vendor account to the group. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the group for the permissions that the vendor requires.
o.D: Create a new identity provider by choosing “AWS account” as the provider type in the IAM console. Supply the vendor’s AWS account ID and user name. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the new provider for the permissions that the vendor requires.

e.why: A cross-account IAM role in the company's account with a trust policy for the vendor's account or role lets the vendor's tool assume it via STS for temporary credentials. Attached policies give least-privilege access, and an external ID is recommended for third parties.

others.B: An IAM user with long-term credentials for a third party is less secure and against best practice.
others.C: IAM groups can contain only users from the same account.
others.D: There is no 'AWS account' identity provider type; IdPs are for SAML or OIDC federation.

e.tip: Third-party or cross-account access = IAM role + trust policy (+ external ID).

q:
A company has deployed a Java Spring Boot application as a pod that runs on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) in private subnets. The application needs to write data to an Amazon DynamoDB table. A solutions architect must ensure that the application can interact with the DynamoDB table without exposing traffic to the internet.

Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to accomplish this goal? (Choose two.)

o.A: Attach an IAM role that has sufficient privileges to the EKS pod.
o.B: Attach an IAM user that has sufficient privileges to the EKS pod.
o.C: Allow outbound connectivity to the DynamoDB table through the private subnets’ network ACLs.
o.D: Create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB.
o.E: Embed the access keys in the Java Spring Boot code.

fixed: Option B text was missing and option D was truncated; both have been reconstructed.

e.why: Giving the pod an IAM role (IAM roles for service accounts or EKS Pod Identity) provides temporary credentials scoped to that pod. A gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB keeps traffic from the private subnets on the AWS network without internet access.

others.B: IAM users cannot be attached to pods; workloads should use roles with temporary credentials.
others.C: Network ACL changes do not create a private path; without an endpoint, traffic would need a NAT or internet route.
others.E: Embedding access keys in code is a security anti-pattern.

e.tip: AWS access from EKS pods = IAM role for the service account; private service access = VPC endpoint.

q:
A company recently migrated its web application to AWS by rehosting the application on Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The company wants to redesign its application architecture to be highly available and fault tolerant. Traffic must reach all running EC2 instances randomly.

Which combination of steps should the company take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy.
o.B: Create an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy.
o.C: Create an Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy.
o.D: Launch three EC2 instances: two instances in one Availability Zone and one instance in another Availability Zone.
o.E: Launch four EC2 instances: two instances in one Availability Zone and two instances in another Availability Zone.

e.why: A Route 53 multivalue answer policy returns up to eight healthy records chosen randomly, spreading traffic across all running instances with health checks. Four instances split two and two across two AZs remain fault tolerant if one AZ is lost.

others.A: Failover routing sends traffic to a primary and uses the secondary only on failure, so it does not reach all instances.
others.B: Weighted routing distributes by assigned weights rather than randomly across all healthy instances.
others.D: An uneven three-instance layout loses two-thirds of capacity if the larger AZ fails.

e.tip: Random distribution across healthy IPs = multivalue answer routing.

q:
A media company collects and analyzes user activity data on premises. The company wants to migrate this capability to AWS. The user activity data store will continue to grow and will be petabytes in size. The company needs to build a highly available data ingestion solution that facilitates on-demand analytics of existing data and new data with SQL.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.B: Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
o.C: Place activity data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure Amazon S3 to run an AWS Lambda function on the data as the data arrives in the S3 bucket.
o.D: Create an ingestion service on Amazon EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Configure the service to forward data to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ database.

e.why: Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed, auto-scaling ingestion service that delivers directly into Amazon Redshift (staging through S3). Redshift supports petabyte-scale SQL analytics on existing and new data, so the combination has the least operational overhead.

others.A: Kinesis Data Streams cannot deliver to S3 by itself (it needs consumers or Firehose), and no SQL query layer is provided.
others.C: S3 plus Lambda provides no SQL analytics capability.
others.D: A custom EC2 ingestion service and RDS have high overhead and RDS does not scale to petabytes.

e.tip: Streaming into Redshift, S3 or OpenSearch with no code = Firehose.

q:
A company collects data from thousands of remote devices by using a RESTful web services application that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance receives the raw data, transforms the raw data, and stores all the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The number of remote devices will increase into the millions soon. The company needs a highly scalable solution that minimizes operational overhead.

Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use AWS Glue to process the raw data in Amazon S3.
o.B: Use Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to different EC2 instances.
o.C: Add more EC2 instances to accommodate the increasing amount of incoming data.
o.D: Send the raw data to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Use EC2 instances to process the data.
o.E: Use Amazon API Gateway to send the raw data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to use the data stream as a source to deliver the data to Amazon S3.

e.why: API Gateway scales to accept requests from millions of devices without servers, Kinesis Data Streams buffers the data, and Firehose delivers it to S3. AWS Glue then transforms the raw data serverlessly, giving high scalability with minimal operations.

others.B: Route 53 routing across EC2 instances still requires managing and scaling servers.
others.C: Adding EC2 instances manually increases operational overhead.
others.D: EC2 consumers for SQS still require managing instances.

e.tip: Massive device ingestion serverless = API Gateway + Kinesis + Firehose.

q:
A company needs to retain its AWS CloudTrail logs for 3 years. The company is enforcing CloudTrail across a set of AWS accounts by using AWS Organizations from the parent account. The CloudTrail target S3 bucket is configured with S3 Versioning enabled. An S3 Lifecycle policy is in place to delete current objects after 3 years.

After the fourth year of use of the S3 bucket, the S3 bucket metrics show that the number of objects has continued to rise. However, the number of new CloudTrail logs that are delivered to the S3 bucket has remained consistent.

Which solution will delete objects that are older than 3 years in the MOST cost-effective manner?

o.A: Configure the organization’s centralized CloudTrail trail to expire objects after 3 years.
o.B: Configure the S3 Lifecycle policy to delete previous versions as well as current versions.
o.C: Create an AWS Lambda function to enumerate and delete objects from Amazon S3 that are older than 3 years.
o.D: Configure the parent account as the owner of all objects that are delivered to the S3 bucket.

e.why: With versioning enabled, the current-version expiration action only adds delete markers and keeps the old versions. Adding a NoncurrentVersionExpiration rule (and expired delete marker cleanup) to the Lifecycle policy actually removes them at no extra cost.

others.A: CloudTrail trails have no setting to expire objects in S3.
others.C: A custom Lambda function costs more and is more effort than a native Lifecycle rule.
others.D: Object ownership does not affect lifecycle deletion of noncurrent versions.

e.tip: Versioned bucket still growing = expire noncurrent versions.

q:
A company has an API that receives real-time data from a fleet of monitoring devices. The API stores this data in an Amazon RDS DB instance for later analysis. The amount of data that the monitoring devices send to the API fluctuates. During periods of heavy traffic, the API often returns timeout errors.

After an inspection of the logs, the company determines that the database is not capable of processing the volume of write traffic that comes from the API. A solutions architect must minimize the number of connections to the database and must ensure that data is not lost during periods of heavy traffic.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Increase the size of the DB instance to an instance type that has more available memory.
o.B: Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ DB instance. Configure the application to write to all active RDS DB instances.
o.C: Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SQS invokes to write data from the queue to the database.
o.D: Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SNS invokes to write data from the topic to the database.

e.why: Writing incoming data to SQS absorbs traffic spikes durably so no data is lost. Lambda consumers with a limited batch size and maximum concurrency write to RDS at a controlled rate, minimizing database connections.

others.A: A larger instance may help but does not cap connections or guarantee no data loss during spikes.
others.B: Multi-AZ standbys are not writable, so writing to all instances is not possible.
others.D: SNS pushes immediately to Lambda with no buffering or throttling, so the database is still overwhelmed.

e.tip: Smooth write spikes to a database = SQS buffer.

q:
A company manages its own Amazon EC2 instances that run MySQL databases. The company is manually managing replication and scaling as demand increases or decreases. The company needs a new solution that simplifies the process of adding or removing compute capacity to or from its database tier as needed. The solution also must offer improved performance, scaling, and durability with minimal effort from operations.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora MySQL.
o.B: Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora PostgreSQL.
o.C: Combine the databases into one larger MySQL database. Run the larger database on larger EC2 instances.
o.D: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group for the database tier. Migrate the existing databases to the new environment.

e.why: Aurora Serverless (v2) for MySQL scales compute capacity up and down automatically. It keeps MySQL compatibility, so no engine change is needed, and Aurora's six-way replicated storage gives better performance and durability with minimal operations effort.

others.B: Aurora PostgreSQL would require migrating from MySQL to a different engine.
others.C: One larger self-managed instance still requires manual scaling and replication.
others.D: Databases cannot simply be auto scaled in an EC2 Auto Scaling group, and replication remains manual.

e.tip: Auto-scaling MySQL compute with minimal effort = Aurora Serverless MySQL.

q:
A company is concerned that two NAT instances in use will no longer be able to support the traffic needed for the company’s application. A solutions architect wants to implement a solution that is highly available, fault tolerant, and automatically scalable.

What should the solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Remove the two NAT instances and replace them with two NAT gateways in the same Availability Zone.
o.B: Use Auto Scaling groups with Network Load Balancers for the NAT instances in different Availability Zones.
o.C: Remove the two NAT instances and replace them with two NAT gateways in different Availability Zones.
o.D: Replace the two NAT instances with Spot Instances in different Availability Zones and deploy a Network Load Balancer.

e.why: NAT gateways are managed, scale automatically up to 100 Gbps, and are redundant within an AZ. Placing one in each of two AZs, with each AZ's private subnets routed to their local gateway, provides high availability and fault tolerance.

others.A: Two NAT gateways in the same AZ fail together if that AZ fails.
others.B: NAT instances behind an NLB are self-managed and do not work as an Auto Scaling NAT solution.
others.D: Spot NAT instances can be interrupted and are still self-managed.

e.tip: NAT HA = one NAT gateway per AZ.

q:
An application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance that has an Elastic IP address in VPC A. The application requires access to a database in VPC B. Both VPCs are in the same AWS account.

Which solution will provide the required access MOST securely?

o.A: Configure a DB instance security group that allows all traffic from the public IP address of the application server in VPC A.
o.B: Configure a VPC peering connection between VPC A and VPC B.
o.C: Make the DB instance publicly accessible. Assign a public IP address to the DB instance.
o.D: Launch an EC2 instance with an Elastic IP address into VPC B. Proxy all requests through the new EC2 instance.

fixed: Options A, B and D were garbled (A missing, D truncated, B replaced by D's tail) and have been reconstructed.

e.why: A VPC peering connection between VPC A and VPC B lets the application reach the database over private IP addresses on the AWS network. Security groups can then allow only the application server, and nothing is exposed publicly.

others.A: Allowing all traffic from a public IP requires the database to be reachable publicly, which is less secure.
others.C: Making the database publicly accessible exposes it to the internet.
others.D: A public proxy instance adds an internet-exposed hop and a single point of failure to manage.

e.tip: Private connectivity between two VPCs = VPC peering (or Transit Gateway at scale).

q: A company runs demonstration environments for its customers on Amazon EC2 instances. Each environment is isolated in its own VPC. The company’s operations team needs to be notified when RDP or SSH access to an environment has been established.

o.A: Configure Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights to create AWS Systems Manager OpsItems when RDP or SSH access is detected.
o.B: Configure the EC2 instances with an IAM instance profile that has an IAM role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy attached.
o.C: Publish VPC flow logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create required metric filters. Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric alarm with a notification action for when the alarm is in the ALARM state.
o.D: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to listen for events of type EC2 Instance State-change Notification. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target. Subscribe the operations team to the topic.

e.why: VPC Flow Logs published to CloudWatch Logs capture accepted connections on ports 22 and 3389. A metric filter counts those events, and a CloudWatch alarm with an SNS notification alerts the operations team when RDP or SSH access occurs.

others.A: CloudWatch Application Insights monitors application health problems, not network RDP or SSH connections.
others.B: An SSM instance profile enables Systems Manager management but does not by itself notify anyone of RDP or SSH sessions.
others.D: Instance state-change events report starts and stops, not login connections.

e.tip: Detect traffic on specific ports = VPC Flow Logs + metric filter + alarm.

q:
A solutions architect has created a new AWS account and must secure AWS account root user access.

Which combination of actions will accomplish this? (Choose two.)

o.A: Ensure the root user uses a strong password.
o.B: Enable multi-factor authentication to the root user.
o.C: Store root user access keys in an encrypted Amazon S3 bucket.
o.D: Add the root user to a group containing administrative permissions.
o.E: Apply the required permissions to the root user with an inline policy document.

e.why: Securing the root user starts with a strong, unique password and MFA, which AWS strongly recommends (and now enforces for many account types). These two actions directly protect root sign-in.

others.C: Root access keys should not exist at all; delete them rather than store them.
others.D: The root user cannot be added to IAM groups.
others.E: IAM policies cannot be attached to the root user, which always has full access.

e.tip: Root user: strong password, MFA, no access keys, use rarely.

q:
A company is building a new web-based customer relationship management application. The application will use several Amazon EC2 instances that are backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application will also use an Amazon Aurora database. All data for the application must be encrypted at rest and in transit.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) certificates on the ALB to encrypt data in transit. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest.
o.B: Use the AWS root account to log in to the AWS Management Console. Upload the company’s encryption certificates. While in the root account, select the option to turn on encryption for all data at rest and in transit for the account.
