o.C: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest. Attach an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate to the ALB to encrypt data in transit.
o.D: Use BitLocker to encrypt all data at rest. Import the company’s TLS certificate keys to AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) Attach the KMS keys to the ALB to encrypt data in transit.

e.why: AWS KMS keys encrypt EBS volumes and Aurora storage at rest. An ACM certificate on the ALB's HTTPS listener encrypts data in transit, which is the standard AWS-native pattern.

others.A: The roles are reversed: KMS does not issue certificates, and ACM does not encrypt storage.
others.B: There is no single account-wide encryption switch, and using the root account for daily tasks is bad practice.
others.D: BitLocker does not encrypt Aurora storage, and KMS keys cannot be attached to an ALB for TLS.

e.tip: At rest = KMS; in transit on ALB or CloudFront = ACM certificate.

q:
A company is moving its on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The database has several applications that write to the same tables. The applications need to be migrated one by one with a month in between each migration. Management has expressed concerns that the database has a high number of reads and writes. The data must be kept in sync across both databases throughout the migration.

What should a solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.
o.B: Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.
o.C: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a memory optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.
o.D: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a compute optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select the largest tables.

e.why: Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL is heterogeneous, so AWS SCT converts the schema. DMS with full load plus CDC on all tables keeps both databases in sync during the month-by-month cutovers, and a memory-optimized replication instance suits heavy read and write CDC workloads.

others.A: DataSync moves files, not database contents, and CDC alone lacks the initial load.
others.B: DataSync cannot migrate a live database, and the schema conversion step is missing.
others.D: Selecting only the largest tables leaves other tables unsynced, and memory-optimized instances are recommended for CDC.

e.tip: Heterogeneous migration = SCT + DMS; stay in sync = full load + CDC.

q:
A company has a three-tier application for image sharing. The application uses an Amazon EC2 instance for the front-end layer, another EC2 instance for the application layer, and a third EC2 instance for a MySQL database. A solutions architect must design a scalable and highly available solution that requires the least amount of change to the application.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon S3 to host the front-end layer. Use AWS Lambda functions for the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use Amazon S3 to store and serve users’ images.
o.B: Use load-balanced Multi-AZ AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments for the front-end layer and the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon RDS DB instance with multiple read replicas to serve users’ images.
o.C: Use Amazon S3 to host the front-end layer. Use a fleet of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group for the application layer. Move the database to a memory optimized instance type to store and serve users’ images.
o.D: Use load-balanced Multi-AZ AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments for the front-end layer and the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. Use Amazon S3 to store and serve users’ images.

e.why: Elastic Beanstalk Multi-AZ, load-balanced environments run the existing front-end and application code with auto scaling and high availability and little change. RDS Multi-AZ provides an HA MySQL database, and S3 is the scalable store for images.

others.A: Rewriting to S3, Lambda and DynamoDB requires major application changes.
others.B: Read replicas do not provide automatic failover, and images do not belong in the database.
others.C: A single memory-optimized database instance is not highly available, and storing images in the database is a poor design.

e.tip: Least change + HA = Beanstalk Multi-AZ + RDS Multi-AZ + S3 for media.

q:
An application running on an Amazon EC2 instance in VPC-A needs to access files in another EC2 instance in VPC-B. Both VPCs are in separate AWS accounts. The network administrator needs to design a solution to configure secure access to EC2 instance in VPC-B from VPC-A. The connectivity should not have a single point of failure or bandwidth concerns.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Set up a VPC peering connection between VPC-A and VPC-B.
o.B: Set up VPC gateway endpoints for the EC2 instance running in VPC-B.
o.C: Attach a virtual private gateway to VPC-B and set up routing from VPC-A.
o.D: Create a private virtual interface (VIF) for the EC2 instance running in VPC-B and add appropriate routes from VPC-A.

fixed: Option A contained answer text instead of option text, option B was missing, and options C and D were truncated; they have been reconstructed.

e.why: VPC peering works across AWS accounts and connects the two VPCs over the AWS network using private IP addresses. A peering connection is not a single physical device, so it has no single point of failure or bandwidth bottleneck.

others.B: Gateway endpoints are only for S3 and DynamoDB, not for reaching EC2 instances in another VPC.
others.C: A virtual private gateway terminates VPN or Direct Connect connections, which adds tunnels with bandwidth limits.
others.D: Private VIFs belong to Direct Connect for on-premises connectivity, not VPC-to-VPC access.

e.tip: Cross-account VPC-to-VPC private access with no single point of failure = VPC peering.

q:
A company wants to experiment with individual AWS accounts for its engineer team. The company wants to be notified as soon as the Amazon EC2 instance usage for a given month exceeds a specific threshold for each account.

What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use Cost Explorer to create a daily report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances. Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.
o.B: Use Cost Explorer to create a monthly report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances. Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.
o.C: Use AWS Budgets to create a cost budget for each account. Set the period to monthly. Set the scope to EC2 instances. Set an alert threshold for the budget. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.
o.D: Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create a report with hourly granularity. Integrate the report data with Amazon Athena. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an Athena query. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.

e.why: AWS Budgets lets you create a monthly cost budget per account scoped to EC2. Alerts are sent through email or SNS when actual or forecast spend crosses a threshold, and the first budgets are free, making it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Cost Explorer reports do not send threshold alerts via SES.
others.B: Cost Explorer reports still have no SES threshold notification capability.
others.D: CUR with Athena and scheduled queries is complex and costs more for a simple threshold alert.

e.tip: Alert when spend or usage exceeds a threshold = AWS Budgets.

q:
A solutions architect needs to design a new microservice for a company’s application. Clients must be able to call an HTTPS endpoint to reach the microservice. The microservice also must use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to authenticate calls. The solutions architect will write the logic for this microservice by using a single AWS Lambda function that is written in Go 1.x.

Which solution will deploy the function in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.A: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure the method to use the Lambda function. Enable IAM authentication on the API.
o.B: Create a Lambda function URL for the function. Specify AWS_IAM as the authentication type.
o.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy the function to Lambda@Edge. Integrate IAM authentication logic into the Lambda@Edge function.
o.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy the function to CloudFront Functions. Specify AWS_IAM as the authentication type.

e.why: API Gateway REST APIs provide an HTTPS endpoint with IAM (SigV4) authorization integrated with Lambda. This is the classic answer, offering throttling, stages and other API management features.

others.B: Lambda function URLs also provide HTTPS with AWS_IAM auth and are simpler, but the keyed answer favours API Gateway.
others.C: Writing custom IAM authentication logic in Lambda@Edge is complex, and Lambda@Edge has runtime restrictions.
others.D: CloudFront Functions support only JavaScript, cannot run Go, and have no AWS_IAM auth type.

e.tip: Function URLs = simplest HTTPS endpoint for one function; API Gateway = full API management.
e.flag: A Lambda function URL with AuthType AWS_IAM (B) gives an HTTPS endpoint with IAM auth for a single function with less setup, so B is arguably the most operationally efficient answer.

q:
A company previously migrated its data warehouse solution to AWS. The company also has an AWS Direct Connect connection. Corporate office users query the data warehouse using a visualization tool. The average size of a query returned by the data warehouse is 50 MB and each webpage sent by the visualization tool is approximately 500 KB. Result sets returned by the data warehouse are not cached.

Which solution provides the LOWEST data transfer egress cost for the company?

o.A: Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over the internet.
o.B: Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse. Access it over the internet.
o.C: Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same AWS Region.
o.D: Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse and access it over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same Region.

e.why: Hosting the visualization tool in the same Region as the warehouse means the 50 MB query results never leave AWS (intra-Region transfer). Only the 500 KB webpages egress, and over Direct Connect, whose data transfer out rates are lower than internet rates.

others.A: 50 MB results egress over the internet at the highest rates.
others.B: Internet egress for webpages costs more than egress over Direct Connect.
others.C: The 50 MB result sets still egress (although at DX rates), which is much more data than 500 KB pages.

e.tip: Minimize egress: keep heavy traffic inside AWS and send only small results out via DX.

q:
An online learning company is migrating to the AWS Cloud. The company maintains its student records in a PostgreSQL database. The company needs a solution in which its data is available and online across multiple AWS Regions at all times.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

o.A: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to a PostgreSQL cluster on Amazon EC2 instances.
o.B: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with the Multi-AZ feature turned on.
o.C: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Create a read replica in another Region.
o.D: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Set up DB snapshots to be copied to another Region.

e.why: RDS for PostgreSQL with a cross-Region read replica keeps a continuously replicated, online copy of the data in another Region. It is managed and can be promoted, giving multi-Region availability with low operational overhead.

others.A: A self-managed PostgreSQL cluster on EC2 has high operational overhead.
others.B: Multi-AZ provides availability within a single Region only.
others.D: Snapshot copies are not online and available at all times.

e.tip: Data in multiple Regions = cross-Region read replica (or Aurora Global Database).

q:
A company hosts its web application on AWS using seven Amazon EC2 instances. The company requires that the IP addresses of all healthy EC2 instances be returned in response to DNS queries.

Which policy should be used to meet this requirement?

o.A: Simple routing policy
o.B: Latency routing policy
o.C: Multivalue routing policy
o.D: Geolocation routing policy

e.why: A Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy returns multiple IP addresses (up to eight healthy records per response) and uses health checks to return only healthy instances.

others.A: Simple routing returns all values but cannot use health checks to omit unhealthy instances.
others.B: Latency routing returns the single record with the lowest latency.
others.D: Geolocation routing returns records based on user location, not all healthy IPs.

e.tip: Multiple healthy IPs in DNS answers = multivalue answer.

q:
A medical research lab produces data that is related to a new study. The lab wants to make the data available with minimum latency to clinics across the country for their on-premises, file-based applications. The data files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket that has read-only permissions for each clinic.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic
o.B: Migrate the files to each clinic’s on-premises applications by using AWS DataSync for processing.
o.C: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic.
o.D: Attach an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to each clinic’s on-premises servers.

e.why: An S3 File Gateway deployed as a VM at each clinic presents the S3 bucket as an NFS or SMB file share to on-premises file-based applications. It caches data locally for low-latency access while S3 remains the source of truth.

others.B: DataSync copies data on a schedule and does not provide ongoing low-latency file access with S3 permissions.
others.C: Volume Gateway presents block iSCSI volumes, not file access to S3 objects.
others.D: EFS is not designed to be mounted directly by remote clinics across the country, and the data is in S3.

e.tip: On-premises file access to S3 = S3 File Gateway.

q:
A company is using a content management system that runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance contains both the web server and the database software. The company must make its website platform highly available and must enable the website to scale to meet user demand.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Move the database to Amazon RDS, and enable automatic backups. Manually launch another EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone. Configure an Application Load Balancer in the Availability Zone, and set the two instances as targets.
o.B: Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora instance with a read replica in the same Availability Zone as the existing EC2 instance. Manually launch another EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone. Configure an Application Load Balancer, and set the two EC2 instances as targets.
o.C: Move the database to Amazon Aurora with a read replica in another Availability Zone. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the EC2 instance. Configure an Application Load Balancer in two Availability Zones. Attach an Auto Scaling group that uses the AMI across two Availability Zones.
o.D: Move the database to a separate EC2 instance, and schedule backups to Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the original EC2 instance. Configure an Application Load Balancer in two Availability Zones. Attach an Auto Scaling group that uses the AMI across two Availability Zones.

e.why: Separating the database into Aurora with a replica in another AZ provides database HA through automatic failover. An AMI-based Auto Scaling group across two AZs behind an ALB makes the web tier both highly available and scalable.

others.A: Everything stays in one AZ, and manually launched instances do not scale.
others.B: A replica and instances all in one AZ are not highly available, and there is no Auto Scaling.
others.D: A self-managed database on a single EC2 instance is a single point of failure.

e.tip: HA + scale = multi-AZ Auto Scaling group + ALB + multi-AZ database.

q:
A company is launching an application on AWS. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to direct traffic to at least two Amazon EC2 instances in a single target group. The instances are in an Auto Scaling group for each environment. The company requires a development environment and a production environment. The production environment will have periods of high traffic.

Which solution will configure the development environment MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Reconfigure the target group in the development environment to have only one EC2 instance as a target.
o.B: Change the ALB balancing algorithm to least outstanding requests.
o.C: Reduce the size of the EC2 instances in both environments.
o.D: Reduce the maximum number of EC2 instances in the development environment’s Auto Scaling group.

e.why: Reducing the development Auto Scaling group's maximum capacity stops dev from scaling out to costly levels while keeping the setup the same. Production is unaffected and can still scale for high traffic.

others.A: Targets are managed by the Auto Scaling group, so manually setting one target is not durable, and the stated minimum is two instances.
others.B: Changing the load balancing algorithm does not reduce cost.
others.C: Shrinking production instances risks performance during high-traffic periods.

e.tip: Dev cost control = cap Auto Scaling capacity or use smaller or fewer instances only in dev.

q:
A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances are in private subnets. A solutions architect implements an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB) and specifies the EC2 instances as the target group. However, the internet traffic is not reaching the EC2 instances.

How should the solutions architect reconfigure the architecture to resolve this issue?

o.A: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer. Configure a NAT gateway in a public subnet to allow internet traffic.
o.B: Move the EC2 instances to public subnets. Add a rule to the EC2 instances’ security groups to allow outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0.
o.C: Update the route tables for the EC2 instances’ subnets to send 0.0.0.0/0 traffic through the internet gateway route. Add a rule to the EC2 instances’ security groups to allow outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0.
o.D: Create public subnets in each Availability Zone. Associate the public subnets with the ALB. Update the route tables for the public subnets with a route to the private subnets.

fixed: Options B and D were garbled (D truncated, B replaced by D's tail) and have been reconstructed.

e.why: An internet-facing ALB must be placed in public subnets, which route to an internet gateway, in each Availability Zone. It can then forward traffic to targets in private subnets, so creating public subnets and associating them with the ALB fixes the problem while the instances stay private.

others.A: A NAT gateway only provides outbound access and cannot accept inbound internet traffic, and an NLB does not fix the subnet placement.
others.B: Moving instances to public subnets exposes them needlessly and does not fix the ALB's subnet placement.
others.C: Routing the private subnets to the internet gateway makes them public, and outbound rules do not help inbound traffic.

e.tip: Internet-facing load balancers live in public subnets; targets can stay private.

q:
A company has deployed a database in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Due to increased transactions, the database support team is reporting slow reads against the DB instance and recommends adding a read replica.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take before implementing this change? (Choose two.)

o.A: Enable binlog replication on the RDS primary node.
o.B: Choose a failover priority for the source DB instance.
o.C: Allow long-running transactions to complete on the source DB instance.
o.D: Create a global table and specify the AWS Regions where the table will be available.
o.E: Enable automatic backups on the source instance by setting the backup retention period to a value other than 0.

e.why: RDS read replicas require automated backups (backup retention greater than 0) on the source. AWS also recommends letting long-running transactions finish before creating a replica, because replica creation starts from a snapshot and long transactions can delay or break replication.

others.A: Binary logging is managed by RDS automatically once backups are enabled; there is no separate setting to turn on.
others.B: Failover priority (tiers) applies to Aurora replicas, not RDS for MySQL source instances.
others.D: Global tables are a DynamoDB feature.

e.tip: RDS read replica prerequisite = automated backups enabled.

q:
A company runs analytics software on Amazon EC2 instances. The software accepts job requests from users to process data that has been uploaded to Amazon S3. Users report that some submitted data is not being processed Amazon CloudWatch reveals that the EC2 instances have a consistent CPU utilization at or near 100%. The company wants to improve system performance and scale the system based on user load.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a copy of the instance. Place all instances behind an Application Load Balancer.
o.B: Create an S3 VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Update the software to reference the endpoint.
o.C: Stop the EC2 instances. Modify the instance type to one with a more powerful CPU and more memory. Restart the instances.
o.D: Route incoming requests to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling group based on queue size. Update the software to read from the queue.

e.why: Putting job requests into SQS ensures none are lost while instances are busy. An EC2 Auto Scaling group scaling on queue depth (or backlog per instance) adds workers with user load and improves throughput.

others.A: A copied instance behind an ALB is a fixed capacity increase with no automatic scaling, and requests can still be dropped.
others.B: An S3 endpoint changes network routing, not CPU saturation.
others.C: Vertical scaling needs downtime and does not scale with user load.

e.tip: Jobs dropped under load = SQS + Auto Scaling on queue depth.

q:
A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a media application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed.

Which AWS solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Create an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol. Connect the application server to the file share.
o.B: Create an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway. Configure tapes to use Amazon S3. Connect the application server to the tape gateway.
o.C: Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
o.D: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.

e.why: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed native Windows file system accessible over SMB. It suits shared storage for a media application in the cloud.

others.A: Volume Gateway exposes iSCSI block volumes, not SMB file shares, and is for hybrid use.
others.B: Tape Gateway provides a virtual tape library for backup, not shared SMB storage.
others.C: A self-managed Windows file server on EC2 is not fully managed.

e.tip: Managed SMB = FSx for Windows (or FSx for NetApp ONTAP).

q:
A company’s security team requests that network traffic be captured in VPC Flow Logs. The logs will be frequently accessed for 90 days and then accessed intermittently.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements when configuring the logs?

o.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch as the target. Set the CloudWatch log group with an expiration of 90 days
o.B: Use Amazon Kinesis as the target. Configure the Kinesis stream to always retain the logs for 90 days.
o.C: Use AWS CloudTrail as the target. Configure CloudTrail to save to an Amazon S3 bucket, and enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
o.D: Use Amazon S3 as the target. Enable an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the logs to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days.

e.why: Delivering VPC Flow Logs to S3 is low cost, and a Lifecycle rule moves logs to S3 Standard-IA after 90 days, matching frequent access for 90 days and intermittent access afterwards.

others.A: Expiring the log group after 90 days deletes the logs, losing the intermittent access afterwards.
others.B: Kinesis Data Streams is not a Flow Logs destination and is not suited to long-term storage.
others.C: CloudTrail records API calls and is not a VPC Flow Logs destination.

e.tip: Flow Logs destinations: CloudWatch Logs, S3, Firehose.

q:
An Amazon EC2 instance is located in a private subnet in a new VPC. This subnet does not have outbound internet access, but the EC2 instance needs the ability to download monthly security updates from an outside vendor.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an internet gateway, and attach it to the VPC. Configure the private subnet route table to use the internet gateway as the default route.
o.C: Create a NAT instance, and place it in the same subnet where the EC2 instance is located. Configure the private subnet route table to use the NAT instance as the default route.
o.B: Create a NAT gateway, and place it in a public subnet. Configure the private subnet route table to use the NAT gateway as the default route.
o.D: Create an internet gateway, and attach it to the VPC. Create a NAT instance, and place it in the same subnet where the EC2 instance is located. Configure the private subnet route table to use the internet gateway as the default route.

fixed: Options A, C and D were truncated or garbled by text splitting and have been reconstructed.

e.why: A NAT gateway in a public subnet, with the private subnet's default route (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to it, lets the instance make outbound connections to download updates. Unsolicited inbound connections from the internet are still blocked.

others.A: Routing the private subnet to the internet gateway makes it a public subnet and requires public IPs on the instance.
others.C: A NAT device must sit in a public subnet; a NAT instance in the private subnet has no internet route.
others.D: Routing the private subnet directly to the internet gateway bypasses the NAT instance and exposes the subnet.

e.tip: Outbound-only internet access from a private subnet = NAT gateway in a public subnet.

q:
A solutions architect needs to design a system to store client case files. The files are core company assets and are important. The number of files will grow over time.

The files must be simultaneously accessible from multiple application servers that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The solution must have built-in redundancy.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
o.B: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
o.C: Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive
o.D: AWS Backup

e.why: Amazon EFS is a managed NFS file system that many EC2 instances can mount simultaneously. It grows elastically and stores data redundantly across multiple AZs.

others.B: EBS volumes attach to a single instance (Multi-Attach is limited) and are AZ-scoped.
others.C: Glacier Deep Archive is archival with hours-long retrieval, not live shared access.
others.D: AWS Backup is a backup service, not primary shared storage.

e.tip: Shared, growing Linux file storage across instances = EFS.

o.A: Deleting IAM users
o.B: Deleting directories
o.C: Deleting Amazon EC2 instances
o.D: Deleting logs from Amazon CloudWatch Logs

fixed: The two IAM policies referenced by the question were missing and have been added from the original question.

e.why: Policy1 allows ec2:*, which includes ec2:TerminateInstances, and nothing denies it, so the engineer can delete EC2 instances. The other actions are either only partly allowed (iam:Get*/List*, logs:Get*/Describe*) or explicitly denied (ds:Delete* in Policy2).

others.A: Only iam:Get* and iam:List* are allowed, so iam:DeleteUser is implicitly denied.
others.B: Policy1 allows ds:*, but Policy2's explicit Deny on ds:Delete* overrides it.
others.D: Only logs:Get* and logs:Describe* are allowed, so deleting logs is implicitly denied.

e.tip: Evaluate IAM as: explicit Deny wins, then an explicit Allow is required, otherwise implicit deny.

q:
A company has an ecommerce checkout workflow that writes an order to a database and calls a service to process the payment. Users are experiencing timeouts during the checkout process. When users resubmit the checkout form, multiple unique orders are created for the same desired transaction.

How should a solutions architect refactor this workflow to prevent the creation of multiple orders?

o.A: Configure the web application to send an order message to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Set the payment service to retrieve the message from Kinesis Data Firehose and process the order.
o.B: Create a rule in AWS CloudTrail to invoke an AWS Lambda function based on the logged application path request. Use Lambda to query the database, call the payment service, and pass in the order information.
o.C: Store the order in the database. Send a message that includes the order number to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Set the payment service to poll Amazon SNS, retrieve the message, and process the order.
o.D: Store the order in the database. Send a message that includes the order number to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Set the payment service to retrieve the message and process the order. Delete the message from the queue.

e.why: Storing the order once and sending its order number to an SQS FIFO queue provides exactly-once processing and message deduplication. The payment service processes each order once and deletes the message, preventing duplicate orders on resubmission.

others.A: Firehose is a delivery stream to destinations, not a queue that consumers retrieve from, and it does not deduplicate.
others.B: CloudTrail logs AWS API calls and does not trigger on application request paths.
others.C: SNS is push-based and cannot be polled, and it offers no deduplication here.

e.tip: Prevent duplicates = SQS FIFO deduplication (or idempotency keys).

q:
A solutions architect is implementing a document review application using an Amazon S3 bucket for storage. The solution must prevent accidental deletion of the documents and ensure that all versions of the documents are available. Users must be able to download, modify, and upload documents.

Which combination of actions should be taken to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Enable a read-only bucket ACL.
o.B: Enable versioning on the bucket.
o.C: Attach an IAM policy to the bucket.
o.D: Enable MFA Delete on the bucket.
o.E: Encrypt the bucket using AWS KMS.

e.why: Versioning keeps every version of each document, so modifications and uploads create new versions and deletes become recoverable delete markers. MFA Delete requires MFA to permanently delete versions or change the versioning state, preventing accidental deletion.

others.A: A read-only ACL would stop users from uploading modified documents.
others.C: IAM policies attach to identities rather than buckets, and a policy alone does not keep versions.
others.E: KMS encryption protects confidentiality but does nothing against deletion.

e.tip: Prevent accidental deletion = Versioning + MFA Delete (or Object Lock).

q:
A company is building a solution that will report Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling events across all the applications in an AWS account. The company needs to use a serverless solution to store the EC2 Auto Scaling status data in Amazon S3. The company then will use the data in Amazon S3 to provide near-real-time updates in a dashboard. The solution must not affect the speed of EC2 instance launches.

How should the company move the data to Amazon S3 to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use an Amazon CloudWatch metric stream to send the EC2 Auto Scaling status data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Store the data in Amazon S3.
o.B: Launch an Amazon EMR cluster to collect the EC2 Auto Scaling status data and send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Store the data in Amazon S3.
o.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function on a schedule. Configure the Lambda function to send the EC2 Auto Scaling status data directly to Amazon S3.
o.D: Use a bootstrap script during the launch of an EC2 instance to install Amazon Kinesis Agent. Configure Kinesis Agent to collect the EC2 Auto Scaling status data and send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Store the data in Amazon S3.

e.why: CloudWatch metric streams continuously push metrics (including EC2 Auto Scaling group metrics) to Kinesis Data Firehose, which delivers them to S3 in near-real time. Both services are fully managed and serverless, and the mechanism sits outside the instance launch path, so launch speed is unaffected.

others.B: EMR is a managed cluster, not serverless, and adds unnecessary infrastructure to run.
others.C: A scheduled Lambda polls on a timer, so it is not near-real time and requires custom collection code.
others.D: Installing Kinesis Agent in a bootstrap script adds work to every launch and slows instance startup, violating the requirement.

e.tip: Metrics to S3/third parties continuously with no code: CloudWatch metric stream -> Firehose.

q:
A company has an application that places hundreds of .csv files into an Amazon S3 bucket every hour. The files are 1 GB in size. Each time a file is uploaded, the company needs to convert the file to Apache Parquet format and place the output file into an S3 bucket.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to download the .csv files, convert the files to Parquet format, and place the output files in an S3 bucket. Invoke the Lambda function for each S3 PUT event.
o.B: Create an Apache Spark job to read the .csv files, convert the files to Parquet format, and place the output files in an S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function for each S3 PUT event to invoke the Spark job.
o.C: Create an AWS Glue table and an AWS Glue crawler for the S3 bucket where the application places the .csv files. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically use Amazon Athena to query the AWS Glue table, convert the query results into Parquet format, and place the output files into an S3 bucket.
o.D: Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the .csv files to Parquet format and place the output files into an S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function for each S3 PUT event to invoke the ETL job.

e.why: An AWS Glue ETL job is a serverless Spark environment that natively converts CSV to Parquet and scales to handle 1 GB files, and a Lambda triggered by S3 PUT events can simply start the job. This gives event-driven conversion with the least operational overhead.

others.A: Lambda has 15-minute, memory and /tmp limits that make converting hundreds of 1 GB files per hour fragile.
others.B: Running your own Spark job requires provisioning and managing a cluster, adding overhead.
others.C: Periodic Athena queries plus a crawler are not per-upload, and add extra moving parts and latency.

e.tip: CSV to Parquet at scale with minimal ops: Glue ETL job.

q:
A company is implementing new data retention policies for all databases that run on Amazon RDS DB instances. The company must retain daily backups for a minimum period of 2 years. The backups must be consistent and restorable.

Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a backup vault in AWS Backup to retain RDS backups. Create a new backup plan with a daily schedule and an expiration period of 2 years after creation. Assign the RDS DB instances to the backup plan.
o.B: Configure a backup window for the RDS DB instances for daily snapshots. Assign a snapshot retention policy of 2 years to each RDS DB instance. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to schedule snapshot deletions.
o.C: Configure database transaction logs to be automatically backed up to Amazon CloudWatch Logs with an expiration period of 2 years.
o.D: Configure an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication task. Deploy a replication instance, and configure a change data capture (CDC) task to stream database changes to Amazon S3 as the target. Configure S3 Lifecycle policies to delete the snapshots after 2 years.

e.why: AWS Backup lets you create a backup plan with a daily schedule and a 2-year retention (lifecycle expiration), storing consistent RDS snapshots in a backup vault. It is centrally managed and far exceeds the 35-day maximum of RDS automated backups.

others.B: RDS automated backup retention maxes out at 35 days, and DLM manages EBS snapshots/AMIs, not RDS snapshots.
others.C: Shipping transaction logs to CloudWatch Logs does not produce consistent, restorable database backups.
others.D: DMS CDC to S3 is replication, not consistent restorable backups, and is complex to restore from.

e.tip: RDS retention beyond 35 days: AWS Backup plan or manual snapshots.

q:
A company’s compliance team needs to move its file shares to AWS. The shares run on a Windows Server SMB file share. A self-managed on-premises Active Directory controls access to the files and folders.

The company wants to use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server as part of the solution. The company must ensure that the on-premises Active Directory groups restrict access to the FSx for Windows File Server SMB compliance shares, folders, and files after the move to AWS. The company has created an FSx for Windows File Server file system.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Active Directory Connector to connect to the Active Directory. Map the Active Directory groups to IAM groups to restrict access.
o.B: Assign a tag with a Restrict tag key and a Compliance tag value. Map the Active Directory groups to IAM groups to restrict access.
o.C: Create an IAM service-linked role that is linked directly to FSx for Windows File Server to restrict access.
o.D: Join the file system to the Active Directory to restrict access.

e.why: Joining FSx for Windows File Server to the self-managed on-premises Active Directory lets existing AD users and groups be used in NTFS ACLs and share permissions. Access to shares, folders and files is then enforced by the AD groups exactly as on premises.

others.A: IAM groups do not control SMB file and folder permissions; NTFS ACLs with AD identities do.
others.B: Tags do not enforce file-level access control on SMB shares.
others.C: A service-linked role governs what FSx can do in AWS, not which users can access files.

e.tip: FSx for Windows access control = join to AD (AWS Managed AD or self-managed).

q:
A company recently announced the deployment of its retail website to a global audience. The website runs on multiple Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancer. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones.

The company wants to provide its customers with different versions of content based on the devices that the customers use to access the website.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Configure Amazon CloudFront to cache multiple versions of the content.
o.B: Configure a host header in a Network Load Balancer to forward traffic to different instances.
o.C: Configure a Lambda@Edge function to send specific objects to users based on the User-Agent header.
o.D: Configure AWS Global Accelerator. Forward requests to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Configure the NLB to set up host-based routing to different EC2 instances.
o.E: Configure AWS Global Accelerator. Forward requests to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Configure the NLB to set up path-based routing to different EC2 instances.

e.why: CloudFront can cache multiple versions of the same object when the cache key includes a device header (such as CloudFront-Is-Mobile-Viewer or User-Agent). A Lambda@Edge function can inspect the User-Agent and return or rewrite to the device-specific object, delivering different content per device globally.

others.B: Network Load Balancers operate at layer 4 and cannot route on host headers.
others.D: Global Accelerator does not inspect HTTP headers, and NLBs cannot do host-based routing.
others.E: NLBs cannot do path-based routing; that is an ALB layer 7 feature.

e.tip: Device-specific content at the edge: CloudFront cache key on device headers plus Lambda@Edge/CloudFront Functions.

q:
A company plans to use Amazon ElastiCache for its multi-tier web application. A solutions architect creates a Cache VPC for the ElastiCache cluster and an App VPC for the application’s Amazon EC2 instances. Both VPCs are in the us-east-1 Region.

The solutions architect must implement a solution to provide the application’s EC2 instances with access to the ElastiCache cluster.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create a peering connection between the VPCs. Add a route table entry for the peering connection in both VPCs. Configure an inbound rule for the ElastiCache cluster’s security group to allow inbound connection from the application’s security group.
o.B: Create a Transit VPC. Update the VPC route tables in the Cache VPC and the App VPC to route traffic through the Transit VPC. Configure an inbound rule for the ElastiCache cluster's security group to allow inbound connection from the application's security group.
o.C: Create a peering connection between the VPCs. Add a route table entry for the peering connection in both VPCs. Configure an inbound rule for the peering connection's security group to allow inbound connection from the application's security group.
o.D: Create a Transit VPC. Update the VPC route tables in the Cache VPC and the App VPC to route traffic through the Transit VPC. Configure an inbound rule for the Transit VPC's security group to allow inbound connection from the application's security group.

fixed: Options B, C and D were garbled by text splitting and have been reconstructed.

e.why: VPC peering is the cheapest way to connect two VPCs in the same Region: there is no hourly charge, and data transfer within an Availability Zone over peering is free. Add peering routes in both VPCs' route tables and allow the application's security group in the ElastiCache cluster's security group.

others.B: A Transit VPC needs extra appliances or instances and costs more than a simple peering connection.
others.C: A peering connection has no security group; the inbound rule must be on the ElastiCache cluster's security group.
others.D: A Transit VPC costs more, and the rule must be on the ElastiCache security group, not the Transit VPC.

e.tip: Connecting two VPCs cheaply = VPC peering; reference the source security group in the target's inbound rule.

q:
A company is building an application that consists of several microservices. The company has decided to use container technologies to deploy its software on AWS. The company needs a solution that minimizes the amount of ongoing effort for maintenance and scaling. The company cannot manage additional infrastructure.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Deploy an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster.
o.B: Deploy the Kubernetes control plane on Amazon EC2 instances that span multiple Availability Zones.
o.C: Deploy an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service with an Amazon EC2 launch type. Specify a desired task number level of greater than or equal to 2.
o.D: Deploy an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service with a Fargate launch type. Specify a desired task number level of greater than or equal to 2.
o.E: Deploy Kubernetes worker nodes on Amazon EC2 instances that span multiple Availability Zones. Create a deployment that specifies two or more replicas for each microservice.

e.why: An ECS cluster with a service using the Fargate launch type means AWS manages the underlying compute, so there are no EC2 instances or control plane to patch or scale. Setting desired tasks to 2 or more provides availability with minimal ongoing maintenance.

others.B: Self-managing a Kubernetes control plane on EC2 is significant infrastructure to operate.
others.C: The EC2 launch type requires managing and scaling the container instances.
others.E: Self-managed Kubernetes worker nodes on EC2 are extra infrastructure to maintain.

e.tip: "Cannot manage infrastructure" for containers = Fargate.

q:
A company has a web application hosted over 10 Amazon EC2 instances with traffic directed by Amazon Route 53. The company occasionally experiences a timeout error when attempting to browse the application. The networking team finds that some DNS queries return IP addresses of unhealthy instances, resulting in the timeout error.

What should a solutions architect implement to overcome these timeout errors?

o.A: Create a Route 53 simple routing policy record for each EC2 instance. Associate a health check with each record.
o.B: Create a Route 53 failover routing policy record for each EC2 instance. Associate a health check with each record.
o.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with EC2 instances as its origin. Associate a health check with the EC2 instances.
o.D: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with a health check in front of the EC2 instances. Route to the ALB from Route 53.

e.why: An ALB performs health checks on its targets and only routes requests to healthy instances, while Route 53 points to the ALB with an alias record. Clients never receive an unhealthy instance IP because they only resolve the load balancer.

others.A: Simple routing records do not support health checks.
others.B: Failover routing supports only a primary and secondary, not distribution across 10 active instances.
others.C: CloudFront does not health-check EC2 origins in this way and would still need a load balancer for distributing dynamic requests.

e.tip: Route 53 health checks are DNS-level and cached by TTL; an ALB gives immediate per-request health awareness.

q:
A solutions architect needs to design a highly available application consisting of web, application, and database tiers. HTTPS content delivery should be as close to the edge as possible, with the least delivery time.

Which solution meets these requirements and is MOST secure?

o.A: Configure a public Application Load Balancer (ALB) with multiple redundant Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver HTTPS content using the public ALB as the origin.
o.B: Configure a public Application Load Balancer with multiple redundant Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver HTTPS content using the EC2 instances as the origin.
o.C: Configure a public Application Load Balancer (ALB) with multiple redundant Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver HTTPS content using the public ALB as the origin.
o.D: Configure a public Application Load Balancer with multiple redundant Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver HTTPS content using the EC2 instances as the origin.

e.why: Placing EC2 instances in private subnets behind a public ALB keeps the servers unreachable from the internet, and using the ALB as the CloudFront origin delivers HTTPS from edge locations with lowest latency. This is both highly available and the most secure arrangement.

others.A: Instances in public subnets are needlessly exposed to the internet.
others.B: Instances in private subnets cannot be reached directly by CloudFront as an origin.
others.D: Public instances as direct origins bypass the load balancer and expose the servers.

e.tip: Most secure web tier: CloudFront -> public ALB -> EC2 in private subnets.

q:
A company has a popular gaming platform running on AWS. The application is sensitive to latency because latency can impact the user experience and introduce unfair advantages to some players. The application is deployed in every AWS Region. It runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are part of Auto Scaling groups configured behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs). A solutions architect needs to implement a mechanism to monitor the health of the application and redirect traffic to healthy endpoints.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Configure an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Add a listener for the port that the application listens on, and attach it to a Regional endpoint in each Region. Add the ALB as the endpoint.
o.B: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and specify the ALB as the origin server. Configure the cache behavior to use origin cache headers. Use AWS Lambda functions to optimize the traffic.
o.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and specify Amazon S3 as the origin server. Configure the cache behavior to use origin cache headers. Use AWS Lambda functions to optimize the traffic.
o.D: Configure an Amazon DynamoDB database to serve as the data store for the application. Create a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster to act as the in-memory cache for DynamoDB hosting the application data.

e.why: AWS Global Accelerator routes users over the AWS global network to the nearest healthy Regional endpoint, using static anycast IPs. It continuously health-checks the ALB endpoints and fails over quickly, which suits latency-sensitive gaming traffic, including non-HTTP protocols.

others.B: CloudFront caching does not help a dynamic, latency-sensitive game and does not natively multi-Region fail over with health checks like this.
others.C: An S3 origin is for static content and does not route to the application ALBs.
others.D: DAX caches DynamoDB reads; it does not monitor endpoint health or redirect traffic.

e.tip: Multi-Region health-based routing with static IPs and low latency (TCP/UDP): Global Accelerator.

q:
A company has one million users that use its mobile app. The company must analyze the data usage in near-real time. The company also must encrypt the data in near-real time and must store the data in a centralized location in Apache Parquet format for further processing.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application to analyze the data. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to send the data to the Kinesis Data Analytics application.
o.B: Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to analyze the data. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to send the data to the EMR cluster.
o.C: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to analyze the data.
o.D: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application to analyze the data.

e.why: Kinesis Data Firehose is fully managed, can encrypt data and convert records to Apache Parquet before delivering to S3, and Kinesis Data Analytics (now Managed Service for Apache Flink) analyzes the stream in near-real time. Both are serverless, giving the least operational overhead.

others.A: Kinesis Data Streams cannot write directly to S3 and adding Lambda glue increases overhead.
others.B: Data Streams cannot store to S3 directly, and EMR is a cluster to manage.
others.C: EMR adds cluster management overhead compared with serverless Kinesis Data Analytics.

e.tip: Firehose: managed delivery to S3 with built-in Parquet/ORC format conversion.

q:
A gaming company has a web application that displays scores. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application stores data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Users are starting to experience long delays and interruptions that are caused by database read performance. The company wants to improve the user experience while minimizing changes to the application’s architecture.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon ElastiCache in front of the database.
o.B: Use RDS Proxy between the application and the database.
o.C: Migrate the application from EC2 instances to AWS Lambda.
o.D: Migrate the database from Amazon RDS for MySQL to Amazon DynamoDB.

fixed: Option B contained answer text instead of option text, and option D was truncated; they have been reconstructed.

e.why: Placing Amazon ElastiCache in front of RDS caches frequently read score data in memory, offloading reads from the database and cutting latency. It improves user experience with minimal change to the existing architecture.

others.B: RDS Proxy pools connections, which helps connection storms but does not reduce read load or speed up read queries.
others.C: Moving compute to Lambda does not address database read performance and is a large architecture change.
others.D: Migrating to DynamoDB requires major application and data model changes.

e.tip: Database read latency on hot data = add a cache such as ElastiCache.

q:
An ecommerce company has noticed performance degradation of its Amazon RDS based web application. The performance degradation is attributed to an increase in the number of read-only SQL queries triggered by business analysts. A solutions architect needs to solve the problem with minimal changes to the existing web application.

What should the solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Export the data to Amazon DynamoDB and have the business analysts run their queries.
o.B: Load the data into Amazon ElastiCache and have the business analysts run their queries.
o.C: Create a read replica of the primary database and have the business analysts run their queries.
o.D: Copy the data into an Amazon Redshift cluster and have the business analysts run their queries.

e.why: An RDS read replica serves the analysts' read-only SQL queries from a separate instance, removing load from the primary. The analysts keep using SQL against the same schema, and the web application needs no changes.

others.A: DynamoDB is NoSQL, so analysts' SQL queries would need rewriting, plus an export pipeline.
others.B: ElastiCache is a cache, not a store analysts can run ad hoc SQL queries against.
others.D: Redshift requires building a data loading pipeline and is more change than needed.

e.tip: Offload read-only reporting from RDS: read replica.

q:
A company is using a centralized AWS account to store log data in various Amazon S3 buckets. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the data is encrypted at rest before the data is uploaded to the S3 buckets. The data also must be encrypted in transit.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Use client-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
o.B: Use server-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
o.C: Create bucket policies that require the use of server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for S3 uploads.
o.D: Enable the security option to encrypt the S3 buckets through the use of a default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key.

e.why: Client-side encryption encrypts the data before it leaves the client, so it is already encrypted at rest when uploaded, and the upload uses HTTPS for encryption in transit. Only client-side encryption meets the 'encrypted before upload' requirement.

others.B: Server-side encryption encrypts after S3 receives the data, not before upload.
others.C: SSE-S3 enforcement still encrypts only after arrival in S3.
others.D: Default KMS bucket encryption is server-side and happens after upload.

e.tip: "Encrypt before uploading" = client-side encryption.

q:
A solutions architect observes that a nightly batch processing job is automatically scaled up for 1 hour before the desired Amazon EC2 capacity is reached. The peak capacity is the ‘same every night and the batch jobs always start at 1 AM. The solutions architect needs to find a cost-effective solution that will allow for the desired EC2 capacity to be reached quickly and allow the Auto Scaling group to scale down after the batch jobs are complete.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Increase the minimum capacity for the Auto Scaling group.
o.B: Increase the maximum capacity for the Auto Scaling group.
o.C: Configure scheduled scaling to scale up to the desired compute level.
o.D: Change the scaling policy to add more EC2 instances during each scaling operation.

e.why: Scheduled scaling raises the Auto Scaling group's capacity at a set time (just before 1 AM) because the peak is predictable, so capacity is ready when jobs start. A scheduled action can then lower capacity, letting the group scale down afterwards, which is cost-effective.

others.A: Raising minimum capacity keeps instances running all day, wasting money.
others.B: Maximum capacity only caps scaling; it does not speed up reaching desired capacity.
others.D: Larger step adjustments still react after load appears and do not pre-provision for a known schedule.

e.tip: Predictable recurring load: scheduled scaling (or predictive scaling).

q:
A company serves a dynamic website from a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website needs to support multiple languages to serve customers around the world. The website’s architecture is running in the us-west-1 Region and is exhibiting high request latency for users that are located in other parts of the world.

The website needs to serve requests quickly and efficiently regardless of a user’s location. However, the company does not want to recreate the existing architecture across multiple Regions.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Replace the existing architecture with a website that is served from an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin. Set the cache behavior settings to cache based on the Accept-Language request header.
o.B: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the ALB as the origin. Set the cache behavior settings to cache based on the Accept-Language request header.
o.C: Create an Amazon API Gateway API that is integrated with the ALB. Configure the API to use the HTTP integration type. Set up an API Gateway stage to enable the API cache based on the Accept-Language request header.
o.D: Launch an EC2 instance in each additional Region and configure NGINX to act as a cache server for that Region. Put all the EC2 instances and the ALB behind an Amazon Route 53 record set with a geolocation routing policy.

fixed: Options B and C were garbled (C truncated, B replaced by C's tail) and have been reconstructed.

e.why: A CloudFront distribution with the existing ALB as origin serves users from edge locations worldwide without rebuilding the stack in other Regions. Caching based on the Accept-Language header stores a separate cached version for each language.

others.A: Replacing a dynamic site with S3 static hosting does not support the dynamic application.
others.C: An API Gateway cache sits in a single Region, so distant users still see high latency.
others.D: Running NGINX cache servers in each Region recreates infrastructure across Regions and adds overhead.

e.tip: Global low latency without multi-Region deployment = CloudFront in front of the existing origin.

q:
A rapidly growing ecommerce company is running its workloads in a single AWS Region. A solutions architect must create a disaster recovery (DR) strategy that includes a different AWS Region. The company wants its database to be up to date in the DR Region with the least possible latency. The remaining infrastructure in the DR Region needs to run at reduced capacity and must be able to scale up if necessary.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LOWEST recovery time objective (RTO)?

o.A: Use an Amazon Aurora global database with a pilot light deployment.
o.B: Use an Amazon Aurora global database with a warm standby deployment.
o.C: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a pilot light deployment.
o.D: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a warm standby deployment.

e.why: Aurora global database replicates to the secondary Region with typically under 1 second of lag using storage-level replication, keeping the DR database current. A warm standby runs a scaled-down but fully functional copy of the infrastructure that can scale up immediately, giving a lower RTO than pilot light.

others.A: Pilot light keeps only core components running, so application servers must be started and scaled, giving a higher RTO than warm standby.
others.C: RDS Multi-AZ is within a single Region and does not replicate to a DR Region.
others.D: Multi-AZ provides no cross-Region copy of the database, so it cannot serve a DR Region.

e.tip: DR RTO order (fastest to slowest): multi-site active/active, warm standby, pilot light, backup and restore.

q:
A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to implement a disaster recovery (DR) solution for the application. The DR solution needs to have a recovery time objective (RTO) of less than 4 hours. The DR solution also needs to use the fewest possible AWS resources during normal operations.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.A: Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to a secondary AWS Region. Automate infrastructure deployment in the secondary Region by using AWS Lambda and custom scripts.
o.B: Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to a secondary AWS Region. Automate infrastructure deployment in the secondary Region by using AWS CloudFormation.
o.C: Launch EC2 instances in a secondary AWS Region. Keep the EC2 instances in the secondary Region active at all times.
o.D: Launch EC2 instances in a secondary Availability Zone. Keep the EC2 instances in the secondary Availability Zone active at all times.

e.why: Copying AMIs to a secondary Region and using CloudFormation to deploy the infrastructure on demand uses almost no resources during normal operation, and a templated stack can be launched well within a 4-hour RTO. CloudFormation is the managed, repeatable way to do this, making it the most operationally efficient.

others.A: Custom Lambda scripts for infrastructure deployment are more effort to build and maintain than CloudFormation.
others.C: Keeping instances running in a second Region all the time consumes the most resources.
others.D: Always-on instances in another AZ use extra resources and do not protect against a Regional outage.

e.tip: Backup and restore plus IaC (CloudFormation) satisfies RTOs of hours at minimal cost.

q:
A company runs an internal browser-based application. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The Auto Scaling group scales up to 20 instances during work hours, but scales down to 2 instances overnight. Staff are complaining that the application is very slow when the day begins, although it runs well by mid-morning.

How should the scaling be changed to address the staff complaints and keep costs to a minimum?

o.A: Implement a scheduled action that sets the desired capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.
o.B: Implement a step scaling action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
o.C: Implement a target tracking action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
o.D: Implement a scheduled action that sets the minimum and maximum capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.

e.why: The keyed answer lowers the target tracking CPU threshold and reduces cooldown so the group starts adding instances earlier and faster as morning load ramps, while still scaling only as much as demand requires. This addresses the slow start while keeping cost to a minimum versus jumping straight to 20 instances.

others.A: Forcing desired capacity to 20 provisions full capacity regardless of actual demand, which may cost more than necessary.
others.B: Step scaling works but requires managing step adjustments and alarms; target tracking is simpler and self-adjusting.
others.D: Setting minimum and maximum to 20 locks the group at 20 instances and prevents scaling down during the day.

e.tip: Many experts prefer a scheduled action (A) for predictable daily ramps; know both arguments.

q:
A company has a multi-tier application deployed on several Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. An Amazon RDS for Oracle instance is the application’ s data layer that uses Oracle-specific PL/SQL functions. Traffic to the application has been steadily increasing. This is causing the EC2 instances to become overloaded and the RDS instance to run out of storage. The Auto Scaling group does not have any scaling metrics and defines the minimum healthy instance count only. The company predicts that traffic will continue to increase at a steady but unpredictable rate before leveling off.

What should a solutions architect do to ensure the system can automatically scale for the increased traffic? (Choose two.)

o.A: Configure storage Auto Scaling on the RDS for Oracle instance.
o.B: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora to use Auto Scaling storage.
o.C: Configure an alarm on the RDS for Oracle instance for low free storage space.
o.D: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the average CPU as the scaling metric.
o.E: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the average free memory as the scaling metric.

e.why: RDS storage autoscaling automatically grows the Oracle instance's storage when free space runs low, with no migration needed. Adding a target tracking policy on average CPU to the Auto Scaling group lets EC2 capacity scale automatically with unpredictable traffic growth.

others.B: Aurora does not support Oracle PL/SQL, so migration would require code changes.
others.C: An alarm only notifies; it does not automatically add storage.
others.E: Free memory is not a default EC2 metric (needs the CloudWatch agent) and is a less suitable scaling signal than CPU here.

e.tip: RDS storage running out: enable storage autoscaling with a maximum storage threshold.

q:
A company provides an online service for posting video content and transcoding it for use by any mobile platform. The application architecture uses Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard to collect and store the videos so that multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances can access the video content for processing. As the popularity of the service has grown over time, the storage costs have become too expensive.

Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?

o.A: Use AWS Storage Gateway for files to store and process the video content.
o.B: Use AWS Storage Gateway for volumes to store and process the video content.
o.C: Use Amazon EFS for storing the video content. Once processing is complete, transfer the files to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS).
o.D: Use Amazon S3 for storing the video content. Move the files temporarily over to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume attached to the server for processing.

e.why: Amazon S3 is far cheaper per GB than EFS Standard for storing a large, growing video library. Instances can copy files temporarily to an EBS volume for processing, so only working data occupies block storage while S3 holds everything durably.

others.A: Storage Gateway is for hybrid on-premises access and adds cost and complexity for a cloud-native workload.
others.B: Volume Gateway serves iSCSI volumes to on-premises hosts and is not a cost fix for EC2 in AWS.
others.C: Keeping content on EFS and then also copying to EBS keeps the expensive EFS storage and adds more.

e.tip: Cost reduction for bulk storage usually means S3 (with lifecycle tiers); EFS IA/archive classes are another option.

q:
A company wants to create an application to store employee data in a hierarchical structured relationship. The company needs a minimum-latency response to high-traffic queries for the employee data and must protect any sensitive data. The company also needs to receive monthly email messages if any financial information is present in the employee data.

Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use Amazon Redshift to store the employee data in hierarchies. Unload the data to Amazon S3 every month.
o.B: Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the employee data in hierarchies. Export the data to Amazon S3 every month.
o.C: Configure Amazon Macie for the AWS account. Integrate Macie with Amazon EventBridge to send monthly events to AWS Lambda.
o.D: Use Amazon Athena to analyze the employee data in Amazon S3. Integrate Athena with Amazon QuickSight to publish analysis dashboards and share the dashboards with users.
o.E: Configure Amazon Macie for the AWS account. Integrate Macie with Amazon EventBridge to send monthly notifications through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) subscription.

e.why: DynamoDB delivers single-digit millisecond latency at high traffic and can model hierarchical data with composite keys, and exporting to S3 lets Macie scan it. Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data like financial information in S3, and its findings sent through EventBridge to an SNS topic provide email notifications.

others.A: Redshift is an analytics warehouse, not designed for minimum-latency high-traffic lookups.
others.C: Sending events to Lambda does not by itself deliver email notifications; SNS is the direct way.
others.D: Athena and QuickSight provide analysis dashboards but do not detect sensitive data or send email alerts.

e.tip: Sensitive data/PII discovery in S3 = Macie; email alert = EventBridge -> SNS.

q:
A company has an application that is backed by an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company’s compliance requirements specify that database backups must be taken every month, must be available for 6 months, and must be retained for 7 years.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an AWS Backup plan to back up the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Specify a lifecycle policy that transitions the backup to cold storage after 6 months. Set the retention period for each backup to 7 years.
o.B: Create a DynamoDB on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Transition the backup to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 6 months. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to delete backups that are older than 7 years.
o.C: Use the AWS SDK to develop a script that creates an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the script on the first day of each month. Create a second script that will run on the second day of each month to transition DynamoDB backups that are older than 6 months to cold storage and to delete backups that are older than 7 years.
o.D: Use the AWS CLI to create an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the command on the first day of each month with a cron expression. Specify in the command to transition the backups to cold storage after 6 months and to delete the backups after 7 years.

e.why: AWS Backup supports DynamoDB with a scheduled monthly backup rule, a lifecycle transition to cold storage after 6 months, and a 7-year retention period, all managed centrally. This meets every compliance requirement without custom code.

others.B: DynamoDB on-demand backups are not stored as S3 objects you manage, so S3 Lifecycle and Glacier transitions cannot be applied.
others.C: Custom scripts add operational burden, and native DynamoDB backups have no cold storage tier outside AWS Backup.
others.D: The CLI create-backup command cannot set cold storage transitions or expiration.

e.tip: Retention plus cold-storage lifecycle for backups = AWS Backup plan.

q:
A company is using Amazon CloudFront with its website. The company has enabled logging on the CloudFront distribution, and logs are saved in one of the company’s Amazon S3 buckets. The company needs to perform advanced analyses on the logs and build visualizations.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with AWS Glue.
o.B: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.
o.C: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with AWS Glue.
o.D: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.

e.why: Amazon Athena runs standard SQL directly against CloudFront logs stored in S3 without loading data, and Amazon QuickSight connects to Athena to build visualizations and dashboards. This is the serverless, purpose-built combination for log analytics and visualization.

others.A: AWS Glue is for ETL and cataloging, not visualization.
others.C: DynamoDB does not query files in S3 with standard SQL, and Glue does not visualize.
others.D: DynamoDB cannot analyze S3 log files with SQL.

e.tip: Query logs in S3 = Athena; visualize = QuickSight.

q:
A company runs a fleet of web servers using an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. After a routine compliance check, the company sets a standard that requires a recovery point objective (RPO) of less than 1 second for all its production databases.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the DB instance.
o.B: Enable auto scaling for the DB instance in one Availability Zone.
o.C: Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and create multiple read replicas in a separate Availability Zone.
o.D: Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) change data capture (CDC) tasks.

e.why: RDS Multi-AZ uses synchronous replication to a standby in another AZ, so committed transactions exist on both and the RPO is effectively zero. On failover no committed data is lost, meeting an RPO of under 1 second.

others.B: RDS has no instance auto scaling within an AZ, and it would not affect RPO.
others.C: Read replicas use asynchronous replication, so lag can exceed 1 second and data can be lost.
others.D: DMS CDC is asynchronous and not designed as a sub-second RPO HA mechanism.

e.tip: Synchronous replication (Multi-AZ) = near-zero RPO; async replicas = possible data loss.

q:
A company runs a web application that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnet of a VPC. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across the public subnets directs web traffic to the EC2 instances. The company wants to implement new security measures to restrict inbound traffic from the ALB to the EC2 instances while preventing access from any other source inside or outside the private subnet of the EC2 instances.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure a route in a route table to direct traffic from the internet to the private IP addresses of the EC2 instances.
o.B: Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to only allow traffic that comes from the security group for the ALB.
o.C: Move the EC2 instances into the public subnet. Give the EC2 instances a set of Elastic IP addresses.
o.D: Configure the security group for the ALB to allow any TCP traffic on any port.

fixed: Option B text was missing and has been reconstructed.

e.why: Referencing the ALB's security group as the only allowed inbound source in the EC2 instances' security group permits only traffic from the load balancer. All other sources, inside or outside the private subnet, are blocked.

others.A: Route tables cannot route internet traffic directly to private IPs, and routing does not restrict sources.
others.C: Moving instances to public subnets with Elastic IPs exposes them to the internet.
others.D: Opening the ALB security group to any TCP traffic weakens security and does not restrict the instances.

e.tip: Allow only the load balancer to reach targets = security group rule that references the ALB's security group.

q:
A research company runs experiments that are powered by a simulation application and a visualization application. The simulation application runs on Linux and outputs intermediate data to an NFS share every 5 minutes. The visualization application is a Windows desktop application that displays the simulation output and requires an SMB file system.

The company maintains two synchronized file systems. This strategy is causing data duplication and inefficient resource usage. The company needs to migrate the applications to AWS without making code changes to either application.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate both applications to AWS Lambda. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to exchange data between the applications.
o.B: Migrate both applications to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon FSx File Gateway for storage.
o.C: Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to exchange data between the applications.
