o.D: Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for storage.

e.why: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides a single file system that is accessible simultaneously over NFS and SMB (multiprotocol). The Linux simulation and Windows visualization apps on EC2 can share the same data without duplication or code changes.

others.A: Rewriting for Lambda and using S3 requires code changes and Lambda does not run Windows desktop apps.
others.B: FSx File Gateway provides on-premises SMB access to FSx for Windows, not NFS, and ECS migration needs changes.
others.C: SQS is a message queue, not a shared file system, so applications would need code changes.

e.tip: Need both NFS and SMB on one file system = FSx for NetApp ONTAP.

q:
As part of budget planning, management wants a report of AWS billed items listed by user. The data will be used to create department budgets. A solutions architect needs to determine the most efficient way to obtain this report information.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Run a query with Amazon Athena to generate the report.
o.B: Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report.
o.C: Access the bill details from the billing dashboard and download the bill.
o.D: Modify a cost budget in AWS Budgets to alert with Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).

e.why: Cost Explorer can group and filter costs by dimensions and cost allocation tags (for example a user or department tag) and the resulting report can be downloaded as CSV. It is the most efficient built-in way to produce a cost-by-user report for budget planning.

others.A: Athena requires setting up CUR delivery and writing queries, which is more work.
others.C: The billing dashboard bill is not broken down by user.
others.D: AWS Budgets sends alerts on thresholds; it does not produce an itemized report by user.

e.tip: Ad-hoc cost reports by tag/service = Cost Explorer; detailed line items = CUR + Athena.

q:
A company hosts its static website by using Amazon S3. The company wants to add a contact form to its webpage. The contact form will have dynamic server-side components for users to input their name, email address, phone number, and user message. The company anticipates that there will be fewer than 100 site visits each month.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Host a dynamic contact form page in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to any third-party email provider.
o.B: Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with an AWS Lambda backend that makes a call to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
o.C: Convert the static webpage to dynamic by deploying Amazon Lightsail. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.
o.D: Create a t2.micro Amazon EC2 instance. Deploy a LAMP (Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP/Perl/Python) stack to host the webpage. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

e.why: API Gateway plus Lambda is serverless and billed per request, so fewer than 100 visits a month cost almost nothing (often within the free tier). The Lambda function calls Amazon SES to email the submitted form, and the static S3 site stays unchanged.

others.A: Running ECS continuously costs far more than needed for a handful of submissions.
others.C: Lightsail adds an always-on server and WorkMail is a mailbox service, not a form email sender.
others.D: An always-on EC2 LAMP instance costs more and adds server management.

e.tip: Low-traffic dynamic feature on a static S3 site: API Gateway + Lambda.

q:
A company has a static website that is hosted on Amazon CloudFront in front of Amazon S3. The static website uses a database backend. The company notices that the website does not reflect updates that have been made in the website’s Git repository. The company checks the continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline between the Git repository and Amazon S3. The company verifies that the webhooks are configured properly and that the CI/CD pipeline is sending messages that indicate successful deployments.

A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that displays the updates on the website.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Add an Application Load Balancer.
o.B: Add Amazon ElastiCache for Redis or Memcached to the database layer of the web application.
o.C: Invalidate the CloudFront cache.
o.D: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to validate the website’s SSL certificate.

e.why: CloudFront is serving cached copies of the old objects until their TTL expires. Creating a CloudFront invalidation (for example for /* or changed paths) forces edge locations to fetch the updated files from S3 so the new deployment appears.

others.A: An ALB does not serve S3 static content and does not affect CloudFront caching.
others.B: Caching the database layer does nothing about stale static files at the CDN edge.
others.D: Certificate validation is unrelated to stale content.

e.tip: Deployed but not visible behind CloudFront = invalidate cache or use versioned file names.

q:
A company wants to migrate a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers: an application tier, a business tier, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server. The company wants to use specific features of SQL Server such as native backups and Data Quality Services. The company also needs to share files for processing between the tiers.

How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?

o.A: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.
o.B: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.
o.C: Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file sharing between the tiers.
o.D: Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for file sharing between the tiers.

e.why: SQL Server native backups and Data Quality Services require full control of SQL Server, so the database runs on EC2 rather than RDS. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides a fully managed SMB share for the Windows tiers to exchange files.

others.A: FSx File Gateway is for giving on-premises clients cached access to FSx, not for sharing between EC2 tiers.
others.C: RDS for SQL Server does not support Data Quality Services, and EFS is NFS-based for Linux, not Windows.
others.D: RDS lacks DQS, and an io2 EBS volume is not a general shared file system for Windows tiers.

e.tip: Need SQL Server features RDS lacks = SQL Server on EC2; Windows file sharing = FSx for Windows.

q:
A company is migrating a Linux-based web server group to AWS. The web servers must access files in a shared file store for some content. The company must not make any changes to the application.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon S3 Standard bucket with access to the web servers.
o.B: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin.
o.C: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on all web servers.
o.D: Configure a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume to all web servers.

e.why: Amazon EFS is a managed NFS file system that multiple Linux instances can mount concurrently using standard file system semantics. The application continues to use file paths, so no changes are needed.

others.A: S3 is object storage accessed via API, which would require application changes.
others.B: CloudFront with S3 is for content delivery, not a mounted shared file store.
others.D: Standard gp3 EBS volumes cannot be attached to multiple instances (Multi-Attach is io1/io2 only and needs a cluster-aware file system).

e.tip: Shared file system for Linux EC2 = EFS; for Windows = FSx for Windows.

q:
A company has an AWS Lambda function that needs read access to an Amazon S3 bucket that is located in the same AWS account.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure manner?

o.A: Apply an S3 bucket policy that grants read access to the S3 bucket.
o.B: Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.
o.C: Embed an access key and a secret key in the Lambda function’s code to grant the required IAM permissions for read access to the S3 bucket.
o.D: Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to all S3 buckets in the account.

e.why: Assigning an IAM execution role to the Lambda function provides temporary, automatically rotated credentials. Scoping the attached policy to read access on only that specific bucket follows least privilege, making it the most secure approach.

others.A: A bucket policy alone works but is not the standard least-privilege identity approach, and still needs a principal; the execution role is preferred.
others.C: Embedding long-term access keys in code is insecure.
others.D: Granting read on all buckets violates least privilege.

e.tip: AWS service needs access = IAM role with least-privilege policy, never embedded keys.

q:
A company hosts a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group that scales in response to user demand. The company wants to optimize cost savings without making a long-term commitment.

Which EC2 instance purchasing option should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Dedicated Instances only
o.B: On-Demand Instances only
o.C: A mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances
o.D: A mix of On-Demand Instances and Reserved Instances

e.why: A mix of On-Demand for the baseline and Spot Instances for scalable capacity reduces cost significantly (Spot can be up to 90% cheaper) with no long-term commitment. Auto Scaling groups support mixed instances policies to combine both.

others.A: Dedicated Instances cost more and do nothing for savings.
others.B: On-Demand only has no commitment but misses Spot savings.
others.D: Reserved Instances require a 1- or 3-year commitment.

e.tip: "No long-term commitment" rules out RIs and Savings Plans.

q:
A media company uses Amazon CloudFront for its publicly available streaming video content. The company wants to secure the video content that is hosted in Amazon S3 by controlling who has access. Some of the company’s users are using a custom HTTP client that does not support cookies. Some of the company’s users are unable to change the hardcoded URLs that they are using for access.

Which services or methods will meet these requirements with the LEAST impact to the users? (Choose two.)

o.A: Signed cookies
o.B: Signed URLs
o.C: AWS AppSync
o.D: JSON Web Token (JWT)
o.E: AWS Secrets Manager

e.why: CloudFront signed cookies control access to multiple files without changing URLs, which suits users with hardcoded URLs. Signed URLs embed the authorization in the URL itself, which suits the custom HTTP client that cannot handle cookies. Together they cover both user groups with the least impact.

others.C: AWS AppSync is a managed GraphQL API service, not a CloudFront content access control.
others.D: JWTs would need custom validation logic at the edge and client changes.
others.E: Secrets Manager stores secrets; it does not control viewer access to CloudFront content.

e.tip: No cookie support -> signed URLs; cannot change URLs -> signed cookies.

q:
A company is preparing a new data platform that will ingest real-time streaming data from multiple sources. The company needs to transform the data before writing the data to Amazon S3. The company needs the ability to use SQL to query the transformed data.

Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.
o.B: Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to stream the data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.
o.C: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to ingest the data. Use Amazon EMR to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.
o.D: Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to stream the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use the Amazon RDS query editor to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.
o.E: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to write the data to Amazon S3. Use the Amazon RDS query editor to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

e.why: Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Data Analytics transforming the stream and Firehose delivering to S3, queried by Athena, is a complete streaming pipeline. Likewise MSK for ingestion with AWS Glue streaming ETL transforming and writing to S3, then Athena for SQL, also meets all requirements.

others.C: DMS is for database migration/replication, not ingesting real-time streams from many sources.
others.D: The RDS query editor cannot query data stored in S3.
others.E: The RDS query editor cannot query S3 data, so SQL over the transformed data fails.

e.tip: SQL over data in S3 = Athena (or Redshift Spectrum).

q:
A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached its end of life. The company wants to use AWS as part of a new backup solution and wants to maintain local access to all the data while it is backed up on AWS. The company wants to ensure that the data backed up on AWS is automatically and securely transferred.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Snowball to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Configure on-premises systems to mount the Snowball S3 endpoint to provide local access to the data.
o.B: Use AWS Snowball Edge to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Use the Snowball Edge file interface to provide on-premises systems with local access to the data.
o.C: Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a cached volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and configure a percentage of data to cache locally. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.
o.D: Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.

e.why: A Storage Gateway stored volume gateway keeps the complete dataset on premises for low-latency local access while asynchronously backing it up to AWS as EBS snapshots. Transfers are automatic and encrypted in transit, meeting all the requirements.

others.A: Snowball is a one-time offline migration device and does not provide ongoing backup or local access.
others.B: Snowball Edge is for transfer or edge compute, not a continuous backup solution with full local access.
others.C: Cached volumes keep only frequently accessed data locally, so not all data remains locally accessible.

e.tip: All data local + async backup = stored volumes; only hot data local = cached volumes.

q:
An application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket. Traffic must not traverse the internet.

How should a solutions architect configure access to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a private hosted zone by using Amazon Route 53.
o.B: Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
o.C: Configure the EC2 instances to use a NAT gateway to access the S3 bucket.
o.D: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the VPC and the S3 bucket.

fixed: Option B was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 adds a route in the VPC route table so traffic to S3 stays on the AWS network and never crosses the internet. Gateway endpoints for S3 have no additional charge.

others.A: A Route 53 private hosted zone handles DNS names but does not create a private network path to S3.
others.C: A NAT gateway sends S3 traffic to the public endpoint through the internet gateway.
others.D: Site-to-Site VPN connects on-premises networks to a VPC; you cannot create a VPN to an S3 bucket.

e.tip: EC2 to S3 privately = gateway VPC endpoint.

q:
An ecommerce company stores terabytes of customer data in the AWS Cloud. The data contains personally identifiable information (PII). The company wants to use the data in three applications. Only one of the applications needs to process the PII. The PII must be removed before the other two applications process the data.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create a proxy application layer to intercept and process the data that each application requests.
o.B: Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Process and transform the data by using S3 Object Lambda before returning the data to the requesting application.
o.C: Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon S3 buckets so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective S3 bucket.
o.D: Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon DynamoDB tables so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective DynamoDB table.

e.why: S3 Object Lambda lets you attach a Lambda function to S3 GET requests via an access point so data is transformed (for example PII redacted) on the fly before it reaches the application. One copy of the data serves all three apps, giving the least operational overhead.

others.A: Building and operating a custom proxy layer adds significant overhead.
others.C: Maintaining three transformed copies requires ongoing processing pipelines and extra storage.
others.D: Three DynamoDB tables duplicate data and require custom transformation pipelines.

e.tip: Modify or redact S3 data per requester without copies = S3 Object Lambda.

q:
A development team has launched a new application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances inside a development VPC. A solutions architect needs to create a new VPC in the same account. The new VPC will be peered with the development VPC. The VPC CIDR block for the development VPC is 192.168.0.0/24. The solutions architect needs to create a CIDR block for the new VPC. The CIDR block must be valid for a VPC peering connection to the development VPC.

What is the SMALLEST CIDR block that meets these requirements?

e.why: Peered VPCs must have non-overlapping CIDR blocks, and a VPC's CIDR must be between /16 and /28. 10.0.1.0/24 does not overlap 192.168.0.0/24 and is valid; it is the smallest valid option offered.

others.A: A /32 is not a valid VPC CIDR size (minimum is /28).
others.B: This overlaps the development VPC exactly, so peering is not allowed.
others.C: A /32 is not a valid VPC CIDR size.

e.tip: VPC CIDR range: /16 to /28; peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs.

q:
A company deploys an application on five Amazon EC2 instances. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributes traffic to the instances by using a target group. The average CPU usage on each of the instances is below 10% most of the time, with occasional surges to 65%.

A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to automate the scalability of the application. The solution must optimize the cost of the architecture and must ensure that the application has enough CPU resources when surges occur.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that enters the ALARM state when the CPUUtilization metric is less than 20%. Create an AWS Lambda function that the CloudWatch alarm invokes to terminate one of the EC2 instances in the ALB target group.
o.B: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set a target tracking scaling policy that is based on the ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, the maximum instances to 6, and the target value to 50%. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.
o.C: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, and the maximum instances to 6. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.
o.D: Create two Amazon CloudWatch alarms. Configure the first CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization metric is below 20%. Configure the second CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization matric is above 50%. Configure the alarms to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an email message. After receiving the message, log in to decrease or increase the number of EC2 instances that are running.

e.why: An Auto Scaling group attached to the existing target group with a target tracking policy on ASGAverageCPUUtilization at 50% automatically adds instances during surges and removes them when CPU is low. Minimum 2 and maximum 6 keep availability while optimizing cost.

others.A: A Lambda that only terminates instances cannot add capacity during surges.
others.C: Without a scaling policy, the group never scales with demand.
others.D: Manual scaling after email alerts is not automated.

e.tip: Keep a metric near a value automatically = target tracking.

q:
A company is running a critical business application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group and access an Amazon RDS DB instance.

The design did not pass an operational review because the EC2 instances and the DB instance are all located in a single Availability Zone. A solutions architect must update the design to use a second Availability Zone.

Which solution will make the application highly available?

o.A: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.
o.B: Provision two subnets that extend across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.
o.C: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
o.D: Provision a subnet that extends across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.

e.why: Subnets are confined to a single Availability Zone, so you create one subnet per AZ and spread the Auto Scaling group across both. Enabling RDS Multi-AZ adds a synchronous standby in the second AZ with automatic failover, making both tiers highly available.

others.A: Connecting the DB instance to each network does not create a standby; it remains a single point of failure.
others.B: Subnets cannot span Availability Zones.
others.D: A subnet cannot extend across Availability Zones.

e.tip: Subnet = one AZ. DB HA = Multi-AZ.

q:
A research laboratory needs to process approximately 8 TB of data. The laboratory requires sub-millisecond latencies and a minimum throughput of 6 GBps for the storage subsystem. Hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux will distribute and process the data.

Which solution will meet the performance requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Sat each volume’ tiering policy to ALL. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the fila system on the EC2 instances.
o.B: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent SSD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent HDD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
o.D: Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume’s tiering policy to NONE. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.

fixed: Option D was truncated and its remainder had been split into a stray option E; D has been completed and E removed.

e.why: FSx for Lustre on persistent SSD storage delivers sub-millisecond latency and very high aggregate throughput for hundreds of Linux clients. Linking it to an S3 bucket lets it import raw data from S3 and export results back.

others.A: Tiering ALL moves data to the capacity pool, which adds latency, and ONTAP is not built for this level of HPC throughput.
others.C: HDD-based Lustre storage cannot deliver sub-millisecond latency.
others.D: FSx for NetApp ONTAP is a general-purpose NAS and is not suited to 6 GBps HPC throughput across hundreds of instances.

e.tip: HPC on Linux with S3 integration and sub-millisecond latency = FSx for Lustre on SSD.

q:
A company needs to migrate a legacy application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud because of hardware capacity constraints. The application runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The application’s database storage continues to grow over time.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon S3.
o.B: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS On-Demand Instances.
o.C: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.
o.D: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS Reserved Instances.

e.why: A 24/7 application gets the largest savings from Reserved Instances for the EC2 tier. Aurora storage automatically grows up to 128 TiB as the database expands, and Aurora Reserved Instances discount the always-on database compute.

others.A: Spot Instances can be interrupted, unsuitable for a 24/7 legacy app, and S3 is not a database replacement.
others.B: On-Demand RDS costs more than reserved capacity for a 24/7 database.
others.D: On-Demand EC2 costs more than Reserved Instances for constant usage.

e.tip: Steady 24/7 usage = Reserved Instances or Savings Plans.

q:
A university research laboratory needs to migrate 30 TB of data from an on-premises Windows file server to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. The laboratory has a 1 Gbps network link that many other departments in the university share.

The laboratory wants to implement a data migration service that will maximize the performance of the data transfer. However, the laboratory needs to be able to control the amount of bandwidth that the service uses to minimize the impact on other departments. The data migration must take place within the next 5 days.

Which AWS solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: AWS Snowcone
o.B: Amazon FSx File Gateway
o.C: AWS DataSync
o.D: AWS Transfer Family

e.why: AWS DataSync transfers data to FSx for Windows File Server with parallel, accelerated transfers and lets you set a bandwidth limit on tasks. 30 TB in 5 days needs about 0.56 Gbps, which fits on the shared 1 Gbps link with throttling.

others.A: Snowcone holds only 8-14 TB and shipping adds time, so it cannot carry 30 TB in time.
others.B: FSx File Gateway provides cached on-premises access to FSx, not a bulk migration service.
others.D: Transfer Family provides SFTP/FTPS/FTP endpoints for S3/EFS, not FSx for Windows migration.

e.tip: Online migration with bandwidth throttling into S3/EFS/FSx = DataSync.

q:
A company wants to create a mobile app that allows users to stream slow-motion video clips on their mobile devices. Currently, the app captures video clips and uploads the video clips in raw format into an Amazon S3 bucket. The app retrieves these video clips directly from the S3 bucket. However, the videos are large in their raw format.

Users are experiencing issues with buffering and playback on mobile devices. The company wants to implement solutions to maximize the performance and scalability of the app while minimizing operational overhead.

Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Deploy Amazon CloudFront for content delivery and caching.
o.B: Use AWS DataSync to replicate the video files across AW'S Regions in other S3 buckets.
o.C: Use Amazon Elastic Transcoder to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.
o.D: Deploy an Auto Sealing group of Amazon EC2 instances in Local Zones for content delivery and caching.
o.E: Deploy an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.

fixed: The question asks for two answers but the key listed only A; the key has been set to A and C, the accepted answer.

e.why: CloudFront caches and delivers the videos from edge locations close to mobile users, which reduces buffering and scales automatically. Amazon Elastic Transcoder (a managed service) converts the large raw videos into mobile-friendly formats and bitrates with no servers to manage.

others.B: Replicating raw files across Regions does not shrink the large videos or cache them near users.
others.D: Running EC2 fleets in Local Zones for caching adds a lot of operational overhead compared with CloudFront.
others.E: A self-managed EC2 transcoding fleet adds operational overhead compared with a managed transcoding service.

e.tip: Video playback issues = transcode with a managed service and deliver with CloudFront.

q:
A company is launching a new application deployed on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster and is using the Fargate launch type for ECS tasks. The company is monitoring CPU and memory usage because it is expecting high traffic to the application upon its launch. However, the company wants to reduce costs when utilization decreases.

What should a solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale at certain periods based on previous traffic patterns.
o.B: Use an AWS Lambda function to scale Amazon ECS based on metric breaches that trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
o.C: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with simple scaling policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
o.D: Use AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.

e.why: ECS service auto scaling uses AWS Application Auto Scaling; a target tracking policy on CPU or memory utilization automatically adds Fargate tasks under load and removes them when utilization falls, reducing cost. It is fully managed with no custom code.

others.A: EC2 Auto Scaling manages EC2 instances, and Fargate tasks have no instances to scale.
others.B: A custom Lambda scaler adds code and maintenance versus built-in service auto scaling.
others.C: EC2 Auto Scaling does not scale Fargate tasks.

e.tip: Scale ECS services, DynamoDB, Aurora replicas, etc. = Application Auto Scaling.

q:
A company recently created a disaster recovery site in a different AWS Region. The company needs to transfer large amounts of data back and forth between NFS file systems in the two Regions on a periodic basis.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS DataSync.
o.B: Use AWS Snowball devices.
o.C: Set up an SFTP server on Amazon EC2.
o.D: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).

e.why: AWS DataSync is a managed service that copies data between NFS file systems (including EFS) across Regions, with scheduling, encryption, integrity checks and incremental transfers. Periodic transfers need no infrastructure to manage.

others.B: Snowball devices are for offline transfer and impractical for periodic Region-to-Region copies.
others.C: An SFTP server on EC2 must be built, secured and maintained.
others.D: DMS migrates databases, not file systems.

e.tip: Scheduled file copies between storage systems/Regions = DataSync.

q:
A company is designing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed.

Which AWS solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
o.B: Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
o.C: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
o.D: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Assign an IAM role to the application to grant access to the S3 bucket. Mount the S3 bucket to the application server.

e.why: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed native Windows file system that SMB clients can access directly. It handles patching, backups and availability, unlike a self-managed file server.

others.A: DataSync moves data; it does not present a mountable shared file system.
others.B: A Windows file share on EC2 is self-managed, not fully managed.
others.D: S3 is object storage and is not natively accessible over SMB.

e.tip: Managed SMB = FSx for Windows (or FSx for ONTAP).

q:
A company wants to run an in-memory database for a latency-sensitive application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes more than 100,000 transactions each minute and requires high network throughput. A solutions architect needs to provide a cost-effective network design that minimizes data transfer charges.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Launch all EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with cluster strategy when launching EC2 instances.
o.B: Launch all EC2 instances in different Availability Zones within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with partition strategy when launching EC2 instances.
o.C: Deploy an Auto Scaling group to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones based on a network utilization target.
o.D: Deploy an Auto Scaling group with a step scaling policy to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones.

e.why: A cluster placement group packs instances close together in one Availability Zone for the lowest latency and highest network throughput. Keeping everything in the same AZ also avoids inter-AZ data transfer charges, making it cost-effective.

others.B: Spreading across AZs incurs inter-AZ data transfer charges and higher latency, and partition groups target fault isolation.
others.C: Multi-AZ Auto Scaling increases cross-AZ traffic costs and latency.
others.D: Step scaling across AZs does not reduce latency or data transfer charges.

e.tip: Lowest latency/highest throughput between instances = cluster placement group (single AZ).

q:
A company that primarily runs its application servers on premises has decided to migrate to AWS. The company wants to minimize its need to scale its Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) storage on premises. The company wants only its recently accessed data to remain stored locally.

Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?

o.A: Amazon S3 File Gateway
o.B: AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
o.C: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volumes
o.D: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes

e.why: Volume Gateway in cached mode presents iSCSI volumes whose primary data lives in S3, while only frequently or recently accessed data is cached locally. This minimizes on-premises iSCSI storage scaling.

others.A: S3 File Gateway presents NFS/SMB file shares, not iSCSI block storage.
others.B: Tape Gateway provides virtual tape libraries for backup software, not general iSCSI volumes.
others.C: Stored volumes keep the full dataset on premises, so local storage still needs to scale.

e.tip: iSCSI + only hot data local = cached volumes.

q:
A company has multiple AWS accounts that use consolidated billing. The company runs several active high performance Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances for 90 days. The company’s finance team has access to AWS Trusted Advisor in the consolidated billing account and all other AWS accounts.

The finance team needs to use the appropriate AWS account to access the Trusted Advisor check recommendations for RDS. The finance team must review the appropriate Trusted Advisor check to reduce RDS costs.

Which combination of steps should the finance team take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the account where the RDS instances are running.
o.B: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the consolidated billing account to see all RDS instance checks at the same time.
o.C: Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
o.D: Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.
o.E: Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon Redshift Reserved Node Optimization.

e.why: In a consolidated billing (Organizations) setup, the management/payer account can view Trusted Advisor recommendations across linked accounts in one place. The Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances check identifies instances with no connections that can be stopped or deleted to cut RDS costs.

others.A: Checking each account separately is less efficient than viewing all from the consolidated billing account.
others.C: The keyed answer prefers the idle instance check; RI optimization is a commitment-based recommendation rather than a direct waste check for these instances.
others.E: Redshift reserved node optimization is unrelated to RDS.

e.tip: Trusted Advisor cost checks include idle RDS instances, underutilized EC2 and RI optimization.

q:
A solutions architect needs to optimize storage costs. The solutions architect must identify any Amazon S3 buckets that are no longer being accessed or are rarely accessed.

Which solution will accomplish this goal with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 Storage Lens dashboard for advanced activity metrics.
o.B: Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 dashboard in the AWS Management Console.
o.C: Turn on the Amazon CloudWatch BucketSizeBytes metric for buckets. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the metrics data with Amazon Athena.
o.D: Turn on AWS CloudTrail for S3 object monitoring. Analyze bucket access patterns by using CloudTrail logs that are integrated with Amazon CloudWatch Logs.

e.why: S3 Storage Lens advanced metrics include activity metrics (such as GET request counts and bytes downloaded) per bucket in a ready-made dashboard, making cold or unused buckets easy to identify. It requires only enabling the feature, so operational overhead is lowest.

others.B: The basic S3 console dashboard does not show per-bucket access pattern analysis.
others.C: BucketSizeBytes measures storage size, not access, and Athena analysis adds work.
others.D: CloudTrail data events plus log analysis is costly and requires building queries.

e.tip: Org-wide S3 usage and activity insights = S3 Storage Lens.

q:
A company sells datasets to customers who do research in artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML). The datasets are large, formatted files that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The company hosts a web application that the customers use to purchase access to a given dataset. The web application is deployed on multiple Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. After a purchase is made, customers receive an S3 signed URL that allows access to the files.

The customers are distributed across North America and Europe. The company wants to reduce the cost that is associated with data transfers and wants to maintain or improve performance.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration on the existing S3 bucket. Direct customer requests to the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.
o.B: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the existing S3 bucket as the origin. Direct customer requests to the CloudFront URL. Switch to CloudFront signed URLs for access control.
o.C: Set up a second S3 bucket in the eu-central-1 Region with S3 Cross-Region Replication between the buckets. Direct customer requests to the closest Region. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.
o.D: Modify the web application to enable streaming of the datasets to end users. Configure the web application to read the data from the existing S3 bucket. Implement access control directly in the application.

e.why: CloudFront caches the datasets at edge locations near customers in North America and Europe, improving performance, and data transfer from S3 to CloudFront is free while CloudFront egress is generally cheaper than S3 internet egress. CloudFront signed URLs keep purchase-based access control.

others.A: Transfer Acceleration adds per-GB charges, increasing rather than reducing transfer cost.
others.C: A replicated bucket doubles storage and adds replication transfer costs.
others.D: Streaming through EC2 adds compute and data transfer cost and effort.

e.tip: Reduce S3 egress cost and latency for global downloads = CloudFront with OAC and signed URLs.

q:
A company is using AWS to design a web application that will process insurance quotes. Users will request quotes from the application. Quotes must be separated by quote type, must be responded to within 24 hours, and must not get lost. The solution must maximize operational efficiency and must minimize maintenance.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Create multiple Amazon Kinesis data streams based on the quote type. Configure the web application to send messages to the proper data stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to use the Kinesis Client Library (KCL) to pool messages from its own data stream.
o.B: Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for each quote type. Subscribe the Lambda function to its associated SNS topic. Configure the application to publish requests for quotes to the appropriate SNS topic.
o.C: Create a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues to the SNS topic. Configure SNS message filtering to publish messages to the proper SQS queue based on the quote type. Configure each backend application server to use its own SQS queue.
o.D: Create multiple Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams based on the quote type to deliver data streams to an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster. Configure the application to send messages to the proper delivery stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to search for the messages from OpenSearch Service and process them accordingly.

e.why: A single SNS topic with SQS queue subscriptions and message filter policies fans out each quote to the queue for its type. SQS durably stores messages (retention up to 14 days), so nothing is lost and backends can process within 24 hours, all with fully managed services.

others.A: Kinesis requires shard management and KCL consumers, which is more maintenance for simple queuing.
others.B: SNS to Lambda has no durable queue for buffering; failed deliveries can be lost without extra DLQ setup.
others.D: Using OpenSearch as a message queue is inappropriate and costly to maintain.

e.tip: Route messages by attribute to different consumers durably = SNS filter policies + SQS fan-out.

q:
A company has an application that runs on several Amazon EC2 instances. Each EC2 instance has multiple Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) data volumes attached to it. The application’s EC2 instance configuration and data need to be backed up nightly. The application also needs to be recoverable in a different AWS Region.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.A: Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application’s EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Region.
o.B: Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EC2 instances as resources.
o.C: Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EBS volumes as resources.
o.D: Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application's EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Availability Zone.

e.why: Adding EC2 instances as resources in an AWS Backup plan creates AMIs that capture both the instance configuration and all attached EBS volumes. The plan runs nightly and can copy backups to another Region for cross-Region recovery, all without custom code.

others.A: Custom Lambda scripts add maintenance and EBS snapshots alone do not capture instance configuration.
others.C: Backing up only EBS volumes misses the EC2 instance configuration.
others.D: Copying to another AZ does not provide cross-Region recovery, and custom code adds overhead.

e.tip: Back up the EC2 instance resource (not just volumes) to capture configuration.

q:
A company is building a mobile app on AWS. The company wants to expand its reach to millions of users. The company needs to build a platform so that authorized users can watch the company’s content on their mobile devices.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Publish content to a public Amazon S3 bucket. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to stream content.
o.B: Set up IPsec VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.
o.C: Use Amazon CloudFront. Provide signed URLs to stream content.
o.D: Set up AWS Client VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.

e.why: CloudFront scales to millions of users and streams content from edge locations, and signed URLs restrict content to authorized users with expiry times. This is the standard pattern for private content delivery to mobile apps.

others.A: A public S3 bucket exposes content to everyone, and KMS does not stream content.
others.B: IPsec VPN from millions of mobile devices is impractical.
others.D: Client VPN for millions of consumer users is impractical and costly.

e.tip: Authorized access to media at scale = CloudFront signed URLs/cookies.

q:
A company has an on-premises MySQL database used by the global sales team with infrequent access patterns. The sales team requires the database to have minimal downtime. A database administrator wants to migrate this database to AWS without selecting a particular instance type in anticipation of more users in the future.

Which service should a solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Amazon Aurora MySQL
o.B: Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL
o.C: Amazon Redshift Spectrum
o.D: Amazon RDS for MySQL

e.why: Aurora Serverless for MySQL automatically scales capacity (ACUs) with demand, so no instance type must be chosen, and it suits infrequent, variable access. It is MySQL-compatible, so migration (for example with DMS) can occur with minimal downtime.

others.A: Provisioned Aurora requires choosing an instance class.
others.C: Redshift Spectrum queries S3 data for analytics; it is not an OLTP MySQL database.
others.D: RDS for MySQL requires selecting an instance type.

e.tip: "No instance type selection" / unpredictable usage = Aurora Serverless.

q:
A company experienced a breach that affected several applications in its on-premises data center. The attacker took advantage of vulnerabilities in the custom applications that were running on the servers. The company is now migrating its applications to run on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to implement a solution that actively scans for vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances and sends a report that details the findings.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy AWS Shield to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Create an AWS Lambda function to log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
o.B: Deploy Amazon Macie and AWS Lambda functions to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
o.C: Turn on Amazon GuardDuty. Deploy the GuardDuty agents to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.
o.D: Turn on Amazon Inspector. Deploy the Amazon Inspector agent to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.

e.why: Amazon Inspector continuously scans EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure, producing detailed findings. A Lambda function can automate report generation and distribution (Inspector v2 now uses the SSM agent rather than a separate Inspector agent).

others.A: AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks; it does not scan for vulnerabilities.
others.B: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3, not vulnerabilities on EC2.
others.C: GuardDuty detects threats from logs and activity; it does not perform vulnerability scans.

e.tip: Vulnerability/CVE scanning = Inspector; threat detection = GuardDuty; PII in S3 = Macie.

q:
A company uses an Amazon EC2 instance to run a script to poll for and process messages in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The company wants to reduce operational costs while maintaining its ability to process a growing number of messages that are added to the queue.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Increase the size of the EC2 instance to process messages faster.
o.B: Use Amazon EventBridge to turn off the EC2 instance when the instance is underutilized.
o.C: Migrate the script on the EC2 instance to an AWS Lambda function with the appropriate runtime.
o.D: Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the script on demand.

e.why: Lambda natively polls SQS through an event source mapping and scales concurrency automatically as the queue grows. You pay only for invocations instead of an always-running instance, reducing operational cost.

others.A: A larger instance costs more and still has fixed capacity.
others.B: Turning off the instance does not handle growing message volume.
others.D: Run Command still requires EC2 and does not scale automatically with queue depth.

e.tip: SQS processing without servers = Lambda event source mapping.

q:
A company uses a legacy application to produce data in CSV format. The legacy application stores the output data in Amazon S3. The company is deploying a new commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) application that can perform complex SQL queries to analyze data that is stored in Amazon Redshift and Amazon S3 only. However, the COTS application cannot process the .csv files that the legacy application produces.

The company cannot update the legacy application to produce data in another format. The company needs to implement a solution so that the COTS application can use the data that the legacy application produces.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs on a schedule. Configure the ETL job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in Amazon Redshift.
o.B: Develop a Python script that runs on Amazon EC2 instances to convert the .csv files to .sql files. Invoke the Python script on a cron schedule to store the output files in Amazon S3.
o.C: Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use an S3 event to invoke the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in the DynamoDB table.
o.D: Use Amazon EventBridge to launch an Amazon EMR cluster on a weekly schedule. Configure the EMR cluster to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in an Amazon Redshift table.

e.why: A scheduled AWS Glue ETL job is serverless and can read the CSV files from S3, transform them, and load them into Amazon Redshift, which the COTS application can query. It requires no infrastructure management.

others.B: Custom Python scripts on EC2 require managing servers, and .sql files are not a queryable format for the COTS app.
others.C: DynamoDB is not a data source the COTS application supports.
others.D: Launching EMR clusters adds operational overhead compared with serverless Glue.

e.tip: Serverless ETL from S3 into Redshift = AWS Glue.

q:
A company recently migrated its entire IT environment to the AWS Cloud. The company discovers that users are provisioning oversized Amazon EC2 instances and modifying security group rules without using the appropriate change control process. A solutions architect must devise a strategy to track and audit these inventory and configuration changes.

Which actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Enable AWS CloudTrail and use it for auditing.
o.B: Use data lifecycle policies for the Amazon EC2 instances.
o.C: Enable AWS Trusted Advisor and reference the security dashboard.
o.D: Enable AWS Config and create rules for auditing and compliance purposes.
o.E: Restore previous resource configurations with an AWS CloudFormation template.

e.why: CloudTrail records who made which API calls, such as launching instances or changing security group rules, providing an audit trail. AWS Config records configuration history and evaluates rules (for example desired instance types or restricted security group rules) to flag noncompliant changes.

others.B: Data lifecycle policies manage EBS snapshots/AMIs, not configuration auditing.
others.C: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks, not change tracking and auditing.
others.E: Restoring configurations with CloudFormation does not track or audit changes.

e.tip: Who did it = CloudTrail; what changed and is it compliant = Config.

q:
A company has hundreds of Amazon EC2 Linux-based instances in the AWS Cloud. Systems administrators have used shared SSH keys to manage the instances. After a recent audit, the company’s security team is mandating the removal of all shared keys. A solutions architect must design a solution that provides secure access to the EC2 instances.

Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of administrative overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to the EC2 instances.
o.B: Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to generate one-time SSH keys on demand.
o.C: Allow shared SSH access to a set of bastion instances. Configure all other instances to allow only SSH access from the bastion instances.
o.D: Use an Amazon Cognito custom authorizer to authenticate users. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate a temporary SSH key.

e.why: Systems Manager Session Manager provides browser or CLI shell access to instances through the SSM Agent using IAM for authorization, with no SSH keys, open inbound ports or bastions. Sessions can be logged, and it scales to hundreds of instances with little administration.

others.B: STS issues temporary AWS credentials, not SSH keys.
others.C: Bastions still rely on shared SSH keys and add servers to manage.
others.D: Building a Cognito plus Lambda key system is complex custom work.

e.tip: Remove SSH keys/bastions = Session Manager (or EC2 Instance Connect).

q:
A company is using a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances to ingest data from on-premises data sources. The data is in JSON format and ingestion rates can be as high as 1 MB/s. When an EC2 instance is rebooted, the data in-flight is lost. The company’s data science team wants to query ingested data in near-real time.

Which solution provides near-real-time data querying that is scalable with minimal data loss?

o.A: Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Use Kinesis Data Analytics to query the data.
o.B: Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon Redshift as the destination. Use Amazon Redshift to query the data.
o.C: Store ingested data in an EC2 instance store. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon S3 as the destination. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
o.D: Store ingested data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Publish data to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Subscribe to the Redis channel to query the data.

e.why: Kinesis Data Streams durably stores records across AZs as soon as they are put, so a reboot of the producer EC2 instance does not lose already-sent data, and it scales with shards well beyond 1 MB/s. Kinesis Data Analytics queries the stream in near-real time.

others.B: Firehose buffers before loading into Redshift, adding latency, and Redshift is less suited to near-real-time queries.
others.C: Instance store data is lost on stop or failure, and Firehose buffering delays queries.
others.D: Redis pub/sub does not persist messages, so data can still be lost.

e.tip: Durable real-time ingestion with SQL analytics on the stream = Kinesis Data Streams + Data Analytics/Flink.

q: What should a solutions architect do to ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted?

o.A: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set.
o.B: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set to private.
o.C: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an aws:SecureTransport header set to true.
o.D: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an x-amz-server-side-encryption header set.

e.why: A bucket policy that denies s3:PutObject when the x-amz-server-side-encryption header is missing ensures every upload requests server-side encryption. (Since January 2023, S3 also encrypts all new objects with SSE-S3 by default.)

others.A: The x-amz-acl header controls access permissions, not encryption.
others.B: Requiring a private ACL does not ensure encryption.
others.C: aws:SecureTransport enforces encryption in transit, not at rest.

e.tip: Enforce encryption at rest in a policy = deny PutObject without x-amz-server-side-encryption.

q:
A solutions architect is designing a multi-tier application for a company. The application's users upload images from a mobile device. The application generates a thumbnail of each image and returns a message to the user to confirm that the image was uploaded successfully.

The thumbnail generation can take up to 60 seconds, but the company wants to provide a faster response time to its users to notify them that the original image was received. The solutions architect must design the application to asynchronously dispatch requests to the different application tiers.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Write a custom AWS Lambda function to generate the thumbnail and alert the user. Use the image upload process as an event source to invoke the Lambda function.
o.B: Create an AWS Step Functions workflow. Configure Step Functions to handle the orchestration between the application tiers and alert the user when thumbnail generation is complete.
o.C: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message queue. As images are uploaded, place a message on the SQS queue for thumbnail generation. Alert the user through an application message that the image was received.
o.D: Create Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification topics and subscriptions. Use one subscription with the application to generate the thumbnail after the image upload is complete. Use a second subscription to message the user's mobile app by way of a push notification after thumbnail generation is complete.

e.why: Placing a message on an SQS queue decouples upload from thumbnail generation, so the application can immediately confirm receipt to the user while workers process thumbnails asynchronously. SQS buffers requests between tiers reliably.

others.A: A single Lambda generating the thumbnail and alerting ties the response to the 60-second processing.
others.B: Step Functions orchestrates workflows but the user notification happens only after completion, not on receipt.
others.D: This notifies the user after thumbnail generation, not quickly when the image is received.

e.tip: Respond fast, process later = decouple with SQS.

q:
A company’s facility has badge readers at every entrance throughout the building. When badges are scanned, the readers send a message over HTTPS to indicate who attempted to access that particular entrance.

A solutions architect must design a system to process these messages from the sensors. The solution must be highly available, and the results must be made available for the company’s security team to analyze.

Which system architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance to serve as the HTTPS endpoint and to process the messages. Configure the EC2 instance to save the results to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.B: Create an HTTPS endpoint in Amazon API Gateway. Configure the API Gateway endpoint to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the messages and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table.
o.C: Use Amazon Route 53 to direct incoming sensor messages to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to process the messages and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table.
o.D: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Configure a Site-to-Site VPN connection from the facility network to the VPC so that sensor data can be written directly to an S3 bucket by way of the VPC endpoint.

e.why: API Gateway provides a highly available, managed HTTPS endpoint that invokes Lambda to process each badge message and store results in DynamoDB. All components are serverless and Multi-AZ, and the security team can analyze the stored data.

others.A: A single EC2 instance is a single point of failure.
others.C: Route 53 is DNS and cannot invoke Lambda or receive HTTPS messages.
others.D: Sensors send HTTPS messages; writing directly to S3 over VPN needs device changes and provides no processing.

e.tip: HTTPS ingestion serverless pattern = API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB.

q:
A company wants to implement a disaster recovery plan for its primary on-premises file storage volume. The file storage volume is mounted from an Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) device on a local storage server. The file storage volume holds hundreds of terabytes (TB) of data.

The company wants to ensure that end users retain immediate access to all file types from the on-premises systems without experiencing latency.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of change to the company's existing infrastructure?

o.A: Provision an Amazon S3 File Gateway as a virtual machine (VM) that is hosted on premises. Set the local cache to 10 TB. Modify existing applications to access the files through the NFS protocol. To recover from a disaster, provision an Amazon EC2 instance and mount the S3 bucket that contains the files.
o.B: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway. Use a data backup solution to back up all existing data to a virtual tape library. Configure the data backup solution to run nightly after the initial backup is complete. To recover from a disaster, provision an Amazon EC2 instance and restore the data to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume from the volumes in the virtual tape library.
o.C: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volume. Set the local cache to 10 TB. Mount the Volume Gateway cached volume to the existing file server by using iSCSI, and copy all files to the storage volume. Configure scheduled snapshots of the storage volume. To recover from a disaster, restore a snapshot to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and attach the EBS volume to an Amazon EC2 instance.
o.D: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volume with the same amount of disk space as the existing file storage volume. Mount the Volume Gateway stored volume to the existing file server by using iSCSI, and copy all files to the storage volume. Configure scheduled snapshots of the storage volume. To recover from a disaster, restore a snapshot to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and attach the EBS volume to an Amazon EC2 instance.

fixed: Options A, B and C were garbled (A and C truncated, B replaced by C's tail) and have been reconstructed.

e.why: A Volume Gateway stored volume keeps the full dataset on premises, so users get immediate, low-latency access to all files, while it asynchronously backs up to AWS as EBS snapshots. It presents iSCSI like the existing device, so changes are minimal, and snapshots can be restored to EBS volumes on EC2 for disaster recovery.

others.A: S3 File Gateway changes the protocol to NFS/SMB, requiring application changes, and a 10 TB cache cannot hold hundreds of TB locally.
others.B: Tape gateway backups give slow restores, and the approach changes the existing backup process significantly.
others.C: Cached volumes keep only 10 TB locally, so data outside the cache is fetched from AWS with added latency.

e.tip: All data must be local with low latency = Volume Gateway stored volumes; only hot data local = cached volumes.

q:
A company is hosting a web application from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses Amazon Cognito as an identity provider to authenticate users and return a JSON Web Token (JWT) that provides access to protected resources that are stored in another S3 bucket.

Upon deployment of the application, users report errors and are unable to access the protected content. A solutions architect must resolve this issue by providing proper permissions so that users can access the protected content.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Update the Amazon Cognito identity pool to assume the proper IAM role for access to the protected content.
o.B: Update the S3 ACL to allow the application to access the protected content.
o.C: Redeploy the application to Amazon S3 to prevent eventually consistent reads in the S3 bucket from affecting the ability of users to access the protected content.
o.D: Update the Amazon Cognito pool to use custom attribute mappings within the identity pool and grant users the proper permissions to access the protected content.

e.why: Cognito identity pools exchange the user pool JWT for temporary AWS credentials by assuming an IAM role. Configuring the identity pool's authenticated role with permissions for the protected S3 bucket lets users access the content.

others.B: ACLs are legacy and do not grant access based on Cognito-authenticated identities.
others.C: S3 now provides strong read-after-write consistency, so consistency is not the cause.
others.D: Attribute mappings alone do not grant AWS permissions without a proper IAM role.

e.tip: User pool = authentication (JWT); identity pool = AWS credentials via IAM role.

q:
An image hosting company uploads its large assets to Amazon S3 Standard buckets. The company uses multipart upload in parallel by using S3 APIs and overwrites if the same object is uploaded again. For the first 30 days after upload, the objects will be accessed frequently. The objects will be used less frequently after 30 days, but the access patterns for each object will be inconsistent. The company must optimize its S3 storage costs while maintaining high availability and resiliency of stored assets.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Move assets to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 30 days.
o.B: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to clean up incomplete multipart uploads.
o.C: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to clean up expired object delete markers.
o.D: Move assets to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
o.E: Move assets to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.

e.why: After 30 days, S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves each object between access tiers based on its own inconsistent pattern with no retrieval fees, keeping multi-AZ resilience. A lifecycle rule to abort incomplete multipart uploads removes orphaned parts that otherwise incur storage charges.

others.C: Expired object delete markers only exist with versioning, which is not described here.
others.D: Standard-IA charges retrieval fees, which can be costly with unpredictable access.
others.E: One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, reducing resilience.

e.tip: Unknown or changing access patterns = Intelligent-Tiering.

q:
A solutions architect must secure a VPC network that hosts Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances contain highly sensitive data and run in a private subnet. According to company policy, the EC2 instances that run in the VPC can access only approved third-party software repositories on the internet for software product updates that use the third party’s URL. Other internet traffic must be blocked.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Update the route table for the private subnet to route the outbound traffic to an AWS Network Firewall firewall. Configure domain list rule groups.
o.B: Set up an AWS WAF firewall. Create a custom set of rules that filter traffic requests based on source and destination IP address range sets.
o.C: Implement strict inbound security group rules. Configure an outbound rule that allows traffic only to the authorized software repositories on the internet by specifying the URLs.
o.D: Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances. Direct all outbound traffic to the ALB. Use a URL-based rule listener in the ALB’s target group for outbound access to the internet.

fixed: Options B and D were garbled (D truncated, B replaced by D's tail) and have been reconstructed.

e.why: AWS Network Firewall inspects traffic routed through it, and its stateful domain list rule groups allow only specified domain names (matched through TLS SNI or HTTP Host headers) while denying everything else. Routing the private subnet's outbound traffic through the firewall enforces the approved-repository policy.

others.B: AWS WAF protects inbound web requests to ALB, API Gateway or CloudFront; it does not filter outbound traffic from EC2.
others.C: Security groups cannot reference URLs or domain names, only IP ranges, ports and other security groups.
others.D: An ALB handles inbound requests to targets; it cannot act as an outbound internet proxy.

e.tip: Filter outbound traffic by domain name = AWS Network Firewall domain list rules.

q:
A company is hosting a three-tier ecommerce application in the AWS Cloud. The company hosts the website on Amazon S3 and integrates the website with an API that handles sales requests. The company hosts the API on three Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The API consists of static and dynamic front-end content along with backend workers that process sales requests asynchronously.

The company is expecting a significant and sudden increase in the number of sales requests during events for the launch of new products.

What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure that all the requests are processed successfully?

o.A: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the dynamic content. Increase the number of EC2 instances to handle the increase in traffic.
o.B: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the static content. Place the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on network traffic.
o.C: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the dynamic content. Add an Amazon ElastiCache instance in front of the ALB to reduce traffic for the API to handle.
o.D: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the static content. Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to receive requests from the website for later processing by the EC2 instances.

e.why: CloudFront offloads static content from the API, and an SQS queue buffers the sudden surge of sales requests so the backend workers process them asynchronously at their own pace. Messages are stored durably, ensuring every request is eventually processed.

others.A: Caching dynamic content does not help sales requests, and a fixed instance increase may still be overwhelmed.
others.B: Auto Scaling takes minutes to react to a sudden spike, so requests can fail meanwhile without buffering.
others.C: ElastiCache cannot sit in front of an ALB, and caching sales transactions is inappropriate.

e.tip: "Ensure all requests are processed" during spikes = buffer with SQS.

q:
A security audit reveals that Amazon EC2 instances are not being patched regularly. A solutions architect needs to provide a solution that will run regular security scans across a large fleet of EC2 instances. The solution should also patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule and provide a report of each instance’s patch status.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Set up Amazon Macie to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up a cron job on each EC2 instance to patch the instance on a regular schedule.
o.B: Turn on Amazon GuardDuty in the account. Configure GuardDuty to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
o.C: Set up Amazon Detective to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
o.D: Turn on Amazon Inspector in the account. Configure Amazon Inspector to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.

e.why: Amazon Inspector automatically and continuously scans EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities across the fleet. Systems Manager Patch Manager applies patches on a schedule via maintenance windows and reports each instance's patch compliance status.

others.A: Macie scans S3 for sensitive data, not EC2 vulnerabilities, and per-instance cron jobs give no central reporting.
others.B: GuardDuty detects threats, not software vulnerabilities, and Session Manager is for shell access, not scheduled patching.
others.C: Detective investigates security findings; it does not scan for vulnerabilities, and EventBridge alone does not patch.

e.tip: Scan = Inspector; patch + compliance report = Patch Manager.

q:
A company is planning to store data on Amazon RDS DB instances. The company must encrypt the data at rest.

What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.A: Create a key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable encryption for the DB instances.
o.B: Create an encryption key. Store the key in AWS Secrets Manager. Use the key to encrypt the DB instances.
o.C: Generate a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.
o.D: Generate a certificate in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.

e.why: RDS encryption at rest is enabled at instance creation using an AWS KMS key (AWS managed or customer managed), encrypting storage, backups, snapshots and replicas. Creating a KMS key and enabling encryption meets the requirement.

others.B: RDS does not use keys stored in Secrets Manager for storage encryption.
others.C: ACM certificates and SSL/TLS protect data in transit, not at rest.
others.D: IAM server certificates and TLS address encryption in transit, not at rest.

e.tip: At rest = KMS; in transit = TLS. Encrypt an existing unencrypted RDS DB via encrypted snapshot copy and restore.

q:
A company must migrate 20 TB of data from a data center to the AWS Cloud within 30 days. The company’s network bandwidth is limited to 15 Mbps and cannot exceed 70% utilization.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Snowball.
o.B: Use AWS DataSync.
o.C: Use a secure VPN connection.
o.D: Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.

e.why: At 70% of 15 Mbps (about 10.5 Mbps), transferring 20 TB would take roughly 176 days, far beyond 30 days. AWS Snowball moves the data offline on a physical device, meeting the deadline without using the network.

others.B: DataSync still uses the limited network link and cannot move 20 TB in 30 days.
others.C: A VPN uses the same constrained bandwidth.
others.D: Transfer Acceleration optimizes the path but cannot exceed the local bandwidth limit.

e.tip: Calculate transfer time: if it exceeds the deadline, use Snow Family.

q:
A company needs to provide its employees with secure access to confidential and sensitive files. The company wants to ensure that the files can be accessed only by authorized users. The files must be downloaded securely to the employees’ devices.

The files are stored in an on-premises Windows file server. However, due to an increase in remote usage, the file server is running out of capacity.
.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate the file server to an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet. Configure the security group to limit inbound traffic to the employees’ IP addresses.
o.B: Migrate the files to an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Integrate the Amazon FSx file system with the on-premises Active Directory. Configure AWS Client VPN.
o.C: Migrate the files to Amazon S3, and create a private VPC endpoint. Create a signed URL to allow download.
o.D: Migrate the files to Amazon S3, and create a public VPC endpoint. Allow employees to sign on with AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On).

e.why: FSx for Windows File Server provides scalable managed SMB storage, and joining it to the on-premises Active Directory keeps existing authorization via NTFS permissions. AWS Client VPN gives remote employees encrypted access to download files securely.
