others.A: A file server in a public subnet exposes sensitive data to the internet and still needs capacity management.
others.C: Signed URLs can be shared with anyone and do not tie access to authorized directory users.
others.D: There is no public VPC endpoint, and this does not address secure SMB file access.

e.tip: Remote secure access to private file shares = FSx + AD + Client VPN.

q:
A company’s application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. On the first day of every month at midnight, the application becomes much slower when the month-end financial calculation batch runs. This causes the CPU utilization of the EC2 instances to immediately peak to 100%, which disrupts the application.

What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure the application is able to handle the workload and avoid downtime?

o.A: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the ALB.
o.B: Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling simple scaling policy based on CPU utilization.
o.C: Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled scaling policy based on the monthly schedule.
o.D: Configure Amazon ElastiCache to remove some of the workload from the EC2 instances.

fixed: Option A was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: The batch runs at a known time (midnight on the first day of each month), so a scheduled scaling action can add capacity just before it starts. This prevents the instant CPU spike from disrupting the application, and another scheduled action can scale back in afterwards.

others.A: CloudFront caches content at the edge but does not add compute for a CPU-heavy batch job.
others.B: Simple scaling reacts only after CPU is already at 100%, and new instances take time to launch.
others.D: ElastiCache caches reads; it does not offload a CPU-bound month-end calculation.

e.tip: Predictable, time-based load = scheduled scaling.

q:
A company wants to give a customer the ability to use on-premises Microsoft Active Directory to download files that are stored in Amazon S3. The customer’s application uses an SFTP client to download the files.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead and no changes to the customer’s application?

o.A: Set up AWS Transfer Family with SFTP for Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
o.B: Set up AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to synchronize the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
o.C: Set up AWS DataSync to synchronize between the on-premises location and the S3 location by using AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On).
o.D: Set up a Windows Amazon EC2 instance with SFTP to connect the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Integrate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).

e.why: AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed SFTP endpoint backed by Amazon S3 and supports Active Directory authentication through AWS Directory Service (AD Connector or Managed AD). The customer keeps using its SFTP client unchanged.

others.B: DMS migrates databases, not files over SFTP.
others.C: DataSync is not an SFTP server for clients and does not use AD for customer downloads.
others.D: A self-managed SFTP server on EC2 adds operational overhead.

e.tip: Managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP into S3 or EFS = Transfer Family.

q:
A company is experiencing sudden increases in demand. The company needs to provision large Amazon EC2 instances from an Amazon Machine Image (AMI). The instances will run in an Auto Scaling group. The company needs a solution that provides minimum initialization latency to meet the demand.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Use the aws ec2 register-image command to create an AMI from a snapshot. Use AWS Step Functions to replace the AMI in the Auto Scaling group.
o.B: Enable Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) fast snapshot restore on a snapshot. Provision an AMI by using the snapshot. Replace the AMI in the Auto Scaling group with the new AMI.
o.C: Enable AMI creation and define lifecycle rules in Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM). Create an AWS Lambda function that modifies the AMI in the Auto Scaling group.
o.D: Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke AWS Backup lifecycle policies that provision AMIs. Configure Auto Scaling group capacity limits as an event source in EventBridge.

e.why: EBS fast snapshot restore makes volumes created from the snapshot fully initialized at creation, avoiding the first-access latency of lazy loading from S3. Building the AMI from that snapshot gives Auto Scaling instances full disk performance immediately.

others.A: Registering an AMI and swapping it with Step Functions does not remove volume initialization latency.
others.C: DLM automates AMI creation and retention but does not reduce initialization latency.
others.D: AWS Backup and EventBridge do not provide pre-warmed volumes.

e.tip: Avoid EBS restore latency/pre-warming = fast snapshot restore.

q:
A company hosts a multi-tier web application that uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster for storage. The application tier is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances. The company’s IT security guidelines mandate that the database credentials be encrypted and rotated every 14 days.

What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

o.A: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret that uses the KMS key with the appropriate credentials. Associate the secret with the Aurora DB cluster. Configure a custom rotation period of 14 days.
o.B: Create two parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: one for the user name as a string parameter and one that uses the SecureString type for the password. Select AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption for the password parameter, and load these parameters in the application tier. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password every 14 days.
o.C: Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system in all EC2 instances of the application tier. Restrict the access to the file on the file system so that the application can read the file and that only super users can modify the file. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the key in Aurora every 14 days and writes new credentials into the file.
o.D: Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon S3 bucket that the application uses to load the credentials. Download the file to the application regularly to ensure that the correct credentials are used. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the Aurora credentials every 14 days and uploads these credentials to the file in the S3 bucket.

e.why: Secrets Manager stores credentials encrypted with a KMS key and has native rotation for Aurora/RDS credentials using AWS-provided rotation functions. Setting a 14-day rotation schedule meets the requirement with the least effort.

others.B: Parameter Store has no built-in rotation, so a custom Lambda must be written and maintained.
others.C: Storing credentials in files on EFS plus custom rotation is error-prone and high effort.
others.D: Credentials files in S3 plus custom rotation and regular downloads add operational effort.

e.tip: Encrypted + automatic rotation of DB credentials = Secrets Manager.

q:
A company has deployed a web application on AWS. The company hosts the backend database on Amazon RDS for MySQL with a primary DB instance and five read replicas to support scaling needs. The read replicas must lag no more than 1 second behind the primary DB instance. The database routinely runs scheduled stored procedures.

As traffic on the website increases, the replicas experience additional lag during periods of peak load. A solutions architect must reduce the replication lag as much as possible. The solutions architect must minimize changes to the application code and must minimize ongoing operational overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Replace the read replicas with Aurora Replicas, and configure Aurora Auto Scaling. Replace the stored procedures with Aurora MySQL native functions.
o.B: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the database. Modify the application to check the cache before the application queries the database. Replace the stored procedures with AWS Lambda functions.
o.C: Migrate the database to a MySQL database that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Choose large, compute optimized EC2 instances for all replica nodes. Maintain the stored procedures on the EC2 instances.
o.D: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Provision a large number of read capacity units (RCUs) to support the required throughput, and configure on-demand capacity scaling. Replace the stored procedures with DynamoDB streams.

fixed: Options B and D were garbled (D truncated, B replaced by D's tail) and have been reconstructed.

e.why: Aurora Replicas share the cluster's storage volume, so replica lag is typically well under 100 ms, and Aurora Auto Scaling adds or removes replicas automatically. Aurora MySQL is compatible with the existing application, keeping code changes minimal and operational overhead low.

others.B: Adding a cache and rewriting stored procedures as Lambda functions requires significant code changes and does not fix replication lag.
others.C: Self-managed MySQL on EC2 increases operational overhead, and bigger instances do not remove the cause of lag.
others.D: Migrating to DynamoDB is a major rewrite, and DynamoDB Streams cannot replace stored procedures.

e.tip: RDS MySQL replica lag problems = migrate to Aurora MySQL with Aurora Replicas.

q:
A solutions architect must create a disaster recovery (DR) plan for a high-volume software as a service (SaaS) platform. All data for the platform is stored in an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster.

The DR plan must replicate data to a secondary AWS Region.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use MySQL binary log replication to an Aurora cluster in the secondary Region. Provision one DB instance for the Aurora cluster in the secondary Region.
o.B: Set up an Aurora global database for the DB cluster. When setup is complete, remove the DB instance from the secondary Region.
o.C: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to continuously replicate data to an Aurora cluster in the secondary Region. Remove the DB instance from the secondary Region.
o.D: Set up an Aurora global database for the DB cluster. Specify a minimum of one DB instance in the secondary Region.

e.why: An Aurora global database replicates storage to the secondary Region with low lag, and the secondary cluster can be headless (no DB instances), so you pay mainly for replicated storage and I/O. Instances are added only during failover, making it the most cost-effective DR replication.

others.A: Binlog replication is more to manage and slower, and keeping an instance running costs more.
others.C: DMS continuous replication requires a replication instance, adding cost and overhead.
others.D: Keeping at least one instance in the secondary Region costs more than a headless secondary.

e.tip: Cheapest Aurora cross-Region DR = headless global database secondary.

q:
A company has a custom application with embedded credentials that retrieves information from an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. Management says the application must be made more secure with the least amount of programming effort.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to create keys. Configure the application to load the database credentials from AWS KMS. Enable automatic key rotation.
o.B: Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function that rotates the credentials in Secret Manager.
o.C: Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Secrets Manager.
o.D: Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Parameter Store. Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Parameter Store.

e.why: Storing the credentials in Secrets Manager removes them from code, and the application retrieves them with a simple SDK call. Secrets Manager provides managed rotation schedules for RDS MySQL using built-in rotation templates, so no custom rotation code is needed.

others.A: KMS stores encryption keys, not database credentials, and key rotation does not rotate DB passwords.
others.B: Writing a custom rotation Lambda is more programming effort than native rotation.
others.D: Parameter Store does not offer automatic credential rotation.

e.tip: Built-in rotation is the differentiator between Secrets Manager and Parameter Store.

q:
A media company hosts its website on AWS. The website application’s architecture includes a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a database that is hosted on Amazon Aurora. The company’s cybersecurity team reports that the application is vulnerable to SQL injection.

How should the company resolve this issue?

o.A: Use AWS WAF in front of the Application Load Balancer. Associate the appropriate web ACLs with AWS WAF.
o.B: Create an ALB listener rule to reply to SQL injections with a fixed response.
o.C: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.
o.D: Set up Amazon Inspector to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.

fixed: Option A was truncated and has been completed; a stray empty option F was removed.

e.why: AWS WAF integrates with the ALB, and web ACLs with SQL injection match rules or AWS managed rule groups inspect requests and block SQL injection attempts before they reach the application.

others.B: ALB listener rules match on paths, headers and similar fields but cannot reliably detect SQL injection payloads.
others.C: Shield Advanced is for DDoS protection; SQL injection filtering comes from WAF rules.
others.D: Amazon Inspector scans for vulnerabilities but does not block requests.

e.tip: SQL injection or XSS protection = AWS WAF web ACL on ALB, API Gateway or CloudFront.

q:
A company has an Amazon S3 data lake that is governed by AWS Lake Formation. The company wants to create a visualization in Amazon QuickSight by joining the data in the data lake with operational data that is stored in an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. The company wants to enforce column-level authorization so that the company’s marketing team can access only a subset of columns in the database.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon EMR to ingest the data directly from the database to the QuickSight SPICE engine. Include only the required columns.
o.B: Use AWS Glue Studio to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Attach an IAM policy to the QuickSight users to enforce column-level access control. Use Amazon S3 as the data source in QuickSight.
o.C: Use AWS Glue Elastic Views to create a materialized view for the database in Amazon S3. Create an S3 bucket policy to enforce column-level access control for the QuickSight users. Use Amazon S3 as the data source in QuickSight.
o.D: Use a Lake Formation blueprint to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Use Lake Formation to enforce column-level access control for the QuickSight users. Use Amazon Athena as the data source in QuickSight.

e.why: A Lake Formation blueprint ingests data from the Aurora database into the governed S3 data lake with little effort. Lake Formation then enforces column-level permissions, and QuickSight queries through Athena, which honors those permissions.

others.A: EMR adds cluster management and does not provide governed column-level authorization.
others.B: IAM policies cannot enforce column-level access on data in S3.
others.C: S3 bucket policies cannot control access at the column level, and Glue Elastic Views never became generally available.

e.tip: Column/row-level permissions on a data lake = Lake Formation, queried via Athena.

q:
A transaction processing company has weekly scripted batch jobs that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The number of transactions can vary, but the baseline CPU utilization that is noted on each run is at least 60%. The company needs to provision the capacity 30 minutes before the jobs run.

Currently, engineers complete this task by manually modifying the Auto Scaling group parameters. The company does not have the resources to analyze the required capacity trends for the Auto Scaling group counts. The company needs an automated way to modify the Auto Scaling group’s desired capacity.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Configure the policy to scale based on the CPU utilization metric. Set the target value for the metric to 60%.
o.B: Create a scheduled scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Set the appropriate desired capacity, minimum capacity, and maximum capacity. Set the recurrence to weekly. Set the start time to 30 minutes before the batch jobs run.
o.C: Create a predictive scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Configure the policy to scale based on forecast. Set the scaling metric to CPU utilization. Set the target value for the metric to 60%. In the policy, set the instances to pre-launch 30 minutes before the jobs run.
o.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge event to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the CPU utilization metric value for the Auto Scaling group reaches 60%. Configure the Lambda function to increase the Auto Scaling group’s desired capacity and maximum capacity by 20%.

e.why: Predictive scaling uses machine learning on historical CPU utilization to forecast capacity needs automatically, so no one has to analyze trends. Its scheduling buffer can pre-launch instances (here 30 minutes) before the forecast load, meeting the requirement with minimal overhead.

others.A: Dynamic target tracking reacts only after load rises, so capacity is not ready 30 minutes early.
others.B: Scheduled scaling requires someone to choose capacity values, which the company cannot analyze.
others.D: A custom Lambda reacting at 60% CPU is reactive and adds code to maintain.

e.tip: Recurring pattern but unknown capacity values = predictive scaling.

q:
A solutions architect is designing a company’s disaster recovery (DR) architecture. The company has a MySQL database that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet with scheduled backup. The DR design needs to include multiple AWS Regions.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Migrate the MySQL database to multiple EC2 instances. Configure a standby EC2 instance in the DR Region. Turn on replication.
o.B: Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS. Use a Multi-AZ deployment. Turn on read replication for the primary DB instance in the different Availability Zones.
o.C: Migrate the MySQL database to an Amazon Aurora global database. Host the primary DB cluster in the primary Region. Host the secondary DB cluster in the DR Region.
o.D: Store the scheduled backup of the MySQL database in an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Use the data backup to restore the database in the DR Region.

e.why: Aurora global database is fully managed and replicates data to a secondary cluster in the DR Region with typically under one second of lag, and supports managed cross-Region failover. This provides multi-Region DR with the least operational overhead.

others.A: Self-managing MySQL replication across EC2 instances is high overhead.
others.B: Multi-AZ and read replicas in other AZs stay within one Region.
others.D: Restoring from replicated backups requires manual work and gives longer RTO and RPO.

e.tip: Managed multi-Region relational DR = Aurora global database.

q:
A company has a Java application that uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to parse messages. The application cannot parse messages that are larger than 256 KB in size. The company wants to implement a solution to give the application the ability to parse messages as large as 50 MB.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the code?

o.A: Use the Amazon SQS Extended Client Library for Java to host messages that are larger than 256 KB in Amazon S3.
o.B: Use Amazon EventBridge to post large messages from the application instead of Amazon SQS.
o.C: Change the limit in Amazon SQS to handle messages that are larger than 256 KB.
o.D: Store messages that are larger than 256 KB in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Configure Amazon SQS to reference this location in the messages.

fixed: Option B text was missing and option C was truncated; both have been reconstructed.

e.why: The Amazon SQS Extended Client Library for Java stores large payloads in Amazon S3 and sends a reference through SQS, then transparently retrieves the payload when messages are received. It is a drop-in wrapper around the SQS client, so code changes are minimal.

others.B: EventBridge events are limited to 256 KB, and switching services requires substantial code changes.
others.C: The SQS message size limit is a fixed service maximum that cannot be raised to 50 MB.
others.D: SQS cannot natively reference EFS, so this would need custom code to store and fetch messages.

e.tip: SQS messages larger than the size limit = SQS Extended Client Library with S3.

q:
A company wants to restrict access to the content of one of its main web applications and to protect the content by using authorization techniques available on AWS. The company wants to implement a serverless architecture and an authentication solution for fewer than 100 users. The solution needs to integrate with the main web application and serve web content globally. The solution must also scale as the company's user base grows while providing the lowest login latency possible.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use Amazon Cognito for authentication. Use Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the web application globally.
o.B: Use AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Use AWS Lambda for authorization. Use an Application Load Balancer to serve the web application globally.
o.C: Use Amazon Cognito for authentication. Use AWS Lambda for authorization. Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to serve the web application globally.
o.D: Use AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Use Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to serve the web application globally.

e.why: Amazon Cognito user pools provide serverless authentication billed per monthly active user (with a free tier that easily covers under 100 users) and scale as the user base grows. Lambda@Edge validates tokens at CloudFront edge locations for low-latency authorization, and CloudFront serves the application globally.

others.B: Managed Microsoft AD is not serverless, is costly for under 100 users, and an ALB is Regional, not global.
others.C: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads to S3; it does not serve a web application globally, and Regional Lambda adds login latency.
others.D: Managed AD is expensive and not serverless, and Elastic Beanstalk does not serve content globally.

e.tip: Serverless auth for web/mobile users = Cognito; edge authorization = Lambda@Edge.

q:
A company has an aging network-attached storage (NAS) array in its data center. The NAS array presents SMB shares and NFS shares to client workstations. The company does not want to purchase a new NAS array. The company also does not want to incur the cost of renewing the NAS array’s support contract. Some of the data is accessed frequently, but much of the data is inactive.

A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that migrates the data to Amazon S3, uses S3 Lifecycle policies, and maintains the same look and feel for the client workstations. The solutions architect has identified AWS Storage Gateway as part of the solution.

Which type of storage gateway should the solutions architect provision to meet these requirements?

o.A: Volume Gateway
o.B: Tape Gateway
o.C: Amazon FSx File Gateway
o.D: Amazon S3 File Gateway

e.why: Amazon S3 File Gateway presents both SMB and NFS file shares to clients while storing files as objects in S3, so S3 Lifecycle policies can tier inactive data. Clients keep the same file share look and feel, with frequently accessed data cached locally.

others.A: Volume Gateway presents iSCSI block volumes, not SMB/NFS shares, and data is not stored as accessible S3 objects for lifecycle rules.
others.B: Tape Gateway emulates tape libraries for backup software.
others.C: FSx File Gateway stores data in FSx for Windows (SMB only), not S3, so S3 Lifecycle policies do not apply.

e.tip: SMB/NFS shares backed by S3 objects = S3 File Gateway.

q:
A company has an application that is running on Amazon EC2 instances. A solutions architect has standardized the company on a particular instance family and various instance sizes based on the current needs of the company.

The company wants to maximize cost savings for the application over the next 3 years. The company needs to be able to change the instance family and sizes in the next 6 months based on application popularity and usage.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Compute Savings Plan
o.B: EC2 Instance Savings Plan
o.C: Zonal Reserved Instances
o.D: Standard Reserved Instances

e.why: Compute Savings Plans give up to about 66% savings over 3 years and automatically apply across any instance family, size, Region, OS and tenancy, plus Fargate and Lambda. That flexibility lets the company change instance family and sizes later while still saving.

others.B: EC2 Instance Savings Plans lock you to one instance family in one Region.
others.C: Zonal Reserved Instances are locked to a specific instance type and AZ.
others.D: Standard Reserved Instances cannot change instance family.

e.tip: Need to change instance family = Compute Savings Plan (or Convertible RIs).

q:
A company collects data from a large number of participants who use wearable devices. The company stores the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table and uses applications to analyze the data. The data workload is constant and predictable. The company wants to stay at or below its forecasted budget for DynamoDB.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use provisioned mode and DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA). Reserve capacity for the forecasted workload.
o.B: Use provisioned mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs).
o.C: Use on-demand mode. Set the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) high enough to accommodate changes in the workload.
o.D: Use on-demand mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) with reserved capacity.

e.why: For a constant, predictable workload, provisioned capacity mode with specified RCUs and WCUs is cheaper than on-demand and keeps costs fixed and predictable within budget. (Reserved capacity can further discount provisioned throughput.)

others.A: Standard-IA lowers storage cost for rarely accessed tables but raises throughput cost, unsuitable for actively analyzed data.
others.C: On-demand mode does not use RCU/WCU settings and costs more per request for steady traffic.
others.D: Reserved capacity is only available for provisioned mode, not on-demand.

e.tip: Predictable DynamoDB traffic = provisioned (+ auto scaling / reserved capacity); spiky/unknown = on-demand.

q:
A company stores confidential data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database in the ap-southeast-3 Region. The database is encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. The company was recently acquired and must securely share a backup of the database with the acquiring company’s AWS account in ap-southeast-3.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a database snapshot. Copy the snapshot to a new unencrypted snapshot. Share the new snapshot with the acquiring company’s AWS account.
o.B: Create a database snapshot. Add the acquiring company’s AWS account to the KMS key policy. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company’s AWS account.
o.C: Create a database snapshot that uses a different AWS managed KMS key. Add the acquiring company’s AWS account to the KMS key alias. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
o.D: Create a database snapshot. Download the database snapshot. Upload the database snapshot to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the acquiring company’s AWS account.

e.why: A snapshot encrypted with a customer managed KMS key can be shared with another account if the key policy grants that account permission to use the key. Sharing the snapshot and the key keeps the backup encrypted and secure.

others.A: Creating an unencrypted copy of confidential data violates security requirements (and encrypted Aurora snapshots cannot simply be copied to unencrypted).
others.C: Snapshots encrypted with AWS managed keys cannot be shared, and permissions are not granted via aliases.
others.D: RDS/Aurora snapshots cannot be downloaded directly, and this is less secure and more complex.

e.tip: Share encrypted snapshots: customer managed key + key policy grant + snapshot share.

q:
A company uses a 100 GB Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server Single-AZ DB instance in the us-east-1 Region to store customer transactions. The company needs high availability and automatic recovery for the DB instance.

The company must also run reports on the RDS database several times a year. The report process causes transactions to take longer than usual to post to the customers’ accounts. The company needs a solution that will improve the performance of the report process.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Modify the DB instance from a Single-AZ DB instance to a Multi-AZ deployment.
o.B: Take a snapshot of the current DB instance. Restore the snapshot to a new RDS deployment in another Availability Zone.
o.C: Create a read replica of the DB instance in a different Availability Zone. Point all requests for reports to the read replica.
o.D: Migrate the database to RDS Custom.
o.E: Use RDS Proxy to limit reporting requests to the maintenance window.

e.why: Converting to Multi-AZ adds a synchronous standby with automatic failover for high availability. A read replica (supported for RDS SQL Server Enterprise/Standard editions) offloads the occasional reporting queries so transaction posting is not slowed.

others.B: A snapshot restore gives a stale, separate copy with no automatic recovery.
others.D: RDS Custom gives OS-level access but does not by itself provide HA or reporting offload.
others.E: RDS Proxy pools connections; it cannot restrict reports to a maintenance window.

e.tip: HA = Multi-AZ; read offload = read replica.

q:
A company is moving its data management application to AWS. The company wants to transition to an event-driven architecture. The architecture needs to be more distributed and to use serverless concepts while performing the different aspects of the workflow. The company also wants to minimize operational overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Build out the workflow in AWS Glue. Use AWS Glue to invoke AWS Lambda functions to process the workflow steps.
o.B: Build out the workflow in AWS Step Functions. Deploy the application on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Step Functions to invoke the workflow steps on the EC2 instances.
o.C: Build out the workflow in Amazon EventBridge. Use EventBridge to invoke AWS Lambda functions on a schedule to process the workflow steps.
o.D: Build out the workflow in AWS Step Functions. Use Step Functions to create a state machine. Use the state machine to invoke AWS Lambda functions to process the workflow steps.

e.why: AWS Step Functions state machines orchestrate distributed workflow steps serverlessly, invoking Lambda functions for each step with built-in retries and error handling. This is event-driven, distributed and has minimal operational overhead.

others.A: AWS Glue is for ETL jobs, not general application workflow orchestration.
others.B: Running steps on EC2 instances is not serverless and adds overhead.
others.C: Scheduled invocations are not an event-driven workflow and lack step orchestration.

e.tip: Serverless orchestration of multi-step workflows = Step Functions.

q:
A company is designing the network for an online multi-player game. The game uses the UDP networking protocol and will be deployed in eight AWS Regions. The network architecture needs to minimize latency and packet loss to give end users a high-quality gaming experience.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Setup a transit gateway in each Region. Create inter-Region peering attachments between each transit gateway.
o.B: Set up AWS Global Accelerator with UDP listeners and endpoint groups in each Region.
o.C: Use Amazon CloudFront with UDP turned on. Configure an origin in each Region.
o.D: Set up a VPC peering mesh between each Region. Turn on UDP for each VPC.

fixed: Option C contained answer text instead of option text, and option D was truncated; they have been reconstructed.

e.why: AWS Global Accelerator supports UDP listeners and brings players onto the AWS global network at the nearest edge location, reducing latency, jitter and packet loss. Endpoint groups in each of the eight Regions provide health-based routing to the closest healthy endpoint.

others.A: Transit gateway peering connects VPC networks but does not improve the path from end users to AWS.
others.C: CloudFront serves HTTP/HTTPS and WebSocket traffic; it cannot carry UDP game traffic.
others.D: VPC peering connects VPCs and has no UDP setting; it does nothing for user-to-AWS latency.

e.tip: UDP plus global users plus low latency = AWS Global Accelerator.

q:
A company hosts a three-tier web application on Amazon EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone. The web application uses a self-managed MySQL database that is hosted on an EC2 instance to store data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. The MySQL database currently uses a 1 TB Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) EBS volume. The company expects traffic of 1,000 IOPS for both reads and writes at peak traffic.

The company wants to minimize any disruptions, stabilize performance, and reduce costs while retaining the capacity for double the IOPS. The company wants to move the database tier to a fully managed solution that is highly available and fault tolerant.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use a Multi-AZ deployment of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with an io2 Block Express EBS volume.
o.B: Use a Multi-AZ deployment of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with a General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volume.
o.C: Use Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering access tiers.
o.D: Use two large EC2 instances to host the database in active-passive mode.

e.why: A 1 TB gp2 volume provides a 3,000 IOPS baseline (3 IOPS per GB), covering 1,000 peak IOPS and double that, at far lower cost than io2. RDS Multi-AZ makes the database fully managed, highly available and fault tolerant.

others.A: io2 Block Express provides far more IOPS than needed at much higher cost.
others.C: S3 storage classes are object storage, not a MySQL database tier.
others.D: Self-managed EC2 database instances are not a fully managed solution.

e.tip: gp2 = 3 IOPS/GiB (burst to 3,000 for small volumes); gp3 = 3,000 IOPS baseline at any size and usually cheaper.

q:
A company hosts a serverless application on AWS. The application uses Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The company notices an increase in application errors that result from database connection timeouts during times of peak traffic or unpredictable traffic. The company needs a solution that reduces the application failures with the least amount of change to the code.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Reduce the Lambda concurrency rate.
o.B: Enable RDS Proxy on the RDS DB instance.
o.C: Resize the RDS DB instance class to accept more connections.
o.D: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand scaling.

e.why: RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections among many concurrent Lambda invocations, preventing connection exhaustion and timeouts during spikes. It requires only changing the database endpoint, so code changes are minimal.

others.A: Reducing Lambda concurrency throttles the application and causes other failures.
others.C: A larger instance raises connection limits but still cannot absorb unpredictable bursts efficiently and costs more.
others.D: Migrating to DynamoDB requires a major rewrite.

e.tip: Lambda + RDS connection problems = RDS Proxy.

q:
A company is migrating an old application to AWS. The application runs a batch job every hour and is CPU intensive. The batch job takes 15 minutes on average with an on-premises server. The server has 64 virtual CPU (vCPU) and 512 GiB of memory.

Which solution will run the batch job within 15 minutes with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Lambda with functional scaling.
o.B: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate.
o.C: Use Amazon Lightsail with AWS Auto Scaling.
o.D: Use AWS Batch on Amazon EC2.

e.why: AWS Batch on EC2 can provision instances with 64 vCPUs and 512 GiB of memory, schedule the hourly job, and scale compute down when idle. It is a managed service, so operational overhead is low.

others.A: Lambda is limited to 15 minutes, 10 GB memory and 6 vCPUs, insufficient for this job.
others.B: Fargate tasks max out at 16 vCPU and 120 GB memory, below the required resources.
others.C: Lightsail does not offer instances this large and is not designed for batch scaling.

e.tip: Large CPU/memory batch jobs = AWS Batch on EC2; Fargate and Lambda have size limits.

q:
A company stores its data objects in Amazon S3 Standard storage. A solutions architect has found that 75% of the data is rarely accessed after 30 days. The company needs all the data to remain immediately accessible with the same high availability and resiliency, but the company wants to minimize storage costs.

Which storage solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Move the data objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days.
o.B: Move the data objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
o.C: Move the data objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.
o.D: Move the data objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) immediately.

e.why: S3 Standard-IA keeps millisecond access and stores data across at least three AZs with the same 99.99% availability design target class tier (99.9% SLA) and 11 nines durability, at lower storage cost. A lifecycle transition after 30 days (the minimum for Standard-IA) cuts costs for the rarely accessed 75%.

others.A: Glacier Deep Archive requires hours to restore, so data is not immediately accessible.
others.C: One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, reducing resiliency.
others.D: One Zone-IA immediately reduces resiliency and incurs costs for frequently accessed new data.

e.tip: Immediate access + multi-AZ resiliency + infrequent = Standard-IA.

q:
A gaming company is moving its public scoreboard from a data center to the AWS Cloud. The company uses Amazon EC2 Windows Server instances behind an Application Load Balancer to host its dynamic application. The company needs a highly available storage solution for the application. The application consists of static files and dynamic server-side code.

Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Store the static files on Amazon S3. Use Amazon CloudFront to cache objects at the edge.
o.B: Store the static files on Amazon S3. Use Amazon ElastiCache to cache objects at the edge.
o.C: Store the server-side code on Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS volume on each EC2 instance to share the files.
o.D: Store the server-side code on Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Mount the FSx for Windows File Server volume on each EC2 instance to share the files.
o.E: Store the server-side code on a General Purpose SSD (gp2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume on each EC2 instance to share the files.

e.why: Storing static files in S3 and caching them with CloudFront offloads static delivery with high availability. FSx for Windows File Server provides a highly available SMB share that all Windows EC2 instances mount to share the server-side code.

others.B: ElastiCache is an in-memory data cache within a Region, not an edge cache for static files.
others.C: EFS uses NFS and is not supported for Windows instances.
others.E: A gp2 EBS volume cannot be shared across multiple instances.

e.tip: Windows shared storage = FSx for Windows; Linux = EFS.

q:
A social media company runs its application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB is the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The application has more than a billion images stored in an Amazon S3 bucket and processes thousands of images each second. The company wants to resize the images dynamically and serve appropriate formats to clients.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Install an external image management library on an EC2 instance. Use the image management library to process the images.
o.B: Create a CloudFront origin request policy. Use the policy to automatically resize images and to serve the appropriate format based on the User-Agent HTTP header in the request.
o.C: Use a Lambda@Edge function with an external image management library. Associate the Lambda@Edge function with the CloudFront behaviors that serve the images.
o.D: Create a CloudFront response headers policy. Use the policy to automatically resize images and to serve the appropriate format based on the User-Agent HTTP header in the request.

e.why: A Lambda@Edge function associated with the image cache behaviors can resize images and select formats (for example WebP based on the Accept header) at the edge using an image library, and CloudFront caches the results. This is managed and scales automatically with little operational overhead.

others.A: Processing thousands of images per second on self-managed EC2 is high operational overhead.
others.B: Origin request policies control which values are forwarded to the origin; they cannot resize images.
others.D: Response headers policies add or modify headers; they cannot transform images.

e.tip: On-the-fly image transformation at the edge = Lambda@Edge (or the Dynamic Image Transformation solution).

q:
A hospital needs to store patient records in an Amazon S3 bucket. The hospital’s compliance team must ensure that all protected health information (PHI) is encrypted in transit and at rest. The compliance team must administer the encryption key for data at rest.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a public SSL/TLS certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Associate the certificate with Amazon S3. Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.
o.B: Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Assign the compliance team to manage the SSE-S3 keys.
o.C: Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.
o.D: Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Use Amazon Macie to protect the sensitive data that is stored in Amazon S3. Assign the compliance team to manage Macie.

e.why: A bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false enforces HTTPS for data in transit. SSE-KMS with a customer managed key lets the compliance team administer the key, its policy and rotation for data at rest.

others.A: ACM public certificates cannot be associated with S3, and S3 endpoints already have their own TLS.
others.B: SSE-S3 keys are fully managed by AWS, so the compliance team cannot administer them.
others.D: Macie discovers sensitive data; it does not encrypt data at rest.

e.tip: Customer-controlled keys = SSE-KMS with a customer managed key; enforce TLS with aws:SecureTransport.

q:
A company uses Amazon API Gateway to run a private gateway with two REST APIs in the same VPC. The BuyStock RESTful web service calls the CheckFunds RESTful web service to ensure that enough funds are available before a stock can be purchased. The company has noticed in the VPC flow logs that the BuyStock RESTful web service calls the CheckFunds RESTful web service over the internet instead of through the VPC. A solutions architect must implement a solution so that the APIs communicate through the VPC.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the code?

o.A: Add an X-API-Key header in the HTTP header for authorization.
o.B: Use an interface endpoint.
o.C: Use a gateway endpoint.
o.D: Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue between the two REST APIs.

e.why: Private API Gateway APIs are accessed through an interface VPC endpoint (execute-api, AWS PrivateLink). Using the interface endpoint keeps BuyStock's calls to CheckFunds within the VPC with little or no code change, especially with private DNS enabled.

others.A: An API key header controls authorization and usage plans, not the network path.
others.C: Gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB.
others.D: Adding SQS between the APIs requires significant code redesign.

e.tip: Gateway endpoints: S3 and DynamoDB only; everything else uses interface endpoints.

q:
A company hosts a multiplayer gaming application on AWS. The company wants the application to read data with sub-millisecond latency and run one-time queries on historical data.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon RDS for data that is frequently accessed. Run a periodic custom script to export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.B: Store the data directly in an Amazon S3 bucket. Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy to move older data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for long-term storage. Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.
o.C: Use Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for data that is frequently accessed. Export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket by using DynamoDB table export. Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.
o.D: Use Amazon DynamoDB for data that is frequently accessed. Turn on streaming to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to read the data from Kinesis Data Streams. Store the records in an Amazon S3 bucket.

e.why: DynamoDB with DAX delivers microsecond to sub-millisecond read latency for frequently accessed data. DynamoDB's native export to S3 requires no custom code, and Athena runs one-time SQL queries on the exported historical data serverlessly.

others.A: RDS does not provide sub-millisecond reads, and custom export scripts add overhead.
others.B: S3 cannot deliver sub-millisecond reads, and Deep Archive data is not directly queryable.
others.D: DynamoDB alone gives single-digit millisecond (not sub-millisecond) reads, and there is no query solution for historical data.

e.tip: Sub-millisecond = in-memory cache (DAX for DynamoDB, ElastiCache otherwise).

q:
A company uses a payment processing system that requires messages for a particular payment ID to be received in the same order that they were sent. Otherwise, the payments might be processed incorrectly.

Which actions should a solutions architect take to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

o.A: Write the messages to an Amazon DynamoDB table with the payment ID as the partition key.
o.B: Write the messages to an Amazon Kinesis data stream with the payment ID as the partition key.
o.C: Write the messages to an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster with the payment ID as the key.
o.D: Write the messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue. Set the message attribute to use the payment ID.
o.E: Write the messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Set the message group to use the payment ID.

fixed: Option D text was missing and option E was truncated; both have been reconstructed.

e.why: Kinesis Data Streams preserves record order within a shard, and using the payment ID as the partition key sends all records for a payment to the same shard. An SQS FIFO queue with the payment ID as the message group ID guarantees ordered delivery for each payment.

others.A: DynamoDB is a database and does not deliver messages in the order they were sent.
others.C: Memcached is a cache with no ordering or messaging semantics.
others.D: SQS standard queues provide best-effort ordering only, and message attributes do not change that.

e.tip: Ordering per key = Kinesis partition key or SQS FIFO message group ID.

q:
A company is building a game system that needs to send unique events to separate leaderboard, matchmaking, and authentication services concurrently. The company needs an AWS event-driven system that guarantees the order of the events.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Amazon EventBridge event bus
o.B: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) FIFO topics
o.C: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) standard topics
o.D: Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues

e.why: SNS FIFO topics deliver messages in strict order with deduplication and fan out to multiple subscribers concurrently (typically SQS FIFO queues for each service). This meets both the concurrent fan-out to leaderboard, matchmaking and authentication and the ordering guarantee.

others.A: EventBridge does not guarantee event ordering.
others.C: SNS standard topics provide best-effort ordering only.
others.D: An SQS FIFO queue delivers to one consumer group; it does not fan out the same event to several services.

e.tip: Ordered fan-out = SNS FIFO -> SQS FIFO.

q:
A hospital is designing a new application that gathers symptoms from patients. The hospital has decided to use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) and Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) in the architecture.

A solutions architect is reviewing the infrastructure design. Data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Only authorized personnel of the hospital should be able to access the data.

Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Turn on server-side encryption on the SQS components. Update the default key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals.
o.B: Turn on server-side encryption on the SNS components by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Apply a key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals.
o.C: Turn on encryption on the SNS components. Update the default key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals. Set a condition in the topic policy to allow only encrypted connections over TLS.
o.D: Turn on server-side encryption on the SQS components by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Apply a key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals. Set a condition in the queue policy to allow only encrypted connections over TLS.
o.E: Turn on server-side encryption on the SQS components by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Apply an IAM policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals. Set a condition in the queue policy to allow only encrypted connections over TLS.

e.why: Enabling SSE with a customer managed KMS key on both SNS and SQS encrypts data at rest, and a key policy limits which principals can use the key to read the data. Adding an aws:SecureTransport condition in the queue policy enforces TLS in transit.

others.A: SQS-managed or AWS managed keys have default policies that cannot be edited, so key usage cannot be restricted that way.
others.C: The default AWS managed key policy for SNS cannot be modified to restrict principals.
others.E: KMS key access is controlled primarily by the key policy; an IAM policy alone cannot restrict key usage to only the authorized principals.

e.tip: To control who can use a key, you need a customer managed key and its key policy.

q:
A company runs a web application that is backed by Amazon RDS. A new database administrator caused data loss by accidentally editing information in a database table. To help recover from this type of incident, the company wants the ability to restore the database to its state from 5 minutes before any change within the last 30 days.

Which feature should the solutions architect include in the design to meet this requirement?

o.A: Read replicas
o.B: Manual snapshots
o.C: Automated backups
o.D: Multi-AZ deployments

e.why: RDS automated backups combine daily snapshots with transaction logs uploaded every 5 minutes, enabling point-in-time restore to any second within the retention period (up to 35 days). Setting retention to 30 days allows restoring to 5 minutes before the bad edit.

others.A: Read replicas replicate the accidental change too.
others.B: Manual snapshots capture only specific moments, not any point in time.
others.D: Multi-AZ synchronously replicates the mistake to the standby.

e.tip: Point-in-time restore (up to 35 days) = automated backups.

q:
A company’s web application consists of an Amazon API Gateway API in front of an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB database. The Lambda function handles the business logic, and the DynamoDB table hosts the data. The application uses Amazon Cognito user pools to identify the individual users of the application. A solutions architect needs to update the application so that only users who have a subscription can access premium content.

Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Enable API caching and throttling on the API Gateway API.
o.B: Set up AWS WAF on the API Gateway API. Create a rule to filter users who have a subscription.
o.C: Apply fine-grained IAM permissions to the premium content in the DynamoDB table.
o.D: Implement API usage plans and API keys to limit the access of users who do not have a subscription.

e.why: API Gateway usage plans with API keys let you give subscribed users keys tied to a plan that grants access to the premium API methods, while non-subscribers are rejected. It is built-in configuration with low operational overhead.

others.A: Caching and throttling control performance and rates, not subscription-based access.
others.B: WAF filters by request attributes like IPs or patterns, not user subscription status.
others.C: Fine-grained DynamoDB IAM permissions require per-user credentials (for example via identity pools) and more setup than usage plans.

e.tip: API keys are for metering/usage plans; for real authorization consider Cognito groups or Lambda authorizers.

q:
A company is using Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to its UDP-based application for users around the world. The application is hosted on redundant servers in the company's on-premises data centers in the United States, Asia, and Europe. The company’s compliance requirements state that the application must be hosted on premises. The company wants to improve the performance and availability of the application.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure three Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. Create an accelerator by using AWS Global Accelerator, and register the NLBs as its endpoints. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the accelerator DNS.
o.B: Configure three Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. Create an accelerator by using AWS Global Accelerator, and register the ALBs as its endpoints. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the accelerator DNS.
o.C: Configure three Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. In Route 53, create a latency-based record that points to the three NLBs, and use it as an origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the CloudFront DNS.
o.D: Configure three Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. In Route 53, create a latency-based record that points to the three ALBs, and use it as an origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the CloudFront DNS.

e.why: Global Accelerator supports UDP and routes users over the AWS backbone to the closest healthy endpoint with fast failover. NLBs in each Region can target the on-premises servers by IP address (over VPN/Direct Connect), so the application stays on premises while gaining performance and availability.

others.B: ALBs do not support UDP.
others.C: CloudFront does not support UDP traffic.
others.D: ALBs and CloudFront do not support UDP.

e.tip: UDP + global performance = Global Accelerator with NLB endpoints.

q:
A solutions architect wants all new users to have specific complexity requirements and mandatory rotation periods for IAM user passwords.

What should the solutions architect do to accomplish this?

o.A: Set an overall password policy for the entire AWS account.
o.B: Set a password policy for each IAM user in the AWS account.
o.C: Use third-party vendor software to set password requirements.
o.D: Attach an Amazon CloudWatch rule to the Create_newuser event to set the password with the appropriate requirements.

e.why: IAM supports a single account-level password policy that sets complexity rules and maximum password age (rotation) for all IAM users. Setting it once applies to all new users and password changes.

others.B: IAM password policies cannot be set per user.
others.C: Third-party software is unnecessary because IAM provides this natively.
others.D: There is no such event-based mechanism to set password requirements; it is far more complex.

e.tip: IAM password policy is account-wide.

q:
A company has migrated an application to Amazon EC2 Linux instances. One of these EC2 instances runs several 1-hour tasks on a schedule. These tasks were written by different teams and have no common programming language. The company is concerned about performance and scalability while these tasks run on a single instance. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to resolve these concerns.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Batch to run the tasks as jobs. Schedule the jobs by using Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events).
o.B: Convert the EC2 instance to a container. Use AWS App Runner to create the container on demand to run the tasks as jobs.
o.C: Copy the tasks into AWS Lambda functions. Schedule the Lambda functions by using Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events).
o.D: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of the EC2 instance that runs the tasks. Create an Auto Scaling group with the AMI to run multiple copies of the instance.

e.why: AWS Batch runs each task as a containerized job regardless of programming language, provisioning and scaling compute as needed. EventBridge schedules the jobs, removing single-instance bottlenecks with low operational overhead; one-hour tasks fit Batch with no time limit.

others.B: App Runner is for web applications and APIs, not scheduled batch jobs.
others.C: Lambda has a 15-minute maximum, so 1-hour tasks cannot run.
others.D: Cloning the whole instance does not distribute individual tasks and scales inefficiently.

e.tip: Jobs longer than 15 minutes rule out Lambda.

q:
A company runs a public three-tier web application in a VPC. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances that run in private subnets need to communicate with a license server over the internet. The company needs a managed solution that minimizes operational maintenance.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Provision a NAT instance in a public subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT instance.
o.B: Provision a NAT instance in a private subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT instance.
o.C: Provision a NAT gateway in a public subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT gateway.
o.D: Provision a NAT gateway in a private subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT gateway.

e.why: A NAT gateway is a managed, highly available (within an AZ) service that lets private-subnet instances initiate outbound internet connections. It must be placed in a public subnet with a route from private subnets, requiring no patching or maintenance.

others.A: NAT instances are self-managed EC2 instances requiring patching and failover handling.
others.B: A NAT instance in a private subnet cannot reach the internet, and it is self-managed.
others.D: A NAT gateway in a private subnet has no route to an internet gateway.

e.tip: Managed outbound internet for private subnets = NAT gateway in a public subnet (one per AZ for resilience).

q:
A company needs to create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster to host a digital media streaming application. The EKS cluster will use a managed node group that is backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes for storage. The company must encrypt all data at rest by using a customer managed key that is stored in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

Which combination of actions will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use a Kubernetes plugin that uses the customer managed key to perform data encryption.
o.B: After creation of the EKS cluster, locate the EBS volumes. Enable encryption by using the customer managed key.
o.C: Enable EBS encryption by default in the AWS Region where the EKS cluster will be created. Select the customer managed key as the default key.
o.D: Create the EKS cluster. Create an IAM role that has a policy that grants permission to the customer managed key. Associate the role with the EKS cluster.
o.E: Store the customer managed key as a Kubernetes secret in the EKS cluster. Use the customer managed key to encrypt the EBS volumes.

e.why: Enabling EBS encryption by default with the customer managed key ensures every new EBS volume for the node group is encrypted automatically. Granting the cluster/node role permission to use the KMS key allows volumes to be created and attached with that key.

others.A: A custom Kubernetes plugin adds operational overhead.
others.B: Existing EBS volumes cannot be encrypted in place; they must be recreated from encrypted snapshots.
others.E: KMS keys cannot be exported to store as Kubernetes secrets.

e.tip: Account/Region-wide EBS encryption by default is the easiest way to enforce encrypted volumes.

q:
A company wants to migrate an Oracle database to AWS. The database consists of a single table that contains millions of geographic information systems (GIS) images that are high resolution and are identified by a geographic code.

When a natural disaster occurs, tens of thousands of images get updated every few minutes. Each geographic code has a single image or row that is associated with it. The company wants a solution that is highly available and scalable during such events.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Store the images and geographic codes in a database table. Use Oracle running on an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.
o.B: Store the images in Amazon S3 buckets. Use Amazon DynamoDB with the geographic code as the key and the image S3 URL as the value.
o.C: Store the images and geographic codes in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) during times of high load.
o.D: Store the images in Amazon S3 buckets. Store geographic codes and image S3 URLs in a database table. Use Oracle running on an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.

e.why: High-resolution images belong in S3, which scales and is cheap, while DynamoDB stores the geographic code as the key and the S3 URL as the value. DynamoDB scales automatically to tens of thousands of updates and is highly available, making it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Storing large images in Oracle on RDS is expensive and scales poorly, plus licensing cost.
others.C: DynamoDB items are limited to 400 KB, too small for high-resolution images, and DAX helps reads, not writes.
others.D: Oracle on RDS adds licensing cost and does not scale writes as easily as DynamoDB.

e.tip: Large binaries in S3, metadata/pointers in a database.

q:
A company has an application that collects data from IoT sensors on automobiles. The data is streamed and stored in Amazon S3 through Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. The data produces trillions of S3 objects each year. Each morning, the company uses the data from the previous 30 days to retrain a suite of machine learning (ML) models.

Four times each year, the company uses the data from the previous 12 months to perform analysis and train other ML models. The data must be available with minimal delay for up to 1 year. After 1 year, the data must be retained for archival purposes.

Which storage solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
o.B: Use the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically move objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
o.C: Use the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
o.D: Use the S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days, and then to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.

e.why: Data is used daily for 30 days, so S3 Standard fits initially; afterwards it is accessed only quarterly, so Standard-IA keeps it immediately available at lower cost. After 1 year it moves to Glacier Deep Archive for cheapest archival, all via lifecycle rules.

others.A: With trillions of objects, Intelligent-Tiering's per-object monitoring fees become very costly for a pattern that is already predictable.
others.B: Intelligent-Tiering's archive tiers are not Deep Archive storage class transitions by age, and monitoring fees remain high.
others.C: Standard-IA for brand-new data that is read every day incurs high retrieval charges.

e.tip: Known access pattern = explicit lifecycle rules; unknown pattern = Intelligent-Tiering.

q:
A company is running several business applications in three separate VPCs within the us-east-1 Region. The applications must be able to communicate between VPCs. The applications also must be able to consistently send hundreds of gigabytes of data each day to a latency-sensitive application that runs in a single on-premises data center.

A solutions architect needs to design a network connectivity solution that maximizes cost-effectiveness.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Configure three AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections from the data center to AWS. Establish connectivity by configuring one VPN connection for each VPC.
o.C: Set up three AWS Direct Connect connections from the data center to a Direct Connect gateway in us-east-1. Establish connectivity by configuring each VPC to use one of the Direct Connect connections.
o.B: Launch a third-party virtual network appliance in each VPC. Establish an IPsec tunnel between the data center and each virtual appliance.
o.D: Set up one AWS Direct Connect connection from the data center to AWS. Create a transit gateway, and attach each VPC to the transit gateway. Establish connectivity between the Direct Connect connection and the transit gateway.

fixed: Options A and B were truncated and have been completed.

e.why: One AWS Direct Connect connection gives consistent, low-latency bandwidth to the data center and lower data transfer out rates than the internet. A transit gateway attached to all three VPCs, and to Direct Connect through a Direct Connect gateway, handles both inter-VPC and on-premises routing cost-effectively.

others.A: VPNs over the internet give inconsistent latency for latency-sensitive traffic and do not connect the VPCs to each other.
others.B: Self-managed appliances and IPsec tunnels over the internet add cost and overhead and give inconsistent latency.
others.C: Three Direct Connect connections cost much more than one shared connection, and they do not provide inter-VPC routing.

e.tip: Many VPCs plus on-premises with consistent performance = one Direct Connect plus a transit gateway.

q:
An ecommerce company is building a distributed application that involves several serverless functions and AWS services to complete order-processing tasks. These tasks require manual approvals as part of the workflow. A solutions architect needs to design an architecture for the order-processing application. The solution must be able to combine multiple AWS Lambda functions into responsive serverless applications. The solution also must orchestrate data and services that run on Amazon EC2 instances, containers, or on-premises servers.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Step Functions to build the application.
o.B: Integrate all the application components in an AWS Glue job.
o.C: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to build the application.
o.D: Use AWS Lambda functions and Amazon EventBridge events to build the application.

e.why: Step Functions orchestrates Lambda functions and services on EC2, containers or on premises (via activities), and supports human approval steps using callback task tokens. It is serverless with built-in state, retries and error handling.

others.B: Glue jobs are for ETL, not general workflow orchestration with approvals.
others.C: SQS decouples components but provides no workflow orchestration or approval logic.
others.D: Lambda plus EventBridge requires building orchestration and state handling yourself.

e.tip: Workflow with manual approval = Step Functions callback pattern (waitForTaskToken).

q:
A company has launched an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Most of the connections to the database come from serverless applications. Application traffic to the database changes significantly at random intervals. At times of high demand, users report that their applications experience database connection rejection errors.

Which solution will resolve this issue with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create a proxy in RDS Proxy. Configure the users’ applications to use the DB instance through RDS Proxy.
o.B: Deploy Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached between the users’ applications and the DB instance.
o.C: Migrate the DB instance to a different instance class that has higher I/O capacity. Configure the users’ applications to use the new DB instance.
o.D: Configure Multi-AZ for the DB instance. Configure the users’ applications to switch between the DB instances.

e.why: RDS Proxy maintains a pool of database connections and multiplexes many short-lived serverless connections onto them, preventing connection rejection during spikes. It is fully managed and only requires pointing applications at the proxy endpoint.

others.B: Memcached caches data but does not manage database connections, and requires code changes.
others.C: Higher I/O capacity does not solve connection exhaustion from bursty serverless clients.
others.D: The Multi-AZ standby cannot accept connections, so it does not add connection capacity.

e.tip: Serverless apps exhausting DB connections = RDS Proxy.

q:
A company recently deployed a new auditing system to centralize information about operating system versions, patching, and installed software for Amazon EC2 instances. A solutions architect must ensure all instances provisioned through EC2 Auto Scaling groups successfully send reports to the auditing system as soon as they are launched and terminated.

Which solution achieves these goals MOST efficiently?

o.A: Use a scheduled AWS Lambda function and run a script remotely on all EC2 instances to send data to the audit system.
o.B: Use EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks to run a custom script to send data to the audit system when instances are launched and terminated.
o.C: Use an EC2 Auto Scaling launch configuration to run a custom script through user data to send data to the audit system when instances are launched and terminated.
o.D: Run a custom script on the instance operating system to send data to the audit system. Configure the script to be invoked by the EC2 Auto Scaling group when the instance starts and is terminated.

e.why: Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks pause instances in Pending:Wait and Terminating:Wait states so a script (for example via EventBridge and Systems Manager or Lambda) can send reports reliably on both launch and termination. This is built in and works for every instance the group launches or terminates.

others.A: A scheduled Lambda misses the exact launch and termination moments and is inefficient.
others.C: User data runs only at launch, not at termination, and launch configurations are deprecated.
others.D: Auto Scaling cannot directly invoke an OS script on termination without lifecycle hooks.

e.tip: Run actions on scale-out/scale-in events = lifecycle hooks.

q:
A company is developing a real-time multiplayer game that uses UDP for communications between the client and servers in an Auto Scaling group. Spikes in demand are anticipated during the day, so the game server platform must adapt accordingly. Developers want to store gamer scores and other non-relational data in a database solution that will scale without intervention.

Which solution should a solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Use Amazon Route 53 for traffic distribution and Amazon Aurora Serverless for data storage.
o.B: Use a Network Load Balancer for traffic distribution and Amazon DynamoDB on-demand for data storage.
o.C: Use a Network Load Balancer for traffic distribution and Amazon Aurora Global Database for data storage.
o.D: Use an Application Load Balancer for traffic distribution and Amazon DynamoDB global tables for data storage.

e.why: A Network Load Balancer supports UDP and scales to handle traffic spikes for the game servers. DynamoDB on-demand stores non-relational data like scores and scales automatically without capacity planning or intervention.

others.A: Route 53 is DNS-based and not a load balancer, and Aurora is relational.
others.C: Aurora Global Database is relational and requires capacity management.
others.D: ALBs do not support UDP.

e.tip: UDP load balancing = NLB; non-relational auto-scaling = DynamoDB on-demand.

q:
A company hosts a frontend application that uses an Amazon API Gateway API backend that is integrated with AWS Lambda. When the API receives requests, the Lambda function loads many libraries. Then the Lambda function connects to an Amazon RDS database, processes the data, and returns the data to the frontend application. The company wants to ensure that response latency is as low as possible for all its users with the fewest number of changes to the company's operations.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Establish a connection between the frontend application and the database to make queries faster by bypassing the API.
o.B: Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function that handles the requests.
o.C: Cache the results of the queries in Amazon S3 for faster retrieval of similar datasets.
o.D: Increase the size of the database to increase the number of connections Lambda can establish at one time.

e.why: Loading many libraries causes cold start latency on new Lambda execution environments. Provisioned concurrency keeps a set number of environments initialized and ready, so all users get consistently low latency with just a configuration change.

others.A: Bypassing the API exposes the database and requires major changes.
others.C: Caching query results in S3 adds code and does not address cold starts.
others.D: A bigger database does not reduce Lambda initialization latency.

e.tip: Lambda cold starts = provisioned concurrency (or SnapStart for Java).

q:
A company is migrating its on-premises workload to the AWS Cloud. The company already uses several Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS DB instances. The company wants a solution that automatically starts and stops the EC2 instances and DB instances outside of business hours. The solution must minimize cost and infrastructure maintenance.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Scale the EC2 instances by using elastic resize. Scale the DB instances to zero outside of business hours.
o.B: Explore AWS Marketplace for partner solutions that will automatically start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
o.C: Launch another EC2 instance. Configure a crontab schedule to run shell scripts that will start and stop the existing EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that will start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function on a schedule.
