e.why: A Lambda function that calls the EC2 and RDS start/stop APIs, invoked by EventBridge scheduled rules, is serverless and costs almost nothing to run. It automatically starts and stops resources around business hours with no infrastructure to maintain.

others.A: EC2 has no elastic resize, and RDS instances cannot scale to zero.
others.B: Marketplace solutions may add licensing cost and dependency on a third party.
others.C: An extra EC2 instance running cron adds cost and maintenance.

e.tip: Scheduled automation without servers = EventBridge Scheduler + Lambda (or Instance Scheduler on AWS).

q:
A company hosts a three-tier web application that includes a PostgreSQL database. The database stores the metadata from documents. The company searches the metadata for key terms to retrieve documents that the company reviews in a report each month. The documents are stored in Amazon S3. The documents are usually written only once, but they are updated frequently.

The reporting process takes a few hours with the use of relational queries. The reporting process must not prevent any document modifications or the addition of new documents. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to speed up the reporting process.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of change to the application code?

o.A: Set up a new Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) cluster that includes a read replica. Scale the read replica to generate the reports.
o.B: Set up a new Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster that includes an Aurora Replica. Issue queries to the Aurora Replica to generate the reports.
o.C: Set up a new Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Configure the reporting module to query the secondary RDS node so that the reporting module does not affect the primary node.
o.D: Set up a new Amazon DynamoDB table to store the documents. Use a fixed write capacity to support new document entries. Automatically scale the read capacity to support the reports.

e.why: Aurora PostgreSQL is compatible with the existing PostgreSQL application, so code changes are minimal. Directing reporting queries to an Aurora Replica offloads the long relational queries so document writes on the primary are not blocked.

others.A: DocumentDB is a MongoDB-compatible document database, requiring rewriting relational queries.
others.C: The standby in a single-standby Multi-AZ RDS deployment cannot serve read traffic.
others.D: DynamoDB requires a redesign and does not support the existing relational queries.

e.tip: A classic Multi-AZ standby is not readable; use read replicas or Multi-AZ DB clusters.

q:
A company has a three-tier application on AWS that ingests sensor data from its users’ devices. The traffic flows through a Network Load Balancer (NLB), then to Amazon EC2 instances for the web tier, and finally to EC2 instances for the application tier. The application tier makes calls to a database.

What should a solutions architect do to improve the security of the data in transit?

o.A: Configure a TLS listener. Deploy the server certificate on the NLB.
o.B: Configure AWS Shield Advanced. Enable AWS WAF on the NLB.
o.C: Change the load balancer to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Enable AWS WAF on the ALB.
o.D: Encrypt the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume on the EC2 instances by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

fixed: Option B text was missing and options A and C were truncated; they have been reconstructed.

e.why: A TLS listener on the NLB with a server certificate (for example from ACM) encrypts client traffic in transit and terminates TLS at the load balancer. This directly improves the security of the sensor data in transit.

others.B: Shield Advanced and WAF protect against attacks; they do not encrypt data in transit, and WAF cannot be attached to an NLB.
others.C: AWS WAF filters web requests but does not encrypt data in transit.
others.D: EBS encryption protects data at rest, not in transit.

e.tip: Data in transit = TLS listeners and certificates; data at rest = KMS encryption.

q:
A company is planning to migrate a commercial off-the-shelf application from its on-premises data center to AWS. The software has a software licensing model using sockets and cores with predictable capacity and uptime requirements. The company wants to use its existing licenses, which were purchased earlier this year.

Which Amazon EC2 pricing option is the MOST cost-effective?

o.A: Dedicated Reserved Hosts
o.B: Dedicated On-Demand Hosts
o.C: Dedicated Reserved Instances
o.D: Dedicated On-Demand Instances

e.why: Socket- and core-based BYOL licensing requires Dedicated Hosts, which expose physical sockets and cores. With predictable capacity and uptime, reserving the Dedicated Hosts gives the largest discount, making Dedicated Reserved Hosts most cost-effective.

others.B: On-Demand Dedicated Hosts support BYOL but cost more than reserved for steady usage.
others.C: Dedicated Instances do not provide visibility into sockets and cores for licensing.
others.D: Dedicated On-Demand Instances lack socket/core visibility and cost more.

e.tip: Per-socket/per-core BYOL = Dedicated Hosts.

q:
A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 Linux instances across multiple Availability Zones. The application needs a storage layer that is highly available and Portable Operating System Interface (POSIX)-compliant. The storage layer must provide maximum data durability and must be shareable across the EC2 instances. The data in the storage layer will be accessed frequently for the first 30 days and will be accessed infrequently after that time.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move infrequently accessed data to S3 Glacier.
o.B: Use the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move infrequently accessed data to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).
o.C: Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard storage class. Create a lifecycle management policy to move infrequently accessed data to EFS Standard-Infrequent Access (EFS Standard-IA).
o.D: Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) One Zone storage class. Create a lifecycle management policy to move infrequently accessed data to EFS One Zone-Infrequent Access (EFS One Zone-IA).

e.why: EFS Standard is a POSIX-compliant shared file system that stores data across multiple AZs for high availability and maximum durability. A lifecycle management policy moves files not accessed for 30 days to EFS Standard-IA, reducing cost.

others.A: S3 is object storage and not POSIX-compliant, and Glacier is not readily accessible.
others.B: S3 is not a POSIX-compliant shared file system.
others.D: EFS One Zone stores data in a single AZ, reducing availability and durability.

e.tip: POSIX shared storage across AZs = EFS Standard with lifecycle to IA.

q:
A solutions architect is creating a new VPC design. There are two public subnets for the load balancer, two private subnets for web servers, and two private subnets for MySQL. The web servers use only HTTPS. The solutions architect has already created a security group for the load balancer allowing port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Company policy requires that each resource has the least access required to still be able to perform its tasks.

Which additional configuration strategy should the solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a security group for the web servers and allow port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Create a security group for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.
o.B: Create a network ACL for the web servers and allow port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Create a network ACL for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.
o.C: Create a security group for the web servers and allow port 443 from the load balancer. Create a security group for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.
o.D: Create a network ACL for the web servers and allow port 443 from the load balancer. Create a network ACL for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.

e.why: Least privilege means each tier accepts traffic only from the tier directly in front of it. Security groups can reference other security groups, so the web server group allows 443 only from the load balancer's security group and the MySQL group allows 3306 only from the web server security group.

others.A: Allowing 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 on private web servers grants far more access than needed, since only the load balancer must reach them.
others.B: Network ACLs are attached to subnets, cannot reference security groups, and opening 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 is not least privilege.
others.D: Network ACLs are stateless subnet-level controls that cannot use a security group as a source, so the 3306 rule as written is impossible.

e.tip: Chain security groups by referencing the upstream tier's security group ID instead of CIDR ranges.

q:
An ecommerce company is running a multi-tier application on AWS. The front-end and backend tiers both run on Amazon EC2, and the database runs on Amazon RDS for MySQL. The backend tier communicates with the RDS instance. There are frequent calls to return identical datasets from the database that are causing performance slowdowns.

Which action should be taken to improve the performance of the backend?

o.A: Implement Amazon SNS to store the database calls.
o.B: Implement Amazon ElastiCache to cache the large datasets.
o.C: Implement an RDS for MySQL read replica to cache database calls.
o.D: Implement Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the calls to the database.

e.why: Repeated identical queries are the textbook case for an in-memory cache. Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) lets the backend serve those datasets from memory with sub-millisecond latency, offloading the RDS instance and fixing the slowdown.

others.A: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub messaging service and cannot store or cache query results.
others.C: A read replica offloads reads but still executes each query against disk-backed storage; it is not a cache and adds replication lag.
others.D: Kinesis Data Firehose delivers streaming data to destinations and does nothing to speed up database reads.

e.tip: Frequent identical reads = ElastiCache; read scaling for varied queries = read replicas.

q:
A new employee has joined a company as a deployment engineer. The deployment engineer will be using AWS CloudFormation templates to create multiple AWS resources. A solutions architect wants the deployment engineer to perform job activities while following the principle of least privilege.

Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to accomplish this goal? (Choose two.)

o.A: Have the deployment engineer use AWS account root user credentials for performing AWS CloudFormation stack operations.
o.B: Create a new IAM user for the deployment engineer and add the IAM user to a group that has the PowerUsers IAM policy attached.
o.C: Create a new IAM user for the deployment engineer and add the IAM user to a group that has the AdministratorAccess IAM policy attached.
o.D: Create a new IAM user for the deployment engineer and add the IAM user to a group that has an IAM policy that allows AWS CloudFormation actions only.
o.E: Create an IAM role for the deployment engineer to explicitly define the permissions specific to the AWS CloudFormation stack and launch stacks using that IAM role.

e.why: Least privilege means giving the engineer only what CloudFormation work requires. An IAM user in a group whose policy allows only CloudFormation actions limits the human's own permissions, and an IAM role scoped to the stack's resources (a CloudFormation service role) lets stacks create resources without giving the user broad direct access.

others.A: Root user credentials have unrestricted access and should never be used for daily tasks.
others.B: PowerUserAccess grants full access to almost all services, far beyond what CloudFormation operations need.
others.C: AdministratorAccess grants full access to everything and violates least privilege.

e.tip: Use a CloudFormation service role so users need only cloudformation:* and iam:PassRole, not every resource permission.

q:
A company is deploying a two-tier web application in a VPC. The web tier is using an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with public subnets that span multiple Availability Zones. The database tier consists of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in separate private subnets. The web tier requires access to the database to retrieve product information.

The web application is not working as intended. The web application reports that it cannot connect to the database. The database is confirmed to be up and running. All configurations for the network ACLs, security groups, and route tables are still in their default states.

What should a solutions architect recommend to fix the application?

o.A: Add an explicit rule to the private subnet’s network ACL to allow traffic from the web tier’s EC2 instances.
o.B: Add a route in the VPC route table to allow traffic between the web tier’s EC2 instances and the database tier.
o.C: Deploy the web tier's EC2 instances and the database tier’s RDS instance into two separate VPCs, and configure VPC peering.
o.D: Add an inbound rule to the security group of the database tier’s RDS instance to allow traffic from the web tiers security group.

e.why: Default network ACLs allow all traffic, and the default VPC route table already includes a local route between all subnets. What blocks the connection is the RDS security group, which by default allows no inbound traffic from the web tier, so an inbound rule on port 3306 referencing the web tier's security group fixes it.

others.A: The default network ACL already allows all inbound and outbound traffic, so no extra ACL rule is needed.
others.B: The local route for the VPC CIDR already exists in every route table, so subnets can already route to each other.
others.C: Splitting into two VPCs with peering adds complexity and still would not fix the security group that is blocking traffic.

e.tip: Default NACL = allow all; default local route = intra-VPC reachability; custom SG = deny all inbound until you add rules.

q:
A company has a large dataset for its online advertising business stored in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in a single Availability Zone. The company wants business reporting queries to run without impacting the write operations to the production DB instance.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Deploy RDS read replicas to process the business reporting queries.
o.B: Scale out the DB instance horizontally by placing it behind an Elastic Load Balancer.
o.C: Scale up the DB instance to a larger instance type to handle write operations and queries.
o.D: Deploy the DB instance in multiple Availability Zones to process the business reporting queries.

e.why: RDS read replicas use asynchronous replication to give a separate, readable copy of the database. Pointing reporting queries at a read replica isolates that read load from the primary, so write performance on production is not affected.

others.B: Elastic Load Balancers do not distribute database connections across RDS instances, and RDS cannot be scaled out for writes this way.
others.C: A bigger instance still serves both workloads on the same database, so heavy reports can still hurt writes, and it costs more.
others.D: In a standard Multi-AZ instance deployment the standby cannot serve reads; it exists only for failover.

e.tip: Multi-AZ = availability; read replicas = read scaling.

q:
A company hosts a three-tier ecommerce application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). All ecommerce data is stored in an Amazon RDS for MariaDB Multi-AZ DB instance.

The company wants to optimize customer session management during transactions. The application must store session data durably.

Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Turn on the sticky sessions feature (session affinity) on the ALB.
o.B: Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store customer session information.
o.C: Deploy an Amazon Cognito user pool to manage user session information.
o.D: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to store customer session information.
o.E: Use AWS Systems Manager Application Manager in the application to manage user session information.

fixed: Option A was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: The key pairs sticky sessions on the ALB, which keeps a user on the same instance during a transaction, with an ElastiCache for Redis cluster as a shared external session store. Redis supports replication, Multi-AZ failover and persistence, so session state survives an instance failing or being scaled in.

others.B: DynamoDB is also a valid durable session store, and many consider it a better fit, but it is not the keyed answer here.
others.C: Cognito user pools handle authentication, not application transaction session state.
others.E: Systems Manager Application Manager is for operations management, not session storage.

e.tip: Shared session state off the instances = ElastiCache (Redis) or DynamoDB; sticky sessions alone are not durable.

q:
A company needs a backup strategy for its three-tier stateless web application. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group with a dynamic scaling policy that is configured to respond to scaling events. The database tier runs on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The web application does not require temporary local storage on the EC2 instances. The company’s recovery point objective (RPO) is 2 hours.

The backup strategy must maximize scalability and optimize resource utilization for this environment.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Take snapshots of Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes of the EC2 instances and database every 2 hours to meet the RPO.
o.B: Configure a snapshot lifecycle policy to take Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots. Enable automated backups in Amazon RDS to meet the RPO.
o.C: Retain the latest Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) of the web and application tiers. Enable automated backups in Amazon RDS and use point-in-time recovery to meet the RPO.
o.D: Take snapshots of Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes of the EC2 instances every 2 hours. Enable automated backups in Amazon RDS and use point-in-time recovery to meet the RPO.

e.why: The web tier is stateless and needs no local storage, so the only backups it needs are current AMIs to relaunch instances through Auto Scaling. RDS automated backups with point-in-time recovery (restore to any second within the retention window, typically within about 5 minutes of now) easily meet a 2-hour RPO with no extra scheduling.

others.A: Snapshotting EBS volumes of stateless, constantly scaling instances wastes storage and effort, and manual snapshots every 2 hours are harder to operate.
others.B: EBS snapshot lifecycle policies on stateless instances add cost without value, since nothing unique lives on those volumes.
others.D: Taking EBS snapshots of stateless instances every 2 hours is unnecessary and uses resources poorly.

e.tip: Stateless tier: back up the AMI, not the volumes.

q:
A company wants to deploy a new public web application on AWS. The application includes a web server tier that uses Amazon EC2 instances. The application also includes a database tier that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance.

The application must be secure and accessible for global customers that have dynamic IP addresses.

How should a solutions architect configure the security groups to meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure the security group for the web servers to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Configure the security group for the DB instance to allow inbound traffic on port 3306 from the security group of the web servers.
o.B: Configure the security group for the web servers to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from the IP addresses of the customers. Configure the security group for the DB instance to allow inbound traffic on port 3306 from the security group of the web servers.
o.C: Configure the security group for the web servers to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from the IP addresses of the customers. Configure the security group for the DB instance to allow inbound traffic on port 3306 from the IP addresses of the customers.
o.D: Configure the security group for the web servers to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Configure the security group for the DB instance to allow inbound traffic on port 3306 from 0.0.0.0/0.

e.why: Global customers with dynamic IPs cannot be allowlisted, so the web tier must accept HTTPS (443) from 0.0.0.0/0. The database should accept 3306 only from the web server security group, keeping it unreachable from the internet.

others.B: Customer IP addresses are dynamic and global, so allowlisting them is impossible to maintain.
others.C: Customers should never connect to the database directly, and their dynamic IPs cannot be listed anyway.
others.D: Opening MySQL 3306 to the whole internet is a serious security risk.

q:
A payment processing company records all voice communication with its customers and stores the audio files in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs to capture the text from the audio files. The company must remove from the text any personally identifiable information (PII) that belongs to customers.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Process the audio files by using Amazon Kinesis Video Streams. Use an AWS Lambda function to scan for known PII patterns.
o.B: When an audio file is uploaded to the S3 bucket, invoke an AWS Lambda function to start an Amazon Textract task to analyze the call recordings.
o.C: Configure an Amazon Transcribe transcription job with PII redaction turned on. When an audio file is uploaded to the S3 bucket, invoke an AWS Lambda function to start the transcription job. Store the output in a separate S3 bucket.
o.D: Create an Amazon Connect contact flow that ingests the audio files with transcription turned on. Embed an AWS Lambda function to scan for known PII patterns. Use Amazon EventBridge to start the contact flow when an audio file is uploaded to the S3 bucket.

e.why: Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text and has built-in PII redaction for transcripts. Starting a Transcribe job from an S3-triggered Lambda function and writing the redacted output to another bucket is a fully managed, event-driven solution.

others.A: Kinesis Video Streams ingests live video, not stored audio files, and pattern-matching PII yourself in Lambda is fragile.
others.B: Amazon Textract pulls text from documents and images, not audio recordings.
others.D: Amazon Connect is a contact center service; using it to process stored files with custom PII scanning is overly complex.

e.tip: Speech to text = Transcribe; document OCR = Textract; PII in free text = Comprehend or Transcribe redaction.

q:
A company is running a multi-tier ecommerce web application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances with an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Amazon RDS is configured with the latest generation DB instance with 2,000 GB of storage in a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. The database performance affects the application during periods of high demand.

A database administrator analyzes the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs and discovers that the application performance always degrades when the number of read and write IOPS is higher than 20,000.

What should a solutions architect do to improve the application performance?

o.A: Replace the volume with a magnetic volume.
o.B: Increase the number of IOPS on the gp3 volume.
o.C: Replace the volume with a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volume.
o.D: Replace the 2,000 GB gp3 volume with two 1,000 GB gp3 volumes.

e.why: The workload needs more than 20,000 sustained IOPS with consistent performance. Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) storage is built for I/O-intensive production databases, giving high, predictable IOPS and better durability, so moving the RDS storage to io2 removes the bottleneck.

others.A: Magnetic storage is legacy and much slower, so it would make performance worse.
others.B: On RDS, gp3 volumes of 400 GiB or more can be provisioned well above 20,000 IOPS, so this could work, but the exam expects io2 for sustained high-IOPS production databases.
others.D: RDS manages its own storage layout; you cannot attach two separate gp3 volumes to an RDS instance.

e.tip: On RDS, gp3 at 400 GiB or more stripes across volumes (baseline 12,000 IOPS, scalable higher); exams still favor io1/io2 for heavy, consistent IOPS.

q:
An IAM user made several configuration changes to AWS resources in their company's account during a production deployment last week. A solutions architect learned that a couple of security group rules are not configured as desired. The solutions architect wants to confirm which IAM user was responsible for making changes.

Which service should the solutions architect use to find the desired information?

o.A: Amazon GuardDuty
o.B: Amazon Inspector
o.C: AWS CloudTrail
o.D: AWS Config

e.why: AWS CloudTrail records API calls, including which IAM identity made the call, when, and from where. Looking up AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress and similar events in CloudTrail event history shows who changed the security group rules.

others.A: GuardDuty detects threats from logs; it does not give an audit trail of who made each configuration change.
others.B: Amazon Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities and network exposure, not who made changes.
others.D: AWS Config records how resource configurations change over time, but CloudTrail is the source for which user made the API call.

e.tip: Who did it = CloudTrail; what changed and is it compliant = Config.

q:
A company has implemented a self-managed DNS service on AWS. The solution consists of the following:

• Amazon EC2 instances in different AWS Regions
• Endpoints of a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator

The company wants to protect the solution against DDoS attacks.

What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.A: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Add the accelerator as a resource to protect.
o.B: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Add the EC2 instances as resources to protect.
o.C: Create an AWS WAF web ACL that includes a rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the accelerator.
o.D: Create an AWS WAF web ACL that includes a rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the EC2 instances.

e.why: AWS Shield Advanced can protect Global Accelerator accelerators directly as protected resources, adding DDoS detection, mitigation and access to the Shield Response Team. Because traffic enters through the accelerator, protecting the accelerator covers the DNS service at its entry point.

others.B: The EC2 instances sit behind the accelerator, so protection belongs on the internet-facing accelerator.
others.C: AWS WAF cannot be associated with Global Accelerator, and WAF handles HTTP layer 7, not DNS/UDP floods.
others.D: WAF cannot be attached directly to EC2 instances, and it does not protect non-HTTP DNS traffic.

e.tip: Shield Advanced protects CloudFront, Route 53, Global Accelerator, ELB and Elastic IPs; WAF only fronts CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito and similar HTTP services.

q:
An ecommerce company needs to run a scheduled daily job to aggregate and filter sales records for analytics. The company stores the sales records in an Amazon S3 bucket. Each object can be up to 10 GB in size. Based on the number of sales events, the job can take up to an hour to complete. The CPU and memory usage of the job are constant and are known in advance.

A solutions architect needs to minimize the amount of operational effort that is needed for the job to run.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Create an AWS Lambda function that has an Amazon EventBridge notification. Schedule the EventBridge event to run once a day.
o.B: Create an AWS Lambda function. Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API, and integrate the API with the function. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that calls the API and invokes the function.
o.C: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an AWS Fargate launch type. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that launches an ECS task on the cluster to run the job.
o.D: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an Amazon EC2 launch type and an Auto Scaling group with at least one EC2 instance. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that launches an ECS task on the cluster to run the job.

e.why: The job can run up to an hour and processes objects up to 10 GB, which rules out Lambda's 15-minute limit. An EventBridge scheduled rule that launches an ECS task on AWS Fargate runs the container with known CPU and memory and no servers to manage, minimizing operational effort.

others.A: Lambda functions time out after 15 minutes, so a job of up to an hour cannot run reliably.
others.B: Adding API Gateway does not remove Lambda's 15-minute limit, and API Gateway's integration timeout is also short.
others.D: The EC2 launch type means managing and paying for always-on instances in an Auto Scaling group, which adds overhead.

e.tip: More than 15 minutes and serverless = Fargate (or AWS Batch on Fargate).

q:
A company needs to transfer 600 TB of data from its on-premises network-attached storage (NAS) system to the AWS Cloud. The data transfer must be complete within 2 weeks. The data is sensitive and must be encrypted in transit. The company’s internet connection can support an upload speed of 100 Mbps.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use Amazon S3 multi-part upload functionality to transfer the files over HTTPS.
o.B: Create a VPN connection between the on-premises NAS system and the nearest AWS Region. Transfer the data over the VPN connection.
o.C: Use the AWS Snow Family console to order several AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices. Use the devices to transfer the data to Amazon S3.
o.D: Set up a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection between the company location and the nearest AWS Region. Transfer the data over a VPN connection into the Region to store the data in Amazon S3.

e.why: At 100 Mbps, 600 TB would take well over a year, so an online transfer cannot finish in 2 weeks. Several Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices (about 80 TB usable each) move the data offline with 256-bit encryption, at a low cost.

others.A: S3 multipart upload over a 100 Mbps link is far too slow for 600 TB in 2 weeks.
others.B: A VPN still runs over the same 100 Mbps internet link, so it is just as slow.
others.D: Direct Connect takes weeks to months to provision, and a 10 Gbps dedicated connection is much more expensive for a one-time move.

e.tip: Do the math: 100 Mbps moves roughly 1 TB per day.

q:
A financial company hosts a web application on AWS. The application uses an Amazon API Gateway Regional API endpoint to give users the ability to retrieve current stock prices. The company’s security team has noticed an increase in the number of API requests. The security team is concerned that HTTP flood attacks might take the application offline.

A solutions architect must design a solution to protect the application from this type of attack.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the API Gateway Regional API endpoint with a maximum TTL of 24 hours.
o.B: Create a Regional AWS WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the API Gateway stage.
o.C: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to monitor the Count metric and alert the security team when the predefined rate is reached.
o.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with Lambda@Edge in front of the API Gateway Regional API endpoint. Create an AWS Lambda function to block requests from IP addresses that exceed the predefined rate.

e.why: An AWS WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule blocks IP addresses that exceed a set request rate, which directly counters HTTP floods. Regional API Gateway stages can be associated with a regional web ACL natively, so this is a managed solution with the least operational overhead.

others.A: Caching stock prices for 24 hours would serve stale data and does not stop floods of uncacheable or varied requests.
others.C: CloudWatch alarms only alert people and do not block the attack.
others.D: Custom Lambda@Edge rate limiting is complex to build and maintain compared with WAF's built-in rate-based rules.

e.tip: HTTP flood or too many requests from an IP = WAF rate-based rule.

q:
A meteorological startup company has a custom web application to sell weather data to its users online. The company uses Amazon DynamoDB to store its data and wants to build a new service that sends an alert to the managers of four internal teams every time a new weather event is recorded. The company does not want this new service to affect the performance of the current application.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

o.A: Use DynamoDB transactions to write new event data to the table. Configure the transactions to notify internal teams.
o.B: Have the current application publish a message to four Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topics. Have each team subscribe to one topic.
o.C: Enable Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the table. Use triggers to write to a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to which the teams can subscribe.
o.D: Add a custom attribute to each record to flag new items. Write a cron job that scans the table every minute for items that are new and notifies an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to which the teams can subscribe.

e.why: DynamoDB Streams records item changes asynchronously, outside the application's write path, so the current app's performance is unaffected. A Lambda trigger on the stream publishes each new event to one SNS topic, and all four teams subscribe to it, which is the least operational overhead.

others.A: DynamoDB transactions guarantee atomic writes and have no notification feature; they also cost more write capacity.
others.B: Changing the app to publish to four topics adds work to the app's own request path and is more to maintain than one topic.
others.D: Scanning the table every minute uses a lot of read capacity, can slow the app, and means managing a cron job.

e.tip: React to DynamoDB changes = Streams + Lambda; fan out = one SNS topic with many subscribers.

q:
A company wants to use the AWS Cloud to make an existing application highly available and resilient. The current version of the application resides in the company's data center. The application recently experienced data loss after a database server crashed because of an unexpected power outage.

The company needs a solution that avoids any single points of failure. The solution must give the application the ability to scale to meet user demand.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance in a Multi-AZ configuration.
o.B: Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone. Deploy the database on an EC2 instance. Enable EC2 Auto Recovery.
o.C: Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance with a read replica in a single Availability Zone. Promote the read replica to replace the primary DB instance if the primary DB instance fails.
o.D: Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Deploy the primary and secondary database servers on EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach to create shared storage between the instances.

e.why: An Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs removes the app tier as a single point of failure and scales with demand. RDS Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby in another AZ with automatic failover, so a crashed database server does not lose committed data.

others.B: A single AZ is a single point of failure, and a database on one EC2 instance can still lose data.
others.C: Read replicas replicate asynchronously and need manual promotion, so data can be lost and failover is not automatic; a single AZ is also a single point of failure.
others.D: EBS Multi-Attach works only within a single AZ and only with io1/io2, so it cannot share storage across AZs; self-managed databases also add overhead.

e.tip: Survive a DB crash with no data loss = RDS Multi-AZ (synchronous replication).

q:
A company needs to ingest and handle large amounts of streaming data that its application generates. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and sends data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, which is configured with default settings. Every other day, the application consumes the data and writes the data to an Amazon S3 bucket for business intelligence (BI) processing. The company observes that Amazon S3 is not receiving all the data that the application sends to Kinesis Data Streams.

What should a solutions architect do to resolve this issue?

o.A: Update the Kinesis Data Streams default settings by modifying the data retention period.
o.B: Update the application to use the Kinesis Producer Library (KPL) to send the data to Kinesis Data Streams.
o.C: Update the number of Kinesis shards to handle the throughput of the data that is sent to Kinesis Data Streams.
o.D: Turn on S3 Versioning within the S3 bucket to preserve every version of every object that is ingested in the S3 bucket.

e.why: Kinesis Data Streams keeps records for 24 hours by default. Because the consumer only reads every other day, records expire before they are read. Raising the retention period (up to 365 days) keeps the data until the consumer processes it.

others.B: The KPL improves producer throughput and batching, but it does not stop records from expiring before the consumer reads them.
others.C: Adding shards helps throughput problems, but the data loss here comes from the retention window, not throttling.
others.D: S3 Versioning keeps object versions after they arrive; it cannot recover data that never reached S3.

e.tip: Kinesis Data Streams retention: 24 hours by default, extendable to 7 days, or up to 365 days with long-term retention.

q:
A developer has an application that uses an AWS Lambda function to upload files to Amazon S3 and needs the required permissions to perform the task. The developer already has an IAM user with valid IAM credentials required for Amazon S3.

What should a solutions architect do to grant the permissions?

o.A: Add required IAM permissions in the resource policy of the Lambda function.
o.B: Create a signed request using the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
o.C: Create a new IAM user and use the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
o.D: Create an IAM execution role with the required permissions and attach the IAM role to the Lambda function.

e.why: Lambda functions should get permissions from an IAM execution role, which supplies temporary credentials that rotate automatically. Attaching a role that grants the needed S3 actions avoids putting long-term IAM user keys in code.

others.A: A Lambda resource-based policy controls who can invoke the function, not what the function can access.
others.B: Putting long-term IAM user credentials in the function to sign requests is insecure and against best practice.
others.C: Making another IAM user and putting its keys in the function has the same problem of hard-coded long-term credentials.

e.tip: Compute services (EC2, Lambda, ECS) get permissions from roles, never from embedded access keys.

q:
A company has deployed a serverless application that invokes an AWS Lambda function when new documents are uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses the Lambda function to process the documents. After a recent marketing campaign, the company noticed that the application did not process many of the documents.

What should a solutions architect do to improve the architecture of this application?

o.A: Set the Lambda function's runtime timeout value to 15 minutes.
o.B: Configure an S3 bucket replication policy. Stage the documents in the S3 bucket for later processing.
o.C: Deploy an additional Lambda function. Load balance the processing of the documents across the two Lambda functions.
o.D: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Send the requests to the queue. Configure the queue as an event source for Lambda.

e.why: A traffic spike can exceed Lambda concurrency limits, and asynchronous S3 invocations that keep failing or are throttled can be dropped. Putting an SQS queue between S3 and Lambda buffers the events durably, so Lambda polls and processes them at a sustainable rate, with retries and an optional dead-letter queue.

others.A: A longer timeout does not fix throttling or dropped events during traffic spikes.
others.B: Replicating the bucket copies objects but adds no reliable processing or retry mechanism.
others.C: Lambda functions cannot be load balanced this way, and a second function draws on the same account concurrency limit.

e.tip: Bursty event processing = decouple with SQS.

q:
A solutions architect is designing the architecture for a software demonstration environment. The environment will run on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The system will experience significant increases in traffic during working hours but is not required to operate on weekends.

Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to ensure that the system can scale to meet demand? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use AWS Auto Scaling to adjust the ALB capacity based on request rate.
o.B: Use AWS Auto Scaling to scale the capacity of the VPC internet gateway.
o.C: Launch the EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions to distribute the load across Regions.
o.D: Use a target tracking scaling policy to scale the Auto Scaling group based on instance CPU utilization.
o.E: Use scheduled scaling to change the Auto Scaling group minimum, maximum, and desired capacity to zero for weekends. Revert to the default values at the start of the week.

e.why: Target tracking on average CPU utilization scales the Auto Scaling group out and in automatically as weekday traffic rises and falls. Scheduled actions that set min, max and desired capacity to zero for the weekend and restore them on Monday handle the known downtime pattern.

others.A: ALB capacity scales automatically and cannot be managed with AWS Auto Scaling.
others.B: Internet gateways scale horizontally and are fully managed, so there is nothing to scale.
others.C: Spreading a demo environment across Regions adds complexity and cost and does not deal with daily or weekend patterns.

e.tip: Predictable time patterns = scheduled scaling; variable load = target tracking.

q:
A solutions architect is designing a two-tiered architecture that includes a public subnet and a database subnet. The web servers in the public subnet must be open to the internet on port 443. The Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in the database subnet must be accessible only to the web servers on port 3306.

Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create a network ACL for the public subnet. Add a rule to deny outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on port 3306.
o.B: Create a security group for the DB instance. Add a rule to allow traffic from the public subnet CIDR block on port 3306.
o.C: Create a security group for the web servers in the public subnet. Add a rule to allow traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 443.
o.D: Create a security group for the DB instance. Add a rule to allow traffic from the web servers’ security group on port 3306.
o.E: Create a security group for the DB instance. Add a rule to deny all traffic except traffic from the web servers’ security group on port 3306.

e.why: The web servers' security group should allow 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 so internet users can reach them. The DB security group should allow 3306 only from the web servers' security group, which restricts database access to those instances.

others.A: Denying outbound 3306 from the public subnet would block the web servers from reaching the database.
others.B: Allowing the whole public subnet CIDR is broader than allowing only the web server security group.
others.E: Security groups support only allow rules; they cannot contain explicit deny rules.

e.tip: Security groups: allow only, stateful, can reference other SGs. NACLs: allow and deny, stateless, CIDR-based.

q:
A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use Lustre clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
o.B: Create an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol. Connect the application server to the file share.
o.C: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system, and configure it to support Lustre. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
o.D: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.

e.why: Amazon FSx for Lustre is a fully managed, high-performance file system that natively supports the Lustre client. It is the only option that gives Lustre access as a managed service.

others.A: DataSync is a data transfer service and does not provide a mountable file system.
others.B: Storage Gateway file gateways expose NFS or SMB, not Lustre.
others.C: Amazon EFS supports NFS only and cannot be configured to support Lustre.

e.tip: Lustre/HPC = FSx for Lustre; Windows SMB = FSx for Windows; Linux NFS = EFS.

q:
A company runs an application that receives data from thousands of geographically dispersed remote devices that use UDP. The application processes the data immediately and sends a message back to the device if necessary. No data is stored.

The company needs a solution that minimizes latency for the data transmission from the devices. The solution also must provide rapid failover to another AWS Region.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each of the two Regions. Configure the NLB to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the data.
o.B: Use AWS Global Accelerator. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each of the two Regions as an endpoint. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster. Set the ECS service as the target for the NLB. Process the data in Amazon ECS.
o.C: Use AWS Global Accelerator. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in each of the two Regions as an endpoint. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster. Set the ECS service as the target for the ALB. Process the data in Amazon ECS.
o.D: Configure an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in each of the two Regions. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster. Set the ECS service as the target for the ALB. Process the data in Amazon ECS.

fixed: Option B text was missing (only its last sentence remained) and has been reconstructed; options C and D were truncated and have been completed.

e.why: The devices use UDP, and Global Accelerator supports UDP, routes users over the AWS backbone from the nearest edge location, and fails over between Regional endpoints in seconds. A Network Load Balancer handles UDP traffic, and ECS on Fargate processes the data without servers to manage.

others.A: Route 53 failover depends on DNS TTLs and health checks, so failover is slower, and an NLB cannot invoke a Lambda function directly.
others.C: An Application Load Balancer only handles HTTP and HTTPS, so it cannot receive UDP traffic.
others.D: An ALB cannot carry UDP, and Route 53 DNS failover is slower than Global Accelerator.

e.tip: UDP plus low latency plus fast Regional failover points to Global Accelerator with NLB endpoints.

q:
A solutions architect must migrate a Windows Internet Information Services (IIS) web application to AWS. The application currently relies on a file share hosted in the user's on-premises network-attached storage (NAS). The solutions architect has proposed migrating the IIS web servers to Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones that are connected to the storage solution, and configuring an Elastic Load Balancer attached to the instances.

Which replacement to the on-premises file share is MOST resilient and durable?

o.A: Migrate the file share to Amazon RDS.
o.B: Migrate the file share to AWS Storage Gateway.
o.C: Migrate the file share to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
o.D: Migrate the file share to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS).

e.why: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a managed, native SMB file system that IIS on Windows can use directly. A Multi-AZ deployment replicates data across AZs with automatic failover, making it the most resilient and durable replacement for the NAS file share.

others.A: Amazon RDS is a relational database, not a file share.
others.B: Storage Gateway is for hybrid access from on premises and adds a gateway appliance that can become a point of failure for EC2 workloads in AWS.
others.D: Amazon EFS uses NFS and is not supported on Windows instances.

e.tip: Windows file share in AWS = FSx for Windows File Server (pick Multi-AZ for resilience).

q:
A company is deploying a new application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application writes data to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. The company needs to ensure that all data that is written to the EBS volumes is encrypted at rest.

Which solution will meet this requirement?

o.A: Create an IAM role that specifies EBS encryption. Attach the role to the EC2 instances.
o.B: Create the EBS volumes as encrypted volumes. Attach the EBS volumes to the EC2 instances.
o.C: Create an EC2 instance tag that has a key of Encrypt and a value of True. Tag all instances that require encryption at the EBS level.
o.D: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key policy that enforces EBS encryption in the account. Ensure that the key policy is active.

e.why: Creating the EBS volumes as encrypted (with KMS) encrypts data at rest, plus snapshots and data moving between the instance and the volume. Turning on EBS encryption by default for the account and Region also enforces this for new volumes.

others.A: IAM roles grant permissions; they cannot make volumes encrypted.
others.C: Tags are just metadata and do not cause any encryption.
others.D: KMS key policies control who can use a key; they cannot force EBS volumes to be encrypted.

e.tip: An unencrypted volume cannot be encrypted in place: snapshot it, copy the snapshot with encryption, then create a new volume.

q:
A company has a web application with sporadic usage patterns. There is heavy usage at the beginning of each month, moderate usage at the start of each week, and unpredictable usage during the week. The application consists of a web server and a MySQL database server running inside the data center. The company would like to move the application to the AWS Cloud, and needs to select a cost-effective database platform that will not require database modifications.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Amazon DynamoDB
o.B: Amazon RDS for MySQL
o.C: MySQL-compatible Amazon Aurora Serverless
o.D: MySQL deployed on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group

e.why: Aurora Serverless is MySQL-compatible, so no database changes are needed. It scales capacity up and down automatically for spiky, unpredictable usage, and you pay only for the capacity you use, which is cost-effective for this pattern.

others.A: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and would require rewriting the application's data layer.
others.B: A provisioned RDS for MySQL instance must be sized for peak load, so it wastes money during quiet periods.
others.D: MySQL on EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group cannot simply scale out a relational database and means heavy self-management.

e.tip: Unpredictable or intermittent relational load = Aurora Serverless v2.

q:
An image-hosting company stores its objects in Amazon S3 buckets. The company wants to avoid accidental exposure of the objects in the S3 buckets to the public. All S3 objects in the entire AWS account need to remain private.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon GuardDuty to monitor S3 bucket policies. Create an automatic remediation action rule that uses an AWS Lambda function to remediate any change that makes the objects public.
o.B: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to find publicly accessible S3 buckets. Configure email notifications in Trusted Advisor when a change is detected. Manually change the S3 bucket policy if it allows public access.
o.C: Use AWS Resource Access Manager to find publicly accessible S3 buckets. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a change is detected. Deploy a Lambda function that programmatically remediates the change.
o.D: Use the S3 Block Public Access feature on the account level. Use AWS Organizations to create a service control policy (SCP) that prevents IAM users from changing the setting. Apply the SCP to the account.

e.why: Account-level S3 Block Public Access overrides any bucket policy or ACL that would make objects public, across every bucket in the account. An SCP that denies s3:PutAccountPublicAccessBlock stops anyone from turning the setting off, which prevents accidental exposure instead of fixing it afterward.

others.A: GuardDuty detects threats and does not monitor or remediate bucket policies the way described, and remediation after the fact still allows exposure.
others.B: Trusted Advisor checks and manual fixes are reactive and leave a window of exposure.
others.C: AWS Resource Access Manager shares resources across accounts and does not detect public S3 buckets.

e.tip: Prevent public S3 = Block Public Access (account level) + SCP to lock it.

q:
An ecommerce company is experiencing an increase in user traffic. The company’s store is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances as a two-tier web application consisting of a web tier and a separate database tier. As traffic increases, the company notices that the architecture is causing significant delays in sending timely marketing and order confirmation email to users. The company wants to reduce the time it spends resolving complex email delivery issues and minimize operational overhead.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a separate application tier using EC2 instances dedicated to email processing.
o.B: Configure the web instance to send email through Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
o.C: Configure the web instance to send email through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
o.D: Create a separate application tier using EC2 instances dedicated to email processing. Place the instances in an Auto Scaling group.

e.why: Amazon SES is a managed email-sending service that handles deliverability, bounces, complaints, reputation and scaling. Sending through SES via its API or SMTP removes the effort of running email infrastructure and fixing delivery problems.

others.A: A dedicated email tier on EC2 still leaves the team running mail servers and debugging delivery issues.
others.C: SNS email notifications are for simple topic alerts to subscribers and do not support custom transactional or marketing email.
others.D: Adding Auto Scaling to self-managed email servers still keeps all the operational burden.

e.tip: Transactional or marketing email = SES.

q:
A company has a business system that generates hundreds of reports each day. The business system saves the reports to a network share in CSV format. The company needs to store this data in the AWS Cloud in near-real time for analysis.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

o.A: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the files to Amazon S3. Create a scheduled task that runs at the end of each day.
o.B: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Update the business system to use a new network share from the S3 File Gateway.
o.C: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the files to Amazon S3. Create an application that uses the DataSync API in the automation workflow.
o.D: Deploy an AWS Transfer for SFTP endpoint. Create a script that checks for new files on the network share and uploads the new files by using SFTP.

e.why: An Amazon S3 File Gateway presents an SMB or NFS share on premises and uploads each file it writes to S3 as an object, in near-real time. Pointing the business system at the new share needs no scheduling or custom code.

others.A: A daily DataSync task is batch, not near-real time.
others.C: Writing an application around the DataSync API adds development and maintenance effort.
others.D: A custom script that watches the share and uploads over SFTP is extra code to build and maintain.

e.tip: On-prem app writes to a file share, data should land in S3 = S3 File Gateway.

q:
A company is storing petabytes of data in Amazon S3 Standard. The data is stored in multiple S3 buckets and is accessed with varying frequency. The company does not know access patterns for all the data. The company needs to implement a solution for each S3 bucket to optimize the cost of S3 usage.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
o.B: Use the S3 storage class analysis tool to determine the correct tier for each object in the S3 bucket. Move each object to the identified storage tier.
o.C: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
o.D: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA).

e.why: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves each object between frequent, infrequent and archive instant access tiers based on its actual access, with no retrieval fees. A lifecycle rule that sends objects to Intelligent-Tiering is a hands-off way to optimize cost when access patterns are unknown.

others.B: Running storage class analysis and moving each object by hand across petabytes takes a lot of ongoing effort.
others.C: Glacier Instant Retrieval has higher retrieval costs, so frequently accessed objects would cost more.
others.D: One Zone-IA lowers durability across AZs and charges retrieval fees, which is bad for frequently accessed data.

e.tip: Unknown or changing access patterns = S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

q:
A rapidly growing global ecommerce company is hosting its web application on AWS. The web application includes static content and dynamic content. The website stores online transaction processing (OLTP) data in an Amazon RDS database The website’s users are experiencing slow page loads.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to resolve this issue? (Choose two.)

o.A: Configure an Amazon Redshift cluster.
o.B: Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution.
o.C: Host the dynamic web content in Amazon S3.
o.D: Create a read replica for the RDS DB instance.
o.E: Configure a Multi-AZ deployment for the RDS DB instance.

e.why: CloudFront caches static and dynamic content at edge locations close to global users, which cuts page load times. An RDS read replica takes read queries off the primary database, easing database contention behind slow dynamic pages.

others.A: Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics and does not speed up OLTP page loads.
others.C: S3 can host only static content; it cannot run dynamic web content.
others.E: Multi-AZ improves availability and does not serve reads or improve performance.

q:
A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Lambda functions to run its application. The company has VPCs with public subnets and private subnets in its AWS account. The EC2 instances run in a private subnet in one of the VPCs. The Lambda functions need direct network access to the EC2 instances for the application to work.

The application will run for at least 1 year. The company expects the number of Lambda functions that the application uses to increase during that time. The company wants to maximize its savings on all application resources and to keep network latency between the services low.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan. Optimize the Lambda functions’ duration and memory usage and the number of invocations. Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnet that contains the EC2 instances.
o.B: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan. Optimize the Lambda functions' duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred. Connect the Lambda functions to a public subnet in the same VPC where the EC2 instances run.
o.C: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Optimize the Lambda functions’ duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred. Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnet that contains the EC2 instances.
o.D: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Optimize the Lambda functions’ duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred. Keep the Lambda functions in the Lambda service VPC.

fixed: Option C showed the answer key instead of its text and has been reconstructed; option D was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: A Compute Savings Plan covers EC2, Fargate and Lambda usage, so it keeps saving money as the number of Lambda functions grows, while an EC2 Instance Savings Plan covers only EC2. Connecting the Lambda functions to the private subnet that holds the EC2 instances gives them direct, low-latency network access.

others.A: An EC2 Instance Savings Plan does not apply to Lambda, so savings on the growing Lambda usage are lost.
others.B: An EC2 Instance Savings Plan does not cover Lambda, and a public subnet is not needed and does not give Lambda functions internet access or better latency.
others.D: Lambda functions in the Lambda service VPC cannot reach the EC2 instances in the private subnet directly.

e.tip: Savings that must cover Lambda or Fargate mean a Compute Savings Plan.

q:
A solutions architect needs to allow team members to access Amazon S3 buckets in two different AWS accounts: a development account and a production account. The team currently has access to S3 buckets in the development account by using unique IAM users that are assigned to an IAM group that has appropriate permissions in the account.

The solutions architect has created an IAM role in the production account. The role has a policy that grants access to an S3 bucket in the production account.

Which solution will meet these requirements while complying with the principle of least privilege?

o.A: Attach the Administrator Access policy to the development account users.
o.B: Add the development account as a principal in the trust policy of the role in the production account.
o.C: Turn off the S3 Block Public Access feature on the S3 bucket in the production account.
o.D: Create a user in the production account with unique credentials for each team member.

e.why: Cross-account access should use role assumption. Adding the development account as a trusted principal in the production role's trust policy lets the existing development users (with sts:AssumeRole permission) assume the role and get only its S3 permissions.

others.A: AdministratorAccess grants far more than S3 access and still does not give access to the production account.
others.C: Turning off Block Public Access would expose the bucket publicly, which is insecure and unnecessary.
others.D: Duplicate users in production mean more credentials to manage instead of reusing roles.

e.tip: Cross-account access = IAM role with a trust policy + sts:AssumeRole.

q:
A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and runs multiple Amazon EC2 workloads in the ap-southeast-2 Region. The company has a service control policy (SCP) that prevents any resources from being created in any other Region. A security policy requires the company to encrypt all data at rest.

An audit discovers that employees have created Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes for EC2 instances without encrypting the volumes. The company wants any new EC2 instances that any IAM user or root user launches in ap-southeast-2 to use encrypted EBS volumes. The company wants a solution that will have minimal effect on employees who create EBS volumes.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: In the Amazon EC2 console, select the EBS encryption account attribute and define a default encryption key.
o.B: Create an IAM permission boundary. Attach the permission boundary to the root organizational unit (OU). Define the boundary to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
o.C: Create an SCP. Attach the SCP to the root organizational unit (OU). Define the SCP to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action whenthe ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
o.D: Update the IAM policies for each account to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
o.E: In the Organizations management account, specify the Default EBS volume encryption setting.

e.why: An SCP on the root OU that denies ec2:CreateVolume when ec2:Encrypted is false blocks unencrypted volumes in member accounts, including for their root users. Pairing it with default EBS encryption means volumes are encrypted automatically, so employees are not disrupted.

others.A: The EBS encryption-by-default account attribute works, but it must be set in each account and Region; the key prefers the organization-wide pairing.
others.B: Permission boundaries attach to IAM users and roles, not to OUs, and they do not affect the root user.
others.D: Editing IAM policies in every account is error-prone and does not restrict the root user.

e.tip: SCPs restrict even the root user of member accounts, but never the management account.
e.flag: EBS encryption by default is a per-account, per-Region EC2 setting; there is no Organizations-wide default EBS encryption setting, so A + C is more accurate than C + E.

q:
A company wants to use an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB cluster to simplify time-consuming database administrative tasks for production database workloads. The company wants to ensure that its database is highly available and will provide automatic failover support in most scenarios in less than 40 seconds. The company wants to offload reads off of the primary instance and keep costs as low as possible.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Create one read replica and point the read workload to the read replica.
o.B: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB duster deployment Create two read replicas and point the read workload to the read replicas.
o.C: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Point the read workload to the secondary instances in the Multi-AZ pair.
o.D: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment Point the read workload to the reader endpoint.

e.why: An RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment has a writer and two readable standby instances in different AZs, with automatic failover typically under 35 seconds. The reader endpoint spreads read traffic across the standbys, offloading the primary without paying for extra read replicas.

others.A: Multi-AZ DB instance failover usually takes 60 to 120 seconds, and the extra read replica adds cost.
others.B: Multi-AZ DB clusters already have readable standbys, so two more read replicas add unnecessary cost.
others.C: In a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment the standby cannot serve read traffic.

e.tip: Multi-AZ DB instance: 1 standby that cannot serve reads. Multi-AZ DB cluster: 2 readable standbys, faster failover.

q:
A company runs a highly available SFTP service. The SFTP service uses two Amazon EC2 Linux instances that run with elastic IP addresses to accept traffic from trusted IP sources on the internet. The SFTP service is backed by shared storage that is attached to the instances. User accounts are created and managed as Linux users in the SFTP servers.

The company wants a serverless option that provides high IOPS performance and highly configurable security. The company also wants to maintain control over user permissions.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with a public endpoint that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the EBS volume to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.
o.B: Create an encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with elastic IP addresses and a VPC endpoint that has internet-facing access. Attach a security group to the endpoint that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the EFS volume to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket with default encryption enabled. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with a public endpoint that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the S3 bucket to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.
o.D: Create an Amazon S3 bucket with default encryption enabled. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with a VPC endpoint that has internal access in a private subnet. Attach a security group that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the S3 bucket to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.

e.why: AWS Transfer Family is a serverless SFTP service. Backing it with Amazon EFS gives shared POSIX storage with high IOPS and keeps control of user permissions through POSIX UID/GID. A VPC-hosted, internet-facing endpoint with Elastic IPs lets you attach a security group that allows only trusted source IPs, which gives highly configurable security.

others.A: Transfer Family supports only S3 or EFS as storage; you cannot attach an EBS volume, and public endpoints cannot use security groups.
others.C: A public Transfer Family endpoint cannot restrict source IPs with security groups, and S3 does not offer the file-level POSIX permissions and IOPS profile the question asks for.
others.D: An internal-only VPC endpoint in a private subnet cannot be reached by trusted clients on the internet.

e.tip: Transfer Family source-IP filtering = VPC endpoint (internet-facing with EIPs) + security group.

q:
A company is developing a new machine learning (ML) model solution on AWS. The models are developed as independent microservices that fetch approximately 1 GB of model data from Amazon S3 at startup and load the data into memory. Users access the models through an asynchronous API. Users can send a request or a batch of requests and specify where the results should be sent.

The company provides models to hundreds of users. The usage patterns for the models are irregular. Some models could be unused for days or weeks. Other models could receive batches of thousands of requests at a time.

Which design should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Direct the requests from the API to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Deploy the models as AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by the NLB.
o.B: Direct the requests from the API to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy the models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use AWS App Mesh to scale the instances of the ECS cluster based on the SQS queue size.
o.C: Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the models as AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by SQS events. Use AWS Auto Scaling to increase the number of vCPUs for the Lambda functions based on the SQS queue size.
o.D: Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from the queue. Enable AWS Auto Scaling on Amazon ECS for both the cluster and copies of the service based on the queue size.

fixed: Option A was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: An SQS queue absorbs irregular, bursty batches of requests and decouples the API from processing. ECS services that read from the queue can scale both the cluster and the number of service tasks based on queue depth, including down to very little capacity when models are idle.

others.A: Models used for batch inference often exceed Lambda limits, and an NLB cannot invoke Lambda functions.
others.B: App Mesh is a service mesh for traffic routing; it does not scale ECS tasks based on queue size.
others.C: Lambda functions do not have configurable vCPUs that AWS Auto Scaling can increase; CPU is tied to memory settings.

e.tip: Irregular, bursty asynchronous work fits a queue with consumers that auto scale on queue depth.

o.A: Role
o.B: Group
o.C: Organization
o.D: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) resource
o.E: Amazon EC2 resource

fixed: The policy JSON was missing from the question. A representative identity-based policy has been added; the answer does not depend on its exact actions.

e.why: Identity-based policies are attached to IAM identities: users, groups and roles. Of the choices, only Role and Group are IAM identities that can have this policy attached.

others.C: An AWS Organizations organization is controlled with service control policies, not identity-based IAM policies.
others.D: An ECS resource is not an IAM principal; ECS tasks receive permissions through an IAM role.
others.E: An EC2 resource is not an IAM principal; instances receive permissions through an instance profile role.

e.tip: Identity-based policies attach to users, groups and roles; resource-based policies attach to resources.

q:
A company is running a custom application on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. The application has frontend nodes that need to run 24 hours a day, 7 days a week and backend nodes that need to run only for a short time based on workload. The number of backend nodes varies during the day.

The company needs to scale out and scale in more instances based on workload.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use Reserved Instances for the frontend nodes. Use AWS Fargate for the backend nodes.
o.B: Use Reserved Instances for the frontend nodes. Use Spot Instances for the backend nodes.
o.C: Use Spot Instances for the frontend nodes. Use Reserved Instances for the backend nodes.
o.D: Use Spot Instances for the frontend nodes. Use AWS Fargate for the backend nodes.

e.why: Frontend nodes run 24/7, so Reserved Instances (or Savings Plans) give the biggest discount for steady usage. Backend nodes run briefly and vary with workload, which fits Spot Instances at up to 90 percent off, assuming the work can tolerate interruption.

others.A: Fargate would mean containerizing the backend, and it usually costs more per compute unit than Spot EC2 for the same work.
others.C: Spot Instances can be interrupted, which is unsuitable for always-on frontend nodes, and RIs waste money on part-time backend nodes.
others.D: Spot is unsuitable for the always-on frontend, and Fargate is not the cheapest option for the backend.

e.tip: Steady 24/7 = RI or Savings Plan; short and flexible = Spot.

q:
A company uses high block storage capacity to runs its workloads on premises. The company's daily peak input and output transactions per second are not more than 15,000 IOPS. The company wants to migrate the workloads to Amazon EC2 and to provision disk performance independent of storage capacity.

Which Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume type will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: GP2 volume type
o.B: io2 volume type
o.C: GP3 volume type
o.D: io1 volume type

e.why: gp3 volumes let you provision IOPS (up to 16,000) and throughput separately from capacity, with a 3,000 IOPS baseline at any size. They cost about 20 percent less per GB than gp2, so they are the most cost-effective choice for a 15,000 IOPS peak.

others.A: gp2 IOPS are tied to volume size (3 IOPS per GB), so performance cannot be provisioned independently of capacity.
others.B: io2 meets the need but costs much more than gp3 for only 15,000 IOPS.
others.D: io1 is also more expensive than gp3 and offers no benefit at this IOPS level.

e.tip: 16,000 IOPS or less and independent of size = gp3; above that or sub-millisecond critical = io2 Block Express.

q:
A company needs to store data from its healthcare application. The application’s data frequently changes. A new regulation requires audit access at all levels of the stored data.

The company hosts the application on an on-premises infrastructure that is running out of storage capacity. A solutions architect must securely migrate the existing data to AWS while satisfying the new regulation.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS DataSync to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log data events.
o.B: Use AWS Snowcone to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log management events.
o.C: Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log data events.
o.D: Use AWS Storage Gateway to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log management events.

e.why: AWS DataSync transfers the existing data to S3 online, securely (TLS) and quickly, with integrity checks. It can also handle the changing data with incremental syncs. CloudTrail data events record object-level S3 API activity (GetObject, PutObject), which gives the audit access at all levels that the regulation requires.

others.B: Snowcone holds only 8 to 14 TB and is offline, and CloudTrail management events do not capture object-level access.
