others.C: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads but is not a migration tool with scheduling and verification for a large dataset.
others.D: CloudTrail management events do not log object-level reads and writes, so they fail the audit requirement.

e.tip: Object-level S3 auditing = CloudTrail data events (management events cover control-plane calls only).

q:
A solutions architect is implementing a complex Java application with a MySQL database. The Java application must be deployed on Apache Tomcat and must be highly available.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy the application in AWS Lambda. Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to connect with the Lambda functions.
o.B: Deploy the application by using AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Configure a load-balanced environment and a rolling deployment policy.
o.C: Migrate the database to Amazon ElastiCache. Configure the ElastiCache security group to allow access from the application.
o.D: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Install a MySQL server on the EC2 instance. Configure the application on the server. Create an AMI. Use the AMI to create a launch template with an Auto Scaling group.

e.why: Elastic Beanstalk has a managed Tomcat platform for Java apps. A load-balanced environment runs instances behind an ELB in an Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs for high availability, and rolling deployments update without full downtime.

others.A: Lambda cannot host a complex Tomcat-based application without major refactoring.
others.C: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, not a replacement for a MySQL relational database.
others.D: Putting MySQL on the same instance as the app means each scaled copy has its own separate database, which breaks data consistency and leaves no HA database.

e.tip: Deploy a web app on a familiar stack (Tomcat, .NET, Node) with little ops work = Elastic Beanstalk.

q:
A serverless application uses Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. The Lambda function needs permissions to read and write to the DynamoDB table.

Which solution will give the Lambda function access to the DynamoDB table MOST securely?

o.A: Create an IAM user with programmatic access to the Lambda function. Attach a policy to the user that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Store the access_key_id and secret_access_key parameters as part of the Lambda environment variables. Ensure that other AWS users do not have read and write access to the Lambda function configuration.
o.B: Create an IAM role that includes Lambda as a trusted service. Attach a policy to the role that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Update the configuration of the Lambda function to use the new role as the execution role.
o.C: Create an IAM user with programmatic access to the Lambda function. Attach a policy to the user that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Store the access_key_id and secret_access_key parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as secure string parameters. Update the Lambda function code to retrieve the secure string parameters before connecting to the DynamoDB table.
o.D: Create an IAM role that includes DynamoDB as a trusted service. Attach a policy to the role that allows read and write access from the Lambda function. Update the code of the Lambda function to attach to the new role as an execution role.

e.why: The secure pattern is an IAM role that trusts the Lambda service (lambda.amazonaws.com), carries a least-privilege DynamoDB policy, and is set as the function's execution role. Lambda then gets temporary credentials that rotate automatically, with no stored keys.

others.A: Long-term access keys in environment variables can leak and must be rotated by hand.
others.C: Parameter Store protects the keys better, but this still relies on long-term IAM user credentials instead of a role.
others.D: The trust policy must trust the Lambda service, not DynamoDB, and roles are set in the function configuration, not attached from code.

o.A: Group members are permitted any Amazon EC2 action within the us-east-1 Region. Statements after the Allow permission are not applied.
o.B: Group members are denied any Amazon EC2 permissions in the us-east-1 Region unless they are logged in with multi-factor authentication (MFA).
o.C: Group members are allowed the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances permissions for all Regions when logged in with multi-factor authentication (MFA). Group members are permitted any other Amazon EC2 action.
o.D: Group members are allowed the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances permissions for the us-east-1 Region only when logged in with multi-factor authentication (MFA). Group members are permitted any other Amazon EC2 action within the us-east-1 Region.

fixed: The IAM policy JSON was missing from the question and has been reconstructed.

e.why: The Allow statement grants all EC2 actions, but only in us-east-1. The Deny statement blocks ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances whenever MFA is not present, so members can stop and terminate instances in us-east-1 only after signing in with MFA, and can perform any other EC2 action in us-east-1.

others.A: An explicit Deny is always evaluated and overrides the Allow, so the statement order does not cancel the Deny.
others.B: Only the stop and terminate actions are denied without MFA; other EC2 actions are allowed without MFA.
others.C: The Allow is limited to us-east-1 by the ec2:Region condition, so permissions do not apply to all Regions.

e.tip: An explicit Deny always wins, regardless of statement order; read each condition carefully.

q:
A manufacturing company has machine sensors that upload .csv files to an Amazon S3 bucket. These .csv files must be converted into images and must be made available as soon as possible for the automatic generation of graphical reports.

The images become irrelevant after 1 month, but the .csv files must be kept to train machine learning (ML) models twice a year. The ML trainings and audits are planned weeks in advance.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

o.A: Launch an Amazon EC2 Spot Instance that downloads the .csv files every hour, generates the image files, and uploads the images to the S3 bucket.
o.B: Design an AWS Lambda function that converts the .csv files into images and stores the images in the S3 bucket. Invoke the Lambda function when a .csv file is uploaded.
o.C: Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier 1 day after they are uploaded. Expire the image files after 30 days.
o.D: Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 1 day after they are uploaded. Expire the image files after 30 days.
o.E: Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 1 day after they are uploaded. Keep the image files in Reduced Redundancy Storage (RRS).

e.why: An S3 event-triggered Lambda function converts each .csv to an image as soon as it arrives, with no idle compute. Lifecycle rules move the .csv files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 day, which is cheap and acceptable because trainings are planned weeks ahead, and expire images after 30 days.

others.A: An hourly Spot Instance batch adds delay instead of making images available as soon as possible, and Spot can be interrupted.
others.D: One Zone-IA costs more than Glacier for data read only twice a year and has lower resilience.
others.E: Standard-IA costs more than Glacier for rarely read data, and Reduced Redundancy Storage is deprecated and does not expire images.

e.tip: Retrieval planned weeks ahead = Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive.

q:
A company has developed a new video game as a web application. The application is in a three-tier architecture in a VPC with Amazon RDS for MySQL in the database layer. Several players will compete concurrently online. The game’s developers want to display a top-10 scoreboard in near-real time and offer the ability to stop and restore the game while preserving the current scores.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Set up an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to cache the scores for the web application to display.
o.B: Set up an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to compute and cache the scores for the web application to display.
o.C: Place an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the web application to cache the scoreboard in a section of the application.
o.D: Create a read replica on Amazon RDS for MySQL to run queries to compute the scoreboard and serve the read traffic to the web application.

e.why: ElastiCache for Redis sorted sets (ZADD, ZREVRANGE) compute a live top-10 leaderboard in memory with very low latency. Redis also supports persistence (snapshots/AOF) and backup and restore, so scores survive stopping and restoring the game.

others.A: Memcached has no sorted sets, persistence or backup and restore, so it cannot reliably keep scores.
others.C: CloudFront caching would serve stale scoreboards and does not compute rankings.
others.D: Running ranking queries over and over on a MySQL read replica is slower and adds replication lag compared with an in-memory sorted set.

e.tip: Leaderboard = Redis sorted sets.

q:
An ecommerce company wants to use machine learning (ML) algorithms to build and train models. The company will use the models to visualize complex scenarios and to detect trends in customer data. The architecture team wants to integrate its ML models with a reporting platform to analyze the augmented data and use the data directly in its business intelligence dashboards.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Glue to create an ML transform to build and train models. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to visualize the data.
o.B: Use Amazon SageMaker to build and train models. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
o.C: Use a pre-built ML Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the AWS Marketplace to build and train models. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to visualize the data.
o.D: Use Amazon QuickSight to build and train models by using calculated fields. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.

e.why: Amazon SageMaker is the managed service for building, training and deploying ML models. Amazon QuickSight is the managed BI service that can visualize the augmented data, and it integrates with SageMaker models for ML-powered insights, with the least operational overhead.

others.A: AWS Glue ML transforms only find matching or duplicate records, and OpenSearch dashboards are not a BI reporting platform.
others.C: Running your own ML AMIs on EC2 means managing infrastructure, which adds overhead.
others.D: QuickSight calculated fields cannot build and train custom ML models.

q:
A company is running its production and nonproduction environment workloads in multiple AWS accounts. The accounts are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to design a solution that will prevent the modification of cost usage tags.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a custom AWS Config rule to prevent tag modification except by authorized principals.
o.B: Create a custom trail in AWS CloudTrail to prevent tag modification.
o.C: Create a service control policy (SCP) to prevent tag modification except by authorized principals.
o.D: Create custom Amazon CloudWatch logs to prevent tag modification.

e.why: Service control policies set preventive guardrails across accounts in AWS Organizations. An SCP that denies tag-changing actions for the cost allocation tag keys, with a condition exempting authorized principals, stops changes before they happen in every member account.

others.A: AWS Config rules detect and report noncompliance after the fact; they do not prevent changes.
others.B: CloudTrail only logs API activity; it cannot block changes.
others.D: CloudWatch Logs stores logs and cannot prevent tag changes.

e.tip: Prevent across accounts = SCP (or tag policies for enforcing tag values); detect = Config.

q:
A company hosts its application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancer in an Auto Scaling group and with an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants to ensure the application can be made available in anotherAWS Region with minimal downtime.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of downtime?

o.A: Create an Auto Scaling group and a load balancer in the disaster recovery Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.
o.B: Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances, load balancers, and DynamoDB tables to be launched when needed Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.
o.C: Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances and a load balancer to be launched when needed. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.
o.D: Create an Auto Scaling group and load balancer in the disaster recovery Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to trigger an AWS Lambda function that updates Amazon Route 53 pointing to the disaster recovery load balancer.

e.why: A warm standby, with an Auto Scaling group and load balancer already running in the DR Region, plus a DynamoDB global table that is already replicating data, keeps both tiers ready. Route 53 DNS failover health checks switch traffic automatically, giving the least downtime.

others.B: Building EC2, load balancers and an empty DynamoDB table from CloudFormation at failover time takes time and has no replicated data.
others.C: Launching compute from a template during an outage still adds provisioning time compared with infrastructure that is already running.
others.D: A custom CloudWatch alarm plus Lambda to update Route 53 reinvents built-in Route 53 failover routing and adds delay and moving parts.

e.tip: Least downtime across Regions = pre-provisioned resources + global tables + Route 53 failover.

q:
A company needs to migrate a MySQL database from its on-premises data center to AWS within 2 weeks. The database is 20 TB in size. The company wants to complete the migration with minimal downtime.

Which solution will migrate the database MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with replication of ongoing changes. Send the Snowball Edge device to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication.
o.B: Order an AWS Snowmobile vehicle. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with ongoing changes. Send the Snowmobile vehicle back to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication.
o.C: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized with GPU device. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with ongoing changes. Send the Snowball device to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication
o.D: Order a 1 GB dedicated AWS Direct Connect connection to establish a connection with the data center. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with replication of ongoing changes.

e.why: A Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device (about 80 TB) moves the 20 TB full load offline cheaply within 2 weeks, using DMS with the device as the target. DMS change data capture then replicates ongoing changes after the data is loaded into AWS, keeping downtime minimal.

others.B: Snowmobile was for exabyte-scale transfers (and is retired), which is far too much for 20 TB.
others.C: Compute Optimized with GPU devices cost more and target edge computing, not bulk storage transfer.
others.D: Direct Connect usually takes longer than 2 weeks to provision and costs more for a one-time migration.

e.tip: Large DB migration with little downtime and limited bandwidth = Snowball Edge + DMS with CDC.

q:
A company moved its on-premises PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The company successfully launched a new product. The workload on the database has increased. The company wants to accommodate the larger workload without adding infrastructure.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Buy reserved DB instances for the total workload. Make the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance larger.
o.B: Make the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance a Multi-AZ DB instance.
o.C: Buy reserved DB instances for the total workload. Add another Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance.
o.D: Make the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance an on-demand DB instance.

e.why: Scaling the existing RDS instance up to a larger class handles more load without adding infrastructure. Buying Reserved DB instances for the steady load gives up to about 69 percent savings over On-Demand, which makes it the most cost-effective option.

others.B: Multi-AZ adds a standby for availability that cannot serve traffic, so it adds cost without adding capacity.
others.C: Adding another DB instance means adding infrastructure, which the company wants to avoid.
others.D: On-Demand pricing is the most expensive option for a steady, ongoing workload and adds no capacity.

q:
A company operates an ecommerce website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in an Auto Scaling group. The site is experiencing performance issues related to a high request rate from illegitimate external systems with changing IP addresses. The security team is worried about potential DDoS attacks against the website. The company must block the illegitimate incoming requests in a way that has a minimal impact on legitimate users.

What should a solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Deploy Amazon Inspector and associate it with the ALB.
o.B: Deploy AWS WAF, associate it with the ALB, and configure a rate-limiting rule.
o.C: Deploy rules to the network ACLs associated with the ALB to block the incomingtraffic.
o.D: Deploy Amazon GuardDuty and enable rate-limiting protection when configuring GuardDuty.

fixed: Option A was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: AWS WAF attaches to an Application Load Balancer and supports rate-based rules that automatically block clients that send too many requests, even when the IP addresses keep changing. Legitimate users who stay under the limit are not affected.

others.A: Amazon Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities and cannot block incoming requests.
others.C: Network ACLs apply to subnets, need fixed IP ranges and cannot keep up with attackers that keep changing addresses.
others.D: GuardDuty detects threats but does not block traffic or offer rate limiting.

e.tip: Blocking floods of HTTP requests from changing IPs means AWS WAF rate-based rules.

q:
A company wants to share accounting data with an external auditor. The data is stored in an Amazon RDS DB instance that resides in a private subnet. The auditor has its own AWS account and requires its own copy of the database.

What is the MOST secure way for the company to share the database with the auditor?

o.A: Create a read replica of the database. Configure IAM standard database authentication to grant the auditor access.
o.B: Export the database contents to text files. Store the files in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create a new IAM user for the auditor. Grant the user access to the S3 bucket.
o.C: Copy a snapshot of the database to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an IAM user. Share the user's keys with the auditor to grant access to the object in the S3 bucket.
o.D: Create an encrypted snapshot of the database. Share the snapshot with the auditor. Allow access to the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key.

e.why: Sharing an encrypted RDS snapshot with the auditor's AWS account, and granting that account access to the customer managed KMS key, lets the auditor restore its own copy. Data stays encrypted, no credentials are shared, and the database is never exposed.

others.A: A read replica stays in the company's account and network, and the auditor needs its own copy, not access to company infrastructure.
others.B: Exporting to text files and creating IAM users loses the database format and adds credential management.
others.C: RDS snapshots cannot simply be copied as files to S3 this way, and sharing IAM user keys is insecure.

e.tip: Encrypted snapshots can be shared only when encrypted with a customer managed KMS key whose policy grants the other account access.

q:
A solutions architect configured a VPC that has a small range of IP addresses. The number of Amazon EC2 instances that are in the VPC is increasing, and there is an insufficient number of IP addresses for future workloads.

Which solution resolves this issue with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Add an additional IPv4 CIDR block to increase the number of IP addresses and create additional subnets in the VPC. Create new resources in the new subnets by using the new CIDR.
o.B: Create a second VPC with additional subnets. Use a peering connection to connect the second VPC with the first VPC. Update the routes and create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.
o.C: Use AWS Transit Gateway to add a transit gateway and connect a second VPC with the first VPC. Update the routes of the transit gateway and VPCs. Create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.
o.D: Create a second VPC. Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection between the first VPC and the second VPC by using a VPN-hosted solution on Amazon EC2 and a virtual private gateway. Update the route between VPCs to the traffic through the VPN. Create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.

fixed: Option C showed the answer key instead of its text and has been reconstructed; options A, B and D were truncated and have been completed.

e.why: A VPC can have secondary IPv4 CIDR blocks added at any time. Adding one and creating new subnets from it gives more IP addresses in the same VPC, with no peering, transit gateway or VPN to build and run.

others.B: A second VPC with peering adds routing and connection management, which is more overhead than extending the existing VPC.
others.C: A transit gateway and a second VPC add cost and routing work that the simple IP shortage does not need.
others.D: A self-managed VPN on EC2 between two VPCs is the most operational overhead of all the options.

e.tip: Running out of IPs in a VPC: add a secondary CIDR block.

q:
A company used an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance during application testing. Before terminating the DB instance at the end of the test cycle, a solutions architect created two backups. The solutions architect created the first backup by using the mysqldump utility to create a database dump. The solutions architect created the second backup by enabling the final DB snapshot option on RDS termination.

The company is now planning for a new test cycle and wants to create a new DB instance from the most recent backup. The company has chosen a MySQL-compatible edition ofAmazon Aurora to host the DB instance.

Which solutions will create the new DB instance? (Choose two.)

o.A: Import the RDS snapshot directly into Aurora.
o.B: Upload the RDS snapshot to Amazon S3. Then import the RDS snapshot into Aurora.
o.C: Upload the database dump to Amazon S3. Then import the database dump into Aurora.
o.D: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to import the RDS snapshot into Aurora.
o.E: Upload the database dump to Amazon S3. Then use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to import the database dump into Aurora.

e.why: An RDS for MySQL snapshot can be restored or migrated directly to an Aurora MySQL DB cluster from the console or CLI. A logical dump can also be loaded into Aurora MySQL; Aurora's native S3 import expects Percona XtraBackup files, but the exam treats staging the dump in S3 and importing it as valid.

others.B: RDS snapshots are managed by AWS and cannot be uploaded or exported to S3 as an importable file for Aurora.
others.D: DMS migrates from live source databases or supported files, not from RDS snapshots.
others.E: DMS cannot use a mysqldump file in S3 as a source.

e.tip: RDS MySQL to Aurora MySQL: restore the snapshot as Aurora, or create an Aurora read replica and promote it.

q:
A company hosts a multi-tier web application on Amazon Linux Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The company observes that the Auto Scaling group launches more On-Demand Instances when the application's end users access high volumes of static web content. The company wants to optimize cost.

What should a solutions architect do to redesign the application MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Update the Auto Scaling group to use Reserved Instances instead of On-Demand Instances.
o.B: Update the Auto Scaling group to scale by launching Spot Instances instead of On-Demand Instances.
o.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to host the static web contents from an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda function behind an Amazon API Gateway API to host the static website contents.

e.why: Static content is what drives the unnecessary scale-out. Serving it from S3 through CloudFront moves that load off the EC2 fleet and caches it at edge locations, so fewer instances are needed and users get lower latency. That is the most cost-effective redesign.

others.A: Reserved Instances only discount instances; they do not stop the fleet from scaling to serve static files, and RIs suit steady usage rather than bursts.
others.B: Spot Instances make each instance cheaper, but the architecture still wastes compute on static files and risks interruptions.
others.D: Lambda with API Gateway is a poor and costly way to serve static files compared with S3 and CloudFront.

e.tip: Static content = S3 + CloudFront; keep the compute for dynamic requests.

q:
A company stores several petabytes of data across multiple AWS accounts. The company uses AWS Lake Formation to manage its data lake. The company's data science team wants to securely share selective data from its accounts with the company's engineering team for analytical purposes.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Copy the required data to a common account. Create an IAM access role in that account. Grant access by specifying a permission policy that includes users from the engineering team accounts as trusted entities.
o.B: Use the Lake Formation permissions Grant command in each account where the data is stored to allow the required engineering team users to access the data.
o.C: Use AWS Data Exchange to privately publish the required data to the required engineering team accounts.
o.D: Use Lake Formation tag-based access control to authorize and grant cross-account permissions for the required data to the engineering team accounts.

e.why: Lake Formation tag-based access control (LF-TBAC) assigns LF-Tags to databases, tables and columns, then grants permissions on tag expressions, including to other accounts. This shares selected data across accounts at scale without copying data or managing grants on each resource.

others.A: Copying petabytes into a common account is expensive and duplicates data that must then be kept in sync.
others.B: Named-resource grants in every account must be maintained one by one and do not scale well.
others.C: AWS Data Exchange is meant for publishing data products to subscribers, which is overkill for internal sharing within a Lake Formation data lake.

e.tip: Lake Formation sharing at scale = LF-Tags (TBAC).

q:
A company wants to host a scalable web application on AWS. The application will be accessed by users from different geographic regions of the world. Application users will be able to download and upload unique data up to gigabytes in size. The development team wants a cost-effective solution to minimize upload and download latency and maximize performance.

What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this?

o.A: Use Amazon S3 with Transfer Acceleration to host the application.
o.B: Use Amazon S3 with CacheControl headers to host the application.
o.C: Use Amazon EC2 with Auto Scaling and Amazon CloudFront to host the application.
o.D: Use Amazon EC2 with Auto Scaling and Amazon ElastiCache to host the application.

e.why: S3 Transfer Acceleration sends uploads and downloads through CloudFront edge locations and over the AWS backbone, which speeds up long-distance transfers of large, unique objects. Users pay the extra per-GB fee only when acceleration actually helps, which keeps it cost-effective.

others.B: CacheControl headers only affect caching; they do nothing for unique uploads or long-distance transfer speed.
others.C: CloudFront helps cacheable downloads, but unique GB-sized objects get little benefit, and running EC2 plus Auto Scaling costs more.
others.D: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache inside the Region and does not reduce global network latency for large file transfers.

e.tip: Fast global uploads to S3 = Transfer Acceleration; for very large files add multipart upload.

q:
A company has hired a solutions architect to design a reliable architecture for its application. The application consists of one Amazon RDS DB instance and two manually provisioned Amazon EC2 instances that run web servers. The EC2 instances are located in a single Availability Zone.

An employee recently deleted the DB instance, and the application was unavailable for 24 hours as a result. The company is concerned with the overall reliability of its environment.

What should the solutions architect do to maximize reliability of the application's infrastructure?

o.A: Delete one EC2 instance and enable termination protection on the other EC2 instance. Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection.
o.B: Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection. Place the EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer, and run them in an EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones.
o.C: Create an additional DB instance along with an Amazon API Gateway and an AWS Lambda function. Configure the application to invoke the Lambda function through API Gateway. Have the Lambda function write the data to the two DB instances.
o.D: Place the EC2 instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group that has multiple subnets located in multiple Availability Zones. Use Spot Instances instead of On-Demand Instances. Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor the health of the instances Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection.

e.why: RDS deletion protection prevents accidental deletion, and Multi-AZ adds a synchronous standby with automatic failover. Putting the web servers in an Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs behind an ALB removes the single-AZ and manual-instance weak points, which maximizes reliability.

others.A: Cutting down to one EC2 instance in one AZ makes reliability worse.
others.C: Writing to two DB instances through API Gateway and Lambda is a fragile, custom replication scheme that does not prevent deletion.
others.D: Spot Instances can be interrupted, which hurts reliability, and there is no load balancer to spread traffic across AZs.

q:
A company is storing 700 terabytes of data on a large network-attached storage (NAS) system in its corporate data center. The company has a hybrid environment with a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection.

After an audit from a regulator, the company has 90 days to move the data to the cloud. The company needs to move the data efficiently and without disruption. The company still needs to be able to access and update the data during the transfer window.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an AWS DataSync agent in the corporate data center. Create a data transfer task Start the transfer to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.B: Back up the data to AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices. Ship the devices to an AWS data center. Mount a target Amazon S3 bucket on the on-premises file system.
o.C: Use rsync to copy the data directly from local storage to a designated Amazon S3 bucket over the Direct Connect connection.
o.D: Back up the data on tapes. Ship the tapes to an AWS data center. Mount a target Amazon S3 bucket on the on-premises file system.

e.why: AWS DataSync runs online transfers over the existing 10 Gbps Direct Connect, and can move 700 TB well within 90 days. It does incremental syncs, so the NAS stays available and editable during the transfer and changes are copied in later passes, with encryption and integrity checks.

others.B: Snowball is offline, so changes made after copying would be missed, and you cannot mount an S3 bucket on the on-prem file system this way.
others.C: rsync cannot write to S3 directly and lacks DataSync's parallel transfers, checks and management.
others.D: Tapes are slow, offline and cannot capture ongoing updates.

e.tip: Good bandwidth + data changing during the move = DataSync.

q:
A company stores data in PDF format in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must follow a legal requirement to retain all new and existing data in Amazon S3 for 7 years.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Turn on the S3 Versioning feature for the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Lifecycle to delete the data after 7 years. Configure multi-factor authentication (MFA) delete for all S3 objects.
o.B: Turn on S3 Object Lock with governance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
o.C: Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
o.D: Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Use S3 Batch Operations to bring the existing data into compliance.

e.why: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode means no user, including root, can delete or overwrite object versions during the 7-year retention period, which meets the legal requirement. S3 Batch Operations can apply Object Lock retention to existing objects in bulk, without recopying them, for the least operational overhead.

others.A: Versioning with MFA delete and lifecycle rules does not legally lock data, and privileged users can still delete it.
others.B: Governance mode can be bypassed by users with special permissions, and recopying every object is high effort.
others.C: Compliance mode is right, but recopying all existing objects takes more effort than Batch Operations.

e.tip: Legal or regulatory WORM = Object Lock compliance mode; existing objects = S3 Batch Operations.

q:
A company has a stateless web application that runs on AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by Amazon API Gateway. The company wants to deploy the application across multiple AWS Regions to provide Regional failover capabilities.

What should a solutions architect do to route traffic to multiple Regions?

o.A: Create Amazon Route 53 health checks for each Region. Use an active-active failover configuration.
o.B: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin for each Region. Use CloudFront health checks to route traffic.
o.C: Create a transit gateway. Attach the transit gateway to the API Gateway endpoint in each Region. Configure the transit gateway to route requests.
o.D: Create an Application Load Balancer in the primary Region. Set the target group to point to the API Gateway endpoint hostnames in each Region.

e.why: Deploying the API Gateway and Lambda stack in several Regions, then using Route 53 records (latency or weighted) with health checks, routes users to healthy Regions and stops sending traffic to an unhealthy one. This active-active setup gives Regional failover for a stateless app.

others.B: CloudFront origin failover is based on error responses rather than health checks, and it works only as primary/secondary origin groups, not multi-Region active routing.
others.C: Transit Gateway connects VPCs and on-prem networks; it cannot attach to or route requests to API Gateway endpoints.
others.D: An ALB in one Region is a single Regional point of failure and cannot target API Gateway hostnames.

q:
A company has two VPCs named Management and Production. The Management VPC uses VPNs through a customer gateway to connect to a single device in the data center. The Production VPC uses a virtual private gateway with two attached AWS Direct Connect connections. The Management and Production VPCs both use a single VPC peering connection to allow communication between the applications.

What should a solutions architect do to mitigate any single point of failure in this architecture?

o.A: Add a set of VPNs between the Management and Production VPCs.
o.B: Add a second virtual private gateway and attach it to the Management VPC.
o.C: Add a second set of VPNs to the Management VPC from a second customer gateway device.
o.D: Add a second VPC peering connection between the Management VPC and the Production VPC.

fixed: Option C showed the answer key instead of its text and has been reconstructed; options B and D were truncated and have been completed.

e.why: The Management VPC connects to the data center through VPN tunnels that end on a single customer gateway device, which is a single point of failure. Adding a second set of VPN connections from a second customer gateway device removes it. The Production VPC already has two Direct Connect connections.

others.A: VPNs between the two VPCs do not address the single on-premises customer gateway.
others.B: A VPC can have only one virtual private gateway attached, and the gateway itself is already highly available.
others.D: VPC peering connections are already highly available, and only one peering connection can exist between two VPCs.

e.tip: For VPN resilience, look for a second customer gateway device on premises.

q:
A company runs its application on an Oracle database. The company plans to quickly migrate to AWS because of limited resources for the database, backup administration, and data center maintenance. The application uses third-party database features that require privileged access.

Which solution will help the company migrate the database to AWS MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. Replace third-party features with cloud services.
o.B: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle. Customize the database settings to support third-party features.
o.C: Migrate the database to an Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) for Oracle. Customize the database settings to support third-party features.
o.D: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL by rewriting the application code to remove dependency on Oracle APEX.

e.why: Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle gives privileged (OS and SYSDBA) access so third-party features can be installed and configured, while AWS still automates backups and much of the administration. That meets the need for privileged access with less effort and cost than running Oracle on EC2.

others.A: Standard RDS for Oracle gives no privileged access, and replacing the third-party features would slow the migration.
others.C: Oracle on EC2 means the company handles all backups, patching and HA, which it lacks resources for.
others.D: Rewriting for PostgreSQL is slow and costly and does not suit a quick migration.

e.tip: Managed database but needs OS or privileged access = RDS Custom (Oracle or SQL Server).

q:
A company has a three-tier web application that is in a single server. The company wants to migrate the application to the AWS Cloud. The company also wants the application to align with the AWS Well-Architected Framework and to be consistent with AWS recommended best practices for security, scalability, and resiliency.

Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

o.A: Create a VPC across two Availability Zones with the application's existing architecture. Host the application with existing architecture on an Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet in each Availability Zone with EC2 Auto Scaling groups. Secure the EC2 instance with security groups and network access control lists (network ACLs).
o.B: Set up security groups and network access control lists (network ACLs) to control access to the database layer. Set up a single Amazon RDS database in a private subnet.
o.C: Create a VPC across two Availability Zones. Refactor the application to host the web tier, application tier, and database tier. Host each tier on its own private subnet with Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and application tier.
o.D: Use a single Amazon RDS database. Allow database access only from the application tier security group.
o.E: Use Elastic Load Balancers in front of the web tier. Control access by using security groups containing references to each layer's security groups.
o.F: Use an Amazon RDS database Multi-AZ cluster deployment in private subnets. Allow database access only from application tier security groups.

e.why: Refactoring into separate web, app and database tiers in private subnets across two AZs, with Auto Scaling, gives scalability and resilience. ELBs in front of the web tier, with security groups that reference each tier's security group, enforce least-privilege access. An RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster in private subnets that accepts connections only from the app tier makes the data layer highly available and secure.

others.A: Lifting the monolith onto EC2 unchanged does not separate tiers and does not follow best practices.
others.B: A single RDS database is a single point of failure, which goes against resiliency guidance.
others.D: A single RDS database has no high availability.

q:
A company is migrating its applications and databases to the AWS Cloud. The company will use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), AWS Direct Connect, and Amazon RDS.

Which activities will be managed by the company's operational team? (Choose three.)

o.A: Management of the Amazon RDS infrastructure layer, operating system, and platforms
o.B: Creation of an Amazon RDS DB instance and configuring the scheduled maintenance window
o.C: Configuration of additional software components on Amazon ECS for monitoring, patch management, log management, and host intrusion detection
o.D: Installation of patches for all minor and major database versions for Amazon RDS
o.E: Ensure the physical security of the Amazon RDS infrastructure in the data center
o.F: Encryption of the data that moves in transit through Direct Connect

e.why: Under the shared responsibility model, customers create RDS instances and choose maintenance windows. Customers configure software on ECS container instances (EC2 launch type), such as monitoring, patching, logging and host intrusion detection. Customers also encrypt data in transit over Direct Connect, which is not encrypted by default, for example by using MACsec or a VPN.

others.A: AWS manages the RDS infrastructure, operating system and database platform.
others.D: AWS applies RDS database engine patches (customers only choose the timing or opt in to version upgrades).
others.E: AWS is responsible for physical security of its data centers.

e.tip: Direct Connect is private but not encrypted; use MACsec or a Site-to-Site VPN over it.

q:
A company runs a Java-based job on an Amazon EC2 instance. The job runs every hour and takes 10 seconds to run. The job runs on a scheduled interval and consumes 1 GB of memory. The CPU utilization of the instance is low except for short surges during which the job uses the maximum CPU available. The company wants to optimize the costs to run the job.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS App2Container (A2C) to containerize the job. Run the job as an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task on AWS Fargate with 0.5 virtual CPU (vCPU) and 1 GB of memory.
o.B: Copy the code into an AWS Lambda function that has 1 GB of memory. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to run the code each hour.
o.C: Use AWS App2Container (A2C) to containerize the job. Install the container in the existing Amazon Machine Image (AMI). Ensure that the schedule stops the container when the task finishes.
o.D: Configure the existing schedule to stop the EC2 instance at the completion of the job and restart the EC2 instance when the next job starts.

e.why: A 10-second hourly job with 1 GB of memory is ideal for Lambda: an EventBridge schedule invokes it, and you pay only for about 10 seconds of compute per hour instead of an idle instance. Lambda assigns CPU in proportion to memory, which is enough for the short CPU bursts.

others.A: Fargate works but has per-task startup overhead and a 1-minute billing minimum, and containerizing adds effort compared with Lambda.
others.C: Running the container on the existing EC2 AMI still keeps an instance running and paid for.
others.D: Stopping and starting EC2 every hour adds boot time and complexity, and per-second billing with a 1-minute minimum still costs more than Lambda.

e.tip: Short, scheduled, under 15 minutes = Lambda + EventBridge Scheduler.

q:
A company wants to implement a backup strategy for Amazon EC2 data and multiple Amazon S3 buckets. Because of regulatory requirements, the company must retain backup files for a specific time period. The company must not alter the files for the duration of the retention period.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault that has a vault lock in governance mode. Create the required backup plan.
o.B: Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to create the required automated snapshot policy.
o.C: Use Amazon S3 File Gateway to create the backup. Configure the appropriate S3 Lifecycle management.
o.D: Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault that has a vault lock in compliance mode. Create the required backup plan.

e.why: AWS Backup centrally backs up EC2 and S3. Vault Lock in compliance mode makes recovery points immutable: once the grace period ends, no one, including root, can delete them or shorten retention, which meets the requirement that files cannot be altered during the retention period.

others.A: Governance mode can be bypassed or removed by users with sufficient IAM permissions, so it does not guarantee immutability.
others.B: Data Lifecycle Manager handles only EBS snapshots and AMIs, not S3, and does not lock them.
others.C: S3 File Gateway is for hybrid file access, not a backup solution with immutable retention.

e.tip: Immutable backups for regulators = AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode.

q:
A company has resources across multiple AWS Regions and accounts. A newly hired solutions architect discovers a previous employee did not provide details about the resources inventory. The solutions architect needs to build and map the relationship details of the various workloads across all accounts.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.A: Use AWS Systems Manager Inventory to generate a map view from the detailed view report.
o.B: Use AWS Step Functions to collect workload details. Build architecture diagrams of the workloads manually.
o.C: Use Workload Discovery on AWS to generate architecture diagrams of the workloads.
o.D: Use AWS X-Ray to view the workload details. Build architecture diagrams with relationships.

e.why: Workload Discovery on AWS is an AWS Solution that crawls resources across accounts and Regions using AWS Config and builds architecture diagrams showing resource relationships automatically. It is the most operationally efficient way to inventory and map undocumented workloads.

others.A: Systems Manager Inventory collects software and configuration data from managed instances and does not map relationships between workloads.
others.B: Collecting data with Step Functions and drawing diagrams by hand is slow and error-prone.
others.D: X-Ray traces requests through instrumented applications, not resources across all accounts.

q:
A company uses AWS Organizations. The company wants to operate some of its AWS accounts with different budgets. The company wants to receive alerts and automatically prevent provisioning of additional resources on AWS accounts when the allocated budget threshold is met during a specific period.

Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

o.A: Use AWS Budgets to create a budget. Set the budget amount under the Cost and Usage Reports section of the required AWS accounts.
o.B: Use AWS Budgets to create a budget. Set the budget amount under the Billing dashboards of the required AWS accounts.
o.C: Create an IAM user for AWS Budgets to run budget actions with the required permissions.
o.D: Create an IAM role for AWS Budgets to run budget actions with the required permissions.
o.E: Add an alert to notify the company when each account meets its budget threshold. Add a budget action that selects the IAM identity created with the appropriate config rule to prevent provisioning of additional resources.
o.F: Add an alert to notify the company when each account meets its budget threshold. Add a budget action that selects the IAM identity created with the appropriate service control policy (SCP) to prevent provisioning of additional resources.

e.why: Create budgets with AWS Budgets in the Billing console. Budget actions need an IAM role that AWS Budgets can assume to run them. Configure an alert and a budget action that applies an SCP to the target accounts when the threshold is reached, which stops new resources from being provisioned.

others.A: Budgets are not set inside Cost and Usage Reports, which are detailed billing exports.
others.C: AWS Budgets uses an IAM role it assumes, not an IAM user.
others.E: AWS Config rules detect noncompliance; they are not a budget action type and cannot block provisioning.

e.tip: Budget actions can apply an IAM policy, apply an SCP, or stop EC2/RDS instances.

q:
A company runs applications on Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region. The company wants to back up the EC2 instances to a second Region. The company also wants to provision EC2 resources in the second Region and manage the EC2 instances centrally from one AWS account.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create a disaster recovery (DR) plan that has a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Configure data replication.
o.B: Create point-in-time Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots of the EC2 instances. Copy the snapshots to the second Region periodically.
o.C: Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup. Configure cross-Region backup to the second Region for the EC2 instances.
o.D: Deploy a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data from the source Region to the second Region.

e.why: AWS Backup centrally manages EC2 backups from one account and can copy recovery points to a second Region automatically with cross-Region copy rules. You can then restore instances there when needed, without paying for standby compute, which makes it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Running a similar fleet in the second Region costs a lot for a backup requirement.
others.B: Copying snapshots periodically by hand takes manual effort, does not give central backup management, and EBS snapshots alone do not capture full instance AMIs.
others.D: Running duplicate instances plus DataSync is costly, and DataSync is not an EC2 backup tool.

q:
A company that uses AWS is building an application to transfer data to a product manufacturer. The company has its own identity provider (IdP). The company wants the IdP to authenticate application users while the users use the application to transfer data. The company must use Applicability Statement 2 (AS2) protocol.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data. Create an AWS Lambda function for IdP authentication.
o.B: Use Amazon AppFlow flows to transfer the data. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task for IdP authentication.
o.C: Use AWS Transfer Family to transfer the data. Create an AWS Lambda function for IdP authentication.
o.D: Use AWS Storage Gateway to transfer the data. Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool for IdP authentication.

e.why: AWS Transfer Family supports the AS2 protocol for business-to-business data exchange. It can use a custom identity provider through a Lambda function (or API Gateway) so the company's own IdP authenticates users.

others.A: DataSync moves data between storage systems and does not support AS2.
others.B: Amazon AppFlow moves data between SaaS apps and AWS services and does not support AS2.
others.D: Storage Gateway offers file, volume and tape interfaces, not AS2.

e.tip: SFTP, FTPS, FTP or AS2 = AWS Transfer Family.

q:
A solutions architect is designing a RESTAPI in Amazon API Gateway for a cash payback service. The application requires 1 GB of memory and 2 GB of storage for its computation resources. The application will require that the data is in a relational format.

Which additional combination ofAWS services will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort? (Choose two.)

o.A: Amazon EC2
o.B: AWS Lambda
o.C: Amazon RDS
o.D: Amazon DynamoDB
o.E: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Services (Amazon EKS)

e.why: Lambda supports up to 10 GB of memory and up to 10 GB of ephemeral /tmp storage, so 1 GB of memory and 2 GB of storage fit serverless compute behind API Gateway. Amazon RDS gives managed relational storage, which together requires the least administrative effort.

others.A: EC2 means managing servers, patching and scaling.
others.D: DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value store, not relational.
others.E: EKS means running and operating Kubernetes, which takes much more admin effort.

q:
A company uses AWS Organizations to run workloads within multiple AWS accounts. A tagging policy adds department tags to AWS resources when the company creates tags.

An accounting team needs to determine spending on Amazon EC2 consumption. The accounting team must determine which departments are responsible for the costs regardless ofAWS account. The accounting team has access to AWS Cost Explorer for all AWS accounts within the organization and needs to access all reports from Cost Explorer.

Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.A: From the Organizations management account billing console, activate a user-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by tag name, and filter by EC2.
o.B: From the Organizations management account billing console, activate an AWS-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by tag name, and filter by EC2.
o.C: From the Organizations member account billing console, activate a user-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by the tag name, and filter by EC2.
o.D: From the Organizations member account billing console, activate an AWS-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by tag name, and filter by EC2.

e.why: Cost allocation tags are activated from the management (payer) account of the organization. Since department is a tag the company created, it is a user-defined tag. After activating it, one Cost Explorer report grouped by the department tag and filtered to EC2 shows spending across all accounts.

others.B: AWS-generated tags use the aws: prefix (like aws:createdBy); department is user-defined.
others.C: In an organization, only the management account can activate cost allocation tags.
others.D: It is both the wrong account and the wrong tag type.

e.tip: Cost allocation tags: activate in the management account; user-defined vs AWS-generated (aws: prefix).

q:
A company wants to securely exchange data between its software as a service (SaaS) application Salesforce account and Amazon S3. The company must encrypt the data at rest by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys (CMKs). The company must also encrypt the data in transit. The company has enabled API access for the Salesforce account.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

o.A: Create AWS Lambda functions to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
o.B: Create an AWS Step Functions workflow. Define the task to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
o.C: Create Amazon AppFlow flows to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
o.D: Create a custom connector for Salesforce to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.

fixed: The question sentence was missing and has been restored.

e.why: Amazon AppFlow is a fully managed integration service with a built-in Salesforce connector. It encrypts data in transit and can encrypt data at rest in S3 with a customer managed KMS key, so no custom code is needed.

others.A: Lambda functions would need custom code for the Salesforce API, authentication and encryption.
others.B: Step Functions orchestrates tasks but still needs custom code to move data from Salesforce.
others.D: Building a custom connector is unnecessary development work when AppFlow already supports Salesforce.

e.tip: SaaS (Salesforce, Zendesk, ServiceNow) to S3 transfers point to Amazon AppFlow.

q:
A company is developing a mobile gaming app in a single AWS Region. The app runs on multiple Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The company stores the app data in Amazon DynamoDB. The app communicates by using TCP traffic and UDP traffic between the users and the servers. The application will be used globally. The company wants to ensure the lowest possible latency for all users.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Global Accelerator to create an accelerator. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) behind an accelerator endpoint that uses Global Accelerator integration and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the ALB.
o.B: Use AWS Global Accelerator to create an accelerator. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) behind an accelerator endpoint that uses Global Accelerator integration and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the NLB.
o.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront content delivery network (CDN) endpoint. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) behind the endpoint and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the NLB. Update CloudFront to use the NLB as the origin.
o.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront content delivery network (CDN) endpoint. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) behind the endpoint and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the ALB. Update CloudFront to use the ALB as the origin.

fixed: Option B text was missing (only a fragment remained) and has been reconstructed; options A, C and D were truncated and have been completed.

e.why: The app uses both TCP and UDP, so it needs a Network Load Balancer, which supports both protocols. Global Accelerator also supports TCP and UDP and routes global users to the nearest edge location and over the AWS backbone, giving the lowest latency.

others.A: An Application Load Balancer only supports HTTP and HTTPS, so it cannot listen on UDP ports.
others.C: CloudFront only delivers HTTP and HTTPS traffic, so it cannot carry the app's UDP traffic.
others.D: CloudFront and an ALB both handle only HTTP and HTTPS, not UDP.

e.tip: TCP and UDP for global users means Global Accelerator in front of an NLB.

q:
A company has an application that processes customer orders. The company hosts the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that saves the orders to an Amazon Aurora database. Occasionally when traffic is high the workload does not process orders fast enough.

What should a solutions architect do to write the orders reliably to the database as quickly as possible?

o.A: Increase the instance size of the EC2 instance when traffic is high. Write orders to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Subscribe the database endpoint to the SNS topic.
o.B: Write orders to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SQS queue and process orders into the database.
o.C: Write orders to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Subscribe the database endpoint to the SNS topic. Use EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SNS topic.
o.D: Write orders to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue when the EC2 instance reaches CPU threshold limits. Use scheduled scaling of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SQS queue and process orders into the database.

e.why: Writing orders to an SQS queue stores each order durably right away, even during spikes. A fleet of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group pulls from the queue and writes to Aurora, scaling with load so orders are processed reliably and as quickly as capacity allows.

others.A: SNS cannot deliver messages to a database endpoint, and a bigger instance does not decouple or buffer load.
others.C: SNS is push-based and does not keep messages for workers to poll, and a database cannot subscribe to a topic.
others.D: Queueing only after hitting a CPU threshold adds complexity, and scheduled scaling does not react to unpredictable spikes.

e.tip: Reliable buffering of bursty writes = SQS + Auto Scaling consumers (scale on queue depth).

q:
An IoT company is releasing a mattress that has sensors to collect data about a user’s sleep. The sensors will send data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The sensors collect approximately 2 MB of data every night for each mattress. The company must process and summarize the data for each mattress. The results need to be available as soon as possible. Data processing will require 1 GB of memory and will finish within 30 seconds.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use AWS Glue with a Scala job
o.B: Use Amazon EMR with an Apache Spark script
o.C: Use AWS Lambda with a Python script
o.D: Use AWS Glue with a PySpark job

e.why: Each job uses 1 GB of memory and finishes in 30 seconds, well within Lambda's 10 GB and 15-minute limits. An S3 event can invoke a Python Lambda function as soon as data arrives, and you pay only per millisecond of execution, which makes it the most cost-effective choice.

others.A: Glue Spark jobs have startup latency and DPU-based minimum billing, which is overkill for 2 MB files.
others.B: EMR clusters cost far more and take much more effort to run for tiny, short jobs.
others.D: PySpark on Glue has the same startup and minimum-cost drawbacks as other Glue Spark jobs.

e.tip: Small, short, event-driven processing = Lambda.

q:
A company hosts an online shopping application that stores all orders in an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instance. Management wants to eliminate single points of failure and has asked a solutions architect to recommend an approach to minimize database downtime without requiring any changes to the application code.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Convert the existing database instance to a Multi-AZ deployment by modifying the database instance and specifying the Multi-AZ option.
o.B: Create a new RDS Multi-AZ deployment. Take a snapshot of the current RDS instance and restore the new Multi-AZ deployment with the snapshot.
o.C: Create a read-only replica of the PostgreSQL database in another Availability Zone. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted record sets to distribute requests across the databases.
o.D: Place the RDS for PostgreSQL database in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum group size of two. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted record sets to distribute requests across instances.

e.why: Modifying the existing RDS instance to Multi-AZ creates a synchronous standby in another AZ with automatic failover. The DB endpoint DNS name does not change, so no application code changes are needed, and the conversion happens online with minimal impact.

others.B: Restoring from a snapshot creates a new endpoint, so the app config must change, and writes made after the snapshot are lost or need a cutover.
others.C: Read replicas are read-only and replicate asynchronously, so weighted routing would send writes to a replica that cannot accept them.
others.D: RDS instances cannot be put in EC2 Auto Scaling groups.

e.tip: Single-AZ to Multi-AZ is a simple modify operation with the same endpoint.

q:
A company is developing an application to support customer demands. The company wants to deploy the application on multiple Amazon EC2 Nitro-based instances within the same Availability Zone. The company also wants to give the application the ability to write to multiple block storage volumes in multiple EC2 Nitro-based instances simultaneously to achieve higher application availability.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use General Purpose SSD (gp3) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach
o.B: Use Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach
o.C: Use Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach
o.D: Use General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach

e.why: EBS Multi-Attach lets one volume attach to up to 16 Nitro-based instances in the same AZ, with simultaneous read and write access. It is supported only on Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes (io1 and io2), so io2 is the right choice.

others.A: gp3 volumes do not support Multi-Attach.
others.B: st1 HDD volumes do not support Multi-Attach.
others.D: gp2 volumes do not support Multi-Attach.

e.tip: Multi-Attach = io1/io2 only, same AZ only, needs a cluster-aware file system.

q:
A company designed a stateless two-tier application that uses Amazon EC2 in a single Availability Zone and an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. New company management wants to ensure the application is highly available.

What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.A: Configure the application to use Multi-AZ EC2 Auto Scaling and create an Application Load Balancer
o.B: Configure the application to take snapshots of the EC2 instances and send them to a different AWS Region
o.C: Configure the application to use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to feed requests to the application
o.D: Configure Amazon Route 53 rules to handle incoming requests and create a Multi-AZ Application Load Balancer

e.why: The database is already Multi-AZ, so the remaining single point of failure is the EC2 tier in one AZ. A Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer spreads the stateless instances across AZs and replaces unhealthy ones, which makes the application highly available.

others.B: Cross-Region snapshots are a backup or DR measure; they do not keep the application available in real time.
others.C: Latency-based routing does not help when every instance is in one AZ.
others.D: A Multi-AZ ALB alone does not help if all EC2 instances are still in one AZ, and Route 53 rules add nothing here.

q: A company uses AWS Organizations. A member account has purchased a Compute Savings Plan. Because of changes in the workloads inside the member account, the account no longer receives the full benefit of the Compute Savings Plan commitment. The company uses less than 50% of its purchased compute power.

o.A: Turn on discount sharing from the Billing Preferences section of the account console in the member account that purchased the Compute Savings Plan.
o.B: Turn on discount sharing from the Billing Preferences section of the account console in the company's Organizations management account.
o.C: Migrate additional compute workloads from another AWS account to the account that has the Compute Savings Plan.
o.D: Sell the excess Savings Plan commitment in the Reserved Instance Marketplace.

e.why: In AWS Organizations, Savings Plans and Reserved Instance discount sharing is controlled from the management account's billing preferences. Turning sharing on there lets unused Compute Savings Plan commitment apply to eligible usage in other accounts in the organization.

others.A: Member accounts cannot turn on organization-wide discount sharing; the setting lives in the management account.
others.C: Migrating workloads between accounts is disruptive, high-effort work just to use a discount that sharing handles automatically.
others.D: Savings Plans cannot be sold; only certain Standard Reserved Instances can be sold on the Reserved Instance Marketplace.

q:
A company is developing a microservices application that will provide a search catalog for customers. The company must use REST APIs to present the frontend of the application to users. The REST APIs must access the backend services that the company hosts in containers in private VPC subnets.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
o.B: Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
o.C: Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
o.D: Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.

e.why: Amazon API Gateway REST APIs meet the REST requirement. A private VPC link (through an NLB, or for HTTP APIs an ALB or Cloud Map) lets API Gateway reach ECS services in private subnets without exposing them to the internet.

others.A: WebSocket APIs are for two-way persistent connections, not the REST interface that is required.
others.C: WebSocket is the wrong API type, and API Gateway does not sit in your VPC with a security group.
others.D: API Gateway is a managed service outside your VPC, so a security group alone cannot give it access to private subnets.

e.tip: API Gateway to private VPC resources = VPC link.

q:
A company stores raw collected data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data is used for several types of analytics on behalf of the company's customers. The type of analytics requested determines the access pattern on the S3 objects.

The company cannot predict or control the access pattern. The company wants to reduce its S3 costs.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use S3 replication to transition infrequently accessed objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
o.B: Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
o.C: Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering
o.D: Use S3 Inventory to identify and transition objects that have not been accessed from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering

e.why: When access patterns cannot be predicted or controlled, S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on their actual use, with no retrieval fees. A lifecycle rule to transition objects into Intelligent-Tiering cuts cost without guessing.

others.A: S3 Replication copies objects to other buckets; it is not a tiering mechanism.
others.B: Moving objects to Standard-IA on a fixed schedule can lead to retrieval fees and minimum storage charges when objects are accessed often after all.
others.D: S3 Inventory lists objects but does not show access and does not transition anything, so it needs manual work.

q:
A company has applications hosted on Amazon EC2 instances with IPv6 addresses. The applications must initiate communications with other external applications using the internet. However the company’s security policy states that any external service cannot initiate a connection to the EC2 instances.

What should a solutions architect recommend to resolve this issue?

o.A: Create a NAT gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
o.B: Create an internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
o.C: Create a virtual private gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
o.D: Create an egress-only internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table

e.why: An egress-only internet gateway is the IPv6 equivalent of a NAT gateway. It allows outbound IPv6 connections to the internet and blocks inbound connections started from outside, which matches the security policy.

others.A: NAT gateways do NAT for IPv4 (plus NAT64), not native IPv6 egress.
others.B: An internet gateway allows two-way IPv6 traffic, so external hosts could start connections.
others.C: A virtual private gateway connects to on-premises networks over VPN, not to the internet.

e.tip: IPv4 outbound only = NAT gateway; IPv6 outbound only = egress-only IGW.

q:
A company is creating an application that runs on containers in a VPC. The application stores and accesses data in an Amazon S3 bucket. During the development phase, the application will store and access 1 TB of data in Amazon S3 each day. The company wants to minimize costs and wants to prevent traffic from traversing the internet whenever possible.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering for the S3 bucket
o.B: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for the S3 bucket
o.C: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. Associate this endpoint with all route tables in the VPC.
o.D: Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. Associate this endpoint with all route tables in the VPC.

fixed: Option C was missing its first sentence and option D was truncated; both have been reconstructed.

e.why: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 is free and keeps traffic between the VPC and S3 on the AWS network. You associate it with route tables, so the containers reach S3 privately without NAT gateway data processing charges.

others.A: Intelligent-Tiering changes storage costs but does nothing to keep traffic off the internet.
others.B: Transfer Acceleration speeds up transfers over the internet through edge locations and costs extra.
others.D: Interface endpoints cost per hour and per GB, and they are not associated with route tables.

e.tip: Private, low-cost S3 access from a VPC means a gateway endpoint.

q:
A company has a mobile chat application with a data store based in Amazon DynamoDB. Users would like new messages to be read with as little latency as possible. A solutions architect needs to design an optimal solution that requires minimal application changes.

Which method should the solutions architect select?

o.A: Configure Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for the new messages table. Update the code to use the DAX endpoint.
o.B: Add DynamoDB read replicas to handle the increased read load. Update the application to point to the read endpoint for the read replicas.
o.C: Double the number of read capacity units for the new messages table in DynamoDB. Continue to use the existing DynamoDB endpoint.
o.D: Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache to the application stack. Update the application to point to the Redis cache endpoint instead of DynamoDB.

fixed: Option B showed the answer key instead of its text and has been reconstructed; options C and D were truncated and have been completed.

e.why: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is an in-memory cache built for DynamoDB that gives microsecond read latency. It is API-compatible with DynamoDB, so the application only needs to switch to the DAX endpoint.

others.B: DynamoDB does not support read replicas; global tables replicate across Regions and do not lower read latency this way.
others.C: More read capacity reduces throttling but does not lower the latency of each read.
others.D: ElastiCache for Redis would need application code changes for caching logic, which goes against minimal changes.

e.tip: Faster DynamoDB reads with minimal code changes means DAX.

q:
A company hosts a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website serves static content. Website traffic is increasing, and the company is concerned about a potential increase in cost.

What should a solutions architect recommend to reduce the potential cost?

o.A: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache state files at edge locations.
o.B: Create an Amazon ElastiCache cluster. Connect the ALB to the ElastiCache cluster to serve cached files.
o.C: Create an AWS WAF web ACL and associate it with the ALB. Add a rule to the web ACL to cache static files.
o.D: Create a second ALB in an alternative AWS Region. Route user traffic to the closest Region to minimize data transfer costs.

fixed: The question sentence was missing and has been restored; option B was replaced by part of option C and has been reconstructed.

e.why: CloudFront caches static content at edge locations, so most requests never reach the ALB and EC2 instances. That reduces the load and the number of instances needed, and CloudFront data transfer is usually cheaper than serving from the origin.

others.B: An ALB cannot connect to ElastiCache to serve files, and ElastiCache is not meant for serving static web content.
others.C: AWS WAF filters requests; it cannot cache static files.
others.D: A second ALB in another Region adds infrastructure cost instead of reducing it.

e.tip: Static content plus rising traffic costs points to CloudFront caching.

q:
A company has multiple VPCs across AWS Regions to support and run workloads that are isolated from workloads in other Regions. Because of a recent application launch requirement, the company’s VPCs must communicate with all other VPCs across all Regions.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of administrative effort?

o.A: Use VPC peering to manage VPC communication in a single Region. Use VPC peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
