o.B: Use AWS Direct Connect gateways across all Regions to connect VPCs across regions and manage VPC communications.
o.C: Use AWS Transit Gateway to manage VPC communication in a single Region and Transit Gateway peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
o.D: Use AWS PrivateLink across all Regions to connect VPCs across Regions and manage VPC communications

e.why: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a Regional hub that connects many VPCs without a full mesh of peering connections. Inter-Region Transit Gateway peering links the hubs, giving any-to-any connectivity across Regions with the least administrative effort.

others.A: Full-mesh VPC peering needs n(n-1)/2 connections and route updates because peering is not transitive, which is heavy to manage.
others.B: Direct Connect gateways connect on-premises networks to VPCs; they do not route traffic between VPCs.
others.D: PrivateLink exposes specific services one way through endpoints, not full network connectivity between VPCs.

e.tip: Many VPCs, transitive routing = Transit Gateway (peer across Regions).

q:
A company is designing a containerized application that will use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The application needs to access a shared file system that is highly durable and can recover data to another AWS Region with a recovery point objective (RPO) of 8 hours. The file system needs to provide a mount target m each Availability Zone within a Region.

A solutions architect wants to use AWS Backup to manage the replication to another Region.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ deployment
o.B: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with a Multi-AZ deployment
o.C: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with the Standard storage class
o.D: Amazon FSx for OpenZFS

e.why: Amazon EFS Standard (Regional) stores data across multiple AZs and gives a mount target in each AZ. ECS tasks can mount it natively, and AWS Backup can copy EFS backups to another Region on a schedule that meets an 8-hour RPO.

others.A: FSx for Windows Multi-AZ uses only two AZs (preferred and standby subnets), not a mount target in every AZ, and it is SMB-oriented.
others.B: FSx for NetApp ONTAP Multi-AZ also spans only two AZs and does not give a mount target in each AZ.
others.D: FSx for OpenZFS is a single-AZ or two-AZ deployment, not a mount target per AZ.

e.tip: Mount target in every AZ, NFS for containers = EFS.

q:
A company is expecting rapid growth in the near future. A solutions architect needs to configure existing users and grant permissions to new users on AWS. The solutions architect has decided to create IAM groups. The solutions architect will add the new users to IAM groups based on department.

Which additional action is the MOST secure way to grant permissions to the new users?

o.A: Apply service control policies (SCPs) to manage access permissions
o.B: Create IAM roles that have least privilege permission. Attach the roles to the IAM groups
o.C: Create an IAM policy that grants least privilege permission. Attach the policy to the IAM groups
o.D: Create IAM roles. Associate the roles with a permissions boundary that defines the maximum permissions

e.why: IAM groups get permissions by attaching IAM policies. A least-privilege customer managed policy attached to each department group automatically applies to all current and new users added to it, which is the most secure and scalable approach.

others.A: SCPs set the maximum permissions for accounts in Organizations; they grant nothing to users.
others.B: Roles cannot be attached to groups; roles are assumed, not attached.
others.D: Permissions boundaries limit maximum permissions but grant nothing on their own, and associating roles does not grant permissions to group users.

q:
A law firm needs to share information with the public. The information includes hundreds of files that must be publicly readable. Modifications or deletions of the files by anyone before a designated future date are prohibited.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

o.A: Upload all files to an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for static website hosting. Grant read-only IAM permissions to any AWS principals that access the S3 bucket until the designated date.
o.B: Create a new Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Use S3 Object Lock with a retention period in accordance with the designated date. Configure the S3 bucket for static website hosting. Set an S3 bucket policy to allow read-only access to the objects.
o.C: Create a new Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Configure an event trigger to run an AWS Lambda function in case of object modification or deletion. Configure the Lambda function to replace the objects with the original versions from a private S3 bucket.
o.D: Upload all files to an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for static website hosting. Select the folder that contains the files. Use S3 Object Lock with a retention period in accordance with the designated date. Grant read-only IAM permissions to any AWS principals that access the S3 bucket.

e.why: S3 Object Lock, which requires versioning and is easiest to enable on a new bucket, set with a retention period up to the designated date prevents changes or deletions. A static website plus a bucket policy that allows public s3:GetObject makes the files publicly readable.

others.A: IAM permissions apply only to AWS principals, not anonymous public users, and nothing stops bucket owners from changing the files.
others.C: Lambda-based restore is reactive; files can still be changed or deleted, briefly exposing wrong content.
others.D: Object Lock cannot be applied by selecting a folder in an existing bucket, and IAM permissions do not give anonymous public read access.

q:
A company is making a prototype of the infrastructure for its new website by manually provisioning the necessary infrastructure. This infrastructure includes an Auto Scaling group, an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon RDS database. After the configuration has been thoroughly validated, the company wants the capability to immediately deploy the infrastructure for development and production use in two Availability Zones in an automated fashion.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Systems Manager to replicate and provision the prototype infrastructure in two Availability Zones
o.B: Define the infrastructure as a template by using the prototype infrastructure as a guide. Deploy the infrastructure with AWS CloudFormation.
o.C: Use AWS Config to record the inventory of resources that are used in the prototype infrastructure. Use AWS Config to deploy the prototype infrastructure into two Availability Zones.
o.D: Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk and configure it to use an automated reference to the prototype infrastructure to automatically deploy new environments in two Availability Zones.

e.why: Defining the validated infrastructure (Auto Scaling group, ALB, RDS across two AZs) as an AWS CloudFormation template gives repeatable infrastructure as code. You can deploy identical development and production stacks immediately and automatically.

others.A: Systems Manager handles operations on existing resources, not replicating whole infrastructure stacks.
others.C: AWS Config records and evaluates resource configurations; it cannot deploy infrastructure.
others.D: Elastic Beanstalk cannot reference a manually built prototype and turn it into new environments automatically.

e.tip: Repeatable environments = CloudFormation (IaC).

q:
A business application is hosted on Amazon EC2 and uses Amazon S3 for encrypted object storage. The chief information security officer has directed that no application traffic between the two services should traverse the public internet.

Which capability should the solutions architect use to meet the compliance requirements?

o.A: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
o.B: VPC endpoint
o.C: Private subnet
o.D: Virtual private gateway

e.why: A VPC endpoint for S3 (a gateway endpoint, or an interface endpoint through PrivateLink) sends EC2 to S3 traffic over the AWS private network instead of the public internet. Bucket policies can then require aws:SourceVpce.

others.A: KMS encrypts data but does not change the network path the traffic takes.
others.C: A private subnet still reaches S3's public endpoints through a NAT gateway and the internet unless a VPC endpoint is used.
others.D: A virtual private gateway is for VPN connections to on-premises networks, not for reaching S3.

q:
A company hosts a three-tier web application in the AWS Cloud. A Multi-AZAmazon RDS for MySQL server forms the database layer Amazon ElastiCache forms the cache layer. The company wants a caching strategy that adds or updates data in the cache when a customer adds an item to the database. The data in the cache must always match the data in the database.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Implement the lazy loading caching strategy
o.B: Implement the write-through caching strategy
o.C: Implement the adding TTL caching strategy
o.D: Implement the AWS AppConfig caching strategy

e.why: With write-through caching, the application writes to the cache at the same moment it writes to the database. The cache therefore always has current data that matches the database, which is exactly what the requirement asks for.

others.A: Lazy loading fills the cache only on a cache miss, so cached data can be stale or missing after database writes.
others.C: Adding a TTL only limits how long stale data lives; it does not keep the cache in sync on every write.
others.D: AWS AppConfig manages application configuration and feature flags, not a database caching strategy.

e.tip: Always consistent = write-through; only cache what is read = lazy loading; combine with TTL for best results.

q:
A company wants to migrate 100 GB of historical data from an on-premises location to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has a 100 megabits per second (Mbps) internet connection on premises. The company needs to encrypt the data in transit to the S3 bucket. The company will store new data directly in Amazon S3.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use the s3 sync command in the AWS CLI to move the data directly to an S3 bucket
o.B: Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data from the on-premises location to an S3 bucket
o.C: Use AWS Snowball to move the data to an S3 bucket
o.D: Set up an IPsec VPN from the on-premises location to AWS. Use the s3 cp command in the AWS CLI to move the data directly to an S3 bucket

e.why: 100 GB over 100 Mbps takes only a few hours, so an online transfer is fine. AWS DataSync is a managed service that encrypts data in transit with TLS, runs parallel transfers, checks integrity and retries automatically, giving a secure migration with little operational overhead.

others.A: aws s3 sync also uses HTTPS and is a reasonable approach, but you must run and monitor it yourself, with no built-in verification, scheduling or reporting.
others.C: Snowball needs days of ordering and shipping, which is slower and more effort for just 100 GB.
others.D: An IPsec VPN is unnecessary because S3 endpoints already use HTTPS, and setting one up adds overhead.

e.tip: Snowball is worth it only when the online transfer would take more than about a week.

q:
A company containerized a Windows job that runs on .NET 6 Framework under a Windows container. The company wants to run this job in the AWS Cloud. The job runs every 10 minutes. The job’s runtime varies between 1 minute and 3 minutes.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create an AWS Lambda function based on the container image of the job. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the function every 10 minutes.
o.B: Use AWS Batch to create a job that uses AWS Fargate resources. Configure the job scheduling to run every 10 minutes.
o.C: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate to run the job. Create a scheduled task based on the container image of the job to run every 10 minutes.
o.D:
Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate to run the job. Create a standalone task based on the container image of the job. Use Windows task scheduler to run the job every
10 minutes.

e.why: ECS on Fargate supports Windows containers, and an EventBridge-driven ECS scheduled task launches the job every 10 minutes. You pay only while each task runs for 1 to 3 minutes, with no servers to manage, which makes it the most cost-effective choice.

others.A: Lambda container images must be Linux-based, so a Windows container cannot run on Lambda.
others.B: AWS Batch on Fargate does not support Windows containers.
others.D: Windows Task Scheduler inside a standalone task would require the task to run all the time, so you pay for idle time.

q:
A company wants to move from many standalone AWS accounts to a consolidated, multi-account architecture. The company plans to create many new AWS accounts for different business units. The company needs to authenticate access to these AWS accounts by using a centralized corporate directory service.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create a new organization in AWS Organizations with all features turned on. Create the new AWS accounts in the organization.
o.B: Set up an Amazon Cognito identity pool. Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to accept Amazon Cognito authentication.
o.C: Configure a service control policy (SCP) to manage the AWS accounts. Add AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to AWS Directory Service.
o.D: Create a new organization in AWS Organizations. Configure the organization's authentication mechanism to use AWS Directory Service directly.
o.E: Set up AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) in the organization. Configure IAM Identity Center, and integrate it with the company's corporate directory service.

e.why: AWS Organizations with all features enabled creates and centrally governs the new business-unit accounts. IAM Identity Center, set up in the organization and connected to the corporate directory (Active Directory through Directory Service, or an external IdP via SAML/SCIM), gives single sign-on to every account.

others.B: Cognito identity pools are for app end users, not workforce access to AWS accounts.
others.C: SCPs limit permissions but do not authenticate anyone, and Identity Center is not added to Directory Service.
others.D: Organizations has no authentication mechanism of its own that can be pointed at Directory Service.

e.tip: Workforce SSO across many accounts = Organizations + IAM Identity Center + corporate IdP.

q:
A company is looking for a solution that can store video archives in AWS from old news footage. The company needs to minimize costs and will rarely need to restore these files. When the files are needed, they must be available in a maximum of five minutes.

What is the MOST cost-effective solution?

o.A: Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Glacier and use Expedited retrievals.
o.B: Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Glacier and use Standard retrievals.
o.C: Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).
o.D: Store the video archives in Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA).

e.why: S3 Glacier storage is very cheap for rarely accessed archives. Expedited retrievals usually return data within 1 to 5 minutes, which meets the 5-minute limit on the rare occasions files are needed.

others.B: Standard Glacier retrievals take 3 to 5 hours, far beyond 5 minutes.
others.C: Standard-IA gives instant access but costs much more to store than Glacier for archives that are rarely read.
others.D: One Zone-IA costs more to store than Glacier and keeps data in only one AZ.

e.tip: Glacier Flexible Retrieval: Expedited 1-5 min, Standard 3-5 h, Bulk 5-12 h. Glacier Instant Retrieval is an alternative with millisecond access.

q:
A company is building a three-tier application on AWS. The presentation tier will serve a static website The logic tier is a containerized application. This application will store data in a relational database. The company wants to simplify deployment and to reduce operational costs.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon S3 to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
o.B: Use Amazon CloudFront to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
o.C: Use Amazon S3 to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
o.D: Use Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.

e.why: S3 hosts the static site cheaply with no servers. ECS on Fargate runs the containers serverlessly with simpler deployment than EKS, and RDS provides a managed relational database, which reduces both operational work and cost.

others.B: CloudFront is a CDN, not a place to store files on its own, and ECS on EC2 means managing container instances.
others.C: EKS adds Kubernetes complexity and a per-cluster control plane fee compared with ECS.
others.D: Hosting static content on EC2 Reserved Instances and running EKS on EC2 is the most operationally heavy option.

e.tip: Simplest container compute = ECS on Fargate.

q:
A company seeks a storage solution for its application. The solution must be highly available and scalable. The solution also must function as a file system be mountable by multiple Linux instances in AWS and on premises through native protocols, and have no minimum size requirements. The company has set up a Site-to-Site VPN for access from its on-premises network to its VPC.

Which storage solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Amazon FSx Multi-AZ deployments
o.B: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach volumes
o.C: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with multiple mount targets
o.D: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a single mount target and multiple access points

e.why: Amazon EFS is an elastic NFS file system with no minimum size that scales automatically. Mount targets in multiple AZs make it highly available, and Linux instances in AWS and on premises (over the Site-to-Site VPN) can mount it with native NFS.

others.A: FSx deployments have minimum storage capacities, and the option does not name an FSx type with native Linux NFS access.
others.B: EBS Multi-Attach volumes are block storage limited to one AZ and cannot be mounted from on premises.
others.D: A single mount target puts the file system in one AZ, so it is not highly available.

q:
A 4-year-old media company is using the AWS Organizations all features feature set to organize its AWS accounts. According to the company's finance team, the billing information on the member accounts must not be accessible to anyone, including the root user of the member accounts.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Add all finance team users to an IAM group. Attach an AWS managed policy named Billing to the group.
o.B: Attach an identity-based policy to deny access to the billing information to all users, including the root user.
o.C: Create a service control policy (SCP) to deny access to the billing information. Attach the SCP to the root organizational unit (OU).
o.D: Convert from the Organizations all features feature set to the Organizations consolidated billing feature set.

e.why: Service control policies apply to every principal in member accounts, including the root user. An SCP on the root OU that denies billing actions (for example aws-portal:*, billing:* or ce:*) blocks access to billing information in all member accounts.

others.A: Granting the finance team billing access does nothing to restrict others.
others.B: Identity-based policies cannot be attached to the root user, so they cannot restrict it.
others.D: Moving to consolidated billing only would remove SCPs, the very feature that is needed.

e.tip: Restrict the root user of member accounts = SCP.

q:
An ecommerce company runs an application in the AWS Cloud that is integrated with an on-premises warehouse solution. The company uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send order messages to an on-premises HTTPS endpoint so the warehouse application can process the orders. The local data center team has detected that some of the order messages were not received.

A solutions architect needs to retain messages that are not delivered and analyze the messages for up to 14 days.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

o.A: Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream target with a retention period of 14 days.
o.B: Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue with a retention period of 14 days between the application and Amazon SNS.
o.C: Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) target with a retention period of 14 days.
o.D: Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon DynamoDB target with a TTL attribute set for a retention period of 14 days.

e.why: SNS subscriptions can have a dead-letter queue, an SQS queue that receives messages SNS could not deliver after its retries. Setting the SQS retention period to its 14-day maximum keeps failed order messages for analysis with only configuration changes.

others.A: SNS dead-letter queues must be SQS queues; Kinesis Data Streams cannot be one.
others.B: Putting SQS in front of SNS does not capture messages that fail to reach the HTTPS endpoint after SNS.
others.D: DynamoDB cannot be an SNS dead-letter queue target.

e.tip: SQS retention: 4 days by default, 1 minute to 14 days configurable.

q:
A gaming company uses Amazon DynamoDB to store user information such as geographic location, player data, and leaderboards. The company needs to configure continuous backups to an Amazon S3 bucket with a minimal amount of coding. The backups must not affect availability of the application and must not affect the read capacity units (RCUs) that are defined for the table.

Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Use an Amazon EMR cluster. Create an Apache Hive job to back up the data to Amazon S3.
o.B: Export the data directly from DynamoDB to Amazon S3 with continuous backups. Turn on point-in-time recovery for the table.
o.C: Configure Amazon DynamoDB Streams. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume the stream and export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda function to export the data from the database tables to Amazon S3 on a regular basis. Turn on point-in-time recovery for the table.

e.why: DynamoDB export to S3 needs point-in-time recovery (continuous backups) enabled. It reads from the PITR backup data, not the live table, so it uses no read capacity and does not affect availability, and it needs no code.

others.A: A Hive job on EMR means building and running a cluster, and scanning the table uses RCUs.
others.C: Streams plus Lambda requires custom code and only captures changes, not a full backup of existing data.
others.D: A Lambda export function requires code, and scanning tables uses RCUs.

q:
A solutions architect is designing an asynchronous application to process credit card data validation requests for a bank. The application must be secure and be able to process each request at least once.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source. Use AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.
o.B: Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source. Use SQS managed encryption keys (SSE-SQS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.
o.C: Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source. Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.
o.D: Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source. Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.

e.why: SQS standard queues guarantee at-least-once delivery and cost less than FIFO queues. SSE-KMS encrypts the sensitive card data, and Lambda's execution role needs kms:Decrypt to read the encrypted messages through the event source mapping.

others.B: FIFO queues cost more and give exactly-once processing, which is not needed, and SSE-SQS gives less key control for bank data.
others.C: FIFO queues are more expensive than needed for at-least-once processing.
others.D: Lambda needs kms:Decrypt on its execution role, not an invocation permission on the key.

e.tip: At least once = SQS standard; exactly once in order = FIFO.

q:
A company has multiple AWS accounts for development work. Some staff consistently use oversized Amazon EC2 instances, which causes the company to exceed the yearly budget for the development accounts. The company wants to centrally restrict the creation of AWS resources in these accounts.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

o.A: Develop AWS Systems Manager templates that use an approved EC2 creation process. Use the approved Systems Manager templates to provision EC2 instances.
o.B: Use AWS Organizations to organize the accounts into organizational units (OUs). Define and attach a service control policy (SCP) to control the usage of EC2 instance types.
o.C: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function when an EC2 instance is created. Stop disallowed EC2 instance types.
o.D: Set up AWS Service Catalog products for the staff to create the allowed EC2 instance types. Ensure that staff can deploy EC2 instances only by using the Service Catalog products.

e.why: Grouping the development accounts into an OU and attaching an SCP that denies ec2:RunInstances unless ec2:InstanceType matches an allowed list blocks oversized instances centrally. It needs no development effort.

others.A: Systems Manager templates do not stop staff from launching instances directly, and building them takes development work.
others.C: EventBridge plus Lambda reacts after creation and needs custom code.
others.D: Service Catalog products take setup work and still need extra IAM restrictions to stop direct launches.

q:
A company wants to use artificial intelligence (AI) to determine the quality of its customer service calls. The company currently manages calls in four different languages, including English. The company will offer new languages in the future. The company does not have the resources to regularly maintain machine learning (ML) models.

The company needs to create written sentiment analysis reports from the customer service call recordings. The customer service call recording text must be translated into English.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

o.A: Use Amazon Comprehend to translate the audio recordings into English.
o.B: Use Amazon Lex to create the written sentiment analysis reports.
o.C: Use Amazon Polly to convert the audio recordings into text.
o.D: Use Amazon Transcribe to convert the audio recordings in any language into text.
o.E: Use Amazon Translate to translate text in any language to English.
o.F: Use Amazon Comprehend to create the sentiment analysis reports.

e.why: Amazon Transcribe converts the call recordings to text (with automatic language identification). Amazon Translate translates that text into English. Amazon Comprehend performs sentiment analysis to produce the reports. All three are fully managed AI services, so no ML models need maintaining.

others.A: Amazon Comprehend analyzes text; it does not translate audio.
others.B: Amazon Lex builds conversational chatbots and does not perform sentiment analysis reporting.
others.C: Amazon Polly converts text to speech, the opposite of what is needed.

e.tip: Speech to text = Transcribe; text to speech = Polly; translation = Translate; sentiment = Comprehend.

o.A: The EC2 instance has a resource-based policy with a Deny statement.
o.B: The principal has not been specified in the policy statement.
o.C: The "Action" field does not grant the actions that are required to terminate the EC2 instance.
o.D: The request to terminate the EC2 instance does not originate from the CIDR blocks 192.0.2.0/24 or 203.0.113.0/24.

fixed: The IAM policy JSON was missing from the question and has been reconstructed.

e.why: The policy allows ec2:TerminateInstances, but an explicit Deny blocks the action when the request does not come from 192.0.2.0/24 or 203.0.113.0/24. The administrator's request came from another IP address, so the Deny applied and returned 403.

others.A: EC2 instances do not support resource-based policies.
others.B: Identity-based policies attached to a role do not include a Principal element; the principal is the role itself.
others.C: The Action field does grant ec2:TerminateInstances; the request fails because of the Deny condition.

e.tip: For an Access Denied puzzle, look for an explicit Deny with a condition such as NotIpAddress.

q:
A company is conducting an internal audit. The company wants to ensure that the data in an Amazon S3 bucket that is associated with the company’s AWS Lake Formation data lake does not contain sensitive customer or employee data. The company wants to discover personally identifiable information (PII) or financial information, including passport numbers and credit card numbers.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure AWS Audit Manager on the account. Select the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS) for auditing.
o.B: Configure Amazon S3 Inventory on the S3 bucket Configure Amazon Athena to query the inventory.
o.C: Configure Amazon Macie to run a data discovery job that uses managed identifiers for the required data types.
o.D: Use Amazon S3 Select to run a report across the S3 bucket.

e.why: Amazon Macie uses managed data identifiers to discover sensitive data in S3, such as passport numbers, credit card numbers and other PII. A sensitive data discovery job on the data lake bucket produces findings that show where this data is.

others.A: Audit Manager collects evidence for compliance frameworks but does not scan S3 object contents for PII.
others.B: S3 Inventory lists object metadata, not object contents.
others.D: S3 Select queries one object at a time with SQL; it has no PII detection.

e.tip: Find PII in S3 = Macie.

q:
A company uses on-premises servers to host its applications. The company is running out of storage capacity. The applications use both block storage and NFS storage. The company needs a high-performing solution that supports local caching without re-architecting its existing applications.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Mount Amazon S3 as a file system to the on-premises servers.
o.B: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway to replace NFS storage.
o.C: Deploy AWS Snowball Edge to provision NFS mounts to on-premises servers.
o.D: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway to replace the block storage.
o.E: Deploy Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volumes and mount them to on-premises servers.

e.why: An S3 File Gateway replaces the NFS storage with NFS shares backed by S3 and caches frequently used data locally. A Volume Gateway in cached mode replaces the block storage with iSCSI volumes backed by AWS, with local caching. Neither requires re-architecting the applications.

others.A: S3 cannot be mounted natively as a file system on servers, and doing so with third-party tools gives no local caching.
others.C: Snowball Edge is for data transfer or edge computing, not ongoing hybrid storage expansion.
others.E: Mounting EFS from on premises gives no local caching and adds WAN latency.

e.tip: Storage Gateway types: S3 File (NFS/SMB to S3), FSx File (SMB), Volume (iSCSI block), Tape (VTL).

q:
A company has a service that reads and writes large amounts of data from an Amazon S3 bucket in the same AWS Region. The service is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances within the private subnet of a VPC. The service communicates with Amazon S3 over a NAT gateway in the public subnet. However, the company wants a solution that will reduce the data output costs.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the public subnet. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 traffic.
o.B: Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the private subnet. Configure the route table for the public subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 traffic.
o.C: Provision a VPC gateway endpoint. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the gateway endpoint as the route for all S3 traffic.
o.D: Provision a second NAT gateway. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use this NAT gateway as the destination for all S3 traffic.

e.why: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint is free and sends S3 traffic from the private subnet over the AWS network through a route table entry. That removes NAT gateway hourly and per-GB processing charges for this heavy traffic, so it is the most cost-effective fix.

others.A: A NAT instance still has instance and management costs, and S3 traffic still leaves through public endpoints.
others.B: A NAT instance must sit in a public subnet, and routing the public subnet through it makes no sense.
others.D: A second NAT gateway adds more hourly and data processing charges.

e.tip: NAT gateway costs for S3 or DynamoDB traffic = add gateway endpoints.

q:
A company uses Amazon S3 to store high-resolution pictures in an S3 bucket. To minimize application changes, the company stores the pictures as the latest version of an S3 object. The company needs to retain only the two most recent versions of the pictures.

The company wants to reduce costs. The company has identified the S3 bucket as a large expense.

Which solution will reduce the S3 costs with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use S3 Lifecycle to delete expired object versions and retain the two most recent versions.
o.B: Use an AWS Lambda function to check for older versions and delete all but the two most recent versions.
o.C: Use S3 Batch Operations to delete noncurrent object versions and retain only the two most recent versions.
o.D: Deactivate versioning on the S3 bucket and retain the two most recent versions.

e.why: S3 Lifecycle noncurrent version expiration can keep a set number of newer noncurrent versions (NewerNoncurrentVersions) and permanently delete older ones automatically. That retains the latest versions and cuts storage cost with no code to run.

others.B: A custom Lambda function to list and delete versions must be built, scheduled and maintained.
others.C: Batch Operations jobs need manifests and repeated manual runs, and they have no built-in way to keep N versions.
others.D: Versioning cannot be turned off once enabled, only suspended, and suspending it would break the version-based design.

e.tip: Keep the last N versions = lifecycle rule with NewerNoncurrentVersions.

q:
A company needs to minimize the cost of its 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection. The company's average connection utilization is less than 10%. A solutions architect must recommend a solution that will reduce the cost without compromising security.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Set up a new 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.
o.B: Set up a new 200 Mbps Direct Connect connection in the AWS Management Console.
o.C: Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 1 Gbps connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.
o.D: Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 200 Mbps hosted connection for an existing AWS account.

e.why: With under 10 percent of 1 Gbps in use (under 100 Mbps), a 200 Mbps hosted connection from a Direct Connect Partner costs much less. It is still a private, dedicated-capacity link, so security is not compromised.

others.A: A new 1 Gbps connection keeps the same oversized capacity, and sharing it with another account raises security concerns.
others.B: Speeds below 1 Gbps (like 200 Mbps) are available only as hosted connections through Partners, not ordered as dedicated connections in the console.
others.C: Ordering another 1 Gbps connection does not lower the cost of unused bandwidth.

e.tip: Dedicated connections: 1, 10, 100 Gbps. Sub-1 Gbps speeds = hosted connection through a Partner.

q:
A company has multiple Windows file servers on premises. The company wants to migrate and consolidate its files into an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. File permissions must be preserved to ensure that access rights do not change.

Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Deploy AWS DataSync agents on premises. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
o.B: Copy the shares on each file server into Amazon S3 buckets by using the AWS CLI. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
o.C: Remove the drives from each file server. Ship the drives to AWS for import into Amazon S3. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
o.D: Order an AWS Snowcone device. Connect the device to the on-premises network. Launch AWS DataSync agents on the device. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
o.E: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Connect the device to the on-premises network. Copy data to the device by using the AWS CLI. Ship the device back to AWS for import into Amazon S3. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.

e.why: AWS DataSync can copy SMB data straight into FSx for Windows File Server and preserves NTFS permissions (ACLs), timestamps and metadata. You can run DataSync agents on premises, or on a Snowcone device that runs the DataSync agent, and transfer to FSx online.

others.B: Copying to S3 with the CLI loses Windows ACLs, so permissions cannot be restored in FSx.
others.C: AWS does not offer an import service for raw drives shipped to it, and S3 would not keep NTFS permissions.
others.E: Copying to Snowball with the AWS CLI puts the files in S3 as objects and loses the NTFS ACLs.

e.tip: Keep Windows ACLs when moving to FSx = DataSync (SMB to FSx).

q:
A company wants to ingest customer payment data into the company's data lake in Amazon S3. The company receives payment data every minute on average. The company wants to analyze the payment data in real time. Then the company wants to ingest the data into the data lake.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.
o.B: Use AWS Glue to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.
o.C: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.
o.D: Use Amazon API Gateway to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.

e.why: Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed ingestion service that delivers directly to S3, with no shards to manage. Kinesis Data Analytics (now Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink) can analyze the stream in real time, which together gives the most operational efficiency.

others.A: Kinesis Data Streams requires managing shards, and writing to S3 requires extra code or a Firehose delivery stream.
others.B: AWS Glue is an ETL service for batch or streaming jobs, not a simple real-time ingestion endpoint.
others.D: API Gateway plus Lambda means custom code for ingestion, analysis and writing to S3.

e.tip: Stream into S3 with no management = Firehose; real-time SQL or Flink = Managed Service for Apache Flink.

q:
A company runs a website that uses a content management system (CMS) on Amazon EC2. The CMS runs on a single EC2 instance and uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance for the data tier. Website images are stored on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that is mounted inside the EC2 instance.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to improve the performance and resilience of the website? (Choose two.)

o.A: Move the website images into an Amazon S3 bucket that is mounted on every EC2 instance
o.B: Share the website images by using an NFS share from the primary EC2 instance. Mount this share on the other EC2 instances.
o.C: Move the website images onto an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that is mounted on every EC2 instance.
o.D: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator for the website
o.E: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the website.

e.why: Moving images to Amazon EFS gives a shared file system that every instance can mount. An AMI-based Auto Scaling group with at least two instances behind an ALB removes the single instance as a point of failure. CloudFront caches images and pages at the edge for better performance.

others.A: S3 cannot be natively mounted as a file system on EC2 for a CMS that expects file storage.
others.B: An NFS share served from one primary instance is still a single point of failure.
others.D: Global Accelerator speeds up TCP/UDP routing but does not cache content, so CloudFront suits a website better.

q:
A company runs an infrastructure monitoring service. The company is building a new feature that will enable the service to monitor data in customer AWS accounts. The new feature will call AWS APIs in customer accounts to describe Amazon EC2 instances and read Amazon CloudWatch metrics.

What should the company do to obtain access to customer accounts in the MOST secure way?

o.A: Ensure that the customers create an IAM role in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions and a trust policy to the company’s account.
o.B: Create a serverless API that implements a token vending machine to provide temporary AWS credentials for a role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions.
o.C: Ensure that the customers create an IAM user in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions. Encrypt and store customer access and secret keys in a secrets management system.
o.D: Ensure that the customers create an Amazon Cognito user in their account to use an IAM role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions. Encrypt and store the Amazon Cognito user and password in a secrets management system.

e.why: The secure cross-account pattern has each customer create an IAM role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions and a trust policy for the company's account, ideally with an external ID. The company assumes the role with STS to get temporary credentials, so no long-term secrets are shared.

others.B: A token vending machine cannot mint credentials in customer accounts without access to them first, and it is complex custom infrastructure.
others.C: Storing customers' long-term IAM user access keys is risky even when encrypted.
others.D: Cognito is for app end-user identity, not cross-account access to AWS APIs, and storing passwords is insecure.

e.tip: Third-party cross-account access = IAM role + external ID (guards against the confused deputy problem).

q:
A company needs to connect several VPCs in the us-east-1 Region that span hundreds of AWS accounts. The company's networking team has its own AWS account to manage the cloud network.

What is the MOST operationally efficient solution to connect the VPCs?

o.A: Set up VPC peering connections between each VPC. Update each associated subnet’s route table.
o.B: Configure a NAT gateway and an internet gateway in each VPC to connect each VPC through the internet.
o.C: Create an AWS Transit Gateway in the networking team’s AWS account. Configure static routes from each VPC.
o.D: Deploy VPN gateways in each VPC. Create a transit VPC in the networking team’s AWS account to connect to each VPC.

fixed: Option C showed the answer key instead of its text and has been reconstructed; options A and D were truncated and have been completed.

e.why: A transit gateway in the networking team's account can be shared with all other accounts through AWS RAM, and every VPC attaches to it in a hub-and-spoke design. This removes the need to manage a mesh of connections across hundreds of accounts.

others.A: A full mesh of VPC peering connections for hundreds of VPCs is very hard to manage.
others.B: Connecting VPCs over the internet through NAT and internet gateways is insecure and does not give private VPC-to-VPC routing.
others.D: A transit VPC with VPN gateways is a legacy design with far more operational work than Transit Gateway.

e.tip: Many VPCs across many accounts in one Region: share a Transit Gateway with AWS RAM.

q:
A company has Amazon EC2 instances that run nightly batch jobs to process data. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group that uses On-Demand billing. If a job fails on one instance, another instance will reprocess the job. The batch jobs run between 12:00 AM and 06:00 AM local time every day.

Which solution will provide EC2 instances to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Purchase a 1-year Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 that covers the instance family of the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
o.B: Purchase a 1-year Reserved Instance for the specific instance type and operating system of the instances in the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
o.C: Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Set the instances to Spot Instances. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.
o.D: Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Increase the instance size. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.

e.why: The batch jobs tolerate interruption, since a failed job is retried on another instance, and they run only 6 hours a night. Spot Instances give up to 90 percent savings for this fault-tolerant, part-time workload, and using them in the Auto Scaling group's launch template is the cheapest option.

others.A: A Savings Plan commits to spending 24 hours a day, but the instances run only 6 hours a day.
others.B: A Reserved Instance bills around the clock for capacity used only a quarter of the day.
others.D: Larger On-Demand instances cost more and add no savings.

e.tip: Interruptible and retryable = Spot.

q:
A social media company is building a feature for its website. The feature will give users the ability to upload photos. The company expects significant increases in demand during large events and must ensure that the website can handle the upload traffic from users.

Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST scalability?

o.A: Upload files from the user's browser to the application servers. Transfer the files to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.B: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file gateway.
o.C: Generate Amazon S3 presigned URLs in the application. Upload files directly from the user's browser into an S3 bucket.
o.D: Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file system.

e.why: Presigned URLs let browsers upload directly to S3 using temporary, limited permissions. S3 scales automatically to very high request rates, and the application servers are taken out of the upload data path, which gives the most scalability during event spikes.

others.A: Routing uploads through application servers makes them a bottleneck that must scale with the upload traffic.
others.B: Storage Gateway is for hybrid access from on premises, and browsers cannot upload to it directly.
others.D: Browsers cannot write to an EFS file system directly; it must be mounted by compute resources.

q:
A company has a web application for travel ticketing. The application is based on a database that runs in a single data center in North America. The company wants to expand the application to serve a global user base. The company needs to deploy the application to multiple AWS Regions. Average latency must be less than 1 second on updates to the reservation database.

The company wants to have separate deployments of its web platform across multiple Regions. However, the company must maintain a single primary reservation database that is globally consistent.

Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Convert the application to use Amazon DynamoDB. Use a global table for the center reservation table. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment.
o.B: Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Deploy Aurora Read Replicas in each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment for access to the database.
o.C: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Deploy MySQL read replicas in each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment for access to the database.
o.D: Migrate the application to an Amazon Aurora Serverless database. Deploy instances of the database to each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment to access the database. Use AWS Lambda functions to process event streams in each Region to synchronize the databases.

fixed: Option A was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: DynamoDB global tables give a multi-Region, multi-active database where every Regional deployment can read and write locally and data replicates automatically. This meets the need for separate Regional deployments that share one reservation table.

others.B: Aurora cross-Region read replicas are read-only, so other Regions must still send writes to the primary Region.
others.C: RDS for MySQL read replicas in other Regions are also read-only and replicate asynchronously.
others.D: Separate Aurora Serverless databases kept in sync with custom Lambda code are complex and not globally consistent.

e.tip: Multi-Region reads and writes with low effort usually points to DynamoDB global tables. The community vote on this question is split with Aurora read replicas.

q:
A company has migrated multiple Microsoft Windows Server workloads to Amazon EC2 instances that run in the us-west-1 Region. The company manually backs up the workloads to create an image as needed.

In the event of a natural disaster in the us-west-1 Region, the company wants to recover workloads quickly in the us-west-2 Region. The company wants no more than 24 hours of data loss on the EC2 instances. The company also wants to automate any backups of the EC2 instances.

Which solutions will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily. Copy the image on demand.
o.B: Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily. Configure the copy to the us-west-2 Region.
o.C: Create backup vaults in us-west-1 and in us-west-2 by using AWS Backup. Create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Create an AWS Lambda function to run as a scheduled job to copy the backup data to us-west-2.
o.D: Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Define the destination for the copy as us-west-2. Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily.
o.E: Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily. Copy on demand to us-west-2.

e.why: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager EBS-backed AMI policies can create AMIs by tag on a schedule (twice a day) and copy them to us-west-2 automatically. AWS Backup plans by tag can likewise back up twice daily with a cross-Region copy to a vault in us-west-2. Both meet the 24-hour RPO with full automation.

others.A: Copying images on demand is manual, so DR copies are not automated.
others.C: A custom Lambda function to copy backups is unnecessary because AWS Backup has built-in cross-Region copy rules.
others.E: Copying on demand to us-west-2 is manual and goes against the automation requirement.

q:
A company operates a two-tier application for image processing. The application uses two Availability Zones, each with one public subnet and one private subnet. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the web tier uses the public subnets. Amazon EC2 instances for the application tier use the private subnets.

Users report that the application is running more slowly than expected. A security audit of the web server log files shows that the application is receiving millions of illegitimate requests from a small number of IP addresses. A solutions architect needs to resolve the immediate performance problem while the company investigates a more permanent solution.

What should the solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

o.A: Modify the inbound security group for the web tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
o.B: Modify the network ACL for the web tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
o.C: Modify the inbound security group for the application tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
o.D: Modify the network ACL for the application tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.

e.why: Network ACLs support explicit deny rules. Adding inbound deny rules for the few attacking IP addresses on the web tier (ALB) subnets drops their traffic before it reaches the load balancer, which immediately eases the performance problem.

others.A: Security groups do not support deny rules.
others.C: Security groups cannot deny, and the app tier only sees traffic from the ALB, not the client IPs.
others.D: The application tier subnets receive traffic from the ALB's private IPs, so denying client IPs there has no effect.

e.tip: Block specific IPs fast = NACL deny (or WAF IP set); security groups cannot deny.

q:
A global marketing company has applications that run in the ap-southeast-2 Region and the eu-west-1 Region. Applications that run in a VPC in eu-west-1 need to communicate securely with databases that run in a VPC in ap-southeast-2.

Which network design will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a VPC peering connection between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. Create an inbound rule in the eu-west-1 application security group that allows traffic from the database server IP addresses in the ap-southeast-2 security group.
o.B: Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPC. Update the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.
o.C: Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPC. Update the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that allows traffic from the eu-west-1 application server IP addresses.
o.D: Create a transit gateway with a peering attachment between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. After the transit gateways are properly peered and routing is configured, create an inbound rule in the database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.

fixed: Option C contained the second half of option D; options A, B, C and D have been reconstructed.

e.why: The two VPCs are in different Regions, so VPC peering works, but a security group rule cannot reference a security group in a peered VPC in another Region. The database security group must therefore allow the application servers' IP addresses, and the subnet route tables must be updated for the peering connection.

others.A: The inbound rule must be on the database security group in ap-southeast-2, not on the application security group in eu-west-1.
others.B: Security group references across an inter-Region peering connection are not supported.
others.D: Security group references are also not supported across inter-Region transit gateway peering.

e.tip: Security group references work across peered VPCs only in the same Region; across Regions, use CIDR or IP rules.

q:
A company is developing software that uses a PostgreSQL database schema. The company needs to configure multiple development environments and databases for the company's developers. On average, each development environment is used for half of the 8-hour workday.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database
o.B: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instances
o.C: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-Compatible database
o.D: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon S3 Object Select

e.why: Aurora On-Demand, which here means Aurora Serverless for PostgreSQL, scales compute with use and can scale to zero or pause when idle, so you pay mostly for the half-day each environment is actually used. That makes it the most cost-effective option for intermittent development databases.

others.A: Provisioned Aurora instances bill every hour whether or not developers use them.
others.B: RDS Single-AZ instances also bill continuously unless someone stops and starts them by hand.
others.D: S3 Select is not a PostgreSQL database and cannot support the schema.

e.tip: Intermittent or dev/test relational workloads = Aurora Serverless v2 (supports auto-pause to zero).

q:
A company uses AWS Organizations with resources tagged by account. The company also uses AWS Backup to back up its AWS infrastructure resources. The company needs to back up all AWS resources.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Config to identify all untagged resources. Tag the identified resources programmatically. Use tags in the backup plan.
o.B: Use AWS Config to identify all resources that are not running. Add those resources to the backup vault.
o.C: Require all AWS account owners to review their resources to identify the resources that need to be backed up.
o.D: Use Amazon Inspector to identify all noncompliant resources.

e.why: AWS Backup plans can select resources by tag. Using AWS Config to find untagged resources and then tagging them programmatically brings every resource into the tag-based backup plan, so all resources are backed up with little ongoing effort.

others.B: Whether a resource is running has nothing to do with backup coverage, and resources are not added to vaults directly.
others.C: Manual reviews by every account owner have high overhead and are error-prone.
others.D: Amazon Inspector scans for vulnerabilities and does not identify resources for backup.

q:
A social media company wants to allow its users to upload images in an application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs a solution that automatically resizes the images so that the images can be displayed on multiple device types. The application experiences unpredictable traffic patterns throughout the day. The company is seeking a highly available solution that maximizes scalability.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a static website hosted in Amazon S3 that invokes AWS Lambda functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.B: Create a static website hosted in Amazon CloudFront that invokes AWS Step Functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon RDS database.
o.C: Create a dynamic website hosted on a web server that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Configure a process that runs on the EC2 instance to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.D: Create a dynamic website hosted on an automatically scaling Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that creates a resize job in Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Set up an image-resizing program that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance to process the resize jobs.

e.why: A static site on Amazon S3 plus AWS Lambda for resizing is fully serverless: S3 is highly available across multiple AZs and Lambda scales automatically per upload, which handles unpredictable traffic and maximizes scalability. Resized images are stored back in S3, which is cheap and durable for object storage.

others.B: CloudFront does not host or execute a website by itself and storing images in Amazon RDS is a poor fit for binary objects.
others.C: A single EC2 instance is a single point of failure and does not scale automatically with unpredictable traffic.
others.D: Processing resize jobs on a single EC2 instance limits scalability and adds operational overhead compared with Lambda.

e.tip: Image upload plus transform with unpredictable traffic: S3 event notification to Lambda, results back to S3.

q:
A company is running a microservices application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to migrate the application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for scalability. The company must configure the Amazon EKS control plane with endpoint private access set to true and endpoint public access set to false to maintain security compliance. The company must also put the data plane in private subnets. However, the company has received error notifications because the node cannot join the cluster.

Which solution will allow the node to join the cluster?

o.A: Grant the required permission in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to the AmazonEKSNodeRole IAM role.
o.B: Create interface VPC endpoints to allow nodes to access the control plane.
o.C: Recreate nodes in the public subnet. Restrict security groups for EC2 nodes.
o.D: Allow outbound traffic in the security group of the nodes.

e.why: With a private-only EKS API endpoint and nodes in private subnets without internet access, nodes must reach AWS services such as Amazon ECR, Amazon EC2, Amazon S3 and AWS STS privately. Creating interface VPC endpoints (plus the S3 gateway endpoint) lets the nodes pull images and register with the cluster without leaving the VPC.

others.A: The node IAM role permissions are standard managed policies; the issue here is network reachability to required AWS service endpoints, not IAM.
others.C: Moving nodes to public subnets violates the compliance requirement that the data plane stays private.
others.D: Security groups allow all outbound by default; without a route or endpoint to AWS services, opening egress rules alone does not help.

e.tip: Private EKS cluster without NAT: add VPC endpoints for ECR (api and dkr), S3, EC2, STS and CloudWatch Logs.

q:
A company is migrating an on-premises application to AWS. The company wants to use Amazon Redshift as a solution.

Which use cases are suitable for Amazon Redshift in this scenario? (Choose three.)

o.A: Supporting data APIs to access data with traditional, containerized, and event-driven applications
o.B: Supporting client-side and server-side encryption
o.C: Building analytics workloads during specified hours and when the application is not active
o.D: Caching data to reduce the pressure on the backend database
o.E: Scaling globally to support petabytes of data and tens of millions of requests per minute
o.F: Creating a secondary replica of the cluster by using the AWS Management Console

e.why: Amazon Redshift supports encryption at rest with AWS KMS or HSM and client-side encryption of loaded data (B), it is built for analytics and BI workloads that can run on a schedule or with pause/resume when the app is idle (C), and it scales to petabytes of data with concurrency scaling and RA3 managed storage (E).

others.A: Serving low-latency data APIs to transactional, containerized and event-driven applications is an OLTP pattern better met by DynamoDB or Aurora, not a data warehouse.
others.D: Caching to offload a backend database is the job of ElastiCache or DAX, not Redshift.
others.F: Redshift has no console feature to create a secondary read replica of a cluster; resilience comes from snapshots, cross-Region snapshot copy and Multi-AZ.

e.tip: Redshift = OLAP data warehouse; caching = ElastiCache; replicas are an RDS/Aurora concept.

q:
A company provides an API interface to customers so the customers can retrieve their financial information. Еhe company expects a larger number of requests during peak usage times of the year.

The company requires the API to respond consistently with low latency to ensure customer satisfaction. The company needs to provide a compute host for the API.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use an Application Load Balancer and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).
o.B: Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency.
o.C: Use an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster.
o.D: Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with reserved concurrency.

e.why: API Gateway with AWS Lambda is serverless, so there is no cluster or host to manage, giving the least operational overhead. Provisioned concurrency keeps a set number of execution environments pre-initialized, eliminating cold starts so latency stays consistently low during peak periods.

others.A: ALB with ECS requires managing tasks, capacity and scaling policies, which is more overhead than Lambda.
others.C: An EKS cluster adds significant operational overhead for Kubernetes management.
others.D: Reserved concurrency only caps or guarantees a share of concurrency; it does not pre-warm environments, so cold starts can still add latency.

e.tip: Provisioned concurrency = no cold starts; reserved concurrency = concurrency limit/guarantee.

q:
A company wants to send all AWS Systems Manager Session Manager logs to an Amazon S3 bucket for archival purposes.

Which solution will meet this requirement with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Enable S3 logging in the Systems Manager console. Choose an S3 bucket to send the session data to.
o.B: Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Export the logs to an S3 bucket from the group for archival purposes.
o.C: Create a Systems Manager document to upload all server logs to a central S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge to run the Systems Manager document against all servers that are in the account daily.
o.D: Install an Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Create a CloudWatch logs subscription that pushes any incoming log events to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Set Amazon S3 as the destination.

e.why: Session Manager has built-in session logging: in the Session Manager preferences you can enable S3 logging and choose a bucket (optionally encrypted), and session data is uploaded automatically. This needs no agents, pipelines or scheduled jobs, so it is the most operationally efficient.

others.B: Installing the CloudWatch agent and exporting log groups to S3 is manual and adds steps; exports are not continuous.
others.C: A custom SSM document run daily by EventBridge is extra custom work and does not capture session data specifically.
others.D: CloudWatch agent plus subscription filter plus Firehose works but is much more infrastructure than the native S3 logging option.

q:
An application uses an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. The RDS database is becoming low on disk space. A solutions architect wants to increase the disk space without downtime.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?

o.A: Enable storage autoscaling in RDS
o.B: Increase the RDS database instance size
o.C: Change the RDS database instance storage type to Provisioned IOPS
o.D: Back up the RDS database, increase the storage capacity, restore the database, and stop the previous instance

e.why: RDS storage autoscaling automatically increases allocated storage when free space runs low, with no downtime and no ongoing manual effort once enabled. This directly solves the low disk space problem with the least effort.

others.B: Changing the instance class changes CPU and memory, not storage, and usually causes a brief outage.
others.C: Switching to Provisioned IOPS changes performance characteristics, not capacity, and does not address running out of space.
others.D: Backup, restore and cutover involves downtime and far more effort.

e.tip: RDS low on storage with no downtime: enable storage autoscaling with a maximum storage threshold.

q:
A consulting company provides professional services to customers worldwide. The company provides solutions and tools for customers to expedite gathering and analyzing data on AWS. The company needs to centrally manage and deploy a common set of solutions and tools for customers to use for self-service purposes.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create AWS CloudFormation templates for the customers.
o.B: Create AWS Service Catalog products for the customers.
o.C: Create AWS Systems Manager templates for the customers.
o.D: Create AWS Config items for the customers.

e.why: AWS Service Catalog lets an organization centrally create, manage and distribute approved portfolios of products (backed by CloudFormation templates) that end users can launch on a self-service basis with governance controls. That matches centrally managing and deploying a common set of solutions for customer self-service.

others.A: Raw CloudFormation templates can be shared but provide no central catalog, versioning governance or self-service portal.
others.C: Systems Manager documents automate operational tasks on instances, not distribution of solution products.
others.D: AWS Config items record resource configuration state; they do not deploy solutions.

e.tip: Self-service, centrally approved products = AWS Service Catalog.

q:
A company is designing a new web application that will run on Amazon EC2 Instances. The application will use Amazon DynamoDB for backend data storage. The application traffic will be unpredictable. The company expects that the application read and write throughput to the database will be moderate to high. The company needs to scale in response to application traffic.

Which DynamoDB table configuration will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
o.B: Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard table class.
o.C: Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
o.D: Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class.

e.why: On-demand capacity mode scales instantly with unpredictable traffic and you pay only per request, avoiding over-provisioning or throttling during spikes. The Standard table class is the cost-effective choice when throughput is moderate to high, since Standard-IA lowers storage cost but raises per-request cost.

others.A: Provisioned with auto scaling reacts slowly to sudden spikes and suits predictable traffic; unpredictable traffic favors on-demand.
others.C: Standard-IA is meant for storage-heavy, rarely accessed tables; with moderate to high throughput it costs more, and provisioned mode fits unpredictable traffic poorly.
others.D: Standard-IA has higher read and write request pricing, which is more expensive for a moderate to high throughput workload.

e.tip: Unpredictable traffic = on-demand; Standard-IA only when storage dominates cost.

q:
A retail company has several businesses. The IT team for each business manages its own AWS account. Each team account is part of an organization in AWS Organizations. Each team monitors its product inventory levels in an Amazon DynamoDB table in the team's own AWS account.

The company is deploying a central inventory reporting application into a shared AWS account. The application must be able to read items from all the teams' DynamoDB tables.

Which authentication option will meet these requirements MOST securely?

o.A: Integrate DynamoDB with AWS Secrets Manager in the inventory application account. Configure the application to use the correct secret from Secrets Manager to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table. Schedule secret rotation for every 30 days.
o.B: In every business account, create an IAM user that has programmatic access. Configure the application to use the correct IAM user access key ID and secret access key to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table. Manually rotate IAM access keys every 30 days.
o.C: In every business account, create an IAM role named BU_ROLE with a policy that gives the role access to the DynamoDB table and a trust policy to trust a specific role in the inventory application account. In the inventory account, create a role named APP_ROLE that allows access to the STS AssumeRole API operation. Configure the application to use APP_ROLE and assume the crossaccount role BU_ROLE to read the DynamoDB table.
o.D: Integrate DynamoDB with AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Generate identity certificates to authenticate DynamoDB. Configure the application to use the correct certificate to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table.

fixed: Option B contained the end of option D instead of its own text and has been reconstructed; option D was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: Cross-account IAM roles give temporary credentials through STS AssumeRole. Each business account trusts a specific role in the inventory account, so the application can read every team's table without any long-term secrets.

others.A: DynamoDB does not authenticate with secrets from Secrets Manager; access is controlled by IAM.
others.B: IAM users with long-term access keys that are rotated by hand are less secure than temporary role credentials.
others.D: DynamoDB does not support authentication with ACM certificates.

e.tip: Cross-account access, most securely: IAM roles with a trust policy and STS AssumeRole.

q:
A company runs container applications by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The company's workload is not consistent throughout the day. The company wants Amazon EKS to scale in and out according to the workload.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use an AWS Lambda function to resize the EKS cluster.
o.B: Use the Kubernetes Metrics Server to activate horizontal pod autoscaling.
o.C: Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to manage the number of nodes in the cluster.
o.D: Use Amazon API Gateway and connect it to Amazon EKS.
o.E: Use AWS App Mesh to observe network activity.

e.why: The Kubernetes Metrics Server supplies CPU and memory metrics so the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler can add or remove pods based on load, and the Cluster Autoscaler adds or removes worker nodes when pods are unschedulable or nodes are underused. Together they scale both pods and nodes with standard, low-overhead tooling.

others.A: A custom Lambda to resize the cluster is bespoke code that adds operational overhead.
others.D: API Gateway is for exposing APIs and does not scale EKS capacity.
others.E: App Mesh provides service mesh observability and traffic control, not autoscaling.

e.tip: EKS scaling: HPA (with Metrics Server) for pods, Cluster Autoscaler or Karpenter for nodes.

q:
A company runs a microservice-based serverless web application. The application must be able to retrieve data from multiple Amazon DynamoDB tables A solutions architect needs to give the application the ability to retrieve the data with no impact on the baseline performance of the application.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.A: AWS AppSync pipeline resolvers
o.B: Amazon CloudFront with Lambda@Edge functions
o.C: Edge-optimized Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions
o.D: Amazon Athena Federated Query with a DynamoDB connector

e.why: AWS AppSync pipeline resolvers execute an ordered sequence of functions that can read from multiple DynamoDB tables in a single GraphQL request, as a fully managed serverless service. The data retrieval is handled by AppSync rather than the application code, so baseline application performance is not affected and operational effort is minimal.

others.B: Lambda@Edge is for customizing CloudFront requests and responses at the edge, not for aggregating data from multiple DynamoDB tables.
others.C: API Gateway with Lambda works but requires writing and maintaining custom aggregation code; edge-optimized endpoints do not help data retrieval.
others.D: Athena Federated Query is for ad hoc analytic SQL and has seconds-level latency, unsuitable for application requests.

e.tip: Combine multiple data sources in one API call serverlessly: AppSync (GraphQL) resolvers.

q:
A company wants to analyze and troubleshoot Access Denied errors and Unauthorized errors that are related to IAM permissions. The company has AWS CloudTrail turned on.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?

o.A: Use AWS Glue and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
o.B: Use AWS Batch and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
o.C: Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon Athena queries to identify the errors.
