o.D: Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon QuickSight. Create a dashboard to identify the errors.

e.why: Amazon Athena can query CloudTrail logs in S3 directly with SQL (the CloudTrail console can even create the Athena table), so you can filter on errorCode values such as AccessDenied and UnauthorizedOperation without building anything. It is serverless and needs only queries, giving the least effort.

others.A: Writing AWS Glue custom scripts is more development effort than SQL queries in Athena.
others.B: AWS Batch with custom scripts requires building and managing compute jobs, which is far more effort.
others.D: QuickSight is a visualization tool and would still need a query layer such as Athena; building dashboards is extra effort.

e.tip: Ad hoc SQL over logs in S3 (CloudTrail, ALB, VPC Flow Logs) = Athena.

q:
A company wants to add its existing AWS usage cost to its operation cost dashboard. A solutions architect needs to recommend a solution that will give the company access to its usage cost programmatically. The company must be able to access cost data for the current year and forecast costs for the next 12 months.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Access usage cost-related data by using the AWS Cost Explorer API with pagination.
o.B: Access usage cost-related data by using downloadable AWS Cost Explorer report .csv files.
o.C: Configure AWS Budgets actions to send usage cost data to the company through FTP.
o.D: Create AWS Budgets reports for usage cost data. Send the data to the company through SMTP.

e.why: The AWS Cost Explorer API provides programmatic access to historical cost and usage data (GetCostAndUsage) and forecasts up to 12 months ahead (GetCostForecast), with pagination for large result sets. It can feed a dashboard directly with no extra infrastructure, so it has the least operational overhead.

others.B: Downloading CSV reports is manual and not programmatic.
others.C: AWS Budgets actions apply controls such as IAM or SCP policies when thresholds are reached; they do not send cost data over FTP.
others.D: Budgets reports are emailed summaries, not programmatic access, and they do not provide full 12-month forecasts for a dashboard.

e.tip: Programmatic cost data and forecasts = Cost Explorer API.

q:
A solutions architect is reviewing the resilience of an application. The solutions architect notices that a database administrator recently failed over the application's Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database writer instance as part of a scaling exercise. The failover resulted in 3 minutes of downtime for the application.

Which solution will reduce the downtime for scaling exercises with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create more Aurora PostgreSQL read replicas in the cluster to handle the load during failover.
o.B: Set up a secondary Aurora PostgreSQL cluster in the same AWS Region. During failover, update the application to use the secondary cluster's writer endpoint.
o.C: Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to handle the load during failover.
o.D: Set up an Amazon RDS proxy for the database. Update the application to use the proxy endpoint.

e.why: Amazon RDS Proxy keeps a pool of database connections and, during an Aurora failover, routes to the new writer without relying on DNS propagation, cutting failover time by up to 66 percent. The application only needs to switch to the proxy endpoint, so it is the lowest-overhead way to reduce downtime.

others.A: More read replicas give more failover targets but do not reduce the DNS and connection reestablishment delay that causes the downtime.
others.B: A second cluster with manual endpoint switching adds cost, replication complexity and more downtime risk.
others.C: An ElastiCache cache can serve some reads but cannot accept writes during the writer failover and adds caching logic.

e.tip: Faster failover and connection pooling for RDS or Aurora = RDS Proxy.

q:
A company has a regional subscription-based streaming service that runs in a single AWS Region. The architecture consists of web servers and application servers on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in Auto Scaling groups behind Elastic Load Balancers. The architecture includes an Amazon Aurora global database cluster that extends across multiple Availability Zones.

The company wants to expand globally and to ensure that its application has minimal downtime.

Which solution will provide the MOST fault tolerance?

o.A: Extend the Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and the application tier to deploy instances in Availability Zones in a second Region. Use an Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.
o.B: Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Add an Aurora PostgreSQL cross-Region Aurora Replica in the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.
o.C: Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Create an Aurora PostgreSQL database in the second Region. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the primary database to the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.
o.D: Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Use an Amazon Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.

e.why: Deploying the web and application tiers in a second Region, using an Aurora global database with storage-level replication (typically under 1 second lag) to that Region, and Route 53 failover routing gives full Regional redundancy. If the primary Region fails, the secondary cluster is promoted to primary, providing the most fault tolerance.

others.A: An Auto Scaling group is a Regional construct and cannot span Availability Zones in a second Region.
others.B: Aurora PostgreSQL does not support standalone cross-Region read replicas; cross-Region replication for it is through Aurora global database.
others.C: AWS DMS replication adds lag and operational overhead and is less resilient than native Aurora global database replication.

e.tip: Multi-Region Aurora with fast recovery = Aurora Global Database plus Route 53 failover.

q:
A data analytics company wants to migrate its batch processing system to AWS. The company receives thousands of small data files periodically during the day through FTP. An on-premises batch job processes the data files overnight. However, the batch job takes hours to finish running.

The company wants the AWS solution to process incoming data files as soon as possible with minimal changes to the FTP clients that send the files. The solution must delete the incoming data files after the files have been processed successfully. Processing for each file needs to take 3-8 minutes.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.A: Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files as objects in Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the objects nightly from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Delete the objects after the job has processed the objects.
o.B: Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the files nightly from the EBS volume. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.
o.C: Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use an Amazon S3 event notification when each file arrives to invoke the job in AWS Batch. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.
o.D: Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files in Amazon S3 Standard. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the files and to delete the files after they are processed. Use an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function when the files arrive.

e.why: AWS Transfer Family provides a managed FTP endpoint that writes directly to Amazon S3, so FTP clients need minimal changes and there is no server to run. An S3 event notification invokes Lambda per file as soon as it arrives, and each 3-8 minute job fits within Lambda's 15-minute limit; the function deletes the object when done, making this the most operationally efficient.

others.A: A self-managed EC2 FTP server and nightly processing from Glacier Flexible Retrieval (which needs restores) defeats the goal of processing files as soon as possible.
others.B: A self-managed FTP server on EC2 with nightly batch processing keeps the delay and adds operational overhead.
others.C: Transfer Family stores files in S3 or EFS, not EBS, and S3 event notifications cannot fire for files on an EBS volume.

e.tip: Managed SFTP/FTP/FTPS into S3 = AWS Transfer Family; per-file processing under 15 minutes = S3 event to Lambda.

q:
A company is migrating its workloads to AWS. The company has transactional and sensitive data in its databases. The company wants to use AWS Cloud solutions to increase security and reduce operational overhead for the databases.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate the databases to Amazon EC2. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
o.B: Migrate the databases to Amazon RDS Configure encryption at rest.
o.C: Migrate the data to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Macie for data security and protection
o.D: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs for data security and protection.

e.why: Amazon RDS is a managed database service that handles patching, backups and high availability, reducing operational overhead for transactional databases. Enabling encryption at rest with AWS KMS protects the sensitive data in storage, backups, snapshots and replicas.

others.A: Self-managed databases on EC2 keep the full operational burden of patching, backups and HA.
others.C: Amazon S3 is object storage, not a transactional database, and Macie only discovers sensitive data rather than securing a database.
others.D: CloudWatch Logs is for monitoring and logging; it does not protect or encrypt the data.

q:
A company has an online gaming application that has TCP and UDP multiplayer gaming capabilities. The company uses Amazon Route 53 to point the application traffic to multiple Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in different AWS Regions. The company needs to improve application performance and decrease latency for the online game in preparation for user growth.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the NLBs. Increase the Cache-Control max-age parameter.
o.B: Replace the NLBs with Application Load Balancers (ALBs). Configure Route 53 to use latency-based routing.
o.C: Add AWS Global Accelerator in front of the NLBs. Configure a Global Accelerator endpoint to use the correct listener ports.
o.D: Add an Amazon API Gateway endpoint behind the NLBs. Enable API caching. Override method caching for the different stages.

e.why: AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs and routes TCP and UDP traffic from the nearest edge location over the AWS global backbone to the closest healthy NLB endpoint. This lowers latency and jitter for multiplayer gaming and supports both protocols on the configured listener ports.

others.A: CloudFront is an HTTP(S) caching CDN and does not accelerate generic UDP game traffic; caching does not apply to live game sessions.
others.B: ALBs only handle HTTP/HTTPS (layer 7) and cannot carry UDP traffic.
others.D: API Gateway handles HTTP/REST/WebSocket APIs, not raw TCP/UDP game traffic, and API caching does not help real-time play.

e.tip: Non-HTTP (UDP/TCP) global acceleration or static IPs = Global Accelerator; HTTP caching = CloudFront.

q:
A company needs to integrate with a third-party data feed. The data feed sends a webhook to notify an external service when new data is ready for consumption. A developer wrote an AWS Lambda function to retrieve data when the company receives a webhook callback. The developer must make the Lambda function available for the third party to call.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Create a function URL for the Lambda function. Provide the Lambda function URL to the third party for the webhook.
o.B: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the Lambda function. Provide the ALB URL to the third party for the webhook.
o.C: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Attach the topic to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SNS topic to the third party for the webhook.
o.D: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Attach the queue to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SQS queue to the third party for the webhook.

e.why: A Lambda function URL is a built-in dedicated HTTPS endpoint for a function that can be created in one step, with optional IAM or no auth plus CORS settings. The third party can POST the webhook directly to it, so no extra services need to be deployed or managed.

others.B: An ALB works but adds cost and infrastructure to manage for a single function endpoint.
others.C: SNS topics do not expose a public hostname that accepts arbitrary webhook HTTP calls; publishing requires signed AWS API requests.
others.D: SQS queues require authenticated AWS API calls and do not provide a simple public webhook URL.

e.tip: Simplest public HTTPS endpoint for one Lambda = function URL.

q:
A company has a workload in an AWS Region. Customers connect to and access the workload by using an Amazon API Gateway REST API. The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company wants to provide individual and secure URLs for all customers.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency? (Choose three.)

o.A: Register the required domain in a registrar. Create a wildcard custom domain name in a Route 53 hosted zone and record in the zone that points to the API Gateway endpoint.
o.B: Request a wildcard certificate that matches the domains in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in a different Region.
o.C: Create hosted zones for each customer as required in Route 53. Create zone records that point to the API Gateway endpoint.
o.D: Request a wildcard certificate that matches the custom domain name in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region.
o.E: Create multiple API endpoints for each customer in API Gateway.
o.F: Create a custom domain name in API Gateway for the REST API. Import the certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).

e.why: Registering the domain and creating a wildcard record (for example *.example.com) in a Route 53 hosted zone gives every customer its own subdomain without per-customer DNS work (A). A wildcard ACM certificate requested in the same Region as a Regional API (D) secures all subdomains, and an API Gateway custom domain name using that ACM certificate (F) maps the subdomains to the REST API.

others.B: For a Regional API endpoint the ACM certificate must be in the same Region as the API (only edge-optimized endpoints use us-east-1).
others.C: Creating a hosted zone per customer is unnecessary operational overhead when a wildcard record covers all customers.
others.E: Creating separate API endpoints for each customer multiplies management effort and is not needed for individual URLs.

e.tip: Per-customer subdomains: wildcard DNS record + wildcard ACM cert + API Gateway custom domain.

q:
A company stores data in Amazon S3. According to regulations, the data must not contain personally identifiable information (PII). The company recently discovered that S3 buckets have some objects that contain PII. The company needs to automatically detect PII in S3 buckets and to notify the company’s security team.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon Macie. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the SensitiveData event type from Macie findings and to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to the security team.
o.B: Use Amazon GuardDuty. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the CRITICAL event type from GuardDuty findings and to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to the security team.
o.C: Use Amazon Macie. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the SensitiveData:S3Object/Personal event type from Macie findings and to send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) notification to the security team.
o.D: Use Amazon GuardDuty. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the CRITICAL event type from GuardDuty findings and to send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) notification to the security team.

e.why: Amazon Macie uses managed data identifiers to automatically discover PII in S3 objects and publishes sensitive data findings to Amazon EventBridge. An EventBridge rule matching the SensitiveData finding types can target an SNS topic to email or notify the security team.

others.B: GuardDuty detects threats and anomalous activity, not PII content in S3 objects.
others.C: Macie is correct, but SQS is a queue for application consumers, not a notification mechanism for people.
others.D: GuardDuty does not detect PII, and SQS does not notify humans.

e.tip: PII in S3 = Macie; notifying people = SNS.

q:
A company wants to build a logging solution for its multiple AWS accounts. The company currently stores the logs from all accounts in a centralized account. The company has created an Amazon S3 bucket in the centralized account to store the VPC flow logs and AWS CloudTrail logs. All logs must be highly available for 30 days for frequent analysis, retained for an additional 60 days for backup purposes, and deleted 90 days after creation.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Transition objects to the S3 Standard storage class 30 days after creation. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.
o.B: Transition objects to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class 30 days after creation. Move all objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class after 90 days. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.
o.C: Transition objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class 30 days after creation. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.
o.D: Transition objects to the S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) storage class 30 days after creation. Move all objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class after 90 days. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.

e.why: Logs stay in S3 Standard for the first 30 days of frequent analysis, then a lifecycle rule transitions them to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval for the 60-day backup period, which has a far lower storage price than Standard-IA. An expiration action deletes the objects at 90 days, matching the retention rules most cost-effectively.

others.A: Objects are already in S3 Standard, so this transition does nothing and keeps paying Standard prices during the backup period.
others.B: Moving to Glacier at day 90 while also expiring at day 90 is contradictory, and Standard-IA costs more than Glacier for rarely accessed backups.
others.D: One Zone-IA reduces availability, the day-90 Glacier transition is pointless with deletion at 90 days, and it costs more than Glacier for backups.

e.tip: Glacier Flexible Retrieval has a 90-day minimum storage charge, but it can still be cheaper than IA for short backup windows; check the math.

q:
A company is building an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for its workloads. All secrets that are stored in Amazon EKS must be encrypted in the Kubernetes etcd key-value store.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage, rotate, and store all secrets in Amazon EKS.
o.B: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Enable Amazon EKS KMS secrets encryption on the Amazon EKS cluster.
o.C: Create the Amazon EKS cluster with default options. Use the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver as an add-on.
o.D: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key with the alias/aws/ebs alias. Enable default Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume encryption for the account.

e.why: Amazon EKS supports envelope encryption of Kubernetes secrets by associating a customer managed AWS KMS key with the cluster. Once enabled, secrets are encrypted with a data key protected by the KMS key before they are stored in etcd, which meets the requirement directly.

others.A: Secrets Manager stores secrets outside the cluster but does not encrypt the Kubernetes secrets that are stored in etcd.
others.C: The EBS CSI driver provisions persistent volumes for pods and has nothing to do with etcd secret encryption.
others.D: EBS default encryption protects EBS volumes; etcd for EKS runs in the AWS-managed control plane and secret envelope encryption is a separate setting. The aws/ebs alias is reserved for the AWS managed key.

e.tip: EKS etcd secret encryption = enable KMS envelope encryption on the cluster.

q:
A company wants to provide data scientists with near real-time read-only access to the company's production Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The database is currently configured as a Single-AZ database. The data scientists use complex queries that will not affect the production database. The company needs a solution that is highly available.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Scale the existing production database in a maintenance window to provide enough power for the data scientists.
o.B: Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ instance deployment with a larger secondary standby instance. Provide the data scientists access to the secondary instance.
o.C: Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ instance deployment. Provide two additional read replicas for the data scientists.
o.D: Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ cluster deployment with two readable standby instances. Provide read endpoints to the data scientists.

e.why: An RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment for PostgreSQL has a writer and two readable standby instances in three AZs, providing high availability with fast failover. The standbys serve read traffic through the reader endpoint with low replication lag, so data scientists get near real-time read-only access without extra read replicas, making it the most cost-effective HA option.

others.A: Scaling up the production instance does not isolate analytic queries from production and stays Single-AZ, so it is not highly available.
others.B: In a Multi-AZ instance deployment the standby cannot serve reads, so data scientists could not use it.
others.C: Multi-AZ instance plus two read replicas means paying for four instances (primary, standby and two replicas), which costs more than a Multi-AZ cluster.

e.tip: Multi-AZ instance standby = not readable; Multi-AZ DB cluster = two readable standbys.

q:
A company runs a three-tier web application in the AWS Cloud that operates across three Availability Zones. The application architecture has an Application Load Balancer, an Amazon EC2 web server that hosts user session states, and a MySQL database that runs on an EC2 instance. The company expects sudden increases in application traffic. The company wants to be able to scale to meet future application capacity demands and to ensure high availability across all three Availability Zones.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.
o.B: Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.
o.C: Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon DynamoDB. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache reads. Store the session data in DynamoDB. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.
o.D: Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL in a single Availability Zone. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.

fixed: Option B text was missing (only its last sentence remained) and has been reconstructed; option C was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: An RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster gives standbys in multiple Availability Zones that can also serve reads. ElastiCache for Redis with replication is highly available for session data and read caching, and an Auto Scaling group across three AZs scales the web tier.

others.B: ElastiCache for Memcached has no replication, so cached session data is lost if a node fails.
others.C: Moving from MySQL to DynamoDB requires a rewrite of the application's data layer.
others.D: A single-AZ RDS instance is not highly available across Availability Zones.

e.tip: Session data that must survive failures belongs in Redis with replication, not Memcached.

q:
A global video streaming company uses Amazon CloudFront as a content distribution network (CDN). The company wants to roll out content in a phased manner across multiple countries. The company needs to ensure that viewers who are outside the countries to which the company rolls out content are not able to view the content.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Add geographic restrictions to the content in CloudFront by using an allow list. Set up a custom error message.
o.B: Set up a new URL tor restricted content. Authorize access by using a signed URL and cookies. Set up a custom error message.
o.C: Encrypt the data for the content that the company distributes. Set up a custom error message.
o.D: Create a new URL for restricted content. Set up a time-restricted access policy for signed URLs.

e.why: CloudFront geographic restrictions with an allow list let you serve content only to viewers in specified countries, blocking everyone else with an HTTP 403, and you can configure a custom error page. As the rollout expands, you simply add countries to the allow list.

others.B: Signed URLs and cookies control access per user, not by viewer country.
others.C: Encryption protects data but does not restrict viewing by geography.
others.D: Time-restricted signed URLs limit access by time, not location.

e.tip: Restrict content by country at the CDN = CloudFront geo restriction (allow or block list).

q:
A company wants to use the AWS Cloud to improve its on-premises disaster recovery (DR) configuration. The company's core production business application uses Microsoft SQL Server Standard, which runs on a virtual machine (VM). The application has a recovery point objective (RPO) of 30 seconds or fewer and a recovery time objective (RTO) of 60 minutes. The DR solution needs to minimize costs wherever possible.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure a multi-site active/active setup between the on-premises server and AWS by using Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise with Always On availability groups.
o.B: Configure a warm standby Amazon RDS for SQL Server database on AWS. Configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to use change data capture (CDC).
o.C: Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery configured to replicate disk changes to AWS as a pilot light.
o.D: Use third-party backup software to capture backups every night. Store a secondary set of backups in Amazon S3.

e.why: The keyed answer uses a warm standby Amazon RDS for SQL Server database kept in sync by AWS DMS with change data capture, so ongoing changes replicate continuously, meeting an RPO of around 30 seconds. A running RDS standby can be promoted and the application redirected well within the 60-minute RTO, without needing SQL Server Enterprise licensing.

others.A: Multi-site active/active with SQL Server Enterprise Always On is the most expensive option and exceeds the RTO need.
others.C: The key treats Elastic Disaster Recovery as not chosen here, although it does offer second-level RPO and minutes-level RTO at low cost.
others.D: Nightly backups give an RPO of up to 24 hours, far beyond 30 seconds.

e.tip: DR patterns by cost: backup/restore < pilot light < warm standby < multi-site active/active.
e.flag: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (C) supports SQL Server Standard on VMs with sub-second-to-seconds RPO, minutes RTO and low-cost staging, so it likely meets the needs more cheaply than a running RDS warm standby with DMS; C is arguably correct.

q:
A company has an on-premises server that uses an Oracle database to process and store customer information. The company wants to use an AWS database service to achieve higher availability and to improve application performance. The company also wants to offload reporting from its primary database system.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.A: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create an Amazon RDS DB instance in multiple AWS Regions. Point the reporting functions toward a separate DB instance from the primary DB instance.
o.B: Use Amazon RDS in a Single-AZ deployment to create an Oracle database. Create a read replica in the same zone as the primary DB instance. Direct the reporting functions to the read replica.
o.C: Use Amazon RDS deployed in a Multi-AZ cluster deployment to create an Oracle database. Direct the reporting functions to use the reader instance in the cluster deployment.
o.D: Use Amazon RDS deployed in a Multi-AZ instance deployment to create an Amazon Aurora database. Direct the reporting functions to the reader instances.

e.why: Amazon Aurora provides storage replicated six ways across three AZs, fast failover and up to 15 low-latency Aurora Replicas, which improves availability and performance. Reporting can be pointed at the reader endpoint to offload the primary, and Aurora is fully managed, making it the most operationally efficient choice despite the Oracle-to-Aurora migration.

others.A: Using DMS to build instances in multiple Regions is complex and is not how you create a highly available deployment.
others.B: Single-AZ with a read replica in the same AZ is not highly available.
others.C: RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments support only MySQL and PostgreSQL, not Oracle.

e.tip: RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster (readable standbys) = MySQL and PostgreSQL only.

q:
A company wants to build a web application on AWS. Client access requests to the website are not predictable and can be idle for a long time. Only customers who have paid a subscription fee can have the ability to sign in and use the web application.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose three.)

o.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve user information from Amazon DynamoDB. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs. Send the API calls to the Lambda function.
o.B: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service behind an Application Load Balancer to retrieve user information from Amazon RDS. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs. Send the API calls to the ECS service.
o.C: Create an Amazon Cognito user pool to authenticate users.
o.D: Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool to authenticate users.
o.E: Use AWS Amplify to serve the frontend web content with HTML, CSS, and JS. Use an integrated Amazon CloudFront configuration.
o.F: Use Amazon S3 static web hosting with PHP, CSS, and JS. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the frontend web content.

fixed: Option A was truncated and has been completed; option B's last sentence has been corrected to refer to the ECS service.

e.why: Lambda, API Gateway and DynamoDB charge only for usage, which suits unpredictable traffic that can be idle for long periods. A Cognito user pool handles sign-up and sign-in for paying customers, and Amplify serves the static frontend through CloudFront.

others.B: ECS tasks, an ALB and RDS run all the time and cost money even when the site is idle.
others.D: Cognito identity pools grant AWS credentials; user pools are what authenticate users.
others.F: S3 static website hosting cannot run PHP, which is server-side code.

e.tip: User sign-in is a Cognito user pool; AWS credentials for users come from an identity pool.

q:
A media company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to deliver content over the internet. The company wants only premium customers to have access to the media streams and file content. The company stores all content in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company also delivers content on demand to customers for a specific purpose, such as movie rentals or music downloads.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Generate and provide S3 signed cookies to premium customers.
o.B: Generate and provide CloudFront signed URLs to premium customers.
o.C: Use origin access control (OAC) to limit the access of non-premium customers.
o.D: Generate and activate field-level encryption to block non-premium customers.

e.why: CloudFront signed URLs restrict access to individual files, which suits on-demand delivery such as a specific movie rental or music download, and can include expiration times and IP restrictions. Only premium customers receive the signed URLs, so others cannot access the content.

others.A: S3 does not have signed cookies; signed cookies are a CloudFront feature and are best for granting access to many files, not individual purchases.
others.C: Origin access control restricts S3 access to CloudFront but cannot distinguish premium from non-premium viewers.
others.D: Field-level encryption protects specific POST form fields and does not control who can view content.

e.tip: CloudFront signed URL = individual files; signed cookies = multiple files or whole sections.

q:
A company runs Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS accounts that are individually bled. The company recently purchased a Savings Pian. Because of changes in the company’s business requirements, the company has decommissioned a large number of EC2 instances. The company wants to use its Savings Plan discounts on its other AWS accounts.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: From the AWS Account Management Console of the management account, turn on discount sharing from the billing preferences section.
o.B: From the AWS Account Management Console of the account that purchased the existing Savings Plan, turn on discount sharing from the billing preferences section. Include all accounts.
o.C: From the AWS Organizations management account, use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Savings Plan with other accounts.
o.D: Create an organization in AWS Organizations in a new payer account. Invite the other AWS accounts to join the organization from the management account.
o.E: Create an organization in AWS Organizations in the existing AWS account with the existing EC2 instances and Savings Plan. Invite the other AWS accounts to join the organization from the management account.

e.why: Savings Plans discounts can be shared only across accounts in the same AWS Organizations consolidated billing family. Creating an organization with a new payer (management) account and inviting the other accounts brings them under consolidated billing (D), and turning on discount sharing in the management account's billing preferences lets the Savings Plan apply across member accounts (A).

others.B: Discount sharing is controlled from the management account of the organization, not from an individual member account.
others.C: Savings Plans cannot be shared through AWS Resource Access Manager.
others.E: This could work technically, but AWS best practice is a dedicated management (payer) account that does not run workloads.

e.tip: Reserved Instance and Savings Plans sharing works through Organizations consolidated billing, toggled in the management account.

q:
A retail company uses a regional Amazon API Gateway API for its public REST APIs. The API Gateway endpoint is a custom domain name that points to an Amazon Route 53 alias record. A solutions architect needs to create a solution that has minimal effects on customers and minimal data loss to release the new version of APIs.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a canary release deployment stage for API Gateway. Deploy the latest API version. Point an appropriate percentage of traffic to the canary stage. After API verification, promote the canary stage to the production stage.
o.B: Create a new API Gateway endpoint with a new version of the API in OpenAPI YAML file format. Use the import-to-update operation in merge mode into the API in API Gateway. Deploy the new version of the API to the production stage.
o.C: Create a new API Gateway endpoint with a new version of the API in OpenAPI JSON file format. Use the import-to-update operation in overwrite mode into the API in API Gateway. Deploy the new version of the API to the production stage.
o.D: Create a new API Gateway endpoint with new versions of the API definitions. Create a custom domain name for the new API Gateway API. Point the Route 53 alias record to the new API Gateway API custom domain name.

e.why: API Gateway canary release deployments let you send a configurable percentage of stage traffic to the new API version while the rest continues on the current version, with separate metrics and logs. After verifying the canary, you promote it to production, so customer impact and data loss are minimal and the existing custom domain and Route 53 alias stay unchanged.

others.B: Import in merge mode deploys directly to production for all users at once, with no gradual verification.
others.C: Overwrite mode replaces the whole API definition for all customers at once, risking breakage.
others.D: Creating a new API and switching the alias record cuts over all traffic at once and DNS caching causes inconsistent behavior.

e.tip: Gradual API rollout in API Gateway = canary release on a stage.

q:
A company wants to direct its users to a backup static error page if the company's primary website is unavailable. The primary website's DNS records are hosted in Amazon Route 53. The domain is pointing to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company needs a solution that minimizes changes and infrastructure overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Update the Route 53 records to use a latency routing policy. Add a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket to the records so that the traffic is sent to the most responsive endpoints.
o.B: Set up a Route 53 active-passive failover configuration. Direct traffic to a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket when Route 53 health checks determine that the ALB endpoint is unhealthy.
o.C: Set up a Route 53 active-active configuration with the ALB and an Amazon EC2 instance that hosts a static error page as endpoints. Configure Route 53 to send requests to the instance only if the health checks fail for the ALB.
o.D: Update the Route 53 records to use a multivalue answer routing policy. Create a health check. Direct traffic to the website if the health check passes. Direct traffic to a static error page that is hosted in Amazon S3 if the health check does not pass.

fixed: Option B text was missing and has been reconstructed; option C was truncated and has been completed.

e.why: A Route 53 failover (active-passive) routing policy sends traffic to the ALB while its health check passes and to a static error page in S3 when the check fails. It needs only DNS record changes and an S3 bucket, so changes and infrastructure are minimal.

others.A: Latency routing picks the fastest endpoint and could send users to the error page even when the site is healthy.
others.C: Running an EC2 instance for an error page adds infrastructure, and an active-active setup sends traffic to both endpoints.
others.D: Multivalue answer routing returns several healthy records at random and is not meant for primary and backup failover.

e.tip: Show a backup or error page when the primary fails: Route 53 failover routing to S3.

q:
A recent analysis of a company's IT expenses highlights the need to reduce backup costs. The company's chief information officer wants to simplify the on-premises backup infrastructure and reduce costs by eliminating the use of physical backup tapes. The company must preserve the existing investment in the on-premises backup applications and workflows.

What should a solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the NFS interface.
o.B: Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the NFS interface.
o.C: Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the iSCSI interface.
o.D: Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the iSCSI-virtual tape library (VTL) interface.

e.why: AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway presents an iSCSI virtual tape library (VTL) that existing backup applications already understand, so workflows are preserved. Virtual tapes are stored in Amazon S3 and can be archived to S3 Glacier or Glacier Deep Archive, eliminating physical tapes and reducing cost.

others.A: The NFS interface is S3 File Gateway, which would require changing tape-based backup workflows to file-based ones.
others.B: Amazon EFS is file storage and would require changing backup application targets and workflows; it is also costlier than tape archives.
others.C: Amazon EFS does not offer an iSCSI interface.

e.tip: Replace physical tapes but keep backup software = Tape Gateway (iSCSI VTL).

q:
A company has data collection sensors at different locations. The data collection sensors stream a high volume of data to the company. The company wants to design a platform on AWS to ingest and process high-volume streaming data. The solution must be scalable and support data collection in near real time. The company must store the data in Amazon S3 for future reporting.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.
o.B: Use AWS Glue to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.
o.C: Use AWS Lambda to deliver streaming data and store the data to Amazon S3.
o.D: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.

e.why: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose (now Amazon Data Firehose) is a fully managed service that ingests high-volume streaming data, scales automatically, buffers and optionally transforms it, and delivers it to Amazon S3 in near real time. No code or servers to manage gives the least operational overhead.

others.B: AWS Glue streaming ETL jobs need to be written, run and paid for continuously and are more effort than Firehose for simple delivery.
others.C: Lambda alone is not an ingestion endpoint for sensor streams and requires custom code to batch and write data.
others.D: AWS DMS migrates and replicates databases; it is not for sensor streaming ingestion.

e.tip: Stream to S3/Redshift/OpenSearch with no code = Firehose.

q:
A company has separate AWS accounts for its finance, data analytics, and development departments. Because of costs and security concerns, the company wants to control which services each AWS account can use.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Systems Manager templates to control which AWS services each department can use.
o.B: Create organization units (OUs) for each department in AWS Organizations. Attach service control policies (SCPs) to the OUs.
o.C: Use AWS CloudFormation to automatically provision only the AWS services that each department can use.
o.D: Set up a list of products in AWS Service Catalog in the AWS accounts to manage and control the usage of specific AWS services.

e.why: Grouping the department accounts into OUs in AWS Organizations and attaching service control policies lets you centrally set the maximum services each account can use, applying to every principal in those accounts. It is policy-only and centrally managed, so it has the least operational overhead.

others.A: Systems Manager documents automate operations; they cannot restrict which AWS services accounts use.
others.C: CloudFormation provisions resources but does not prevent users from using other services directly.
others.D: Service Catalog curates approved products but does not block access to other services unless combined with restrictive IAM in every account.

e.tip: Restrict services per account centrally = SCPs on OUs.

q:
A company has created a multi-tier application for its ecommerce website. The website uses an Application Load Balancer that resides in the public subnets, a web tier in the public subnets, and a MySQL cluster hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnets. The MySQL database needs to retrieve product catalog and pricing information that is hosted on the internet by a third-party provider. A solutions architect must devise a strategy that maximizes security without increasing operational overhead.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy a NAT instance in the VPC. Route all the internet-based traffic through the NAT instance.
o.B: Deploy a NAT gateway in the public subnets. Modify the private subnet route table to direct all internet-bound traffic to the NAT gateway.
o.C: Configure an internet gateway and attach it to the VPC. Modify the private subnet route table to direct internet-bound traffic to the internet gateway.
o.D: Configure a virtual private gateway and attach it to the VPC. Modify the private subnet route table to direct internet-bound traffic to the virtual private gateway.

fixed: Option C contained the end of option D and has been reconstructed; options A and D were truncated and have been completed.

e.why: A NAT gateway in a public subnet lets instances in private subnets start outbound connections to the internet, such as calls to the third-party provider, while blocking inbound connections. It is a managed service, so there is no extra operational overhead.

others.A: A NAT instance is an EC2 instance that you must patch, scale and make highly available.
others.C: Routing private subnets to an internet gateway would make them public and does not work for instances without public IPs.
others.D: A virtual private gateway connects to on-premises networks through VPN, not to the internet.

e.tip: Outbound-only internet access for private subnets with low overhead: NAT gateway.

q:
A company is using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt AWS Lambda environment variables. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the required permissions are in place to decrypt and use the environment variables.

Which steps must the solutions architect take to implement the correct permissions? (Choose two.)

o.A: Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda resource policy.
o.B: Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda execution role.
o.C: Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda function policy.
o.D: Allow the Lambda execution role in the AWS KMS key policy.
o.E: Allow the Lambda resource policy in the AWS KMS key policy.

e.why: For a customer managed KMS key, Lambda decrypts environment variables using the function's execution role, so the execution role needs kms:Decrypt permission in its IAM policy (B). The KMS key policy must also allow that execution role to use the key (D), because key policies are the primary control for KMS key access.

others.A: A Lambda resource-based policy controls who can invoke or manage the function, not what the function can access.
others.C: The function policy is the same as the resource policy and governs invocation, not KMS access.
others.E: Key policies grant access to principals such as roles, not to a Lambda resource policy.

e.tip: Function's outbound permissions = execution role; who can invoke = resource policy.

q: A company has a financial application that produces reports. The reports average 50 KB in size and are stored in Amazon S3. The reports are frequently accessed during the first week after production and must be stored for several years. The reports must be retrievable within 6 hours. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use S3 Standard. Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the reports to S3 Glacier after 7 days.
o.B: Use S3 Standard. Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the reports to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 7 days.
o.C: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to transition the reports to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) and S3 Glacier.
o.D: Use S3 Standard. Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the reports to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.

e.why: S3 Standard serves the frequent access in the first week, then a lifecycle rule moves reports to S3 Glacier (Flexible Retrieval), whose standard retrievals complete in about 3-5 hours, meeting the 6-hour requirement at a much lower storage cost than IA for multi-year retention.

others.B: Standard-IA has millisecond access but costs several times more than Glacier for years of storage when retrieval within 6 hours is acceptable; small objects also incur a 128 KB minimum charge.
others.C: Intelligent-Tiering is configured by access tiers, not lifecycle rules to Standard-IA, and has per-object monitoring fees; objects under 128 KB are not auto-tiered.
others.D: Glacier Deep Archive standard retrieval takes up to 12 hours, exceeding the 6-hour limit.

e.tip: Retrieval within hours: Glacier Flexible (3-5 h standard); Deep Archive is up to 12 h (48 h bulk).

q: A company needs to optimize the cost of its Amazon EC2 instances. The company also needs to change the type and family of its EC2 instances every 2-3 months. What should the company do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Purchase Partial Upfront Reserved Instances for a 3-year term.
o.B: Purchase a No Upfront Compute Savings Plan for a 1-year term.
o.C: Purchase All Upfront Reserved Instances for a 1-year term.
o.D: Purchase an All Upfront EC2 Instance Savings Plan for a 1-year term.

e.why: A Compute Savings Plan applies automatically to any EC2 instance family, size, Region, OS or tenancy (plus Fargate and Lambda), so changing instance type and family every few months keeps the discount. A 1-year No Upfront term reduces cost without a large upfront payment or long commitment.

others.A: Standard Reserved Instances are tied to an instance family; a 3-year term is a long commitment that does not match frequent family changes.
others.C: Standard Reserved Instances lock in an instance family and Region, so changing families loses the discount.
others.D: EC2 Instance Savings Plans are tied to one instance family in a Region, so changing family breaks coverage.

e.tip: Changing instance family/Region/compute service = Compute Savings Plan.

q: A solutions architect needs to review a company's Amazon S3 buckets to discover personally identifiable information (PII). The company stores the PII data in the us-east-1 Region and us-west-2 Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Configure Amazon Macie in each Region. Create a job to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
o.B: Configure AWS Security Hub for all Regions. Create an AWS Config rule to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
o.C: Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
o.D: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.

e.why: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover PII in S3. Macie is a Regional service, so enabling it in us-east-1 and us-west-2 and creating sensitive data discovery jobs (or automated discovery) analyzes the buckets with minimal setup.

others.B: Security Hub aggregates findings and AWS Config evaluates resource configuration; neither inspects object contents for PII.
others.C: Amazon Inspector scans EC2, ECR images and Lambda for vulnerabilities, not S3 data for PII.
others.D: GuardDuty detects threats and suspicious activity, not PII in objects.

e.tip: PII discovery in S3 = Macie (enable per Region).

q: A company's SAP application has a backend SQL Server database in an on-premises environment. The company wants to migrate its on-premises application and database server to AWS. The company needs an instance type that meets the high demands of its SAP database. On-premises performance data shows that both the SAP application and the database have high memory utilization. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use the compute optimized instance family for the application. Use the memory optimized instance family for the database.
o.B: Use the storage optimized instance family for both the application and the database.
o.C: Use the memory optimized instance family for both the application and the database.
o.D: Use the high performance computing (HPC) optimized instance family for the application. Use the memory optimized instance family for the database.

e.why: Performance data shows high memory utilization for both the SAP application and the SQL Server database, so memory optimized instances (such as R or X families, which include SAP-certified sizes) fit both tiers. Matching instance family to the observed bottleneck is the deciding factor.

others.A: Compute optimized instances have a low memory-to-vCPU ratio, which does not suit the memory-heavy application tier.
others.B: Storage optimized instances target high local disk I/O, not memory demand.
others.D: HPC instances are designed for tightly coupled compute workloads, not a memory-heavy SAP application tier.

e.tip: Match the bottleneck: memory = R/X, CPU = C, local I/O = I/D, HPC = Hpc.

q: A company runs an application in a VPC with public and private subnets. The VPC extends across multiple Availability Zones. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. The application uses an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. A solutions architect needs to design a secure solution to establish a connection between the EC2 instances and the SQS queue. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the private subnets. Add to the endpoint a security group that has an inbound access rule that allows traffic from the EC2 instances that are in the private subnets.
o.B: Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the public subnets. Attach to the interface endpoint a VPC endpoint policy that allows access from the EC2 instances that are in the private subnets.
o.C: Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the public subnets. Attach an Amazon SQS access policy to the interface VPC endpoint that allows requests from only a specified VPC endpoint.
o.D: Implement a gateway endpoint for Amazon SQS. Add a NAT gateway to the private subnets. Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instances that allows access to the SQS queue.

e.why: An interface VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) for SQS places ENIs in the private subnets, so instances reach SQS privately without traversing the internet. The security group on the endpoint must allow inbound HTTPS from the EC2 instances, giving a secure, tightly scoped connection.

others.B: Placing the endpoint in public subnets is unnecessary; the endpoint should be in the subnets where the instances run, and an endpoint policy alone does not cover network access.
others.C: An SQS access policy is attached to the queue, not to the VPC endpoint, and the public subnet placement is unnecessary.
others.D: Gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB, and a NAT gateway would route traffic over the internet.

e.tip: Gateway endpoints: only S3 and DynamoDB; everything else uses interface endpoints.

q: A solutions architect is using an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy a three-tier web application. The web application consists of a web tier and an application tier that stores and retrieves user data in Amazon DynamoDB tables. The web and application tiers are hosted on Amazon EC2 instances, and the database tier is not publicly accessible. The application EC2 instances need to access the DynamoDB tables without exposing API credentials in the template. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an IAM role to read the DynamoDB tables. Associate the role with the application instances by referencing an instance profile.
o.B: Create an IAM role that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Add the role to the EC2 instance profile, and associate the instance profile with the application instances.
o.C: Use the parameter section in the AWS CloudFormation template to have the user input access and secret keys from an already-created IAM user that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables.
o.D: Create an IAM user in the AWS CloudFormation template that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Use the GetAtt function to retrieve the access and secret keys, and pass them to the application instances through the user data.

e.why: An IAM role with the needed DynamoDB read and write permissions, attached to the instances through an instance profile, gives the application temporary credentials automatically from the instance metadata service. No access keys appear in the template, user data or code.

others.A: A role that only reads DynamoDB is insufficient because the application must store as well as retrieve data.
others.C: Passing long-term access keys as parameters exposes credentials and requires rotation.
others.D: Creating an IAM user and passing its keys through user data embeds long-term secrets on instances, which is insecure.

e.tip: EC2 access to AWS services = IAM role via instance profile, never access keys.

q: A solutions architect manages an analytics application. The application stores large amounts of semistructured data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The solutions architect wants to use parallel data processing to process the data more quickly. The solutions architect also wants to use information that is stored in an Amazon Redshift database to enrich the data. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon Athena to process the S3 data. Use AWS Glue with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
o.B: Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon EMR with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
o.C: Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to move the S3 data into Amazon Redshift so that the data can be enriched.
o.D: Use AWS Glue to process the S3 data. Use AWS Lake Formation with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.

e.why: Amazon EMR runs distributed frameworks such as Apache Spark that process large semistructured S3 datasets in parallel. EMR Spark can also read from Amazon Redshift (for example with the Spark Redshift connector) to join and enrich the S3 data in the same job.

others.A: Athena is interactive SQL querying rather than a parallel processing framework for heavy transformations, and splitting work between Athena and Glue is more complex.
others.C: Kinesis Data Streams is for real-time streaming ingestion, not for moving existing S3 data into Redshift.
others.D: Lake Formation manages data lake permissions and governance; it does not enrich data with Redshift information.

e.tip: Big data parallel processing with Spark/Hadoop = EMR.

q: A company has two VPCs that are located in the us-west-2 Region within the same AWS account. The company needs to allow network traffic between these VPCs. Approximately 500 GB of data transfer will occur between the VPCs each month. What is the MOST cost-effective solution to connect these VPCs?

o.A: Implement AWS Transit Gateway to connect the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the transit gateway for inter-VPC communication.
o.B: Implement an AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPN tunnel for inter-VPC communication.
o.C: Set up a VPC peering connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPC peering connection for inter-VPC communication.
o.D: Set up a 1 GB AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the Direct Connect connection for inter-VPC communication.

e.why: VPC peering connects two VPCs privately over the AWS network with no hourly charge and no per-GB processing fee; within the same AZ traffic is free and across AZs standard inter-AZ data transfer applies. For two VPCs in one Region it is the cheapest option.

others.A: Transit Gateway charges per attachment hour and per GB processed, which is unnecessary for only two VPCs.
others.B: Site-to-Site VPN is meant for on-premises connectivity and adds hourly charges and throughput limits.
others.D: Direct Connect connects on-premises networks to AWS; it is costly and not used to link two VPCs.

e.tip: Two VPCs, simple and cheap = VPC peering; many VPCs = Transit Gateway.

q: A company hosts multiple applications on AWS for different product lines. The applications use different compute resources, including Amazon EC2 instances and Application Load Balancers. The applications run in different AWS accounts under the same organization in AWS Organizations across multiple AWS Regions. Teams for each product line have tagged each compute resource in the individual accounts. The company wants more details about the cost for each product line from the consolidated billing feature in Organizations. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Select a specific AWS generated tag in the AWS Billing console.
o.B: Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Billing console.
o.C: Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Resource Groups console.
o.D: Activate the selected tag from each AWS account.
o.E: Activate the selected tag from the Organizations management account.

e.why: The teams applied their own tags, which are user-defined tags; to use them in billing reports and Cost Explorer you select them in the Billing console (B). Cost allocation tags are activated from the Organizations management account (payer account) for consolidated billing (E), after which costs can be grouped by product line.

others.A: AWS-generated tags such as aws:createdBy do not represent the teams' product line tags.
others.C: Resource Groups organize resources but do not activate tags for cost allocation.
others.D: In consolidated billing, only the management account can activate cost allocation tags, not each member account.

e.tip: Cost allocation tags must be activated in the payer (management) account.

q: A company's solutions architect is designing an AWS multi-account solution that uses AWS Organizations. The solutions architect has organized the company's accounts into organizational units (OUs). The solutions architect needs a solution that will identify any changes to the OU hierarchy. The solution also needs to notify the company's operations team of any changes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use account drift notifications to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
o.B: Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use AWS Config aggregated rules to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
o.C: Use AWS Service Catalog to create accounts in Organizations. Use an AWS CloudTrail organization trail to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
o.D: Use AWS CloudFormation templates to create accounts in Organizations. Use the drift detection operation on a stack to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.

e.why: AWS Control Tower continuously detects landing zone drift, including changes to the OU hierarchy such as moving, creating or deleting OUs or accounts outside Control Tower, and publishes drift notifications to an SNS topic in the audit account. Subscribing the operations team to that topic gives built-in detection and notification with the least overhead.

others.B: AWS Config rules evaluate resource configurations, and there is no managed Config rule for Organizations OU hierarchy changes.
others.C: A CloudTrail organization trail records the API calls but you would still have to build filtering and alerting yourself.
others.D: CloudFormation drift detection only covers resources managed by the stack and does not track OU structure changes.

e.tip: OU/landing zone change detection with notifications = Control Tower drift.

q: A company's website handles millions of requests each day, and the number of requests continues to increase. A solutions architect needs to improve the response time of the web application. The solutions architect determines that the application needs to decrease latency when retrieving product details from the Amazon DynamoDB table. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

o.A: Set up a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Route all read requests through DAX.
o.B: Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Redis between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Redis.
o.C: Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Memcached.
o.D: Set up Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the table, and have AWS Lambda read from the table and populate Amazon ElastiCache. Route all read requests through ElastiCache.

e.why: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, DynamoDB-compatible in-memory cache that cuts read latency from milliseconds to microseconds. It is API-compatible with DynamoDB, so the application needs minimal code changes and no cache-population logic, giving the least operational overhead.

others.B: ElastiCache for Redis works but requires the application to implement caching logic such as cache-aside and invalidation.
others.C: ElastiCache for Memcached also requires custom caching code and lacks DynamoDB API compatibility.
others.D: Streams plus Lambda to populate ElastiCache is a custom pipeline with more components to build and operate.

e.tip: Cache for DynamoDB with minimal code change = DAX.

q: A solutions architect needs to ensure that API calls to Amazon DynamoDB from Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC do not travel across the internet. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create a route table entry for the endpoint.
o.B: Create a gateway endpoint for DynamoDB.
o.C: Create an interface endpoint for Amazon EC2.
o.D: Create an elastic network interface for the endpoint in each of the subnets of the VPC.
o.E: Create a security group entry in the endpoint's security group to provide access.

e.why: A gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB (B) keeps traffic on the AWS network, and it works by adding a route with the DynamoDB prefix list targeting the endpoint in the subnet route tables (A). Together these ensure API calls from instances never traverse the internet.

others.C: An interface endpoint for Amazon EC2 provides private access to the EC2 API, not to DynamoDB.
others.D: Gateway endpoints do not use elastic network interfaces; ENIs are used by interface endpoints.
others.E: Gateway endpoints do not have security groups; access is controlled with route tables and endpoint policies.

e.tip: Gateway endpoint = route table entry, no ENI or security group; interface endpoint = ENI plus security group.

q: A company runs its applications on both Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters and on-premises Kubernetes clusters. The company wants to view all clusters and workloads from a central location. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to collect and group the cluster information.
o.B: Use Amazon EKS Connector to register and connect all Kubernetes clusters.
o.C: Use AWS Systems Manager to collect and view the cluster information.
o.D: Use Amazon EKS Anywhere as the primary cluster to view the other clusters with native Kubernetes commands.

e.why: Amazon EKS Connector lets you register any conformant Kubernetes cluster, including on-premises clusters, with Amazon EKS so you can view clusters and their workloads in the EKS console alongside EKS clusters. It only needs an agent deployed on each cluster, giving a central view with the least overhead.

others.A: Container Insights collects metrics and logs, but it is a monitoring tool and does not give a unified cluster and workload inventory view of external clusters.
others.C: Systems Manager manages nodes and does not provide a Kubernetes cluster and workload view.
others.D: EKS Anywhere is for running EKS-managed clusters on premises; it is not a central viewer for other clusters and would need cluster rebuilds.

e.tip: View on-premises or other Kubernetes clusters in the EKS console = EKS Connector.

q: A company is building an ecommerce application and needs to store sensitive customer information. The company needs to give customers the ability to complete purchase transactions on the website. The company also needs to ensure that sensitive customer data is protected, even from database administrators. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Store sensitive data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use EBS encryption to encrypt the data. Use an IAM instance role to restrict access.
o.B: Store sensitive data in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) client-side encryption to encrypt the data.
o.C: Store sensitive data in Amazon S3. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) server-side encryption to encrypt the data. Use S3 bucket policies to restrict access.
o.D: Store sensitive data in Amazon FSx for Windows Server. Mount the file share on application servers. Use Windows file permissions to restrict access.

e.why: Amazon RDS for MySQL supports transactional purchase workloads, and encrypting the sensitive fields client-side with AWS KMS (for example via the AWS Encryption SDK) before writing them means the database only stores ciphertext. Database administrators can query the tables but cannot read the plaintext without KMS key permissions.

others.A: EBS encryption is transparent to anyone with access to the instance, so administrators could still read the data, and a raw volume is not a transactional database.
others.C: S3 server-side encryption decrypts automatically for authorized users, and S3 is not a transactional database for purchases.
others.D: FSx for Windows file shares are not a transactional database and file permissions do not protect data from administrators.

e.tip: Protect data even from DBAs = client-side (application-level) encryption.

q: A company has an on-premises MySQL database that handles transactional data. The company is migrating the database to the AWS Cloud. The migrated database must maintain compatibility with the company's applications that use the database. The migrated database also must scale automatically during periods of increased demand. Which migration solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use native MySQL tools to migrate the database to Amazon RDS for MySQL. Configure elastic storage scaling.
o.B: Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift by using the mysqldump utility. Turn on Auto Scaling for the Amazon Redshift cluster.
o.C: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon Aurora. Turn on Aurora Auto Scaling.
o.D: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Configure an Auto Scaling policy.

e.why: Amazon Aurora MySQL is wire-compatible with MySQL so applications keep working, and AWS DMS can migrate the database with minimal downtime. Aurora Auto Scaling adds or removes Aurora Replicas based on load, and Aurora storage grows automatically, so the database scales with demand.

others.A: RDS storage autoscaling only grows disk space; it does not scale compute to handle increased demand.
others.B: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse, not a transactional MySQL-compatible database.
others.D: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and is not compatible with applications built for MySQL.

q: A company runs multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances in a VPC across two Availability Zones. The instances host applications that use a hierarchical directory structure. The applications need to read and write rapidly and concurrently to shared storage. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Allow access from all the EC2 instances in the VPC.
o.B: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system from each EC2 instance.
o.C: Create a file system on a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Attach the EBS volume to all the EC2 instances.
o.D: Create file systems on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that are attached to each EC2 instance. Synchronize the EBS volumes across the different EC2 instances.

e.why: Amazon EFS is a fully managed NFS file system with a hierarchical directory structure that many Linux instances across multiple AZs can mount concurrently with read-after-write consistency. It scales throughput and capacity automatically for rapid concurrent reads and writes.

others.A: Amazon S3 is object storage with a flat namespace, not a POSIX file system for concurrent file-level writes.
others.C: EBS Multi-Attach works only within a single AZ, requires a cluster-aware file system and supports limited instances.
others.D: Synchronizing separate EBS volumes is custom, error-prone and not truly shared storage.

e.tip: Shared POSIX file system across AZs for Linux = EFS; Windows = FSx for Windows.

q: A solutions architect is designing a workload that will store hourly energy consumption by business tenants in a building. The sensors will feed a database through HTTP requests that will add up usage for each tenant. The solutions architect must use managed services when possible. The workload will receive more features in the future as the solutions architect adds independent components. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table.
o.B: Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the processed data.
o.C: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in a Microsoft SQL Server Express database on an Amazon EC2 instance.
o.D: Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) shared file system to store the processed data.

e.why: API Gateway receives the sensor HTTP requests, Lambda processes and aggregates usage, and DynamoDB stores per-tenant totals with atomic counters, all fully managed and serverless. Each piece is decoupled, so independent components can be added later with the least operational overhead.

others.B: An ELB with an EC2 Auto Scaling group requires managing instances, and S3 is not suited to incrementally adding up usage values.
others.C: SQL Server Express on a self-managed EC2 instance is not a managed database and adds patching and backup overhead.
others.D: EC2 instances plus EFS require server management and a file system is a poor fit for summing per-tenant usage.

e.tip: Managed HTTP ingestion = API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB.

q: A solutions architect is designing the storage architecture for a new web application used for storing and viewing engineering drawings. All application components will be deployed on the AWS infrastructure. The application design must support caching to minimize the amount of time that users wait for the engineering drawings to load. The application must be able to store petabytes of data. Which combination of storage and caching should the solutions architect use?

o.A: Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront
o.B: Amazon S3 Glacier with Amazon ElastiCache
o.C: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes with Amazon CloudFront
o.D: AWS Storage Gateway with Amazon ElastiCache

e.why: Amazon S3 stores virtually unlimited data (petabytes) durably and cheaply, and Amazon CloudFront caches the drawings at edge locations close to users. This combination minimizes load times while scaling storage without limits.

others.B: S3 Glacier is archive storage with retrieval delays of minutes to hours, unsuitable for viewing drawings on demand.
others.C: EBS volumes are limited in size per volume and attached to single instances, so they do not scale to petabytes for a web application.
others.D: Storage Gateway is for hybrid on-premises access to AWS storage, which is not needed when everything runs on AWS.

q: An Amazon EventBridge rule targets a third-party API. The third-party API has not received any incoming traffic. A solutions architect needs to determine whether the rule conditions are being met and if the rule's target is being invoked. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Check for metrics in Amazon CloudWatch in the namespace for AWS/Events.
o.B: Review events in the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) dead-letter queue.
o.C: Check for the events in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
o.D: Check the trails in AWS CloudTrail for the EventBridge events.

e.why: EventBridge publishes rule metrics to CloudWatch in the AWS/Events namespace, including MatchedEvents (rule conditions met), Invocations (target invoked) and FailedInvocations. Checking these shows whether the rule matches and whether delivery to the API destination is attempted or failing.
