others.B: A dead-letter queue only exists if one was configured and only shows failed deliveries, not whether the rule matched.
others.C: EventBridge does not write rule matches to CloudWatch Logs by default unless you add a log group as a target.
others.D: CloudTrail records API calls such as PutRule, not each event match or target invocation.

e.tip: Is my EventBridge rule firing? Check MatchedEvents and Invocations metrics in AWS/Events.

q: A company has a large workload that runs every Friday evening. The workload runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in two Availability Zones in the us-east-1 Region. Normally, the company must run no more than two instances at all times. However, the company wants to scale up to six instances each Friday to handle a regularly repeating increased workload. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create a reminder in Amazon EventBridge to scale the instances.
o.B: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a scheduled action.
o.C: Create an Auto Scaling group that uses manual scaling.
o.D: Create an Auto Scaling group that uses automatic scaling.

e.why: An Auto Scaling group with a scheduled action can raise the desired and maximum capacity to six instances every Friday evening and lower it back to two afterward, using a recurring cron schedule. This fits a predictable, recurring load pattern with no manual work.

others.A: An EventBridge reminder would still require a person or extra automation to change capacity.
others.C: Manual scaling requires someone to change capacity every week.
others.D: Dynamic scaling reacts to metrics after load rises, while the known weekly schedule is handled more simply and proactively by scheduled scaling.

e.tip: Predictable recurring load = scheduled scaling.

q: A company is creating a REST API. The company has strict requirements for the use of TLS. The company requires TLSv1.3 on the API endpoints. The company also requires a specific public third-party certificate authority (CA) to sign the TLS certificate. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use a local machine to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CImport the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.
o.B: Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.
o.C: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CA. Import the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.
o.D: Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.

e.why: ACM cannot issue certificates signed by an external public CA, so the certificate must be obtained from the third-party CA and imported into ACM. An API Gateway custom domain name can then use the imported ACM certificate with a security policy that supports TLS 1.3 to serve the API endpoint.

others.B: ACM only issues certificates from Amazon's own CA (or AWS Private CA), not from a specific third-party public CA.
others.C: ACM cannot create third-party-signed certificates, and Lambda function URLs do not support custom certificates or custom domains.
others.D: ACM cannot issue a third-party-signed certificate, and function URLs cannot use your own certificate.

e.tip: Third-party CA certificate = import into ACM; ACM-issued certs are always Amazon-signed.

q: A company runs an application on AWS. The application receives inconsistent amounts of usage. The application uses AWS Direct Connect to connect to an on-premises MySQL-compatible database. The on-premises database consistently uses a minimum of 2 GiB of memory. The company wants to migrate the on-premises database to a managed AWS service. The company wants to use auto scaling capabilities to manage unexpected workload increases. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

o.A: Provision an Amazon DynamoDB database with default read and write capacity settings.
o.B: Provision an Amazon Aurora database with a minimum capacity of 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU).
o.C: Provision an Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 database with a minimum capacity of 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU).
o.D: Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL database with 2 GiB of memory.

e.why: Aurora Serverless v2 is MySQL-compatible, fully managed and scales capacity automatically in fine-grained ACU increments as demand changes. Each ACU provides about 2 GiB of memory, so a minimum of 1 ACU covers the 2 GiB baseline while scaling up handles unexpected spikes with the least administration.

others.A: DynamoDB is not MySQL compatible and would require rewriting the application.
others.B: Provisioned Aurora uses instance classes and does not use ACUs or scale compute automatically.
others.D: A fixed RDS for MySQL instance with 2 GiB does not scale compute automatically for unexpected load.

e.tip: 1 ACU = about 2 GiB memory; variable load on relational DB = Aurora Serverless v2.

q: A company wants to use an event-driven programming model with AWS Lambda. The company wants to reduce startup latency for Lambda functions that run on Java 11. The company does not have strict latency requirements for the applications. The company wants to reduce cold starts and outlier latencies when a function scales up. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure Lambda provisioned concurrency.
o.B: Increase the timeout of the Lambda functions.
o.C: Increase the memory of the Lambda functions.
o.D: Configure Lambda SnapStart.

e.why: Lambda SnapStart for Java initializes the function once, snapshots the memory and disk state, and resumes new execution environments from the cached snapshot, reducing startup latency by up to 10 times. It has no extra charge for Java runtimes, making it the most cost-effective way to cut cold starts when strict latency is not required.

others.A: Provisioned concurrency eliminates cold starts but charges for pre-initialized environments continuously, which is more expensive.
others.B: Increasing the timeout lets functions run longer but does not reduce cold start latency.
others.C: More memory adds CPU and may speed initialization slightly but raises cost and does not address cold starts as effectively.

e.tip: Java cold starts, cost-sensitive = SnapStart; strict latency = provisioned concurrency.

q: A financial services company launched a new application that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The company uses the application to track stock market trends. The company needs to operate the application for only 2 hours at the end of each week. The company needs to optimize the cost of running the database. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL database cluster.
o.B: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora MySQL database cluster.
o.C: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs MySQL. Purchase an instance reservation for the EC2 instance.
o.D: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses MySQL container images to run tasks.

e.why: Aurora Serverless v2 for MySQL scales capacity automatically and can scale down to a low minimum (and now auto-pause at 0 ACUs) when idle, so you pay mainly for the 2 hours of weekly use plus storage. That makes it the most cost-effective managed option for such an intermittent workload.

others.B: A provisioned Aurora cluster bills for instances around the clock even when the application is unused.
others.C: A reserved EC2 instance is paid for all week and adds database management overhead.
others.D: Running MySQL on ECS adds container and storage management and is not a managed database.

e.tip: Intermittent or idle-heavy relational workload = Aurora Serverless v2.

q: A company deploys its applications on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) behind an Application Load Balancer in an AWS Region. The application needs to store data in a PostgreSQL database engine. The company wants the data in the database to be highly available. The company also needs increased capacity for read workloads. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Create an Amazon DynamoDB database table configured with global tables.
o.B: Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ deployments.
o.C: Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment.
o.D: Create an Amazon RDS database configured with cross-Region read replicas.

e.why: An RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment for PostgreSQL has one writer and two readable standbys in three AZs, giving high availability with fast failover and extra read capacity through the reader endpoint. It delivers both needs in one managed configuration, which is the most operationally efficient.

others.A: DynamoDB is not PostgreSQL, so the application would require a rewrite.
others.B: A Multi-AZ instance deployment has a standby that cannot serve reads, so read capacity does not increase.
others.D: Cross-Region read replicas add read capacity but add cross-Region cost and complexity and do not give automatic HA failover.

e.tip: HA plus readable standbys in one setting = Multi-AZ DB cluster.

q: A company is building a RESTful serverless web application on AWS by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The users of this web application will be geographically distributed, and the company wants to reduce the latency of API requests to these users. Which type of endpoint should a solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

o.A: Private endpoint
o.B: Regional endpoint
o.C: Interface VPC endpoint
o.D: Edge-optimized endpoint

e.why: An edge-optimized API Gateway endpoint routes requests through the CloudFront edge network to the API's Region, so geographically distributed clients connect to a nearby edge location and get lower latency. This is the endpoint type designed for globally distributed users.

others.A: Private endpoints are reachable only from within a VPC through an interface endpoint, not by public users.
others.B: Regional endpoints suit clients in the same Region; distant users would connect directly to that Region with higher latency.
others.C: An interface VPC endpoint provides private access from a VPC and does nothing for internet users.

e.tip: Global clients = edge-optimized; same-Region clients = Regional; VPC-only = private.

q: A company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve content pages for its website. The company needs to ensure that clients use a TLS certificate when accessing the company's website. The company wants to automate the creation and renewal of the TLS certificates. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Use a CloudFront security policy to create a certificate.
o.B: Use a CloudFront origin access control (OAC) to create a certificate.
o.C: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use DNS validation for the domain.
o.D: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use email validation for the domain.

e.why: AWS Certificate Manager issues free public TLS certificates that integrate with CloudFront (the certificate must be in us-east-1). With DNS validation, ACM renews the certificate automatically as long as the CNAME validation record remains, so creation and renewal are fully automated.

others.A: A CloudFront security policy selects allowed TLS protocol versions and ciphers; it does not create certificates.
others.B: Origin access control secures CloudFront access to S3 origins and has nothing to do with certificates.
others.D: Email validation requires someone to respond to emails for issuance and renewal, so it is not fully automated.

e.tip: Automatic ACM renewal = DNS validation.

q: A company deployed a serverless application that uses Amazon DynamoDB as a database layer. The application has experienced a large increase in users. The company wants to improve database response time from milliseconds to microseconds and to cache requests to the database. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
o.B: Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift.
o.C: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS.
o.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.

e.why: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a managed, write-through in-memory cache for DynamoDB that reduces read response times from milliseconds to microseconds. Because DAX is API-compatible with DynamoDB, the serverless application needs minimal changes, giving the least operational overhead.

others.B: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics, not a low-latency cache for an application database.
others.C: Migrating to RDS is a large redesign and does not provide microsecond caching.
others.D: ElastiCache for Redis could cache data but requires custom caching logic in the application.

e.tip: Microsecond reads for DynamoDB = DAX.

q: A company runs an application that uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The application receives traffic only on weekdays during business hours. The company wants to optimize costs and reduce operational overhead based on this usage. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use the Instance Scheduler on AWS to configure start and stop schedules.
o.B: Turn off automatic backups. Create weekly manual snapshots of the database.
o.C: Create a custom AWS Lambda function to start and stop the database based on minimum CPU utilization.
o.D: Purchase All Upfront reserved DB instances.

e.why: Instance Scheduler on AWS is an AWS solution that automatically starts and stops RDS and EC2 instances on defined schedules, such as weekday business hours. Stopping the database outside those hours means paying only for storage during idle time, with no custom code to maintain.

others.B: Turning off automatic backups reduces data protection and barely affects cost, since compute remains the main expense.
others.C: A custom CPU-based Lambda function adds code to build and maintain and is less reliable than a schedule for known hours.
others.D: Reserved instances lower the hourly rate but you still pay for the instance 24/7 even though it is used only during business hours.

e.tip: Known on/off hours = schedule start/stop (Instance Scheduler); note stopped RDS restarts automatically after 7 days.

q: A company uses locally attached storage to run a latency-sensitive application on premises. The company is using a lift and shift method to move the application to the AWS Cloud. The company does not want to change the application architecture. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system to run the application.
o.B: Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP2 volume to run the application.
o.C: Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system to run the application.
o.D: Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP3 volume to run the application.

e.why: Hosting the application on EC2 with an EBS gp3 volume keeps a block-storage, single-instance design comparable to locally attached disks, so the architecture does not change. gp3 provides a baseline of 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s independent of size, at about 20 percent lower cost per GB than gp2, making it the most cost-effective choice.

others.A: FSx for Lustre is a shared high-performance file system, which changes the architecture and costs more.
others.B: gp2 works but costs more per GB than gp3, and its performance is tied to volume size.
others.C: FSx for OpenZFS is a shared network file system, which changes the storage architecture and adds cost.

e.tip: gp3 beats gp2 on price and decouples IOPS from size.

q: A company runs a stateful production application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application requires at least two EC2 instances to always be running. A solutions architect needs to design a highly available and fault-tolerant architecture for the application. The solutions architect creates an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances. Which set of additional steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements?

o.A: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy one On-Demand Instance in one Availability Zone and one On-Demand Instance in a second Availability Zone.
o.B: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two On-Demand Instances in a second Availability Zone.
o.C: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy four Spot Instances in one Availability Zone.
o.D: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two Spot Instances in a second Availability Zone.

e.why: Setting the Auto Scaling group minimum to four with two On-Demand Instances in each of two Availability Zones ensures that if an entire AZ fails, two instances are still running, satisfying the at-least-two requirement. On-Demand Instances avoid Spot interruptions for a stateful production application.

others.A: With one instance per AZ, an AZ outage leaves only one instance running until replacement, violating the two-instance requirement.
others.C: Spot Instances can be interrupted and a single AZ is not fault tolerant.
others.D: Spot Instances in one AZ can be reclaimed, so losing the On-Demand AZ could leave fewer than two instances.

e.tip: Fault tolerant = survive the loss of one AZ with the required capacity still running.

q: An ecommerce company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company hosts its website on premises and in the AWS Cloud. The company's on-premises data center is near the us-west-1 Region. The company uses the eu-central-1 Region to host the website. The company wants to minimize load time for the website as much as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Set up a geolocation routing policy. Send the traffic that is near us-west-1 to the on-premises data center. Send the traffic that is near eu-central-1 to eu-central-1.
o.B: Set up a simple routing policy that routes all traffic that is near eu-central-1 to eu-central-1 and routes all traffic that is near the on-premises datacenter to the on-premises data center.
o.C: Set up a latency routing policy. Associate the policy with us-west-1.
o.D: Set up a weighted routing policy. Split the traffic evenly between eu-central-1 and the on-premises data center.

e.why: A geolocation routing policy sends users based on their location: users near us-west-1 go to the nearby on-premises data center and users near eu-central-1 go to the AWS Region. This directs each user to the closest site to minimize load time and works with non-AWS endpoints.

others.B: Simple routing returns the same records to everyone and cannot route based on user location.
others.C: Latency routing uses AWS Region latency data; associating it with us-west-1 for on-premises servers would be an approximation, and this option sets only one Region.
others.D: Weighted routing splits traffic evenly regardless of where users are, increasing load time for many users.

q: A company has 5 PB of archived data on physical tapes. The company needs to preserve the data on the tapes for another 10 years for compliance purposes. The company wants to migrate to AWS in the next 6 months. The data center that stores the tapes has a 1 Gbps uplink internet connectivity. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Read the data from the tapes on premises. Stage the data in a local NFS storage. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
o.B: Use an on-premises backup application to read the data from the tapes and to write directly to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
o.C: Order multiple AWS Snowball devices that have Tape Gateway. Copy the physical tapes to virtual tapes in Snowball. Ship the Snowball devices to AWS. Create a lifecycle policy to move the tapes to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
o.D: Configure an on-premises Tape Gateway. Create virtual tapes in the AWS Cloud. Use backup software to copy the physical tape to the virtual tape.

e.why: At 1 Gbps, 5 PB would take over a year to upload, missing the 6-month deadline. Snowball devices with Tape Gateway let you copy physical tapes to virtual tapes offline, ship them to AWS, and then archive the virtual tapes to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, the lowest-cost storage for 10-year compliance retention.

others.A: Transferring 5 PB over a 1 Gbps link with DataSync takes well over a year, and Glacier Flexible Retrieval costs more than Deep Archive.
others.B: Writing directly over the network suffers the same bandwidth limit and cannot finish in 6 months.
others.D: An on-premises Tape Gateway still uploads over the 1 Gbps connection, which is too slow for 5 PB.

e.tip: Estimate transfer time: 1 Gbps is roughly 10 TB per day at best; petabytes means Snow Family.

q: A company is deploying an application that processes large quantities of data in parallel. The company plans to use Amazon EC2 instances for the workload. The network architecture must be configurable to prevent groups of nodes from sharing the same underlying hardware. Which networking solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Run the EC2 instances in a spread placement group.
o.B: Group the EC2 instances in separate accounts.
o.C: Configure the EC2 instances with dedicated tenancy.
o.D: Configure the EC2 instances with shared tenancy.

e.why: A spread placement group places each instance on distinct underlying hardware with separate racks, power and network, and partition placement groups extend this to groups of nodes on separate partitions. This lets you configure the placement so instances do not share the same hardware, reducing correlated failures.

others.B: Separate accounts do not control physical hardware placement.
others.C: Dedicated tenancy isolates your instances from other customers but your own instances can still share the same host hardware.
others.D: Shared tenancy gives no control over hardware placement.

e.tip: Spread = max 7 instances per AZ on distinct hardware; partition = groups of instances on separate racks for large distributed workloads.

q: A solutions architect is designing a disaster recovery (DR) strategy to provide Amazon EC2 capacity in a failover AWS Region. Business requirements state that the DR strategy must meet capacity in the failover Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Purchase On-Demand Instances in the failover Region.
o.B: Purchase an EC2 Savings Plan in the failover Region.
o.C: Purchase regional Reserved Instances in the failover Region.
o.D: Purchase a Capacity Reservation in the failover Region.

e.why: On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve EC2 capacity for a specific instance type in a specific Availability Zone for any duration, guaranteeing that the capacity will be available when failover happens. This is the only option that explicitly guarantees capacity in the DR Region.

others.A: On-Demand Instances have no capacity guarantee and may hit insufficient capacity errors during a regional event.
others.B: Savings Plans are a pricing commitment and do not reserve capacity.
others.C: Regional Reserved Instances provide a discount but do not reserve capacity; only zonal RIs reserve capacity.

e.tip: Guaranteed capacity = Capacity Reservation (or zonal RI); Savings Plans and regional RIs are just discounts.

q: A company has five organizational units (OUs) as part of its organization in AWS Organizations. Each OU correlates to the five businesses that the company owns. The company's research and development (R&D) business is separating from the company and will need its own organization. A solutions architect creates a separate new management account for this purpose. What should the solutions architect do next in the new management account?

o.A: Have the R&D AWS account be part of both organizations during the transition.
o.B: Invite the R&D AWS account to be part of the new organization after the R&D AWS account has left the prior organization.
o.C: Create a new R&D AWS account in the new organization. Migrate resources from the prior R&D AWS account to the new R&D AWS account.
o.D: Have the R&D AWS account join the new organization. Make the new management account a member of the prior organization.

e.why: An AWS account can belong to only one organization at a time. The R&D account must first leave the prior organization (which requires it to have standalone billing information), and then the new management account invites it to join the new organization.

others.A: An account cannot be a member of two organizations at the same time.
others.C: Creating a new account and migrating resources is unnecessary effort when the existing account can move.
others.D: A management account cannot be a member of another organization, and an account cannot be in two organizations.

e.tip: Moving accounts between organizations: leave the old one, then accept the invitation to the new one.

q: A company is designing a solution to capture customer activity in different web applications to process analytics and make predictions. Customer activity in the web applications is unpredictable and can increase suddenly. The company requires a solution that integrates with other web applications. The solution must include an authorization step for security purposes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Authorization is resolved at the GWLB.
o.B: Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis data stream that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.
o.C: Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an API Gateway Lambda authorizer to resolve authorization.
o.D: Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.

e.why: Amazon API Gateway provides a public endpoint that other web applications can integrate with, and a Lambda authorizer performs the authorization step before requests are accepted. API Gateway can proxy directly to Kinesis Data Firehose, which scales automatically with sudden spikes and delivers the data to S3 for analytics.

others.A: A Gateway Load Balancer is for deploying third-party virtual appliances such as firewalls and cannot perform authorization; ECS on EFS adds management.
others.B: Kinesis Data Streams does not store data in S3 by itself, and a separate Lambda function is not an authorization step in the request path.
others.D: A Gateway Load Balancer is not meant for web application ingestion, and the setup requires managing containers and storage.

e.tip: Custom authorization in front of an API = API Gateway Lambda authorizer (or Cognito authorizer).

q: An ecommerce company wants a disaster recovery solution for its Amazon RDS DB instances that run Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise Edition. The company's current recovery point objective (RPO) and recovery time objective (RTO) are 24 hours. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create a cross-Region read replica and promote the read replica to the primary instance.
o.B: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create RDS cross-Region replication.
o.C: Use cross-Region replication every 24 hours to copy native backups to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.D: Copy automatic snapshots to another Region every 24 hours.

e.why: With an RPO and RTO of 24 hours, copying RDS automated snapshots to another Region daily (RDS supports cross-Region automated backup replication) is enough: in a disaster you restore from the most recent copy. It avoids paying for a continuously running standby, making it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: A cross-Region read replica runs a second Enterprise Edition instance continuously, which is expensive and exceeds the requirement.
others.B: DMS cross-Region replication requires running a replication instance and a target database continuously, adding cost.
others.C: Native backups to S3 with cross-Region replication work but involve more setup and slower restores than snapshot copies.

e.tip: Long RPO/RTO (hours) = backup and restore; seconds/minutes = replicas or warm standby.

q: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer that has sticky sessions enabled. The web server currently hosts the user session state. The company wants to ensure high availability and avoid user session state loss in the event of a web server outage. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance to store the session data. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Memcached to store the session state.
o.B: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state.
o.C: Use an AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store session data. Update the application to use AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store the session state.
o.D: Use Amazon RDS to store the session state. Update the application to use Amazon RDS to store the session state.

e.why: Storing session state in Amazon ElastiCache for Redis moves it off the web servers, so an instance failure does not lose sessions. Redis supports replication with Multi-AZ automatic failover and persistence, providing high availability for the session store.

others.A: Memcached has no replication or persistence, so a node failure loses session data.
others.C: Storage Gateway cached volumes are for hybrid on-premises storage, not a session store for EC2 applications.
others.D: RDS can store sessions but has higher latency and is more costly than an in-memory store for session data.

e.tip: HA session store = ElastiCache for Redis (or DynamoDB); Memcached lacks replication.

q: A company migrated a MySQL database from the company's on-premises data center to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The company sized the RDS DB instance to meet the company's average daily workload. Once a month, the database performs slowly when the company runs queries for a report. The company wants to have the ability to run reports and maintain the performance of the daily workloads. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a read replica of the database. Direct the queries to the read replica.
o.B: Create a backup of the database. Restore the backup to another DB instance. Direct the queries to the new database.
o.C: Export the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the S3 bucket.
o.D: Resize the DB instance to accommodate the additional workload.

e.why: An RDS read replica is kept in sync asynchronously with the primary, and directing the monthly reporting queries to the replica offloads them from the primary. The daily workload keeps its performance without resizing the primary.

others.B: Restoring a backup each month gives stale data and requires repeated manual effort.
others.C: Exporting to S3 and querying with Athena adds a data pipeline and data may be stale.
others.D: Resizing the instance for a once-a-month peak means paying for extra capacity all month.

e.tip: Offload reporting from the primary = read replica.

q: A company runs a container application by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application includes microservices that manage customers and place orders. The company needs to route incoming requests to the appropriate microservices. Which solution will meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision a Network Load Balancer.
o.B: Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision an Application Load Balancer.
o.C: Use an AWS Lambda function to connect the requests to Amazon EKS.
o.D: Use Amazon API Gateway to connect the requests to Amazon EKS.

e.why: The AWS Load Balancer Controller creates an Application Load Balancer from Kubernetes Ingress resources, and the ALB does path-based and host-based layer 7 routing to the customer and order microservices. One ALB can serve multiple services, making it the most cost-effective way to route requests.

others.A: A Network Load Balancer works at layer 4 and cannot route by URL path or host to different microservices.
others.C: A Lambda function to forward requests is custom code that adds latency and cost.
others.D: API Gateway in front of EKS still needs a load balancer or VPC link and adds per-request cost.

e.tip: Path/host routing to Kubernetes services = ALB via AWS Load Balancer Controller Ingress.

q: A company uses AWS and sells access to copyrighted images. The company’s global customer base needs to be able to access these images quickly. The company must deny access to users from specific countries. The company wants to minimize costs as much as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) and public bucket access. Provide customers with a link to the S3 bucket.
o.B: Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Create an IAM user for each customer. Add the users to a group that has permission to access the S3 bucket.
o.C: Use Amazon EC2 instances that are behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) to store the images. Deploy the instances only in the countries the company services. Provide customers with links to the ALBs for their specific country's instances.
o.D: Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Use Amazon CloudFront to distribute the images with geographic restrictions. Provide a signed URL for each customer to access the data in CloudFront.

e.why: S3 stores the images cheaply and CloudFront caches them at edge locations so global customers get fast access. CloudFront geographic restrictions block viewers from specific countries, and signed URLs ensure only paying customers can download the copyrighted images, all at low cost.

others.A: A public bucket exposes copyrighted images to anyone and MFA does not apply to anonymous public access; there is no country blocking or global caching.
others.B: Creating an IAM user per customer does not scale, is not meant for end customers, and provides no geo blocking or edge caching.
others.C: EC2 instances and ALBs for storing images are costly, and deploying per country does not actually block users from other countries.

e.tip: Paid content + country blocking + global speed = S3 + CloudFront signed URLs + geo restriction.

q: A solutions architect is designing a highly available Amazon ElastiCache for Redis based solution. The solutions architect needs to ensure that failures do not result in performance degradation or loss of data locally and within an AWS Region. The solution needs to provide high availability at the node level and at the Region level. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Multi-AZ Redis replication groups with shards that contain multiple nodes.
o.B: Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Redis append only files (AOF) turned on.
o.C: Use a Multi-AZ Redis cluster with more than one read replica in the replication group.
o.D: Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Auto Scaling turned on.

e.why: A Multi-AZ Redis replication group with cluster mode shards, each containing a primary and replicas in different AZs, provides node-level redundancy and automatic failover to a replica in another AZ. Spreading shards and replicas across AZs protects against both node failures and AZ failures within the Region without losing data or capacity.

others.B: AOF persistence helps recover data after a restart but does not provide Multi-AZ failover, and it is not supported on newer Redis versions in ElastiCache.
others.C: More read replicas in a single replication group helps, but without sharding the loss of capacity affects the whole dataset; the key prefers sharded Multi-AZ groups.
others.D: Auto Scaling adjusts capacity for load and does not provide failover or data protection.

e.tip: ElastiCache Redis HA = Multi-AZ with automatic failover and replicas in other AZs.

q: A company plans to migrate to AWS and use Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances for its application. During the migration testing phase, a technical team observes that the application takes a long time to launch and load memory to become fully productive. Which solution will reduce the launch time of the application during the next testing phase?

o.A: Launch two or more EC2 On-Demand Instances. Turn on auto scaling features and make the EC2 On-Demand Instances available during the next testing phase.
o.B: Launch EC2 Spot Instances to support the application and to scale the application so it is available during the next testing phase.
o.C: Launch the EC2 On-Demand Instances with hibernation turned on. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools during the next testing phase.
o.D: Launch EC2 On-Demand Instances with Capacity Reservations. Start additional EC2 instances during the next testing phase.

e.why: EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools keep pre-initialized instances ready, and with hibernation the instances' in-memory state (RAM) is saved to EBS. When scaled out, hibernated instances resume with memory already loaded, eliminating the long launch and warm-up time.

others.A: Running more instances with auto scaling does not reduce the time each new instance needs to launch and load memory.
others.B: Spot Instances lower cost but still need the same launch and load time and can be interrupted.
others.D: Capacity Reservations guarantee capacity but do not speed up application initialization.

e.tip: Slow-to-initialize apps = Auto Scaling warm pools (stopped, running or hibernated).

q: A company's applications run on Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. The company notices that its applications experience sudden traffic increases on random days of the week. The company wants to maintain application performance during sudden traffic increases. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use manual scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
o.B: Use predictive scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
o.C: Use dynamic scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
o.D: Use schedule scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.

e.why: Dynamic scaling (for example target tracking on CPU or request count) adds instances in response to real-time metrics when sudden traffic arrives on unpredictable days and removes them afterward. You pay for extra capacity only when needed, making it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Manual scaling cannot react quickly to sudden, random spikes.
others.B: Predictive scaling relies on recurring daily or weekly patterns, which do not exist for random traffic.
others.D: Scheduled scaling needs known times, but the spikes happen on random days.

e.tip: Random spikes = dynamic (target tracking); recurring pattern = predictive or scheduled.

q: An ecommerce application uses a PostgreSQL database that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. During a monthly sales event, database usage increases and causes database connection issues for the application. The traffic is unpredictable for subsequent monthly sales events, which impacts the sales forecast. The company needs to maintain performance when there is an unpredictable increase in traffic. Which solution resolves this issue in the MOST cost-effective way?

o.A: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora Serverless v2.
o.B: Enable auto scaling for the PostgreSQL database on the EC2 instance to accommodate increased usage.
o.C: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with a larger instance type.
o.D: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Redshift to accommodate increased usage.

e.why: Aurora Serverless v2 is PostgreSQL-compatible and scales capacity automatically in fine-grained increments as demand rises, then scales back down after the sales event. You pay only for capacity used, which handles unpredictable spikes cost-effectively and avoids connection issues caused by an undersized server.

others.B: A single PostgreSQL database on EC2 cannot be auto scaled like a stateless tier; Auto Scaling would launch separate, inconsistent databases.
others.C: A larger RDS instance means paying for peak capacity all month while traffic is unpredictable.
others.D: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse and not suitable as a transactional ecommerce database.

e.tip: Unpredictable relational load, pay for usage = Aurora Serverless v2.

q: A company hosts an internal serverless application on AWS by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The company’s employees report issues with high latency when they begin using the application each day. The company wants to reduce latency. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Increase the API Gateway throttling limit.
o.B: Set up a scheduled scaling to increase Lambda provisioned concurrency before employees begin to use the application each day.
o.C: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to initiate a Lambda function as a target for the alarm at the beginning of each day.
o.D: Increase the Lambda function memory.

e.why: The latency at the start of each day comes from Lambda cold starts after the functions sit idle overnight. Using Application Auto Scaling scheduled actions to raise provisioned concurrency just before employees start keeps execution environments pre-initialized, eliminating the cold start latency, and can be lowered after hours to save cost.

others.A: Throttling limits control request rates; they do not reduce cold-start latency.
others.C: Invoking one function from an alarm warms at most a single environment and is a fragile workaround.
others.D: More memory can speed execution somewhat but does not eliminate cold starts.

e.tip: Predictable daily cold starts = scheduled provisioned concurrency.

q: A research company uses on-premises devices to generate data for analysis. The company wants to use the AWS Cloud to analyze the data. The devices generate .csv files and support writing the data to an SMB file share. Company analysts must be able to use SQL commands to query the data. The analysts will run queries periodically throughout the day. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose three.)

o.A: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway on premises in Amazon S3 File Gateway mode.
o.B: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway on premises in Amazon FSx File Gateway made.
o.C: Set up an AWS Glue crawler to create a table based on the data that is in Amazon S3.
o.D: Set up an Amazon EMR cluster with EMR File System (EMRFS) to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.
o.E: Set up an Amazon Redshift cluster to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.
o.F: Setup Amazon Athena to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.

e.why: An S3 File Gateway presents an SMB share on premises that the devices write .csv files to, storing them as objects in S3 (A). An AWS Glue crawler infers the schema and creates a table in the Data Catalog (C), and Amazon Athena lets analysts run SQL on the S3 data paying only per query (F), which is most cost-effective for periodic queries.

others.B: FSx File Gateway caches access to FSx for Windows File Server, which stores files in FSx rather than S3 and costs more for this use case.
others.D: An EMR cluster is costly and operationally heavy for periodic SQL queries.
others.E: A running Redshift cluster costs more than per-query Athena for occasional queries.

e.tip: SMB/NFS to S3 = S3 File Gateway; ad hoc SQL on S3 = Glue crawler + Athena.

q: A company wants to use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) clusters and Amazon RDS DB instances to build and run a payment processing application. The company will run the application in its on-premises data center for compliance purposes. A solutions architect wants to use AWS Outposts as part of the solution. The solutions architect is working with the company's operational team to build the application. Which activities are the responsibility of the company's operational team? (Choose three.)

o.A: Providing resilient power and network connectivity to the Outposts racks
o.B: Managing the virtualization hypervisor, storage systems, and the AWS services that run on Outposts
o.C: Physical security and access controls of the data center environment
o.D: Availability of the Outposts infrastructure including the power supplies, servers, and networking equipment within the Outposts racks
o.E: Physical maintenance of Outposts components
o.F: Providing extra capacity for Amazon ECS clusters to mitigate server failures and maintenance events

e.why: Under the Outposts shared responsibility model, the customer must provide resilient power, cooling and network connectivity to the racks (A), physical security and access control for the data center (C), and plan for enough spare capacity (such as additional ECS capacity) to tolerate server failures and maintenance (F).

others.B: AWS manages the Outposts hypervisor, storage systems and AWS services running on the Outpost.
others.D: AWS is responsible for the availability of the Outposts infrastructure inside the racks, including servers, power supplies and networking equipment.
others.E: AWS performs physical maintenance and replacement of Outposts components.

e.tip: Outposts: customer handles the facility (power, network, security) and capacity planning; AWS handles the rack hardware and software.

q: A company is planning to migrate a TCP-based application into the company's VPC. The application is publicly accessible on a nonstandard TCP port through a hardware appliance in the company's data center. This public endpoint can process up to 3 million requests per second with low latency. The company requires the same level of performance for the new public endpoint in AWS. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

o.A: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Configure the NLB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.
o.B: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the ALB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.
o.C: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution that listens on the TCP port that the application requires. Use an Application Load Balancer as the origin.
o.D: Deploy an Amazon API Gateway API that is configured with the TCP port that the application requires. Configure AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency to process the requests.

e.why: A Network Load Balancer operates at layer 4, supports any TCP port, and can handle millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency. It can be internet-facing with static IPs, matching the hardware appliance's performance for a nonstandard TCP port.

others.B: An ALB works at layer 7 for HTTP/HTTPS only and cannot handle raw TCP traffic.
others.C: CloudFront handles HTTP/HTTPS on standard ports and cannot listen on arbitrary TCP ports.
others.D: API Gateway handles HTTP/REST/WebSocket APIs, not raw TCP on a custom port.

e.tip: TCP/UDP, extreme performance or static IPs = NLB.

q: A company runs its critical database on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The company wants to migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime and data loss. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create a DB snapshot of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance to populate a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
o.B: Create an Aurora read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Promote the Aurora read replicate to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
o.C: Use data import from Amazon S3 to migrate the database to an Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
o.D: Use the pg_dump utility to back up the RDS for PostgreSQL database. Restore the backup to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.

e.why: Creating an Aurora read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL instance continuously replicates data into a new Aurora cluster. When replica lag reaches zero, you stop writes briefly and promote the replica to a standalone Aurora PostgreSQL cluster, giving minimal downtime and data loss with very little operational effort.

others.A: Restoring from a snapshot misses all writes made after the snapshot, causing data loss or longer downtime.
others.C: Importing from S3 requires exporting data first and does not keep the target in sync, causing downtime.
others.D: pg_dump and restore requires downtime for consistency and is slow and manual for a critical database.

e.tip: RDS MySQL/PostgreSQL to Aurora with minimal downtime = Aurora read replica, then promote.

q: A company's infrastructure consists of hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage. A solutions architect must ensure that every EC2 instance can be recovered after a disaster. What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of effort?

o.A: Take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance. Create an AWS CloudFormation template to launch new EC2 instances from the EBS storage.
o.B: Take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to set the environment based on the EC2 template and attach the EBS storage.
o.C: Use AWS Backup to set up a backup plan for the entire group of EC2 instances. Use the AWS Backup API or the AWS CLI to speed up the restore process for multiple EC2 instances.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda function to take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance and copy the Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). Create another Lambda function to perform the restores with the copied AMIs and attach the EBS storage.

e.why: AWS Backup centrally automates backup plans for EC2 instances, creating AMIs with EBS snapshots on a schedule with retention rules and optional cross-Region or cross-account copies. Restores can be scripted for many instances with the AWS Backup API or CLI, giving recoverability for hundreds of instances with the least effort.

others.A: Manual snapshots per instance plus custom CloudFormation templates require significant ongoing effort.
others.B: Elastic Beanstalk is an application deployment service, not a DR mechanism for existing EC2 instances.
others.D: Custom Lambda functions for backup and restore must be written and maintained, which is more effort than AWS Backup.

e.tip: Centralized, policy-based backup across services = AWS Backup.

q: A company recently migrated to the AWS Cloud. The company wants a serverless solution for large-scale parallel on-demand processing of a semistructured dataset. The data consists of logs, media files, sales transactions, and IoT sensor data that is stored in Amazon S3. The company wants the solution to process thousands of items in the dataset in parallel. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Use the AWS Step Functions Map state in Inline mode to process the data in parallel.
o.B: Use the AWS Step Functions Map state in Distributed mode to process the data in parallel.
o.C: Use AWS Glue to process the data in parallel.
o.D: Use several AWS Lambda functions to process the data in parallel.

e.why: The Step Functions Map state in Distributed mode runs up to 10,000 parallel child workflow executions and can iterate directly over objects in an S3 bucket or items in large S3 files. It is serverless and designed for large-scale parallel processing of S3 datasets, giving the most operational efficiency.

others.A: Inline Map mode supports only up to 40 concurrent iterations and limited state history, so it does not scale to thousands of items.
others.C: AWS Glue suits ETL jobs but is less suited to arbitrary per-item processing of mixed media, logs and IoT data on demand.
others.D: Coordinating several Lambda functions manually requires custom orchestration, error handling and fan-out logic.

e.tip: Massive parallel processing over S3 objects = Step Functions Distributed Map.

q: A company will migrate 10 PB of data to Amazon S3 in 6 weeks. The current data center has a 500 Mbps uplink to the internet. Other on-premises applications share the uplink. The company can use 80% of the internet bandwidth for this one-time migration task. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 and to automatically verify the data.
o.B: Use rsync to transfer the data directly to Amazon S3.
o.C: Use the AWS CLI and multiple copy processes to send the data directly to Amazon S3.
o.D: Order multiple AWS Snowball devices. Copy the data to the devices. Send the devices to AWS to copy the data to Amazon S3.

e.why: 80 percent of 500 Mbps is 400 Mbps, about 4.3 TB per day, so moving 10 PB over the network would take around 6 years. Multiple AWS Snowball devices transfer the data offline and AWS imports it into S3, which is the only way to finish in 6 weeks.

others.A: DataSync still uses the 400 Mbps link, which is far too slow for 10 PB in 6 weeks.
others.B: rsync over the same limited link is too slow and cannot write directly to S3.
others.C: Parallel CLI copies cannot exceed the available bandwidth, so the transfer would still take years.

e.tip: Calculate days = data / bandwidth; if it exceeds the deadline, use Snow Family.

q: A company has several on-premises Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (ISCSI) network storage servers. The company wants to reduce the number of these servers by moving to the AWS Cloud. A solutions architect must provide low-latency access to frequently used data and reduce the dependency on on-premises servers with a minimal number of infrastructure changes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway.
o.B: Deploy Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage with backups to Amazon S3.
o.C: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is configured with stored volumes.
o.D: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is configured with cached volumes.

e.why: A Storage Gateway volume gateway presents iSCSI volumes, so existing iSCSI clients need minimal changes. In cached volume mode the primary data is stored in S3 while frequently accessed data is cached locally for low latency, reducing the on-premises storage footprint.

others.A: S3 File Gateway provides NFS/SMB file shares, not iSCSI block storage, so it would require infrastructure changes.
others.B: EBS volumes attach only to EC2 instances in AWS and cannot be mounted by on-premises iSCSI servers.
others.C: Stored volumes keep the full dataset on premises with asynchronous backup to AWS, so it does not reduce on-premises storage dependency.

e.tip: Volume gateway: cached = data in S3, hot cache locally; stored = data locally, snapshots in AWS.

q: A solutions architect is designing an application that will allow business users to upload objects to Amazon S3. The solution needs to maximize object durability. Objects also must be readily available at any time and for any length of time. Users will access objects frequently within the first 30 days after the objects are uploaded, but users are much less likely to access objects that are older than 30 days. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Glacier after 30 days.
o.B: Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
o.C: Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.
o.D: Store all the objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.

e.why: S3 Standard handles frequent access for the first 30 days, then a lifecycle rule moves objects to S3 Standard-IA, which keeps millisecond access and multi-AZ eleven-nines durability at a lower storage price. This satisfies immediate availability for any length of time while minimizing cost.

others.A: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval requires restores taking minutes to hours, so objects are not readily available.
others.C: One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, which reduces resilience and does not maximize durability against AZ loss.
others.D: Intelligent-Tiering already moves objects between tiers automatically; adding a lifecycle rule to Standard-IA is redundant and Intelligent-Tiering adds monitoring fees.

e.tip: Needs instant access + rarely read = Standard-IA; One Zone-IA only for re-creatable data.

q: A company has migrated a two-tier application from its on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The data tier is a Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for Oracle with 12 TB of General Purpose SSD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage. The application is designed to process and store documents in the database as binary large objects (blobs) with an average document size of 6 MB. The database size has grown over time, reducing the performance and increasing the cost of storage. The company must improve the database performance and needs a solution that is highly available and resilient. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Reduce the RDS DB instance size. Increase the storage capacity to 24 TiB. Change the storage type to Magnetic.
o.B: Increase the RDS DB instance size. Increase the storage capacity to 24 TiChange the storage type to Provisioned IOPS.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the application to store documents in the S3 bucket. Store the object metadata in the existing database.
o.D: Create an Amazon DynamoDB table. Update the application to use DynamoDB. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate data from the Oracle database to DynamoDB.

e.why: Storing 6 MB documents as blobs bloats the RDS database, increasing expensive EBS storage and hurting performance. Moving the documents to Amazon S3, which is highly durable, highly available and much cheaper per GB, and keeping only metadata and S3 keys in the database shrinks the database and improves performance most cost-effectively.

others.A: Magnetic storage is legacy, slower and would further hurt performance.
others.B: A larger instance and Provisioned IOPS storage greatly increase cost while keeping the blobs in the database.
others.D: DynamoDB items are limited to 400 KB, so 6 MB documents cannot be stored as items, and the rewrite is significant.

e.tip: Large binary objects belong in S3 with pointers in the database.

q: A company has an application that serves clients that are deployed in more than 20.000 retail storefront locations around the world. The application consists of backend web services that are exposed over HTTPS on port 443. The application is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The retail locations communicate with the web application over the public internet. The company allows each retail location to register the IP address that the retail location has been allocated by its local ISP. The company's security team recommends to increase the security of the application endpoint by restricting access to only the IP addresses registered by the retail locations. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALB. Use IP rule sets on the ALB to filter traffic. Update the IP addresses in the rule to include the registered IP addresses.
o.B: Deploy AWS Firewall Manager to manage the ALConfigure firewall rules to restrict traffic to the ALModify the firewall rules to include the registered IP addresses.
o.C: Store the IP addresses in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure an AWS Lambda authorization function on the ALB to validate that incoming requests are from the registered IP addresses.
o.D: Configure the network ACL on the subnet that contains the public interface of the ALB. Update the ingress rules on the network ACL with entries for each of the registered IP addresses.

e.why: Associating an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALB and using an IP set match rule lets you allow only the registered retail IP addresses and block everything else. IP sets can hold up to 10,000 CIDRs each and several can be referenced, so 20,000 addresses fit, and they can be updated without touching the application.

others.B: Firewall Manager centrally manages WAF and security group policies across accounts; it is unnecessary for one ALB and still relies on WAF rules.
others.C: ALBs do not support Lambda authorizers; that is an API Gateway feature.
others.D: Network ACLs are limited to about 20 rules by default (40 maximum), far too few for 20,000 IP addresses.

e.tip: Large IP allow lists in front of ALB, API Gateway or CloudFront = AWS WAF IP sets.

q: A company is building a data analysis platform on AWS by using AWS Lake Formation. The platform will ingest data from different sources such as Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS. The company needs a secure solution to prevent access to portions of the data that contain sensitive information. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an IAM role that includes permissions to access Lake Formation tables.
o.B: Create data filters to implement row-level security and cell-level security.
o.C: Create an AWS Lambda function that removes sensitive information before Lake Formation ingests the data.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that periodically queries and removes sensitive information from Lake Formation tables.

e.why: Lake Formation data filters provide column-level, row-level and cell-level security on Data Catalog tables, so users can query tables while sensitive portions are hidden. It is built-in, declarative permission management, which has the least operational overhead.

others.A: An IAM role granting table access gives access to entire tables and cannot hide specific rows or cells.
others.C: A Lambda function that strips data before ingestion removes it for everyone and is custom code to maintain.
others.D: Periodically deleting sensitive data with Lambda is custom, error prone and leaves exposure windows.

e.tip: Fine-grained access in a data lake = Lake Formation data filters (row, column and cell level).

q: A company deploys Amazon EC2 instances that run in a VPC. The EC2 instances load source data into Amazon S3 buckets so that the data can be processed in the future. According to compliance laws, the data must not be transmitted over the public internet. Servers in the company's on-premises data center will consume the output from an application that runs on the EC2 instances. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon EC2. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.
o.B: Deploy a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises network and the VPC.
o.C: Set up an AWS Transit Gateway connection from the VPC to the S3 buckets. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.
o.D: Set up proxy EC2 instances that have routes to NAT gateways. Configure the proxy EC2 instances to fetch S3 data and feed the application instances.

e.why: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 lets the EC2 instances write to S3 over the AWS network without traversing the internet. AWS Direct Connect provides a private dedicated connection between the on-premises data center and the VPC, so the output is consumed without using the public internet.

others.A: An interface endpoint for EC2 covers the EC2 API, not S3, and Site-to-Site VPN traffic travels over the public internet, even though encrypted.
others.C: Transit Gateway does not connect directly to S3 buckets, and the VPN uses the public internet.
others.D: NAT gateways send S3 traffic over the public internet, violating the compliance requirement.

e.tip: No public internet at all: VPC endpoints inside AWS, Direct Connect to on-premises (VPN still rides the internet).

q: A company has an application with a REST-based interface that allows data to be received in near-real time from a third-party vendor. Once received, the application processes and stores the data for further analysis. The application is running on Amazon EC2 instances. The third-party vendor has received many 503 Service Unavailable Errors when sending data to the application. When the data volume spikes, the compute capacity reaches its maximum limit and the application is unable to process all requests. Which design should a solutions architect recommend to provide a more scalable solution?

o.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the data. Process the data using AWS Lambda functions.
o.B: Use Amazon API Gateway on top of the existing application. Create a usage plan with a quota limit for the third-party vendor.
o.C: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to ingest the data. Put the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
o.D: Repackage the application as a container. Deploy the application using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) using the EC2 launch type with an Auto Scaling group.

e.why: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams ingests and buffers high-volume data in near real time and scales with shards (or on-demand mode), so spikes are absorbed instead of returning 503 errors. Lambda consumes records from the stream and scales processing automatically, decoupling ingestion from compute capacity.

others.B: A usage plan quota throttles the vendor, which rejects data instead of processing it.
others.C: SNS is a pub/sub notification service without durable buffering for stream processing, and the vendor's REST calls would still hit limited EC2 capacity.
others.D: Containerizing on ECS with the EC2 launch type still has a capacity ceiling and does not buffer spikes.

e.tip: Ingestion spikes overwhelming compute = put a buffer (Kinesis or SQS) in front and decouple.

q: A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. The application needs to process sensitive information from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application must not use the internet to connect to the S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure an internet gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the internet gateway. Update the application to use the new internet gateway.
o.B: Configure a VPN connection. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPN connection. Update the application to use the new VPN connection.
o.C: Configure a NAT gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the NAT gateway. Update the application to use the new NAT gateway.
o.D: Configure a VPC endpoint. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPC endpoint. Update the application to use the new VPC endpoint.

e.why: A VPC endpoint for S3 (gateway or interface) gives the private subnet a route to S3 over the AWS network without internet access. The bucket policy can restrict access with the aws:SourceVpce condition so only requests through that endpoint are allowed.

others.A: An internet gateway sends traffic over the public internet, and bucket policies cannot reference an internet gateway.
others.B: A VPN connects networks to the VPC; it does not provide private access from the VPC to S3.
others.C: A NAT gateway routes S3 traffic through the internet path, violating the requirement.

e.tip: Restrict a bucket to VPC traffic = VPC endpoint plus aws:SourceVpce in the bucket policy.

q: A company uses Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to run a container application. The EKS cluster stores sensitive information in the Kubernetes secrets object. The company wants to ensure that the information is encrypted. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use the container application to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
o.B: Enable secrets encryption in the EKS cluster by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
o.C: Implement an AWS Lambda function to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
o.D: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

e.why: Amazon EKS supports envelope encryption of Kubernetes secrets with an AWS KMS key, which can be enabled on new or existing clusters with one setting. Secrets are then encrypted before being stored in etcd, without any application changes, giving the least operational overhead.

others.A: Encrypting in the application requires code changes and key handling in every container.
others.C: A Lambda function for encryption is custom code and does not integrate with Kubernetes secrets.
others.D: Parameter Store would move secrets outside Kubernetes and require application and integration changes.

e.tip: EKS secrets encryption at rest = KMS envelope encryption setting on the cluster.

q: A company is designing a new multi-tier web application that consists of the following components: • Web and application servers that run on Amazon EC2 instances as part of Auto Scaling groups • An Amazon RDS DB instance for data storage A solutions architect needs to limit access to the application servers so that only the web servers can access them. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy AWS PrivateLink in front of the application servers. Configure the network ACL to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
o.B: Deploy a VPC endpoint in front of the application servers. Configure the security group to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
o.C: Deploy a Network Load Balancer with a target group that contains the application servers' Auto Scaling group. Configure the network ACL to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
o.D: Deploy an Application Load Balancer with a target group that contains the application servers' Auto Scaling group. Configure the security group to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.

e.why: An Application Load Balancer in front of the application tier's Auto Scaling group distributes traffic from the web servers, and the application servers' security group allows inbound traffic only from the ALB (with the ALB's security group allowing only the web servers' security group). Security group referencing is stateful and adapts automatically as instances scale.

others.A: PrivateLink is for exposing services across VPCs or accounts, and network ACLs cannot reference changing Auto Scaling instances.
others.B: VPC endpoints provide access to AWS or PrivateLink services; they are not placed in front of your own servers inside the same VPC.
others.C: Network ACLs are subnet-level, stateless and IP-based, so they cannot easily restrict access to dynamically scaling web servers.

e.tip: Tier-to-tier access control = security groups that reference other security groups.

q: A company runs a critical, customer-facing application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application has a microservices architecture. The company needs to implement a solution that collects, aggregates, and summarizes metrics and logs from the application in a centralized location. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Run the Amazon CloudWatch agent in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.
o.B: Run AWS App Mesh in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the App Mesh console.
o.C: Configure AWS CloudTrail to capture data events. Query CloudTrail by using Amazon OpenSearch Service.
o.D: Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.

e.why: CloudWatch Container Insights collects, aggregates and summarizes metrics and logs from EKS clusters, nodes, pods and services (now with enhanced observability), and displays them in curated CloudWatch dashboards. It is purpose-built for containerized microservices, providing the centralized view required.

others.A: Running the plain CloudWatch agent collects raw metrics and logs but does not automatically aggregate and summarize them per cluster, pod and service.
others.B: App Mesh is a service mesh for traffic management and is being discontinued; it is not a centralized metrics and log console.
others.C: CloudTrail data events record AWS API activity, not application metrics and logs.

e.tip: Container (ECS/EKS) metrics and logs summarized = CloudWatch Container Insights.

q: A company has deployed its newest product on AWS. The product runs in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer. The company stores the product’s objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company recently experienced malicious attacks against its systems. The company needs a solution that continuously monitors for malicious activity in the AWS account, workloads, and access patterns to the S3 bucket. The solution must also report suspicious activity and display the information on a dashboard. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure Amazon Macie to monitor and report findings to AWS Config.
o.B: Configure Amazon Inspector to monitor and report findings to AWS CloudTrail.
o.C: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor and report findings to AWS Security Hub.
o.D: Configure AWS Config to monitor and report findings to Amazon EventBridge.

e.why: Amazon GuardDuty continuously monitors CloudTrail management and S3 data events, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs and runtime activity to detect malicious behavior in the account, workloads and S3 access patterns. Its findings integrate with AWS Security Hub, which aggregates and displays them on dashboards.

others.A: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 rather than monitoring for malicious activity, and AWS Config is not a findings dashboard.
others.B: Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities, and CloudTrail records API calls; it does not display security findings.
others.D: AWS Config evaluates resource configuration compliance, not malicious activity.

e.tip: Threat detection = GuardDuty; central findings dashboard = Security Hub.

q: A company wants to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The data center hosts a storage server that stores data in an NFS-based file system. The storage server holds 200 GB of data. The company needs to migrate the data without interruption to existing services. Multiple resources in AWS must be able to access the data by using the NFS protocol. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system.
o.B: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to receive the data.
o.D: Manually use an operating system copy command to push the data into the AWS destination.
o.E: Install an AWS DataSync agent in the on-premises data center. Use a DataSync task between the on-premises location and AWS.

e.why: Amazon EFS provides a managed NFS file system that many AWS resources can mount concurrently (B). An AWS DataSync agent on premises copies the 200 GB from the NFS server to EFS online, with incremental transfers and verification, so existing services keep running during migration (E).

others.A: FSx for Lustre is a high-performance file system for HPC workloads and is more expensive than EFS for general NFS use.
others.C: Amazon S3 is object storage and is not accessed natively with NFS by AWS resources.
others.D: Manual OS copy commands lack incremental sync, verification and scheduling, risking interruption and inconsistency.

e.tip: NFS migration to AWS = DataSync to EFS.

q: A company wants to use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for its Amazon EC2 instances that have an SMB file share mounted as a volume in the us-east-1 Region. The company has a recovery point objective (RPO) of 5 minutes for planned system maintenance or unplanned service disruptions. The company needs to replicate the file system to the us-west-2 Region. The replicated data must not be deleted by any user for 5 years. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Single-AZ 2 deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.
o.B: Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Multi-AZ deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.
o.C: Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Multi-AZ deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.
o.D: Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Single-AZ 2 deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.

e.why: A Multi-AZ FSx for Windows File Server deployment keeps a standby file server in another AZ, so planned maintenance and AZ disruptions fail over automatically with minimal data loss. AWS Backup copies backups to us-west-2, and Vault Lock in compliance mode with a 5-year minimum retention prevents anyone, including the root user, from deleting them.
