others.A: Single-AZ 2 deployments have no standby in another AZ, so maintenance or an AZ disruption causes downtime and potential data loss.
others.B: Governance mode lets users with sufficient IAM permissions remove the lock or delete backups, so data is not protected from all users.
others.D: Single-AZ 2 is not resilient to AZ disruptions, and governance mode allows privileged deletion.

e.tip: Undeletable by anyone = compliance mode (Vault Lock or S3 Object Lock); governance mode can be bypassed.

q: A solutions architect is designing a security solution for a company that wants to provide developers with individual AWS accounts through AWS Organizations, while also maintaining standard security controls. Because the individual developers will have AWS account root user-level access to their own accounts, the solutions architect wants to ensure that the mandatory AWS CloudTrail configuration that is applied to new developer accounts is not modified. Which action meets these requirements?

o.A: Create an IAM policy that prohibits changes to CloudTrail. and attach it to the root user.
o.B: Create a new trail in CloudTrail from within the developer accounts with the organization trails option enabled.
o.C: Create a service control policy (SCP) that prohibits changes to CloudTrail, and attach it the developer accounts.
o.D: Create a service-linked role for CloudTrail with a policy condition that allows changes only from an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in the management account.

e.why: Service control policies in AWS Organizations restrict the maximum permissions for every principal in member accounts, including the root user. An SCP that denies CloudTrail actions such as StopLogging, DeleteTrail and UpdateTrail, attached to the developer accounts, prevents modification of the mandatory trail.

others.A: IAM policies cannot be attached to the root user, which has full permissions in its account.
others.B: An organization trail must be created from the management account (or delegated admin), and creating one does not stop developers from changing other settings.
others.D: Service-linked roles are defined by AWS services and cannot be used to block root user changes.

e.tip: Only SCPs can restrict a member account's root user.

q: A company is planning to deploy a business-critical application in the AWS Cloud. The application requires durable storage with consistent, low-latency performance. Which type of storage should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Instance store volume
o.B: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster
o.C: Provisioned IOPS SSD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume
o.D: Throughput Optimized HDD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume

e.why: Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) EBS volumes are designed for business-critical, latency-sensitive workloads, delivering consistent single-digit millisecond (io2 Block Express sub-millisecond) latency at the provisioned IOPS. EBS data persists independently of the instance and is replicated within the AZ, giving durability.

others.A: Instance store volumes are ephemeral; data is lost if the instance stops or fails, so it is not durable.
others.B: ElastiCache for Memcached is an in-memory cache without persistence or replication, so it is not durable storage.
others.D: Throughput Optimized HDD is for large sequential workloads and does not provide consistent low latency.

e.tip: Durable + consistent low latency + critical = Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2).

q: An online photo-sharing company stores its photos in an Amazon S3 bucket that exists in the us-west-1 Region. The company needs to store a copy of all new photos in the us-east-1 Region. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

o.A: Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy photos from the existing S3 bucket to the second S3 bucket.
o.B: Create a cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) configuration of the existing S3 bucket. Specify us-east-1 in the CORS rule's AllowedOrigin element.
o.C: Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1 across multiple Availability Zones. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to save photos into the second S3 bucket.
o.D: Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure S3 event notifications on object creation and update events to invoke an AWS Lambda function to copy photos from the existing S3 bucket to the second S3 bucket.

e.why: S3 Cross-Region Replication automatically and asynchronously copies new objects from the us-west-1 bucket to a bucket in us-east-1 once a replication rule is configured (with versioning on both buckets). It is fully managed, so it requires the least operational effort.

others.B: CORS controls which web origins can access the bucket from browsers; it does not copy objects.
others.C: S3 Lifecycle rules transition storage classes or expire objects within a bucket; they cannot copy objects to another bucket. All Standard buckets already span multiple AZs.
others.D: A Lambda function triggered by events works but is custom code to maintain, more effort than built-in replication.

e.tip: Copy new objects to another Region = CRR (existing objects need S3 Batch Replication).

q: A company is creating a new web application for its subscribers. The application will consist of a static single page and a persistent database layer. The application will have millions of users for 4 hours in the morning, but the application will have only a few thousand users during the rest of the day. The company's data architects have requested the ability to rapidly evolve their schema. Which solutions will meet these requirements and provide the MOST scalability? (Choose two.)

o.A: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB as the database solution. Provision on-demand capacity.
o.B: Deploy Amazon Aurora as the database solution. Choose the serverless DB engine mode.
o.C: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB as the database solution. Ensure that DynamoDB auto scaling is enabled.
o.D: Deploy the static content into an Amazon S3 bucket. Provision an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin.
o.E: Deploy the web servers for static content across a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. Configure the instances to periodically refresh the content from an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume.

e.why: DynamoDB is schemaless, allowing the data architects to evolve the schema rapidly, and on-demand capacity instantly accommodates the swing from millions of users in the morning to a few thousand later without capacity planning (A). Hosting the static single page in S3 behind CloudFront scales virtually without limit and caches content globally (D).

others.B: Aurora is relational with a fixed schema, which makes rapid schema evolution harder, and it scales less than DynamoDB for millions of users.
others.C: DynamoDB auto scaling reacts more slowly to sharp spikes, risking throttling, so on-demand offers more scalability for this pattern.
others.E: An EC2 fleet with EFS for static content adds management and scales less well than S3 with CloudFront.

e.tip: Flexible schema + spiky traffic = DynamoDB on-demand; static site = S3 + CloudFront.

q: A company uses Amazon API Gateway to manage its REST APIs that third-party service providers access. The company must protect the REST APIs from SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

o.A: Configure AWS Shield.
o.B: Configure AWS WAF.
o.C: Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS Shield in CloudFront.
o.D: Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS WAF in CloudFront.

e.why: AWS WAF can be associated directly with an API Gateway REST API stage and includes managed rule groups that detect SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. Attaching a web ACL with these rules is the most operationally efficient protection.

others.A: AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks, not application-layer SQL injection or XSS.
others.C: Shield does not inspect for SQL injection or XSS, and adding CloudFront is unnecessary.
others.D: WAF on CloudFront would work, but adding a CloudFront distribution is extra setup when WAF attaches directly to API Gateway.

e.tip: SQLi/XSS = AWS WAF; DDoS = Shield.

q: A company wants to provide users with access to AWS resources. The company has 1,500 users and manages their access to on-premises resources through Active Directory user groups on the corporate network. However, the company does not want users to have to maintain another identity to access the resources. A solutions architect must manage user access to the AWS resources while preserving access to the on-premises resources. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an IAM user for each user in the company. Attach the appropriate policies to each user.
o.B: Use Amazon Cognito with an Active Directory user pool. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached.
o.C: Define cross-account roles with the appropriate policies attached. Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.
o.D: Configure Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2 0-based federation. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.

e.why: SAML 2.0 federation between Active Directory (through AD FS or IAM Identity Center) and AWS lets users sign in with their existing corporate credentials. IAM roles with the appropriate policies are mapped to AD groups, so access is managed through existing group membership with no second identity and on-premises access unchanged.

others.A: Creating 1,500 IAM users means a second identity for each user and heavy administrative overhead.
others.B: Cognito user pools are for customer-facing application users, not workforce federation to AWS resources from Active Directory.
others.C: Cross-account roles alone do not authenticate users from Active Directory; federation is still required.

e.tip: Corporate directory to AWS console/API access = SAML federation or IAM Identity Center.

q: A company is hosting a website behind multiple Application Load Balancers. The company has different distribution rights for its content around the world. A solutions architect needs to ensure that users are served the correct content without violating distribution rights. Which configuration should the solutions architect choose to meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure Amazon CloudFront with AWS WAF.
o.B: Configure Application Load Balancers with AWS WAF
o.C: Configure Amazon Route 53 with a geolocation policy
o.D: Configure Amazon Route 53 with a geoproximity routing policy

e.why: A Route 53 geolocation routing policy answers DNS queries based on the user's location (continent, country or US state), so each region's users are routed to the ALB serving content they are licensed to see. This enforces distribution rights by location, with a default record for unmatched locations.

others.A: CloudFront with WAF geo match can block countries but does not route users to different region-specific content origins as directly.
others.B: WAF on ALBs can block by country but does not direct users to the correct regional content.
others.D: Geoproximity routing is based on distance and adjustable bias, not political boundaries, so it cannot reliably enforce country-based rights.

e.tip: Content by country or legal rights = geolocation; nearest by distance with bias = geoproximity.

q: A company stores its data on premises. The amount of data is growing beyond the company's available capacity. The company wants to migrate its data from the on-premises location to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs a solution that will automatically validate the integrity of the data after the transfer. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Order an AWS Snowball Edge device. Configure the Snowball Edge device to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket
o.B: Deploy an AWS DataSync agent on premises. Configure the DataSync agent to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises Configure the S3 File Gateway to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket
o.D: Configure an accelerator in Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration on premises. Configure the accelerator to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.

e.why: AWS DataSync transfers data online from on-premises storage to Amazon S3 and automatically performs data integrity verification during and after the transfer using checksums. An on-premises agent plus a task gives managed, validated migration.

others.A: Snowball Edge is an offline transfer device shipped to AWS, not an online transfer to S3.
others.C: S3 File Gateway provides file share access backed by S3; it is not a migration tool with automatic post-transfer validation.
others.D: S3 Transfer Acceleration is a bucket feature that speeds uploads over long distances; there is no on-premises accelerator and no automatic integrity validation task.

e.tip: Online migration with built-in verification = DataSync.

q: A company wants to migrate two DNS servers to AWS. The servers host a total of approximately 200 zones and receive 1 million requests each day on average. The company wants to maximize availability while minimizing the operational overhead that is related to the management of the two servers. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create 200 new hosted zones in the Amazon Route 53 console Import zone files.
o.B: Launch a single large Amazon EC2 instance Import zone tiles. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms and notifications to alert the company about any downtime.
o.C: Migrate the servers to AWS by using AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS). Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms and notifications to alert the company about any downtime.
o.D: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones. Import zone files. Set the desired capacity to 1 and the maximum capacity to 3 for the Auto Scaling group. Configure scaling alarms to scale based on CPU utilization.

e.why: Amazon Route 53 is a managed DNS service with a 100 percent availability SLA that easily handles 1 million queries a day. Creating hosted zones and importing the existing zone files removes the need to manage DNS servers at all, maximizing availability with minimal overhead.

others.B: A single EC2 instance is a single point of failure and still requires server management.
others.C: Migrating the servers with SMS (now discontinued) keeps self-managed DNS servers and their overhead.
others.D: Self-managed DNS on an Auto Scaling group still requires server management and scaling by CPU is not how DNS availability is achieved.

e.tip: Managed authoritative DNS = Route 53 (import zone files).

q: A global company runs its applications in multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. The company's applications use multipart uploads to upload data to multiple Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions. The company wants to report on incomplete multipart uploads for cost compliance purposes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Configure AWS Config with a rule to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
o.B: Create a service control policy (SCP) to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
o.C: Configure S3 Storage Lens to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
o.D: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.

e.why: S3 Storage Lens provides organization-wide visibility across accounts and Regions with metrics that include incomplete multipart upload bytes and object counts. Once configured at the organization level, it reports these metrics in a dashboard automatically, giving the least operational overhead.

others.A: AWS Config evaluates resource configurations and has no rule for counting incomplete multipart uploads.
others.B: SCPs restrict permissions; they cannot generate reports.
others.D: Multi-Region Access Points route requests to buckets across Regions and do not report on uploads.

e.tip: Org-wide S3 usage and cost metrics, including incomplete multipart uploads = S3 Storage Lens; clean up with lifecycle AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload.

q: A company runs a production database on Amazon RDS for MySQL. The company wants to upgrade the database version for security compliance reasons. Because the database contains critical data, the company wants a quick solution to upgrade and test functionality without losing any data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an RDS manual snapshot. Upgrade to the new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
o.B: Use native backup and restore. Restore the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
o.C: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
o.D: Use Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments to deploy and test production changes.

e.why: Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments create a staging (green) environment that replicates from production (blue), where you can upgrade the MySQL version and test. Switchover typically takes under a minute with guardrails that prevent data loss, making it the quickest low-overhead upgrade path.

others.A: A snapshot plus in-place upgrade does not allow testing before production changes and requires downtime and restore if issues occur.
others.B: Native backup and restore is manual, slow and risks losing writes made after the backup.
others.C: Setting up DMS replication to a new instance requires more configuration and cutover work than Blue/Green Deployments.

e.tip: Safe RDS major version upgrade with testing = Blue/Green Deployments.

q: A solutions architect is creating a data processing job that runs once daily and can take up to 2 hours to complete. If the job is interrupted, it has to restart from the beginning. How should the solutions architect address this issue in the MOST cost-effective manner?

o.A: Create a script that runs locally on an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance that is triggered by a cron job.
o.B: Create an AWS Lambda function triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
o.C: Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Fargate task triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
o.D: Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task running on Amazon EC2 triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.

e.why: A Fargate task triggered by an EventBridge schedule runs the job serverlessly with no time limit, so the 2-hour job completes without interruption. You pay only for the vCPU and memory used while the task runs, making it most cost-effective for a once-daily job.

others.A: A Reserved Instance is paid for 24 hours a day for a job that runs 2 hours, and adds server management.
others.B: Lambda has a maximum run time of 15 minutes, so a 2-hour job would be interrupted.
others.D: ECS on EC2 requires running and managing container instances, which costs more for a short daily job.

e.tip: Jobs longer than 15 minutes, serverless = Fargate (or AWS Batch); Lambda caps at 15 minutes.

q: A social media company wants to store its database of user profiles, relationships, and interactions in the AWS Cloud. The company needs an application to monitor any changes in the database. The application needs to analyze the relationships between the data entities and to provide recommendations to users. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
o.B: Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.
o.C: Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
o.D: Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.

e.why: Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database built for analyzing relationships such as social connections and generating recommendations. Neptune Streams records every change to the graph in order, which an application can consume to monitor changes, with no extra service to manage.

others.A: Neptune is right, but adding Kinesis Data Streams requires extra plumbing since Neptune already provides native change streams.
others.C: QLDB is a ledger database for immutable records, not relationship analysis, and it reached end of support in 2025.
others.D: Neptune Streams only works with Neptune, not QLDB.

e.tip: Relationships, social graphs, recommendations = Neptune.

q: A company is creating a new application that will store a large amount of data. The data will be analyzed hourly and will be modified by several Amazon EC2 Linux instances that are deployed across multiple Availability Zones. The needed amount of storage space will continue to grow for the next 6 months. Which storage solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Store the data in Amazon S3 Glacier. Update the S3 Glacier vault policy to allow access to the application instances.
o.B: Store the data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume on the application instances.
o.C: Store the data in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the file system on the application instances.
o.D: Store the data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Provisioned IOPS volume shared between the application instances.

e.why: Amazon EFS is a managed NFS file system that many EC2 Linux instances across multiple AZs can mount and modify concurrently. It grows and shrinks automatically as data is added, so the growing storage need over 6 months requires no provisioning.

others.A: S3 Glacier is archival storage with slow retrieval and cannot be mounted or modified frequently.
others.B: A standard EBS volume attaches to one instance in one AZ and has a fixed provisioned size.
others.D: EBS Multi-Attach works only for io1/io2 within one AZ and needs a cluster-aware file system, so it cannot be shared across AZs.

e.tip: Shared, growing storage for many Linux instances across AZs = EFS.

q: A company manages an application that stores data on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Increases in traffic are causing performance problems. The company determines that database queries are the primary reason for the slow performance. What should a solutions architect do to improve the application's performance?

o.A: Serve read traffic from the Multi-AZ standby replica.
o.B: Configure the DB instance to use Transfer Acceleration.
o.C: Create a read replica from the source DB instance. Serve read traffic from the read replica.
o.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose between the application and Amazon RDS to increase the concurrency of database requests.

e.why: Creating an RDS read replica and directing read queries to it offloads read traffic from the primary, increasing total query capacity. Replicas use asynchronous replication and can be scaled out to several replicas if needed.

others.A: In an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment the standby cannot serve read traffic; it exists only for failover.
others.B: Transfer Acceleration is an S3 feature and does not apply to RDS.
others.D: Kinesis Data Firehose is for streaming delivery to destinations like S3; it does not sit in front of RDS to speed up queries.

e.tip: Multi-AZ instance = HA only; read replicas = read scaling.

q: A company collects 10 GB of telemetry data daily from various machines. The company stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket in a source data account. The company has hired several consulting agencies to use this data for analysis. Each agency needs read access to the data for its analysts. The company must share the data from the source data account by choosing a solution that maximizes security and operational efficiency. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure S3 global tables to replicate data for each agency.
o.B: Make the S3 bucket public for a limited time. Inform only the agencies.
o.C: Configure cross-account access for the S3 bucket to the accounts that the agencies own.
o.D: Set up an IAM user for each analyst in the source data account. Grant each user access to the S3 bucket.

e.why: Granting cross-account access through a bucket policy (or roles the agencies assume) lets each agency use its own AWS account and identities to read the data in place. No data is copied or made public, and the company does not manage users for the agencies, maximizing security and operational efficiency.

others.A: S3 has no global tables feature (that is DynamoDB), and replicating data per agency adds cost and overhead.
others.B: Making the bucket public exposes the data to anyone, which is insecure.
others.D: Creating IAM users for every analyst in the source account is a large administrative burden and creates long-term credentials.

e.tip: Share S3 with other AWS accounts = cross-account bucket policy or IAM roles.

q: A company uses Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP in its primary AWS Region for CIFS and NFS file shares. Applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances access the file shares. The company needs a storage disaster recovery (DR) solution in a secondary Region. The data that is replicated in the secondary Region needs to be accessed by using the same protocols as the primary Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to copy the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Replicate the S3 bucket to the secondary Region.
o.B: Create a backup of the FSx for ONTAP volumes by using AWS Backup. Copy the volumes to the secondary Region. Create a new FSx for ONTAP instance from the backup.
o.C: Create an FSx for ONTAP instance in the secondary Region. Use NetApp SnapMirror to replicate data from the primary Region to the secondary Region.
o.D: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Migrate the current data to the volume. Replicate the volume to the secondary Region.

e.why: NetApp SnapMirror is built into FSx for NetApp ONTAP and replicates volumes asynchronously to another FSx for ONTAP file system in the secondary Region. The DR file system serves the same NFS and CIFS/SMB protocols, so applications can fail over with the least operational overhead.

others.A: A custom Lambda copying data to S3 changes the access protocol to object storage and is custom code to maintain.
others.B: Backup and restore gives a longer RTO and RPO, and creating a new file system during DR adds work.
others.D: EFS supports only NFS, not CIFS/SMB, and requires migrating the data.

e.tip: FSx for ONTAP cross-Region DR = SnapMirror.

q: A development team is creating an event-based application that uses AWS Lambda functions. Events will be generated when files are added to an Amazon S3 bucket. The development team currently has Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) configured as the event target from Amazon S3. What should a solutions architect do to process the events from Amazon S3 in a scalable way?

o.A: Create an SNS subscription that processes the event in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) before the event runs in Lambda.
o.B: Create an SNS subscription that processes the event in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) before the event runs in Lambda
o.C: Create an SNS subscription that sends the event to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Configure the SOS queue to trigger a Lambda function.
o.D: Create an SNS subscription that sends the event to AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS). Configure the Lambda function to poll from the SMS event.

e.why: Subscribing an Amazon SQS queue to the SNS topic (fanout) buffers S3 events durably, and an SQS event source mapping triggers Lambda, which scales pollers with queue depth. This decouples event bursts from processing and enables retries and dead-letter queues, so events are processed reliably at scale.

others.A: Adding ECS processing before Lambda introduces unnecessary infrastructure and does not provide buffering.
others.B: An EKS cluster in the path adds significant operational overhead without adding scalability.
others.D: AWS Server Migration Service is a (discontinued) server migration tool and cannot receive SNS events.

e.tip: SNS to SQS fanout, then SQS to Lambda, is the standard scalable, decoupled event pattern.

q: A solutions architect is designing a new service behind Amazon API Gateway. The request patterns for the service will be unpredictable and can change suddenly from 0 requests to over 500 per second. The total size of the data that needs to be persisted in a backend database is currently less than 1 GB with unpredictable future growth. Data can be queried using simple key-value requests. Which combination ofAWS services would meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: AWS Fargate
o.B: AWS Lambda
o.C: Amazon DynamoDB
o.D: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
o.E: MySQL-compatible Amazon Aurora

e.why: AWS Lambda scales from zero to hundreds of concurrent executions almost instantly and charges nothing when idle, fitting the unpredictable 0 to 500+ requests per second pattern behind API Gateway (B). Amazon DynamoDB is a serverless key-value database that scales storage and throughput automatically (C).

others.A: Fargate tasks take time to start and scale, and they cost money even when idle.
others.D: EC2 Auto Scaling launches instances in minutes, too slow for sudden jumps from zero, and requires server management.
others.E: Aurora MySQL is relational and is more than needed for simple key-value queries, and scaling connections from Lambda is harder.

e.tip: Spiky API + key-value data = API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB.

q: A company collects and shares research data with the company's employees all over the world. The company wants to collect and store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket and process the data in the AWS Cloud. The company will share the data with the company's employees. The company needs a secure solution in the AWS Cloud that minimizes operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use an AWS Lambda function to create an S3 presigned URL. Instruct employees to use the URL.
o.B: Create an IAM user for each employee. Create an IAM policy for each employee to allow S3 access. Instruct employees to use the AWS Management Console.
o.C: Create an S3 File Gateway. Create a share for uploading and a share for downloading. Allow employees to mount shares on their local computers to use S3 File Gateway.
o.D: Configure AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoints. Select the custom identity provider options. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage the user credentials Instruct employees to use Transfer Family.

e.why: A Lambda function can generate S3 presigned URLs that grant time-limited access to specific objects using the function's role permissions. Employees can upload or download through the URL without AWS credentials, giving secure sharing with minimal operational overhead and no infrastructure to run.

others.B: Creating IAM users and policies for every employee worldwide is heavy administration and creates long-term credentials.
others.C: S3 File Gateway must be deployed on premises near users, which does not suit a global workforce and adds infrastructure to manage.
others.D: Transfer Family with a custom identity provider and Secrets Manager adds endpoint costs and credential management overhead.

e.tip: Temporary access to S3 objects without AWS credentials = presigned URLs.

q: A company is building a new furniture inventory application. The company has deployed the application on a fleet ofAmazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in their VPC. A solutions architect has observed that incoming traffic seems to favor one EC2 instance, resulting in latency for some requests. What should the solutions architect do to resolve this issue?

o.A: Disable session affinity (sticky sessions) on the ALB
o.B: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer
o.C: Increase the number of EC2 instances in each Availability Zone
o.D: Adjust the frequency of the health checks on the ALB's target group

e.why: With sticky sessions (session affinity) enabled, the ALB binds clients to the same target using a cookie, so some instances can receive a disproportionate share of traffic. Disabling stickiness lets the ALB distribute requests evenly across healthy targets, reducing latency.

others.B: An NLB also balances traffic but would not fix the stickiness configuration and loses layer 7 features.
others.C: Adding instances does not help if sticky sessions keep routing many clients to the same instance.
others.D: Health check frequency affects how quickly unhealthy targets are detected, not traffic distribution among healthy ones.

e.tip: Uneven load on one target behind an ALB: suspect sticky sessions.

q: A company has an application workflow that uses an AWS Lambda function to download and decrypt files from Amazon S3. These files are encrypted using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that will ensure the required permissions are set correctly. Which combination of actions accomplish this? (Choose two.)

o.A: Attach the kms:decrypt permission to the Lambda function’s resource policy
o.B: Grant the decrypt permission for the Lambda IAM role in the KMS key's policy
o.C: Grant the decrypt permission for the Lambda resource policy in the KMS key's policy.
o.D: Create a new IAM policy with the kms:decrypt permission and attach the policy to the Lambda function.
o.E: Create a new IAM role with the kms:decrypt permission and attach the execution role to the Lambda function.

e.why: The Lambda function calls KMS using its execution role, so you create an IAM role with kms:Decrypt (and s3:GetObject) permissions and attach it as the function's execution role (E). The KMS key policy must also allow that role to use the key for decryption (B), because key policies control who can use KMS keys.

others.A: A Lambda resource policy controls who can invoke the function, not what the function can access.
others.C: Key policies grant permissions to principals such as roles, not to a Lambda resource policy.
others.D: IAM policies cannot be attached directly to a Lambda function; they are attached to its execution role.

e.tip: Lambda outbound permissions = execution role; KMS also requires the key policy to allow the role.

q: A company wants to monitor its AWS costs for financial review. The cloud operations team is designing an architecture in the AWS Organizations management account to query AWS Cost and Usage Reports for all member accounts. The team must run this query once a month and provide a detailed analysis of the bill. Which solution is the MOST scalable and cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

o.A: Enable Cost and Usage Reports in the management account. Deliver reports to Amazon Kinesis. Use Amazon EMR for analysis.
o.B: Enable Cost and Usage Reports in the management account. Deliver the reports to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Athena for analysis.
o.C: Enable Cost and Usage Reports for member accounts. Deliver the reports to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Redshift for analysis.
o.D: Enable Cost and Usage Reports for member accounts. Deliver the reports to Amazon Kinesis. Use Amazon QuickSight tor analysis.

e.why: Cost and Usage Reports enabled in the Organizations management account automatically include usage for all member accounts, and CUR delivers natively to Amazon S3. Amazon Athena queries the CUR files in place with serverless, pay-per-query SQL, which is the most scalable and cost-effective choice for a once-a-month analysis.

others.A: CUR cannot be delivered to Kinesis, and running EMR for a monthly query adds cost and cluster management.
others.C: Enabling CUR per member account is unnecessary because the management account already sees consolidated billing data, and a Redshift cluster is costly for a monthly query.
others.D: CUR does not deliver to Kinesis, and per-member-account reports add needless effort.

e.tip: CUR + S3 + Athena is the standard pattern for ad hoc or periodic bill analysis; the management account's CUR covers all member accounts.

q: A company wants to run a gaming application on Amazon EC2 instances that are part of an Auto Scaling group in the AWS Cloud. The application will transmit data by using UDP packets. The company wants to ensure that the application can scale out and in as traffic increases and decreases. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Attach a Network Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.
o.B: Attach an Application Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.
o.C: Deploy an Amazon Route 53 record set with a weighted policy to route traffic appropriately.
o.D: Deploy a NAT instance that is configured with port forwarding to the EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group.

e.why: A Network Load Balancer operates at layer 4 and supports UDP listeners and target groups, and it can be attached to an Auto Scaling group so new instances are registered automatically as the group scales out and in.

others.B: An Application Load Balancer only handles HTTP/HTTPS (and gRPC) at layer 7 and cannot forward UDP traffic.
others.C: Route 53 weighted records do not register Auto Scaling instances dynamically or balance per-connection load.
others.D: A NAT instance is for outbound internet access from private subnets, not for load balancing inbound traffic, and it is a single point of failure.

e.tip: UDP, TCP, static IPs or extreme performance means NLB; HTTP path/host routing means ALB.

q: A company runs several websites on AWS for its different brands. Each website generates tens of gigabytes of web traffic logs each day. A solutions architect needs to design a scalable solution to give the company's developers the ability to analyze traffic patterns across all the company's websites. This analysis by the developers will occur on demand once a week over the course of several months. The solution must support queries with standard SQL. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena tor analysis.
o.B: Store the logs in Amazon RDS. Use a database client for analysis.
o.C: Store the logs in Amazon OpenSearch Service. Use OpenSearch Service for analysis.
o.D: Store the logs in an Amazon EMR cluster Use a supported open-source framework for SQL-based analysis.

e.why: Storing logs in Amazon S3 is the cheapest durable storage for tens of GB per day, and Amazon Athena runs standard SQL directly on the S3 data with no infrastructure, charging only per query. Because analysis is only weekly and on demand, paying nothing between queries makes this the most cost-effective option.

others.B: Loading large volumes of logs into RDS requires a continuously running, provisioned database that is costly and not designed for log analytics at scale.
others.C: OpenSearch Service needs an always-on cluster sized for the data, which is expensive for weekly queries and is not standard SQL-first.
others.D: An EMR cluster storing data in HDFS must run continuously and requires cluster management, increasing cost.

e.tip: Infrequent, on-demand SQL over files in S3 = Athena.

q: An international company has a subdomain for each country that the company operates in. The subdomains are formatted as example.com, country1.example.com, and country2.example.com. The company's workloads are behind an Application Load Balancer. The company wants to encrypt the website data that is in transit. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) console to request a public certificate for the apex top domain example com and a wildcard certificate for *.example.com.
o.B: Use the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) console to request a private certificate for the apex top domain example.com and a wildcard certificate for *.example.com.
o.C: Use the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) console to request a public and private certificate for the apex top domain example.com.
o.D: Validate domain ownership by email address. Switch to DNS validation by adding the required DNS records to the DNS provider.
o.E: Validate domain ownership for the domain by adding the required DNS records to the DNS provider.

e.why: A public ACM certificate is required for internet-facing TLS on an ALB, and one certificate can cover the apex example.com plus the wildcard *.example.com to secure every country subdomain. DNS validation by adding the CNAME records ACM provides proves domain ownership and lets ACM renew the certificate automatically.

others.B: Private certificates from ACM Private CA are not trusted by public browsers, so they are unsuitable for a public website.
others.C: Requesting both public and private certificates for only the apex domain does not cover the country subdomains, and the private one is unnecessary.
others.D: Email validation followed by switching to DNS validation is a confused, unnecessary step; you simply choose DNS validation when requesting.

e.tip: ACM public cert + DNS validation = automatic renewal; wildcard covers one subdomain level.

q: A company is required to use cryptographic keys in its on-premises key manager. The key manager is outside of the AWS Cloud because of regulatory and compliance requirements. The company wants to manage encryption and decryption by using cryptographic keys that are retained outside of the AWS Cloud and that support a variety of external key managers from different vendors. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS CloudHSM key store backed by a CloudHSM cluster.
o.B: Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) external key store backed by an external key manager.
o.C: Use the default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) managed key store.
o.D: Use a custom key store backed by an AWS CloudHSM cluster.

e.why: An AWS KMS external key store (XKS) lets KMS keys be backed by key material held in an external key manager outside AWS, reached via an XKS proxy, and it supports external key managers from multiple vendors. Applications keep using standard KMS APIs and integrated AWS services, giving the least operational overhead while keys never leave the on-premises manager.

others.A: A CloudHSM key store keeps keys inside AWS on CloudHSM hardware, violating the requirement that keys stay outside the AWS Cloud.
others.C: The default KMS key store holds keys in AWS-managed HSMs inside AWS, not in the company's external key manager.
others.D: A custom key store backed by CloudHSM still stores keys in AWS and adds HSM cluster management.

e.tip: Keys must stay outside AWS but use KMS = KMS External Key Store (XKS).

q: A solutions architect needs to host a high performance computing (HPC) workload in the AWS Cloud. The workload will run on hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances and will require parallel access to a shared file system to enable distributed processing of large datasets. Datasets will be accessed across multiple instances simultaneously. The workload requires access latency within 1 ms. After processing has completed, engineers will need access to the dataset for manual postprocessing. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) as a shared file system. Access the dataset from Amazon EFS.
o.B: Mount an Amazon S3 bucket to serve as the shared file system. Perform postprocessing directly from the S3 bucket.
o.C: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre as a shared file system. Link the file system to an Amazon S3 bucket for postprocessing.
o.D: Configure AWS Resource Access Manager to share an Amazon S3 bucket so that it can be mounted to all instances for processing and postprocessing.

e.why: Amazon FSx for Lustre is a parallel, high-performance file system built for HPC with sub-millisecond latency and massive throughput across hundreds of instances. It can be linked to an S3 bucket via a data repository association so results are exported to S3 for later postprocessing.

others.A: EFS offers shared NFS access but is not designed for HPC-scale parallel throughput and its latency is generally higher than FSx for Lustre.
others.B: S3 is object storage; mounting it via tools does not provide a POSIX parallel file system with sub-millisecond latency.
others.D: AWS RAM shares resources across accounts and cannot make an S3 bucket mountable as a shared file system.

e.tip: HPC + parallel file system + S3 integration = FSx for Lustre.

q: A gaming company is building an application with Voice over IP capabilities. The application will serve traffic to users across the world. The application needs to be highly available with an automated failover across AWS Regions. The company wants to minimize the latency of users without relying on IP address caching on user devices. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Global Accelerator with health checks.
o.B: Use Amazon Route 53 with a geolocation routing policy.
o.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that includes multiple origins.
o.D: Create an Application Load Balancer that uses path-based routing.

e.why: AWS Global Accelerator gives users two static anycast IP addresses and routes traffic over the AWS global network to the nearest healthy Regional endpoint, supporting UDP for VoIP. Its health checks fail over between Regions in seconds without depending on DNS changes, so client IP or DNS caching does not delay failover.

others.B: Route 53 geolocation routing depends on DNS, so failover is affected by DNS caching on clients, and it does not optimize the network path.
others.C: CloudFront is for HTTP/HTTPS content delivery and does not handle UDP-based VoIP traffic.
others.D: An ALB is a Regional resource with no cross-Region failover and does not support UDP.

e.tip: Non-HTTP (UDP/TCP) global traffic with fast Regional failover and static IPs = Global Accelerator.

q: A weather forecasting company needs to process hundreds of gigabytes of data with sub-millisecond latency. The company has a high performance computing (HPC) environment in its data center and wants to expand its forecasting capabilities. A solutions architect must identify a highly available cloud storage solution that can handle large amounts of sustained throughput. Files that are stored in the solution should be accessible to thousands of compute instances that will simultaneously access and process the entire dataset. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre scratch file systems.
o.B: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre persistent file systems.
o.C: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Bursting Throughput mode.
o.D: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Provisioned Throughput mode.

e.why: FSx for Lustre provides sub-millisecond latency and hundreds of GB/s of throughput for thousands of concurrent compute instances. Persistent file systems replicate data within an Availability Zone and replace failed file servers automatically, meeting the high availability and sustained-throughput requirements.

others.A: Scratch file systems do not replicate data and are intended for temporary, short-term processing, so they are not highly available.
others.C: EFS Bursting mode cannot deliver sustained HPC throughput with sub-millisecond latency to thousands of instances.
others.D: EFS Provisioned Throughput still does not match the latency and parallel throughput of FSx for Lustre for HPC workloads.

e.tip: FSx for Lustre: scratch = cheap and temporary; persistent = durable and highly available.

q: An ecommerce company runs a PostgreSQL database on premises. The database stores data by using high IOPS Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) block storage. The daily peak I/O transactions per second do not exceed 15,000 IOPS. The company wants to migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and provision disk IOPS performance independent of disk storage capacity. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure the General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
o.B: Configure the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
o.C: Configure the General Purpose SSD (gp3) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
o.D: Configure the EBS magnetic volume type to achieve maximum IOPS.

e.why: gp3 volumes let you provision IOPS (up to 16,000 on RDS gp3 depending on storage size thresholds) and throughput independently of storage capacity at a lower price than io1. Since the peak does not exceed 15,000 IOPS, gp3 is the most cost-effective choice.

others.A: gp2 IOPS scale with volume size (3 IOPS per GB) and cannot be provisioned independently of capacity.
others.B: io1 can provide 15,000 IOPS independently but costs significantly more per GB and per IOPS than gp3.
others.D: Magnetic storage is legacy, offers very low IOPS, and cannot meet 15,000 IOPS.

e.tip: Need IOPS independent of size cheaply = gp3; io1/io2 only when you need beyond gp3 limits or higher durability.

q: A company wants to migrate its on-premises Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise edition database to AWS. The company's online application uses the database to process transactions. The data analysis team uses the same production database to run reports for analytical processing. The company wants to reduce operational overhead by moving to managed services wherever possible. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Migrate to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SOL Server. Use read replicas for reporting purposes
o.B: Migrate to Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2. Use Always On read replicas for reporting purposes
o.C: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB. Use DynamoDB on-demand replicas for reporting purposes
o.D: Migrate to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Use Aurora read replicas for reporting purposes

e.why: Amazon RDS for SQL Server is a managed service that supports the Enterprise edition, so the database can be migrated without rewriting the application. RDS for SQL Server read replicas (Enterprise edition) offload reporting queries from the production instance, minimizing operational overhead.

others.B: Running SQL Server on EC2 with Always On requires managing the OS, patching, backups and clustering yourself, which is more overhead.
others.C: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database; migrating a relational SQL Server workload requires a full redesign, and on-demand replicas are not a reporting feature.
others.D: Migrating to Aurora MySQL requires schema and code conversion from T-SQL, adding significant effort.

e.tip: Managed + minimal change for SQL Server = RDS for SQL Server; read replicas for reporting.

q: A company stores a large volume of image files in an Amazon S3 bucket. The images need to be readily available for the first 180 days. The images are infrequently accessed for the next 180 days. After 360 days, the images need to be archived but must be available instantly upon request. After 5 years, only auditors can access the images. The auditors must be able to retrieve the images within 12 hours. The images cannot be lost during this process. A developer will use S3 Standard storage for the first 180 days. The developer needs to configure an S3 Lifecycle rule. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 180 days. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
o.B: Transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 180 days. S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
o.C: Transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 180 days, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
o.D: Transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 180 days, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.

e.why: S3 Standard-IA stores data across multiple Availability Zones, so images will not be lost, and it is cheaper for infrequently accessed objects after 180 days. Glacier Instant Retrieval gives millisecond access for archived data after 360 days, and Glacier Deep Archive's standard retrieval within 12 hours suits auditor access after 5 years at the lowest cost.

others.A: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, so an AZ loss could lose images, violating the durability requirement.
others.B: One Zone-IA risks data loss, and Glacier Flexible Retrieval does not provide instant access after 360 days.
others.D: Glacier Flexible Retrieval takes minutes to hours to restore, failing the instant-availability requirement after 360 days.

e.tip: Archive but instant access = Glacier Instant Retrieval; retrieval within 12 hours = Deep Archive.

q: A company has a large data workload that runs for 6 hours each day. The company cannot lose any data while the process is running. A solutions architect is designing an Amazon EMR cluster configuration to support this critical data workload. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure a long-running cluster that runs the primary node and core nodes on On-Demand Instances and the task nodes on Spot Instances.
o.B: Configure a transient cluster that runs the primary node and core nodes on On-Demand Instances and the task nodes on Spot Instances.
o.C: Configure a transient cluster that runs the primary node on an On-Demand Instance and the core nodes and task nodes on Spot Instances.
o.D: Configure a long-running cluster that runs the primary node on an On-Demand Instance, the core nodes on Spot Instances, and the task nodes on Spot Instances.

e.why: A transient EMR cluster runs only for the 6-hour daily job and then terminates, avoiding paying for idle capacity. Keeping the primary and core nodes on On-Demand Instances protects HDFS data and cluster state from Spot interruptions, while task nodes (compute only, no HDFS) can safely use cheaper Spot Instances.

others.A: A long-running cluster pays for capacity during the 18 idle hours each day, which is less cost-effective.
others.C: Core nodes store HDFS data; running them on Spot risks data loss if instances are reclaimed.
others.D: Long-running wastes money and Spot core nodes risk losing data.

e.tip: EMR: primary and core on On-Demand for reliability, task nodes on Spot; transient clusters for periodic jobs.

q: A company maintains an Amazon RDS database that maps users to cost centers. The company has accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs a solution that will tag all resources that are created in a specific AWS account in the organization. The solution must tag each resource with the cost center ID of the user who created the resource. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Move the specific AWS account to a new organizational unit (OU) in Organizations from the management account. Create a service control policy (SCP) that requires all existing resources to have the correct cost center tag before the resources are created. Apply the SCP to the new OU.
o.B: Create an AWS Lambda function to tag the resources after the Lambda function looks up the appropriate cost center from the RDS database. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS CloudTrail events to invoke the Lambda function.
o.C: Create an AWS CloudFormation stack to deploy an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to look up the appropriate cost center from the RDS database and to tag resources. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke the CloudFormation stack.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda function to tag the resources with a default value. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS CloudTrail events to invoke the Lambda function when a resource is missing the cost center tag.

e.why: CloudTrail records every resource-creation API call along with the identity of the caller, and an EventBridge rule can match those events and invoke a Lambda function in near real time. The function looks up the caller's cost center in the RDS database and applies the correct tag to the new resource.

others.A: SCPs can deny actions lacking tags but cannot look up a user's cost center or add tags, and existing resources cannot be required to be tagged before they are created.
others.C: A scheduled rule invoking a CloudFormation stack is not event-driven and does not tie resources to the user who created them.
others.D: Tagging with a default value does not meet the requirement to use each creator's cost center ID.

e.tip: React to API activity = CloudTrail event -> EventBridge rule -> Lambda.

q: A company recently migrated its web application to the AWS Cloud. The company uses an Amazon EC2 instance to run multiple processes to host the application. The processes include an Apache web server that serves static content. The Apache web server makes requests to a PHP application that uses a local Redis server for user sessions. The company wants to redesign the architecture to be highly available and to use AWS managed solutions. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to host the static content and the PHP application. Configure Elastic Beanstalk to deploy its EC2 instance into a public subnet. Assign a public IP address.
o.B: Use AWS Lambda to host the static content and the PHP application. Use an Amazon API Gateway REST API to proxy requests to the Lambda function. Set the API Gateway CORS configuration to respond to the domain name. Configure Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to handle session information.
o.C: Keep the backend code on the EC2 instance. Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster that has Multi-AZ enabled. Configure the ElastiCache for Redis cluster in cluster mode. Copy the frontend resources to Amazon S3. Configure the backend code to reference the EC2 instance.
o.D: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 endpoint to an S3 bucket that is configured to host the static content. Configure an Application Load Balancer that targets an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service that runs AWS Fargate tasks for the PHP application. Configure the PHP application to use an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster that runs in multiple Availability Zones.

e.why: CloudFront with an S3 origin serves the static content in a highly available, managed way. The PHP application runs on ECS with Fargate behind an ALB across multiple AZs, and sessions move to a Multi-AZ ElastiCache for Redis cluster so any task can serve any user, giving a highly available design built on managed services.

others.A: A single Elastic Beanstalk EC2 instance in a public subnet is not highly available and does not externalize the Redis session store.
others.B: Lambda does not natively host a traditional Apache/PHP application without significant refactoring, and serving static content through Lambda is inefficient.
others.C: The backend stays on a single EC2 instance, which remains a single point of failure.

e.tip: HA redesign: static to S3/CloudFront, stateless compute behind ALB, sessions in ElastiCache or DynamoDB.

q: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that has a target group. The company designed the application to work with session affinity (sticky sessions) for a better user experience. The application must be available publicly over the internet as an endpoint. A WAF must be applied to the endpoint for additional security. Session affinity (sticky sessions) must be configured on the endpoint. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create a public Network Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
o.B: Create a Gateway Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
o.C: Create a public Application Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
o.D: Create a second target group. Add Elastic IP addresses to the EC2 instances.
o.E: Create a web ACL in AWS WAF. Associate the web ACL with the endpoint

e.why: An Application Load Balancer supports sticky sessions through load-balancer-generated or application cookies on its target groups and can be public. AWS WAF web ACLs can be associated directly with an ALB, adding layer 7 protection to the endpoint.

others.A: AWS WAF cannot be associated with a Network Load Balancer, so it cannot meet the WAF requirement.
others.B: A Gateway Load Balancer is for inline third-party virtual appliances, not for exposing a public web application with sticky sessions.
others.D: A second target group and Elastic IPs add nothing toward WAF protection or session affinity.

e.tip: AWS WAF attaches to ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito and App Runner, not NLB.

q: A company runs a website that stores images of historical events. Website users need the ability to search and view images based on the year that the event in the image occurred. On average, users request each image only once or twice a year. The company wants a highly available solution to store and deliver the images to users. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Store images in Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
o.B: Store images in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
o.C: Store images in Amazon S3 Standard. Use S3 Standard to directly deliver images by using a static website.
o.D: Store images in Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use S3 Standard-IA to directly deliver images by using a static website.

e.why: Images accessed only once or twice a year are a good fit for S3 Standard-IA, which has a lower storage price than S3 Standard while keeping millisecond access and multi-AZ high availability. S3 can serve the objects directly, so no servers are needed and it is the most cost-effective option.

others.A: EBS is tied to a single instance and AZ and needs a running EC2 web server, which is costly and not highly available.
others.B: EFS plus EC2 web servers costs more for storage and compute than S3 for rarely accessed images.
others.C: S3 Standard works but costs more for storage than Standard-IA for objects that are rarely accessed.

e.tip: Rarely accessed but needs immediate access and multi-AZ durability = S3 Standard-IA.

q: A company has multiple AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations that different business units use. The company has multiple offices around the world. The company needs to update security group rules to allow new office CIDR ranges or to remove old CIDR ranges across the organization. The company wants to centralize the management of security group rules to minimize the administrative overhead that updating CIDR ranges requires. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create VPC security groups in the organization's management account. Update the security groups when a CIDR range update is necessary.
o.B: Create a VPC customer managed prefix list that contains the list of CIDRs. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the prefix list across the organization. Use the prefix list in the security groups across the organization.
o.C: Create an AWS managed prefix list. Use an AWS Security Hub policy to enforce the security group update across the organization. Use an AWS Lambda function to update the prefix list automatically when the CIDR ranges change.
o.D: Create security groups in a central administrative AWS account. Create an AWS Firewall Manager common security group policy for the whole organization. Select the previously created security groups as primary groups in the policy.

e.why: A customer managed prefix list holds the office CIDRs in one place, and AWS RAM can share it with the whole organization. Security groups in every account reference the prefix list, so adding or removing a CIDR is a single edit that propagates everywhere at no extra cost.

others.A: Security groups are VPC- and account-scoped and cannot be used directly by other accounts' resources, so this does not centralize rules.
others.C: AWS managed prefix lists are for AWS service ranges and cannot be edited by customers, and Security Hub does not enforce security group content.
others.D: Firewall Manager can centralize security groups but carries per-policy charges and requires additional setup, so it is less cost-effective than a shared prefix list.

e.tip: Shared list of CIDRs across accounts = customer managed prefix list shared via AWS RAM.

q: A company uses an on-premises network-attached storage (NAS) system to provide file shares to its high performance computing (HPC) workloads. The company wants to migrate its latency-sensitive HPC workloads and its storage to the AWS Cloud. The company must be able to provide NFS and SMB multi-protocol access from the file system. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST latency? (Choose two.)

o.A: Deploy compute optimized EC2 instances into a cluster placement group.
o.B: Deploy compute optimized EC2 instances into a partition placement group.
o.C: Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system.
o.D: Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system.
o.E: Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system.

e.why: A cluster placement group packs instances close together in one AZ for the lowest network latency and highest throughput between nodes, which suits latency-sensitive HPC. Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is the FSx option that provides simultaneous NFS and SMB multi-protocol access to the same data.

others.B: Partition placement groups spread instances across racks for fault isolation (e.g. HDFS, Cassandra), not for lowest latency.
others.C: FSx for Lustre is POSIX/Lustre-client based and does not provide SMB access.
others.D: FSx for OpenZFS supports NFS (and SMB is not native for multi-protocol access), so it does not meet the NFS plus SMB requirement.

e.tip: NFS + SMB on the same file system = FSx for NetApp ONTAP; lowest inter-node latency = cluster placement group.

q: A company is relocating its data center and wants to securely transfer 50 TB of data to AWS within 2 weeks. The existing data center has a Site-to-Site VPN connection to AWS that is 90% utilized. Which AWS service should a solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

o.A: AWS DataSync with a VPC endpoint
o.B: AWS Direct Connect
o.C: AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized
o.D: AWS Storage Gateway

e.why: With the VPN already 90% utilized, transferring 50 TB online in 2 weeks is impractical. A Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device holds around 80 TB usable, encrypts data with KMS-managed keys, and is shipped to AWS, meeting the secure 2-week transfer requirement.

others.A: DataSync would still use the nearly saturated VPN link, which cannot move 50 TB in 2 weeks.
others.B: Provisioning a new Direct Connect connection often takes weeks or months, risking the 2-week deadline, and is costly for a one-time move.
others.D: Storage Gateway also relies on the existing saturated network link and is designed for hybrid access rather than bulk migration.

e.tip: Tens of TB, limited bandwidth, short deadline = Snowball Edge.

q: A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances in an Auto Scaling group. Application peak hours occur at the same time each day. Application users report slow application performance at the start of peak hours. The application performs normally 2-3 hours after peak hours begin. The company wants to ensure that the application works properly at the start of peak hours. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic properly to the instances.
o.B: Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on memory utilization.
o.C: Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on CPU utilization.
o.D: Configure a scheduled scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances before peak hours.

e.why: Peak hours occur at the same time every day, so a scheduled scaling action can add instances before the peak begins. This avoids the lag of reactive dynamic scaling, so capacity is already in service when users arrive.

others.A: An ALB distributes load but does not add the capacity that is missing at the start of the peak.
others.B: Dynamic scaling on memory reacts only after load rises (and requires a custom metric), so slowness at the start of peak persists.
others.C: Dynamic scaling on CPU also reacts after demand increases, causing the same warm-up delay.

e.tip: Predictable, recurring load = scheduled scaling (or predictive scaling).

q: A company runs applications on AWS that connect to the company's Amazon RDS database. The applications scale on weekends and at peak times of the year. The company wants to scale the database more effectively for its applications that connect to the database. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon DynamoDB with connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the DynamoDB endpoint.
o.B: Use Amazon RDS Proxy with a target group for the database. Change the applications to use the RDS Proxy endpoint.
o.C: Use a custom proxy that runs on Amazon EC2 as an intermediary to the database. Change the applications to use the custom proxy endpoint.
o.D: Use an AWS Lambda function to provide connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the Lambda function.

e.why: Amazon RDS Proxy is a fully managed connection pooler that shares and reuses database connections, absorbing connection spikes as applications scale out. Applications only need to point to the proxy endpoint, which gives the least operational overhead.

others.A: Moving to DynamoDB requires redesigning the data model and application, and DynamoDB does not use connection pooling target groups.
others.C: A custom proxy on EC2 must be built, scaled, patched and made highly available by the company.
others.D: Lambda is not a connection pooler and would add complexity and latency for every database request.

e.tip: Too many DB connections from scaling apps or Lambda = RDS Proxy.

q: A company uses AWS Cost Explorer to monitor its AWS costs. The company notices that Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage and snapshot costs increase every month. However, the company does not purchase additional EBS storage every month. The company wants to optimize monthly costs for its current storage usage. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs to monitor the storage utilization of Amazon EBS. Use Amazon EBS Elastic Volumes to reduce the size of the EBS volumes.
o.B: Use a custom script to monitor space usage. Use Amazon EBS Elastic Volumes to reduce the size of the EBS volumes.
o.C: Delete all expired and unused snapshots to reduce snapshot costs.
o.D: Delete all nonessential snapshots. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to create and manage the snapshots according to the company's snapshot policy requirements.

e.why: Growing snapshot costs come from accumulating snapshots. Deleting nonessential snapshots cuts current costs, and Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager automates snapshot creation and retention so old snapshots are deleted per policy, with minimal ongoing effort.

others.A: EBS Elastic Volumes cannot decrease volume size, and CloudWatch Logs does not natively report EBS disk usage.
others.B: A custom script adds operational overhead, and Elastic Volumes cannot shrink volumes.
others.C: A one-time deletion helps but does not prevent snapshots from accumulating again, so costs will keep rising.

e.tip: Automate EBS snapshot retention = Data Lifecycle Manager (or AWS Backup).

q: A company is developing a new application on AWS. The application consists of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster, an Amazon S3 bucket that contains assets for the application, and an Amazon RDS for MySQL database that contains the dataset for the application. The dataset contains sensitive information. The company wants to ensure that only the ECS cluster can access the data in the RDS for MySQL database and the data in the S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt both the S3 bucket and the RDS for MySQL database. Ensure that the KMS key policy includes encrypt and decrypt permissions for the ECS task execution role.
o.B: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key to encrypt both the S3 bucket and the RDS for MySQL database. Ensure that the S3 bucket policy specifies the ECS task execution role as a user.
o.C: Create an S3 bucket policy that restricts bucket access to the ECS task execution role. Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon RDS for MySQL. Update the RDS for MySQL security group to allow access from only the subnets that the ECS cluster will generate tasks in.
o.D: Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon RDS for MySQL. Update the RDS for MySQL security group to allow access from only the subnets that the ECS cluster will generate tasks in. Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from only the S3 VPC endpoint.

e.why: A customer managed KMS key lets the company control exactly which principals can use the key through its key policy. Encrypting both the S3 bucket and the RDS database with this key and granting encrypt/decrypt only to the ECS task role restricts who can use the key material.

others.B: AWS managed keys have key policies that cannot be edited, so access cannot be limited to the ECS role, and naming a role as a 'user' in a bucket policy is not meaningful.
others.C: An RDS interface VPC endpoint is for the RDS management API, not database connections, so it does not restrict data access.
others.D: The RDS VPC endpoint again covers only the management API, so this does not control database data access as intended.

e.tip: Only a customer managed key lets you edit the key policy. Note: RDS decrypts transparently for any authenticated DB user, so network and DB auth controls still matter in practice.

q: A company has a web application that runs on premises. The application experiences latency issues during peak hours. The latency issues occur twice each month. At the start of a latency issue, the application's CPU utilization immediately increases to 10 times its normal amount. The company wants to migrate the application to AWS to improve latency. The company also wants to scale the application automatically when application demand increases. The company will use AWS Elastic Beanstalk for application deployment. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use burstable performance instances in unlimited mode. Configure the environment to scale based on requests.
o.B: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use compute optimized instances. Configure the environment to scale based on requests.
o.C: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use compute optimized instances. Configure the environment to scale on a schedule.
o.D: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use burstable performance instances in unlimited mode. Configure the environment to scale on predictive metrics.

e.why: Burstable (T-family) instances in unlimited mode can sustain CPU well above baseline whenever needed, absorbing the instant 10x CPU spike while new instances launch. Scaling the Elastic Beanstalk environment on requests adds capacity automatically when demand increases.

others.B: Compute optimized instances cost more for a workload that is normally low, and they cannot instantly absorb a 10x spike before scaling completes.
others.C: Scheduled scaling does not fit spikes that are not tied to known times, and compute optimized instances are over-provisioned for normal load.
others.D: Predictive scaling needs regular, cyclical patterns with enough history; two spikes a month are a poor fit.

e.tip: T instances in unlimited mode handle unpredictable CPU bursts without credit exhaustion.

q: A company has customers located across the world. The company wants to use automation to secure its systems and network infrastructure. The company's security team must be able to track and audit all incremental changes to the infrastructure. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
o.B: Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
o.C: Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.
o.D: Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.

e.why: AWS CloudFormation provisions the infrastructure as code, automating secure, repeatable deployments. AWS Config records configuration changes to resources over time, giving the security team a timeline of incremental changes to track and audit.

others.A: AWS Organizations manages accounts and policies; it does not provision infrastructure.
others.C: Organizations does not provision infrastructure, and Service Catalog does not track configuration changes.
others.D: Service Catalog publishes approved products but does not audit incremental resource configuration changes.

e.tip: Provision = CloudFormation; record and audit config changes = AWS Config; who made the API call = CloudTrail.

q: A startup company is hosting a website for its customers on an Amazon EC2 instance. The website consists of a stateless Python application and a MySQL database. The website serves only a small amount of traffic. The company is concerned about the reliability of the instance and needs to migrate to a highly available architecture. The company cannot modify the application code. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to achieve high availability for the website? (Choose two.)

o.A: Provision an internet gateway in each Availability Zone in use.
o.B: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance.
o.C: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB, and enable DynamoDB auto scaling.
o.D: Use AWS DataSync to synchronize the database data across multiple EC2 instances.
o.E: Create an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic to an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances that are distributed across two Availability Zones.
