e.why: Migrating MySQL to RDS Multi-AZ gives a synchronous standby in another AZ with automatic failover, without code changes. Placing the stateless Python application in an Auto Scaling group across two AZs behind an ALB removes the single-instance point of failure.

others.A: An internet gateway is a highly available, VPC-level resource; you cannot and need not create one per AZ.
others.C: Moving to DynamoDB requires changing the application code, which is not allowed.
others.D: DataSync transfers files; it is not a database replication or HA mechanism.

e.tip: Classic HA combo: ALB + multi-AZ Auto Scaling group + RDS Multi-AZ.

q: A company is moving its data and applications to AWS during a multiyear migration project. The company wants to securely access data on Amazon S3 from the company's AWS Region and from the company's on-premises location. The data must not traverse the internet. The company has established an AWS Direct Connect connection between its Region and its on-premises location. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create gateway endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the gateway endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
o.B: Create a gateway in AWS Transit Gateway to access Amazon S3 securely from the Region and the on-premises location.
o.C: Create interface endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the interface endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
o.D: Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key to access the data securely from the Region and the on-premises location.

e.why: S3 interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) have private IP addresses in the VPC, so they can be reached from on premises over Direct Connect as well as from within the Region. Traffic stays on private connectivity and does not traverse the internet.

others.A: S3 gateway endpoints work only for traffic originating in the VPC and cannot be used from on-premises networks.
others.B: Transit Gateway connects VPCs and networks but does not itself provide private access to S3.
others.D: A KMS key provides encryption, not a private network path, so traffic could still traverse the internet.

e.tip: On-prem private access to S3 = interface endpoint; in-VPC only and free = gateway endpoint.

q: A company created a new organization in AWS Organizations. The organization has multiple accounts for the company's development teams. The development team members use AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to access the accounts. For each of the company's applications, the development teams must use a predefined application name to tag resources that are created. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that gives the development team the ability to create resources only if the application name tag has an approved value. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an IAM group that has a conditional Allow policy that requires the application name tag to be specified for resources to be created.
o.B: Create a cross-account role that has a Deny policy for any resource that has the application name tag.
o.C: Create a resource group in AWS Resource Groups to validate that the tags are applied to all resources in all accounts.
o.D: Create a tag policy in Organizations that has a list of allowed application names.

e.why: An Organizations tag policy can define the application name tag key and its allowed values, and with enforcement enabled for specified resource types, noncompliant tagging operations are prevented. It applies centrally across all accounts in the organization.

others.A: IAM groups are not used with IAM Identity Center users in member accounts, and per-account IAM policies are harder to manage centrally across the organization.
others.B: A Deny for resources that have the tag would block the correctly tagged resources, the opposite of the goal.
others.C: Resource Groups organizes and views resources; it does not validate or enforce tag values.

e.tip: Standardize allowed tag values across an organization = tag policies (often paired with an SCP requiring the tag).

q: A company runs its databases on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company wants a secure solution to manage the master user password by rotating the password every 30 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule a custom AWS Lambda function to rotate the password every 30 days.
o.B: Use the modify-db-instance command in the AWS CLI to change the password.
o.C: Integrate AWS Secrets Manager with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.
o.D: Integrate AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.

e.why: AWS Secrets Manager integrates natively with RDS (including RDS-managed master user passwords) and provides built-in automatic rotation on a schedule such as every 30 days. No custom code is required, so it has the least operational overhead.

others.A: A custom Lambda function on an EventBridge schedule must be written and maintained, adding overhead.
others.B: Running modify-db-instance manually is not automated and the new password still has to be stored securely.
others.D: Parameter Store has no built-in rotation for RDS credentials.

e.tip: Automatic credential rotation = Secrets Manager; Parameter Store has no native rotation.

q: A company performs tests on an application that uses an Amazon DynamoDB table. The tests run for 4 hours once a week. The company knows how many read and write operations the application performs to the table each second during the tests. The company does not currently use DynamoDB for any other use case. A solutions architect needs to optimize the costs for the table. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Choose on-demand mode. Update the read and write capacity units appropriately.
o.B: Choose provisioned mode. Update the read and write capacity units appropriately.
o.C: Purchase DynamoDB reserved capacity for a 1-year term.
o.D: Purchase DynamoDB reserved capacity for a 3-year term.

e.why: The tests have known, steady read and write rates, so provisioned mode can be set to exactly that capacity during the 4-hour window and lowered afterward. Provisioned capacity costs less per request than on-demand when utilization is predictable.

others.A: On-demand mode does not use read and write capacity unit settings, and it is priced higher per request for a known, steady load.
others.C: Reserved capacity requires a 1-year commitment for continuous capacity, wasteful for 4 hours a week.
others.D: A 3-year reservation is even more wasteful for a weekly 4-hour test.

e.tip: Known, predictable throughput = provisioned mode; unknown or spiky = on-demand.

q: A company runs its applications on Amazon EC2 instances. The company performs periodic financial assessments of its AWS costs. The company recently identified unusual spending. The company needs a solution to prevent unusual spending. The solution must monitor costs and notify responsible stakeholders in the event of unusual spending. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use an AWS Budgets template to create a zero spend budget.
o.B: Create an AWS Cost Anomaly Detection monitor in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console.
o.C: Create AWS Pricing Calculator estimates for the current running workload pricing details.
o.D: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor costs and to identify unusual spending.

e.why: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to monitor spending patterns continuously and sends alerts through email or SNS to stakeholders when unusual spend is detected. This directly meets the requirement to monitor costs and notify on anomalies.

others.A: A zero spend budget alerts on any spend at all, which is not useful for an account that already runs workloads.
others.C: Pricing Calculator produces estimates; it does not monitor actual spend or notify anyone.
others.D: CloudWatch billing alarms only alert on fixed thresholds and do not identify unusual spending patterns.

e.tip: Unusual or unexpected spend = Cost Anomaly Detection; fixed thresholds = AWS Budgets.

q: A marketing company receives a large amount of new clickstream data in Amazon S3 from a marketing campaign. The company needs to analyze the clickstream data in Amazon S3 quickly. Then the company needs to determine whether to process the data further in the data pipeline. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create external tables in a Spark catalog. Configure jobs in AWS Glue to query the data.
o.B: Configure an AWS Glue crawler to crawl the data. Configure Amazon Athena to query the data.
o.C: Create external tables in a Hive metastore. Configure Spark jobs in Amazon EMR to query the data.
o.D: Configure an AWS Glue crawler to crawl the data. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to use SQL to query the data.

e.why: An AWS Glue crawler infers the schema of the clickstream data and registers tables in the Glue Data Catalog. Amazon Athena can then query the data in S3 immediately with serverless SQL, giving a quick analysis with the least operational overhead.

others.A: Writing and running Glue Spark jobs to query data requires more development effort than ad hoc Athena SQL.
others.C: Running EMR with a Hive metastore and Spark jobs requires cluster management.
others.D: Kinesis Data Analytics is for streaming data, not for querying data already at rest in S3.

e.tip: Quick SQL on S3 data = Glue crawler + Athena.

q: A company runs an SMB file server in its data center. The file server stores large files that the company frequently accesses for up to 7 days after the file creation date. After 7 days, the company needs to be able to access the files with a maximum retrieval time of 24 hours. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS DataSync to copy data that is older than 7 days from the SMB file server to AWS.
o.B: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway to increase the company's storage space. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.
o.C: Create an Amazon FSx File Gateway to increase the company's storage space. Create an Amazon S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data after 7 days.
o.D: Configure access to Amazon S3 for each user. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days.

e.why: Amazon S3 File Gateway presents an SMB share backed by S3 and caches recently used files locally for fast access during the first 7 days. An S3 Lifecycle rule then moves objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, whose standard retrieval completes within 12 hours (bulk within 48), meeting the 24-hour retrieval limit at the lowest cost.

others.A: DataSync only copies data; it does not provide ongoing SMB access or a tiering policy for older files.
others.C: FSx File Gateway caches FSx for Windows File Server shares, which do not support S3 Lifecycle transitions.
others.D: Giving each user direct S3 access breaks the SMB file-share workflow and adds per-user administration.

e.tip: SMB/NFS on premises backed by S3 with lifecycle tiering = S3 File Gateway.

q: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application uses a database that runs on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The application performs slowly when traffic increases. The database experiences a heavy read load during periods of high traffic. Which actions should a solutions architect take to resolve these performance issues? (Choose two.)

o.A: Turn on auto scaling for the DB instance.
o.B: Create a read replica for the DB instance. Configure the application to send read traffic to the read replica.
o.C: Convert the DB instance to a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Configure the application to send read traffic to the standby DB instance.
o.D: Create an Amazon ElastiCache cluster. Configure the application to cache query results in the ElastiCache cluster.
o.E: Configure the Auto Scaling group subnets to ensure that the EC2 instances are provisioned in the same Availability Zone as the DB instance.

e.why: A read replica offloads read queries from the primary RDS for PostgreSQL instance, and the application can send read traffic to it. ElastiCache caches frequently requested query results in memory, further reducing database read load and latency during traffic spikes.

others.A: RDS storage auto scaling only grows storage; it does not add compute for read load.
others.C: The standby in a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment cannot serve read traffic.
others.E: Placing instances in the same AZ as the database reduces resilience and does not address read load.

e.tip: Read-heavy RDS = read replicas and/or ElastiCache; Multi-AZ instance standby is for HA only.

q: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to run an application. The company creates one snapshot of each EBS volume every day to meet compliance requirements. The company wants to implement an architecture that prevents the accidental deletion of EBS volume snapshots. The solution must not change the administrative rights of the storage administrator user. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort?

o.A: Create an IAM role that has permission to delete snapshots. Attach the role to a new EC2 instance. Use the AWS CLI from the new EC2 instance to delete snapshots.
o.B: Create an IAM policy that denies snapshot deletion. Attach the policy to the storage administrator user.
o.C: Add tags to the snapshots. Create retention rules in Recycle Bin for EBS snapshots that have the tags.
o.D: Lock the EBS snapshots to prevent deletion.

e.why: EBS Snapshot Lock lets you lock snapshots for a retention period (governance or compliance mode) so they cannot be deleted, regardless of the user's IAM permissions. It is applied directly to the snapshots, so the storage administrator's rights are unchanged and effort is minimal.

others.A: Creating a role and EC2 instance for deletions adds effort and does not prevent the administrator from deleting snapshots.
others.B: Attaching a deny policy changes the storage administrator's administrative rights, which is not allowed.
others.C: Recycle Bin allows recovery after deletion rather than preventing deletion, and requires tagging every snapshot.

e.tip: Prevent deletion = Snapshot Lock; recover after accidental deletion = Recycle Bin.

q: A company's application uses Network Load Balancers, Auto Scaling groups, Amazon EC2 instances, and databases that are deployed in an Amazon VPC. The company wants to capture information about traffic to and from the network interfaces in near real time in its Amazon VPC. The company wants to send the information to Amazon OpenSearch Service for analysis. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the log group. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the logs from the log group to OpenSearch Service.
o.B: Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the log group. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the logs from the log group to OpenSearch Service.
o.C: Create a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the trail. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the logs from the trail to OpenSearch Service.
o.D: Create a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the trail. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the logs from the trail to OpenSearch Service.

e.why: VPC Flow Logs capture IP traffic information for network interfaces and can publish to a CloudWatch Logs log group. A subscription filter can stream that log group to Kinesis Data Firehose, which delivers to OpenSearch Service natively in near real time without custom consumers.

others.A: Kinesis Data Streams cannot write directly to OpenSearch; it would require custom consumer code.
others.C: CloudTrail records API calls, not network traffic, and Flow Logs cannot be sent to a trail.
others.D: Flow Logs cannot be delivered to CloudTrail, so this pipeline does not exist.

e.tip: Firehose has native delivery to OpenSearch, S3, Redshift and Splunk; Data Streams needs consumers.

q: A company is developing an application that will run on a production Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The EKS cluster has managed node groups that are provisioned with On-Demand Instances. The company needs a dedicated EKS cluster for development work. The company will use the development cluster infrequently to test the resiliency of the application. The EKS cluster must manage all the nodes. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create a managed node group that contains only Spot Instances.
o.B: Create two managed node groups. Provision one node group with On-Demand Instances. Provision the second node group with Spot Instances.
o.C: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a launch configuration that uses Spot Instances. Configure the user data to add the nodes to the EKS cluster.
o.D: Create a managed node group that contains only On-Demand Instances.

e.why: Using two managed node groups, one On-Demand and one Spot, keeps the nodes fully managed by EKS while cutting cost with Spot capacity. The On-Demand group keeps baseline cluster components running when Spot Instances are interrupted, allowing resiliency testing of the application.

others.A: An all-Spot node group is cheapest but risks losing all nodes at once during interruptions, leaving the cluster unable to run baseline workloads.
others.C: A self-managed Auto Scaling group with user data is not managed by EKS and uses deprecated launch configurations.
others.D: An all On-Demand node group is the most expensive option for an infrequently used dev cluster.

e.tip: Cost-optimized EKS: mix On-Demand for baseline with Spot node groups for the rest.

q: A company stores sensitive data in Amazon S3. A solutions architect needs to create an encryption solution. The company needs to fully control the ability of users to create, rotate, and disable encryption keys with minimal effort for any data that must be encrypted. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use default server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) to store the sensitive data.
o.B: Create a customer managed key by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Use the new key to encrypt the S3 objects by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
o.C: Create an AWS managed key by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Use the new key to encrypt the S3 objects by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
o.D: Download S3 objects to an Amazon EC2 instance. Encrypt the objects by using customer managed keys. Upload the encrypted objects back into Amazon S3.

e.why: A customer managed KMS key gives the company full control over key creation, key policies, rotation (automatic or on demand) and enabling or disabling the key. SSE-KMS applies that key to S3 objects transparently, so encryption requires minimal effort.

others.A: With SSE-S3, AWS manages the keys and users cannot create, rotate or disable them.
others.C: Customers cannot create AWS managed keys or control their rotation or disabling; AWS creates and manages them.
others.D: Downloading, encrypting and re-uploading objects through EC2 is high effort and error prone.

e.tip: Need control over rotate/disable/policy = customer managed KMS key.

q: A company wants to back up its on-premises virtual machines (VMs) to AWS. The company's backup solution exports on-premises backups to an Amazon S3 bucket as objects. The S3 backups must be retained for 30 days and must be automatically deleted after 30 days. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

o.A: Create an S3 bucket that has S3 Object Lock enabled.
o.B: Create an S3 bucket that has object versioning enabled.
o.C: Configure a default retention period of 30 days for the objects.
o.D: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to protect the objects for 30 days.
o.E: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to expire the objects after 30 days.
o.F: Configure the backup solution to tag the objects with a 30-day retention period

e.why: S3 Object Lock (which requires versioning and is enabled on the bucket) with a default retention period of 30 days prevents the backups from being deleted or overwritten during that period. An S3 Lifecycle expiration rule then deletes the objects automatically after 30 days.

others.B: Versioning alone does not prevent deletion and is enabled automatically when Object Lock is enabled.
others.D: Lifecycle policies cannot protect objects from deletion; they only transition or expire them.
others.F: Tags do not enforce any retention; S3 does not act on a tag value as a lock.

e.tip: Retain (WORM) = Object Lock retention; delete afterwards = Lifecycle expiration.

q: A solutions architect needs to copy files from an Amazon S3 bucket to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system and another S3 bucket. The files must be copied continuously. New files are added to the original S3 bucket consistently. The copied files should be overwritten only if the source file changes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an AWS DataSync location for both the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Create a task for the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Set the transfer mode to transfer only data that has changed.
o.B: Create an AWS Lambda function. Mount the file system to the function. Set up an S3 event notification to invoke the function when files are created and changed in Amazon S3. Configure the function to copy files to the file system and the destination S3 bucket.
o.C: Create an AWS DataSync location for both the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Create a task for the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Set the transfer mode to transfer all data.
o.D: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in the same VPC as the file system. Mount the file system. Create a script to routinely synchronize all objects that changed in the origin S3 bucket to the destination S3 bucket and the mounted file system.

e.why: AWS DataSync supports S3 as a source and both S3 and EFS as destinations, and tasks can run on a schedule for continuous copying. Setting the transfer mode to transfer only data that has changed means destination files are overwritten only when the source changes, all with a managed service.

others.B: A custom Lambda function with EFS mount and event notifications must be built and maintained, adding operational overhead.
others.C: Transferring all data every time wastes time and bandwidth and rewrites unchanged files.
others.D: An EC2 instance with a sync script requires managing servers and custom code.

e.tip: Managed recurring copy between S3, EFS, FSx = DataSync with changed-data-only mode.

q: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and stores data on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. The company must ensure that all data is encrypted at rest by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The company must be able to control rotation of the encryption keys. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create a customer managed key. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
o.B: Use an AWS managed key to encrypt the EBS volumes. Use the key to configure automatic key rotation.
o.C: Create an external KMS key with imported key material. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
o.D: Use an AWS owned key to encrypt the EBS volumes.

e.why: A customer managed KMS key lets the company enable automatic rotation and choose the rotation period, or rotate on demand, giving it control of rotation. EBS encryption with that key is native and transparent, so operational overhead is low.

others.B: AWS managed keys rotate automatically every year on AWS's schedule and the customer cannot configure their rotation.
others.C: Imported key material does not support automatic rotation, so rotation must be done manually, adding overhead.
others.D: AWS owned keys are fully controlled by AWS and are not visible to or controllable by the customer.

e.tip: Control rotation with least effort = customer managed key with automatic rotation.

q: A company needs a solution to enforce data encryption at rest on Amazon EC2 instances. The solution must automatically identify noncompliant resources and enforce compliance policies on findings. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

o.A: Use an IAM policy that allows users to create only encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Config and AWS Systems Manager to automate the detection and remediation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
o.B: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to manage access to encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Lambda and Amazon EventBridge to automate the detection and remediation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
o.C: Use Amazon Macie to detect unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation rules to automatically encrypt existing and new EBS volumes.
o.D: Use Amazon inspector to detect unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation rules to automatically encrypt existing and new EBS volumes.

e.why: An IAM policy using the ec2:Encrypted condition can block creation of unencrypted EBS volumes. AWS Config's managed rule encrypted-volumes detects noncompliant volumes automatically, and its remediation actions run Systems Manager Automation documents to fix findings, with little custom work.

others.B: KMS controls key access but does not detect unencrypted volumes, and Lambda plus EventBridge requires custom detection and remediation code.
others.C: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in S3; it does not assess EBS volume encryption.
others.D: Amazon Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities and network exposure, not EBS encryption compliance.

e.tip: Detect and auto-remediate noncompliant config = AWS Config rules + SSM Automation remediation.

q: A company is migrating its multi-tier on-premises application to AWS. The application consists of a single-node MySQL database and a multi-node web tier. The company must minimize changes to the application during the migration. The company wants to improve application resiliency after the migration. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Migrate the web tier to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
o.B: Migrate the database to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer.
o.C: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment.
o.D: Migrate the web tier to an AWS Lambda function.
o.E: Migrate the database to an Amazon DynamoDB table.

e.why: Moving the web tier to EC2 in an Auto Scaling group behind an ALB is a lift-and-shift that adds self-healing and multi-AZ resiliency. Migrating MySQL to RDS Multi-AZ keeps the same engine with minimal changes and adds automatic failover to a standby.

others.B: A single-node MySQL database cannot simply be scaled behind an NLB; multiple independent instances would not share consistent data.
others.D: Rewriting the web tier as Lambda functions requires significant application changes.
others.E: DynamoDB is NoSQL and would require rewriting the data layer.

e.tip: Minimal change + resiliency = EC2 ASG/ALB and RDS Multi-AZ.

q: A company wants to migrate its web applications from on premises to AWS. The company is located close to the eu-central-1 Region. Because of regulations, the company cannot launch some of its applications in eu-central-1. The company wants to achieve single-digit millisecond latency. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy the applications in eu-central-1. Extend the company’s VPC from eu-central-1 to an edge location in Amazon CloudFront.
o.B: Deploy the applications in AWS Local Zones by extending the company's VPC from eu-central-1 to the chosen Local Zone.
o.C: Deploy the applications in eu-central-1. Extend the company’s VPC from eu-central-1 to the regional edge caches in Amazon CloudFront.
o.D: Deploy the applications in AWS Wavelength Zones by extending the company’s VPC from eu-central-1 to the chosen Wavelength Zone.

e.why: AWS Local Zones are extensions of a parent Region placed in metro areas, letting you extend the VPC from eu-central-1 into a Local Zone in a different location. Workloads run outside the eu-central-1 Region itself, satisfying the regulatory constraint, while still achieving single-digit millisecond latency for nearby users.

others.A: CloudFront edge locations cache content; you cannot extend a VPC or run applications in them.
others.C: Regional edge caches are part of CloudFront's caching tier and cannot host VPC workloads.
others.D: Wavelength Zones are embedded in telecom 5G networks for mobile-device latency, not general on-premises web application migration.

e.tip: Low latency to a metro area via VPC extension = Local Zones; 5G mobile edge = Wavelength.

q: A company’s ecommerce website has unpredictable traffic and uses AWS Lambda functions to directly access a private Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The company wants to maintain predictable database performance and ensure that the Lambda invocations do not overload the database with too many connections. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Point the client driver at an RDS custom endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions inside a VPC.
o.B: Point the client driver at an RDS proxy endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions inside a VPC.
o.C: Point the client driver at an RDS custom endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions outside a VPC.
o.D: Point the client driver at an RDS proxy endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions outside a VPC.

e.why: RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections, so bursts of Lambda invocations do not open too many connections and database performance stays predictable. Because the RDS instance is private, the Lambda functions must be attached to the VPC to reach the proxy endpoint.

others.A: RDS custom endpoints are an Aurora feature for grouping instances and do not pool connections.
others.C: Custom endpoints do not pool connections, and Lambda outside the VPC cannot reach a private database.
others.D: RDS Proxy is only reachable from within the VPC, so Lambda outside the VPC cannot use it.

e.tip: Lambda + relational DB connection storms = RDS Proxy, Lambda in the VPC.

q: A company is creating an application. The company stores data from tests of the application in multiple on-premises locations. The company needs to connect the on-premises locations to VPCs in an AWS Region in the AWS Cloud. The number of accounts and VPCs will increase during the next year. The network architecture must simplify the administration of new connections and must provide the ability to scale. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

o.A: Create a peering connection between the VPCs. Create a VPN connection between the VPCs and the on-premises locations.
o.B: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. On the instance, include VPN software that uses a VPN connection to connect all VPCs and on-premises locations.
o.C: Create a transit gateway. Create VPC attachments for the VPC connections. Create VPN attachments for the on-premises connections.
o.D: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises locations and a central VPC. Connect the central VPC to other VPCs by using peering connections.

e.why: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a regional hub: VPCs attach with VPC attachments and on-premises sites with Site-to-Site VPN attachments. New accounts and VPCs are added with a single attachment (and can be shared via AWS RAM), avoiding a mesh of peering connections and scaling with minimal administration.

others.A: VPC peering is non-transitive and grows as a full mesh, and per-VPC VPNs multiply connections to manage.
others.B: A self-managed VPN EC2 instance is a single point of failure and requires ongoing management.
others.D: Peering is non-transitive, so on-premises traffic cannot route through the central VPC to other peered VPCs.

e.tip: Many VPCs + on-prem sites, scaling = Transit Gateway hub.

q: A company that uses AWS needs a solution to predict the resources needed for manufacturing processes each month. The solution must use historical values that are currently stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has no machine learning (ML) experience and wants to use a managed service for the training and predictions. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Deploy an Amazon SageMaker model. Create a SageMaker endpoint for inference.
o.B: Use Amazon SageMaker to train a model by using the historical data in the S3 bucket.
o.C: Configure an AWS Lambda function with a function URL that uses Amazon SageMaker endpoints to create predictions based on the inputs.
o.D: Configure an AWS Lambda function with a function URL that uses an Amazon Forecast predictor to create a prediction based on the inputs.
o.E: Train an Amazon Forsecast predictor by using the historical data in the S3 bucket.

e.why: Amazon Forecast is a fully managed time-series forecasting service that requires no ML expertise: you import historical data from S3 and train a predictor. A Lambda function with a function URL can then query the Forecast predictor to return predictions for given inputs.

others.A: Deploying SageMaker models and endpoints requires ML knowledge to build, tune and host models.
others.B: Training a model in SageMaker requires choosing algorithms and ML expertise the company lacks.
others.C: Using SageMaker endpoints depends on building and deploying a custom model, which requires ML experience.

e.tip: Time-series forecasting without ML expertise = Amazon Forecast. Note: AWS closed Forecast to new customers in 2024; SageMaker Canvas is now the suggested no-code alternative.

q: A company manages AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) and AWS Control Tower are configured for the accounts. The company wants to manage multiple user permissions across all the accounts. The permissions will be used by multiple IAM users and must be split between the developer and administrator teams. Each team requires different permissions. The company wants a solution that includes new users that are hired on both teams. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create individual users in IAM Identity Center for each account. Create separate developer and administrator groups in IAM Identity Center. Assign the users to the appropriate groups. Create a custom IAM policy for each group to set fine-grained permissions.
o.B: Create individual users in IAM Identity Center for each account. Create separate developer and administrator groups in IAM Identity Center. Assign the users to the appropriate groups. Attach AWS managed IAM policies to each user as needed for fine-grained permissions.
o.C: Create individual users in IAM Identity Center. Create new developer and administrator groups in IAM Identity Center. Create new permission sets that include the appropriate IAM policies for each group. Assign the new groups to the appropriate accounts. Assign the new permission sets to the new groups. When new users are hired, add them to the appropriate group.
o.D: Create individual users in IAM Identity Center. Create new permission sets that include the appropriate IAM policies for each user. Assign the users to the appropriate accounts. Grant additional IAM permissions to the users from within specific accounts. When new users are hired, add them to IAM Identity Center and assign them to the accounts.

e.why: With IAM Identity Center, you create groups for developers and administrators, define permission sets containing the needed policies, and assign each group plus permission set to the appropriate accounts. New hires simply join a group to inherit all access across accounts, minimizing ongoing effort.

others.A: Identity Center users are not created per account, and custom IAM policies per group do not use permission sets for multi-account access.
others.B: Attaching managed policies to each user individually does not scale and ignores permission sets.
others.D: Per-user permission sets and extra per-account IAM grants create high ongoing administrative overhead.

e.tip: Multi-account access with Identity Center: groups + permission sets assigned to accounts.

q: A company wants to standardize its Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume encryption strategy. The company also wants to minimize the cost and configuration effort required to operate the volume encryption check. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Write API calls to describe the EBS volumes and to confirm the EBS volumes are encrypted. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an AWS Lambda function to run the API calls.
o.B: Write API calls to describe the EBS volumes and to confirm the EBS volumes are encrypted. Run the API calls on an AWS Fargate task.
o.C: Create an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy that requires the use of tags on EBS volumes. Use AWS Cost Explorer to display resources that are not properly tagged. Encrypt the untagged resources manually.
o.D: Create an AWS Config rule for Amazon EBS to evaluate if a volume is encrypted and to flag the volume if it is not encrypted.

e.why: AWS Config's managed rule encrypted-volumes continuously evaluates EBS volumes and flags any that are not encrypted. It needs no custom code or compute, so it minimizes both cost and configuration effort while standardizing the encryption check.

others.A: A scheduled Lambda function with custom API calls must be written, tested and maintained.
others.B: Running custom checks on Fargate tasks adds code, scheduling and compute costs.
others.C: Tags and Cost Explorer do not indicate encryption status, and manual encryption is error prone.

e.tip: Continuous compliance checks on resource configuration = AWS Config managed rules.

q: A company regularly uploads GB-sized files to Amazon S3. After the company uploads the files, the company uses a fleet of Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to transcode the file format. The company needs to scale throughput when the company uploads data from the on-premises data center to Amazon S3 and when the company downloads data from Amazon S3 to the EC2 instances. Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use the S3 bucket access point instead of accessing the S3 bucket directly.
o.B: Upload the files into multiple S3 buckets.
o.C: Use S3 multipart uploads.
o.D: Fetch multiple byte-ranges of an object in parallel.
o.E: Add a random prefix to each object when uploading the files.

e.why: S3 multipart upload splits large files into parts uploaded in parallel, raising upload throughput from on premises. Byte-range fetches download multiple ranges of the same object in parallel, scaling download throughput to the EC2 instances.

others.A: Access points simplify access control; they do not increase transfer throughput.
others.B: Spreading files across buckets adds complexity and does not speed up individual large transfers.
others.E: Random prefixes are no longer needed since S3 scales to 3,500 PUT and 5,500 GET requests per second per prefix, and they do not speed up single large files.

e.tip: Big uploads = multipart; big downloads = parallel byte-range GETs.

q: A solutions architect is designing a shared storage solution for a web application that is deployed across multiple Availability Zones. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. The company plans to make frequent changes to the content. The solution must have strong consistency in returning the new content as soon as the changes occur. Which solutions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) block storage that is mounted to the individual EC2 instances.
o.B: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on the individual EC2 instances.
o.C: Create a shared Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume on the individual EC2 instances.
o.D: Use AWS DataSync to perform continuous synchronization of data between EC2 hosts in the Auto Scaling group.
o.E: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the web content. Set the metadata for the Cache-Control header to no-cache. Use Amazon CloudFront to deliver the content.

e.why: Amazon EFS is a shared, multi-AZ file system that provides strong read-after-write consistency to all mounted EC2 instances. S3 also provides strong read-after-write consistency, and setting Cache-Control: no-cache makes CloudFront revalidate with the origin so the newest content is returned immediately.

others.A: Volume Gateway iSCSI volumes are block storage for on-premises use and cannot be shared safely across multiple EC2 instances.
others.C: EBS volumes are AZ-scoped, and Multi-Attach is limited to io1/io2 in one AZ and requires a cluster-aware file system.
others.D: DataSync runs scheduled transfers and does not provide immediate, strongly consistent shared storage.

e.tip: Shared file storage across AZs = EFS; S3 is strongly consistent for reads after writes.

q: A company is deploying an application in three AWS Regions using an Application Load Balancer. Amazon Route 53 will be used to distribute traffic between these Regions. Which Route 53 configuration should a solutions architect use to provide the MOST high-performing experience?

o.A: Create an A record with a latency policy.
o.B: Create an A record with a geolocation policy.
o.C: Create a CNAME record with a failover policy.
o.D: Create a CNAME record with a geoproximity policy.

e.why: A Route 53 latency-based routing policy sends each user to the Region with the lowest measured network latency for that user, providing the best performance. An A record (alias) can point to each Region's ALB.

others.B: Geolocation routes by the user's location for compliance or localization, which does not always give the lowest latency.
others.C: Failover routing is active-passive for disaster recovery, not performance across three active Regions.
others.D: Geoproximity routes by geographic distance with bias, which is not the same as measured latency, and needs Traffic Flow.

e.tip: 'Best performance' across Regions in Route 53 = latency routing.

q: A company has a web application that includes an embedded NoSQL database. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone. A recent increase in traffic requires the application to be highly available and for the database to be eventually consistent. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer. Maintain the embedded NoSQL database with its replication service on the EC2 instances.
o.B: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer. Migrate the embedded NoSQL database to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
o.C: Modify the Auto Scaling group to use EC2 instances across three Availability Zones. Maintain the embedded NoSQL database with its replication service on the EC2 instances.
o.D: Modify the Auto Scaling group to use EC2 instances across three Availability Zones. Migrate the embedded NoSQL database to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).

e.why: Spreading the Auto Scaling group across three Availability Zones makes the web tier highly available. Migrating the embedded NoSQL database to DynamoDB with AWS DMS gives a fully managed, multi-AZ database that supports eventually consistent reads, removing database management overhead.

others.A: An NLB does not improve availability over an ALB here, and the instances remain in one AZ with a self-managed database.
others.B: Swapping to an NLB does not fix the single-AZ compute tier.
others.C: Keeping the embedded database replication on EC2 means managing database replication and recovery yourself.

e.tip: HA = multiple AZs; least overhead for NoSQL = DynamoDB.

q: A company is building a shopping application on AWS. The application offers a catalog that changes once each month and needs to scale with traffic volume. The company wants the lowest possible latency from the application. Data from each user's shopping cart needs to be highly available. User session data must be available even if the user is disconnected and reconnects. What should a solutions architect do to ensure that the shopping cart data is preserved at all times?

o.A: Configure an Application Load Balancer to enable the sticky sessions feature (session affinity) for access to the catalog in Amazon Aurora.
o.B: Configure Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to cache catalog data from Amazon DynamoDB and shopping cart data from the user's session.
o.C: Configure Amazon OpenSearch Service to cache catalog data from Amazon DynamoDB and shopping cart data from the user's session.
o.D: Configure an Amazon EC2 instance with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage for the catalog and shopping cart. Configure automated snapshots.

e.why: ElastiCache for Redis provides sub-millisecond in-memory access for caching the slowly changing catalog from DynamoDB. It also stores shopping cart and session data outside the web servers, with Multi-AZ replication for high availability, so the cart persists when a user disconnects and reconnects to any server.

others.A: Sticky sessions tie users to one instance, so cart data is lost if that instance fails, and Aurora is not a low-latency cache.
others.C: OpenSearch Service is a search and analytics engine, not a low-latency session or cache store.
others.D: A single EC2 instance with EBS is a single point of failure and does not scale with traffic.

e.tip: Externalize session state to ElastiCache (Redis) or DynamoDB for HA and scaling.

q: A company is building a microservices-based application that will be deployed on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The microservices will interact with each other. The company wants to ensure that the application is observable to identify performance issues in the future. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure the application to use Amazon ElastiCache to reduce the number of requests that are sent to the microservices.
o.B: Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to collect metrics from the EKS clusters. Configure AWS X-Ray to trace the requests between the microservices.
o.C: Configure AWS CloudTrail to review the API calls. Build an Amazon QuickSight dashboard to observe the microservice interactions.
o.D: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to understand the performance of the application.

e.why: CloudWatch Container Insights collects, aggregates and summarizes metrics and logs from EKS clusters, nodes, pods and services. AWS X-Ray provides distributed tracing of requests across the microservices, revealing latency and errors between services.

others.A: ElastiCache reduces load but provides no observability into performance issues.
others.C: CloudTrail logs AWS API calls, not application-level requests between microservices.
others.D: Trusted Advisor gives account-level best-practice checks, not application performance insight.

e.tip: Metrics for containers = Container Insights; request tracing across services = X-Ray.

q: A company needs to provide customers with secure access to its data. The company processes customer data and stores the results in an Amazon S3 bucket. All the data is subject to strong regulations and security requirements. The data must be encrypted at rest. Each customer must be able to access only their data from their AWS account. Company employees must not be able to access the data. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Provision an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate for each customer. Encrypt the data client-side. In the private certificate policy, deny access to the certificate for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.
o.B: Provision a separate AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key for each customer. Encrypt the data server-side. In the S3 bucket policy, deny decryption of data for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.
o.C: Provision a separate AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key for each customer. Encrypt the data server-side. In each KMS key policy, deny decryption of data for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.
o.D: Provision an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate for each customer. Encrypt the data client-side. In the public certificate policy, deny access to the certificate for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.

e.why: A separate KMS key per customer with SSE-KMS encrypts each customer's data at rest. Each key policy can deny kms:Decrypt to all principals except the customer's IAM role (cross-account), so only that customer can decrypt their data and company employees cannot.

others.A: ACM certificates are for TLS, not data encryption, and ACM has no certificate policies controlling decryption.
others.B: S3 bucket policies cannot control KMS decryption permissions; decryption rights are governed by the KMS key policy.
others.D: Public ACM certificates cannot be used to encrypt data and have no such access policy.

e.tip: Who can decrypt is controlled by the KMS key policy; per-tenant keys isolate tenants.

q: A solutions architect creates a VPC that includes two public subnets and two private subnets. A corporate security mandate requires the solutions architect to launch all Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. However, when the solutions architect launches an EC2 instance that runs a web server on ports 80 and 443 in a private subnet, no external internet traffic can connect to the server. What should the solutions architect do to resolve this issue?

o.A: Attach the EC2 instance to an Auto Scaling group in a private subnet. Ensure that the DNS record for the website resolves to the Auto Scaling group identifier.
o.B: Provision an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB) in a public subnet. Add the EC2 instance to the target group that is associated with the ALEnsure that the DNS record for the website resolves to the ALB.
o.C: Launch a NAT gateway in a private subnet. Update the route table for the private subnets to add a default route to the NAT gateway. Attach a public Elastic IP address to the NAT gateway.
o.D: Ensure that the security group that is attached to the EC2 instance allows HTTP traffic on port 80 and HTTPS traffic on port 443. Ensure that the DNS record for the website resolves to the public IP address of the EC2 instance.

e.why: An internet-facing Application Load Balancer in the public subnets receives internet traffic on ports 80 and 443 and forwards it to the EC2 instance in the private subnet registered in its target group. Pointing DNS at the ALB keeps the instance private, meeting the mandate.

others.A: An Auto Scaling group identifier is not a DNS target, and instances in a private subnet remain unreachable from the internet.
others.C: A NAT gateway only allows outbound traffic from private subnets and must sit in a public subnet; it does not accept inbound connections.
others.D: Instances in a private subnet have no route from the internet gateway, so security group rules and a public IP will not help.

e.tip: Private instances serving the internet = public ALB/NLB in front; NAT is outbound only.

q: A company is deploying a new application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with an AWS Fargate cluster. The application needs a storage solution for data persistence. The solution must be highly available and fault tolerant. The solution also must be shared between multiple application containers. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes in the same Availability Zones where EKS worker nodes are placed. Register the volumes in a StorageClass object on an EKS cluster. Use EBS Multi-Attach to share the data between containers.
o.B: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Register the file system in a StorageClass object on an EKS cluster. Use the same file system for all containers.
o.C: Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Register the volume in a StorageClass object on an EKS cluster. Use the same volume for all containers.
o.D: Create Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file systems in the same Availability Zones where EKS worker nodes are placed. Register the file systems in a StorageClass object on an EKS cluster. Create an AWS Lambda function to synchronize the data between file systems.

e.why: Amazon EFS is a regional, multi-AZ file system that can be mounted by many pods concurrently, and EKS on Fargate supports EFS through the EFS CSI driver. Registering it in a StorageClass and sharing one file system gives highly available, shared persistent storage with minimal management.

others.A: Fargate pods cannot mount EBS volumes, and EBS Multi-Attach is limited to a single AZ.
others.C: An EBS volume lives in one AZ and cannot be shared across pods on Fargate, so it is neither shared nor fault tolerant.
others.D: Multiple EFS file systems synchronized by Lambda add unnecessary complexity; a single EFS file system is already multi-AZ.

e.tip: Fargate persistent shared storage = EFS.

q: A company has an application that uses Docker containers in its local data center. The application runs on a container host that stores persistent data in a volume on the host. The container instances use the stored persistent data. The company wants to move the application to a fully managed service because the company does not want to manage any servers or storage infrastructure. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with self-managed nodes. Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume attached to an Amazon EC2 instance. Use the EBS volume as a persistent volume mounted in the containers.
o.B: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an AWS Fargate launch type. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Add the EFS volume as a persistent storage volume mounted in the containers.
o.C: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an AWS Fargate launch type. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Map the S3 bucket as a persistent storage volume mounted in the containers.
o.D: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an Amazon EC2 launch type. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Add the EFS volume as a persistent storage volume mounted in the containers.

e.why: ECS with the Fargate launch type removes all server management, and Amazon EFS volumes can be mounted into Fargate tasks as persistent, shared storage that AWS fully manages. This meets the no-servers, no-storage-infrastructure requirement.

others.A: Self-managed EKS nodes and an EC2-attached EBS volume require managing servers and storage.
others.C: S3 cannot be mapped natively as a persistent volume in ECS task definitions; it is object storage, not a file system mount.
others.D: The EC2 launch type requires the company to manage the container instances.

e.tip: Serverless containers needing persistent volumes = Fargate + EFS.

q: A gaming company wants to launch a new internet-facing application in multiple AWS Regions. The application will use the TCP and UDP protocols for communication. The company needs to provide high availability and minimum latency for global users. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create internal Network Load Balancers in front of the application in each Region.
o.B: Create external Application Load Balancers in front of the application in each Region.
o.C: Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator to route traffic to the load balancers in each Region.
o.D: Configure Amazon Route 53 to use a geolocation routing policy to distribute the traffic.
o.E: Configure Amazon CloudFront to handle the traffic and route requests to the application in each Region

e.why: Network Load Balancers handle both TCP and UDP traffic in each Region. AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs and routes users over the AWS global network to the nearest healthy Regional NLB endpoint, giving low latency and fast cross-Region failover.

others.B: Application Load Balancers do not support UDP.
others.D: Geolocation routing relies on DNS and does not optimize latency or provide fast failover.
others.E: CloudFront serves HTTP/HTTPS traffic and does not proxy arbitrary TCP and UDP game traffic.

e.tip: Global TCP+UDP with HA and low latency = Global Accelerator + NLBs.

q: A city has deployed a web application running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application's users have reported sporadic performance, which appears to be related to DDoS attacks originating from random IP addresses. The city needs a solution that requires minimal configuration changes and provides an audit trail for the DDoS sources. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Enable an AWS WAF web ACL on the ALB, and configure rules to block traffic from unknown sources.
o.B: Subscribe to Amazon Inspector. Engage the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT) to integrate mitigating controls into the service.
o.C: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Engage the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT) to integrate mitigating controls into the service.
o.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the application, and set the ALB as the origin. Enable an AWS WAF web ACL on the distribution, and configure rules to block traffic from unknown sources

e.why: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS protection for ALBs, detailed attack diagnostics and reporting that serves as an audit trail, and access to the Shield Response Team (formerly DRT) to apply mitigations. It requires minimal configuration changes to the existing architecture.

others.A: WAF rules blocking 'unknown sources' are impractical for random IPs and do not give DDoS attack diagnostics.
others.B: Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability scanner, and the DDoS Response Team is only available with Shield Advanced.
others.D: Adding CloudFront changes the architecture and DNS, and WAF alone lacks DDoS attack reporting and expert response.

e.tip: DDoS protection + attack visibility + expert response team = Shield Advanced.

q: A company copies 200 TB of data from a recent ocean survey onto AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices. The company has a high performance computing (HPC) cluster that is hosted on AWS to look for oil and gas deposits. A solutions architect must provide the cluster with consistent sub-millisecond latency and high-throughput access to the data on the Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices. The company is sending the devices back to AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Import the data into the S3 bucket. Configure an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway to use the S3 bucket. Access the file gateway from the HPC cluster instances.
o.B: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Import the data into the S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system, and integrate it with the S3 bucket. Access the FSx for Lustre file system from the HPC cluster instances.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket and an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Import the data into the S3 bucket. Copy the data from the S3 bucket to the EFS file system. Access the EFS file system from the HPC cluster instances.
o.D: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Import the data directly into the FSx for Lustre file system. Access the FSx for Lustre file system from the HPC cluster instances.

e.why: Snowball Edge devices import data into Amazon S3. Linking an FSx for Lustre file system to the S3 bucket presents the data to the HPC cluster as a high-throughput parallel file system with consistent sub-millisecond latency, lazily loading or preloading objects from S3.

others.A: Storage Gateway file gateway is for on-premises access to S3 and does not deliver HPC-grade throughput and latency in AWS.
others.C: EFS does not match FSx for Lustre performance for HPC, and copying 200 TB adds time and cost.
others.D: Snowball Edge import jobs land data in S3, not directly into an FSx for Lustre file system.

e.tip: Snowball imports to S3; then FSx for Lustre linked to S3 for HPC.

q: A company has NFS servers in an on-premises data center that need to periodically back up small amounts of data to Amazon S3. Which solution meets these requirements and is MOST cost-effective?

o.A: Set up AWS Glue to copy the data from the on-premises servers to Amazon S3.
o.B: Set up an AWS DataSync agent on the on-premises servers, and sync the data to Amazon S3.
o.C: Set up an SFTP sync using AWS Transfer for SFTP to sync data from on premises to Amazon S3.
o.D: Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises data center and a VPC, and copy the data to Amazon S3.

e.why: AWS DataSync uses an on-premises agent to read from NFS shares and transfer data to S3 on a schedule, with incremental transfers, encryption and integrity checks. Paying per GB transferred makes it cost-effective for small periodic backups.

others.A: AWS Glue is an ETL service and cannot read from on-premises NFS servers for backup.
others.C: Transfer Family incurs hourly endpoint charges and requires an SFTP client workflow, making it costlier and less suitable.
others.D: Direct Connect is expensive and slow to provision for small, periodic backups.

e.tip: Scheduled NFS/SMB to S3 transfers = DataSync.

q: An online video game company must maintain ultra-low latency for its game servers. The game servers run on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs a solution that can handle millions of UDP internet traffic requests each second. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure an Application Load Balancer with the required protocol and ports for the internet traffic. Specify the EC2 instances as the targets.
o.B: Configure a Gateway Load Balancer for the internet traffic. Specify the EC2 instances as the targets.
o.C: Configure a Network Load Balancer with the required protocol and ports for the internet traffic. Specify the EC2 instances as the targets.
o.D: Launch an identical set of game servers on EC2 instances in separate AWS Regions. Route internet traffic to both sets of EC2 instances.

e.why: A Network Load Balancer operates at layer 4, supports UDP, and can handle millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency. Registering the game server EC2 instances as targets provides this cost-effectively.

others.A: Application Load Balancers do not support UDP.
others.B: Gateway Load Balancers are for inline virtual appliances such as firewalls, not distributing client traffic to game servers.
others.D: Duplicating servers across Regions increases cost and does not by itself load balance UDP traffic.

e.tip: UDP + millions of requests per second + low latency = NLB.

q: A company runs a three-tier application in a VPC. The database tier uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The company plans to migrate the RDS for MySQL DB instance to an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. The company needs a solution that replicates the data changes that happen during the migration to the new database. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) Schema Conversion to transform the database objects.
o.B: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) Schema Conversion to create an Aurora PostgreSQL read replica on the RDS for MySQL DB instance.
o.C: Configure an Aurora MySQL read replica for the RDS for MySQL DB instance.
o.D: Define an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) task with change data capture (CDC) to migrate the data.
o.E: Promote the Aurora PostgreSQL read replica to a standalone Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster when the replica lag is zero.

e.why: Moving from MySQL to PostgreSQL is a heterogeneous migration, so DMS Schema Conversion is used to convert the schema and database objects to Aurora PostgreSQL. A DMS task with full load plus change data capture (CDC) then copies the data and continuously replicates ongoing changes until cutover.

others.B: DMS Schema Conversion converts schemas; it cannot create an Aurora PostgreSQL read replica of an RDS for MySQL instance.
others.C: An Aurora MySQL read replica keeps the MySQL engine, not the required PostgreSQL target.
others.E: Cross-engine Aurora PostgreSQL read replicas of RDS for MySQL do not exist, so there is nothing to promote.

e.tip: Heterogeneous migration = schema conversion (DMS SC/SCT) + DMS full load and CDC.

q: A company hosts a database that runs on an Amazon RDS instance that is deployed to multiple Availability Zones. The company periodically runs a script against the database to report new entries that are added to the database. The script that runs against the database negatively affects the performance of a critical application. The company needs to improve application performance with minimal costs. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Add functionality to the script to identify the instance that has the fewest active connections. Configure the script to read from that instance to report the total new entries.
o.B: Create a read replica of the database. Configure the script to query only the read replica to report the total new entries.
o.C: Instruct the development team to manually export the new entries for the day in the database at the end of each day.
o.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache to cache the common queries that the script runs against the database.

e.why: A read replica serves read-only queries from an asynchronously replicated copy, so pointing the reporting script at it removes the load from the primary. It is a simple configuration change with low cost and no code complexity.

others.A: In a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment the standby cannot be read, so the script cannot pick a less busy instance; this also requires custom logic.
others.C: Manual daily exports are labor intensive and error prone.
others.D: Caching rarely helps a script that looks for new entries, and it adds a service plus application changes.

e.tip: Offload reporting reads = read replica.

q: A company is using an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to present its application to the internet. The company finds abnormal traffic access patterns across the application. A solutions architect needs to improve visibility into the infrastructure to help the company understand these abnormalities better. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

o.A: Create a table in Amazon Athena for AWS CloudTrail logs. Create a query for the relevant information.
o.B: Enable ALB access logging to Amazon S3. Create a table in Amazon Athena, and query the logs.
o.C: Enable ALB access logging to Amazon S3. Open each file in a text editor, and search each line for the relevant information.
o.D: Use Amazon EMR on a dedicated Amazon EC2 instance to directly query the ALB to acquire traffic access log information.

e.why: ALB access logs record each request's client IP, path, latency, status codes and user agent, delivered to S3. Defining an Athena table over the logs lets you run SQL queries to analyze abnormal patterns without managing any infrastructure.

others.A: CloudTrail captures AWS API calls, not HTTP requests reaching the ALB.
others.C: Manually searching log files in a text editor is not operationally efficient.
others.D: EMR cannot query an ALB directly, and running a cluster adds overhead.

e.tip: Analyze ALB/CloudFront/VPC logs in S3 = Athena.

q: A company wants to use NAT gateways in its AWS environment. The company's Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets must be able to connect to the public internet through the NAT gateways. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create public NAT gateways in the same private subnets as the EC2 instances.
o.B: Create private NAT gateways in the same private subnets as the EC2 instances.
o.C: Create public NAT gateways in public subnets in the same VPCs as the EC2 instances.
o.D: Create private NAT gateways in public subnets in the same VPCs as the EC2 instances.

e.why: A public NAT gateway must be placed in a public subnet (one with a route to the internet gateway) and has an Elastic IP. Private subnet route tables send 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway, allowing outbound internet access.

others.A: A public NAT gateway in a private subnet has no route to the internet gateway, so traffic cannot reach the internet.
others.B: Private NAT gateways are for connecting to other VPCs or on-premises networks, not the public internet.
others.D: Private NAT gateways cannot provide internet access regardless of subnet.

e.tip: Public NAT gateway lives in a public subnet; private subnets route to it.

q: A company has an organization in AWS Organizations. The company runs Amazon EC2 instances across four AWS accounts in the root organizational unit (OU). There are three nonproduction accounts and one production account. The company wants to prohibit users from launching EC2 instances of a certain size in the nonproduction accounts. The company has created a service control policy (SCP) to deny access to launch instances that use the prohibited types. Which solutions to deploy the SCP will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Attach the SCP to the root OU for the organization.
o.B: Attach the SCP to the three nonproduction Organizations member accounts.
o.C: Attach the SCP to the Organizations management account.
o.D: Create an OU for the production account. Attach the SCP to the OU. Move the production member account into the new OU.
o.E: Create an OU for the required accounts. Attach the SCP to the OU. Move the nonproduction member accounts into the new OU.

e.why: An SCP attached directly to each of the three nonproduction member accounts restricts only those accounts. Alternatively, moving the nonproduction accounts into a new OU and attaching the SCP to that OU applies the restriction to them while leaving the production account unaffected.

others.A: Attaching to the root OU would also restrict the production account.
others.C: SCPs do not affect the management account, so this restricts nothing.
others.D: Attaching the SCP to a production OU restricts the wrong account.

e.tip: SCPs never restrict the management account; scope them with OUs or direct account attachment.

q: A company’s website hosted on Amazon EC2 instances processes classified data stored in Amazon S3. Due to security concerns, the company requires a private and secure connection between its EC2 resources and Amazon S3. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Set up S3 bucket policies to allow access from a VPC endpoint.
o.B: Set up an IAM policy to grant read-write access to the S3 bucket.
o.C: Set up a NAT gateway to access resources outside the private subnet.
o.D: Set up an access key ID and a secret access key to access the S3 bucket.

e.why: A VPC gateway endpoint for S3 keeps traffic between the EC2 instances and S3 on the AWS network without traversing the internet. A bucket policy with an aws:SourceVpce condition allows access only from that endpoint, securing the classified data.

others.B: An IAM policy grants permission but does not make the network path private.
others.C: A NAT gateway sends traffic to S3's public endpoints over the internet path.
others.D: Static access keys are a credential (and a poor practice on EC2), not a private connection.

e.tip: Private EC2-to-S3 = VPC endpoint + bucket policy restricting aws:SourceVpce.

q: An ecommerce company runs its application on AWS. The application uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster in Multi-AZ mode for the underlying database. During a recent promotional campaign, the application experienced heavy read load and write load. Users experienced timeout issues when they attempted to access the application. A solutions architect needs to make the application architecture more scalable and highly available. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST downtime?

o.A: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that has the Aurora cluster as a source. Create an AWS Lambda function to log the state change events of the Aurora cluster. Add the Lambda function as a target for the EventBridge rule. Add additional reader nodes to fail over to.
o.B: Modify the Aurora cluster and activate the zero-downtime restart (ZDR) feature. Use Database Activity Streams on the cluster to track the cluster status.
o.C: Add additional reader instances to the Aurora cluster. Create an Amazon RDS Proxy target group for the Aurora cluster.
o.D: Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache. Replicate data from the Aurora cluster to Redis by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with a write-around approach.

e.why: Adding Aurora reader instances scales out read capacity and provides additional failover targets, with no downtime to add them. RDS Proxy pools connections and reduces failover time by keeping client connections open, improving scalability and availability for the heavy load.

others.A: Logging state changes with EventBridge and Lambda provides monitoring, not additional capacity.
others.B: Zero-downtime restart relates to patching, and Database Activity Streams monitor activity; neither adds capacity.
others.D: Replicating Aurora to Redis with DMS is complex, not a standard caching pattern, and does not help write load.

e.tip: Aurora read scaling = more readers; connection storms and faster failover = RDS Proxy.

q: A company is designing a web application on AWS. The application will use a VPN connection between the company’s existing data centers and the company's VPCs. The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS service. The application must use private DNS records to communicate with the on-premises services from a VPC. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure manner?

o.A: Create a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint. Create a resolver rule. Associate the resolver rule with the VPC.
o.B: Create a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint. Create a resolver rule. Associate the resolver rule with the VPC.
o.C: Create a Route 53 private hosted zone. Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC.
o.D: Create a Route 53 public hosted zone. Create a record for each service to allow service communication

e.why: A Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint forwards DNS queries from the VPC to on-premises DNS servers over the VPN. A forwarding resolver rule for the on-premises domain, associated with the VPC, lets resources resolve private on-premises records without exposing them publicly.

others.B: An inbound endpoint lets on-premises systems resolve AWS-hosted names, the opposite direction.
others.C: A private hosted zone would require duplicating on-premises records in AWS rather than resolving them from the on-premises DNS.
others.D: A public hosted zone exposes internal service records on the internet, which is insecure.

e.tip: VPC -> on-prem DNS = outbound endpoint; on-prem -> VPC DNS = inbound endpoint.

q: A company is running a photo hosting service in the us-east-1 Region. The service enables users across multiple countries to upload and view photos. Some photos are heavily viewed for months, and others are viewed for less than a week. The application allows uploads of up to 20 MB for each photo. The service uses the photo metadata to determine which photos to display to each user. Which solution provides the appropriate user access MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Store the photos in Amazon DynamoDB. Turn on DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache frequently viewed items.
o.B: Store the photos in the Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Store the photo metadata and its S3 location in DynamoDB.
o.C: Store the photos in the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to move photos older than 30 days to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Use the object tags to keep track of metadata.
o.D: Store the photos in the Amazon S3 Glacier storage class. Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to move photos older than 30 days to the S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class. Store the photo metadata and its S3 location in Amazon OpenSearch Service.

e.why: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves each photo between access tiers based on its own access pattern, handling photos popular for months and those viewed for a week, with no retrieval fees. DynamoDB stores the metadata and S3 location for fast queries to decide which photos to display.

others.A: DynamoDB items are limited to 400 KB, so 20 MB photos cannot be stored, and it is costly for blobs.
others.C: A fixed 30-day transition does not fit photos that stay popular for months, and object tags are not queryable metadata storage.
others.D: Glacier classes require restores and are unsuitable for photos users view on demand.

e.tip: Unknown or varying access patterns = S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

q: A company runs a highly available web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The company uses Amazon CloudWatch metrics. As the traffic to the web application increases, some EC2 instances become overloaded with many outstanding requests. The CloudWatch metrics show that the number of requests processed and the time to receive the responses from some EC2 instances are both higher compared to other EC2 instances. The company does not want new requests to be forwarded to the EC2 instances that are already overloaded. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use the round robin routing algorithm based on the RequestCountPerTarget and ActiveConnectionCount CloudWatch metrics.
o.B: Use the least outstanding requests algorithm based on the RequestCountPerTarget and ActiveConnectionCount CloudWatch metrics.
o.C: Use the round robin routing algorithm based on the RequestCount and TargetResponseTime CloudWatch metrics.
o.D: Use the least outstanding requests algorithm based on the RequestCount and TargetResponseTime CloudWatch metrics.

e.why: The least outstanding requests (LOR) algorithm on an ALB target group routes each new request to the target with the fewest in-flight requests, so overloaded instances receive fewer new requests. RequestCountPerTarget and ActiveConnectionCount are the CloudWatch metrics that show per-target load to confirm the effect.
