others.A: Round robin ignores how busy each target is, so overloaded instances keep receiving requests.
others.C: Round robin does not account for outstanding requests on each target.
others.D: LOR is right, but RequestCount and TargetResponseTime are aggregate metrics that do not show per-target load as directly.

e.tip: Uneven request durations on ALB = least outstanding requests routing.

q: A company uses Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda to run multiple workloads in the company's AWS account. The company wants to fully make use of its Compute Savings Plans. The company wants to receive notification when coverage of the Compute Savings Plans drops. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Create a daily budget for the Savings Plans by using AWS Budgets. Configure the budget with a coverage threshold to send notifications to the appropriate email message recipients.
o.B: Create a Lambda function that runs a coverage report against the Savings Plans. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to email the report to the appropriate email message recipients.
o.C: Create an AWS Budgets report for the Savings Plans budget. Set the frequency to daily.
o.D: Create a Savings Plans alert subscription. Enable all notification options. Enter an email address to receive notifications.

e.why: AWS Budgets supports Savings Plans coverage budgets: you set a coverage target threshold and a daily period, and Budgets sends notifications when coverage falls below it. It is fully managed, so no code is required.

others.B: A custom Lambda report with SES requires building and maintaining code.
others.C: A Budgets report delivers periodic reports but does not alert when coverage drops below a threshold.
others.D: Savings Plans alert subscriptions notify about expirations and renewals of plans, not coverage drops.

e.tip: Coverage or utilization alerts for RIs/Savings Plans = AWS Budgets coverage/utilization budgets.

q: A company runs a real-time data ingestion solution on AWS. The solution consists of the most recent version of Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK). The solution is deployed in a VPC in private subnets across three Availability Zones. A solutions architect needs to redesign the data ingestion solution to be publicly available over the internet. The data in transit must also be encrypted. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Configure public subnets in the existing VPC. Deploy an MSK cluster in the public subnets. Update the MSK cluster security settings to enable mutual TLS authentication.
o.B: Create a new VPC that has public subnets. Deploy an MSK cluster in the public subnets. Update the MSK cluster security settings to enable mutual TLS authentication.
o.C: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that uses private subnets. Configure an ALB security group inbound rule to allow inbound traffic from the VPC CIDR block for HTTPS protocol.
o.D: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) that uses private subnets. Configure an NLB listener for HTTPS communication over the internet.

e.why: Amazon MSK supports public access only for clusters in public subnets with public access turned on, and it requires TLS encryption in transit with an authentication method such as mutual TLS (or SASL/SCRAM, IAM). Adding public subnets to the existing VPC and enabling mutual TLS is the most direct path.

others.B: Creating a new VPC adds work and network reconfiguration without benefit.
others.C: MSK uses the Kafka protocol, not HTTP, and an internal ALB restricted to the VPC CIDR is not public.
others.D: An NLB in private subnets is internal, and Kafka clients need broker-level addressing that a simple HTTPS listener does not provide.

e.tip: MSK public access requires public subnets, TLS in transit and an auth method enabled.

q: A company wants to migrate an on-premises legacy application to AWS. The application ingests customer order files from an on-premises enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. The application then uploads the files to an SFTP server. The application uses a scheduled job that checks for order files every hour. The company already has an AWS account that has connectivity to the on-premises network. The new application on AWS must support integration with the existing ERP system. The new application must be secure and resilient and must use the SFTP protocol to process orders from the ERP system immediately. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP internet-facing server in two Availability Zones. Use Amazon S3 storage. Create an AWS Lambda function to process order files. Use S3 Event Notifications to send s3:ObjectCreated:* events to the Lambda function.
o.B: Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP internet-facing server in one Availability Zone. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) storage. Create an AWS Lambda function to process order files. Use a Transfer Family managed workflow to invoke the Lambda function.
o.C: Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP internal server in two Availability Zones. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) storage. Create an AWS Step Functions state machine to process order files. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to invoke the state machine to periodically check Amazon EFS for order files.
o.D: Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP internal server in two Availability Zones. Use Amazon S3 storage. Create an AWS Lambda function to process order files. Use a Transfer Family managed workflow to invoke the Lambda function.

e.why: An internal Transfer Family SFTP endpoint in two AZs is reachable from on premises over the existing private connectivity, keeping it secure and resilient. Storing files in S3 and using a Transfer Family managed workflow to invoke Lambda processes each order file immediately on upload.

others.A: An internet-facing endpoint is unnecessary exposure when private connectivity exists, making it less secure.
others.B: A single AZ is not resilient, and the endpoint is unnecessarily internet facing.
others.C: Periodic scheduled polling does not process orders immediately.

e.tip: Transfer Family managed workflows trigger post-upload processing; internal endpoints for private access.

q: A company’s applications use Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark to process data on premises. The existing infrastructure is not scalable and is complex to manage. A solutions architect must design a scalable solution that reduces operational complexity. The solution must keep the data processing on premises. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN to access the on-premises Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) data and application. Use an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.
o.B: Use AWS DataSync to connect to the on-premises Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) cluster. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.
o.C: Migrate the Apache Hadoop application and the Apache Spark application to Amazon EMR clusters on AWS Outposts. Use the EMR clusters to process the data.
o.D: Use an AWS Snowball device to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.

e.why: AWS Outposts brings AWS infrastructure on premises, and Amazon EMR can run on Outposts. This keeps data processing in the data center while gaining managed, scalable Hadoop and Spark clusters with less operational complexity.

others.A: Running EMR in the Region moves the processing to AWS, violating the on-premises requirement.
others.B: DataSync copies data to AWS, so processing would happen in the cloud, not on premises.
others.D: Snowball migrates data to S3, again moving the processing to AWS.

e.tip: Must stay on premises but want AWS services = Outposts.

q: A company is migrating a large amount of data from on-premises storage to AWS. Windows, Mac, and Linux based Amazon EC2 instances in the same AWS Region will access the data by using SMB and NFS storage protocols. The company will access a portion of the data routinely. The company will access the remaining data infrequently. The company needs to design a solution to host the data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume that uses EFS Intelligent-Tiering. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to the EFS volume.
o.B: Create an Amazon FSx for ONTAP instance. Create an FSx for ONTAP file system with a root volume that uses the auto tiering policy. Migrate the data to the FSx for ONTAP volume.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket by using an AWS Storage Gateway Amazon S3 File Gateway.
o.D: Create an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system. Migrate the data to the new volume.

e.why: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP serves the same data over both SMB and NFS to Windows, macOS and Linux clients. Its auto tiering policy moves cold data automatically from SSD to the lower-cost capacity pool tier, fitting the mix of frequent and infrequent access with minimal management.

others.A: Amazon EFS supports NFS only, not SMB for Windows clients.
others.C: S3 File Gateway is designed for on-premises access, adding a gateway to manage for in-Region EC2 clients.
others.D: FSx for OpenZFS supports NFS but not SMB multi-protocol access.

e.tip: SMB + NFS together = FSx for NetApp ONTAP.

q: A manufacturing company runs its report generation application on AWS. The application generates each report in about 20 minutes. The application is built as a monolith that runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The application requires frequent updates to its tightly coupled modules. The application becomes complex to maintain as the company adds new features. Each time the company patches a software module, the application experiences downtime. Report generation must restart from the beginning after any interruptions. The company wants to redesign the application so that the application can be flexible, scalable, and gradually improved. The company wants to minimize application downtime. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Run the application on AWS Lambda as a single function with maximum provisioned concurrency.
o.B: Run the application on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances as microservices with a Spot Fleet default allocation strategy.
o.C: Run the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) as microservices with service auto scaling.
o.D: Run the application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk as a single application environment with an all-at-once deployment strategy.

e.why: Decomposing the monolith into microservices on Amazon ECS lets each module be updated, deployed and scaled independently with rolling deployments, minimizing downtime. Service auto scaling adjusts capacity, and long-running 20-minute report jobs are not limited the way Lambda would be.

others.A: Lambda's 15-minute maximum timeout cannot run 20-minute reports, and a single function keeps the monolith.
others.B: Spot interruptions would force report generation to restart, increasing disruption.
others.D: A single environment with all-at-once deployments causes downtime on every update.

e.tip: Lambda max timeout is 15 minutes; microservices on containers for gradual modernization.

q: A company wants to rearchitect a large-scale web application to a serverless microservices architecture. The application uses Amazon EC2 instances and is written in Python. The company selected one component of the web application to test as a microservice. The component supports hundreds of requests each second. The company wants to create and test the microservice on an AWS solution that supports Python. The solution must also scale automatically and require minimal infrastructure and minimal operational support. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use a Spot Fleet with auto scaling of EC2 instances that run the most recent Amazon Linux operating system.
o.B: Use an AWS Elastic Beanstalk web server environment that has high availability configured.
o.C: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Launch Auto Scaling groups of self-managed EC2 instances.
o.D: Use an AWS Lambda function that runs custom developed code.

e.why: AWS Lambda natively supports Python, scales automatically to handle hundreds of requests per second, and requires no servers to provision or manage. This makes it the serverless microservice option with minimal infrastructure and operational support.

others.A: A Spot Fleet of EC2 instances requires managing servers and handling Spot interruptions, and is not serverless.
others.B: Elastic Beanstalk still runs and manages EC2 instances under the hood, so it is not serverless.
others.C: EKS with self-managed EC2 nodes involves significant cluster and node management.

e.tip: Serverless microservice with minimal ops = Lambda (often behind API Gateway).

q: A company has an AWS Direct Connect connection from its on-premises location to an AWS account. The AWS account has 30 different VPCs in the same AWS Region. The VPCs use private virtual interfaces (VIFs). Each VPC has a CIDR block that does not overlap with other networks under the company's control. The company wants to centrally manage the networking architecture while still allowing each VPC to communicate with all other VPCs and on-premises networks. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

o.A: Create a transit gateway, and associate the Direct Connect connection with a new transit VIF. Turn on the transit gateway's route propagation feature.
o.B: Create a Direct Connect gateway. Recreate the private VIFs to use the new gateway. Associate each VPC by creating new virtual private gateways.
o.C: Create a transit VPConnect the Direct Connect connection to the transit VPCreate a peering connection between all other VPCs in the Region. Update the route tables.
o.D: Create AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections from on premises to each VPC. Ensure that both VPN tunnels are UP for each connection. Turn on the route propagation feature.

e.why: A transit gateway associated with a Direct Connect gateway over a transit VIF gives on premises a single connection to all 30 VPCs. With VPC attachments and route propagation, every VPC can reach every other VPC and on premises through one centrally managed hub.

others.B: A Direct Connect gateway with virtual private gateways connects VPCs to on premises but does not enable VPC-to-VPC traffic.
others.C: A full mesh of peering connections among 30 VPCs is a lot of connections and route table management.
others.D: Thirty separate VPN connections add overhead, do not connect VPCs to each other, and ignore Direct Connect.

e.tip: DX + many VPCs needing full connectivity = transit VIF -> DX gateway -> Transit Gateway.

q: A company has applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances connect to Amazon RDS databases by using an IAM role that has associated policies. The company wants to use AWS Systems Manager to patch the EC2 instances without disrupting the running applications. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a new IAM role. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the new IAM role. Attach the new IAM role to the EC2 instances and the existing IAM role.
o.B: Create an IAM user. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the IAM user. Configure Systems Manager to use the IAM user to manage the EC2 instances.
o.C: Enable Default Host Configuration Management in Systems Manager to manage the EC2 instances.
o.D: Remove the existing policies from the existing IAM role. Add the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the existing IAM role.

e.why: Default Host Management Configuration lets Systems Manager manage all EC2 instances in the Region automatically using an account-level role, without changing the instances' existing IAM instance profiles. The instances can then be patched while the RDS access role stays intact, so applications are not disrupted.

others.A: An EC2 instance can have only one instance profile (one role), so you cannot attach a second role alongside the existing one.
others.B: Systems Manager does not use IAM users to manage EC2 instances; the SSM Agent needs role credentials.
others.D: Removing the existing policies would break the applications' access to RDS.

e.tip: SSM without touching instance roles = Default Host Management Configuration (needs IMDSv2 and recent agent); otherwise add AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore to the existing role.

q: A company runs container applications by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) and the Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler. The workload is not consistent throughout the day. A solutions architect notices that the number of nodes does not automatically scale out when the existing nodes have reached maximum capacity in the cluster, which causes performance issues. Which solution will resolve this issue with the LEAST administrative overhead?

o.A: Scale out the nodes by tracking the memory usage.
o.B: Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to manage the number of nodes in the cluster.
o.C: Use an AWS Lambda function to resize the EKS cluster automatically.
o.D: Use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to distribute the workload.

e.why: The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler scales pods but not nodes. The Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler watches for pods that cannot be scheduled due to insufficient capacity and adjusts the node group's Auto Scaling group size automatically, with little administration.

others.A: Scaling on node memory usage is a manual or custom metric approach that does not react to unschedulable pods.
others.C: A custom Lambda function to resize the cluster adds code and maintenance.
others.D: An Auto Scaling group alone is not aware of pending Kubernetes pods; it needs Cluster Autoscaler (or Karpenter) to drive it.

e.tip: HPA scales pods; Cluster Autoscaler or Karpenter scales nodes.

q: A company maintains about 300 TB in Amazon S3 Standard storage month after month. The S3 objects are each typically around 50 GB in size and are frequently replaced with multipart uploads by their global application. The number and size of S3 objects remain constant, but the company's S3 storage costs are increasing each month. How should a solutions architect reduce costs in this situation?

o.A: Switch from multipart uploads to Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.
o.B: Enable an S3 Lifecycle policy that deletes incomplete multipart uploads.
o.C: Configure S3 inventory to prevent objects from being archived too quickly.
o.D: Configure Amazon CloudFront to reduce the number of objects stored in Amazon S3.

e.why: When multipart uploads are interrupted or never completed, the uploaded parts remain stored and billed but are invisible as objects. A Lifecycle rule with AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload deletes those orphaned parts after a set number of days, stopping the growing storage cost.

others.A: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads over long distances but costs extra and does not remove orphaned parts.
others.C: S3 Inventory reports on objects; it does not prevent archiving or remove storage.
others.D: CloudFront caches content for delivery; it does not reduce the objects stored in S3.

e.tip: Rising S3 cost with constant object counts = incomplete multipart uploads; add an abort lifecycle rule.

q: A company has deployed a multiplayer game for mobile devices. The game requires live location tracking of players based on latitude and longitude. The data store for the game must support rapid updates and retrieval of locations. The game uses an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with read replicas to store the location data. During peak usage periods, the database is unable to maintain the performance that is needed for reading and writing updates. The game's user base is increasing rapidly. What should a solutions architect do to improve the performance of the data tier?

o.A: Take a snapshot of the existing DB instance. Restore the snapshot with Multi-AZ enabled.
o.B: Migrate from Amazon RDS to Amazon OpenSearch Service with OpenSearch Dashboards.
o.C: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the existing DB instance. Modify the game to use DAX.
o.D: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the existing DB instance. Modify the game to use Redis.

e.why: ElastiCache for Redis provides sub-millisecond reads and writes in memory and includes native geospatial commands (GEOADD, GEOSEARCH) suited to live latitude and longitude tracking. Placing it in front of PostgreSQL offloads the high-frequency location reads and writes as the user base grows.

others.A: Multi-AZ adds high availability, not read or write performance, and the standby cannot serve traffic.
others.B: OpenSearch Service is built for search and analytics, not rapid transactional updates as the primary store.
others.C: DAX works only with DynamoDB and cannot cache an RDS for PostgreSQL database.

e.tip: DAX is DynamoDB-only; Redis has built-in geospatial support.

q: A company stores critical data in Amazon DynamoDB tables in the company's AWS account. An IT administrator accidentally deleted a DynamoDB table. The deletion caused a significant loss of data and disrupted the company's operations. The company wants to prevent this type of disruption in the future. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Configure a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for delete actions. Create an AWS Lambda function to automatically restore deleted DynamoDB tables.
o.B: Create a backup and restore plan for the DynamoDB tables. Recover the DynamoDB tables manually.
o.C: Configure deletion protection on the DynamoDB tables.
o.D: Enable point-in-time recovery on the DynamoDB tables.

e.why: DynamoDB deletion protection prevents a table from being deleted by anyone until the setting is explicitly turned off. It is a simple table setting that directly prevents the disruption, with the least operational overhead.

others.A: A CloudTrail, EventBridge and Lambda restore pipeline is complex, and a deleted table cannot be restored without backups.
others.B: Backups help recovery but still cause disruption and require manual restore work.
others.D: Point-in-time recovery aids recovery after the fact but does not prevent the deletion or the resulting disruption.

e.tip: Prevent accidental deletion = deletion protection; recover = PITR or backups.

q: A company has an on-premises data center that is running out of storage capacity. The company wants to migrate its storage infrastructure to AWS while minimizing bandwidth costs. The solution must allow for immediate retrieval of data at no additional cost. How can these requirements be met?

o.A: Deploy Amazon S3 Glacier Vault and enable expedited retrieval. Enable provisioned retrieval capacity for the workload.
o.B: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway using cached volumes. Use Storage Gateway to store data in Amazon S3 while retaining copies of frequently accessed data subsets locally.
o.C: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway using stored volumes to store data locally. Use Storage Gateway to asynchronously back up point-in-time snapshots of the data to Amazon S3.
o.D: Deploy AWS Direct Connect to connect with the on-premises data center. Configure AWS Storage Gateway to store data locally. Use Storage Gateway to asynchronously back up point-in-time snapshots of the data to Amazon S3.

e.why: Storage Gateway cached volumes keep the primary data in Amazon S3, freeing on-premises capacity, while caching frequently accessed data locally for low-latency retrieval. Local cache hits need no transfer, minimizing bandwidth costs, and there are no retrieval fees for data in S3.

others.A: Glacier expedited retrieval and provisioned capacity cost extra, violating the no-additional-cost retrieval requirement.
others.C: Stored volumes keep the full dataset on premises, so they do not relieve the storage capacity shortage.
others.D: Direct Connect adds cost, and stored volumes still keep all data on premises.

e.tip: Cached volumes = primary in AWS, hot data local; stored volumes = primary local, async backup to AWS.

q: A company runs a three-tier web application in a VPC across multiple Availability Zones. Amazon EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group for the application tier. The company needs to make an automated scaling plan that will analyze each resource's daily and weekly historical workload trends. The configuration must scale resources appropriately according to both the forecast and live changes in utilization. Which scaling strategy should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Implement dynamic scaling with step scaling based on average CPU utilization from the EC2 instances.
o.B: Enable predictive scaling to forecast and scale. Configure dynamic scaling with target tracking
o.C: Create an automated scheduled scaling action based on the traffic patterns of the web application.
o.D: Set up a simple scaling policy. Increase the cooldown period based on the EC2 instance startup time.

e.why: Predictive scaling analyzes historical daily and weekly load to forecast capacity and launch instances ahead of demand. Combining it with dynamic target tracking scaling handles real-time deviations from the forecast, meeting both requirements.

others.A: Step scaling only reacts to live CPU changes and does not use historical forecasting.
others.C: Scheduled scaling uses fixed times you define, not automated analysis of trends or reaction to live changes.
others.D: Simple scaling with cooldowns is reactive, slow, and uses no forecast.

e.tip: Forecast + live adjustments = predictive scaling plus target tracking.

q: A package delivery company has an application that uses Amazon EC2 instances and an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. As the application becomes more popular, EC2 instance usage increases only slightly. DB cluster usage increases at a much faster rate. The company adds a read replica, which reduces the DB cluster usage for a short period of time. However, the load continues to increase. The operations that cause the increase in DB cluster usage are all repeated read statements that are related to delivery details. The company needs to alleviate the effect of repeated reads on the DB cluster. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Implement an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster between the application and the DB cluster.
o.B: Add an additional read replica to the DB cluster.
o.C: Configure Aurora Auto Scaling for the Aurora read replicas.
o.D: Modify the DB cluster to have multiple writer instances.

e.why: The load comes from repeated identical reads, which ElastiCache for Redis can serve from memory with sub-millisecond latency instead of hitting Aurora. Caching these results removes most of the read load at lower cost than continually adding replicas.

others.B: Another read replica only adds capacity temporarily, as already observed, and costs more as load grows.
others.C: Aurora Auto Scaling adds replicas as load grows, increasing cost without addressing the repetitive reads.
others.D: Multiple writers do not address a read-heavy workload, and Aurora MySQL multi-master is no longer supported for new clusters.

e.tip: Repeated identical reads = cache (ElastiCache); not more replicas.

q: A company has an application that uses an Amazon DynamoDB table for storage. A solutions architect discovers that many requests to the table are not returning the latest data. The company's users have not reported any other issues with database performance. Latency is in an acceptable range. Which design change should the solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Add read replicas to the table.
o.B: Use a global secondary index (GSI).
o.C: Request strongly consistent reads for the table.
o.D: Request eventually consistent reads for the table.

e.why: DynamoDB reads are eventually consistent by default and may not reflect a recent write. Setting ConsistentRead to true requests strongly consistent reads that always return the most recent data, at double the read capacity cost, which is acceptable since latency is fine.

others.A: DynamoDB has no read replicas within a Region; global table replicas are eventually consistent.
others.B: Global secondary indexes support only eventually consistent reads.
others.D: Eventually consistent reads are the default and cause the stale data problem.

e.tip: Stale DynamoDB reads = use strongly consistent reads (not supported on GSIs or across global table Regions).

q: A company has deployed its application on Amazon EC2 instances with an Amazon RDS database. The company used the principle of least privilege to configure the database access credentials. The company's security team wants to protect the application and the database from SQL injection and other web-based attacks. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use security groups and network ACLs to secure the database and application servers.
o.B: Use AWS WAF to protect the application. Use RDS parameter groups to configure the security settings.
o.C: Use AWS Network Firewall to protect the application and the database.
o.D: Use different database accounts in the application code for different functions. Avoid granting excessive privileges to the database users.

e.why: AWS WAF provides managed rule groups that block SQL injection, cross-site scripting and other web attacks before they reach the application. RDS parameter groups allow database security settings, such as enforcing SSL connections, to be configured centrally without managing servers.

others.A: Security groups and NACLs filter by IP, port and protocol and cannot inspect requests for SQL injection.
others.C: Network Firewall can do some inspection but is more complex to deploy and manage than WAF for web attacks.
others.D: Separate database accounts limit privileges but do not block SQL injection or web exploits.

e.tip: SQL injection / XSS protection = AWS WAF (layer 7).

q: An ecommerce company runs applications in AWS accounts that are part of an organization in AWS Organizations. The applications run on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL databases across all the accounts. The company needs to prevent malicious activity and must identify abnormal failed and incomplete login attempts to the databases. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.A: Attach service control policies (SCPs) to the root of the organization to identity the failed login attempts.
o.B: Enable the Amazon RDS Protection feature in Amazon GuardDuty for the member accounts of the organization.
o.C: Publish the Aurora general logs to a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Export the log data to a central Amazon S3 bucket.
o.D: Publish all the Aurora PostgreSQL database events in AWS CloudTrail to a central Amazon S3 bucket.

e.why: GuardDuty RDS Protection analyzes Aurora login activity and detects anomalous behaviour such as unusual failed or incomplete login attempts. It can be enabled across member accounts from a delegated administrator in Organizations, with no agents or log pipelines to manage.

others.A: SCPs restrict permissions; they do not detect or report login attempts.
others.C: Exporting general logs to S3 requires building custom analysis to detect anomalies.
others.D: CloudTrail records AWS API calls, not database login attempts.

e.tip: Anomalous Aurora logins = GuardDuty RDS Protection.

q: A company has an AWS Direct Connect connection from its corporate data center to its VPC in the us-east-1 Region. The company recently acquired a corporation that has several VPCs and a Direct Connect connection between its on-premises data center and the eu-west-2 Region. The CIDR blocks for the VPCs of the company and the corporation do not overlap. The company requires connectivity between two Regions and the data centers. The company needs a solution that is scalable while reducing operational overhead. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Set up inter-Region VPC peering between the VPC in us-east-1 and the VPCs in eu-west-2.
o.B: Create private virtual interfaces from the Direct Connect connection in us-east-1 to the VPCs in eu-west-2.
o.C: Establish VPN appliances in a fully meshed VPN network hosted by Amazon EC2. Use AWS VPN CloudHub to send and receive data between the data centers and each VPC.
o.D: Connect the existing Direct Connect connection to a Direct Connect gateway. Route traffic from the virtual private gateways of the VPCs in each Region to the Direct Connect gateway.

e.why: A Direct Connect gateway is a global resource that connects virtual private gateways in multiple Regions to Direct Connect connections. Attaching both companies' DX connections and VPC virtual private gateways to the DX gateway gives scalable connectivity between the data centers and the VPCs in both Regions.

others.A: VPC peering does not provide connectivity to the data centers and scales poorly.
others.B: A private VIF connects to a single virtual private gateway in one Region unless a Direct Connect gateway is used.
others.C: Self-managed VPN appliances on EC2 add significant operational overhead.

e.tip: Direct Connect to VPCs in multiple Regions = Direct Connect gateway.

q: A company is developing a mobile game that streams score updates to a backend processor and then posts results on a leaderboard. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that can handle large traffic spikes, process the mobile game updates in order of receipt, and store the processed updates in a highly available database. The company also wants to minimize the management overhead required to maintain the solution. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Push score updates to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Process the updates in Kinesis Data Streams with AWS Lambda. Store the processed updates in Amazon DynamoDB.
o.B: Push score updates to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Process the updates with a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances set up for Auto Scaling. Store the processed updates in Amazon Redshift.
o.C: Push score updates to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the SNS topic to process the updates. Store the processed updates in a SQL database running on Amazon EC2.
o.D: Push score updates to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances with Auto Scaling to process the updates in the SQS queue. Store the processed updates in an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.

e.why: Kinesis Data Streams absorbs large traffic spikes and preserves ordering of records within each shard. Lambda processes the stream serverlessly, and DynamoDB stores the processed updates in a highly available, fully managed database, minimizing management.

others.B: EC2 consumers require server management, and Redshift is a data warehouse, not a low-latency leaderboard store.
others.C: SNS does not guarantee ordering for standard topics, and a SQL database on EC2 requires management.
others.D: A standard SQS queue does not guarantee ordering, and EC2 workers add management overhead.

e.tip: Ordered streaming ingestion with spikes = Kinesis Data Streams (per-shard order).

q: A company has multiple AWS accounts with applications deployed in the us-west-2 Region. Application logs are stored within Amazon S3 buckets in each account. The company wants to build a centralized log analysis solution that uses a single S3 bucket. Logs must not leave us-west-2, and the company wants to incur minimal operational overhead. Which solution meets these requirements and is MOST cost-effective?

o.A: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy that copies the objects from one of the application S3 buckets to the centralized S3 bucket.
o.B: Use S3 Same-Region Replication to replicate logs from the S3 buckets to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.
o.C: Write a script that uses the PutObject API operation every day to copy the entire contents of the buckets to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.
o.D: Write AWS Lambda functions in these accounts that are triggered every time logs are delivered to the S3 buckets (s3:ObjectCreated:* event). Copy the logs to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.

e.why: S3 Same-Region Replication automatically copies new log objects from each account's bucket to a central bucket in us-west-2, keeping data in the Region. It is fully managed, supports cross-account replication, and requires no custom code.

others.A: S3 Lifecycle policies transition or expire objects; they cannot copy objects to another bucket.
others.C: A daily script copying entire buckets is wasteful, costly in requests, and adds operational overhead.
others.D: Lambda functions in every account add code to maintain and per-invocation cost.

e.tip: Copy objects automatically within a Region = SRR; across Regions = CRR.

q: A company has an application that delivers on-demand training videos to students around the world. The application also allows authorized content developers to upload videos. The data is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-2 Region. The company has created an S3 bucket in the eu-west-2 Region and an S3 bucket in the ap-southeast-1 Region. The company wants to replicate the data to the new S3 buckets. The company needs to minimize latency for developers who upload videos and students who stream videos near eu-west-2 and ap-southeast-1. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the application? (Choose two.)

o.A: Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the eu-west-2 S3 bucket. Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the ap-southeast-1 S3 bucket.
o.B: Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the eu-west-2 S3 bucket. Configure one-way replication from the eu-west-2 S3 bucket to the ap-southeast-1 S3 bucket.
o.C: Configure two-way (bidirectional) replication among the S3 buckets that are in all three Regions.
o.D: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point. Modify the application to use the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Multi-Region Access Point for video streaming. Do not modify the application for video uploads.
o.E: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point. Modify the application to use the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Multi-Region Access Point for video streaming and uploads.

e.why: An S3 Multi-Region Access Point gives one global endpoint that routes both uploads and downloads to the closest bucket over the AWS network, so using its ARN for streaming and uploads minimizes latency in each Region. Because uploads can land in any of the three buckets, two-way (bidirectional) replication keeps all buckets in sync.

others.A: One-way replication from us-east-2 cannot propagate uploads that land in eu-west-2 or ap-southeast-1 buckets.
others.B: Chained one-way replication does not sync uploads made to the ap-southeast-1 or eu-west-2 buckets back to the others.
others.D: Leaving uploads on the us-east-2 bucket keeps upload latency high for developers near the other Regions.

e.tip: Multi-Region Access Point for active-active reads and writes needs bidirectional replication.

q: A company has a new mobile app. Anywhere in the world, users can see local news on topics they choose. Users also can post photos and videos from inside the app. Users access content often in the first minutes after the content is posted. New content quickly replaces older content, and then the older content disappears. The local nature of the news means that users consume 90% of the content within the AWS Region where it is uploaded. Which solution will optimize the user experience by providing the LOWEST latency for content uploads?

o.A: Upload and store content in Amazon S3. Use Amazon CloudFront for the uploads.
o.B: Upload and store content in Amazon S3. Use S3 Transfer Acceleration for the uploads.
o.C: Upload content to Amazon EC2 instances in the Region that is closest to the user. Copy the data to Amazon S3.
o.D: Upload and store content in Amazon S3 in the Region that is closest to the user. Use multiple distributions of Amazon CloudFront.

e.why: S3 Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through the nearest CloudFront edge location and then over the optimized AWS backbone to the bucket, reducing upload latency for users far from the bucket. Content is stored in S3 in the Region where it is consumed, which suits the local nature of the news.

others.A: CloudFront is optimized for content delivery; using it for uploads (PUT/POST) is possible but not the purpose-built way to accelerate S3 uploads.
others.C: Uploading to EC2 and then copying to S3 adds servers, latency and operational burden.
others.D: Multiple CloudFront distributions add complexity and improve downloads rather than upload latency.

e.tip: Faster long-distance uploads to S3 = Transfer Acceleration.

q: A company is building a new application that uses serverless architecture. The architecture will consist of an Amazon API Gateway REST API and AWS Lambda functions to manage incoming requests. The company wants to add a service that can send messages received from the API Gateway REST API to multiple target Lambda functions for processing. The service must offer message filtering that gives the target Lambda functions the ability to receive only the messages the functions need. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues to the SNS topic. Configure the target Lambda functions to poll the different SQS queues.
o.B: Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to Amazon EventBridge. Configure EventBridge to invoke the target Lambda functions.
o.C: Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK). Configure Amazon MSK to publish the messages to the target Lambda functions.
o.D: Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Configure the target Lambda functions to poll the different SQS queues.

e.why: An SNS topic fans out each message to multiple subscriber SQS queues, and SNS subscription filter policies ensure each queue, and therefore each target Lambda function, receives only the messages it needs. SQS adds buffering and retries, and Lambda polls the queues through managed event source mappings.

others.B: EventBridge with rules can also filter and route to Lambda, but this bank's key prefers the SNS fan-out with filtering pattern; in practice EventBridge is also a reasonable choice.
others.C: MSK requires cluster management and does not provide simple per-consumer message filtering.
others.D: Sending to multiple SQS queues directly from API Gateway requires separate integrations and has no built-in filtering.

e.tip: Fan-out with per-subscriber filtering = SNS filter policies (often SNS -> SQS -> Lambda).

q: A company migrated millions of archival files to Amazon S3. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that will encrypt all the archival data by using a customer-provided key. The solution must encrypt existing unencrypted objects and future objects. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering an Amazon S3 Inventory report. Configure an S3 Batch Operations job to encrypt the objects from the list with a server-side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C). Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C).
o.B: Use S3 Storage Lens metrics to identify unencrypted S3 buckets. Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
o.C: Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering the AWS usage report for Amazon S3. Configure an AWS Batch job to encrypt the objects from the list with a server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
o.D: Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering the AWS usage report for Amazon S3. Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C).

e.why: An S3 Inventory report can list objects with their encryption status so unencrypted objects can be identified. S3 Batch Operations can then copy each object in place with new encryption settings, and default encryption is configured so future objects are also encrypted.

others.B: Storage Lens gives aggregate metrics, not per-object lists, and SSE-KMS does not use a customer-provided key.
others.C: The usage report does not list objects, AWS Batch is not the S3 Batch Operations service, and SSE-KMS is not a customer-provided key.
others.D: The usage report cannot identify unencrypted objects and this does nothing to encrypt existing objects.

e.tip: Find unencrypted objects = S3 Inventory; re-encrypt at scale = S3 Batch Operations copy.
e.flag: S3 default bucket encryption only supports SSE-S3, SSE-KMS or DSSE-KMS, not SSE-C, and S3 now disables SSE-C on new buckets by default, so A cannot work exactly as written; it is still the closest option, but in practice a customer managed KMS key (or imported key material) with SSE-KMS would be used.

q: The DNS provider that hosts a company's domain name records is experiencing outages that cause service disruption for a website running on AWS. The company needs to migrate to a more resilient managed DNS service and wants the service to run on AWS. What should a solutions architect do to rapidly migrate the DNS hosting service?

o.A: Create an Amazon Route 53 public hosted zone for the domain name. Import the zone file containing the domain records hosted by the previous provider.
o.B: Create an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone for the domain name. Import the zone file containing the domain records hosted by the previous provider.
o.C: Create a Simple AD directory in AWS. Enable zone transfer between the DNS provider and AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for the domain records.
o.D: Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the VPC. Specify the IP addresses that the provider's DNS will forward DNS queries to. Configure the provider's DNS to forward DNS queries for the domain to the IP addresses that are specified in the inbound endpoint.

e.why: Route 53 public hosted zones provide highly available, managed authoritative DNS for internet domains on AWS. Importing the existing zone file into a new public hosted zone and then updating the registrar's name servers migrates the DNS records rapidly.

others.B: A private hosted zone answers only queries from associated VPCs, so the public website would not resolve on the internet.
others.C: Simple AD and Directory Service provide directory DNS for internal domains, not public authoritative DNS hosting.
others.D: A Resolver inbound endpoint answers queries from on-premises networks into a VPC; it still depends on the failing provider.

e.tip: Public website DNS on AWS = Route 53 public hosted zone; import a zone file to migrate quickly.

q: A company is building an application on AWS that connects to an Amazon RDS database. The company wants to manage the application configuration and to securely store and retrieve credentials for the database and other services. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

o.A: Use AWS AppConfig to store and manage the application configuration. Use AWS Secrets Manager to store and retrieve the credentials.
o.B: Use AWS Lambda to store and manage the application configuration. Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to store and retrieve the credentials.
o.C: Use an encrypted application configuration file. Store the file in Amazon S3 for the application configuration. Create another S3 file to store and retrieve the credentials.
o.D: Use AWS AppConfig to store and manage the application configuration. Use Amazon RDS to store and retrieve the credentials.

e.why: AWS AppConfig is a managed service for storing, validating and deploying application configuration. AWS Secrets Manager securely stores credentials for RDS and other services, supports retrieval via API and offers built-in rotation, giving the least administrative overhead.

others.B: Lambda is a compute service, not a configuration store; Parameter Store can hold secrets but lacks built-in rotation.
others.C: Self-managed encrypted files in S3 require custom handling for access, encryption and rotation.
others.D: Amazon RDS is not a service for storing and retrieving application or service credentials.

e.tip: App config = AppConfig; credentials with rotation = Secrets Manager.

q: To meet security requirements, a company needs to encrypt all of its application data in transit while communicating with an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. A recent security audit revealed that encryption at rest is enabled using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS), but data in transit is not enabled. What should a solutions architect do to satisfy the security requirements?

o.A: Enable IAM database authentication on the database.
o.B: Provide self-signed certificates. Use the certificates in all connections to the RDS instance.
o.C: Take a snapshot of the RDS instance. Restore the snapshot to a new instance with encryption enabled.
o.D: Download AWS-provided root certificates. Provide the certificates in all connections to the RDS instance.

e.why: RDS for MySQL supports TLS connections using certificates signed by the RDS certificate authority. Downloading the AWS-provided root (CA bundle) certificates and using them in all client connections, optionally enforcing require_secure_transport, encrypts data in transit.

others.A: IAM database authentication controls how users authenticate; it does not by itself enforce encryption of all application traffic.
others.B: RDS does not let you install self-signed server certificates; clients must trust the RDS CA certificates.
others.C: Restoring a snapshot with encryption enabled addresses encryption at rest, which is already enabled.

e.tip: RDS in-transit encryption = use RDS CA certificates for TLS; at-rest encryption must be set at creation.

q: A company is designing a new web service that will run on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. However, many of the web service clients can only reach IP addresses authorized on their firewalls. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet the clients’ needs?

o.A: A Network Load Balancer with an associated Elastic IP address.
o.B: An Application Load Balancer with an associated Elastic IP address.
o.C: An A record in an Amazon Route 53 hosted zone pointing to an Elastic IP address.
o.D: An EC2 instance with a public IP address running as a proxy in front of the load balancer.

e.why: A Network Load Balancer can be assigned one Elastic IP address per Availability Zone subnet, giving clients fixed IP addresses to allow on their firewalls. The NLB then distributes traffic to the EC2 instances.

others.B: Application Load Balancers do not support Elastic IP addresses; their IPs change.
others.C: An A record pointing to an Elastic IP would bypass the load balancer, since you cannot attach that EIP to an ALB.
others.D: A single proxy instance is a single point of failure and adds management overhead.

e.tip: Static IPs for a load balancer = NLB with Elastic IPs (or Global Accelerator in front of an ALB).

q: A company has established a new AWS account. The account is newly provisioned and no changes have been made to the default settings. The company is concerned about the security of the AWS account root user. What should be done to secure the root user?

o.A: Create IAM users for daily administrative tasks. Disable the root user.
o.B: Create IAM users for daily administrative tasks. Enable multi-factor authentication on the root user.
o.C: Generate an access key for the root user. Use the access key for daily administration tasks instead of the AWS Management Console.
o.D: Provide the root user credentials to the most senior solutions architect. Have the solutions architect use the root user for daily administration tasks.

e.why: Best practice is to protect the root user with MFA and avoid using it for daily tasks. Creating IAM users or roles for administrative work limits root use to the few tasks that require it.

others.A: The root user of a standalone account cannot simply be disabled; it is needed for certain account-level tasks.
others.C: Root access keys should never be created; they grant unrestricted access and are a major security risk.
others.D: Sharing root credentials for daily administration violates least privilege and best practice.

e.tip: Root user: enable MFA, no access keys, use only for root-only tasks.

q: A company is deploying an application that processes streaming data in near-real time. The company plans to use Amazon EC2 instances for the workload. The network architecture must be configurable to provide the lowest possible latency between nodes. Which combination of network solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Enable and configure enhanced networking on each EC2 instance.
o.B: Group the EC2 instances in separate accounts.
o.C: Run the EC2 instances in a cluster placement group.
o.D: Attach multiple elastic network interfaces to each EC2 instance.
o.E: Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) optimized instance types.

e.why: Enhanced networking (ENA) provides higher bandwidth, higher packets per second and lower latency between instances. A cluster placement group places instances close together in one AZ on a low-latency, high-throughput network segment, minimizing node-to-node latency.

others.B: Separating instances into different accounts adds no network performance benefit.
others.D: Multiple ENIs provide more interfaces or subnets, not lower latency between nodes.
others.E: EBS-optimized instances improve storage I/O throughput, not inter-node network latency.

e.tip: Lowest inter-node latency = cluster placement group + enhanced networking (ENA/EFA).

q: A financial services company wants to shut down two data centers and migrate more than 100 TB of data to AWS. The data has an intricate directory structure with millions of small files stored in deep hierarchies of subfolders. Most of the data is unstructured, and the company’s file storage consists of SMB-based storage types from multiple vendors. The company does not want to change its applications to access the data after migration. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Direct Connect to migrate the data to Amazon S3.
o.B: Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon FSx for Lustre.
o.C: Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
o.D: Use AWS Direct Connect to migrate the data on-premises file storage to an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway.

e.why: FSx for Windows File Server provides native SMB file shares with the same directory semantics, so applications keep working without changes. AWS DataSync efficiently migrates millions of small files and deep directory trees from SMB sources, preserving metadata, with little operational effort.

others.A: Direct Connect is a network link, not a migration tool, and S3 is object storage, which would require application changes.
others.B: FSx for Lustre does not provide SMB access, so applications would need to change.
others.D: A volume gateway exposes iSCSI block volumes, not SMB file shares.

e.tip: SMB workloads with no app changes = FSx for Windows File Server; migrate with DataSync.

q: A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage AWS accounts that contain applications. The company sets up a dedicated monitoring member account in the organization. The company wants to query and visualize observability data across the accounts by using Amazon CloudWatch. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Enable CloudWatch cross-account observability for the monitoring account. Deploy an AWS CloudFormation template provided by the monitoring account in each AWS account to share the data with the monitoring account.
o.B: Set up service control policies (SCPs) to provide access to CloudWatch in the monitoring account under the Organizations root organizational unit (OU).
o.C: Configure a new IAM user in the monitoring account. In each AWS account, configure an IAM policy to have access to query and visualize the CloudWatch data in the account. Attach the new IAM policy to the new IAM user.
o.D: Create a new IAM user in the monitoring account. Create cross-account IAM policies in each AWS account. Attach the IAM policies to the new IAM user.

e.why: CloudWatch cross-account observability lets a monitoring account act as a sink that can view and query metrics, logs and traces from linked source accounts. The monitoring account provides a CloudFormation template (or Organizations-wide setup) that each source account deploys to link and share its data.

others.B: SCPs only limit permissions; they cannot grant access or share CloudWatch data.
others.C: Policies in other accounts cannot be attached to an IAM user in the monitoring account, and this does not enable a unified CloudWatch view.
others.D: IAM policies are account-scoped and cannot be attached to users in another account; this is not how CloudWatch cross-account works.

e.tip: Central monitoring account across an organization = CloudWatch cross-account observability (OAM sinks and links).

q: A company’s website is used to sell products to the public. The site runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). There is also an Amazon CloudFront distribution, and AWS WAF is being used to protect against SQL injection attacks. The ALB is the origin for the CloudFront distribution. A recent review of security logs revealed an external malicious IP that needs to be blocked from accessing the website. What should a solutions architect do to protect the application?

o.A: Modify the network ACL on the CloudFront distribution to add a deny rule for the malicious IP address.
o.B: Modify the configuration of AWS WAF to add an IP match condition to block the malicious IP address.
o.C: Modify the network ACL for the EC2 instances in the target groups behind the ALB to deny the malicious IP address.
o.D: Modify the security groups for the EC2 instances in the target groups behind the ALB to deny the malicious IP address.

e.why: AWS WAF is already protecting the CloudFront distribution, so adding an IP set match rule that blocks the malicious IP stops it at the edge. Because CloudFront is in front, the ALB and instances see CloudFront IPs, so blocking must happen in WAF.

others.A: CloudFront distributions do not have network ACLs.
others.C: Behind CloudFront and the ALB, the instances receive traffic from the ALB, not the client IP, so a NACL rule would not match.
others.D: Security groups only support allow rules and cannot deny specific IPs.

e.tip: Block a client IP behind CloudFront = WAF IP set rule; security groups cannot deny.

q: A company sets up an organization in AWS Organizations that contains 10 AWS accounts. A solutions architect must design a solution to provide access to the accounts for several thousand employees. The company has an existing identity provider (IdP). The company wants to use the existing IdP for authentication to AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create IAM users for the employees in the required AWS accounts. Connect IAM users to the existing IdP. Configure federated authentication for the IAM users.
o.B: Set up AWS account root users with user email addresses and passwords that are synchronized from the existing IdP.
o.C: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Connect IAM Identity Center to the existing IdP. Provision users and groups from the existing IdP.
o.D: Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share access to the AWS accounts with the users in the existing IdP.

e.why: IAM Identity Center integrates with an external IdP via SAML 2.0 and SCIM to provision users and groups automatically. Permission sets then grant thousands of employees access across all 10 accounts in the organization, using the existing IdP for authentication.

others.A: Creating thousands of IAM users per account is unmanageable and defeats federation.
others.B: Root users must never be shared or used for employee access.
others.D: AWS RAM shares resources such as subnets or transit gateways, not account access for users.

e.tip: Workforce SSO across Organizations accounts with an existing IdP = IAM Identity Center.

q: A solutions architect is designing an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) authorization model for a company's AWS account. The company has designated five specific employees to have full access to AWS services and resources in the AWS account. The solutions architect has created an IAM user for each of the five designated employees and has created an IAM user group. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Attach the AdministratorAccess resource-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
o.B: Attach the SystemAdministrator identity-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
o.C: Attach the AdministratorAccess identity-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
o.D: Attach the SystemAdministrator resource-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.

e.why: AdministratorAccess is an AWS managed identity-based policy that grants full access to all AWS services and resources. Attaching it to an IAM user group and adding the five users gives them full access with central management.

others.A: AdministratorAccess is an identity-based policy; resource-based policies are attached to resources, not to IAM groups.
others.B: SystemAdministrator is a job-function policy with limited permissions, not full access.
others.D: SystemAdministrator is not full access, and resource-based policies cannot be attached to groups.

e.tip: IAM groups take identity-based policies only; full access = AdministratorAccess.

q: A company has a multi-tier payment processing application that is based on virtual machines (VMs). The communication between the tiers occurs asynchronously through a third-party middleware solution that guarantees exactly-once delivery. The company needs a solution that requires the least amount of infrastructure management. The solution must guarantee exactly-once delivery for application messaging. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use AWS Lambda for the compute layers in the architecture.
o.B: Use Amazon EC2 instances for the compute layers in the architecture.
o.C: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) as the messaging component between the compute layers.
o.D: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the messaging component between the compute layers.
o.E: Use containers that are based on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) for the compute layers in the architecture.

e.why: SQS FIFO queues provide exactly-once processing and ordered delivery with deduplication, replacing the middleware's guarantee. AWS Lambda runs the compute tiers without any servers to manage, minimizing infrastructure management.

others.B: EC2 instances require managing servers, patching and scaling.
others.C: Standard SNS topics provide at-least-once delivery, not exactly-once.
others.E: EKS still requires cluster and container management compared with Lambda.

e.tip: Exactly-once messaging on AWS = SQS FIFO (or SNS FIFO to SQS FIFO).

q: A company has a nightly batch processing routine that analyzes report files that an on-premises file system receives daily through SFTP. The company wants to move the solution to the AWS Cloud. The solution must be highly available and resilient. The solution also must minimize operational effort. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Deploy AWS Transfer for SFTP and an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for storage. Use an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group with a scheduled scaling policy to run the batch operation.
o.B: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance that runs Linux and an SFTP service. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for storage. Use an Auto Scaling group with the minimum number of instances and desired number of instances set to 1.
o.C: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance that runs Linux and an SFTP service. Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for storage. Use an Auto Scaling group with the minimum number of instances and desired number of instances set to 1.
o.D: Deploy AWS Transfer for SFTP and an Amazon S3 bucket for storage. Modify the application to pull the batch files from Amazon S3 to an Amazon EC2 instance for processing. Use an EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group with a scheduled scaling policy to run the batch operation.

e.why: AWS Transfer Family for SFTP is a fully managed, multi-AZ SFTP endpoint, and Amazon EFS provides highly available, regional file storage that keeps the existing file-system workflow. An Auto Scaling group with scheduled scaling launches the batch EC2 instance only for the nightly run, minimizing operational effort.

others.B: A self-managed SFTP server on one EC2 instance with a single-AZ EBS volume is neither highly available nor low effort.
others.C: Running and patching your own SFTP service on EC2 adds operational effort compared with Transfer Family.
others.D: S3 works with Transfer Family, but the application would need to be modified to pull files from S3, adding effort.

e.tip: Managed SFTP = Transfer Family (backed by S3 or EFS).

q: A company has users all around the world accessing its HTTP-based application deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions. The company wants to improve the availability and performance of the application. The company also wants to protect the application against common web exploits that may affect availability, compromise security, or consume excessive resources. Static IP addresses are required. What should a solutions architect recommend to accomplish this?

o.A: Put the EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the NLBs. Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator and register the NLBs as endpoints.
o.B: Put the EC2 instances behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the ALBs. Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator and register the ALBs as endpoints.
o.C: Put the EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the NLBs. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the NLBs.
o.D: Put the EC2 instances behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the ALBs. Deploy AWS WAF on the CloudFront distribution.

e.why: AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and routes users to the nearest healthy Regional endpoint, improving availability and performance. Application Load Balancers in each Region handle HTTP traffic and support AWS WAF to block common web exploits.

others.A: AWS WAF cannot be attached to Network Load Balancers.
others.C: WAF cannot be deployed on NLBs, and CloudFront does not provide static IP addresses.
others.D: CloudFront does not offer static IP addresses for clients to allow, and a Route 53 latency record cannot be a CloudFront origin in this way.

e.tip: Static IPs + WAF for HTTP apps across Regions = Global Accelerator in front of ALBs with WAF.

q: A company’s data platform uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. The database has multiple read replicas and multiple DB instances across different Availability Zones. Users have recently reported errors from the database that indicate that there are too many connections. The company wants to reduce the failover time by 20% when a read replica is promoted to primary writer. Which solution will meet this requirement?

o.A: Switch from Aurora to Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ cluster deployment.
o.B: Use Amazon RDS Proxy in front of the Aurora database.
o.C: Switch to Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for read connections.
o.D: Switch to Amazon Redshift with relocation capability.

e.why: RDS Proxy pools and shares connections, eliminating 'too many connections' errors. It also maintains client connections during failover and routes to the new writer without waiting for DNS propagation, reducing Aurora failover times by up to 66%, well beyond the 20% goal.

others.A: Moving to RDS Multi-AZ DB clusters is a migration away from Aurora and does not solve connection exhaustion.
others.C: DynamoDB with DAX would require a complete application and data model rewrite.
others.D: Redshift is a data warehouse, not a transactional replacement, and relocation is unrelated to failover of Aurora.

e.tip: RDS Proxy: connection pooling + faster failover.

q: A company stores text files in Amazon S3. The text files include customer chat messages, date and time information, and customer personally identifiable information (PII). The company needs a solution to provide samples of the conversations to an external service provider for quality control. The external service provider needs to randomly pick sample conversations up to the most recent conversation. The company must not share the customer PII with the external service provider. The solution must scale when the number of customer conversations increases. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an Object Lambda Access Point. Create an AWS Lambda function that redacts the PII when the function reads the file. Instruct the external service provider to access the Object Lambda Access Point.
o.B: Create a web application on an Amazon EC2 instance that presents a list of the files, redacts the PII from the files, and allows the external service provider to download new versions of the files that have the PII redacted.
o.C: Create an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create an AWS Lambda function that reads only the data in the files that does not contain PII. Configure the Lambda function to store the non-PII data in the DynamoDB table when a new file is written to Amazon S3. Grant the external service provider access to the DynamoDB table.

fixed: The source listed options A, B and D; they have been relabeled A, B and C.

e.why: S3 Object Lambda runs a Lambda function on each GET request, so the PII can be redacted as files are read. The provider reads from the Object Lambda Access Point, no copies of the data are needed, and it scales automatically.

others.B: A custom web application on EC2 has to be built, scaled and maintained.
others.C: Copying non-PII data to DynamoDB changes the data format and adds a pipeline to maintain.

e.tip: Transform or redact S3 data as it is read: S3 Object Lambda.

q: A company is running a legacy system on an Amazon EC2 instance. The application code cannot be modified, and the system cannot run on more than one instance. A solutions architect must design a resilient solution that can improve the recovery time for the system. What should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Enable termination protection for the EC2 instance.
o.B: Configure the EC2 instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
o.C: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to recover the EC2 instance in case of failure.
o.D: Launch the EC2 instance with two Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that use RAID configurations for storage redundancy.

e.why: A CloudWatch alarm with the EC2 recover action automatically recovers the instance onto new hardware when system status checks fail, keeping its instance ID, private IP, Elastic IP and EBS volumes. This improves recovery time for a single-instance system without code changes.

others.A: Termination protection only prevents accidental termination; it does not help recovery from failures.
others.B: EC2 instances have no Multi-AZ deployment option, and the system cannot run on more than one instance.
others.D: RAID across EBS volumes protects storage only, not recovery from host or instance failure.

e.tip: Single EC2 instance, faster recovery = CloudWatch alarm EC2 recover action (or simplified automatic recovery).

q: A company wants to deploy its containerized application workloads to a VPC across three Availability Zones. The company needs a solution that is highly available across Availability Zones. The solution must require minimal changes to the application. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon ECS Service Auto Scaling to use target tracking scaling. Set the minimum capacity to 3. Set the task placement strategy type to spread with an Availability Zone attribute.
o.B: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) self-managed nodes. Configure Application Auto Scaling to use target tracking scaling. Set the minimum capacity to 3.
o.C: Use Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Launch three EC2 instances in a spread placement group. Configure an Auto Scaling group to use target tracking scaling. Set the minimum capacity to 3.
o.D: Use an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to connect to a VPC. Configure Application Auto Scaling to use Lambda as a scalable target. Set the minimum capacity to 3.

e.why: Amazon ECS runs the existing containers with minimal changes. ECS Service Auto Scaling with target tracking keeps at least three tasks, and the spread placement strategy on the attribute:ecs.availability-zone distributes tasks across the three AZs for high availability.

others.B: Self-managed EKS nodes require managing node lifecycle and patching, adding operational overhead.
others.C: Plain EC2 instances do not run container workloads in a managed way, and Reserved Instances are a pricing choice, not an HA design.
others.D: Lambda requires refactoring the containerized application into functions, and minimum capacity of 3 is not a Lambda concept.

e.tip: ECS task spread across AZs: placement strategy spread on attribute:ecs.availability-zone.

q: A media company stores movies in Amazon S3. Each movie is stored in a single video file that ranges from 1 GB to 10 GB in size. The company must be able to provide the streaming content of a movie within 5 minutes of a user purchase. There is higher demand for movies that are less than 20 years old than for movies that are more than 20 years old. The company wants to minimize hosting service costs based on demand. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Store all media content in Amazon S3. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move media data into the Infrequent Access tier when the demand for a movie decreases.
o.B: Store newer movie video files in S3 Standard. Store older movie video files in S3 Standard-infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). When a user orders an older movie, retrieve the video file by using standard retrieval.
o.C: Store newer movie video files in S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Store older movie video files in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. When a user orders an older movie, retrieve the video file by using expedited retrieval.
o.D: Store newer movie video files in S3 Standard. Store older movie video files in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. When a user orders an older movie, retrieve the video file by using bulk retrieval.

e.why: Keeping newer, high-demand movies in S3 Standard and older, less-requested movies in S3 Standard-IA lowers storage cost for the older titles. Standard-IA still provides millisecond access, so older movies can be streamed immediately, well within 5 minutes of purchase.

others.A: Moving data per movie based on fluctuating demand is not something Lifecycle rules can track; they work on object age, not demand.
others.C: Glacier Flexible Retrieval expedited retrieval usually takes 1-5 minutes but is not guaranteed without provisioned capacity, and files up to 10 GB add retrieval cost.
others.D: Bulk retrieval from Glacier Flexible Retrieval takes 5-12 hours, missing the 5-minute requirement.

e.tip: Need fast access to rarely used objects = Standard-IA; Glacier retrieval times rarely fit minutes-level SLAs.

q: A solutions architect needs to design the architecture for an application that a vendor provides as a Docker container image. The container needs 50 GB of storage available for temporary files. The infrastructure must be serverless. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the Docker container image with an Amazon S3 mounted volume that has more than 50 GB of space.
o.B: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the Docker container image with an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that has more than 50 GB of space.
o.C: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type. Create a task definition for the container image with an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Create a service with that task definition.
o.D: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses the Amazon EC2 launch type with an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that has more than 50 GB of space. Create a task definition for the container image. Create a service with that task definition.

e.why: ECS on Fargate is serverless and runs any Docker image. Mounting an Amazon EFS volume in the task definition provides 50 GB or more of shared, elastic storage for temporary files with no servers to manage (Fargate ephemeral storage up to 200 GiB is also an option).

others.A: Lambda cannot mount S3 as a volume, and its /tmp storage is limited to 10 GB.
others.B: Lambda cannot attach EBS volumes.
others.D: The EC2 launch type requires managing container instances, so it is not serverless.

e.tip: Lambda ephemeral storage max is 10 GB; Fargate supports up to 200 GiB plus EFS.

q: A company needs to use its on-premises LDAP directory service to authenticate its users to the AWS Management Console. The directory service is not compatible with Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML). Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) between AWS and the on-premises LDAP.
o.B: Create an IAM policy that uses AWS credentials, and integrate the policy into LDAP.
