o.C: Set up a process that rotates the IAM credentials whenever LDAP credentials are updated.
o.D: Develop an on-premises custom identity broker application or process that uses AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to get short-lived credentials.

e.why: Because the LDAP directory does not support SAML, a custom identity broker authenticates users against LDAP and then calls AWS STS (AssumeRole or GetFederationToken) to obtain temporary credentials. The broker can generate a console sign-in URL from those credentials for console access.

others.A: IAM Identity Center federates with SAML 2.0 IdPs or AD via AWS Directory Service; it cannot connect directly to a non-SAML LDAP directory.
others.B: IAM policies cannot be integrated into LDAP for authentication.
others.C: Rotating long-term IAM credentials whenever LDAP changes is insecure and complex, and still is not federation.

e.tip: Non-SAML identity store = custom identity broker with STS temporary credentials.

q: A company stores multiple Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) in an AWS account to launch its Amazon EC2 instances. The AMIs contain critical data and configurations that are necessary for the company’s operations. The company wants to implement a solution that will recover accidentally deleted AMIs quickly and efficiently. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots of the AMIs. Store the snapshots in a separate AWS account.
o.B: Copy all AMIs to another AWS account periodically.
o.C: Create a retention rule in Recycle Bin.
o.D: Upload the AMIs to an Amazon S3 bucket that has Cross-Region Replication.

e.why: Recycle Bin supports EBS-backed AMIs: a retention rule keeps deregistered AMIs for a set period, so accidentally deleted AMIs can be restored quickly. It requires only a one-time rule configuration, giving the least operational overhead.

others.A: Snapshots of AMIs in another account require rebuilding and re-registering AMIs, which is slower and more effort.
others.B: Periodically copying AMIs to another account adds ongoing work and cost.
others.D: AMIs are not uploaded to S3 buckets for replication; this is not a supported recovery method.

e.tip: Recover accidentally deleted EBS snapshots or AMIs = Recycle Bin retention rules.

q: A company has 150 TB of archived image data stored on-premises that needs to be moved to the AWS Cloud within the next month. The company’s current network connection allows up to 100 Mbps uploads for this purpose during the night only. What is the MOST cost-effective mechanism to move this data and meet the migration deadline?

o.A: Use AWS Snowmobile to ship the data to AWS.
o.B: Order multiple AWS Snowball devices to ship the data to AWS.
o.C: Enable Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration and securely upload the data.
o.D: Create an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint and establish a VPN to upload the data.

e.why: At 100 Mbps only at night, uploading 150 TB would take many months. Multiple Snowball Edge devices (about 80 TB usable each) can be shipped, loaded and returned within the month, and are far cheaper than Snowmobile for this volume.

others.A: Snowmobile was intended for 10 PB-scale migrations, is overkill for 150 TB, and has been discontinued.
others.C: Transfer Acceleration does not increase the limited 100 Mbps nightly bandwidth.
others.D: A VPN and VPC endpoint still rely on the same slow link and cannot move 150 TB in a month.

e.tip: Quick math: 100 Mbps is about 1 TB per day at full utilization; tens to hundreds of TB on limited links = Snowball.

q: A company wants to migrate its three-tier application from on premises to AWS. The web tier and the application tier are running on third-party virtual machines (VMs). The database tier is running on MySQL. The company needs to migrate the application by making the fewest possible changes to the architecture. The company also needs a database solution that can restore data to a specific point in time. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Migrate the web tier and the application tier to Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon RDS for MySQL in private subnets.
o.B: Migrate the web tier to Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Migrate the application tier to EC2 instances in private subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon Aurora MySQL in private subnets.
o.C: Migrate the web tier to Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Migrate the application tier to EC2 instances in private subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon RDS for MySQL in private subnets.
o.D: Migrate the web tier and the application tier to Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon Aurora MySQL in public subnets.

e.why: Keeping a public web tier and private application tier on EC2 mirrors the existing architecture with minimal changes. Aurora MySQL is MySQL-compatible, supports point-in-time recovery from continuous backups, and is fully managed in private subnets, minimizing operational overhead.

others.A: Putting the web tier in private subnets would require adding a load balancer or other changes for internet access.
others.C: RDS for MySQL also supports point-in-time recovery, but the key prefers Aurora MySQL for its managed storage and resilience with lower overhead.
others.D: Placing the database and all tiers in public subnets is insecure.

e.tip: Both RDS and Aurora support PITR; never put databases in public subnets.

q: A development team is collaborating with another company to create an integrated product. The other company needs to access an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue that is contained in the development team's account. The other company wants to poll the queue without giving up its own account permissions to do so. How should a solutions architect provide access to the SQS queue?

o.A: Create an instance profile that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
o.B: Create an IAM policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
o.C: Create an SQS access policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
o.D: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) access policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.

e.why: An SQS access policy is a resource-based policy on the queue that can grant another AWS account's principals permissions such as sqs:ReceiveMessage. The other company keeps using its own identities and permissions without assuming a role in the development team's account.

others.A: Instance profiles attach roles to EC2 instances in the same account and do not grant cross-account queue access.
others.B: An IAM identity policy in the development team's account cannot grant permissions to principals in another account.
others.D: An SNS access policy controls an SNS topic, not access to an SQS queue.

e.tip: Cross-account access without assuming a role = resource-based policy (SQS queue policy).

q: A company’s developers want a secure way to gain SSH access on the company's Amazon EC2 instances that run the latest version of Amazon Linux. The developers work remotely and in the corporate office. The company wants to use AWS services as a part of the solution. The EC2 instances are hosted in a VPC private subnet and access the internet through a NAT gateway that is deployed in a public subnet. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create a bastion host in the same subnet as the EC2 instances. Grant the ec2:CreateVpnConnection IAM permission to the developers. Install EC2 Instance Connect so that the developers can connect to the EC2 instances.
o.B: Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the corporate network and the VPC. Instruct the developers to use the Site-to-Site VPN connection to access the EC2 instances when the developers are on the corporate network. Instruct the developers to set up another VPN connection for access when they work remotely.
o.C: Create a bastion host in the public subnet of the VPConfigure the security groups and SSH keys of the bastion host to only allow connections and SSH authentication from the developers’ corporate and remote networks. Instruct the developers to connect through the bastion host by using SSH to reach the EC2 instances.
o.D: Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore IAM policy to an IAM role that is associated with the EC2 instances. Instruct the developers to use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to access the EC2 instances.

e.why: With the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy on the instance role, the SSM Agent (preinstalled on Amazon Linux) connects outbound through the NAT gateway. Developers then use Session Manager, including SSH tunneling through it, from anywhere with IAM authentication and logging, without bastion hosts or open inbound ports, and with no extra charge.

others.A: A bastion host in a private subnet is unreachable from the internet, and ec2:CreateVpnConnection is unrelated to SSH access.
others.B: Site-to-Site VPN costs money per hour and still requires a separate solution for remote developers.
others.C: A bastion host costs money to run, requires key management, and exposes SSH to the internet.

e.tip: Secure shell access without bastions or open ports = Session Manager.

q: A pharmaceutical company is developing a new drug. The volume of data that the company generates has grown exponentially over the past few months. The company's researchers regularly require a subset of the entire dataset to be immediately available with minimal lag. However, the entire dataset does not need to be accessed on a daily basis. All the data currently resides in on-premises storage arrays, and the company wants to reduce ongoing capital expenses. Which storage solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Run AWS DataSync as a scheduled cron job to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket on an ongoing basis.
o.B: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway with an Amazon S3 bucket as the target storage. Migrate the data to the Storage Gateway appliance.
o.C: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway with cached volumes with an Amazon S3 bucket as the target storage. Migrate the data to the Storage Gateway appliance.
o.D: Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection from the on-premises environment to AWS. Migrate data to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.

e.why: Storage Gateway volume gateway with cached volumes stores the full dataset in Amazon S3 while keeping frequently accessed subsets cached locally for low-latency access. This removes the need to buy more on-premises storage arrays, reducing capital expenses.

others.A: Migrating data to S3 with DataSync leaves researchers without low-latency local access to the working subset.
others.B: File gateway also caches data locally, but the data currently resides on block storage arrays, which map more directly to volume gateway cached volumes.
others.D: EFS over a VPN gives higher-latency access for researchers and no local cache.

e.tip: Block storage arrays to cloud with local cache = cached volume gateway.

q: A company has a business-critical application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application stores data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company must be able to revert the table to any point within the last 24 hours. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Configure point-in-time recovery for the table.
o.B: Use AWS Backup for the table.
o.C: Use an AWS Lambda function to make an on-demand backup of the table every hour.
o.D: Turn on streams on the table to capture a log of all changes to the table in the last 24 hours. Store a copy of the stream in an Amazon S3 bucket.

e.why: DynamoDB point-in-time recovery continuously backs up the table and lets you restore to any second within the last 35 days, covering the 24-hour requirement. It is enabled with a single setting, giving the least operational overhead.

others.B: AWS Backup schedules backups at intervals, so it cannot restore to an arbitrary point unless you also enable continuous backups, adding configuration.
others.C: Hourly on-demand backups via Lambda only allow restoring to hourly points and require custom code.
others.D: Streams hold changes for only 24 hours and require building a custom replay mechanism to restore.

e.tip: Restore DynamoDB to any second in the last 35 days = PITR.

q: A company hosts an application used to upload files to an Amazon S3 bucket. Once uploaded, the files are processed to extract metadata, which takes less than 5 seconds. The volume and frequency of the uploads varies from a few files each hour to hundreds of concurrent uploads. The company has asked a solutions architect to design a cost-effective architecture that will meet these requirements. What should the solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Configure AWS CloudTrail trails to log S3 API calls. Use AWS AppSync to process the files.
o.B: Configure an object-created event notification within the S3 bucket to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the files.
o.C: Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process and send data to Amazon S3. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the files.
o.D: Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to process the files uploaded to Amazon S3. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the files.

e.why: S3 object-created event notifications can invoke a Lambda function directly for each upload. Lambda scales automatically from a few invocations an hour to hundreds of concurrent ones, the sub-5-second job fits well inside the 15-minute limit, and you pay only per invocation. That makes it the most cost-effective event-driven design for spiky, unpredictable upload volumes.

others.A: CloudTrail is for auditing API calls, not for triggering processing, and AppSync is a GraphQL API service, not a file processor.
others.C: Kinesis Data Streams adds shard costs and complexity, and the files are already landing in S3, so a stream is unnecessary.
others.D: SNS cannot process files itself; adding it between S3 and Lambda only adds an extra hop when S3 can invoke Lambda directly.

e.tip: S3 upload plus short processing usually means an S3 event notification invoking Lambda.

q: A company’s application is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances and uses AWS Lambda functions for an event-driven architecture. The company uses nonproduction development environments in a different AWS account to test new features before the company deploys the features to production. The production instances show constant usage because of customers in different time zones. The company uses nonproduction instances only during business hours on weekdays. The company does not use the nonproduction instances on the weekends. The company wants to optimize the costs to run its application on AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use On-Demand Instances for the production instances. Use Dedicated Hosts for the nonproduction instances on weekends only.
o.B: Use Reserved Instances for the production instances and the nonproduction instances. Shut down the nonproduction instances when not in use.
o.C: Use Compute Savings Plans for the production instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the nonproduction instances. Shut down the nonproduction instances when not in use.
o.D: Use Dedicated Hosts for the production instances. Use EC2 Instance Savings Plans for the nonproduction instances.

e.why: Production runs constantly, so a Compute Savings Plan gives up to about 66% off for a 1- or 3-year commitment and stays flexible across instance family, Region and even Lambda, which the app also uses. Nonproduction runs only on weekday business hours, so On-Demand Instances that are stopped outside those hours avoid paying for idle capacity, unlike a commitment.

others.A: On-Demand for steady production wastes the commitment discount, and Dedicated Hosts are expensive and unnecessary.
others.B: Reserved Instances for nonproduction are billed 24/7 whether the instances run or not, so shutting them down saves nothing.
others.D: Dedicated Hosts for production are costly with no stated licensing need, and an Instance Savings Plan commitment is wasted on part-time nonproduction use.

e.tip: Use a commitment (RI or Savings Plan) for steady 24/7 load and On-Demand that you stop when idle for part-time load. Compute Savings Plans also cover Lambda and Fargate.

q: A company stores data in an on-premises Oracle relational database. The company needs to make the data available in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for analysis. The company uses an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to connect its on-premises network to AWS. The company must capture the changes that occur to the source database during the migration to Aurora PostgreSQL. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to convert the Oracle schema to Aurora PostgreSQL schema. Use the AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) full-load migration task to migrate the data.
o.B: Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Import the S3 data to Aurora PostgreSQL by using the Aurora PostgreSQL aws_s3 extension.
o.C: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to convert the Oracle schema to Aurora PostgreSQL schema. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the existing data and replicate the ongoing changes.
o.D: Use an AWS Snowball device to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Import the S3 data to Aurora PostgreSQL by using the Aurora PostgreSQL aws_s3 extension.

e.why: Moving from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL is a heterogeneous migration, so AWS SCT converts the schema. AWS DMS then does a full load plus change data capture (CDC) to replicate ongoing changes over the existing VPN. The requirement to capture changes during the migration is what CDC delivers.

others.A: A full-load-only DMS task does not capture changes made during the migration.
others.B: DataSync copies files, not live database changes, so it gives no CDC or schema conversion.
others.D: Snowball is an offline bulk transfer with no ongoing change capture, and it is not needed when a VPN exists.

e.tip: Heterogeneous migration means SCT plus DMS. The phrase 'ongoing changes' means a DMS full load plus CDC.

q: A company built an application with Docker containers and needs to run the application in the AWS Cloud. The company wants to use a managed service to host the application. The solution must scale in and out appropriately according to demand on the individual container services. The solution also must not result in additional operational overhead or infrastructure to manage. Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate.
o.B: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate.
o.C: Provision an Amazon API Gateway API. Connect the API to AWS Lambda to run the containers.
o.D: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes.
o.E: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes.

e.why: AWS Fargate is serverless compute for containers, so there are no EC2 worker nodes to patch or scale. Both ECS on Fargate and EKS on Fargate run Docker containers as a managed service, and each service scales in and out on its own (for ECS, through Service Auto Scaling).

others.C: Lambda can run container images but is not a general host for long-running Docker services, and API Gateway adds unrelated components.
others.D: ECS on EC2 means managing and scaling the EC2 container instances yourself, which is extra infrastructure.
others.E: EKS with EC2 worker nodes requires managing node groups, which adds operational overhead.

e.tip: 'No infrastructure to manage' for containers usually means Fargate (with ECS or EKS).

q: An ecommerce company is running a seasonal online sale. The company hosts its website on Amazon EC2 instances spanning multiple Availability Zones. The company wants its website to manage sudden traffic increases during the sale. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create an Auto Scaling group that is large enough to handle peak traffic load. Stop half of the Amazon EC2 instances. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the stopped instances to scale out when traffic increases.
o.B: Create an Auto Scaling group for the website. Set the minimum size of the Auto Scaling group so that it can handle high traffic volumes without the need to scale out.
o.C: Use Amazon CloudFront and Amazon ElastiCache to cache dynamic content with an Auto Scaling group set as the origin. Configure the Auto Scaling group with the instances necessary to populate CloudFront and ElastiCache. Scale in after the cache is fully populated.
o.D: Configure an Auto Scaling group to scale out as traffic increases. Create a launch template to start new instances from a preconfigured Amazon Machine Image (AMI).

e.why: An Auto Scaling group with dynamic scaling adds instances only as traffic grows and removes them afterwards, so you pay for peak capacity only while it is needed. A launch template that points to a preconfigured AMI lets new instances boot quickly, ready to serve, during sudden spikes.

others.A: Keeping a full peak-sized fleet, even partly stopped, still pays for EBS volumes and means manual work. It is not a normal scaling design.
others.B: Setting the minimum size for peak traffic means paying for peak capacity all the time, which is not cost-effective.
others.C: Scaling in once caches are 'fully populated' does not work for dynamic content that changes, and it adds ElastiCache cost and complexity.

e.tip: Cost-effective elasticity means dynamic scaling from a golden AMI, not over-provisioning.

q: A solutions architect must provide an automated solution for a company's compliance policy that states security groups cannot include a rule that allows SSH from 0.0.0.0/0. The company needs to be notified if there is any breach in the policy. A solution is needed as soon as possible. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Write an AWS Lambda script that monitors security groups for SSH being open to 0.0.0.0/0 addresses and creates a notification every time it finds one.
o.B: Enable the restricted-ssh AWS Config managed rule and generate an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification when a noncompliant rule is created.
o.C: Create an IAM role with permissions to globally open security groups and network ACLs. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to generate a notification every time the role is assumed by a user.
o.D: Configure a service control policy (SCP) that prevents non-administrative users from creating or editing security groups. Create a notification in the ticketing system when a user requests a rule that needs administrator permissions.

e.why: AWS Config has a managed rule, restricted-ssh (INCOMING_SSH_DISABLED), that checks security groups for SSH open to 0.0.0.0/0. It is ready to use immediately, and compliance-change events can go to SNS through EventBridge. Nothing has to be written or maintained, which matches 'as soon as possible' and 'least operational overhead'.

others.A: A custom Lambda monitor must be written, scheduled and maintained, which is more overhead than a managed rule.
others.C: Watching role assumption does not detect the actual rule, and creating a role that can open security groups globally works against the goal.
others.D: An SCP blocking security group edits plus a ticketing process is heavy-handed and manual, and it does not detect existing breaches.

e.tip: For compliance detection with notification, look for an AWS Config managed rule plus SNS/EventBridge.

q: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes. A company has deployed an application in an AWS account. The application consists of microservices that run on AWS Lambda and Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). A separate team supports each microservice. The company has multiple AWS accounts and wants to give each team its own account for its microservices. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that will provide service-to-service communication over HTTPS (port 443). The solution also must provide a service registry for service discovery. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

o.A: Create an inspection VPC. Deploy an AWS Network Firewall firewall to the inspection VPC. Attach the inspection VPC to a new transit gateway. Route VPC-to-VPC traffic to the inspection VPC. Apply firewall rules to allow only HTTPS communication.
o.B: Create a VPC Lattice service network. Associate the microservices with the service network. Define HTTPS listeners for each service. Register microservice compute resources as targets. Identify VPCs that need to communicate with the services. Associate those VPCs with the service network.
o.C: Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) with an HTTPS listener and target groups for each microservice. Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service for each microservice. Create an interface VPC endpoint in each VPC that needs to consume that microservice.
o.D: Create peering connections between VPCs that contain microservices. Create a prefix list for each service that requires a connection to a client. Create route tables to route traffic to the appropriate VPC. Create security groups to allow only HTTPS communication.

e.why: Amazon VPC Lattice is built for service-to-service connectivity across accounts and VPCs. It provides a service network, HTTP/HTTPS listeners, targets that can be Lambda, EKS/IP or instances, and a built-in service directory for discovery. Sharing it through AWS RAM avoids managing peering, transit gateways or many endpoints, so it has the least administrative overhead.

others.A: An inspection VPC with Network Firewall and a transit gateway controls traffic but provides no service registry and is heavy to operate.
others.C: An NLB plus a PrivateLink endpoint service per microservice, with endpoints in every consumer VPC, does not scale well administratively and has no service discovery.
others.D: VPC peering meshes with prefix lists and route tables are manual, do not scale, and provide no service registry.

e.tip: Cross-account microservice connectivity with service discovery points to VPC Lattice.

q: A company has a mobile game that reads most of its metadata from an Amazon RDS DB instance. As the game increased in popularity, developers noticed slowdowns related to the game's metadata load times. Performance metrics indicate that simply scaling the database will not help. A solutions architect must explore all options that include capabilities for snapshots, replication, and sub-millisecond response times. What should the solutions architect recommend to solve these issues?

o.A: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora with Aurora Replicas.
o.B: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB with global tables.
o.C: Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis layer in front of the database.
o.D: Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached layer in front of the database.

e.why: ElastiCache for Redis (now also Valkey) sits in front of RDS as a cache with sub-millisecond reads for metadata. It also supports snapshots/backups and replication, with replicas and Multi-AZ failover. It meets all three stated capabilities without migrating the database.

others.A: Aurora Replicas improve read scale but give millisecond latency, not sub-millisecond, and the metrics say scaling the database will not help.
others.B: Migrating to DynamoDB global tables is a big re-architecture. DynamoDB alone is single-digit milliseconds, and global replication is not needed.
others.D: Memcached has no snapshot/backup or replication support.

e.tip: Redis vs Memcached: if the question needs snapshots, replication, persistence or advanced data types, choose Redis.

q: A company uses AWS Organizations for its multi-account AWS setup. The security organizational unit (OU) of the company needs to share approved Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) with the development OU. The AMIs are created by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted snapshots. Which solution will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Add the development team's OU Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to the launch permission list for the AMIs.
o.B: Add the Organizations root Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to the launch permission list for the AMIs.
o.C: Update the key policy to allow the development team's OU to use the AWS KMS keys that are used to decrypt the snapshots.
o.D: Add the development team’s account Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to the launch permission list for the AMIs.
o.E: Recreate the AWS KMS key. Add a key policy to allow the Organizations root Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to use the AWS KMS key.

e.why: An AMI can be shared with an organizational unit by adding the OU ARN to its launch permissions. Because the backing snapshots are encrypted with a customer managed KMS key, the key policy must also let principals in that OU use the key (for example kms:Decrypt and kms:CreateGrant, often scoped with aws:PrincipalOrgPaths). Without this, launches fail.

others.B: Sharing with the organization root ARN shares the AMI with the whole organization, not just the development OU, which grants too much access.
others.D: Adding individual account ARNs works but must be repeated for each account. The requirement is to share with the OU.
others.E: There is no need to recreate the key, and granting the whole organization root is broader than the development OU.

e.tip: Sharing encrypted AMIs takes two things: launch permissions and KMS key access. The default aws/ebs key cannot be shared.

q: A data analytics company has 80 offices that are distributed globally. Each office hosts 1 PB of data and has between 1 and 2 Gbps of internet bandwidth. The company needs to perform a one-time migration of a large amount of data from its offices to Amazon S3. The company must complete the migration within 4 weeks. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Establish a new 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to each office. Transfer the data to Amazon S3.
o.B: Use multiple AWS Snowball Edge storage-optimized devices to store and transfer the data to Amazon S3.
o.C: Use an AWS Snowmobile to store and transfer the data to Amazon S3.
o.D: Set up an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway to transfer the data to Amazon S3.

e.why: 80 PB at 1-2 Gbps per office would take months over the internet, missing the 4-week deadline. Several Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices per office (about 80-210 TB each) can be loaded in parallel and shipped, which is the cost-effective offline option for data spread across many sites.

others.A: Ordering 80 Direct Connect connections at 10 Gbps takes weeks to months to provision and is very expensive for a one-time move.
others.C: AWS Snowmobile has been discontinued, and one truck could not serve 80 globally distributed offices anyway.
others.D: Volume Gateway still sends data over the limited internet links, so it cannot move 1 PB per office in 4 weeks.

e.tip: Work out transfer time first (1 PB at 1 Gbps is roughly 93 days). If it misses the deadline, use the Snow Family.

q: A company has an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that contains a reference dataset. The company has applications on Amazon EC2 instances that need to read the dataset. However, the applications must not be able to change the dataset. The company wants to use IAM access control to prevent the applications from being able to modify or delete the dataset. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Mount the EFS file system in read-only mode from within the EC2 instances.
o.B: Create a resource policy for the EFS file system that denies the elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite action to the IAM roles that are attached to the EC2 instances.
o.C: Create an identity policy for the EFS file system that denies the elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite action on the EFS file system.
o.D: Create an EFS access point for each application. Use Portable Operating System Interface (POSIX) file permissions to allow read-only access to files in the root directory.

e.why: An EFS file system policy is a resource-based IAM policy. Denying elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite (and ClientRootAccess if needed) to the EC2 instance roles enforces read-only access at the service using IAM authorization when clients mount with IAM. This meets the requirement to use IAM access control.

others.A: A read-only mount is a client-side setting that the application or OS could change. It is not IAM-based control.
others.C: Identity policies attach to principals, not to the file system. As worded, this is not a valid way to attach a policy to EFS.
others.D: POSIX permissions through access points are file-system level, not IAM access control, and they are more work per application.

e.tip: For EFS, IAM authorization uses ClientMount, ClientWrite and ClientRootAccess in the file system (resource) policy.

q: A company has hired an external vendor to perform work in the company’s AWS account. The vendor uses an automated tool that is hosted in an AWS account that the vendor owns. The vendor does not have IAM access to the company’s AWS account. The company needs to grant the vendor access to the company’s AWS account. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?

o.A: Create an IAM role in the company’s account to delegate access to the vendor’s IAM role. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the role for the permissions that the vendor requires.
o.B: Create an IAM user in the company’s account with a password that meets the password complexity requirements. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.
o.C: Create an IAM group in the company’s account. Add the automated tool’s IAM user from the vendor account to the group. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the group for the permissions that the vendor requires.
o.D: Create an IAM user in the company’s account that has a permission boundary that allows the vendor’s account. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.

e.why: A cross-account IAM role with a trust policy naming the vendor's account or role, ideally with an external ID, lets the vendor's tool assume temporary credentials limited to the attached policies. No long-term credentials are shared, which is the most secure pattern for third-party access.

others.B: An IAM user with a password creates long-term credentials that must be shared and rotated, which is less secure.
others.C: IAM groups can only contain users from the same account. You cannot add another account's user.
others.D: Permissions boundaries limit an identity's maximum permissions; they do not allow another account to use a user. This still relies on long-term user credentials.

e.tip: Third-party or cross-account access means an IAM role with a trust policy and an external ID.

q: A company wants to run its experimental workloads in the AWS Cloud. The company has a budget for cloud spending. The company's CFO is concerned about cloud spending accountability for each department. The CFO wants to receive notification when the spending threshold reaches 60% of the budget. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use cost allocation tags on AWS resources to label owners. Create usage budgets in AWS Budgets. Add an alert threshold to receive notification when spending exceeds 60% of the budget.
o.B: Use AWS Cost Explorer forecasts to determine resource owners. Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to create alert threshold notifications when spending exceeds 60% of the budget.
o.C: Use cost allocation tags on AWS resources to label owners. Use AWS Support API on AWS Trusted Advisor to create alert threshold notifications when spending exceeds 60% of the budget.
o.D: Use AWS Cost Explorer forecasts to determine resource owners. Create usage budgets in AWS Budgets. Add an alert threshold to receive notification when spending exceeds 60% of the budget.

e.why: Cost allocation tags (for example owner or department) make spending traceable to each department once they are activated in Billing. AWS Budgets can then track costs against a budget, with an alert threshold at 60% that notifies the CFO by email or SNS.

others.B: Cost Explorer forecasts do not identify owners, and Cost Anomaly Detection alerts on unusual spend patterns, not a percentage of a budget.
others.C: Trusted Advisor and the Support API do not provide budget threshold alerts.
others.D: Cost Explorer forecasts cannot determine who owns resources; tags are needed for accountability.

e.tip: Notification at X% of budget means AWS Budgets. Per-department accountability means cost allocation tags.

q: A company wants to deploy an internal web application on AWS. The web application must be accessible only from the company's office. The company needs to download security patches for the web application from the internet. The company has created a VPC and has configured an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to the company's office. A solutions architect must design a secure architecture for the web application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets behind a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). Attach an internet gateway to the VPC. Set the inbound source of the ALB's security group to 0.0.0.0/0.
o.B: Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets behind an internal Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy NAT gateways in public subnets. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC. Set the inbound source of the ALB's security group to the company's office network CIDR block.
o.C: Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets behind an internal Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy NAT gateways in private subnets. Attach an internet gateway to the VPSet the outbound destination of the ALB’s security group to the company's office network CIDR block.
o.D: Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets behind a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). Attach an internet gateway to the VPC. Set the outbound destination of the ALB’s security group to 0.0.0.0/0.

e.why: An internal ALB in private subnets can be reached only from inside the VPC, including the office over the Site-to-Site VPN. Limiting its security group inbound rule to the office CIDR restricts access further. NAT gateways in public subnets, with an internet gateway, give the private instances outbound-only internet access to download patches.

others.A: A public ALB open to 0.0.0.0/0 exposes the app to the internet, which breaks the office-only requirement.
others.C: NAT gateways must be in public subnets. Setting only outbound rules on the ALB security group does not restrict who can reach it.
others.D: A public ALB with outbound 0.0.0.0/0 does not restrict inbound access to the office.

e.tip: Private app with outbound patching means private subnets plus a NAT gateway in a public subnet. Office-only access means an internal ALB over VPN or Direct Connect.

q: A company maintains its accounting records in a custom application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to migrate the data to an AWS managed service for development and maintenance of the application data. The solution must require minimal operational support and provide immutable, cryptographically verifiable logs of data changes. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Redshift cluster.
o.B: Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Neptune cluster.
o.C: Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Timestream database.
o.D: Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) ledger.

e.why: Amazon QLDB is a fully managed ledger database with an immutable, append-only journal that is cryptographically verifiable using SHA-256 hash chaining. It matches the requirement for verifiable logs of data changes with minimal operations.

others.A: Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics and has no immutable, verifiable change history.
others.B: Neptune is a graph database and does not provide a cryptographically verifiable journal.
others.C: Timestream is a time-series database for metrics and IoT, not a verifiable ledger.

e.tip: Immutable, cryptographically verifiable history points to QLDB on the exam. In practice QLDB reached end of support in July 2025; AWS suggests Aurora PostgreSQL with audit tables instead.

q: A company's marketing data is uploaded from multiple sources to an Amazon S3 bucket. A series of data preparation jobs aggregate the data for reporting. The data preparation jobs need to run at regular intervals in parallel. A few jobs need to run in a specific order later. The company wants to remove the operational overhead of job error handling, retry logic, and state management. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use an AWS Lambda function to process the data as soon as the data is uploaded to the S3 bucket. Invoke other Lambda functions at regularly scheduled intervals.
o.B: Use Amazon Athena to process the data. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to invoke Athena on a regular internal.
o.C: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to process the data. Use an AWS Step Functions state machine to run the DataBrew data preparation jobs.
o.D: Use AWS Data Pipeline to process the data. Schedule Data Pipeline to process the data once at midnight.

e.why: AWS Glue DataBrew provides managed, visual data preparation jobs. An AWS Step Functions state machine can orchestrate them with Parallel states for concurrent jobs and sequential states for ordered ones, plus built-in Retry/Catch error handling and state management. Running the state machine on a schedule meets the regular-interval requirement.

others.A: Chaining Lambda functions yourself leaves error handling, retries and state tracking to custom code.
others.B: Athena queries scheduled by EventBridge offer no orchestration of ordered steps or retry and state handling.
others.D: AWS Data Pipeline is in maintenance mode, and a single midnight run does not meet the parallel and ordered requirements.

e.tip: Removing error handling, retry logic and state management usually means Step Functions.

q: A solutions architect is designing a payment processing application that runs on AWS Lambda in private subnets across multiple Availability Zones. The application uses multiple Lambda functions and processes millions of transactions each day. The architecture must ensure that the application does not process duplicate payments. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket with an event notification to invoke another Lambda function to process the due payments.
o.B: Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure another Lambda function to poll the SQS queue and to process the due payments.
o.C: Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Configure another Lambda function to poll the FIFO queue and to process the due payments.
o.D: Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Store the due payments in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure streams on the DynamoDB table to invoke another Lambda function to process the due payments.

e.why: SQS FIFO queues provide exactly-once processing: within the 5-minute deduplication interval, duplicate messages are dropped using a content-based or explicit MessageDeduplicationId. A Lambda function polling the FIFO queue processes each payment once, in order per message group, which prevents duplicate payment processing.

others.A: S3 event notifications are delivered at least once and can occasionally be duplicated, so they do not guarantee no duplicates.
others.B: SQS Standard queues offer at-least-once delivery, so the same payment could be processed twice.
others.D: DynamoDB Streams with Lambda can retry batches, and nothing deduplicates payments that are inserted twice.

e.tip: 'No duplicates' or 'exactly-once' means SQS FIFO. Making the consumer idempotent is still best practice.

q: A company runs multiple workloads in its on-premises data center. The company's data center cannot scale fast enough to meet the company's expanding business needs. The company wants to collect usage and configuration data about the on-premises servers and workloads to plan a migration to AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Set the home AWS Region in AWS Migration Hub. Use AWS Systems Manager to collect data about the on-premises servers.
o.B: Set the home AWS Region in AWS Migration Hub. Use AWS Application Discovery Service to collect data about the on-premises servers.
o.C: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to create the relevant templates. Use AWS Trusted Advisor to collect data about the on-premises servers.
o.D: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to create the relevant templates. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to collect data about the on-premises servers.

e.why: AWS Application Discovery Service collects server configuration, utilization and dependency data from on-premises environments, either agentless through the Agentless Collector or with the Discovery Agent. Its data is stored in the AWS Migration Hub home Region for migration planning. This directly meets the 'collect usage and configuration data' requirement.

others.A: Systems Manager manages servers but is not the migration discovery tool, and it requires the SSM agent and hybrid activation on every server.
others.C: SCT converts database schemas, and Trusted Advisor checks AWS accounts, not on-premises servers.
others.D: SCT and DMS are database migration tools and do not inventory on-premises servers.

e.tip: Discovering on-premises servers before migration means Application Discovery Service plus the Migration Hub home Region.

q: A company has an organization in AWS Organizations that has all features enabled. The company requires that all API calls and logins in any existing or new AWS account must be audited. The company needs a managed solution to prevent additional work and to minimize costs. The company also needs to know when any AWS account is not compliant with the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices (FSBP) standard. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Deploy an AWS Control Tower environment in the Organizations management account. Enable AWS Security Hub and AWS Control Tower Account Factory in the environment.
o.B: Deploy an AWS Control Tower environment in a dedicated Organizations member account. Enable AWS Security Hub and AWS Control Tower Account Factory in the environment.
o.C: Use AWS Managed Services (AMS) Accelerate to build a multi-account landing zone (MALZ). Submit an RFC to self-service provision Amazon GuardDuty in the MALZ.
o.D: Use AWS Managed Services (AMS) Accelerate to build a multi-account landing zone (MALZ). Submit an RFC to self-service provision AWS Security Hub in the MALZ.

e.why: AWS Control Tower must be set up from the Organizations management account. It creates a landing zone with an organization-wide CloudTrail trail that audits API calls and logins in all existing and new enrolled accounts. Account Factory provisions new compliant accounts, and Security Hub with the FSBP standard reports noncompliant accounts, all as managed services with little overhead.

others.B: Control Tower cannot be launched from a member account; it must be deployed in the management account.
others.C: AMS Accelerate is an operations service with added cost, and GuardDuty detects threats but does not check FSBP compliance.
others.D: AMS adds cost and a request-for-change (RFC) process, which is more overhead and expense than Control Tower plus Security Hub.

e.tip: Control Tower always runs from the management account. FSBP compliance is reported by Security Hub.

q: A company has stored 10 TB of log files in Apache Parquet format in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company occasionally needs to use SQL to analyze the log files. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Migrate the data from the S3 bucket into Aurora by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Issue SQL statements to the Aurora database.
o.B: Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Use Redshift Spectrum to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.
o.C: Create an AWS Glue crawler to store and retrieve table metadata from the S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.
o.D: Create an Amazon EMR cluster. Use Apache Spark SQL to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.

e.why: Amazon Athena is serverless and runs SQL directly on Parquet data in S3, charging only for data scanned. Columnar Parquet keeps scans small. A Glue crawler fills in the Data Catalog table metadata. For occasional queries there is nothing to keep running, so this is the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Migrating 10 TB into Aurora means paying for a database running constantly and running a DMS migration, all for occasional queries.
others.B: Redshift Spectrum needs a Redshift cluster (or Serverless) to be provisioned, which costs more than Athena for occasional use.
others.D: An EMR cluster with Spark SQL needs cluster management and compute costs, which is too much for ad hoc SQL.

e.tip: Occasional SQL on data in S3 means Athena (plus the Glue Data Catalog).

q: A company needs a solution to prevent AWS CloudFormation stacks from deploying AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) resources that include an inline policy or “*” in the statement. The solution must also prohibit deployment of Amazon EC2 instances with public IP addresses. The company has AWS Control Tower enabled in its organization in AWS Organizations. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Control Tower proactive controls to block deployment of EC2 instances with public IP addresses and inline policies with elevated access or “*”.
o.B: Use AWS Control Tower detective controls to block deployment of EC2 instances with public IP addresses and inline policies with elevated access or “*”.
o.C: Use AWS Config to create rules for EC2 and IAM compliance. Configure the rules to run an AWS Systems Manager Session Manager automation to delete a resource when it is not compliant.
o.D: Use a service control policy (SCP) to block actions for the EC2 instances and IAM resources if the actions lead to noncompliance.

e.why: AWS Control Tower proactive controls are implemented as CloudFormation Hooks. They check resources before CloudFormation provisions them and block noncompliant ones, for example IAM policies with inline policies or wildcards, and EC2 instances with public IPs. This prevents the deployments rather than detecting them afterwards.

others.B: Detective controls (AWS Config rules) only flag noncompliance after resources exist; they do not block deployment.
others.C: Config rules with remediation react after the fact, and Session Manager is a shell-access tool, not a remediation mechanism.
others.D: SCPs act on API actions and some condition keys and cannot easily inspect policy document contents such as inline policies with '*'. They are also not CloudFormation-aware.

e.tip: In Control Tower: preventive means SCPs, detective means Config rules, and proactive means CloudFormation Hooks that block before provisioning.

q: A company's web application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud recently increased in popularity. The web application currently exists on a single Amazon EC2 instance in a single public subnet. The web application has not been able to meet the demand of the increased web traffic. The company needs a solution that will provide high availability and scalability to meet the increased user demand without rewriting the web application. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Replace the EC2 instance with a larger compute optimized instance.
o.B: Configure Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with multiple Availability Zones in private subnets.
o.C: Configure a NAT gateway in a public subnet to handle web requests.
o.D: Replace the EC2 instance with a larger memory optimized instance.
o.E: Configure an Application Load Balancer in a public subnet to distribute web traffic.

e.why: An EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones in private subnets gives scalability and high availability without code changes. An internet-facing Application Load Balancer in public subnets spreads web traffic across the healthy instances in the group.

others.A: A bigger instance is still a single point of failure in one AZ, so it is not highly available.
others.C: A NAT gateway only provides outbound internet access for private resources; it cannot serve inbound web requests.
others.D: Vertical scaling to a memory-optimized instance still leaves one instance in one AZ, with no high availability.

e.tip: High availability and scalability without a rewrite means an ALB plus a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group.

q: A company has AWS Lambda functions that use environment variables. The company does not want its developers to see environment variables in plaintext. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy code to Amazon EC2 instances instead of using Lambda functions.
o.B: Configure SSL encryption on the Lambda functions to use AWS CloudHSM to store and encrypt the environment variables.
o.C: Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Configure the Lambda functions to use the certificate to encrypt the environment variables.
o.D: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Enable encryption helpers on the Lambda functions to use the KMS key to store and encrypt the environment variables.

e.why: Lambda environment variables are encrypted at rest with KMS. Using a customer managed KMS key with the console's encryption helpers encrypts values client-side before they are stored. Developers who lack kms:Decrypt on the key see only ciphertext, while the function decrypts at runtime.

others.A: Moving to EC2 does not solve the visibility problem and adds operational burden.
others.B: Lambda environment variables cannot be encrypted with SSL or CloudHSM; SSL/TLS protects data in transit.
others.C: ACM certificates are for TLS and cannot be used to encrypt Lambda environment variables.

e.tip: For truly secret values, Secrets Manager or Parameter Store SecureString is often preferred, but KMS encryption helpers are the direct answer here.

q: An analytics company uses Amazon VPC to run its multi-tier services. The company wants to use RESTful APIs to offer a web analytics service to millions of users. Users must be verified by using an authentication service to access the APIs. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool for user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway REST APIs with a Cognito authorizer.
o.B: Configure an Amazon Cognito identity pool for user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs with a Cognito authorizer.
o.C: Configure an AWS Lambda function to handle user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway REST APIs with a Lambda authorizer.
o.D: Configure an IAM user to handle user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs with an IAM authorizer.

e.why: An Amazon Cognito user pool is a managed user directory that handles sign-up, sign-in and token issuance and scales to millions of users. API Gateway REST APIs support a native Cognito user pool authorizer that validates the tokens without custom code, which gives the most operational efficiency.

others.B: Identity pools issue temporary AWS credentials rather than authenticating users as a user directory, and HTTP APIs use a JWT authorizer rather than a 'Cognito authorizer'.
others.C: A custom Lambda authentication service and Lambda authorizer must be built and maintained.
others.D: IAM users cannot be created for millions of end users and are not meant for customer authentication.

e.tip: End-user authentication for APIs means a Cognito user pool. AWS credentials for end users means a Cognito identity pool.

q: A company has a mobile app for customers. The app’s data is sensitive and must be encrypted at rest. The company uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The company needs a solution that prevents the accidental deletion of KMS keys. The solution must use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send an email notification to administrators when a user attempts to delete a KMS key. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts when a user tries to delete a KMS key. Configure an AWS Config rule that cancels any deletion of a KMS key. Add the AWS Config rule as a target of the EventBridge rule. Create an SNS topic that notifies the administrators.
o.B: Create an AWS Lambda function that has custom logic to prevent KMS key deletion. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is activated when a user tries to delete a KMS key. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the Lambda function when the DeleteKey operation is performed. Create an SNS topic. Configure the EventBridge rule to publish an SNS message that notifies the administrators.
o.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts when the KMS DeleteKey operation is performed. Configure the rule to initiate an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Configure the runbook to cancel the deletion of the KMS key. Create an SNS topic. Configure the EventBridge rule to publish an SNS message that notifies the administrators.
o.D: Create an AWS CloudTrail trail. Configure the trail to deliver logs to a new Amazon CloudWatch log group. Create a CloudWatch alarm based on the metric filter for the CloudWatch log group. Configure the alarm to use Amazon SNS to notify the administrators when the KMS DeleteKey operation is performed.

e.why: An EventBridge rule matching the KMS deletion API call (recorded by CloudTrail) can start a Systems Manager Automation runbook that calls CancelKeyDeletion during the 7-30 day waiting period, and also publish to an SNS topic that emails administrators. Both actions use managed services with no custom code.

others.A: An AWS Config rule is not a valid EventBridge target and cannot cancel key deletion.
others.B: A custom Lambda function plus a CloudWatch alarm adds code and components, which is more overhead than a managed runbook.
others.D: A CloudTrail metric filter and alarm only notifies administrators; it does not prevent the deletion.

e.tip: In reality the API is ScheduleKeyDeletion, and KMS keys always have a 7-30 day pending-deletion window in which deletion can be cancelled.

q: A company wants to analyze and generate reports to track the usage of its mobile app. The app is popular and has a global user base. The company uses a custom report building program to analyze application usage. The program generates multiple reports during the last week of each month. The program takes less than 10 minutes to produce each report. The company rarely uses the program to generate reports outside of the last week of each month The company wants to generate reports in the least amount of time when the reports are requested. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Run the program by using Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to start the EC2 instances when reports are requested. Run the EC2 instances continuously during the last week of each month.
o.B: Run the program in AWS Lambda. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to run a Lambda function when reports are requested.
o.C: Run the program in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Schedule Amazon ECS to run the program when reports are requested.
o.D: Run the program by using Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Create an Amazon EventBndge rule to start the EC2 instances when reports are requested. Run the EC2 instances continuously during the last week of each month.

e.why: Each report finishes in under 10 minutes, within Lambda's 15-minute limit. Lambda starts immediately and runs many reports in parallel, and you pay only for execution time. For rare, bursty use it avoids paying for idle EC2 for a whole week and gives the fastest turnaround.

others.A: Running On-Demand instances continuously all week pays for idle time between requests.
others.C: ECS tasks start more slowly and need cluster and task setup, and 'schedule when requested' is awkward compared with event-driven Lambda.
others.D: Spot Instances can be interrupted, and running them continuously still pays for idle capacity.

e.tip: Short (under 15 minutes), infrequent, on-demand jobs suit Lambda.

q: A company is designing a tightly coupled high performance computing (HPC) environment in the AWS Cloud. The company needs to include features that will optimize the HPC environment for networking and storage. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure custom routing for the accelerator.
o.B: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Configure the file system with scratch storage.
o.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the viewer protocol policy to be HTTP and HTTPS.
o.D: Launch Amazon EC2 instances. Attach an Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to the instances.
o.E: Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk deployment to manage the environment.

e.why: Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) gives EC2 instances OS-bypass, low-latency, high-throughput networking for tightly coupled MPI workloads, which is the networking optimization. FSx for Lustre with scratch storage provides a high-performance parallel file system for HPC at low cost, which is the storage optimization.

others.A: Global Accelerator speeds up internet traffic from users to applications, not node-to-node HPC traffic.
others.C: CloudFront is a CDN for content delivery and does nothing for HPC cluster performance.
others.E: Elastic Beanstalk is for deploying web applications, not for tuning HPC networking or storage.

e.tip: For HPC, EFA handles networking, FSx for Lustre handles storage, and cluster placement groups help latency.

q: A company needs a solution to prevent photos with unwanted content from being uploaded to the company's web application. The solution must not involve training a machine learning (ML) model. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create and deploy a model by using Amazon SageMaker Autopilot. Create a real-time endpoint that the web application invokes when new photos are uploaded.
o.B: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon Rekognition to detect unwanted content. Create a Lambda function URL that the web application invokes when new photos are uploaded.
o.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront function that uses Amazon Comprehend to detect unwanted content. Associate the function with the web application.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon Rekognition Video to detect unwanted content. Create a Lambda function URL that the web application invokes when new photos are uploaded.

e.why: Amazon Rekognition image moderation (DetectModerationLabels) detects unsafe or unwanted content in photos with pretrained models, so no ML training is required. A Lambda function exposed through a function URL lets the web app check each upload before accepting it.

others.A: SageMaker Autopilot trains a model, which the requirement rules out.
others.C: Comprehend analyzes text, not images, and CloudFront Functions cannot call other AWS services.
others.D: Rekognition Video is for video streams and files; photos use the Rekognition Image API.

e.tip: Image or video moderation without training means Rekognition. Text analysis means Comprehend.

q: A company uses AWS to run its ecommerce platform. The platform is critical to the company's operations and has a high volume of traffic and transactions. The company configures a multi-factor authentication (MFA) device to secure its AWS account root user credentials. The company wants to ensure that it will not lose access to the root user account if the MFA device is lost. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Set up a backup administrator account that the company can use to log in if the company loses the MFA device.
o.B: Add multiple MFA devices for the root user account to handle the disaster scenario.
o.C: Create a new administrator account when the company cannot access the root account.
o.D: Attach the administrator policy to another IAM user when the company cannot access the root account.

e.why: The root user can have up to 8 MFA devices registered, including FIDO security keys, virtual and hardware TOTP devices. Registering more than one, kept securely, means losing a single device does not lock the company out of root.

others.A: A backup administrator account cannot sign in as root or perform root-only tasks, so root access would still be lost.
others.C: Creating an admin account after losing root access does not restore root access, and you may not be able to create one without access.
others.D: An IAM user with AdministratorAccess still cannot perform root-only tasks or recover root MFA.

e.tip: AWS supports multiple MFA devices (up to 8) for root and IAM users.

q: A social media company is creating a rewards program website for its users. The company gives users points when users create and upload videos to the website. Users redeem their points for gifts or discounts from the company's affiliated partners. A unique ID identifies users. The partners refer to this ID to verify user eligibility for rewards. The partners want to receive notification of user IDs through an HTTP endpoint when the company gives users points. Hundreds of vendors are interested in becoming affiliated partners every day. The company wants to design an architecture that gives the website the ability to add partners rapidly in a scalable way. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

o.A: Create an Amazon Timestream database to keep a list of affiliated partners. Implement an AWS Lambda function to read the list. Configure the Lambda function to send user IDs to each partner when the company gives users points.
o.B: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Choose an endpoint protocol. Subscribe the partners to the topic. Publish user IDs to the topic when the company gives users points.
o.C: Create an AWS Step Functions state machine. Create a task for every affiliated partner. Invoke the state machine with user IDs as input when the company gives users points.
o.D: Create a data stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Implement producer and consumer applications. Store a list of affiliated partners in the data stream. Send user IDs when the company gives users points.

e.why: An SNS topic fans out each published message to all subscribers. Partners subscribe with HTTP/HTTPS endpoints, and SNS handles delivery retries. Adding hundreds of partners a day only means adding subscriptions, with no code changes, so it has the least implementation effort and scales well.

others.A: A Timestream list plus custom Lambda delivery code means building your own fan-out and retry logic, and Timestream is a time-series database, not a registry.
others.C: A Step Functions task per partner requires editing the state machine for every new partner, which does not scale.
others.D: Kinesis Data Streams needs custom producers and consumers and is not a partner registry or HTTP push mechanism.

e.tip: Push to many HTTP endpoints (pub/sub fan-out) means SNS.

q: A company needs to extract the names of ingredients from recipe records that are stored as text files in an Amazon S3 bucket. A web application will use the ingredient names to query an Amazon DynamoDB table and determine a nutrition score. The application can handle non-food records and errors. The company does not have any employees who have machine learning knowledge to develop this solution. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function when PutObject requests occur. Program the Lambda function to analyze the object and extract the ingredient names by using Amazon Comprehend. Store the Amazon Comprehend output in the DynamoDB table.
o.B: Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function when PutObject requests occur. Program the Lambda function to analyze the object by using Amazon Forecast to extract the ingredient names. Store the Forecast output in the DynamoDB table.
o.C: Use S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function when PutObject requests occur. Use Amazon Polly to create audio recordings of the recipe records. Save the audio files in the S3 bucket. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send a URL as a message to employees. Instruct the employees to listen to the audio files and calculate the nutrition score. Store the ingredient names in the DynamoDB table.
o.D: Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a PutObject request occurs. Program the Lambda function to analyze the object and extract the ingredient names by using Amazon SageMaker. Store the inference output from the SageMaker endpoint in the DynamoDB table.

e.why: Amazon Comprehend is a managed NLP service that needs no ML expertise. Entity detection, or custom entity recognition trained only on labelled examples rather than ML code, can extract ingredient names from text. An S3 event notification invoking Lambda on each upload is the simplest, pay-per-use way to process each file.

others.B: Amazon Forecast does time-series forecasting, not text extraction.
others.C: Polly converts text to speech, and manual listening by staff is slow and costly, not an automated solution.
others.D: SageMaker requires ML knowledge to build, train and host a model, and endpoints cost more.

e.tip: Text understanding means Comprehend, images mean Rekognition, documents or OCR mean Textract, and forecasting means Forecast.

q: A company needs to create an AWS Lambda function that will run in a VPC in the company's primary AWS account. The Lambda function needs to access files that the company stores in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. The EFS file system is located in a secondary AWS account. As the company adds files to the file system, the solution must scale to meet the demand. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create a new EFS file system in the primary account. Use AWS DataSync to copy the contents of the original EFS file system to the new EFS file system.
o.B: Create a VPC peering connection between the VPCs that are in the primary account and the secondary account.
o.C: Create a second Lambda function in the secondary account that has a mount that is configured for the file system. Use the primary account's Lambda function to invoke the secondary account's Lambda function.
o.D: Move the contents of the file system to a Lambda layer. Configure the Lambda layer's permissions to allow the company's secondary account to use the Lambda layer.

e.why: Lambda can mount an EFS file system in another account when the function's VPC has network connectivity to the EFS mount targets, for example through VPC peering, plus suitable file system policy permissions. Peering has no hourly charge, and EFS scales automatically as files are added, so this is the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Copying to a second EFS with DataSync doubles storage costs and creates ongoing sync work.
others.C: A second Lambda proxying file access doubles invocations, adds latency and complicates file access.
others.D: Lambda layers are limited to 250 MB unzipped, are static, and cannot grow as files are added.

e.tip: Cross-account or cross-VPC EFS access needs network connectivity (peering or Transit Gateway) plus mount target DNS/IP resolution.

q: A financial company needs to handle highly sensitive data. The company will store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs to ensure that the data is encrypted in transit and at rest. The company must manage the encryption keys outside the AWS Cloud. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Encrypt the data in the S3 bucket with server-side encryption (SSE) that uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key.
o.B: Encrypt the data in the S3 bucket with server-side encryption (SSE) that uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key.
o.C: Encrypt the data in the S3 bucket with the default server-side encryption (SSE).
o.D: Encrypt the data at the company's data center before storing the data in the S3 bucket.

e.why: The company must manage keys outside AWS, so client-side encryption in its own data center before upload is required for data at rest. Uploading over HTTPS (TLS), enforced by a bucket policy with aws:SecureTransport, covers encryption in transit. AWS never has the keys.

others.A: A KMS customer managed key is still managed inside AWS KMS (even with imported material), not outside the AWS Cloud.
others.B: AWS managed KMS keys are fully controlled by AWS.
others.C: Default SSE-S3 uses keys owned and managed by S3.

e.tip: Keys must stay outside AWS means client-side encryption (or SSE-C, or an XKS external key store).

q: A company wants to run its payment application on AWS. The application receives payment notifications from mobile devices. Payment notifications require a basic validation before they are sent for further processing. The backend processing application is long running and requires compute and memory to be adjusted. The company does not want to manage the infrastructure. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Integrate the queue with an Amazon EventBridge rule to receive payment notifications from mobile devices. Configure the rule to validate payment notifications and send the notifications to the backend application. Deploy the backend application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) Anywhere. Create a standalone cluster.
o.B: Create an Amazon API Gateway API. Integrate the API with an AWS Step Functions state machine to receive payment notifications from mobile devices. Invoke the state machine to validate payment notifications and send the notifications to the backend application. Deploy the backend application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Configure an EKS cluster with self-managed nodes.
o.C: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Integrate the queue with an Amazon EventBridge rule to receive payment notifications from mobile devices. Configure the rule to validate payment notifications and send the notifications to the backend application. Deploy the backend application on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Configure a Spot Fleet with a default allocation strategy.
o.D: Create an Amazon API Gateway API. Integrate the API with AWS Lambda to receive payment notifications from mobile devices. Invoke a Lambda function to validate payment notifications and send the notifications to the backend application. Deploy the backend application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon ECS with an AWS Fargate launch type.

e.why: API Gateway receives mobile requests, and a Lambda integration does the lightweight validation serverlessly. The long-running backend runs on ECS with Fargate, where task CPU and memory can be adjusted without managing servers. Everything is managed, so operational overhead is lowest.

others.A: EventBridge rules cannot run validation logic, and EKS Anywhere means running your own on-premises Kubernetes infrastructure.
others.B: EKS with self-managed nodes requires managing EC2 worker nodes, and Step Functions is heavier than needed for simple validation.
others.C: Spot Instances can be interrupted and must be managed, which does not suit long-running payment processing, and EventBridge cannot validate.

e.tip: Long-running containers with adjustable CPU and memory and no infrastructure to manage means ECS on Fargate.

q: A solutions architect is designing a user authentication solution for a company. The solution must invoke two-factor authentication for users that log in from inconsistent geographical locations, IP addresses, or devices. The solution must also be able to scale up to accommodate millions of users. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure Amazon Cognito user pools for user authentication. Enable the risk-based adaptive authentication feature with multifactor authentication (MFA).
o.B: Configure Amazon Cognito identity pools for user authentication. Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA).
o.C: Configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users for user authentication. Attach an IAM policy that allows the AllowManageOwnUserMFA action.
o.D: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) authentication for user authentication. Configure the permission sets to require multi-factor authentication (MFA).

e.why: Amazon Cognito user pools scale to millions of users. Their threat protection (advanced security) feature provides risk-based adaptive authentication, which scores each sign-in on signals such as new device, location or IP address and can require MFA only for risky attempts. That matches 'invoke 2FA for inconsistent locations, IPs or devices'.

others.B: Identity pools federate identities into AWS credentials; they do not authenticate users or do adaptive MFA.
others.C: IAM users are for workforce access to AWS, not millions of application users, and there is no risk-based MFA.
others.D: IAM Identity Center is for workforce SSO into AWS accounts and apps, not for customer-scale app authentication with adaptive risk checks.

e.tip: 'Adaptive' or 'risk-based' MFA for app users points to Cognito user pool threat protection.

q: A company has an Amazon S3 data lake. The company needs a solution that transforms the data from the data lake and loads the data into a data warehouse every day. The data warehouse must have massively parallel processing (MPP) capabilities. Data analysts then need to create and train machine learning (ML) models by using SQL commands on the data. The solution must use serverless AWS services wherever possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Run a daily Amazon EMR job to transform the data and load the data into Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon Redshift ML to create and train the ML models.
