o.B: Run a daily Amazon EMR job to transform the data and load the data into Amazon Aurora Serverless. Use Amazon Aurora ML to create and train the ML models.
o.C: Run a daily AWS Glue job to transform the data and load the data into Amazon Redshift Serverless. Use Amazon Redshift ML to create and train the ML models.
o.D: Run a daily AWS Glue job to transform the data and load the data into Amazon Athena tables. Use Amazon Athena ML to create and train the ML models.

e.why: AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service for the daily transform and load. Amazon Redshift Serverless provides an MPP data warehouse without clusters to manage. Redshift ML lets analysts create and train models with SQL CREATE MODEL statements, using SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes. This is the all-serverless combination that meets every requirement.

others.A: EMR and provisioned Redshift both involve managing clusters, which breaks the 'serverless wherever possible' requirement.
others.B: Aurora is an OLTP database, not an MPP warehouse, and Aurora ML calls existing models rather than training them with SQL.
others.D: Athena is a query engine, not a data warehouse you load data into. Athena ML only invokes SageMaker endpoints; it does not train models.

e.tip: SQL-based ML training means Redshift ML. Serverless ETL means Glue.

q: A company runs containers in a Kubernetes environment in the company's local data center. The company wants to use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) and other AWS managed services. Data must remain locally in the company's data center and cannot be stored in any remote site or cloud to maintain compliance. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy AWS Local Zones in the company's data center.
o.B: Use an AWS Snowmobile in the company's data center.
o.C: Install an AWS Outposts rack in the company's data center.
o.D: Install an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized node in the data center.

e.why: AWS Outposts racks bring AWS infrastructure and services, including EKS (local or extended clusters), EC2, EBS and S3 on Outposts, into the customer's own data center. Data stays on premises for compliance while the company uses AWS managed services.

others.A: Local Zones are AWS-operated sites in metro areas, not inside the customer's data center, so data would sit in a remote site.
others.B: Snowmobile was a data transfer truck (now discontinued), not a platform for running EKS.
others.D: Snowball Edge is mainly for data transfer or limited edge compute and does not provide managed EKS for ongoing production use.

e.tip: AWS services in your own data center with data residency on premises means Outposts.

q: A social media company has workloads that collect and process data. The workloads store the data in on-premises NFS storage. The data store cannot scale fast enough to meet the company’s expanding business needs. The company wants to migrate the current data store to AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Set up an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway. Use an Amazon S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to the appropriate storage class.
o.B: Set up an AWS Storage Gateway Amazon S3 File Gateway. Use an Amazon S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to the appropriate storage class.
o.C: Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard-Infrequent Access (Standard-IA) storage class. Activate the infrequent access lifecycle policy.
o.D: Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) One Zone-Infrequent Access (One Zone-IA) storage class. Activate the infrequent access lifecycle policy.

e.why: S3 File Gateway presents NFS (or SMB) shares to existing workloads and stores the files as objects in Amazon S3, which scales without limit. S3 Lifecycle policies can then move older data to cheaper storage classes. Pairing the NFS interface with low-cost S3 storage makes it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Volume Gateway provides iSCSI block volumes, not NFS file shares, and its data is stored as EBS snapshots that S3 Lifecycle policies cannot tier.
others.C: EFS storage costs more per GB than S3, and these options do not address how on-premises workloads would reach EFS.
others.D: EFS One Zone-IA is cheaper than EFS Standard but still costs more than S3 tiers, and it has single-AZ durability risk.

e.tip: On-premises NFS or SMB backed by cheap, scalable S3 storage means S3 File Gateway.

q: A company uses high concurrency AWS Lambda functions to process a constantly increasing number of messages in a message queue during marketing events. The Lambda functions use CPU intensive code to process the messages. The company wants to reduce the compute costs and to maintain service latency for its customers. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure reserved concurrency for the Lambda functions. Decrease the memory allocated to the Lambda functions.
o.B: Configure reserved concurrency for the Lambda functions. Increase the memory according to AWS Compute Optimizer recommendations.
o.C: Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda functions. Decrease the memory allocated to the Lambda functions.
o.D: Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda functions. Increase the memory according to AWS Compute Optimizer recommendations.

e.why: For CPU-intensive Lambda code, more memory also means proportionally more vCPU, so runs are shorter. Billing is memory times duration, so the right-sized memory recommended by Compute Optimizer can lower cost overall. Provisioned concurrency keeps environments initialized to avoid cold starts during events, preserving latency, and its lower per-GB-second duration rate helps when it is highly used.

others.A: Reserved concurrency only caps or guarantees concurrency and can cause throttling, and less memory slows CPU-bound code.
others.B: Reserved concurrency does nothing for cold-start latency and can throttle during growing events.
others.C: Decreasing memory cuts CPU, increasing duration and latency for CPU-bound code.

e.tip: Lambda CPU scales with memory. Provisioned concurrency avoids cold starts, while reserved concurrency limits or guarantees capacity.

q: A company runs its workloads on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The container images that the ECS task definition uses need to be scanned for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs). New container images that are created also need to be scanned. Which solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the workloads?

o.A: Use Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) as a private image repository to store the container images. Specify scan on push filters for the ECR basic scan.
o.B: Store the container images in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Macie to scan the images. Use an S3 Event Notification to initiate a Macie scan for every event with an s3:ObjectCreated:Put event type.
o.C: Deploy the workloads to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) as a private image repository. Specify scan on push filters for the ECR enhanced scan.
o.D: Store the container images in an Amazon S3 bucket that has versioning enabled. Configure an S3 Event Notification for s3:ObjectCreated:* events to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to initiate an Amazon Inspector scan.

e.why: ECS pulls images natively from Amazon ECR, so moving images to ECR needs only a change to the image URI. ECR basic scanning with scan-on-push filters scans new images for CVEs automatically, and existing images can be scanned on demand. This is the fewest changes to the workloads.

others.B: Macie finds sensitive data in S3, not software vulnerabilities, and ECS does not run images from S3.
others.C: Migrating the workloads to EKS is a major change, which breaks the 'fewest changes' requirement.
others.D: Container images are not stored in or run from S3 for ECS, and Inspector does not scan S3 objects as container images.

e.tip: Container CVE scanning means ECR image scanning: basic (Clair/AWS native) or enhanced (Inspector).

q: A company uses an AWS Batch job to run its end-of-day sales process. The company needs a serverless solution that will invoke a third-party reporting application when the AWS Batch job is successful. The reporting application has an HTTP API interface that uses username and password authentication. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to match incoming AWS Batch job SUCCEEDED events. Configure the third-party API as an EventBridge API destination with a username and password. Set the API destination as the EventBridge rule target.
o.B: Configure Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to match incoming AWS Batch job SUCCEEDED events. Configure an AWS Lambda function to invoke the third-party API by using a username and password. Set the Lambda function as the EventBridge rule target.
o.C: Configure an AWS Batch job to publish job SUCCEEDED events to an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure an HTTP proxy integration on the API Gateway REST API to invoke the third-party API by using a username and password.
o.D: Configure an AWS Batch job to publish job SUCCEEDED events to an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure a proxy integration on the API Gateway REST API to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to invoke the third-party API by using a username and password.

e.why: AWS Batch sends job state-change events, including SUCCEEDED, to EventBridge by default. An EventBridge rule can target an API destination, which uses an EventBridge connection storing Basic auth (username and password) in Secrets Manager. It calls the third-party HTTP API serverlessly with no code.

others.B: EventBridge Scheduler runs schedules; it does not match incoming events. A Lambda function also adds code that is not needed.
others.C: Batch jobs do not natively publish events to API Gateway, and this adds unnecessary components.
others.D: This adds API Gateway and Lambda code, and Batch does not publish to API Gateway on its own.

e.tip: Calling an external HTTP API from an event without code means an EventBridge API destination.

q: A company collects and processes data from a vendor. The vendor stores its data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database in the vendor's own AWS account. The company’s VPC does not have an internet gateway, an AWS Direct Connect connection, or an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. The company needs to access the data that is in the vendor database. Which solution will meet this requirement?

o.A: Instruct the vendor to sign up for the AWS Hosted Connection Direct Connect Program. Use VPC peering to connect the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC.
o.B: Configure a client VPN connection between the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC. Use VPC peering to connect the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC.
o.C: Instruct the vendor to create a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Place the NLB in front of the Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Use AWS PrivateLink to integrate the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC.
o.D: Use AWS Transit Gateway to integrate the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC. Use VPC peering to connect the company’s VPC and the vendor's VPC.

e.why: With no internet gateway, VPN or Direct Connect, AWS PrivateLink gives private access across accounts. The vendor puts an NLB in front of the RDS instance (using its IP as a target) and publishes a VPC endpoint service. The company creates an interface endpoint to it, and traffic stays on the AWS network with no route-table or CIDR coupling.

others.A: The Direct Connect hosted connection program is for on-premises connectivity and is irrelevant between two VPCs.
others.B: Client VPN is for individual users connecting to a VPC, not a VPC-to-VPC link.
others.D: Transit Gateway and VPC peering together are redundant, and either one needs route and CIDR coordination with the vendor. PrivateLink exposes only the one service.

e.tip: Expose one service privately to another account or VPC means PrivateLink (an NLB endpoint service).

q: A company wants to set up Amazon Managed Grafana as its visualization tool. The company wants to visualize data from its Amazon RDS database as one data source. The company needs a secure solution that will not expose the data over the internet. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace without a VPC. Create a public endpoint for the RDS database. Configure the public endpoint as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.
o.B: Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace in a VPC. Create a private endpoint for the RDS database. Configure the private endpoint as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.
o.C: Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace without a VPCreate an AWS PrivateLink endpoint to establish a connection between Amazon Managed Grafana and Amazon RDS. Set up Amazon RDS as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.
o.D: Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace in a VPC. Create a public endpoint for the RDS database. Configure the public endpoint as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.

e.why: Amazon Managed Grafana workspaces can be configured with VPC outbound connectivity to reach data sources in private subnets. Connecting to the RDS instance's private endpoint keeps traffic inside the VPC and never exposes the database to the internet.

others.A: A public RDS endpoint exposes the database over the internet.
others.C: RDS databases are not exposed as AWS PrivateLink endpoint services for Grafana to use this way. Grafana needs VPC connectivity to reach a private DB.
others.D: Using a public RDS endpoint again exposes data over the internet, even if the workspace is in a VPC.

e.tip: For private data sources, connect Managed Grafana to the VPC instead of making the database public.

q: A company hosts a data lake on Amazon S3. The data lake ingests data in Apache Parquet format from various data sources. The company uses multiple transformation steps to prepare the ingested data. The steps include filtering of anomalies, normalizing of data to standard date and time values, and generation of aggregates for analyses. The company must store the transformed data in S3 buckets that data analysts access. The company needs a prebuilt solution for data transformation that does not require code. The solution must provide data lineage and data profiling. The company needs to share the data transformation steps with employees throughout the company. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure an AWS Glue Studio visual canvas to transform the data. Share the transformation steps with employees by using AWS Glue jobs.
o.B: Configure Amazon EMR Serverless to transform the data. Share the transformation steps with employees by using EMR Serverless jobs.
o.C: Configure AWS Glue DataBrew to transform the data. Share the transformation steps with employees by using DataBrew recipes.
o.D: Create Amazon Athena tables for the data. Write Athena SQL queries to transform the data. Share the Athena SQL queries with employees.

e.why: AWS Glue DataBrew is a no-code visual data preparation tool with over 250 prebuilt transformations, such as filtering anomalies and normalizing dates. It provides data profiling and data lineage views. Transformation steps are saved as reusable, shareable recipes, with outputs written to S3.

others.A: Glue Studio jobs generate code-based ETL and do not provide DataBrew-style profiling or shareable recipe steps.
others.B: EMR Serverless needs Spark or Hive code and has no built-in profiling or lineage.
others.D: Athena SQL queries require writing code and offer no data profiling or lineage.

e.tip: No-code data preparation with profiling, lineage and recipes means Glue DataBrew.

q: A solutions architect runs a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances that are in individual target groups behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Users can reach the application through a public website. The solutions architect wants to allow engineers to use a development version of the website to access one specific development EC2 instance to test new features for the application. The solutions architect wants to use an Amazon Route 53 hosted zone to give the engineers access to the development instance. The solution must automatically route to the development instance even if the development instance is replaced. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an A Record for the development website that has the value set to the ALB. Create a listener rule on the ALB that forwards requests for the development website to the target group that contains the development instance.
o.B: Recreate the development instance with a public IP address. Create an A Record for the development website that has the value set to the public IP address of the development instance.
o.C: Create an A Record for the development website that has the value set to the ALB. Create a listener rule on the ALB to redirect requests for the development website to the public IP address of the development instance.
o.D: Place all the instances in the same target group. Create an A Record for the development website. Set the value to the ALB. Create a listener rule on the ALB that forwards requests for the development website to the target group.

e.why: A Route 53 alias A record for the development hostname pointing at the ALB, plus a host-header listener rule that forwards that hostname to the dev instance's target group, routes engineers correctly. A replacement instance only needs to be registered in that target group, for example by an Auto Scaling group, so DNS never changes.

others.B: A record pointing at an instance's public IP breaks when the instance is replaced and its IP changes.
others.C: ALB redirect actions go to a hostname or URL, and redirecting to a public IP breaks when the instance is replaced.
others.D: Putting all instances in one target group means the listener rule cannot single out the development instance.

e.tip: Route by hostname to different backends means ALB host-based routing rules to separate target groups.

q: A company runs a container application on a Kubernetes cluster in the company's data center. The application uses Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) to communicate with a message queue. The data center cannot scale fast enough to meet the company’s expanding business needs. The company wants to migrate the workloads to AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Migrate the container application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to retrieve the messages.
o.B: Migrate the container application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon MQ to retrieve the messages.
o.C: Use highly available Amazon EC2 instances to run the application. Use Amazon MQ to retrieve the messages.
o.D: Use AWS Lambda functions to run the application. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to retrieve the messages.

e.why: The app already runs on Kubernetes and uses AMQP. Amazon EKS lets the same manifests run on managed Kubernetes, and Amazon MQ (ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ) supports AMQP natively, so no code changes are needed. Both are managed services, which minimizes operational overhead.

others.A: SQS does not speak AMQP, so the application would have to be rewritten, and moving from Kubernetes to ECS means redoing the deployments.
others.C: Self-managed EC2 instances mean operating servers yourself, which is more overhead than EKS.
others.D: Rewriting to Lambda and SQS needs significant code changes and drops AMQP support.

e.tip: Existing protocols such as AMQP, MQTT, STOMP or JMS mean Amazon MQ. Existing Kubernetes means EKS.

q: An online gaming company hosts its platform on Amazon EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) across multiple AWS Regions. The NLBs can route requests to targets over the internet. The company wants to improve the customer playing experience by reducing end-to-end load time for its global customer base. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region to replace the existing NLBs. Register the existing EC2 instances as targets for the ALBs in each Region.
o.B: Configure Amazon Route 53 to route equally weighted traffic to the NLBs in each Region.
o.C: Create additional NLBs and EC2 instances in other Regions where the company has large customer bases.
o.D: Create a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure the existing NLBs as target endpoints.

e.why: AWS Global Accelerator gives two static anycast IPs that bring players onto the AWS global network at the nearest edge location, then route over AWS's backbone to the closest healthy NLB endpoint in each Region. It cuts latency and jitter for TCP/UDP gaming traffic and supports NLBs as endpoints.

others.A: ALBs are Layer 7 and handle only HTTP/HTTPS, which does not suit game traffic, and swapping load balancers does not reduce global latency.
others.B: Equal weighted routing ignores user location and can send players to far-away Regions.
others.C: More Regions may help some users but is costly and still lacks smart routing to the nearest endpoint.

e.tip: Non-HTTP (TCP/UDP) global performance with static IPs means Global Accelerator. HTTP caching means CloudFront.

q: A company has an on-premises application that uses SFTP to collect financial data from multiple vendors. The company is migrating to the AWS Cloud. The company has created an application that uses Amazon S3 APIs to upload files from vendors. Some vendors run their systems on legacy applications that do not support S3 APIs. The vendors want to continue to use SFTP-based applications to upload data. The company wants to use managed services for the needs of the vendors that use legacy applications. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) instance to replicate data from the storage of the vendors that use legacy applications to Amazon S3. Provide the vendors with the credentials to access the AWS DMS instance.
o.B: Create an AWS Transfer Family endpoint for vendors that use legacy applications.
o.C: Configure an Amazon EC2 instance to run an SFTP server. Instruct the vendors that use legacy applications to use the SFTP server to upload data.
o.D: Configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway for vendors that use legacy applications to upload files to an SMB file share.

e.why: AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed SFTP (also FTPS, FTP, AS2) endpoint that stores uploads directly in Amazon S3. Legacy vendors keep their SFTP clients and the company runs no servers.

others.A: DMS migrates databases; it is not an SFTP upload service for vendors.
others.C: A self-managed EC2 SFTP server needs patching, scaling and HA work, which is more overhead.
others.D: S3 File Gateway exposes SMB or NFS, not SFTP, and needs a gateway appliance.

e.tip: Managed SFTP into S3 or EFS means AWS Transfer Family.

q: A marketing team wants to build a campaign for an upcoming multi-sport event. The team has news reports from the past five years in PDF format. The team needs a solution to extract insights about the content and the sentiment of the news reports. The solution must use Amazon Textract to process the news reports. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Provide the extracted insights to Amazon Athena for analysis. Store the extracted insights and analysis in an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.B: Store the extracted insights in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use Amazon SageMaker to build a sentiment model.
o.C: Provide the extracted insights to Amazon Comprehend for analysis. Save the analysis to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.D: Store the extracted insights in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize and analyze the data.

e.why: Textract extracts the text from the PDF reports. Amazon Comprehend, a managed NLP service, then performs sentiment analysis plus key phrase and entity extraction to give content insights. Results are saved to S3 with no model building, which keeps overhead lowest.

others.A: Athena queries structured data with SQL; it cannot perform sentiment analysis on text.
others.B: Building a custom SageMaker sentiment model adds major overhead when Comprehend does this out of the box.
others.D: QuickSight visualizes data but does not derive sentiment from raw text.

e.tip: Textract to Comprehend is the standard pipeline for document OCR followed by NLP or sentiment.

q: A company's application runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in multiple Availability Zones. The application needs to ingest real-time data from third-party applications. The company needs a data ingestion solution that places the ingested raw data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create Amazon Kinesis data streams for data ingestion. Create Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams to consume the Kinesis data streams. Specify the S3 bucket as the destination of the delivery streams.
o.B: Create database migration tasks in AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Specify replication instances of the EC2 instances as the source endpoints. Specify the S3 bucket as the target endpoint. Set the migration type to migrate existing data and replicate ongoing changes.
o.C: Create and configure AWS DataSync agents on the EC2 instances. Configure DataSync tasks to transfer data from the EC2 instances to the S3 bucket.
o.D: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection to the application for data ingestion. Create Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams to consume direct PUT operations from the application. Specify the S3 bucket as the destination of the delivery streams.

e.why: Kinesis Data Streams ingests real-time data from third-party producers. Amazon Data Firehose, which can use a data stream as its source, buffers the records and delivers them to an S3 bucket with no custom consumers, landing raw data in S3 as required.

others.B: DMS migrates databases and cannot ingest arbitrary real-time application data.
others.C: DataSync moves files between storage systems in batches; it does not ingest real-time streams.
others.D: Direct Connect is a private link to on-premises networks and is irrelevant for third-party application data ingestion.

e.tip: Real-time ingestion landing in S3 means Kinesis Data Streams and/or Firehose. Firehose alone often suffices.

q: A company’s application is receiving data from multiple data sources. The size of the data varies and is expected to increase over time. The current maximum size is 700 KB. The data volume and data size continue to grow as more data sources are added. The company decides to use Amazon DynamoDB as the primary database for the application. A solutions architect needs to identify a solution that handles the large data sizes. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to filter the data that exceeds DynamoDB item size limits. Store the larger data in an Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) database.
o.B: Store the large data as objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. In a DynamoDB table, create an item that has an attribute that points to the S3 URL of the data.
o.C: Split all incoming large data into a collection of items that have the same partition key. Write the data to a DynamoDB table in a single operation by using the BatchWriteItem API operation.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses gzip compression to compress the large objects as they are written to a DynamoDB table.

e.why: DynamoDB items are limited to 400 KB, and the data is already 700 KB and growing. The standard pattern stores the payload in S3, which allows objects up to 50 TB, and keeps a DynamoDB item with metadata and the S3 key or URL. This scales with no custom size-handling logic.

others.A: Running a second database (DocumentDB) and splitting logic across stores adds operational complexity.
others.C: Chunking data across items requires custom reassembly, BatchWriteItem is not atomic, and it is limited to 25 items and 16 MB.
others.D: Compression may not keep growing data under 400 KB, and it adds processing overhead.

e.tip: DynamoDB item limit is 400 KB. For large payloads, store them in S3 and keep a pointer in DynamoDB.

q: A company is migrating a legacy application from an on-premises data center to AWS. The application relies on hundreds of cron jobs that run between 1 and 20 minutes on different recurring schedules throughout the day. The company wants a solution to schedule and run the cron jobs on AWS with minimal refactoring. The solution must support running the cron jobs in response to an event in the future. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a container image for the cron jobs. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to create a recurring schedule. Run the cron job tasks as AWS Lambda functions.
o.B: Create a container image for the cron jobs. Use AWS Batch on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with a scheduling policy to run the cron jobs.
o.C: Create a container image for the cron jobs. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to create a recurring schedule. Run the cron job tasks on AWS Fargate.
o.D: Create a container image for the cron jobs. Create a workflow in AWS Step Functions that uses a Wait state to run the cron jobs at a specified time. Use the RunTask action to run the cron job tasks on AWS Fargate.

e.why: EventBridge Scheduler supports cron, rate and one-time schedules at scale and can launch ECS tasks on Fargate directly. Containerizing the existing cron scripts needs minimal refactoring, and Fargate has no 15-minute limit, so 1-20 minute jobs run reliably. One-time schedules cover running a job at a future time.

others.A: Lambda's 15-minute maximum timeout cannot handle jobs that run up to 20 minutes.
others.B: AWS Batch scheduling policies control fair-share job ordering, not time-based cron triggers.
others.D: Building Step Functions workflows with Wait states for hundreds of cron jobs is cumbersome and costly compared with Scheduler.

e.tip: Jobs over 15 minutes cannot run on Lambda. Use EventBridge Scheduler with ECS on Fargate for containerized cron.

q: A company uses Salesforce. The company needs to load existing data and ongoing data changes from Salesforce to Amazon Redshift for analysis. The company does not want the data to travel over the public internet. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

o.A: Establish a VPN connection from the VPC to Salesforce. Use AWS Glue DataBrew to transfer data.
o.B: Establish an AWS Direct Connect connection from the VPC to Salesforce. Use AWS Glue DataBrew to transfer data.
o.C: Create an AWS PrivateLink connection in the VPC to Salesforce. Use Amazon AppFlow to transfer data.
o.D: Create a VPC peering connection to Salesforce. Use Amazon AppFlow to transfer data.

e.why: Amazon AppFlow is a no-code SaaS integration service with a native Salesforce connector. It supports full and incremental (change) transfers into Redshift. AppFlow can use AWS PrivateLink to Salesforce so data does not travel over the public internet, giving the least development effort.

others.A: You cannot set up a VPN to Salesforce's SaaS platform this way, and DataBrew is a data preparation tool, not a Salesforce ingestion service.
others.B: Direct Connect to Salesforce is not a standard option, and DataBrew still does not handle ongoing Salesforce change ingestion.
others.D: You cannot peer a VPC with Salesforce, because peering works only between AWS VPCs.

e.tip: SaaS (Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk) to AWS with no code means AppFlow.

q: A company recently migrated its application to AWS. The application runs on Amazon EC2 Linux instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The application stores data in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that uses EFS Standard-Infrequent Access storage. The application indexes the company's files. The index is stored in an Amazon RDS database. The company needs to optimize storage costs with some application and services changes. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create an Amazon S3 bucket that uses an Intelligent-Tiering lifecycle policy. Copy all files to the S3 bucket. Update the application to use Amazon S3 API to store and retrieve files.
o.B: Deploy Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file shares. Update the application to use CIFS protocol to store and retrieve files.
o.C: Deploy Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system shares. Update the application to use the new mount point to store and retrieve files.
o.D: Create an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Copy all files to the S3 bucket. Update the application to use Amazon S3 API to store and retrieve files as standard retrievals.

e.why: S3 storage costs much less than EFS, and S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent, infrequent and archive instant access tiers based on usage, with no retrieval fees. The question allows 'some application changes', so switching the app to the S3 API in exchange for the lowest storage cost is acceptable.

others.B: FSx for Windows File Server costs more and needs a protocol change to SMB/CIFS for Linux apps, so it does not save money.
others.C: FSx for OpenZFS uses provisioned capacity and generally costs more than S3 for this use.
others.D: Glacier Flexible Retrieval takes minutes to hours to retrieve files, which is unsuitable for an application that reads files on demand.

e.tip: Unknown or changing access patterns with the lowest cost means S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

q: A robotics company is designing a solution for medical surgery. The robots will use advanced sensors, cameras, and AI algorithms to perceive their environment and to complete surgeries. The company needs a public load balancer in the AWS Cloud that will ensure seamless communication with backend services. The load balancer must be capable of routing traffic based on the query strings to different target groups. The traffic must also be encrypted. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use a Network Load Balancer with a certificate attached from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Use query parameter-based routing.
o.B: Use a Gateway Load Balancer. Import a generated certificate in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Attach the certificate to the load balancer. Use HTTP path-based routing.
o.C: Use an Application Load Balancer with a certificate attached from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Use query parameter-based routing.
o.D: Use a Network Load Balancer. Import a generated certificate in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Attach the certificate to the load balancer. Use query parameter-based routing.

e.why: Only the Application Load Balancer (Layer 7) supports listener rules that route on query string parameters, as well as path, host and headers, to different target groups. An HTTPS listener with an ACM certificate gives free, auto-renewing TLS encryption.

others.A: NLBs work at Layer 4 and cannot inspect or route on query strings.
others.B: Gateway Load Balancers are for inline virtual appliances (GENEVE), do not terminate TLS, and do not do HTTP routing.
others.D: NLBs cannot do query-parameter routing, and ACM is preferred over IAM certificate storage.

e.tip: Any HTTP content-based routing (path, host, header, query string) means ALB.

q: A company has an application that runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The application uses a MySQL database that runs on the same EC2 instance. The company needs a highly available and automatically scalable solution to handle increased traffic. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy the application to EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Create an Amazon Redshift cluster that has multiple MySQL-compatible nodes.
o.B: Deploy the application to EC2 instances that are configured as a target group behind an Application Load Balancer. Create an Amazon RDS for MySQL cluster that has multiple instances.
o.C: Deploy the application to EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Create an Amazon Aurora Serverless MySQL cluster for the database layer.
o.D: Deploy the application to EC2 instances that are configured as a target group behind an Application Load Balancer. Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster that uses the MySQL connector.

e.why: An Auto Scaling group behind an ALB makes the web tier highly available across AZs and lets it scale automatically. Aurora Serverless (v2) is MySQL-compatible, scales database capacity automatically with load, and stores data across 3 AZs with failover. Both tiers become highly available and automatically scalable.

others.A: Redshift is a data warehouse, not a MySQL-compatible OLTP database.
others.B: A static target group without Auto Scaling does not scale automatically, and a provisioned RDS cluster does not auto-scale compute.
others.D: ElastiCache is a cache, not a replacement for the MySQL database, and there is no Auto Scaling for the app tier.

e.tip: 'Automatically scalable' relational DB often means Aurora Serverless v2.

q: A company is planning to migrate data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data must be encrypted at rest within the S3 bucket. The encryption key must be rotated automatically every year. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Migrate the data to the S3 bucket. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). Use the built-in key rotation behavior of SSE-S3 encryption keys.
o.B: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Enable automatic key rotation. Set the S3 bucket's default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket.
o.C: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Set the S3 bucket's default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket. Manually rotate the KMS key every year.
o.D: Use customer key material to encrypt the data. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key without key material. Import the customer key material into the KMS key. Enable automatic key rotation.

e.why: A KMS customer managed key with automatic rotation enabled rotates key material yearly by default (configurable from 90 to 2560 days). Setting it as the bucket's default encryption (SSE-KMS) encrypts all migrated data with no manual rotation work. It also makes the yearly rotation verifiable.

others.A: SSE-S3 keys are fully managed by AWS, and you cannot configure or verify a yearly rotation schedule for them.
others.C: Manual rotation adds operational overhead when automatic rotation is available.
others.D: KMS keys with imported key material do not support automatic rotation, and imported material adds key management work.

e.tip: Automatic yearly rotation you control means a KMS customer managed key with rotation enabled. Imported material cannot auto-rotate.

q: A company is migrating applications from an on-premises Microsoft Active Directory that the company manages to AWS. The company deploys the applications in multiple AWS accounts. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage the accounts centrally. The company's security team needs a single sign-on solution across all the company's AWS accounts. The company must continue to manage users and groups that are in the on-premises Active Directory. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Enterprise Edition Active Directory in AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Configure the Active Directory to be the identity source for AWS IAM Identity Center.
o.B: Enable AWS IAM Identity Center. Configure a two-way forest trust relationship to connect the company's self-managed Active Directory with IAM Identity Center by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory.
o.C: Use AWS Directory Service and create a two-way trust relationship with the company's self-managed Active Directory.
o.D: Deploy an identity provider (IdP) on Amazon EC2. Link the IdP as an identity source within AWS IAM Identity Center.

e.why: IAM Identity Center provides SSO across all accounts in the organization. Using AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the identity source, with a two-way forest trust to the self-managed on-premises AD, lets users and groups stay managed on premises while Identity Center can sync them and authenticate through the trust.

others.A: A standalone Managed Microsoft AD without a trust would require recreating and managing users in AWS instead of on premises.
others.C: A Directory Service trust alone does not provide SSO across AWS accounts without IAM Identity Center.
others.D: Running a self-managed IdP on EC2 adds operational overhead and duplicates what the AD integration already offers.

e.tip: On-premises AD to Identity Center works through AD Connector or Managed Microsoft AD with a two-way trust.

q: A company is planning to deploy its application on an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 cluster. The application will receive large amounts of traffic. The company wants to optimize the storage performance of the cluster as the load on the application increases. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure the cluster to use the Aurora Standard storage configuration.
o.B: Configure the cluster storage type as Provisioned IOPS.
o.C: Configure the cluster storage type as General Purpose.
o.D: Configure the cluster to use the Aurora I/O-Optimized storage configuration.

e.why: Aurora I/O-Optimized removes per-request I/O charges in exchange for higher compute and storage prices. It gives predictable, better price-performance for I/O-heavy, high-traffic workloads, and AWS says it saves money once I/O exceeds about 25% of total Aurora spend. It also supports Serverless v2.

others.A: Aurora Standard charges per I/O request, which becomes expensive under heavy, growing I/O.
others.B: Provisioned IOPS is an RDS/EBS storage type, not an Aurora cluster storage option.
others.C: General Purpose (gp2/gp3) is an RDS/EBS storage type, not an Aurora option.

e.tip: Aurora storage choices are Standard (pay per I/O) or I/O-Optimized (no I/O charges). Choose I/O-Optimized for I/O-heavy workloads.

q: A financial services company that runs on AWS has designed its security controls to meet industry standards. The industry standards include the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS). The company's third-party auditors need proof that the designed controls have been implemented and are functioning correctly. The company has hundreds of AWS accounts in a single organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to monitor the current state of the controls across accounts. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Designate one account as the Amazon Inspector delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. Integrate Inspector with Organizations to discover and scan resources across all AWS accounts. Enable Inspector industry standards for NIST and PCI DSS.
o.B: Designate one account as the Amazon GuardDuty delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. In the designated GuardDuty administrator account, enable GuardDuty to protect all member accounts. Enable GuardDuty industry standards for NIST and PCI DSS.
o.C: Configure an AWS CloudTrail organization trail in the Organizations management account. Designate one account as the compliance account. Enable CloudTrail security standards for NIST and PCI DSS in the compliance account.
o.D: Designate one account as the AWS Security Hub delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. In the designated Security Hub administrator account, enable Security Hub for all member accounts. Enable Security Hub standards for NIST and PCI DSS.

e.why: AWS Security Hub (now Security Hub CSPM) runs automated, continuous control checks against standards including NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 and PCI DSS. With a delegated administrator and Organizations integration, it aggregates compliance status across hundreds of accounts, giving auditors evidence that controls are implemented and working.

others.A: Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities and network exposure; it does not evaluate NIST or PCI DSS control standards.
others.B: GuardDuty is threat detection and has no NIST or PCI DSS compliance standards.
others.C: CloudTrail records API activity and has no security standards to enable.

e.tip: Compliance against standards (CIS, FSBP, NIST, PCI) points to Security Hub. AWS Audit Manager is another audit-evidence option.

q: A company uses an Amazon S3 bucket as its data lake storage platform. The S3 bucket contains a massive amount of data that is accessed randomly by multiple teams and hundreds of applications. The company wants to reduce the S3 storage costs and provide immediate availability for frequently accessed objects. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

o.A: Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects to the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class.
o.B: Store objects in Amazon S3 Glacier. Use S3 Select to provide applications with access to the data.
o.C: Use data from S3 storage class analysis to create S3 Lifecycle rules to automatically transition objects to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class.
o.D: Transition objects to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Create an AWS Lambda function to transition objects to the S3 Standard storage class when they are accessed by an application.

e.why: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves each object between access tiers based on its own access pattern, with millisecond retrieval in the frequent, infrequent and archive instant tiers and no retrieval fees. It suits unpredictable, random access by many apps, and a single Lifecycle rule makes it the most operationally efficient choice.

others.B: Glacier objects need restores before access, so data is not immediately available, and S3 Select is being retired for new customers.
others.C: Standard-IA has retrieval fees and does not move objects back when they get busy, so random hot data costs more.
others.D: A custom Lambda function to move objects back to Standard adds code, overhead and transition costs.

e.tip: Random or unknown access patterns plus cost savings means Intelligent-Tiering.

q: A company has 5 TB of datasets. The datasets consist of 1 million user profiles and 10 million connections. The user profiles have connections as many-to-many relationships. The company needs a performance efficient way to find mutual connections up to five levels. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the datasets. Use Amazon Athena to perform SQL JOIN queries to find connections.
o.B: Use Amazon Neptune to store the datasets with edges and vertices. Query the data to find connections.
o.C: Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the datasets. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize connections.
o.D: Use Amazon RDS to store the datasets with multiple tables. Perform SQL JOIN queries to find connections.

e.why: Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database that stores profiles as vertices and connections as edges. Multi-hop traversals such as mutual connections up to five levels deep run efficiently with Gremlin, openCypher or SPARQL, avoiding the exponential cost of repeated SQL self-joins.

others.A: Athena SQL with five-level self-joins over 10 million relationships would be slow and costly.
others.C: QuickSight visualizes data; it does not run graph traversal queries.
others.D: Relational multi-level JOINs over many-to-many relationships perform poorly as depth increases.

e.tip: Relationships, social networks or 'friends of friends' means Neptune.

q: A company needs a secure connection between its on-premises environment and AWS. This connection does not need high bandwidth and will handle a small amount of traffic. The connection should be set up quickly. What is the MOST cost-effective method to establish this type of connection?

o.A: Implement a client VPN.
o.B: Implement AWS Direct Connect.
o.C: Implement a bastion host on Amazon EC2.
o.D: Implement an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection.

e.why: An AWS Site-to-Site VPN can be configured in minutes over the existing internet connection. It gives an encrypted IPsec tunnel between the on-premises network and a VPC, with low hourly and data charges, which fits low bandwidth, quick setup and lowest cost.

others.A: Client VPN connects individual user devices, not a whole on-premises network, and charges per connection.
others.B: Direct Connect takes weeks to provision and is costly, which is overkill for small traffic volumes.
others.C: A bastion host provides administrative SSH or RDP access, not a network-to-network secure connection.

e.tip: Quick, cheap, low-bandwidth link means Site-to-Site VPN. High bandwidth or consistent performance means Direct Connect.

q: A company has an on-premises SFTP file transfer solution. The company is migrating to the AWS Cloud to scale the file transfer solution and to optimize costs by using Amazon S3. The company's employees will use their credentials for the on-premises Microsoft Active Directory (AD) to access the new solution. The company wants to keep the current authentication and file access mechanisms. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Configure an S3 File Gateway. Create SMB file shares on the file gateway that use the existing Active Directory to authenticate.
o.B: Configure an Auto Scaling group with Amazon EC2 instances to run an SFTP solution. Configure the group to scale up at 60% CPU utilization.
o.C: Create an AWS Transfer Family server with SFTP endpoints. Choose the AWS Directory Service option as the identity provider. Use AD Connector to connect the on-premises Active Directory.
o.D: Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoint. Configure the endpoint to use the AWS Directory Service option as the identity provider to connect to the existing Active Directory.

e.why: AWS Transfer Family provides managed SFTP endpoints backed by S3. Choosing AWS Directory Service as the identity provider, with AD Connector pointing at the on-premises AD, lets employees authenticate with their existing AD credentials over SFTP. No servers or user copies need to be managed.

others.A: S3 File Gateway provides SMB/NFS, not SFTP, so the file access mechanism would change.
others.B: A self-managed SFTP fleet on EC2 brings patching, scaling and integration overhead.
others.D: Transfer Family cannot connect directly to an on-premises AD; it needs an AWS Directory Service directory such as AD Connector or Managed Microsoft AD.

e.tip: Transfer Family identity providers are service-managed, AWS Directory Service (Managed AD or AD Connector), or a custom provider through Lambda or API Gateway.

q: A company is designing an event-driven order processing system. Each order requires multiple validation steps after the order is created. An idempotent AWS Lambda function performs each validation step. Each validation step is independent from the other validation steps. Individual validation steps need only a subset of the order event information. The company wants to ensure that each validation step Lambda function has access to only the information from the order event that the function requires. The components of the order processing system should be loosely coupled to accommodate future business changes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for each validation step. Create a new Lambda function to transform the order data to the format that each validation step requires and to publish the messages to the appropriate SQS queues. Subscribe each validation step Lambda function to its corresponding SQS queue.
o.B: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the validation step Lambda functions to the SNS topic. Use message body filtering to send only the required data to each subscribed Lambda function.
o.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge event bus. Create an event rule for each validation step. Configure the input transformer to send only the required data to each target validation step Lambda function.
o.D: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create a new Lambda function to subscribe to the SQS queue and to transform the order data to the format that each validation step requires. Use the new Lambda function to perform synchronous invocations of the validation step Lambda functions in parallel on separate threads.

e.why: EventBridge rules decouple producers from consumers, and each rule can target one validation Lambda. An input transformer on each target passes only the fields that function needs, enforcing least information. New validation steps are added just by adding rules, which keeps the design loosely coupled.

others.A: A custom transformer Lambda that knows every queue tightly couples the system and adds code.
others.B: SNS message filtering decides whether a subscriber gets a message; it cannot trim the payload, so each function would receive the full order.
others.D: A central Lambda making synchronous parallel calls is tightly coupled and fragile.

e.tip: Reshape or trim the event payload per target means an EventBridge input transformer.

q: A company is migrating a three-tier application to AWS. The application requires a MySQL database. In the past, the application users reported poor application performance when creating new entries. These performance issues were caused by users generating different real-time reports from the application during working hours. Which solution will improve the performance of the application when it is moved to AWS?

o.A: Import the data into an Amazon DynamoDB table with provisioned capacity. Refactor the application to use DynamoDB for reports.
o.B: Create the database on a compute optimized Amazon EC2 instance. Ensure compute resources exceed the on-premises database.
o.C: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster with multiple read replicas. Configure the application to use the reader endpoint for reports.
o.D: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster. Configure the application to use the backup instance of the cluster as an endpoint for the reports.

e.why: Aurora MySQL with Aurora Replicas offloads the heavy real-time reporting reads to replicas through the reader endpoint, which load-balances across them. The writer instance then stays free for inserts, improving write performance. Multi-AZ adds high availability.

others.A: Moving reports to DynamoDB requires a major refactor and duplicating data, and it is poorly suited to ad hoc reporting.
others.B: A bigger self-managed EC2 database keeps reads and writes contending on the same instance.
others.D: A Multi-AZ standby cannot serve reads, and there is no 'backup instance' endpoint for reports.

e.tip: Reporting slows down writes means read replicas and a reader endpoint.

q: A company is expanding a secure on-premises network to the AWS Cloud by using an AWS Direct Connect connection. The on-premises network has no direct internet access. An application that runs on the on-premises network needs to use an Amazon S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create a public virtual interface (VIF). Route the AWS traffic over the public VIF.
o.B: Create a VPC and a NAT gateway. Route the AWS traffic from the on-premises network to the NAT gateway.
o.C: Create a VPC and an Amazon S3 interface endpoint. Route the AWS traffic from the on-premises network to the S3 interface endpoint.
o.D: Create a VPC peering connection between the on-premises network and Direct Connect. Route the AWS traffic over the peering connection.

e.why: An S3 interface endpoint (PrivateLink) in a VPC has private IP addresses that on-premises hosts can reach over a Direct Connect private VIF. Traffic to S3 needs no internet access, and only endpoint hourly and per-GB charges apply.

others.A: A public VIF reaches all AWS public endpoints and advertises public prefixes, which is less suited to a closed network that cannot have internet-style access. It also offers less control than a private endpoint.
others.B: A NAT gateway cannot be used by on-premises traffic through Direct Connect to reach S3 (transitive routing is not supported), and it adds processing charges.
others.D: VPC peering is only between VPCs; you cannot peer an on-premises network with Direct Connect.

e.tip: On premises reaching S3 privately over Direct Connect or VPN means an S3 interface endpoint. Gateway endpoints are not reachable from on premises.

q: A company serves its website by using an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The website does not require a database. The company is expanding, and the company's engineering team deploys the website to a second Region. The company wants to distribute traffic across both Regions to accommodate growth and for disaster recovery purposes. The solution should not serve traffic from a Region in which the website is unhealthy. Which policy or resource should the company use to meet these requirements?

o.A: An Amazon Route 53 simple routing policy
o.B: An Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy
o.C: An Application Load Balancer in one Region with a target group that specifies the EC2 instance IDs from both Regions
o.D: An Application Load Balancer in one Region with a target group that specifies the IP addresses of the EC2 instances from both Regions

e.why: Route 53 multivalue answer routing returns up to eight healthy records chosen at random. Associating Route 53 health checks with each Region's endpoint spreads traffic across both Regions and stops returning an unhealthy Region, meeting both the growth and DR requirements.

others.A: Simple routing does not support health checks, so it could keep sending users to an unhealthy Region.
others.C: An ALB target group cannot register EC2 instance IDs from another Region.
others.D: Cross-Region IP targets would need private connectivity, and a single-Region ALB is itself a single point of failure for DR.

e.tip: Health checks work with failover, weighted, latency, geolocation and multivalue routing, but not simple routing.

q: A company runs its applications on Amazon EC2 instances that are backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). The EC2 instances run the most recent Amazon Linux release. The applications are experiencing availability issues when the company's employees store and retrieve files that are 25 GB or larger. The company needs a solution that does not require the company to transfer files between EC2 instances. The files must be available across many EC2 instances and across multiple Availability Zones. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate all the files to an Amazon S3 bucket. Instruct the employees to access the files from the S3 bucket.
o.B: Take a snapshot of the existing EBS volume. Mount the snapshot as an EBS volume across the EC2 instances. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.
o.C: Mount an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system across all the EC2 instances. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.
o.D: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the EC2 instances. Configure new EC2 instances from the AMI that use an instance store volume. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.

e.why: Amazon EFS is a regional, elastic NFS file system that many Linux EC2 instances across multiple AZs can mount at the same time. Large files stay available everywhere without copying between instances, and EFS scales throughput and capacity automatically.

others.A: Making employees switch to S3 changes how they access files and does not give the EC2 applications a shared file system.
others.B: EBS volumes created from snapshots are separate copies. Multi-Attach is limited to io1/io2 in a single AZ and needs a cluster-aware file system.
others.D: Instance store is ephemeral and local to each instance, so files are neither shared nor durable.

e.tip: Shared file storage across many Linux instances and AZs means EFS. For Windows, use FSx for Windows File Server.

q: A company is running a highly sensitive application on Amazon EC2 backed by an Amazon RDS database. Compliance regulations mandate that all personally identifiable information (PII) be encrypted at rest. Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of changes to the infrastructure?

o.A: Deploy AWS Certificate Manager to generate certificates. Use the certificates to encrypt the database volume.
o.B: Deploy AWS CloudHSM, generate encryption keys, and use the keys to encrypt database volumes.
o.C: Configure SSL encryption using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt database volumes.
o.D: Configure Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) encryption and Amazon RDS encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt instance and database volumes.

e.why: EBS encryption and RDS encryption both use AWS KMS keys to encrypt data at rest, along with snapshots and backups, transparently. Existing unencrypted RDS instances and EBS volumes are encrypted by copying a snapshot with encryption and restoring it. This uses native features, so infrastructure changes are minimal.

others.A: ACM certificates are for TLS in transit and cannot encrypt volumes.
others.B: CloudHSM requires building and managing an HSM cluster and integrating it yourself, which is a big infrastructure change.
others.C: SSL/TLS encrypts data in transit, not at rest.

e.tip: At rest means KMS-based EBS, RDS or S3 encryption. In transit means TLS (ACM).

q: A company runs an AWS Lambda function in private subnets in a VPC. The subnets have a default route to the internet through an Amazon EC2 NAT instance. The Lambda function processes input data and saves its output as an object to Amazon S3. Intermittently, the Lambda function times out while trying to upload the object because of saturated traffic on the NAT instance's network. The company wants to access Amazon S3 without traversing the internet. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Replace the EC2 NAT instance with an AWS managed NAT gateway.
o.B: Increase the size of the EC2 NAT instance in the VPC to a network optimized instance type.
o.C: Provision a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPUpdate the route tables of the subnets accordingly.
o.D: Provision a transit gateway. Place transit gateway attachments in the private subnets where the Lambda function is running.

e.why: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint adds a route-table entry (an S3 prefix list) that sends S3 traffic from the private subnets directly to S3 over the AWS network. Traffic bypasses the saturated NAT instance and the internet, and gateway endpoints have no hourly or data charges.

others.A: A NAT gateway adds bandwidth, but S3 traffic would still go through NAT and out to the public S3 endpoint, with per-GB processing fees.
others.B: A larger NAT instance may ease saturation but still sends S3 traffic through NAT and the internet path.
others.D: A transit gateway connects VPCs and networks; it does not give private access to S3.

e.tip: Private and free S3 or DynamoDB access from a VPC means a gateway endpoint.

q: A news company that has reporters all over the world is hosting its broadcast system on AWS. The reporters send live broadcasts to the broadcast system. The reporters use software on their phones to send live streams through the Real Time Messaging Protocol (RTMP). A solutions architect must design a solution that gives the reporters the ability to send the highest quality streams. The solution must provide accelerated TCP connections back to the broadcast system. What should the solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

o.A: Amazon CloudFront
o.B: AWS Global Accelerator
o.C: AWS Client VPN
o.D: Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Elastic IP addresses

e.why: AWS Global Accelerator routes TCP (and UDP) traffic from the nearest edge location over the AWS global backbone to the regional endpoint, and terminates TCP close to the client. This improves throughput and reliability for RTMP streams sent by reporters worldwide.

others.A: CloudFront is mainly for delivering HTTP(S) content to viewers and does not accelerate RTMP ingest; RTMP distributions were retired.
others.C: Client VPN gives remote network access but does not accelerate connections and adds encryption overhead.
others.D: Elastic IPs give static addresses but no global network acceleration.

e.tip: Accelerate non-HTTP TCP/UDP traffic globally means Global Accelerator.

q: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) to run its self-managed database. The company has 350 TB of data spread across all EBS volumes. The company takes daily EBS snapshots and keeps the snapshots for 1 month. The daily change rate is 5% of the EBS volumes. Because of new regulations, the company needs to keep the monthly snapshots for 7 years. The company needs to change its backup strategy to comply with the new regulations and to ensure that data is available with minimal administrative effort. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier for 1 month. Copy the monthly snapshot to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive with a 7-year retention period.
o.B: Continue with the current EBS snapshot policy. Add a new policy to move the monthly snapshot to Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive with a 7-year retention period.
o.C: Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier for 1 month. Keep the monthly snapshot in the standard tier for 7 years. Use incremental snapshots.
o.D: Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier. Use EBS direct APIs to take snapshots of all the EBS volumes every month. Store the snapshots in an Amazon S3 bucket in the Infrequent Access tier for 7 years.

e.why: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policies can automatically move monthly snapshots to EBS Snapshots Archive and keep them for 7 years. Archive costs about 75% less than standard snapshot storage, with a 90-day minimum and 24-72 hour restores, which suits regulatory retention. Daily snapshots keep their current policy, so administrative effort is minimal.

others.A: EBS snapshots cannot be copied directly into S3 Glacier Deep Archive as an option; this needs custom export tooling.
others.C: Keeping 84 monthly snapshots in the standard tier for 7 years costs far more than the archive tier.
others.D: Building EBS direct API exports to S3 is custom work with high operational overhead.

e.tip: Long-term retention of EBS snapshots means EBS Snapshots Archive through Data Lifecycle Manager or AWS Backup.

q: A company runs an application on several Amazon EC2 instances that store persistent data on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. The company needs to replicate the data to another AWS Region by using an AWS managed service solution. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use the EFS-to-EFS backup solution to replicate the data to an EFS file system in another Region.
o.B: Run a nightly script to copy data from the EFS file system to an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication on the S3 bucket.
o.C: Create a VPC in another Region. Establish a cross-Region VPC peer. Run a nightly rsync to copy data from the original Region to the new Region.
o.D: Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan with a rule that takes a daily backup and replicates it to another Region. Assign the EFS file system resource to the backup plan.

e.why: AWS Backup is a managed service that can schedule daily EFS backups and copy each recovery point to a vault in another Region using a copy rule in the backup plan. It needs no scripts or infrastructure, which makes it a cost-effective managed cross-Region solution among the options.

others.A: The EFS-to-EFS backup solution was an older CloudFormation and Lambda solution that has been retired in favour of AWS Backup and EFS replication.
others.B: A nightly script to S3 plus cross-Region replication is custom and not a managed EFS replication approach.
others.C: Cross-Region peering with rsync scripts is self-managed and operationally heavy.

e.tip: Native EFS Replication now also copies a file system to another Region continuously. Among these options, AWS Backup is the managed answer.

q: An ecommerce company is migrating its on-premises workload to the AWS Cloud. The workload currently consists of a web application and a backend Microsoft SQL database for storage. The company expects a high volume of customers during a promotional event. The new infrastructure in the AWS Cloud must be highly available and scalable. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

o.A: Migrate the web application to two Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server with read replicas in both Availability Zones.
o.B: Migrate the web application to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to two EC2 instances across separate AWS Regions with database replication.
o.C: Migrate the web application to Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ deployment.
o.D: Migrate the web application to three Amazon EC2 instances across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to three EC2 instances across three Availability Zones.

e.why: An Auto Scaling group of web EC2 instances across two AZs behind an ALB scales with promotional demand and is highly available. Amazon RDS for SQL Server with Multi-AZ gives a managed database with automatic synchronous standby failover. Both tiers use managed features, so administrative overhead is lowest.

others.A: Two fixed instances without Auto Scaling cannot scale for the event, and read replicas do not give automatic write failover.
others.B: Self-managed SQL Server on EC2 across Regions with replication means heavy database administration.
others.D: Fixed instance counts do not scale, and self-managed databases on EC2 add overhead.

e.tip: HA plus scalable plus least admin means ASG with ALB for the app and RDS Multi-AZ for the database.

q: A company has an on-premises business application that generates hundreds of files each day. These files are stored on an SMB file share and require a low-latency connection to the application servers. A new company policy states all application-generated files must be copied to AWS. There is already a VPN connection to AWS. The application development team does not have time to make the necessary code modifications to move the application to AWS. Which service should a solutions architect recommend to allow the application to copy files to AWS?

o.A: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
o.B: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
o.C: AWS Snowball
o.D: AWS Storage Gateway

e.why: AWS Storage Gateway, using S3 File Gateway, presents an on-premises SMB share backed by Amazon S3 and caches data locally for low-latency access. The application keeps writing to an SMB share with no code changes, while files are copied to AWS over the existing VPN.

others.A: EFS is NFS for Linux and is hosted in AWS, so it neither provides an on-premises low-latency SMB share nor avoids changes.
others.B: FSx for Windows lives in AWS; on-premises servers would reach it over the VPN with higher latency, unless an FSx File Gateway were added.
others.C: Snowball is for one-time offline bulk transfers, not continuous daily file copies.

e.tip: On premises keeps using SMB or NFS while data lands in AWS means Storage Gateway (S3 or FSx File Gateway).

q: A company has 15 employees. The company stores employee start dates in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants to send an email message to each employee on the day of the employee's work anniversary. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Create a script that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Use a cron job to run this script every day on an Amazon EC2 instance.
o.B: Create a script that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Use a cron job to run this script every day on an Amazon EC2 instance.
o.C: Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Schedule this Lambda function to run every day.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Schedule this Lambda function to run every day.

e.why: A Lambda function scheduled daily by EventBridge Scheduler or a rule can scan the small 15-item table and publish emails through SNS. It is serverless and costs almost nothing, with no servers or cron hosts to manage, which gives the most operational efficiency.

others.A: An EC2 instance running cron must be patched and kept running all the time, which is more overhead for a tiny daily task.
others.B: SQS cannot send emails, and an EC2 cron host adds overhead.
others.D: SQS is a queue and cannot deliver email to employees.

e.tip: Simple scheduled tasks mean an EventBridge schedule plus Lambda. Email notification means SNS (or SES for custom emails).

q: A company’s application is running on Amazon EC2 instances within an Auto Scaling group behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. Based on the application's history, the company anticipates a spike in traffic during a holiday each year. A solutions architect must design a strategy to ensure that the Auto Scaling group proactively increases capacity to minimize any performance impact on application users. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to scale up the EC2 instances when CPU utilization exceeds 90%.
o.B: Create a recurring scheduled action to scale up the Auto Scaling group before the expected period of peak demand.
o.C: Increase the minimum and maximum number of EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group during the peak demand period.
o.D: Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to send alerts when there are autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH events.

e.why: The spike happens at a known date each year, so an Auto Scaling scheduled action, recurring through a cron expression, can raise desired, minimum and maximum capacity ahead of the holiday. Capacity is ready before users arrive, which is proactive rather than reactive scaling.

others.A: A CPU alarm at 90% is reactive; it scales only after performance has already degraded.
others.C: Manually changing min and max is not automated and risks being forgotten. A scheduled action does this automatically.
others.D: SNS notifications on launches only send alerts; they do not add capacity.

e.tip: Known future peaks mean scheduled scaling. Recurring patterns learned from history can also use predictive scaling.

q: A company uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases for its data tier. The company must implement password rotation for the databases. Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager. Enable automatic rotation on the secret.
o.B: Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Enable automatic rotation on the parameter.
o.C: Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Write an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password.
o.D: Store the password in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable automatic rotation on the AWS KMS key.

e.why: AWS Secrets Manager has built-in managed rotation for Amazon RDS PostgreSQL. You can turn on rotation, or let RDS manage the master user password in Secrets Manager, and it updates both the secret and the database password on a schedule with no custom code.

others.B: Parameter Store has no built-in automatic rotation for parameters.
others.C: Writing and maintaining your own rotation Lambda function is more operational overhead.
others.D: KMS key rotation rotates encryption key material, not database passwords, and KMS does not store passwords.

e.tip: Automatic database credential rotation means Secrets Manager.

q: A company runs its application on Oracle Database Enterprise Edition. The company needs to migrate the application and the database to AWS. The company can use the Bring Your Own License (BYOL) model while migrating to AWS. The application uses third-party database features that require privileged access. A solutions architect must design a solution for the database migration. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Oracle by using native tools. Replace the third-party features with AWS Lambda.
o.B: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle by using native tools. Customize the new database settings to support the third-party features.
o.C: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Customize the new database settings to support the third-party features.
o.D: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Rewrite the application code to remove the dependency on third-party features.

e.why: Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle is a managed database that gives privileged (OS and database) access, so third-party features that need elevated access can be installed and configured. It supports BYOL for Enterprise Edition, so it keeps managed benefits while meeting the privileged-access requirement cost-effectively.

others.A: Standard RDS for Oracle does not allow privileged OS access, and replacing the features with Lambda would mean a rewrite.
others.C: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and cannot host an Oracle application or its third-party features.
others.D: Migrating to PostgreSQL and rewriting code costs significant effort and removes needed features.

e.tip: Managed Oracle or SQL Server with OS or privileged access means RDS Custom.

q: A large international university has deployed all of its compute services in the AWS Cloud. These services include Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS, and Amazon DynamoDB.
