The university currently relies on many custom scripts to back up its infrastructure. However, the university wants to centralize management and automate data backups as much as possible by using AWS native options. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use third-party backup software with an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway virtual tape library.
o.B: Use AWS Backup to configure and monitor all backups for the services in use.
o.C: Use AWS Config to set lifecycle management to take snapshots of all data sources on a schedule.
o.D: Use AWS Systems Manager State Manager to manage the configuration and monitoring of backup tasks.

e.why: AWS Backup is the native, centralized service for policy-based backup plans across EC2, EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS and more. It schedules, retains, monitors and reports on backups from one console and replaces the custom scripts.

others.A: Third-party software plus a tape gateway is not AWS native centralization and adds licences and complexity.
others.C: AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance; it does not take snapshots or manage backups.
others.D: State Manager enforces instance configuration; it is not a backup service for RDS or DynamoDB.

e.tip: Centralize or automate backups across AWS services means AWS Backup (with Organizations backup policies for many accounts).

q: A company wants to build a map of its IT infrastructure to identify and enforce policies on resources that pose security risks. The company's security team must be able to query data in the IT infrastructure map and quickly identify security risks. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon RDS to store the data. Use SQL to query the data to identify security risks.
o.B: Use Amazon Neptune to store the data. Use SPARQL to query the data to identify security risks.
o.C: Use Amazon Redshift to store the data. Use SQL to query the data to identify security risks.
o.D: Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the data. Use PartiQL to query the data to identify security risks.

e.why: An IT infrastructure map is a highly connected graph of resources and their relationships. Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database that stores this as vertices and edges and supports graph queries (SPARQL, Gremlin or openCypher). Security teams can quickly traverse relationships, such as which resources expose a risky path, with little operational overhead.

others.A: Relational SQL with many joins is cumbersome and slow for traversing complex relationships.
others.C: Redshift is an analytics warehouse, not suited to relationship traversal queries.
others.D: DynamoDB PartiQL works on key-value data and does not support graph traversal.

e.tip: Relationships between entities (networks, fraud, knowledge graphs, infrastructure maps) mean Neptune.

q: A large company wants to provide its globally located developers separate, limited size, managed PostgreSQL databases for development purposes. The databases will be low volume. The developers need the databases only when they are actively working. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Give the developers the ability to launch separate Amazon Aurora instances. Set up a process to shut down Aurora instances at the end of the workday and to start Aurora instances at the beginning of the next workday.
o.B: Develop an AWS Service Catalog product that enforces size restrictions for launching Amazon Aurora instances. Give the developers access to launch the product when they need a development database.
o.C: Create an Amazon Aurora Serverless cluster. Develop an AWS Service Catalog product to launch databases in the cluster with the default capacity settings. Grant the developers access to the product.
o.D: Monitor AWS Trusted Advisor checks for idle Amazon RDS databases. Create a process to terminate identified idle RDS databases.

e.why: Aurora Serverless (v2 can scale down to 0 ACUs with auto-pause) automatically scales capacity to low developer usage and pauses or shrinks when idle, so you pay only while developers work. A Service Catalog product lets developers self-provision governed, size-limited databases.

others.A: Scripting start and stop of provisioned Aurora instances is operational work and does not match irregular working times across time zones.
others.B: Provisioned Aurora instances bill while running even when idle, which is less cost-effective than serverless.
others.D: Terminating idle databases destroys developers' data and is reactive, not a provisioning solution.

e.tip: Intermittent, unpredictable, low-volume database use means Aurora Serverless v2 (scale to zero).

q: A company is building a web application that serves a content management system. The content management system runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Users are constantly adding and updating files, blogs, and other website assets in the content management system. A solutions architect must implement a solution in which all the EC2 instances share up-to-date website content with the least possible lag time. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Update the EC2 user data in the Auto Scaling group lifecycle policy to copy the website assets from the EC2 instance that was launched most recently. Configure the ALB to make changes to the website assets only in the newest EC2 instance.
o.B: Copy the website assets to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Configure each EC2 instance to mount the EFS file system locally. Configure the website hosting application to reference the website assets that are stored in the EFS file system.
o.C: Copy the website assets to an Amazon S3 bucket. Ensure that each EC2 instance downloads the website assets from the S3 bucket to the attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Run the S3 sync command once each hour to keep files up to date.
o.D: Restore an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshot with the website assets. Attach the EBS snapshot as a secondary EBS volume when a new EC2 instance is launched. Configure the website hosting application to reference the website assets that are stored in the secondary EBS volume.

e.why: Amazon EFS is a shared NFS file system that all instances in the Auto Scaling group across AZs mount at the same time. Any file a user adds or updates is visible to every instance right away, giving the least lag with no syncing.

others.A: Copying assets from the newest instance via user data is fragile, and ALBs cannot direct writes to a specific instance this way.
others.C: An hourly S3 sync means up to an hour of stale content and extra complexity.
others.D: EBS volumes restored from snapshots are point-in-time copies that do not stay in sync.

e.tip: Shared, always up-to-date content for many web servers means EFS.

q: A company's web application consists of multiple Amazon EC2 instances that run behind an Application Load Balancer in a VPC. An Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance contains the data. The company needs the ability to automatically detect and respond to suspicious or unexpected behavior in its AWS environment. The company already has added AWS WAF to its architecture. What should a solutions architect do next to protect against threats?

o.A: Use Amazon GuardDuty to perform threat detection. Configure Amazon EventBridge to filter for GuardDuty findings and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to adjust the AWS WAF rules.
o.B: Use AWS Firewall Manager to perform threat detection. Configure Amazon EventBridge to filter for Firewall Manager findings and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to adjust the AWS WAF web ACL.
o.C: Use Amazon Inspector to perform threat detection and to update the AWS WAF rules. Create a VPC network ACL to limit access to the web application.
o.D: Use Amazon Macie to perform threat detection and to update the AWS WAF rules. Create a VPC network ACL to limit access to the web application.

e.why: Amazon GuardDuty continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs and other sources to detect suspicious behaviour. Its findings go to EventBridge, where a rule can invoke Lambda to update AWS WAF rules or IP sets automatically, for example to block malicious IPs. This covers automatic detection and response.

others.B: Firewall Manager centrally manages firewall policies; it does not detect threats or produce threat findings.
others.C: Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, not runtime suspicious behaviour, and it does not update WAF rules.
others.D: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 and is not a general threat detection service.

e.tip: Suspicious or unexpected behaviour means GuardDuty. Automated response means EventBridge plus Lambda.

q: A company is planning to run a group of Amazon EC2 instances that connect to an Amazon Aurora database. The company has built an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the EC2 instances and the Aurora DB cluster. The company wants to allow the instances to authenticate to the database in a secure way. The company does not want to maintain static database credentials. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

o.A: Create a database user with a user name and password. Add parameters for the database user name and password to the CloudFormation template. Pass the parameters to the EC2 instances when the instances are launched.
o.B: Create a database user with a user name and password. Store the user name and password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the EC2 instances to retrieve the database credentials from Parameter Store.
o.C: Configure the DB cluster to use IAM database authentication. Create a database user to use with IAM authentication. Associate a role with the EC2 instances to allow applications on the instances to access the database.
o.D: Configure the DB cluster to use IAM database authentication with an IAM user. Create a database user that has a name that matches the IAM user. Associate the IAM user with the EC2 instances to allow applications on the instances to access the database.

e.why: IAM database authentication for Aurora lets applications use short-lived authentication tokens (valid 15 minutes) generated with the EC2 instance role's credentials instead of static passwords. You enable it on the cluster, create a DB user with the IAM plugin, and grant rds-db:connect to the role. There are no secrets to store or rotate.

others.A: Passing static credentials as CloudFormation parameters keeps long-lived passwords around, which the requirement prohibits.
others.B: Parameter Store still holds static credentials that must be maintained and rotated.
others.D: IAM users cannot be associated with EC2 instances, and their long-term access keys are less secure than roles.

e.tip: No static DB credentials for EC2 or Lambda means IAM database authentication through an instance role.

q: A company wants to configure its Amazon CloudFront distribution to use SSL/TLS certificates. The company does not want to use the default domain name for the distribution. Instead, the company wants to use a different domain name for the distribution. Which solution will deploy the certificate without incurring any additional costs?

o.A: Request an Amazon issued private certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.
o.B: Request an Amazon issued private certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-west-1 Region.
o.C: Request an Amazon issued public certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.
o.D: Request an Amazon issued public certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-west-1 Region.

e.why: CloudFront requires ACM certificates to be in us-east-1 (N. Virginia). ACM public certificates are free and auto-renew, so requesting a public certificate in us-east-1 for the custom domain enables HTTPS on the distribution at no extra cost.

others.A: Private certificates need AWS Private CA, which is paid, and are not trusted by public browsers.
others.B: Private certificates cost money, and CloudFront cannot use certificates from us-west-1.
others.D: CloudFront only uses ACM certificates from us-east-1.

e.tip: CloudFront certificates must be in us-east-1. Regional ALB certificates must be in the ALB's Region.

q: A company creates operations data and stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. For the company's annual audit, an external consultant needs to access an annual report that is stored in the S3 bucket. The external consultant needs to access the report for 7 days. The company must implement a solution to allow the external consultant access to only the report. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Create a new S3 bucket that is configured to host a public static website. Migrate the operations data to the new S3 bucket. Share the S3 website URL with the external consultant.
o.B: Enable public access to the S3 bucket for 7 days. Remove access to the S3 bucket when the external consultant completes the audit.
o.C: Create a new IAM user that has access to the report in the S3 bucket. Provide the access keys to the external consultant. Revoke the access keys after 7 days.
o.D: Generate a presigned URL that has the required access to the location of the report on the S3 bucket. Share the presigned URL with the external consultant.

e.why: An S3 presigned URL grants temporary access to one specific object using the signer's permissions. With SigV4 it can be valid for up to 7 days when signed with IAM user credentials. The consultant gets exactly the report for the required period, with no IAM users or bucket policy changes to manage.

others.A: A public static website exposes the operations data to anyone, and migrating data is unnecessary work.
others.B: Making the bucket public exposes all data, not only the report, and it is insecure.
others.C: Creating and later revoking an IAM user with access keys is more overhead and risk than a presigned URL.

e.tip: Temporary access to one object for an outsider means a presigned URL (maximum 7 days with IAM user credentials; shorter with role credentials).

q: A company plans to run a high performance computing (HPC) workload on Amazon EC2 Instances. The workload requires low-latency network performance and high network throughput with tightly coupled node-to-node communication. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure the EC2 instances to be part of a cluster placement group.
o.B: Launch the EC2 instances with Dedicated Instance tenancy.
o.C: Launch the EC2 instances as Spot Instances.
o.D: Configure an On-Demand Capacity Reservation when the EC2 instances are launched.

e.why: A cluster placement group packs instances close together inside one Availability Zone on a low-latency, high-bisection-bandwidth network segment. It gives the lowest latency and highest per-flow throughput for tightly coupled node-to-node HPC traffic, and EFA can be added on top.

others.B: Dedicated Instance tenancy isolates hardware for compliance or licensing; it does not improve network latency.
others.C: Spot Instances lower cost but can be interrupted, and they do not improve networking.
others.D: Capacity Reservations guarantee capacity, not network proximity or performance.

e.tip: Placement groups: cluster for low latency (HPC), spread for isolating critical instances, partition for large distributed systems (HDFS, Cassandra).

q: A company has primary and secondary data centers that are 500 miles (804.7 km) apart and interconnected with high-speed fiber-optic cable. The company needs a highly available and secure network connection between its data centers and a VPC on AWS for a mission-critical workload. A solutions architect must choose a connection solution that provides maximum resiliency. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Two AWS Direct Connect connections from the primary data center terminating at two Direct Connect locations on two separate devices
o.B: A single AWS Direct Connect connection from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at one Direct Connect location on the same device
o.C: Two AWS Direct Connect connections from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at two Direct Connect locations on two separate devices
o.D: A single AWS Direct Connect connection from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at one Direct Connect location on two separate devices

e.why: AWS's maximum resiliency model for critical workloads uses separate connections terminating on separate devices in more than one Direct Connect location, with redundancy at each site. Two connections from each data center to two locations on separate devices survive the loss of a device, a location or an entire data center.

others.A: All connections come from the primary data center only, so losing that site loses all connectivity.
others.B: A single location on the same device is a single point of failure.
others.D: A single Direct Connect location is still a single point of failure if that location goes down.

e.tip: Direct Connect resiliency levels: development (1 location), high (2 locations, 1 connection each), maximum (2 locations, 2 connections each on separate devices).

q: A company runs several Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances that have high utilization. The RDS DB instances run in member accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company's finance team has access to the organization's management account and member accounts. The finance team wants to find ways to optimize costs by using AWS Trusted Advisor. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations in the management account.
o.B: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations in the member accounts where the RDS DB instances are running.
o.C: Review the Trusted Advisor checks for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
o.D: Review the Trusted Advisor checks for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.
o.E: Review the Trusted Advisor checks for compute optimization. Crosscheck the results by using AWS Compute Optimizer.

e.why: In Organizations, Trusted Advisor's organizational view in the management account aggregates check results from all member accounts, so the finance team can review everything centrally. The databases are On-Demand and highly utilized, so the Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization check shows savings from buying RIs.

others.B: Checking each member account separately works but is less efficient than the aggregated management-account view.
others.D: The instances are highly utilized, so the Idle DB Instances check will not find savings.
others.E: Compute Optimizer focuses on EC2, EBS, Lambda and similar resources. For heavily used On-Demand RDS, the RI purchase recommendation is the relevant cost lever.

e.tip: Steady, high-utilization On-Demand usage means buy Reserved Instances or Savings Plans.

q: A solutions architect is creating an application. The application will run on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets across multiple Availability Zones in a VPC. The EC2 instances will frequently access large files that contain confidential information. These files are stored in Amazon S3 buckets for processing. The solutions architect must optimize the network architecture to minimize data transfer costs. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. In the route tables for the private subnets, add an entry for the gateway endpoint.
o.B: Create a single NAT gateway in a public subnet. In the route tables for the private subnets, add a default route that points to the NAT gateway.
o.C: Create an AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPIn the route tables for the private subnets, add an entry for the interface endpoint.
o.D: Create one NAT gateway for each Availability Zone in public subnets. In each of the route tables for the private subnets, add a default route that points to the NAT gateway in the same Availability Zone.

e.why: An S3 gateway endpoint lets private-subnet instances reach S3 through a route-table entry, with no hourly or per-GB endpoint charges, and the traffic stays on the AWS network. This minimizes data transfer cost for frequent large-file access and keeps confidential data off the internet.

others.B: A NAT gateway charges per GB processed, which is expensive for large files, and one NAT gateway is a single AZ point of failure.
others.C: Interface endpoints charge hourly and per GB, and they use DNS rather than route-table entries.
others.D: NAT gateways in every AZ multiply the hourly and processing costs.

e.tip: S3 gateway endpoint is free. S3 interface endpoint is paid and is needed for on-premises or cross-Region access.

q: A company wants to relocate its on-premises MySQL database to AWS. The database accepts regular imports from a client-facing application, which causes a high volume of write operations. The company is concerned that the amount of traffic might be causing performance issues within the application. How should a solutions architect design the architecture on AWS?

o.A: Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with Provisioned IOPS SSD storage. Monitor write operation metrics by using Amazon CloudWatch. Adjust the provisioned IOPS if necessary.
o.B: Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with General Purpose SSD storage. Place an Amazon ElastiCache cluster in front of the DB instance. Configure the application to query ElastiCache instead.
o.C: Provision an Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) instance with a memory optimized instance type. Monitor Amazon CloudWatch for performance-related issues. Change the instance class if necessary.
o.D: Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system in General Purpose performance mode. Monitor Amazon CloudWatch for IOPS bottlenecks. Change to Provisioned Throughput performance mode if necessary.

e.why: Amazon RDS for MySQL with Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) delivers consistent, high write IOPS for heavy import traffic. CloudWatch metrics such as WriteIOPS and WriteLatency show performance, and the provisioned IOPS can be raised when needed without downtime.

others.B: ElastiCache speeds up reads, not heavy writes, and querying the cache does not relieve write pressure.
others.C: DocumentDB is a MongoDB-compatible document store and would require rewriting a MySQL application.
others.D: EFS is a file system, not a relational database for MySQL.

e.tip: Write-heavy relational workloads needing consistent IOPS mean Provisioned IOPS (io1/io2). gp3 lets you set IOPS independently at lower cost.

q: A company runs an application in the AWS Cloud that generates sensitive archival data files. The company wants to rearchitect the application's data storage. The company wants to encrypt the data files and to ensure that third parties do not have access to the data before the data is encrypted and sent to AWS. The company has already created an Amazon S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure the S3 bucket to use client-side encryption with an Amazon S3 managed encryption key. Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
o.B: Configure the S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
o.C: Configure the S3 bucket to use dual-layer server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
o.D: Configure the application to use client-side encryption with a key stored in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Configure the application to store the archival files in the S3 bucket.

e.why: Client-side encryption in the application, for example with the AWS Encryption SDK or S3 Encryption Client using a KMS key, encrypts files before they leave the application. Only ciphertext is sent to and stored in S3, so no third party, AWS included, sees plaintext before encryption.

others.A: Client-side encryption with an S3 managed key is not a valid combination; S3 managed keys are used only server-side.
others.B: SSE-KMS encrypts only after the data arrives at S3, so it travels as plaintext (inside TLS) and is handled by AWS before encryption.
others.C: DSSE-KMS is still server-side and encrypts only after S3 receives the data.

e.tip: Encrypted before it reaches AWS means client-side encryption.

q: A company uses Amazon RDS with default backup settings for its database tier. The company needs to make a daily backup of the database to meet regulatory requirements. The company must retain the backups for 30 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Write an AWS Lambda function to create an RDS snapshot every day.
o.B: Modify the RDS database to have a retention period of 30 days for automated backups.
o.C: Use AWS Systems Manager Maintenance Windows to modify the RDS backup retention period.
o.D: Create a manual snapshot every day by using the AWS CLI. Modify the RDS backup retention period.

e.why: RDS automated backups take a daily snapshot plus transaction logs. Their retention can be set from the default 7 days up to 35 days, so changing it to 30 days meets the requirement with a single setting and no scripts.

others.A: A custom Lambda snapshot function needs code and cleanup logic for 30-day retention, which is more overhead.
others.C: Using Maintenance Windows to change retention is unnecessary indirection; you can just modify the setting once.
others.D: Manual daily CLI snapshots are operational toil and are not deleted automatically after 30 days.

e.tip: RDS automated backup retention ranges from 0 to 35 days. Longer retention needs manual snapshots or AWS Backup.

q: A company that runs its application on AWS uses an Amazon Aurora DB cluster as its database. During peak usage hours when multiple users access and read the data, the monitoring system shows degradation of database performance for the write queries. The company wants to increase the scalability of the application to meet peak usage demands. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create a second Aurora DB cluster. Configure a copy job to replicate the users’ data to the new database. Update the application to use the second database to read the data.
o.B: Create an Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster in front of the existing Aurora DB cluster. Update the application to use the DAX cluster for read-only queries. Write data directly to the Aurora DB cluster.
o.C: Create an Aurora read replica in the existing Aurora DB cluster. Update the application to use the replica endpoint for read-only queries and to use the cluster endpoint for write queries.
o.D: Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Copy the users' data to the Redshift cluster. Update the application to connect to the Redshift cluster and to perform read-only queries on the Redshift cluster.

e.why: Adding an Aurora Replica to the existing cluster shares the same storage volume, so there is no data copying. Routing read-only queries to the reader endpoint and writes to the cluster (writer) endpoint offloads read traffic so write performance recovers. This is the cheapest scaling path.

others.A: A second cluster plus a copy job duplicates storage and adds replication lag and complexity.
others.B: DAX works only with DynamoDB, not Aurora.
others.D: Redshift is for analytics, and copying data there costs more and is unsuitable for application reads.

e.tip: Reads slowing writes in Aurora means add Aurora Replicas and use the reader endpoint.

q: A company's near-real-time streaming application is running on AWS. As the data is ingested, a job runs on the data and takes 30 minutes to complete. The workload frequently experiences high latency due to large amounts of incoming data. A solutions architect needs to design a scalable and serverless solution to enhance performance. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest the data.
o.B: Use AWS Lambda with AWS Step Functions to process the data.
o.C: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to ingest the data.
o.D: Use Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to process the data.
o.E: Use AWS Fargate with Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to process the data.

e.why: Amazon Data Firehose is serverless, scales automatically for streaming ingestion, and buffers the incoming data. ECS on AWS Fargate runs the 30-minute processing job in serverless containers that scale out with load and have no time limit. Together they form a scalable, serverless pipeline.

others.B: Lambda functions are limited to 15 minutes, so a 30-minute job cannot run in one function, and splitting it adds complexity.
others.C: DMS migrates databases and does not ingest streaming application data.
others.D: EC2 Auto Scaling groups are not serverless and require server management.

e.tip: Jobs over 15 minutes in serverless architectures mean Fargate (or AWS Batch on Fargate).

q: A company runs a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. The application needs to write sensitive data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data cannot be sent over the public internet. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Create a route in the VPC route table to the endpoint.
o.B: Create an internal Network Load Balancer that has the S3 bucket as the target.
o.C: Deploy the S3 bucket inside the VPCreate a route in the VPC route table to the bucket.
o.D: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPC and an S3 regional endpoint.

e.why: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint adds a prefix-list route so EC2 traffic to S3 stays on the AWS network and never crosses the public internet. Endpoint and bucket policies can further restrict access, which suits sensitive data.

others.B: NLBs cannot target S3 buckets; targets must be instances, IPs, ALBs or Lambda.
others.C: S3 buckets are regional services and cannot be deployed inside a VPC.
others.D: Direct Connect links on-premises networks to AWS, not a VPC to S3.

e.tip: VPC to S3 privately means a gateway endpoint (or an interface endpoint when on-premises access is needed).

q: A company runs its production workload on Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. A solutions architect needs to analyze the current EBS volume cost and to recommend optimizations. The recommendations need to include estimated monthly saving opportunities. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon Inspector reporting to generate EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
o.B: Use AWS Systems Manager reporting to determine EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
o.C: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics reporting to determine EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
o.D: Use AWS Compute Optimizer to generate EBS volume recommendations for optimization.

e.why: AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes CloudWatch utilization metrics for EBS volumes and recommends better volume types, sizes, IOPS or throughput, for example gp2 to gp3. It also shows the estimated monthly savings opportunity for each recommendation.

others.A: Inspector assesses vulnerabilities, not cost optimization.
others.B: Systems Manager handles operations and inventory but does not produce EBS cost recommendations with savings estimates.
others.C: CloudWatch provides raw metrics only, with no optimization recommendations or savings estimates.

e.tip: Right-sizing recommendations with savings estimates for EC2, EBS, Lambda, ECS on Fargate or RDS come from Compute Optimizer.

q: A global company runs its workloads on AWS. The company's application uses Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions for sensitive data storage and analysis. The company stores millions of objects in multiple S3 buckets daily. The company wants to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon S3 Storage Lens to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
o.B: Enable IAM Access Analyzer for S3 to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
o.C: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.

fixed: The source listed options B, C and D; they have been relabeled A, B and C, so the answer key changes from B to A.

e.why: S3 Storage Lens gives organization-wide visibility into all buckets across accounts and Regions, including data protection metrics that show which buckets do not have versioning enabled.

others.B: IAM Access Analyzer for S3 reports buckets that are shared or public, not their versioning status.
others.C: A Multi-Region Access Point routes requests across buckets in several Regions; it does not report bucket settings.

e.tip: Account-wide or organization-wide S3 usage and configuration metrics point to S3 Storage Lens.

q: A company wants to enhance its ecommerce order-processing application that is deployed on AWS. The application must process each order exactly once without affecting the customer experience during unpredictable traffic surges. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Put all the orders in the SQS queue. Configure an AWS Lambda function as the target to process the orders.
o.B: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) standard topic. Publish all the orders to the SNS standard topic. Configure the application as a notification target.
o.C: Create a flow by using Amazon AppFlow. Send the orders to the flow. Configure an AWS Lambda function as the target to process the orders.
o.D: Configure AWS X-Ray in the application to track the order requests. Configure the application to process the orders by pulling the orders from Amazon CloudWatch.

e.why: SQS FIFO queues provide exactly-once processing through deduplication IDs within a 5-minute window, and they keep order per message group. The queue absorbs unpredictable surges by decoupling order intake from Lambda processing, so customers are not affected.

others.B: SNS standard topics have at-least-once delivery, so duplicates are possible, and there is no buffering for consumers.
others.C: AppFlow is for SaaS data integration, not transactional order queueing.
others.D: X-Ray is for tracing and CloudWatch is for monitoring; neither is an order queue.

e.tip: Exactly-once plus buffering surges means SQS FIFO (high-throughput mode for higher TPS).

q: A company has two AWS accounts: Production and Development. The company needs to push code changes in the Development account to the Production account. In the alpha phase, only two senior developers on the development team need access to the Production account. In the beta phase, more developers will need access to perform testing. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create two policy documents by using the AWS Management Console in each account. Assign the policy to developers who need access.
o.B: Create an IAM role in the Development account. Grant the IAM role access to the Production account. Allow developers to assume the role.
o.C: Create an IAM role in the Production account. Define a trust policy that specifies the Development account. Allow developers to assume the role.
o.D: Create an IAM group in the Production account. Add the group as a principal in a trust policy that specifies the Production account. Add developers to the group.

e.why: The role must live in the account that owns the resources (Production), with a trust policy that trusts the Development account. Development admins then allow only selected developers (two at first, more later) to call sts:AssumeRole on it. Access grows by updating permissions in Development, without creating users in Production.

others.A: Creating separate policies and users in each account duplicates identities and does not give cross-account access.
others.B: A role in Development cannot grant permissions to Production resources; the role must be in the target account.
others.D: IAM groups cannot be principals in a trust policy.

e.tip: Cross-account access means the role sits in the target (resource) account and trusts the source account.

q: A company wants to restrict access to the content of its web application. The company needs to protect the content by using authorization techniques that are available on AWS. The company also wants to implement a serverless architecture for authorization and authentication that has low login latency. The solution must integrate with the web application and serve web content globally. The application currently has a small user base, but the company expects the application's user base to increase. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure Amazon Cognito for authentication. Implement Lambda@Edge for authorization. Configure Amazon CloudFront to serve the web application globally.
o.B: Configure AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Implement AWS Lambda for authorization. Use an Application Load Balancer to serve the web application globally.
o.C: Configure Amazon Cognito for authentication. Implement AWS Lambda for authorization. Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to serve the web application globally.
o.D: Configure AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Implement Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to serve the web application globally.

e.why: Amazon Cognito provides serverless, scalable user authentication that issues JWTs. Lambda@Edge runs authorization checks on those tokens at CloudFront edge locations close to users for low latency. CloudFront serves the web application globally, and all three services scale with a growing user base.

others.B: Managed Microsoft AD is not serverless or designed for customer logins, and an ALB is regional, not global delivery.
others.C: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads to S3; it is not a global content delivery or authorization layer.
others.D: Managed Microsoft AD is not serverless customer identity, and Elastic Beanstalk is regional, not global delivery.

e.tip: Global, low-latency authorization at the edge means CloudFront plus Lambda@Edge (or CloudFront Functions) with Cognito tokens.

q: A development team uses multiple AWS accounts for its development, staging, and production environments. Team members have been launching large Amazon EC2 instances that are underutilized. A solutions architect must prevent large instances from being launched in all accounts. How can the solutions architect meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Update the IAM policies to deny the launch of large EC2 instances. Apply the policies to all users.
o.B: Define a resource in AWS Resource Access Manager that prevents the launch of large EC2 instances.
o.C: Create an IAM role in each account that denies the launch of large EC2 instances. Grant the developers IAM group access to the role.
o.D: Create an organization in AWS Organizations in the management account with the default policy. Create a service control policy (SCP) that denies the launch of large EC2 instances, and apply it to the AWS accounts.

e.why: An SCP in AWS Organizations, attached to the accounts or their OU, can deny ec2:RunInstances when the ec2:InstanceType condition matches large types. It applies to every principal in those accounts, including admins, from one central policy, so overhead is lowest.

others.A: Updating IAM policies for every user in every account takes more effort and can be bypassed by admins.
others.B: AWS RAM shares resources; it does not restrict instance launches.
others.C: A deny role is ineffective, because developers can still launch through their own permissions without assuming it.

e.tip: Guardrails across many accounts mean SCPs (with conditions such as ec2:InstanceType or aws:RequestedRegion).

q: A company has migrated a fleet of hundreds of on-premises virtual machines (VMs) to Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run a diverse fleet of Windows Server versions along with several Linux distributions. The company wants a solution that will automate inventory and updates of the operating systems. The company also needs a summary of common vulnerabilities of each instance for regular monthly reviews. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.A: Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to manage all the EC2 instances. Configure AWS Security Hub to produce monthly reports.
o.B: Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to manage all the EC2 instances. Deploy Amazon Inspector, and configure monthly reports.
o.C: Set up AWS Shield Advanced, and configure monthly reports. Deploy AWS Config to automate patch installations on the EC2 instances.
o.D: Set up Amazon GuardDuty in the account to monitor all EC2 instances. Deploy AWS Config to automate patch installations on the EC2 instances.

e.why: Systems Manager Patch Manager and Inventory automate OS updates and software inventory across mixed Windows Server versions and Linux distributions. Amazon Inspector continuously scans EC2 instances for software CVEs, and its findings can be exported as reports, giving each instance's vulnerability summary for monthly reviews.

others.A: Security Hub aggregates findings but does not scan instances for CVEs itself; it depends on Inspector for that.
others.C: Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks, and AWS Config does not install patches.
others.D: GuardDuty detects threats rather than listing vulnerabilities, and Config does not apply patches.

e.tip: Patching means Systems Manager Patch Manager. CVE scanning means Inspector.

q: A company hosts its application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. The application connects to an Amazon DynamoDB table. For disaster recovery (DR) purposes, the company wants to ensure that the application is available from another AWS Region with minimal downtime. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST downtime?

o.A: Create an Auto Scaling group and an ELB in the DR Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.
o.B: Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances, ELBs, and DynamoDB tables to be launched when necessary. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.
o.C: Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances and an ELB to be launched when necessary. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.
o.D: Create an Auto Scaling group and an ELB in the DR Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm with an evaluation period of 10 minutes to invoke an AWS Lambda function that updates Amazon Route 53 to point to the DR Region's ELB.

e.why: A warm standby keeps an Auto Scaling group and ELB already running in the DR Region. DynamoDB global tables replicate data across Regions in about a second, and Route 53 DNS failover with health checks switches traffic automatically. With everything pre-provisioned, downtime is lowest.

others.B: Launching all resources, including DynamoDB tables, from CloudFormation at failover time takes much longer and the data would not be replicated.
others.C: Provisioning EC2 and ELB only at failover time (pilot light) adds minutes of recovery time.
others.D: A 10-minute CloudWatch evaluation plus a Lambda DNS update is slower and more fragile than Route 53 health-check failover.

e.tip: DR strategies from slowest to fastest: backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, multi-site active/active.

q: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. The application needs to store and retrieve data in Amazon S3 buckets. According to regulatory requirements, the data must not travel across the public internet. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Deploy a NAT gateway to access the S3 buckets.
o.B: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway to access the S3 buckets.
o.C: Deploy an S3 interface endpoint to access the S3 buckets.
o.D: Deploy an S3 gateway endpoint to access the S3 buckets.

e.why: An S3 gateway endpoint gives instances in a private subnet private access to S3 over the AWS network through route-table entries, at no additional charge. It is the most cost-effective way to keep the traffic off the public internet.

others.A: A NAT gateway sends traffic to S3's public endpoints and charges hourly and per GB.
others.B: Storage Gateway is for on-premises access to AWS storage, not EC2-to-S3 connectivity.
others.C: An interface endpoint also works privately but costs hourly and per GB, unlike the free gateway endpoint.

e.tip: From inside the VPC the gateway endpoint is the cheapest S3 path. Interface endpoints are for on-premises or cross-Region access.

q: A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 instances that run in a single Availability Zone. The application is accessible by using the transport layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model. The company needs the application architecture to have high availability. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

o.A: Configure new EC2 instances in a different Availability Zone. Use Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to all instances.
o.B: Configure a Network Load Balancer in front of the EC2 instances.
o.C: Configure a Network Load Balancer for TCP traffic to the instances. Configure an Application Load Balancer for HTTP and HTTPS traffic to the instances.
o.D: Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to run application health checks on the instances.
o.E: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm. Configure the alarm to restart EC2 instances that transition to a stopped state.

e.why: The application uses the transport layer (Layer 4, TCP/UDP), so a Network Load Balancer fits it. An Auto Scaling group spanning multiple AZs with health checks replaces failed instances and spreads capacity across AZs. The NLB in front sends traffic only to healthy targets, giving cost-effective high availability.

others.A: Route 53 DNS routing to instances is slower to react to failures and still needs manual instance management, with no self-healing.
others.C: Adding an ALB as well is unnecessary cost; the app is Layer 4 and one NLB is enough.
others.E: Restarting stopped instances in one AZ does not protect against an AZ failure.

e.tip: Layer 4 means NLB. Layer 7 (HTTP) means ALB. High availability means Multi-AZ Auto Scaling with health checks.

q: A company uses Amazon S3 to host its static website. The company wants to add a contact form to the webpage. The contact form will have dynamic server-side components for users to input their name, email address, phone number, and user message. The company expects fewer than 100 site visits each month. The contact form must notify the company by email when a customer fills out the form. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Host the dynamic contact form in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to a third-party email provider.
o.B: Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint that returns the contact form from an AWS Lambda function. Configure another Lambda function on the API Gateway to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
o.C: Host the website by using AWS Amplify Hosting for static content and dynamic content. Use server-side scripting to build the contact form. Configure Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to deliver the message to the company.
o.D: Migrate the website from Amazon S3 to Amazon EC2 instances that run Windows Server. Use Internet Information Services (IIS) for Windows Server to host the webpage. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

e.why: With fewer than 100 visits a month, API Gateway plus Lambda costs effectively nothing (pay per request, mostly within the free tier) and needs no servers. One Lambda function serves or handles the form, and another publishes to an SNS topic with an email subscription, so the company gets an email for each submission. This is the most cost-effective serverless design.

others.A: An ECS service running all the time costs far more than needed for 100 visits a month, and SES does not need a third-party provider.
others.C: SQS is a queue and cannot deliver email notifications, and the Amplify server-side setup adds unnecessary components.
others.D: Windows EC2 with IIS runs all the time and costs much more, and WorkMail is a mailbox service, not a notification mechanism.

e.tip: Very low, sporadic traffic means serverless pay-per-request (API Gateway, Lambda, SNS or SES).

q: A company creates dedicated AWS accounts in AWS Organizations for its business units. Recently, an important notification was sent to the root user email address of a business unit account instead of the assigned account owner. The company wants to ensure that all future notifications can be sent to different employees based on the notification categories of billing, operations, or security. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?

o.A: Configure each AWS account to use a single email address that the company manages. Ensure that all account owners can access the email account to receive notifications. Configure alternate contacts for each AWS account with corresponding distribution lists for the billing team, the security team, and the operations team for each business unit.
o.B: Configure each AWS account to use a different email distribution list for each business unit that the company manages. Configure each distribution list with administrator email addresses that can respond to alerts. Configure alternate contacts for each AWS account with corresponding distribution lists for the billing team, the security team, and the operations team for each business unit.
o.C: Configure each AWS account root user email address to be the individual company managed email address of one person from each business unit. Configure alternate contacts for each AWS account with corresponding distribution lists for the billing team, the security team, and the operations team for each business unit.
o.D: Configure each AWS account root user to use email aliases that go to a centralized mailbox. Configure alternate contacts for each account by using a single business managed email distribution list each for the billing team, the security team, and the operations team.

e.why: Pointing root user emails to company-controlled aliases that land in a centrally secured mailbox means no individual owns root recovery, and important root notices are not missed. Setting AWS alternate contacts for billing, operations and security to dedicated, business-managed distribution lists routes each notification category to the right team, which is the most secure and controlled approach.

others.A: A single shared mailbox that all account owners can access spreads root email access widely, weakening root account security.
others.B: Separate per-business-unit lists that include administrators widen who can receive root password-reset emails and duplicate management.
others.C: Tying a root email to one individual creates a single point of failure and risk if that person leaves.

e.tip: Use alternate contacts (billing, operations, security) for notification routing. Keep root email on a secured, centrally controlled address.

q: A company runs an ecommerce application on AWS. Amazon EC2 instances process purchases and store the purchase details in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. Customers are experiencing application timeouts during times of peak usage. A solutions architect needs to rearchitect the application so that the application can scale to meet peak usage demands. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

o.A: Configure an Auto Scaling group of new EC2 instances to retry the purchases until the processing is complete. Update the applications to connect to the DB cluster by using Amazon RDS Proxy.
o.B: Configure the application to use an Amazon ElastiCache cluster in front of the Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
o.C: Update the application to send the purchase requests to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure an Auto Scaling group of new EC2 instances that read from the SQS queue.
o.D: Configure an AWS Lambda function to retry the ticket purchases until the processing is complete.
o.E: Configure an Amazon AP! Gateway REST API with a usage plan.

e.why: Putting purchase requests on an SQS queue decouples intake from processing, so spikes are buffered instead of timing out. An Auto Scaling group of workers, which can scale on queue depth, processes messages at a sustainable rate. ElastiCache in front of Aurora serves repeated reads such as product data, cutting database load cheaply.

others.A: Retrying purchases from extra instances adds load during peaks. RDS Proxy helps with connection pooling but does not buffer demand.
others.D: A Lambda function that keeps retrying purchases increases pressure on the database instead of smoothing it.
others.E: API Gateway usage plans throttle clients, which rejects customers rather than scaling to meet peak demand.

e.tip: Timeouts at peak usually mean decouple with SQS plus worker scaling, and cache reads.

q: A company that uses AWS Organizations runs 150 applications across 30 different AWS accounts. The company used AWS Cost and Usage Report to create a new report in the management account. The report is delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket that is replicated to a bucket in the data collection account. The company’s senior leadership wants to view a custom dashboard that provides NAT gateway costs each day starting at the beginning of the current month. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Share an Amazon QuickSight dashboard that includes the requested table visual. Configure QuickSight to use AWS DataSync to query the new report.
o.B: Share an Amazon QuickSight dashboard that includes the requested table visual. Configure QuickSight to use Amazon Athena to query the new report.
o.C: Share an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard that includes the requested table visual. Configure CloudWatch to use AWS DataSync to query the new report.
o.D: Share an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard that includes the requested table visual. Configure CloudWatch to use Amazon Athena to query the new report.

e.why: Amazon Athena can query Cost and Usage Report data stored in S3 directly (AWS provides Athena integration for CUR). Amazon QuickSight uses Athena as a data source to build and share a custom dashboard of daily NAT gateway costs month-to-date with senior leadership.

others.A: DataSync is a data transfer service and cannot act as a query engine for QuickSight.
others.C: CloudWatch dashboards do not query CUR files, and DataSync cannot run queries.
others.D: CloudWatch dashboards cannot use Athena to query CUR data for custom cost tables.

e.tip: Custom cost dashboards from CUR mean CUR in S3, queried with Athena, shown in QuickSight (for example the CUDOS dashboards).

q: A company is hosting a high-traffic static website on Amazon S3 with an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has a default TTL of 0 seconds. The company wants to implement caching to improve performance for the website. However, the company also wants to ensure that stale content is not served for more than a few minutes after a deployment. Which combination of caching methods should a solutions architect implement to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Set the CloudFront default TTL to 2 minutes.
o.B: Set a default TTL of 2 minutes on the S3 bucket.
o.C: Add a Cache-Control private directive to the objects in Amazon S3.
o.D: Create an AWS Lambda@Edge function to add an Expires header to HTTP responses. Configure the function to run on viewer response.
o.E: Add a Cache-Control max-age directive of 24 hours to the objects in Amazon S3. On deployment, create a CloudFront invalidation to clear any changed files from edge caches.

e.why: A CloudFront default TTL of 2 minutes caches objects without Cache-Control headers briefly, so content is never more than a few minutes stale. For objects with a long max-age (24 hours), an invalidation on each deployment removes changed files from edge caches immediately. Together these give good cache hit rates without stale content after deployments.

others.B: S3 buckets have no TTL setting; TTLs are set in CloudFront or through object Cache-Control headers.
others.C: Cache-Control: private stops CloudFront from caching, which defeats the performance goal.
others.D: An Expires header added on viewer response affects only browser caching, not CloudFront edge caching, and adds Lambda@Edge cost.

e.tip: For CloudFront freshness, use TTLs or Cache-Control max-age plus invalidations (or versioned file names) on deploy.

q: A company runs its application by using Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Lambda functions. The EC2 instances run in private subnets of a VPC. The Lambda functions need direct network access to the EC2 instances for the application to work. The application will run for 1 year. The number of Lambda functions that the application uses will increase during the 1-year period. The company must minimize costs on all application resources. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan. Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnets that contain the EC2 instances.
o.B: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan. Connect the Lambda functions to new public subnets in the same VPC where the EC2 instances run.
o.C: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnets that contain the EC2 instances.
o.D: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Keep the Lambda functions in the Lambda service VPC.

e.why: A Compute Savings Plan covers EC2 and Lambda (and Fargate) usage, so it discounts both the instances and the growing Lambda usage for the 1-year term. Attaching the Lambda functions to the same VPC private subnets gives them direct private network access to the EC2 instances.

others.A: An EC2 Instance Savings Plan does not cover Lambda, so the growing Lambda costs stay at full price.
others.B: An EC2 Instance Savings Plan does not cover Lambda, and Lambda functions in public subnets do not get public IPs, so there is no benefit.
others.D: Functions in the Lambda service VPC cannot reach private EC2 instances in the customer VPC.

e.tip: Savings Plans: Compute covers EC2, Fargate and Lambda. EC2 Instance covers only EC2 in one family and Region. SageMaker has its own plan.

q: A company has deployed a multi-account strategy on AWS by using AWS Control Tower. The company has provided individual AWS accounts to each of its developers. The company wants to implement controls to limit AWS resource costs that the developers incur. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Instruct each developer to tag all their resources with a tag that has a key of CostCenter and a value of the developer's name. Use the required-tags AWS Config managed rule to check for the tag. Create an AWS Lambda function to terminate resources that do not have the tag. Configure AWS Cost Explorer to send a daily report to each developer to monitor their spending.
o.B: Use AWS Budgets to establish budgets for each developer account. Set up budget alerts for actual and forecast values to notify developers when they exceed or expect to exceed their assigned budget. Use AWS Budgets actions to apply a DenyAll policy to the developer's IAM role to prevent additional resources from being launched when the assigned budget is reached.
o.C: Use AWS Cost Explorer to monitor and report on costs for each developer account. Configure Cost Explorer to send a daily report to each developer to monitor their spending. Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to detect anomalous spending and provide alerts.
o.D: Use AWS Service Catalog to allow developers to launch resources within a limited cost range. Create AWS Lambda functions in each AWS account to stop running resources at the end of each work day. Configure the Lambda functions to resume the resources at the start of each work day.

e.why: AWS Budgets can track each developer account with alerts on actual and forecasted spend. Budget actions can automatically apply an IAM policy, such as DenyAll, or an SCP when the threshold is reached, which enforces the limit with no custom code. This gives the least operational overhead.

others.A: Tagging rules, custom termination Lambda functions and daily reports are complex and depend on developers' cooperation.
others.C: Cost Explorer reports and Anomaly Detection only inform; they do not limit spending.
others.D: Service Catalog plus custom start and stop Lambda functions in every account adds significant overhead and does not cap costs.

e.tip: To enforce a spending limit automatically, use AWS Budgets actions (apply an IAM policy or SCP, or stop EC2/RDS instances).

q: A solutions architect is designing a three-tier web application. The architecture consists of an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a web tier that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. The application tier with the business logic runs on EC2 instances in private subnets. The database tier consists of Microsoft SQL Server that runs on EC2 instances in private subnets. Security is a high priority for the company. Which combination of security group configurations should the solutions architect use? (Choose three.)

o.A: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound HTTPS traffic from the security group for the ALB.
o.B: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow outbound HTTPS traffic to 0.0.0.0/0.
o.C: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound Microsoft SQL Server traffic from the security group for the application tier.
o.D: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow outbound HTTPS traffic and Microsoft SQL Server traffic to the security group for the web tier.
o.E: Configure the security group for the application tier to allow inbound HTTPS traffic from the security group for the web tier.
o.F: Configure the security group for the application tier to allow outbound HTTPS traffic and Microsoft SQL Server traffic to the security group for the web tier.

e.why: Least-privilege chaining uses security group references between tiers. The web tier accepts HTTPS only from the ALB's security group. The app tier accepts HTTPS only from the web tier's security group. The database tier accepts SQL Server traffic (TCP 1433) only from the app tier's security group. Security groups are stateful, so return traffic is allowed automatically.

others.B: Outbound HTTPS from the web tier to 0.0.0.0/0 is overly broad and unnecessary for tier communication.
others.D: The database should never initiate traffic to the web tier; responses are handled by statefulness.
others.F: The app tier needs no outbound connections to the web tier, and SQL traffic should go to the database tier, not the web tier.

e.tip: Reference upstream security group IDs as sources for each tier, and rely on statefulness for return traffic.

q: A company has released a new version of its production application. The company's workload uses Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, AWS Fargate, and Amazon SageMaker. The company wants to cost optimize the workload now that usage is at a steady state. The company wants to cover the most services with the fewest savings plans. Which combination of savings plans will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 and SageMaker.
o.B: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for Amazon EC2, Lambda, and SageMaker.
o.C: Purchase a SageMaker Savings Plan.
o.D: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for Lambda, Fargate, and Amazon EC2.
o.E: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 and Fargate.

e.why: A Compute Savings Plan applies to EC2, Lambda and Fargate in one commitment. SageMaker usage is covered only by a SageMaker Savings Plan. These two plans cover all four services with the fewest plans.

others.A: EC2 Instance Savings Plans cover only EC2 in a specific family and Region, not SageMaker.
others.B: Compute Savings Plans do not cover SageMaker.
others.E: EC2 Instance Savings Plans do not cover Fargate.

e.tip: Compute Savings Plans cover EC2, Fargate and Lambda. SageMaker needs a separate SageMaker Savings Plan.

q: A company uses a Microsoft SQL Server database. The company's applications are connected to the database. The company wants to migrate to an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database with minimal changes to the application code. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to rewrite the SQL queries in the applications.
o.B: Enable Babelfish on Aurora PostgreSQL to run the SQL queries from the applications.
o.C: Migrate the database schema and data by using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
o.D: Use Amazon RDS Proxy to connect the applications to Aurora PostgreSQL.
o.E: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to rewrite the SQL queries in the applications.

e.why: Babelfish for Aurora PostgreSQL understands the SQL Server wire protocol (TDS) and T-SQL, so applications keep their existing queries and drivers with minimal code change. SCT (or the Babelfish Compass assessment) and DMS move the schema and data into Aurora PostgreSQL.

others.A: Rewriting application SQL contradicts the minimal-code-change goal. SCT converts database schema and code, not application query rewriting at scale.
others.D: RDS Proxy pools connections but does not translate T-SQL or the SQL Server protocol.
others.E: DMS migrates data and does not rewrite application SQL queries.

e.tip: SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal app changes means Babelfish.

q: A company plans to rehost an application to Amazon EC2 instances that use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) as the attached storage. A solutions architect must design a solution to ensure that all newly created Amazon EBS volumes are encrypted by default. The solution must also prevent the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure the EC2 account attributes to always encrypt new EBS volumes.
o.B: Use AWS Config. Configure the encrypted-volumes identifier. Apply the default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key.
o.C: Configure AWS Systems Manager to create encrypted copies of the EBS volumes. Reconfigure the EC2 instances to use the encrypted volumes.
o.D: Create a customer managed key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Configure AWS Migration Hub to use the key when the company migrates workloads.

e.why: EBS encryption by default is an account-level, per-Region EC2 setting. Once enabled, every new EBS volume and snapshot copy is encrypted automatically with the default or chosen KMS key, and unencrypted volumes cannot be created. It satisfies both requirements with one setting.

others.B: The AWS Config encrypted-volumes rule only detects unencrypted volumes after creation; it does not prevent or encrypt them.
others.C: Creating encrypted copies with Systems Manager is a reactive manual workflow that does not stop unencrypted creation.
others.D: Migration Hub tracks migrations and does not enforce EBS encryption.

e.tip: EBS encryption by default is set per Region, so enable it in every Region you use. Combine it with SCPs (ec2:Encrypted) for extra enforcement.

q: An ecommerce company wants to collect user clickstream data from the company's website for real-time analysis. The website experiences fluctuating traffic patterns throughout the day. The company needs a scalable solution that can adapt to varying levels of traffic. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use a data stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams in on-demand mode to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Lambda to process the data in real time.
o.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Glue to process the data in real time.
o.C: Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Glue to process the data in real time.
o.D: Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (previously known as Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics) to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Lambda to process the data in real time.

e.why: Kinesis Data Streams in on-demand mode automatically scales shard capacity with fluctuating throughput, so there is no capacity planning. Lambda's Kinesis event source mapping processes records in near real time and scales with the stream, giving a fully elastic clickstream pipeline.

others.B: Firehose buffers data for delivery (seconds to minutes), and Glue is a batch or streaming ETL service, not ideal for this real-time per-event processing.
others.C: Kinesis Video Streams is for video and media streams, not clickstream events.
others.D: Managed Service for Apache Flink processes streams; it is not an ingestion endpoint for capturing data from websites.

e.tip: Unpredictable streaming throughput means Kinesis Data Streams on-demand mode.

q: A global company runs its workloads on AWS. The company's application uses Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions for sensitive data storage and analysis. The company stores millions of objects in multiple S3 buckets daily. The company wants to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Set up an AWS CloudTrail event that has a rule to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
o.B: Use Amazon S3 Storage Lens to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
o.C: Enable IAM Access Analyzer for S3 to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
o.D: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.

e.why: S3 Storage Lens gives organization-wide, multi-Region visibility of S3, including data protection metrics such as the count of buckets with versioning enabled. Drilling down identifies buckets without versioning, with no custom tooling.

others.A: CloudTrail records API events; it cannot list the current versioning state of existing buckets.
others.C: IAM Access Analyzer for S3 reports public or cross-account access, not versioning status.
others.D: Multi-Region Access Points route requests across Regions and do not audit bucket configuration.

e.tip: An AWS Config s3-bucket-versioning-enabled rule (with an aggregator) is another valid way to find these buckets.

q: A company needs to optimize its Amazon S3 storage costs for an application that generates many files that cannot be recreated. Each file is approximately 5 MB and is stored in Amazon S3 Standard storage. The company must store the files for 4 years before the files can be deleted. The files must be immediately accessible. The files are frequently accessed in the first 30 days of object creation, but they are rarely accessed after the first 30 days. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move the files to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval 30 days after object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
o.B: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move the files to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 30 days after object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
o.C: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move the files to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days after object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
o.D: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move the files to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days after object creation. Move the files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval 4 years after object creation.

e.why: After 30 days the files are rarely accessed but must still be retrievable immediately. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval gives millisecond access at about 68% lower storage cost than Standard-IA, and the files are large enough (5 MB) that its 128 KB minimum and 90-day minimum do not matter. An expiration action deletes the files after 4 years.

others.B: One Zone-IA keeps data in a single AZ, which is risky for files that cannot be recreated, and it costs more than Glacier Instant Retrieval for rarely accessed data.
others.C: Standard-IA provides immediate access but costs more per GB than Glacier Instant Retrieval for rarely accessed data.
others.D: Moving files to Glacier Flexible Retrieval at 4 years is wrong, because the files should be deleted then, and Standard-IA costs more in the meantime.

e.tip: Rarely accessed, needs millisecond access, kept for months or years means S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.

q: A company runs its critical storage application in the AWS Cloud. The application uses Amazon S3 in two AWS Regions. The company wants the application to send remote user data to the nearest S3 bucket with no public network congestion. The company also wants the application to fail over with the least amount of management of Amazon S3. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Implement an active-active design between the two Regions. Configure the application to use the regional S3 endpoints closest to the user.
o.B: Use an active-passive configuration with S3 Multi-Region Access Points. Create a global endpoint for each of the Regions.
o.C: Send user data to the regional S3 endpoints closest to the user. Configure an S3 cross-account replication rule to keep the S3 buckets synchronized.
o.D: Set up Amazon S3 to use Multi-Region Access Points in an active-active configuration with a single global endpoint. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication.

e.why: S3 Multi-Region Access Points provide a single global endpoint that routes requests over the AWS global network (through AWS Global Accelerator) to the closest bucket, avoiding public internet congestion. In active-active mode with Cross-Region Replication keeping buckets in sync, failover is automatic and needs very little S3 management.

others.A: Making the application choose Regional endpoints means custom routing and failover logic, and traffic uses the public internet.
others.B: A Multi-Region Access Point has one global endpoint, not one per Region, and active-passive does not send users to the nearest bucket.
others.C: Cross-account replication is not the issue, and Regional endpoints do not avoid internet congestion or give automatic failover.

e.tip: A single global S3 endpoint with routing to the nearest bucket and failover means Multi-Region Access Points plus CRR.

q: A company is migrating a data center from its on-premises location to AWS. The company has several legacy applications that are hosted on individual virtual servers. Changes to the application designs cannot be made. Each individual virtual server currently runs as its own EC2 instance. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the applications are reliable and fault tolerant after migration to AWS. The applications will run on Amazon EC2 instances. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a minimum of one and a maximum of one. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of each application instance. Use the AMI to create EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group Configure an Application Load Balancer in front of the Auto Scaling group.
o.B: Use AWS Backup to create an hourly backup of the EC2 instance that hosts each application. Store the backup in Amazon S3 in a separate Availability Zone. Configure a disaster recovery process to restore the EC2 instance for each application from its most recent backup.
o.C: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of each application instance. Launch two new EC2 instances from the AMI. Place each EC2 instance in a separate Availability Zone. Configure a Network Load Balancer that has the EC2 instances as targets.
o.D: Use AWS Mitigation Hub Refactor Spaces to migrate each application off the EC2 instance. Break down functionality from each application into individual components. Host each application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an AWS Fargate launch type.

e.why: An Auto Scaling group with minimum and maximum of 1, launched from each app's AMI (and spanning multiple AZ subnets), keeps exactly one instance running. It automatically replaces the instance in a healthy AZ if it fails ELB health checks, giving self-healing reliability without changing the legacy apps. This suits apps that cannot run as multiple concurrent instances.

others.B: Hourly backups with manual restores give slow recovery and possible data loss, so they are not fault tolerant.
others.C: Running two active instances may break legacy apps that were not designed for concurrency or shared state, which would require design changes.
others.D: Refactoring into containers violates the 'no design changes' constraint (and the service is Migration Hub Refactor Spaces).

e.tip: An ASG with min = max = 1 is the standard self-healing pattern for single-instance legacy applications.

q: A company wants to isolate its workloads by creating an AWS account for each workload. The company needs a solution that centrally manages networking components for the workloads. The solution also must create accounts with automatic security controls (guardrails). Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS Control Tower to deploy accounts. Create a networking account that has a VPC with private subnets and public subnets. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the subnets with the workload accounts.
o.B: Use AWS Organizations to deploy accounts. Create a networking account that has a VPC with private subnets and public subnets. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the subnets with the workload accounts.
o.C: Use AWS Control Tower to deploy accounts. Deploy a VPC in each workload account. Configure each VPC to route through an inspection VPC by using a transit gateway attachment.
o.D: Use AWS Organizations to deploy accounts. Deploy a VPC in each workload account. Configure each VPC to route through an inspection VPC by using a transit gateway attachment.

e.why: AWS Control Tower Account Factory creates accounts with preventive and detective guardrails automatically.
