A central networking account that owns a VPC and shares its subnets with workload accounts through AWS RAM (VPC sharing) centralizes network management while each workload stays isolated in its own account.

others.B: Plain AWS Organizations account creation does not apply guardrails automatically.
others.C: A VPC in every account plus transit gateway and inspection routing is more networking to manage than sharing central subnets.
others.D: Organizations alone has no automatic guardrails, and per-account VPCs with a transit gateway add overhead.

e.tip: Central networking for many accounts means VPC sharing through RAM. Automatic guardrails mean Control Tower.

q: A company hosts a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website serves static content. Website traffic is increasing. The company wants to minimize the website hosting costs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Move the website to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the S3 bucket.
o.B: Move the website to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon ElastiCache cluster for the S3 bucket.
o.C: Move the website to AWS Amplify. Configure an ALB to resolve to the Amplify website.
o.D: Move the website to AWS Amplify. Configure EC2 instances to cache the website.

e.why: Static content does not need EC2 or an ALB. Hosting it in S3 with CloudFront in front removes server costs, scales automatically, and caches at edge locations. With Origin Access Control and CloudFront's lower egress pricing, costs stay low as traffic grows.

others.B: ElastiCache cannot sit in front of S3 for web serving, and it adds cluster costs.
others.C: An ALB in front of Amplify is unnecessary and adds cost; Amplify already provides hosting and a CDN.
others.D: EC2 caching instances bring back the server costs the company wants to remove.

e.tip: Static website at the lowest cost means S3 plus CloudFront.

q: A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a media application that the company hosts on AWS. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access stored data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

o.A: Create an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol. Connect the application server to the file share.
o.B: Create an AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway. Configure tapes to use Amazon S3. Connect the application server to the Tape Gateway.
o.C: Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
o.D: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Connect the application server to the file system.

e.why: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed native Windows file system with SMB support, Active Directory integration, Multi-AZ options and automatic backups. Application servers connect over SMB with no servers to manage, giving the least administrative overhead.

others.A: Volume Gateway provides iSCSI block volumes, not SMB file shares, and is meant for hybrid on-premises use.
others.B: Tape Gateway provides a virtual tape library for backup software, not shared SMB storage.
others.C: A self-managed Windows file server on EC2 needs patching, backups and HA work.

e.tip: SMB in AWS means FSx for Windows File Server (or FSx for NetApp ONTAP). NFS for Linux means EFS.

q: A company is designing its production application's disaster recovery (DR) strategy. The application is backed by a MySQL database on an Amazon Aurora cluster in the us-east-1 Region. The company has chosen the us-west-1 Region as its DR Region. The company's target recovery point objective (RPO) is 5 minutes and the target recovery time objective (RTO) is 20 minutes. The company wants to minimize configuration changes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Create an Aurora read replica in us-west-1 similar in size to the production application's Aurora MySQL cluster writer instance.
o.B: Convert the Aurora cluster to an Aurora global database. Configure managed failover.
o.C: Create a new Aurora cluster in us-west-1 that has Cross-Region Replication.
o.D: Create a new Aurora cluster in us-west-1. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to sync both clusters.

e.why: Aurora Global Database replicates storage to the secondary Region with typically under 1 second of lag, far inside the 5-minute RPO. A managed planned switchover or failover promotes us-west-1 in minutes, well inside the 20-minute RTO. Converting an existing cluster to a global database needs no application or schema changes, and the global writer endpoint keeps configuration changes minimal.

others.A: A cross-Region Aurora MySQL read replica uses binlog replication with higher lag and requires manual promotion, which is less efficient.
others.C: 'Cross-Region Replication' for a new standalone cluster is effectively binlog replication with manual failover and more configuration.
others.D: DMS-based sync is self-managed, has higher lag and adds operational overhead.

e.tip: Cross-Region Aurora DR with an RPO of seconds and an RTO of about a minute means Aurora Global Database.

q: A company runs a critical data analysis job each week before the first day of the work week. The job requires at least 1 hour to complete the analysis. The job is stateful and cannot tolerate interruptions. The company needs a solution to run the job on AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a container for the job. Schedule the job to run as an AWS Fargate task on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster by using Amazon EventBridge Scheduler.
o.B: Configure the job to run in an AWS Lambda function. Create a scheduled rule in Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function.
o.C: Configure an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 Spot Instances that run Amazon Linux. Configure a crontab entry on the instances to run the analysis.
o.D: Configure an AWS DataSync task to run the job. Configure a cron expression to run the task on a schedule.

e.why: The job is stateful, runs longer than an hour, and cannot be interrupted. A container run as an ECS task on Fargate has no maximum runtime and runs on on-demand capacity, and EventBridge Scheduler can start it on a weekly cron schedule without any servers to manage.

others.B: Lambda functions time out after 15 minutes, so a job of an hour or more cannot run in one.
others.C: Spot Instances can be reclaimed at two minutes' notice, which breaks a stateful job that cannot be interrupted.
others.D: DataSync moves data between storage systems and cannot run analysis code.

e.tip: If a job runs longer than 15 minutes, rule out Lambda. If it cannot be interrupted, rule out Spot.

q: A company runs workloads in the AWS Cloud. The company wants to centrally collect security data to assess security across the entire company and to improve workload protection. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

o.A: Configure a data lake in AWS Lake Formation. Use AWS Glue crawlers to ingest the security data into the data lake.
o.B: Configure an AWS Lambda function to collect the security data in .csv format. Upload the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.C: Configure a data lake in Amazon Security Lake to collect the security data. Upload the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.D: Configure an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance to load the security data into an Amazon RDS cluster.

e.why: Amazon Security Lake automatically collects security data from AWS services and third-party sources, normalizes it to the OCSF format, and stores it in an S3 data lake that it manages, across accounts and Regions. That gives central security analysis with the least development effort.

others.A: Lake Formation with Glue crawlers means building and maintaining your own ingestion pipelines and schema normalization for security logs.
others.B: A custom Lambda collector that writes CSV files is development-heavy and does not normalize the data or cover many sources.
others.D: DMS migrates databases. It does not collect security logs, and RDS is not a security data lake.

e.tip: When a question says to centralize security data in OCSF across the organization, the answer is Security Lake.

q: A company is migrating five on-premises applications to VPCs in the AWS Cloud. Each application is currently deployed in isolated virtual networks on premises and should be deployed similarly in the AWS Cloud. The applications need to reach a shared services VPC. All the applications must be able to communicate with each other. If the migration is successful, the company will repeat the migration process for more than 100 applications. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

o.A: Deploy software VPN tunnels between the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC.
o.B: Deploy VPC peering connections between the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC through the peering connection.
o.C: Deploy an AWS Direct Connect connection between the application VPCs and the shared services VPAdd routes from the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC and the applications VPCs. Add routes from the shared services VPC subnets to the applications VPCs.
o.D: Deploy a transit gateway with associations between the transit gateway and the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets and the application VPCs to the shared services VPC through the transit gateway.

e.why: A transit gateway is a regional hub-and-spoke router. Each VPC attaches once, and route tables control which VPCs can talk to each other and to the shared services VPC. This scales to more than 100 application VPCs without a full mesh of connections, so it has the least administrative overhead.

others.A: Software VPN tunnels between VPCs mean managing many appliances and tunnels, which does not scale.
others.B: VPC peering is not transitive, so the applications would need a full mesh of n(n-1)/2 peering connections to reach each other.
others.C: Direct Connect links on-premises networks to AWS. It does not connect one VPC to another.

e.tip: When many VPCs must reach each other or a shared VPC, choose Transit Gateway.

q: A company wants to use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to run its on-premises application in a hybrid environment. The application currently runs on containers on premises. The company needs a single container solution that can scale in an on-premises, hybrid, or cloud environment. The company must run new application containers in the AWS Cloud and must use a load balancer for HTTP traffic. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Set up an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type for the cloud application containers. Use an Amazon ECS Anywhere external launch type for the on-premises application containers.
o.B: Set up an Application Load Balancer for cloud ECS services.
o.C: Set up a Network Load Balancer for cloud ECS services.
o.D: Set up an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type. Use Fargate for the cloud application containers and the on-premises application containers.
o.E: Set up an ECS cluster that uses the Amazon EC2 launch type for the cloud application containers. Use Amazon ECS Anywhere with an AWS Fargate launch type for the on-premises application containers.

e.why: ECS Anywhere uses the EXTERNAL launch type to register on-premises servers with the same ECS control plane, and Fargate runs the cloud containers. Together they give one container platform across on-premises and cloud. An Application Load Balancer is the layer 7 load balancer meant for HTTP traffic to the cloud ECS services.

others.C: A Network Load Balancer works at layer 4. For HTTP traffic, an ALB is the better choice.
others.D: Fargate runs only in AWS and cannot run containers on premises.
others.E: ECS Anywhere cannot use the Fargate launch type. On-premises capacity must use the EXTERNAL launch type.

e.tip: ECS Anywhere uses the EXTERNAL launch type. Fargate is never available on premises.

q: A company is migrating its workloads to AWS. The company has sensitive and critical data in on-premises relational databases that run on SQL Server instances. The company wants to use the AWS Cloud to increase security and reduce operational overhead for the databases. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate the databases to Amazon EC2 instances. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
o.B: Migrate the databases to a Multi-AZ Amazon RDS for SQL Server DB instance. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
o.C: Migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Macie to ensure data security.
o.D: Migrate the databases to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to ensure data security.

e.why: RDS for SQL Server is managed: AWS handles patching, backups, and failover, which cuts operational overhead. Multi-AZ adds high availability for critical data, and KMS encryption at rest improves security. The engine stays SQL Server, so the relational workload does not need to be redesigned.

others.A: SQL Server on EC2 leaves patching, backups, and high availability with the company, so overhead does not drop.
others.C: S3 with Macie is object storage and data discovery. It cannot replace a relational SQL Server database.
others.D: DynamoDB is NoSQL and would require a rewrite, and CloudWatch Logs does not secure data.

q: A company wants to migrate an application to AWS. The company wants to increase the application's current availability. The company wants to use AWS WAF in the application's architecture. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Auto Scaling group that contains multiple Amazon EC2 instances that host the application across two Availability Zones. Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and set the Auto Scaling group as the target. Connect a WAF to the ALB.
o.B: Create a cluster placement group that contains multiple Amazon EC2 instances that hosts the application. Configure an Application Load Balancer and set the EC2 instances as the targets. Connect a WAF to the placement group.
o.C: Create two Amazon EC2 instances that host the application across two Availability Zones. Configure the EC2 instances as the targets of an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Connect a WAF to the ALB.
o.D: Create an Auto Scaling group that contains multiple Amazon EC2 instances that host the application across two Availability Zones. Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and set the Auto Scaling group as the target. Connect a WAF to the Auto Scaling group.

e.why: An Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones replaces unhealthy instances and scales with demand. An ALB spreads traffic across the zones. AWS WAF can be associated with an ALB, which makes this the highly available design with WAF in the right place.

others.B: A cluster placement group puts instances in a single AZ, which lowers availability, and WAF cannot be attached to a placement group.
others.C: Two fixed instances with no Auto Scaling cannot self-heal or scale, so availability is lower.
others.D: WAF cannot be attached to an Auto Scaling group. It attaches to ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito, App Runner, or Verified Access.

e.tip: WAF attaches to CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito user pools, App Runner, and Verified Access. It never attaches to EC2 instances or Auto Scaling groups.

q: A company manages a data lake in an Amazon S3 bucket that numerous applications access. The S3 bucket contains a unique prefix for each application. The company wants to restrict each application to its specific prefix and to have granular control of the objects under each prefix. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create dedicated S3 access points and access point policies for each application.
o.B: Create an S3 Batch Operations job to set the ACL permissions for each object in the S3 bucket.
o.C: Replicate the objects in the S3 bucket to new S3 buckets for each application. Create replication rules by prefix.
o.D: Replicate the objects in the S3 bucket to new S3 buckets for each application. Create dedicated S3 access points for each application.

e.why: S3 access points give each application its own endpoint with its own policy, and that policy can be scoped to the application's prefix and specific actions. This gives granular access per prefix on one bucket without copying data or writing one large bucket policy, so it has the least operational overhead.

others.B: Setting per-object ACLs with Batch Operations is hard to manage, and AWS recommends disabling ACLs.
others.C: Replicating data into separate buckets per application duplicates storage and adds replication to manage.
others.D: Replication duplicates the data needlessly, because access points work directly on the existing bucket.

e.tip: Many applications sharing one bucket, each limited to its own prefix, points to S3 Access Points.

q: A company has an application that customers use to upload images to an Amazon S3 bucket. Each night, the company launches an Amazon EC2 Spot Fleet that processes all the images that the company received that day. The processing for each image takes 2 minutes and requires 512 MB of memory. A solutions architect needs to change the application to process the images when the images are uploaded. Which change will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use S3 Event Notifications to write a message with image details to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure an AWS Lambda function to read the messages from the queue and to process the images.
o.B: Use S3 Event Notifications to write a message with image details to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure an EC2 Reserved Instance to read the messages from the queue and to process the images.
o.C: Use S3 Event Notifications to publish a message with image details to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure a container instance in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to subscribe to the topic and to process the images.
o.D: Use S3 Event Notifications to publish a message with image details to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application to subscribe to the topic and to process the images.

e.why: Each image needs only 2 minutes and 512 MB, which fits well within Lambda's 15-minute and 10 GB limits. S3 event notifications send messages to SQS, which buffers bursts, and Lambda polls the queue and is billed only while it processes. Nothing sits idle, so this is the most cost-effective option.

others.B: A Reserved Instance runs and is billed around the clock even when there are no uploads.
others.C: An ECS container instance is an always-on EC2 host, so you pay for idle capacity.
others.D: Elastic Beanstalk runs always-on EC2 instances and adds more infrastructure than the task needs.

e.tip: Short, event-driven, low-memory work is a Lambda job.

q: A company wants to improve the availability and performance of its hybrid application. The application consists of a stateful TCP-based workload hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in different AWS Regions and a stateless UDP-based workload hosted on premises. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to improve availability and performance? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator. Add the load balancers as endpoints.
o.B: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the load balancers.
o.C: Configure two Application Load Balancers in each Region. The first will route to the EC2 endpoints, and the second will route to the on-premises endpoints.
o.D: Configure a Network Load Balancer in each Region to address the EC2 endpoints. Configure a Network Load Balancer in each Region that routes to the on-premises endpoints.
o.E: Configure a Network Load Balancer in each Region to address the EC2 endpoints. Configure an Application Load Balancer in each Region that routes to the on-premises endpoints.

e.why: Global Accelerator supports both TCP and UDP. It gives static anycast IPs, sends users over the AWS global network to the nearest healthy endpoint, and fails over quickly. Network Load Balancers also handle TCP and UDP: one in each Region fronts the EC2 instances, and another reaches the on-premises UDP servers as IP targets.

others.B: CloudFront serves HTTP and HTTPS content. It does not accelerate arbitrary TCP or UDP workloads.
others.C: Application Load Balancers handle only HTTP and HTTPS, so they cannot carry raw TCP or UDP traffic.
others.E: An ALB cannot carry the UDP traffic to the on-premises workload.

e.tip: For UDP or non-HTTP TCP, choose NLB plus Global Accelerator, not ALB plus CloudFront.

q: A company runs a self-managed Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Daily snapshots are taken of the EBS volumes. Recently, all the company’s EBS snapshots were accidentally deleted while running a snapshot cleaning script that deletes all expired EBS snapshots. A solutions architect needs to update the architecture to prevent data loss without retaining EBS snapshots indefinitely. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

o.A: Change the IAM policy of the user to deny EBS snapshot deletion.
o.B: Copy the EBS snapshots to another AWS Region after completing the snapshots daily.
o.C: Create a 7-day EBS snapshot retention rule in Recycle Bin and apply the rule for all snapshots.
o.D: Copy EBS snapshots to Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).

e.why: Recycle Bin retention rules keep deleted EBS snapshots for a set period, here 7 days, and they can be restored during that window. Accidental deletions can be undone, snapshots expire from the bin automatically so nothing is kept forever, and no code changes are needed.

others.A: Denying deletion through IAM would stop the cleanup script from removing expired snapshots, so snapshots would pile up indefinitely.
others.B: Copying snapshots to another Region costs more, and the same script could still delete the copies.
others.D: You cannot copy EBS snapshots straight into a chosen S3 storage class. It would also take custom work and still not guard against deletion.

e.tip: For accidental deletion of EBS snapshots or AMIs, use Recycle Bin.

q: A company wants to use an AWS CloudFormation stack for its application in a test environment. The company stores the CloudFormation template in an Amazon S3 bucket that blocks public access. The company wants to grant CloudFormation access to the template in the S3 bucket based on specific user requests to create the test environment. The solution must follow security best practices. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Configure the CloudFormation stack to use the S3 object URL.
o.B: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API that has the S3 bucket as the target. Configure the CloudFormation stack to use the API Gateway URL.
o.C: Create a presigned URL for the template object. Configure the CloudFormation stack to use the presigned URL.
o.D: Allow public access to the template object in the S3 bucket. Block the public access after the test environment is created.

e.why: A presigned URL grants temporary access to one specific object using the creator's credentials. The bucket stays private, and access is granted per request and expires on its own, which follows least-privilege best practice.

others.A: A gateway VPC endpoint is a network path from a VPC. It does not authorize CloudFormation to read the template, and CloudFormation does not run inside your VPC.
others.B: An API Gateway proxy to S3 adds complexity and more attack surface for no benefit.
others.D: Making the object public, even for a short time, breaks the block-public-access requirement and best practice.

e.tip: For temporary, scoped access to a single private S3 object, use a presigned URL.

q: A company has applications that run in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company outsources operational support of the applications. The company needs to provide access for the external support engineers without compromising security. The external support engineers need access to the AWS Management Console. The external support engineers also need operating system access to the company’s fleet ofAmazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux in private subnets. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?

o.A: Confirm that AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is installed on all instances. Assign an instance profile with the necessary policy to connect to Systems Manager. Use AWS IAM Identity Center to provide the external support engineers console access. Use Systems Manager Session Manager to assign the required permissions.
o.B: Confirm that AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is installed on all instances. Assign an instance profile with the necessary policy to connect to Systems Manager. Use Systems Manager Session Manager to provide local IAM user credentials in each AWS account to the external support engineers for console access.
o.C: Confirm that all instances have a security group that allows SSH access only from the external support engineers’ source IP address ranges. Provide local IAM user credentials in each AWS account to the external support engineers for console access. Provide each external support engineer an SSH key pair to log in to the application instances.
o.D: Create a bastion host in a public subnet. Set up the bastion host security group to allow access from only the external engineers’ IP address ranges. Ensure that all instances have a security group that allows SSH access from the bastion host. Provide each external support engineer an SSH key pair to log in to the application instances. Provide local account IAM user credentials to the engineers for console access.

e.why: IAM Identity Center gives the external engineers federated console access to every account in the organization through permission sets, without long-lived IAM users. Session Manager gives them audited operating system shells on private instances through the SSM Agent and an instance profile, with no SSH keys, open inbound ports, or bastion host.

others.B: Local IAM users in each account mean long-lived credentials, and Session Manager does not hand out console credentials.
others.C: Opening SSH and handing out key pairs and IAM user credentials increases exposure and key-management risk.
others.D: A bastion host with SSH keys and local IAM users is less secure and has more overhead than Session Manager with Identity Center.

e.tip: For secure shell access to private instances, choose Session Manager. For workforce console access across an organization, choose IAM Identity Center.

q: A company uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to run its applications in the us-east-1 Region. The company also uses machine learning (ML) models to forecast annual revenue based on near real-time reports. The reports are generated by using the same RDS for PostgreSQL database. The database performance slows during business hours. The company needs to improve database performance. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create a cross-Region read replica. Configure the reports to be generated from the read replica.
o.B: Activate Multi-AZ DB instance deployment for RDS for PostgreSQL. Configure the reports to be generated from the standby database.
o.C: Use AWS Data Migration Service (AWS DMS) to logically replicate data to a new database. Configure the reports to be generated from the new database.
o.D: Create a read replica in us-east-1. Configure the reports to be generated from the read replica.

e.why: An RDS for PostgreSQL read replica in the same Region takes the reporting reads off the primary using asynchronous replication. Keeping it in us-east-1 avoids cross-Region data transfer charges and extra latency, which makes it the cheapest way to restore performance.

others.A: A cross-Region replica adds inter-Region transfer cost and replication lag with no benefit for this requirement.
others.B: In a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment, the standby cannot serve reads. It exists only for failover.
others.C: A separate database fed by DMS logical replication costs more and needs more management than a native read replica.

e.tip: A classic Multi-AZ standby is not readable. Multi-AZ DB clusters have readable standbys, but read replicas are the usual answer for offloading reads.

q: A company hosts its multi-tier, public web application in the AWS Cloud. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances, and its database runs on Amazon RDS. The company is anticipating a large increase in sales during an upcoming holiday weekend. A solutions architect needs to build a solution to analyze the performance of the web application with a granularity of no more than 2 minutes. What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.A: Send Amazon CloudWatch logs to Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon QuickS ght to perform further analysis.
o.B: Enable detailed monitoring on all EC2 instances. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to perform further analysis.
o.C: Create an AWS Lambda function to fetch EC2 logs from Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to perform further analysis.
o.D: Send EC2 logs to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Redshift to fetch logs from the S3 bucket to process raw data for further analysis with Amazon QuickSight.

e.why: By default, EC2 sends CloudWatch metrics every 5 minutes. Detailed monitoring sends them every 1 minute, which meets the requirement of no more than 2 minutes, and the metrics can be analyzed in CloudWatch straight away with no pipelines to build.

others.A: Exporting logs to Redshift and QuickSight is heavy and does not change the 5-minute metric interval.
others.C: Fetching logs with a Lambda function does not improve EC2 metric granularity and adds custom work.
others.D: An S3, Redshift, and QuickSight log pipeline is complex and is not near-real-time performance monitoring.

e.tip: Basic monitoring is 5 minutes, detailed monitoring is 1 minute, and high-resolution custom metrics go down to 1 second.

q: A company runs an application that stores and shares photos. Users upload the photos to an Amazon S3 bucket. Every day, users upload approximately 150 photos. The company wants to design a solution that creates a thumbnail of each new photo and stores the thumbnail in a second S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke a script every minute on a long-running Amazon EMR cluster. Configure the script to generate thumbnails for the photos that do not have thumbnails. Configure the script to upload the thumbnails to the second S3 bucket.
o.B: Configure an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke a script every minute on a memory-optimized Amazon EC2 instance that is always on. Configure the script to generate thumbnails for the photos that do not have thumbnails. Configure the script to upload the thumbnails to the second S3 bucket.
o.C: Configure an S3 event notification to invoke an AWS Lambda function each time a user uploads a new photo to the application. Configure the Lambda function to generate a thumbnail and to upload the thumbnail to the second S3 bucket.
o.D: Configure S3 Storage Lens to invoke an AWS Lambda function each time a user uploads a new photo to the application. Configure the Lambda function to generate a thumbnail and to upload the thumbnail to a second S3 bucket.

e.why: About 150 uploads a day is a low, event-driven volume. An S3 event notification that invokes Lambda creates each thumbnail on upload, and you pay only for those short invocations, with no idle compute, so it is the most cost-effective option.

others.A: A long-running EMR cluster is far too costly for creating a few thumbnails.
others.B: An always-on memory-optimized EC2 instance is billed constantly for very little work.
others.D: S3 Storage Lens provides storage analytics and cannot invoke Lambda on uploads.

q: A company has stored millions of objects across multiple prefixes in an Amazon S3 bucket by using the Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class. The company needs to delete all data older than 3 years except for a subset of data that must be retained. The company has identified the data that must be retained and wants to implement a serverless solution. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use S3 Inventory to list all objects. Use the AWS CLI to create a script that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance that deletes objects from the inventory list.
o.B: Use AWS Batch to delete objects older than 3 years except for the data that must be retained.
o.C: Provision an AWS Glue crawler to query objects older than 3 years. Save the manifest file of old objects. Create a script to delete objects in the manifest.
o.D: Enable S3 Inventory. Create an AWS Lambda function to filter and delete objects. Invoke the Lambda function with S3 Batch Operations to delete objects by using the inventory reports.

e.why: S3 Inventory gives a list of all objects, which can be filtered to exclude the data that must be kept. S3 Batch Operations then runs a Lambda function on each object in the manifest to delete it, at the scale of millions of objects, and the whole process is serverless.

others.A: Running a CLI script on an EC2 instance is not serverless.
others.B: AWS Batch runs compute jobs on EC2 or Fargate and has no native logic for deleting selected S3 objects. It also needs more setup.
others.C: Glue crawlers catalog data schemas. They do not list objects by age, and the deletion script still needs somewhere to run.

e.tip: For large-scale actions on S3 objects, use S3 Inventory as the manifest and Batch Operations to run the action.

q: A company is building an application on AWS. The application uses multiple AWS Lambda functions to retrieve sensitive data from a single Amazon S3 bucket for processing. The company must ensure that only authorized Lambda functions can access the data. The solution must comply with the principle of least privilege. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Grant full S3 bucket access to all Lambda functions through a shared IAM role.
o.B: Configure the Lambda functions to run within a VPC. Configure a bucket policy to grant access based on the Lambda functions' VPC endpoint IP addresses.
o.C: Create individual IAM roles for each Lambda function. Grant the IAM roles access to the S3 bucket. Assign each IAM role as the Lambda execution role for its corresponding Lambda function.
o.D: Configure a bucket policy granting access to the Lambda functions based on their function ARNs.

e.why: Giving each Lambda function its own execution role, with only the S3 permissions that function needs, follows least privilege. Only functions whose roles allow access can read the bucket, and each grant can be scoped and audited on its own.

others.A: A shared role with full bucket access gives every function more than it needs, which breaks least privilege.
others.B: Lambda functions in a VPC have no fixed IP addresses, and VPC endpoint policies use endpoint IDs, not IPs, so IP-based control is unreliable.
others.D: Bucket policies identify callers by principal, here the execution role. A function ARN is not a principal that the policy can match on.

q: A company has developed a non-production application that is composed of multiple microservices for each of the company's business units. A single development team maintains all the microservices. The current architecture uses a static web frontend and a Java-based backend that contains the application logic. The architecture also uses a MySQL database that the company hosts on an Amazon EC2 instance. The company needs to ensure that the application is secure and available globally. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon CloudFront and AWS Amplify to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that the microservices access by using Amazon API Gateway. Migrate the MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance.
o.B: Use Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3 to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that the microservices access by using Amazon API Gateway. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL.
o.C: Use Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3 to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that are in a target group behind a Network Load Balancer. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL.
o.D: Use Amazon S3 to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that are in a target group behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance.

e.why: S3 with CloudFront serves the static frontend globally and securely, using OAC and edge caching. Lambda behind API Gateway removes servers from the microservices, and RDS for MySQL is a managed database. Every layer is managed, so this has the least operational overhead.

others.A: Leaving MySQL on an EC2 Reserved Instance means the company still manages the database.
others.C: A Network Load Balancer cannot have Lambda functions as targets. Only an ALB supports Lambda targets.
others.D: Without CloudFront the frontend is not delivered globally, and MySQL stays self-managed on EC2.

q: A video game company is deploying a new gaming application to its global users. The company requires a solution that will provide near real-time reviews and rankings of the players. A solutions architect must design a solution to provide fast access to the data. The solution must also ensure the data persists on disks in the event that the company restarts the application. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin. Store the player data in the S3 bucket.
o.B: Create Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions. Store the player data on the EC2 instances. Configure Amazon Route 53 with geolocation records to direct users to the closest EC2 instance.
o.C: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis duster. Store the player data in the ElastiCache cluster.
o.D: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached duster. Store the player data in the ElastiCache cluster.

e.why: ElastiCache for Redis gives sub-millisecond reads and its sorted sets suit leaderboards and rankings. Redis also persists data to disk with RDB snapshots and AOF and supports replication, so the data survives a restart, and it is a managed service.

others.A: S3 behind CloudFront is not built for near-real-time updates to rankings.
others.B: Self-managed EC2 instances in several Regions add heavy operational overhead and no built-in ranking features.
others.D: Memcached has no persistence or replication, so the data is lost on restart.

e.tip: Leaderboards and rankings point to Redis sorted sets. If the cache must persist, rule out Memcached.

q: A company is designing an application on AWS that processes sensitive data. The application stores and processes financial data for multiple customers. To meet compliance requirements, the data for each customer must be encrypted separately at rest by using a secure, centralized key management solution. The company wants to use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to implement encryption. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Generate a unique encryption key for each customer. Store the keys in an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable server-side encryption.
o.B: Deploy a hardware security appliance in the AWS environment that securely stores customer-provided encryption keys. Integrate the security appliance with AWS KMS to encrypt the sensitive data in the application.
o.C: Create a single AWS KMS key to encrypt all sensitive data across the application.
o.D: Create separate AWS KMS keys for each customer's data that have granular access control and logging enabled.

e.why: A separate customer managed KMS key for each customer isolates each customer's encryption. Key policies and grants give fine-grained access control, and CloudTrail logs every key use. KMS is centralized and managed, so the overhead stays low.

others.A: Storing raw keys in an S3 bucket is insecure and is not centralized key management.
others.B: Running your own hardware security appliance adds a lot of operational overhead compared with native KMS keys.
others.C: A single key for all customers does not encrypt each customer's data separately.

q: A company needs to design a resilient web application to process customer orders. The web application must automatically handle increases in web traffic and application usage without affecting the customer experience or losing customer orders. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use a NAT gateway to manage web traffic. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups to receive, process, and store processed customer orders. Use an AWS Lambda function to capture and store unprocessed orders.
o.B: Use a Network Load Balancer (NLB) to manage web traffic. Use an Application Load Balancer to receive customer orders from the NLUse Amazon Redshift with a Multi-AZ deployment to store unprocessed and processed customer orders.
o.C: Use a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) to manage web traffic. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to receive and process customer orders. Use the GWLB to capture and store unprocessed orders. Use Amazon DynamoDB to store processed customer orders.
o.D: Use an Application Load Balancer to manage web traffic. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups to receive and process customer orders. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to store unprocessed orders. Use Amazon RDS with a Multi-AZ deployment to store processed customer orders.

e.why: An ALB spreads web traffic across an Auto Scaling group that scales with demand. An SQS queue holds orders that have not been processed yet, so none are lost during spikes, and RDS Multi-AZ stores the processed orders durably with failover. The tiers are decoupled and resilient.

others.A: A NAT gateway carries outbound traffic from private subnets. It does not load balance incoming web traffic.
others.B: Redshift is a data warehouse, not an order store, and the NLB-to-ALB chain adds nothing.
others.C: A Gateway Load Balancer is for third-party network appliances and cannot store orders.

q: A company is using AWS DataSync to migrate millions of files from an on-premises system to AWS. The files are 10 KB in size on average. The company wants to use Amazon S3 for file storage. For the first year after the migration, the files will be accessed once or twice and must be immediately available. After 1 year, the files must be archived for at least 7 years. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use an archive tool to group the files into large objects. Use DataSync to migrate the objects. Store the objects in S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for the first year. Use a lifecycle configuration to transition the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.
o.B: Use an archive tool to group the files into large objects. Use DataSync to copy the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use a lifecycle configuration to transition the files to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.
o.C: Configure the destination storage class for the files as S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.
o.D: Configure a DataSync task to transfer the files to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use a lifecycle configuration to transition the files to S3 Deep Archive after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.

e.why: Millions of 10 KB files cost a lot as separate S3 objects: each object incurs request charges, and Glacier Instant Retrieval bills each object as at least 128 KB. Bundling them into large archives removes most of that. Glacier Instant Retrieval gives immediate access at low storage cost for data read once or twice a year, and a lifecycle rule then moves the archives to Deep Archive, the cheapest class, for the 7-year retention.

others.B: Standard-IA costs more than Glacier Instant Retrieval for data read so rarely, and Instant Retrieval is a poor long-term archive tier compared with Deep Archive.
others.C: Unbundled 10 KB objects are billed at the 128 KB minimum in Glacier Instant Retrieval, and each also carries per-object transition charges, while Flexible Retrieval costs more than Deep Archive.
others.D: Unbundled small objects incur Standard-IA's 128 KB minimum charge and per-object transition costs, and Standard-IA storage costs more than Glacier Instant Retrieval.

e.tip: Very small objects cost more in IA and Glacier classes because of the minimum billable object size and per-request fees. Combine them first.

q: A company recently performed a lift and shift migration of its on-premises Oracle database workload to run on an Amazon EC2 memory optimized Linux instance. The EC2 Linux instance uses a 1 TB Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume with 64,000 IOPS. The database storage performance after the migration is slower than the performance of the on-premises database. Which solution will improve storage performance?

o.A: Add more Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volumes. Use OS commands to create a Logical Volume Management (LVM) stripe.
o.B: Increase the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume to more than 64,000 IOPS.
o.C: Increase the size of the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume to 2 TB.
o.D: Change the EC2 Linux instance to a storage optimized instance type. Do not change the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume.

e.why: An io1 volume tops out at 64,000 IOPS, and this volume is already at that limit. Attaching several io1 volumes and striping them with LVM in RAID 0 adds their IOPS and throughput together. That is the only listed way to get more performance.

others.B: io1 cannot be provisioned above 64,000 IOPS per volume. Going higher needs io2 Block Express.
others.C: Making the volume bigger does not raise IOPS past the 64,000 ceiling.
others.D: A storage optimized instance adds local instance store, not EBS performance, and a memory optimized instance suits Oracle better.

e.tip: When a single volume is at its maximum IOPS, stripe several volumes with RAID 0 or switch to io2 Block Express.

q: A company is migrating from a monolithic architecture for a web application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 to a serverless microservices architecture. The company wants to use AWS services that support an event-driven, loosely coupled architecture. The company wants to use the publish/subscribe (pub/sub) pattern. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure an Amazon API Gateway REST API to invoke an AWS Lambda function that publishes events to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure one or more subscribers to read events from the SQS queue.
o.B: Configure an Amazon API Gateway REST API to invoke an AWS Lambda function that publishes events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure one or more subscribers to receive events from the SNS topic.
o.C: Configure an Amazon API Gateway WebSocket API to write to a data stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with enhanced fan-out. Configure one or more subscribers to receive events from the data stream.
o.D: Configure an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API to invoke an AWS Lambda function that publishes events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure one or more subscribers to receive events from the topic.

e.why: SNS gives managed pub/sub that fans events out to many subscribers. API Gateway HTTP APIs cost about 70% less than REST APIs and have lower latency. That makes HTTP API, then Lambda, then SNS the most cost-effective serverless event-driven design.

others.A: SQS is a point-to-point queue, not pub/sub. Each message goes to one consumer.
others.B: This design works but uses the more expensive REST API without needing its extra features.
others.C: Kinesis with enhanced fan-out costs far more for shards and per-consumer throughput and is meant for streaming.

e.tip: If no REST-only feature such as API keys, usage plans, or WAF is needed, an HTTP API is the cheaper choice.

q: A company recently migrated a monolithic application to an Amazon EC2 instance and Amazon RDS. The application has tightly coupled modules. The existing design of the application gives the application the ability to run on only a single EC2 instance. The company has noticed high CPU utilization on the EC2 instance during peak usage times. The high CPU utilization corresponds to degraded performance on Amazon RDS for read requests. The company wants to reduce the high CPU utilization and improve read request performance. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Resize the EC2 instance to an EC2 instance type that has more CPU capacity. Configure an Auto Scaling group with a minimum and maximum size of 1. Configure an RDS read replica for read requests.
o.B: Resize the EC2 instance to an EC2 instance type that has more CPU capacity. Configure an Auto Scaling group with a minimum and maximum size of 1. Add an RDS read replica and redirect all read/write traffic to the replica.
o.C: Configure an Auto Scaling group with a minimum size of 1 and maximum size of 2. Resize the RDS DB instance to an instance type that has more CPU capacity.
o.D: Resize the EC2 instance to an EC2 instance type that has more CPU capacity. Configure an Auto Scaling group with a minimum and maximum size of 1. Resize the RDS DB instance to an instance type that has more CPU capacity.

e.why: The tightly coupled application can run on only one instance, so the fix is to scale vertically to an instance type with more CPU. An Auto Scaling group with min and max of 1 still replaces a failed instance. An RDS read replica takes read requests off the primary, which improves read performance.

others.B: Read replicas are read-only, so sending write traffic to the replica would fail.
others.C: A maximum of 2 would run a second instance, which the application cannot support, and it does not offload reads.
others.D: Making the RDS instance bigger helps but costs more than a read replica, which is the standard way to offload read traffic.

q: A company needs to grant a team of developers access to the company's AWS resources. The company must maintain a high level of security for the resources. The company requires an access control solution that will prevent unauthorized access to the sensitive data. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Share the IAM user credentials for each development team member with the rest of the team to simplify access management and to streamline development workflows.
o.B: Define IAM roles that have fine-grained permissions based on the principle of least privilege. Assign an IAM role to each developer.
o.C: Create IAM access keys to grant programmatic access to AWS resources. Allow only developers to interact with AWS resources through API calls by using the access keys.
o.D: Create an AWS Cognito user pool. Grant developers access to AWS resources by using the user pool.

e.why: IAM roles with fine-grained, least-privilege policies give developers temporary credentials limited to what each one needs. That prevents unauthorized access to sensitive data and avoids long-lived shared secrets.

others.A: Sharing credentials removes accountability and is a serious security anti-pattern.
others.C: Long-lived access keys are risky, and creating them does nothing to scope permissions.
others.D: Cognito user pools authenticate users of your application, not developers who need access to AWS resources.

q: A company hosts a monolithic web application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Application users have recently reported poor performance at specific times. Analysis of Amazon CloudWatch metrics shows that CPU utilization is 100% during the periods of poor performance. The company wants to resolve this performance issue and improve application availability. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use AWS Compute Optimizer to obtain a recommendation for an instance type to scale vertically.
o.B: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the web server. Reference the AMI in a new launch template.
o.C: Create an Auto Scaling group and an Application Load Balancer to scale vertically.
o.D: Use AWS Compute Optimizer to obtain a recommendation for an instance type to scale horizontally.
o.E: Create an Auto Scaling group and an Application Load Balancer to scale horizontally.

e.why: Compute Optimizer studies CloudWatch usage and recommends the right instance size, so each instance is not starved of CPU. An Auto Scaling group behind an ALB then scales out horizontally and spreads instances across AZs, which improves availability. Together they fix the CPU problem cost-effectively.

others.B: An AMI and launch template are setup steps for an Auto Scaling group. By themselves they neither fix the CPU problem nor add availability.
others.C: Auto Scaling groups and ALBs scale horizontally by adding instances, not vertically.
others.D: Compute Optimizer recommends instance types and sizes, which is vertical rightsizing. It does not plan horizontal scaling.

q: A company runs all its business applications in the AWS Cloud. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts. A solutions architect needs to review all permissions that are granted to IAM users to determine which IAM users have more permissions than required. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

o.A: Use Network Access Analyzer to review all access permissions in the company's AWS accounts.
o.B: Create an AWS CloudWatch alarm that activates when an IAM user creates or modifies resources in an AWS account.
o.C: Use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Access Analyzer to review all the company’s resources and accounts.
o.D: Use Amazon Inspector to find vulnerabilities in existing IAM policies.

e.why: IAM Access Analyzer reports unused access, such as unused roles, users, access keys, passwords, and permissions, and it generates policies from recorded activity. It can use the organization as its zone of trust, so it finds over-permissioned IAM users across all accounts with little effort.

others.A: Network Access Analyzer examines network reachability paths, not IAM permissions.
others.B: A CloudWatch alarm on resource changes does not judge whether a user has excess permissions.
others.D: Amazon Inspector scans EC2, ECR, and Lambda for software vulnerabilities, not IAM policies.

e.tip: For over-privileged IAM users or unused access, use IAM Access Analyzer.

q: A company needs to implement a new data retention policy for regulatory compliance. As part of this policy, sensitive documents that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket must be protected from deletion or modification for a fixed period of time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Activate S3 Object Lock on the required objects and enable governance mode.
o.B: Activate S3 Object Lock on the required objects and enable compliance mode.
o.C: Enable versioning on the S3 bucket. Set a lifecycle policy to delete the objects after a specified period.
o.D: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval for the retention duration.

e.why: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode means no user, including the root user, can overwrite or delete a protected object version, or shorten its retention, until the retention period ends. That is the fixed-period protection that regulations require.

others.A: In governance mode, users with s3:BypassGovernanceRetention can still delete or change objects, so it is not strict enough for regulatory compliance.
others.C: Versioning with an expiration rule deletes data and does not stop anyone from deleting or modifying it.
others.D: Moving objects to Glacier changes the storage class but does not protect them from deletion.

e.tip: Compliance mode means nobody can delete, even root. Governance mode lets privileged users bypass the lock.

q: A company runs its customer-facing web application on containers. The workload uses Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate. The web application is resource intensive. The web application needs to be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week for customers. The company expects the application to experience short bursts of high traffic. The workload must be highly available. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate. Conduct load testing by using a third-party tool. Rightsize the Fargate tasks in Amazon CloudWatch.
o.B: Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate for steady state and Fargate Spot for burst traffic.
o.C: Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate Spot for steady state and Fargate for burst traffic.
o.D: Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate. Use AWS Compute Optimizer to rightsize the Fargate task.

e.why: Compute Optimizer gives rightsizing recommendations for the CPU and memory of ECS services on Fargate, based on CloudWatch usage. Rightsizing a resource-intensive task cuts cost while keeping regular Fargate capacity, which a customer-facing app that runs 24/7 needs to stay highly available.

others.A: Running third-party load tests and analyzing them by hand takes more effort and is less reliable than Compute Optimizer's automated recommendations.
others.B: Fargate Spot tasks can be interrupted at two minutes' notice, which is risky for customer-facing bursts on a workload that must be highly available.
others.C: Running steady-state traffic on Fargate Spot would put the always-on customer workload at risk of interruption.

q: A company is building an application in the AWS Cloud. The application is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company uses Amazon Route 53 for the DNS. The company needs a managed solution with proactive engagement to detect against DDoS attacks. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Enable AWS Config. Configure an AWS Config managed rule that detects DDoS attacks.
o.B: Enable AWS WAF on the ALCreate an AWS WAF web ACL with rules to detect and prevent DDoS attacks. Associate the web ACL with the ALB.
o.C: Store the ALB access logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to detect and take automated preventative actions for DDoS attacks.
o.D: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Configure hosted zones in Route 53. Add ALB resources as protected resources.

e.why: Shield Advanced gives managed DDoS detection and mitigation for ALB and Route 53 hosted zones. It includes the Shield Response Team, and with proactive engagement the SRT contacts you when a protected resource's health checks show an attack. That proactive engagement is the deciding requirement.

others.A: AWS Config checks resource configuration compliance and does not detect DDoS attacks.
others.B: WAF rate-based rules help against layer 7 floods, but WAF alone has no managed response team or proactive engagement.
others.C: GuardDuty does not analyze ALB access logs or take automated DDoS-prevention actions.

e.tip: The words proactive engagement or DDoS response team mean Shield Advanced.

q: A company hosts a video streaming web application in a VPC. The company uses a Network Load Balancer (NLB) to handle TCP traffic for real-time data processing. There have been unauthorized attempts to access the application. The company wants to improve application security with minimal architectural change to prevent unauthorized attempts to access the application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Implement a series of AWS WAF rules directly on the NLB to filter out unauthorized traffic.
o.B: Recreate the NLB with a security group to allow only trusted IP addresses.
o.C: Deploy a second NLB in parallel with the existing NLB configured with a strict IP address allow list.
o.D: Use AWS Shield Advanced to provide enhanced DDoS protection and prevent unauthorized access attempts.

e.why: The keyed answer reasons that AWS Shield Advanced protects the NLB from attack traffic with managed DDoS detection and mitigation, without changing the existing architecture.

others.A: AWS WAF cannot be associated with a Network Load Balancer. It works only with layer 7 resources.
others.B: The key treats rebuilding the NLB with a security group as more of an architectural change. This is disputed (see flag).
others.C: A second NLB in parallel adds complexity and does not secure the existing endpoint.

e.tip: An NLB can have security groups only if they are attached when it is created. You cannot add them to an NLB created without them.
e.flag: Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks, not unauthorized access. NLBs now support security groups, but only when they are created, so recreating the NLB with a security group that allows only trusted IP addresses (B) is the better answer.

q: A healthcare company is developing an AWS Lambda function that publishes notifications to an encrypted Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. The notifications contain protected health information (PHI). The SNS topic uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys for encryption. The company must ensure that the application has the necessary permissions to publish messages securely to the SNS topic. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

o.A: Create a resource policy for the SNS topic that allows the Lambda function to publish messages to the topic.
o.B: Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for the SNS topic instead of customer managed keys.
o.C: Create a resource policy for the encryption key that the SNS topic uses that has the necessary AWS KMS permissions.
o.D: Specify the Lambda function's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in the SNS topic's resource policy.
o.E: Associate an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API with the SNS topic to control access to the topic by using API Gateway resource policies.
o.F: Configure a Lambda execution role that has the necessary IAM permissions to use a customer managed key in AWS KMS.

e.why: Publishing to an SNS topic encrypted with a customer managed key needs three permissions. The topic's resource policy must allow the Lambda function's role to call sns:Publish. The KMS key policy must allow kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt. The Lambda execution role must have IAM permissions for sns:Publish and for that KMS key.

others.B: Customer managed keys already are SSE-KMS keys, and switching to the AWS managed key would weaken control over PHI encryption.
others.D: Lambda calls SNS using its execution role, so the topic policy names the role ARN as the principal, not the function ARN.
others.E: API Gateway is not needed for Lambda to publish to SNS and adds nothing to authorization.

q: A company has an employee web portal. Employees log in to the portal to view payroll details. The company is developing a new system to give employees the ability to upload scanned documents for reimbursement. The company runs a program to extract text-based data from the documents and attach the extracted information to each employee’s reimbursement IDs for processing. The employee web portal requires 100% uptime. The document extract program runs infrequently throughout the day on an on-demand basis. The company wants to build a scalable and cost-effective new system that will require minimal changes to the existing web portal. The company does not want to make any code changes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

o.A: Run Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances in an Auto Scaling group for the web portal. Use an AWS Lambda function to run the document extract program. Invoke the Lambda function when an employee uploads a new reimbursement document.
o.B: Run Amazon EC2 Spot Instances in an Auto Scaling group for the web portal. Run the document extract program on EC2 Spot Instances. Start document extract program instances when an employee uploads a new reimbursement document.
o.C: Purchase a Savings Plan to run the web portal and the document extract program. Run the web portal and the document extract program in an Auto Scaling group.
o.D: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to host the web portal. Use Amazon API Gateway and an AWS Lambda function for the existing functionalities. Use the Lambda function to run the document extract program. Invoke the Lambda function when the API that is associated with a new document upload is called.

e.why: Keeping the web portal on On-Demand EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group avoids any code changes and gives uninterrupted capacity for 100% uptime. The extraction program runs only occasionally, so running it as a Lambda function triggered on upload costs nothing while idle and scales automatically. That is the least implementation effort.

others.B: Spot Instances can be interrupted, which conflicts with 100% uptime, and launching instances for each upload is slow and complex.
others.C: A Savings Plan commits spend to always-on capacity for a program that runs only now and then, and it changes nothing about the architecture.
others.D: Rebuilding the portal on S3 and Lambda requires code changes, which the company does not want.

q: A media company has a multi-account AWS environment in the us-east-1 Region. The company has an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic in a production account that publishes performance metrics. The company has an AWS Lambda function in an administrator account to process and analyze log data. The Lambda function that is in the administrator account must be invoked by messages from the SNS topic that is in the production account when significant metrics are reported. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create an IAM resource policy for the Lambda function that allows Amazon SNS to invoke the function.
o.B: Implement an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue in the administrator account to buffer messages from the SNS topic that is in the production account. Configure the SQS queue to invoke the Lambda function.
o.C: Create an IAM policy for the SNS topic that allows the Lambda function to subscribe to the topic.
o.D: Use an Amazon EventBridge rule in the production account to capture the SNS topic notifications. Configure the EventBridge rule to forward notifications to the Lambda function that is in the administrator account.
o.E: Store performance metrics in an Amazon S3 bucket in the production account. Use Amazon Athena to analyze the metrics from the administrator account.

e.why: For SNS to invoke a Lambda function in another account, two policies are needed. The function's resource-based policy, added with lambda add-permission, must allow sns.amazonaws.com from the production topic's ARN to invoke it. The topic's access policy must allow the administrator account to subscribe the function to the topic. Both together complete the cross-account subscription.

others.B: An SQS buffer is not required, because SNS can invoke a Lambda function in another account directly.
others.D: EventBridge does not capture SNS notifications as events in this way, so this adds an unnecessary hop.
others.E: S3 with Athena gives batch analysis and does not invoke the function when significant metrics are reported.

q: A company is migrating an application from an on-premises location to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The company must use a custom subnet for pods that are in the company's VPC to comply with requirements. The company also needs to ensure that the pods can communicate securely within the pods' VPC. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure AWS Transit Gateway to directly manage custom subnet configurations for the pods in Amazon EKS.
o.B: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection from the company's on-premises IP address ranges to the EKS pods.
o.C: Use the Amazon VPC CNI plugin for Kubernetes. Define custom subnets in the VPC cluster for the pods to use.
o.D: Implement a Kubernetes network policy that has pod anti-affinity rules to restrict pod placement to specific nodes that are within custom subnets.

e.why: The Amazon VPC CNI plugin gives pods real VPC IP addresses. Its custom networking feature, configured with ENIConfig resources, places pod interfaces in specified subnets. Pods then talk natively and privately within the VPC and can use security groups for pods.

others.A: Transit Gateway connects VPCs and networks. It does not control which subnets EKS pods get IPs from.
others.B: Direct Connect is about on-premises connectivity and does not set pod subnets.
others.D: Network policies and anti-affinity rules control traffic and scheduling. They do not assign pods to custom subnets.

q: A company hosts an ecommerce application that stores all data in a single Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance that is fully managed by AWS. The company needs to mitigate the risk of a single point of failure. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

o.A: Modify the RDS DB instance to use a Multi-AZ deployment. Apply the changes during the next maintenance window.
o.B: Migrate the current database to a new Amazon DynamoDB Multi-AZ deployment. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with a heterogeneous migration strategy to migrate the current RDS DB instance to DynamoDB tables.
o.C: Create a new RDS DB instance in a Multi-AZ deployment. Manually restore the data from the existing RDS DB instance from the most recent snapshot.
o.D: Configure the DB instance in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum group size of three. Use Amazon Route 53 simple routing to distribute requests to all DB instances.

e.why: Changing an existing RDS instance to Multi-AZ is a single setting. RDS creates a synchronous standby in another AZ with automatic failover and no data migration. That removes the single point of failure with the least effort.

others.B: Moving from relational MySQL to DynamoDB is a heterogeneous migration and requires a major rewrite.
others.C: Building a new instance and restoring from a snapshot takes manual work and loses data written since the snapshot.
others.D: RDS cannot run in an EC2 Auto Scaling group, and simple routing across separate databases would not keep the data consistent.

q: A company has multiple Microsoft Windows SMB file servers and Linux NFS file servers for file sharing in an on-premises environment. As part of the company's AWS migration plan, the company wants to consolidate the file servers in the AWS Cloud. The company needs a managed AWS storage service that supports both NFS and SMB access. The solution must be able to share between protocols. The solution must have redundancy at the Availability Zone level. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for storage. Configure multi-protocol access.
o.B: Create two Amazon EC2 instances. Use one EC2 instance for Windows SMB file server access and one EC2 instance for Linux NFS file server access.
o.C: Use Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for SMB access. Use Amazon FSx for Lustre for NFS access.
o.D: Use Amazon S3 storage. Access Amazon S3 through an Amazon S3 File Gateway.

e.why: FSx for NetApp ONTAP is a managed file system that supports NFS and SMB on the same volumes, and multiprotocol access lets the same data be shared between Windows and Linux clients. A Multi-AZ deployment gives redundancy across Availability Zones.

others.B: Self-managed EC2 file servers are not managed, cannot share data between protocols, and lack AZ redundancy.
others.C: Two separate file systems cannot share the same data across both protocols, and FSx for Lustre is a high-performance computing file system, not a general NFS share.
others.D: S3 File Gateway runs as an appliance and fits hybrid caching. It is not a consolidated managed multi-protocol NAS in AWS.

e.tip: If you need NFS and SMB on the same data, choose FSx for NetApp ONTAP.

q: A software company needs to upgrade a critical web application. The application currently runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance that the company hosts in a public subnet. The EC2 instance runs a MySQL database. The application's DNS records are published in an Amazon Route 53 zone. A solutions architect must reconfigure the application to be scalable and highly available. The solutions architect must also reduce MySQL read latency. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Launch a second EC2 instance in a second AWS Region. Use a Route 53 failover routing policy to redirect the traffic to the second EC2 instance.
o.B: Create and configure an Auto Scaling group to launch private EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. Add the instances to a target group behind a new Application Load Balancer.
o.C: Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster. Create the primary DB instance and reader DB instance in separate Availability Zones.
o.D: Create and configure an Auto Scaling group to launch private EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions. Add the instances to a target group behind a new Application Load Balancer.
o.E: Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster with cross-Region read replicas.

e.why: An Auto Scaling group of private instances across multiple AZs behind an ALB makes the web tier scalable and highly available. Aurora MySQL with a reader in another AZ gives automatic failover and offloads reads, which reduces read latency.

others.A: A single standby instance in another Region with failover routing does not scale and leaves the database unchanged.
others.D: An Auto Scaling group and an ALB are regional, so neither can span multiple Regions.
others.E: Cross-Region replicas add replication lag and do not reduce read latency for users in the primary Region.

q: A company runs thousands of AWS Lambda functions. The company needs a solution to securely store sensitive information that all the Lambda functions use. The solution must also manage the automatic rotation of the sensitive information. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create HTTP security headers by using Lambda@Edge to retrieve and create sensitive information
o.B: Create a Lambda layer that retrieves sensitive information
o.C: Store sensitive information in AWS Secrets Manager
o.D: Store sensitive information in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
o.E: Create a Lambda consumer with dedicated throughput to retrieve sensitive information and create environmental variables

e.why: Secrets Manager stores sensitive values encrypted with KMS and rotates them automatically on a schedule using rotation functions. A shared Lambda layer, such as the AWS Parameters and Secrets Lambda Extension or a common retrieval library, lets thousands of functions fetch and cache the secrets the same way, with little ongoing overhead.

others.A: Lambda@Edge runs at CloudFront edge locations to change HTTP requests and responses. It is not a secrets store.
others.D: Parameter Store SecureString parameters have no built-in automatic rotation.
others.E: Dedicated-throughput consumers belong to Kinesis, and writing secrets into environment variables would break automatic rotation.

e.tip: If the question requires automatic secret rotation, choose Secrets Manager over Parameter Store.

q: A company has an internal application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The EC2 instances are compute optimized and use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. The company wants to identify cost optimizations across the EC2 instances, the Auto Scaling group, and the EBS volumes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Create a new AWS Cost and Usage Report. Search the report for cost recommendations for the EC2 instances the Auto Scaling group, and the EBS volumes.
o.B: Create new Amazon CloudWatch billing alerts. Check the alert statuses for cost recommendations for the EC2 instances, the Auto Scaling group, and the EBS volumes.
o.C: Configure AWS Compute Optimizer for cost recommendations for the EC2 instances, the Auto Scaling group and the EBS volumes.
o.D: Configure AWS Compute Optimizer for cost recommendations for the EC2 instances. Create a new AWS Cost and Usage Report. Search the report for cost recommendations for the Auto Scaling group and the EBS volumes.

e.why: Compute Optimizer gives rightsizing and cost recommendations for EC2 instances, Auto Scaling groups, and EBS volumes, as well as Lambda, ECS on Fargate, and more, all from one service. Turning it on covers every resource in the question with the least operational effort.

others.A: The Cost and Usage Report is raw billing data and contains no optimization recommendations.
others.B: Billing alerts warn about spend thresholds and do not give recommendations.
others.D: Compute Optimizer already covers Auto Scaling groups and EBS, so adding a CUR search is extra work for nothing.

q: A company is running a media store across multiple Amazon EC2 instances distributed across multiple Availability Zones in a single VPC. The company wants a high-performing solution to share data between all the EC2 instances, and prefers to keep the data within the VPC only. What should a solutions architect recommend?

o.A: Create an Amazon S3 bucket and call the service APIs from each instance's application
o.B: Create an Amazon S3 bucket and configure all instances to access it as a mounted volume
o.C: Configure an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and mount it across all instances
o.D: Configure an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system and mount it across all instances

e.why: Amazon EFS is a shared NFS file system that instances in every AZ of the VPC can mount at the same time through mount targets in the VPC. It gives high-performance shared access, and the traffic stays inside the VPC.

others.A: Calling the S3 APIs is object storage, not a shared file system, and by default the traffic goes to a public endpoint.
