others.B: Mounting S3 as a volume needs third-party or Mountpoint tools and does not give full file system semantics or high performance.
others.C: An EBS volume lives in one AZ, and Multi-Attach works only for io1 and io2 within that AZ, so it cannot be shared across AZs.

e.tip: For a file system shared by instances in many AZs, choose EFS. EBS is limited to one AZ.

q: A company uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL instance. To prepare for end-of-year processing, the company added a read replica to accommodate extra read-only queries from the company's reporting tool. The read replica CPU usage was 60% and the primary instance CPU usage was 60%. After end-of-year activities are complete, the read replica has a constant 25% CPU usage. The primary instance still has a constant 60% CPU usage. The company wants to rightsize the database and still provide enough performance for future growth. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Delete the read replica Do not make changes to the primary instance
o.B: Resize the read replica to a smaller instance size Do not make changes to the primary instance
o.C: Resize the read replica to a larger instance size Resize the primary instance to a smaller instance size
o.D: Delete the read replica Resize the primary instance to a larger instance

e.why: After the peak, the read replica runs at only 25% CPU, so it is oversized, while the primary at a steady 60% has reasonable headroom. Downsizing the replica cuts cost, keeps reporting reads off the primary, and leaves the primary sized for growth.

others.A: Deleting the replica would push the reporting load back onto the primary and raise its CPU.
others.C: Enlarging the underused replica and shrinking a primary at 60% CPU is the opposite of rightsizing.
others.D: Deleting the replica and enlarging the primary costs more and gives up the separation of read traffic.

q: A company is migrating its databases to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company is migrating its applications to Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to optimize costs for long-running workloads. Which solution will meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use On-Demand Instances for the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL workloads. Purchase a 1 year Compute Savings Plan with the No Upfront option for the EC2 instances.
o.B: Purchase Reserved Instances for a 1 year term with the No Upfront option for the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL workloads. Purchase a 1 year EC2 Instance Savings Plan with the No Upfront option for the EC2 instances.
o.C: Purchase Reserved Instances for a 1 year term with the Partial Upfront option for the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL workloads. Purchase a 1 year EC2 Instance Savings Plan with the Partial Upfront option for the EC2 instances.
o.D: Purchase Reserved Instances for a 3 year term with the All Upfront option for the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL workloads. Purchase a 3 year EC2 Instance Savings Plan with the All Upfront option for the EC2 instances.

e.why: For long-running, steady workloads, the largest discounts come from a 3-year term paid All Upfront. RDS Reserved Instances cover the PostgreSQL databases and an EC2 Instance Savings Plan covers the EC2 instances.

others.A: On-Demand RDS gets no discount, and a 1-year No Upfront Compute Savings Plan gives the smallest savings.
others.B: A 1-year No Upfront commitment gives lower discounts than a 3-year All Upfront one.
others.C: A 1-year Partial Upfront commitment is still less cost-effective than 3-year All Upfront.

e.tip: The deepest discount is the longest term with the most paid upfront.

q: A company is using an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The company must ensure that Kubernetes service accounts in the EKS cluster have secure and granular access to specific AWS resources by using IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA). Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create an IAM policy that defines the required permissions Attach the policy directly to the IAM role of the EKS nodes.
o.B: Implement network policies within the EKS cluster to prevent Kubernetes service accounts from accessing specific AWS services.
o.C: Modify the EKS cluster's IAM role to include permissions for each Kubernetes service account. Ensure a one-to-one mapping between IAM roles and Kubernetes roles.
o.D: Define an IAM role that includes the necessary permissions. Annotate the Kubernetes service accounts with the Amazon ResourceName (ARN) of the IAM role.
o.E: Set up a trust relationship between the IAM roles for the service accounts and an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider.

e.why: IRSA works in two parts. You create an IAM role whose trust policy trusts the cluster's IAM OIDC identity provider, scoped to the service account's namespace and name. You then annotate the Kubernetes service account with the role ARN. Pods using that service account get temporary credentials for only that role.

others.A: Attaching policies to the node role gives the permissions to every pod on the node, which is not granular.
others.B: Kubernetes network policies control pod network traffic, not IAM permissions to AWS APIs.
others.C: The cluster IAM role is for the EKS control plane and is not passed to service accounts.

e.tip: IRSA means an OIDC provider, a role trust policy, and a service account annotation. EKS Pod Identity is the newer alternative.

q: A company regularly uploads confidential data to Amazon S3 buckets for analysis. The company's security policies mandate that the objects must be encrypted at rest. The company must automatically rotate the encryption key every year. The company must be able to track key rotation by using AWS CloudTrail. The company also must minimize costs for the encryption key. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)
o.B: Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3)
o.C: Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS)
o.D: Use server-side encryption with customer managed AWS KMS keys

e.why: SSE-KMS with the AWS managed key aws/s3 is rotated automatically every year. Its use is recorded in CloudTrail, and it has no monthly key charge, unlike a customer managed key, which costs 1 USD per month. Enabling S3 Bucket Keys cuts KMS request costs further.

others.A: With SSE-C the customer supplies and rotates the keys, so there is no automatic rotation or KMS tracking.
others.B: SSE-S3 keys are fully managed by S3 and are invisible to KMS and CloudTrail, so rotation cannot be tracked.
others.D: Customer managed keys support yearly rotation but cost 1 USD per key per month, so they do not minimize key cost.

q: A company has migrated several applications to AWS in the past 3 months. The company wants to know the breakdown of costs for each of these applications. The company wants to receive a regular report that includes this information. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Use AWS Budgets to download data for the past 3 months into a .csv file. Look up the desired information.
o.B: Load AWS Cost and Usage Reports into an Amazon RDS DB instance. Run SQL queries to get the desired information.
o.C: Tag all the AWS resources with a key for cost and a value of the application's name. Activate cost allocation tags. Use Cost Explorerto get the desired information.
o.D: Tag all the AWS resources with a key for cost and a value of the application's name. Use the AWS Billing and Cost Management console todownload bills for the past 3 months. Look up the desired information.

e.why: Tagging resources by application and activating those tags as cost allocation tags in the Billing console lets Cost Explorer group and filter costs by application. Cost Explorer can also send regular reports. This is low cost and needs no extra infrastructure.

others.A: AWS Budgets tracks spend against thresholds and is not a per-application breakdown from untagged data.
others.B: Loading the CUR into RDS means paying for and running a database.
others.D: Tags must be activated as cost allocation tags before they appear in billing data, and downloading bills is manual.

e.tip: Tags only show up in cost reports after you activate them as cost allocation tags.

q: An ecommerce company is preparing to deploy a web application on AWS to ensure continuous service for customers. The architecture includes a web application that the company hosts on Amazon EC2 instances, a relational database in Amazon RDS, and static assets that the company stores in Amazon S3. The company wants to design a robust and resilient architecture for the application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone. Deploy an RDS DB instance in the same Availability Zone. Use Amazon S3 with versioning enabled to store static assets.
o.B: Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Deploy a Multi-AZ RDS DB instance. Use Amazon CloudFront to distribute static assets.
o.C: Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone. Deploy an RDS DB instance in a second Availability Zone for cross-AZ redundancy. Serve static assets directly from the EC2 instances.
o.D: Use AWS Lambda functions to serve the web application. Use Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 for the database. Store static assets in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) One Zone-Infrequent Access (One Zone-IA).

e.why: A multi-AZ Auto Scaling group keeps the web tier running if an AZ fails, and Multi-AZ RDS adds automatic database failover. CloudFront serves static assets from S3 with caching and durability. Together these give a resilient design for continuous service.

others.A: Putting everything in a single AZ is a single point of failure.
others.C: Single-AZ EC2 instances serving the static assets are still a single point of failure.
others.D: EFS One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, which undermines resilience, and it is a poor choice for web static assets.

q: An ecommerce company runs several internal applications in multiple AWS accounts. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage its AWS accounts. A security appliance in the company's networking account must inspect interactions between applications across AWS accounts. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in the networking account to send traffic to the security appliance. Configure the application accounts to send traffic to the NLB by using an interface VPC endpoint in the application accounts.
o.B: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in the application accounts to send traffic directly to the security appliance.
o.C: Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in the networking account to send traffic to the security appliance. Configure the application accounts to send traffic to the GWLB by using an interface GWLB endpoint in the application accounts.
o.D: Deploy an interface VPC endpoint in the application accounts to send traffic directly to the security appliance.

e.why: A Gateway Load Balancer is built to put third-party security appliances inline. It forwards traffic transparently over GENEVE and scales the appliance fleet. Gateway Load Balancer endpoints in the application accounts' VPCs, which work through PrivateLink, steer traffic across accounts to the central appliances for inspection.

others.A: An NLB behind an interface endpoint is for exposing a service. It does not route traffic transparently inline for inspection.
others.B: An ALB is a layer 7 proxy that ends connections and cannot steer traffic to appliances in another account.
others.D: An interface endpoint cannot send traffic straight to an appliance. It needs a PrivateLink service, such as GWLB, behind it.

e.tip: Inline inspection with third-party firewall or IDS appliances means Gateway Load Balancer and GWLB endpoints.

q: A company runs its production workload on an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster that includes six Aurora Replicas. The company wants near-real-time reporting queries from one of its departments to be automatically distributed across three of the Aurora Replicas. Those three replicas have a different compute and memory specification from the rest of the DB cluster. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Create and use a custom endpoint for the workload
o.B: Create a three-node cluster clone and use the reader endpoint
o.C: Use any of the instance endpoints for the selected three nodes
o.D: Use the reader endpoint to automatically distribute the read-only workload

e.why: An Aurora custom endpoint groups chosen DB instances, here the three replicas with different specs, and load balances connections across only those instances. The department's reporting queries are spread across them automatically.

others.B: A clone is a separate cluster that does not receive near-real-time production changes once it is created.
others.C: Instance endpoints point at one instance each, so the application would have to balance the load itself.
others.D: The reader endpoint balances across all six replicas, not just the three chosen ones.

e.tip: To send a workload to a subset of Aurora instances, use a custom endpoint.

q: A company runs a Node js function on a server in its on-premises data center. The data center stores data in a PostgreSQL database. The company stores the credentials in a connection string in an environment variable on the server. The company wants to migrate its application to AWS and to replace the Node.js application server with AWS Lambda. The company also wants to migrate to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and to ensure that the database credentials are securely managed. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Store the database credentials as a parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store Configure Parameter Store to automatically rotate the secrets every 30 days. Update the Lambda function to retrieve the credentials from the parameter.
o.B: Store the database credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure Secrets Manager to automatically rotate the credentials every 30 days. Update the Lambda function to retrieve the credentials from the secret.
o.C: Store the database credentials as an encrypted Lambda environment variable. Write a custom Lambda function to rotate the credentials. Schedule the Lambda function to run every 30 days.
o.D: Store the database credentials as a key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Configure automatic rotation for the key. Update the Lambda function to retneve the credentials from the KMS key.

e.why: Secrets Manager stores the RDS credentials encrypted and has built-in rotation for RDS for PostgreSQL, set here to every 30 days. Lambda fetches the secret at runtime. This is secure, managed credential handling with the least operational overhead.

others.A: Parameter Store has no built-in automatic rotation.
others.C: Writing your own rotation function and storing credentials in environment variables means more custom code and upkeep.
others.D: KMS stores encryption keys, not database credentials, and rotating the key does not change the password.

q: A company wants to replicate existing and ongoing data changes from an on-premises Oracle database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. The amount of data to replicate varies throughout each day. The company wants to use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) for data replication. The solution must allocate only the capacity that the replication instance requires. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure the AWS DMS replication instance with a Multi-AZ deployment to provision instances across multiple Availability Zones.
o.B: Create an AWS DMS Serverless replication task to analyze and replicate the data while provisioning the required capacity.
o.C: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale the size of the AWS DMS replication instance up or down based on the amount of data toreplicate.
o.D: Provision AWS DMS replication capacity by using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an AWS Fargate launch type to analyze and replicate the data while provisioning the required capacity.

e.why: DMS Serverless provisions replication capacity automatically and scales it with the actual workload, measured in DMS capacity units, so it allocates only what is needed. It supports full load plus ongoing change data capture from Oracle to RDS for Oracle.

others.A: Multi-AZ adds high availability but does not right-size capacity for a load that varies through the day.
others.C: EC2 Auto Scaling cannot manage DMS replication instances.
others.D: DMS does not run on ECS or Fargate.

q: A company has a multi-tier web application. The application's internal service components are deployed on Amazon EC2 instances. The internal service components need to access third-party software as a service (SaaS) APIs that are hosted on AWS. The company needs to provide secure and private connectivity from the application's internal services to the third-party SaaS application. The company needs to ensure that there is minimal public internet exposure. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Implement an AWS Site-to-Site VPN to establish a secure connection with the third-party SaaS provider.
o.B: Deploy AWS Transit Gateway to manage and route traffic between the application's VPC and the third-party SaaS provider.
o.C: Configure AWS PrivateLink to allow only outbound traffic from the VPC without enabling the third-party SaaS provider to establish.
o.D: Use AWS PrivateLink to create a private connection between the application's VPC and the third-party SaaS provider.

e.why: SaaS providers on AWS can publish an endpoint service behind an NLB. The consumer creates an interface VPC endpoint to it through AWS PrivateLink, and traffic then stays on the AWS network with private IPs and no internet exposure.

others.A: A Site-to-Site VPN connects to customer networks. It is not how you reach a SaaS service hosted on AWS, and it is heavier to run.
others.B: Transit Gateway needs the provider's VPC attached and exposes whole networks, not just one service.
others.C: PrivateLink is consumer-initiated and does not let the provider open connections into your VPC anyway. The real need is private access to the SaaS service, not an outbound-only setup.

e.tip: For private access to a SaaS service on AWS, use PrivateLink.

q: A solutions architect needs to connect a company's corporate network to its VPC to allow on-premises access to its AWS resources. The solution must provide encryption of all traffic between the corporate network and the VPC at the network layer and the session layer. The solution also must provide security controls to prevent unrestricted access between AWS and the on-premises systems. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Configure AWS Direct Connect to connect to the VPC. Configure the VPC route tables to allow and deny traffic between AWS and on premises as required.
o.B: Create an IAM policy to allow access to the AWS Management Console only from a defined set of corporate IP addresses. Restrict user access based on job responsibility by using an IAM policy and roles.
o.C: Configure AWS Site-to-Site VPN to connect to the VPConfigure route table entries to direct traffic from on premises to the VPConfigure instance security groups and network ACLs to allow only required traffic from on premises.
o.D: Configure AWS Transit Gateway to connect to the VPC. Configure route table entries to direct traffic from on premises to the VPC. Configure instance security groups and network ACLs to allow only required traffic from on premises.

e.why: Site-to-Site VPN encrypts all traffic between the corporate network and the VPC with IPsec at the network layer. Route tables, security groups, and network ACLs then allow only the traffic that is needed, which prevents unrestricted access between the environments.

others.A: Direct Connect is not encrypted by default, and route tables are not fine-grained security controls.
others.B: IAM console restrictions do not provide network connectivity or encryption.
others.D: Transit Gateway alone does not encrypt traffic or connect to on premises. It would still need a VPN or Direct Connect attachment.

q: A company has a custom application with embedded credentials that retrieves information from a database in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB cluster. The company needs to make the application more secure with minimal programming effort. The company has created credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Store the credentials in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Create keys in AWS KMS. Configure the application to load the database credentials from AWS KMS. Enable automatic key rotation
o.B: Store the credentials in encrypted local storage. Configure the application to load the database credentials from the local storage. Set up a credentials rotation schedule by creating a cron job.
o.C: Store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Set up a credentials rotation schedule by creating an AWS Lambda function for Secrets Manager.
o.D: Store the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Parameter Store. Set up a credentials rotation schedule in the RDS for MySQL database by using Parameter Store.

e.why: Secrets Manager removes the embedded credentials. The application loads them through an API call, which is a small code change. A rotation schedule, run by a Lambda rotation function that Secrets Manager provides for RDS MySQL, changes the password automatically.

others.A: KMS manages encryption keys, not database credentials, and rotating a key does not rotate the database password.
others.B: Encrypted local storage with a cron job is a custom, fragile solution that keeps secrets on the host.
others.D: Parameter Store cannot rotate credentials, and RDS has no rotation setting driven by Parameter Store.

q: A company wants to move its application to a serverless solution. The serverless solution needs to analyze existing data and new data by using SQL. The company stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data must be encrypted at rest and replicated to a different AWS Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create a new S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS multi-Region keys (SSE-KMS). Configure Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Load the data into the new S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
o.B: Create a new S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). Configure Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Load the data into the new S3 bucket. Use Amazon RDS to query the data.
o.C: Configure Cross-Region Replication (CRR) on the existing S3 bucket. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
o.D: Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) on the existing S3 bucket. Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS multi-Region keys (SSE-KMS). Use Amazon RDS to query the data.

e.why: Turning on CRR for the existing bucket, with S3 Batch Replication for objects already in it, replicates the data to the other Region. SSE-S3 provides encryption at rest at no extra cost or key management. Athena is serverless SQL directly on S3, so this has the least overhead.

others.A: Creating a new bucket and loading the data into it is extra work, and multi-Region KMS keys add management that the requirements do not need.
others.B: RDS is not serverless SQL over S3, and a new bucket means unnecessary data movement.
others.D: RDS cannot query data in S3 directly and is not serverless.

e.tip: For serverless SQL on data in S3, use Athena.

q: A company has a web application that has thousands of users. The application uses 8-10 user-uploaded images to generate AI images. Users can download the generated AI images once every 6 hours. The company also has a premium user option that gives users the ability to download the generated AI images anytime. The company uses the user-uploaded images to run AI model training twice a year. The company needs a storage solution to store the images. Which storage solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Move uploaded images to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive. Move premium user-generated AI images to S3 Standard. Move non-premium user-generated AI images to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).
o.B: Move uploaded images to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive Move all generated AI images to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
o.C: Move uploaded images to Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA). Move premium user-generated AI images to S3 Standard. Move non-premium user-generated AI images to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).
o.D: Move uploaded images to Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA). Move all generated AI images to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.

e.why: The uploaded images are used for training only twice a year, so Glacier Deep Archive's very low storage price fits, and its retrieval time of up to 48 hours is acceptable. Premium users need downloads at any time, which suits S3 Standard. Non-premium users download at most every 6 hours, which suits the cheaper Standard-IA with millisecond access.

others.B: Glacier Flexible Retrieval takes minutes to hours to retrieve, which is too slow for premium on-demand downloads.
others.C: One Zone-IA costs more than Deep Archive for data read only twice a year, and it lacks multi-AZ resilience.
others.D: Glacier Flexible Retrieval is too slow for user downloads, and One Zone-IA costs more for the training images.

q: A company is developing machine learning (ML) models on AWS. The company is developing the ML models as independent microservices. The microservices fetch approximately 1 GB of model data from Amazon S3 at startup and load the data into memory. Users access the ML models through an asynchronous API. Users can send a request or a batch of requests. The company provides the ML models to hundreds of users. The usage patterns for the models are irregular. Some models are not used for days or weeks. Other models receive batches of thousands of requests at a time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Direct the requests from the API to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Deploy the ML models as AWS Lambda functions that the NLB will invoke. Use auto scaling to scale the Lambda functions based on the traffic that the NLB receives.
o.B: Direct the requests from the API to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy the ML models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that the ALB will invoke. Use auto scaling to scale the ECS cluster instances based on the traffic that the ALB receives.
o.C: Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the ML models as AWS Lambda functions that SQS events will invoke. Use auto scaling to increase the number of vCPUs for the Lambda functions based on the size of the SQS queue.
o.D: Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the ML models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from the queue. Use auto scaling for Amazon ECS to scale both the cluster capacity and number of the services based on the size of the SQS queue.

e.why: An SQS queue buffers the asynchronous batch requests. ECS services poll it and scale task count and cluster capacity, through capacity providers, based on queue depth, scaling to zero for models that sit idle. Containers can load 1 GB of model data into memory once and reuse it.

others.A: An NLB cannot invoke Lambda, since only ALB supports Lambda targets, and loading 1 GB per cold start is inefficient.
others.B: An ALB is for synchronous requests. For asynchronous bursts, scaling on queue depth handles load better.
others.C: You cannot auto scale the vCPUs of a Lambda function. They are set by its memory setting.

q: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application stores data in an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. The company needs to create a disaster recovery (DR) solution. The acceptable recovery time for the DR solution is up to 30 minutes. The DR solution does not need to support customer usage when the primary infrastructure is healthy. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Deploy the DR infrastructure in a second AWS Region with an ALB and an Auto Scaling group. Set the desired capacity and maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group to a minimum value. Convert the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to an Aurora global database. Configure Amazon Route 53 for an active-passive failover with ALB endpoints.
o.B: Deploy the DR infrastructure in a second AWS Region with an ALUpdate the Auto Scaling group to include EC2 instances from the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Convert the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to an Aurora global database.
o.C: Back up the Aurora MySQL DB cluster data by using AWS Backup. Deploy the DR infrastructure in a second AWS Region with an ALB. Update the Auto Scaling group to include EC2 instances from the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Create an Aurora MySQL DB cluster in the second Region Restore the data from the backup.
o.D: Back up the infrastructure configuration by using AWS Backup. Use the backup to create the required infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Set the Auto Scaling group desired capacity to zero. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Convert the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to an Aurora global database.

e.why: A 30-minute RTO with no active use of the DR site fits pilot light or warm standby. A minimal Auto Scaling group and ALB in a second Region, an Aurora global database with replication lag usually under 1 second and managed failover, and Route 53 active-passive failover meet the RTO at low cost.

others.B: An Auto Scaling group cannot span Regions, and active-active is not needed while the primary is healthy.
others.C: Restoring Aurora from a backup can exceed 30 minutes, and active-active is unnecessary.
others.D: AWS Backup cannot back up and recreate whole infrastructure configurations such as ALBs and Auto Scaling groups.

q: A company is migrating its data processing application to the AWS Cloud. The application processes several short-lived batch jobs that cannot be disrupted. Data is generated after each batch job is completed. The data is accessed for 30 days and retained for 2 years. The company wants to keep the cost of running the application in the AWS Cloud as low as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Migrate the data processing application to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Store the data in Amazon S3 Standard. Move the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Instant. Retrieval after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.
o.B: Migrate the data processing application to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Store the data in Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. Move the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.
o.C: Deploy Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to run the batch jobs. Store the data in Amazon S3 Standard. Move the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.
o.D: Deploy Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances to run the batch jobs. Store the data in Amazon S3 Standard. Move the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.

e.why: The batch jobs cannot be disrupted, so they need On-Demand capacity rather than Spot. The data is read for 30 days in S3 Standard. It is then kept only for retention, so Glacier Deep Archive is the cheapest place for it, and an expiration rule deletes it at 2 years.

others.A: Spot Instances can interrupt the jobs, and Glacier Instant Retrieval costs more than Deep Archive for data that is only retained.
others.B: Glacier Instant Retrieval for the first 30 days of active access has high retrieval fees and a 90-day minimum storage charge.
others.C: Spot Instances can interrupt the jobs, which cannot be disrupted.

q: A company needs to design a hybrid network architecture. The company's workloads are currently stored in the AWS Cloud and in on-premises data centers. The workloads require single-digit latencies to communicate. The company uses an AWS Transit Gateway transit gateway to connect multiple VPCs. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

o.A: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to each VPC.
o.B: Associate an AWS Direct Connect gateway with the transit gateway that is attached to the VPCs.
o.C: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to an AWS Direct Connect gateway.
o.D: Establish an AWS Direct Connect connection. Create a transit virtual interface (VIF) to a Direct Connect gateway.
o.E: Associate AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections with the transit gateway that is attached to the VPCs.

e.why: Direct Connect gives private, consistent low-latency links that meet the single-digit latency need. A transit VIF to a Direct Connect gateway, with that gateway associated with the existing transit gateway, reaches all attached VPCs over one connection, which is cost-effective.

others.A: VPN connections to each VPC run over the internet with variable latency and add many tunnels to manage.
others.C: Site-to-Site VPN cannot attach to a Direct Connect gateway in that way. VPN latency is variable anyway.
others.E: VPN connections to the transit gateway go over the internet and cannot guarantee low, consistent latency.

q: A global ecommerce company runs its critical workloads on AWS. The workloads use an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance that is configured for a Multi-AZ deployment. Customers have reported application timeouts when the company undergoes database failovers. The company needs a resilient solution to reduce failover time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon RDS Proxy. Assign the proxy to the DB instance.
o.B: Create a read replica for the DB instance. Move the read traffic to the read replica.
o.C: Enable Performance Insights. Monitor the CPU load to identify the timeouts.
o.D: Take regular automatic snapshots. Copy the automatic snapshots to multiple AWS Regions.

e.why: RDS Proxy keeps a pool of connections to the database. During a Multi-AZ failover it reroutes to the new primary without waiting for DNS to propagate, cutting failover times by up to 66% and keeping client connections open. That reduces timeouts.

others.B: A read replica offloads reads but does not change how long a Multi-AZ failover takes.
others.C: Performance Insights only shows where load comes from and does not reduce failover time.
others.D: Cross-Region snapshots support disaster recovery but do not speed up failover.

e.tip: For faster RDS failover or connection storms, use RDS Proxy.

q: A company has multiple Amazon RDS DB instances that run in a development AWS account. All the instances have tags to identify them as development resources. The company needs the development DB instances to run on a schedule only during business hours. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to identify RDS instances that need to be stopped. Create an AWS Lambda function to start and stop the RDS instances.
o.B: Create an AWS Trusted Advisor report to identify RDS instances to be started and stopped. Create an AWS Lambda function to start and stop the RDS instances.
o.C: Create AWS Systems Manager State Manager associations to start and stop the RDS instances.
o.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes AWS Lambda functions to start and stop the RDS instances.

e.why: EventBridge Scheduler or scheduled rules run cron expressions for business hours and invoke Lambda functions. The functions call StartDBInstance and StopDBInstance on the instances that have the development tag. It is simple, serverless, and needs little upkeep.

others.A: CloudWatch alarms respond to metric thresholds, not to a time schedule.
others.B: Trusted Advisor gives recommendations and cannot drive a start and stop schedule.
others.C: State Manager can run Automation runbooks on a schedule, but the keyed answer treats an EventBridge schedule as the simpler pattern.

e.tip: Anything that runs on a time schedule points to EventBridge Scheduler or scheduled rules.

q: A consumer survey company has gathered data for several years from a specific geographic region. The company stores this data in an Amazon S3 bucket in an AWS Region. The company has started to share this data with a marketing firm in a new geographic region. The company has granted the firm's AWS account access to the S3 bucket. The company wants to minimize the data transfer costs when the marketing firm requests data from the S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure the Requester Pays feature on the company’s S3 bucket.
o.B: Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) from the company’s S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm’s S3 buckets.
o.C: Configure AWS Resource Access Manager to share the S3 bucket with the marketing firm AWS account.
o.D: Configure the company’s S3 bucket to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering Sync the S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm’s S3 buckets.

e.why: Requester Pays makes the requester's account, here the marketing firm, pay the request and data transfer charges for downloads from the bucket. The bucket owner's data transfer costs drop to nothing.

others.B: Cross-Region Replication makes the company pay for inter-Region transfer and for replicating years of data.
others.C: S3 buckets cannot be shared through AWS Resource Access Manager in this way, and it would not change who pays for transfer.
others.D: Intelligent-Tiering optimizes storage class, and syncing to another bucket still incurs transfer charges.

q: A company uses AWS to host its public ecommerce website. The website uses an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator for traffic from the internet. The Global Accelerator accelerator forwards the traffic to an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that is the entry point for an Auto Scaling group. The company recently identified a DDoS attack on the website. The company needs a solution to mitigate future attacks. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

o.A: Configure an AWS WAF web ACL for the Global Accelerator accelerator to block traffic by using rate-based rules
o.B: Configure an AWS Lambda function to read the ALB metrics to block attacks by updating a VPC network ACL
o.C: Configure an AWS WAF web ACL on the ALB to block traffic by using rate-based rules
o.D: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the Global Accelerator accelerator

e.why: AWS WAF can be associated with the ALB. A rate-based rule automatically blocks IP addresses that go over a request threshold, which mitigates HTTP flood DDoS attacks at layer 7. Global Accelerator already brings Shield Standard protection at layers 3 and 4, so adding WAF to the ALB takes the least effort.

others.A: AWS WAF cannot be associated with a Global Accelerator accelerator.
others.B: A custom Lambda function that updates network ACLs takes a lot of effort, and network ACLs have low rule limits.
others.D: CloudFront cannot use a Global Accelerator accelerator as its origin in this design, and the change would re-architect the entry point.

q: A company uses an Amazon DynamoDB table to store data that the company receives from devices. The DynamoDB table supports a customer-facing website to display recent activity on customer devices. The company configured the table with provisioned throughput for writes and reads. The company wants to calculate performance metrics for customer device data on a daily basis. The solution must have minimal effect on the table's provisioned read and write capacity. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use an Amazon Athena SQL query with the Amazon Athena DynamoDB connector to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.
o.B: Use an AWS Glue job with the AWS Glue DynamoDB export connector to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.
o.C: Use an Amazon Redshift COPY command to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.
o.D: Use an Amazon EMR job with an Apache Hive external table to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.

e.why: The AWS Glue DynamoDB export connector uses DynamoDB's export to S3 feature, which relies on point-in-time recovery. The export reads from backups and does not use the table's provisioned read capacity, so the daily metric jobs have minimal effect on the live table.

others.A: The Athena DynamoDB connector scans the live table and uses its read capacity.
others.C: A Redshift COPY from DynamoDB reads the table directly and uses provisioned read capacity.
others.D: EMR Hive external tables over DynamoDB scan the table and use read capacity.

e.tip: If an analytics job must not consume a DynamoDB table's capacity, export the table to S3 first.

q: A solutions architect is designing the cloud architecture for a new stateless application that will be deployed on AWS. The solutions architect created an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) and launch template for the application. Based on the number of jobs that need to be processed, the processing must run in parallel while adding and removing application Amazon EC2 instances as needed. The application must be loosely coupled. The job items must be durably stored. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Auto Scaling group by using the launch template with the scaling policy set to add and remove EC2 instances based on CPU usage.
o.B: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Auto Scaling group by using the launch template with the scaling policy set to add and remove EC2 instances based on network usage.
o.C: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Auto Scaling group by using the launch template with the scaling policy set to add and remove EC2 instances based on the number of items in the SQS queue.
o.D: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Auto Scaling group by using the launch template with the scaling policy set to add and remove EC2 instances based on the number of messages published to the SNS topic.

e.why: An SQS queue stores jobs durably and decouples the producers from the workers. Scaling the Auto Scaling group on the number of messages in the queue, ideally the backlog per instance, adds and removes instances to match the job count, and the instances process jobs in parallel.

others.A: SNS pushes messages to subscribers and does not store jobs durably, and CPU usage does not reflect the job backlog.
others.B: Network usage does not reflect how many jobs are waiting.
others.D: SNS does not store jobs, and the number of published messages does not show how much work is outstanding.

e.tip: For durable jobs plus worker scaling, use SQS and scale on queue depth.

q: A global ecommerce company uses a monolithic architecture. The company needs a solution to manage the increasing volume of product data. The solution must be scalable and have a modular service architecture. The company needs to maintain its structured database schemas. The company also needs a storage solution to store product data and product images. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group to deploy a containerized application. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute web traffic. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance to store product data and product images.
o.B: Use AWS Lambda functions to manage the existing monolithic application. Use Amazon DynamoDB to store product data and product images. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) for event-driven communication between the Lambda functions.
o.C: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with an Amazon EC2 deployment to deploy a containerized application. Use an Amazon Aurora cluster to store the product data. Use AWS Step Functions to manage workflows. Store the product images in Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
o.D: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate to deploy a containerized application. Use Amazon RDS with a Multi-AZ deployment to store the product data. Store the product images in an Amazon S3 bucket.

e.why: ECS on Fargate runs modular containerized services with no servers to manage. RDS Multi-AZ keeps the structured relational schemas with managed high availability, and S3 is the scalable, low-cost place to store product images. This has the least operational overhead.

others.A: Containers on self-managed EC2 instances add overhead, and storing images in RDS is inefficient.
others.B: DynamoDB does not keep the structured relational schemas, and lifting a monolith into Lambda is impractical.
others.C: EKS on EC2 adds operational overhead, and Glacier Deep Archive is far too slow for serving product images.

q: A company is migrating an application from an on-premises environment to AWS. The application will store sensitive data in Amazon S3. The company must encrypt the data before storing the data in Amazon S3. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Encrypt the data by using client-side encryption with customer managed keys.
o.B: Encrypt the data by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
o.C: Encrypt the data by using server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C).
o.D: Encrypt the data by using client-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys.

e.why: Encrypting the data before it is stored in S3 means encrypting on the client side, before upload. Client-side encryption with customer managed keys, for example through the AWS Encryption SDK with a KMS key, makes sure S3 receives only ciphertext.

others.B: With SSE-KMS, S3 encrypts the data after it arrives, so the data is not encrypted before it reaches S3.
others.C: SSE-C is still server-side encryption: S3 encrypts with your key after receiving plaintext over HTTPS.
others.D: S3 managed keys are used only for server-side encryption and cannot be used for client-side encryption.

e.tip: The phrase before storing in S3 or before sending means client-side encryption.

q: A company wants to create an Amazon EMR cluster that multiple teams will use. The company wants to ensure that each team’s big data workloads can access only the AWS services that each team needs to interact with. The company does not want the workloads to have access to Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) on the cluster’s underlying EC2 instances. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Configure interface VPC endpoints for each AWS service that the teams need. Use the required interface VPC endpoints to submit the big data workloads.
o.B: Create EMR runtime roles. Configure the cluster to use the runtime roles. Use the runtime roles to submit the big data workloads.
o.C: Create an EC2 IAM instance profile that has the required permissions for each team. Use the instance profile to submit the big data workloads.
o.D: Create an EMR security configuration that has the EnableApplicationScopedIAMRole option set to false. Use the security configuration to submit the big data workloads.

e.why: EMR runtime roles let each team's job, submitted as an EMR step or through Lake Formation, assume its own IAM role with only the permissions that team needs. When runtime roles are enabled, EMR blocks workloads from using the instance profile through IMDS, which meets the requirement to deny IMDSv2 access.

others.A: VPC endpoints give private network paths but do not limit each team's IAM permissions or block IMDS.
others.C: An instance profile is shared across the whole cluster and is reached through IMDS, which is exactly what must be avoided.
others.D: Setting the application-scoped IAM role option to false does not give each team scoped roles.

q: A solutions architect is designing an application that helps users fill out and submit registration forms. The solutions architect plans to use a two-tier architecture that includes a web application server tier and a worker tier. The application needs to process submitted forms quickly. The application needs to process each form exactly once. The solution must ensure that no data is lost. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue between the web application server tier and the worker tier to store and forward form data.
o.B: Use an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API between the web application server tier and the worker tier to store and forward form data.
o.C: Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue between the web application server tier and the worker tier to store and forward form data.
o.D: Use an AWS Step Functions workflow. Create a synchronous workflow between the web application server tier and the worker tier that stores and forwards form data.

e.why: An SQS FIFO queue provides exactly-once processing through deduplication IDs within a 5-minute window, preserves ordering, and stores messages durably across multiple AZs. That decouples the web and worker tiers without losing data or processing a form twice.

others.B: API Gateway forwards requests but does not durably store and forward messages to workers.
others.C: A standard queue delivers at least once, so a form can be processed more than once.
others.D: A synchronous Step Functions workflow tightly couples the tiers and is not a buffer between them.

e.tip: The phrase exactly once means an SQS FIFO queue.

q: A finance company uses an on-premises search application to collect streaming data from various producers. The application provides real-time updates to search and visualization features. The company is planning to migrate to AWS and wants to use an AWS native solution. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon EC2 instances to ingest and process the data streams to Amazon S3 buckets tor storage. Use Amazon Athena to search the data. Use Amazon Managed Grafana to create visualizations.
o.B: Use Amazon EMR to ingest and process the data streams to Amazon Redshift for storage. Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to search the data. Use Amazon QuickSight to create visualizations.
o.C: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to ingest and process the data streams to Amazon DynamoDB for storage. Use Amazon CloudWatch to create graphical dashboards to search and visualize the data.
o.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest and process the data streams to Amazon OpenSearch Service. Use OpenSearch Service to search the data. Use Amazon QuickSight to create visualizations.

e.why: Kinesis Data Streams ingests streaming data from many producers in real time, with Firehose or a consumer loading it continuously into OpenSearch Service. OpenSearch gives near-real-time full-text search and analytics, and QuickSight builds visualizations.

others.A: Self-managed EC2 ingestion plus Athena queries over S3 is not real-time search.
others.B: EMR and Redshift Spectrum are batch analytics, not real-time search.
others.C: DynamoDB with CloudWatch dashboards does not give full-text search.

q: A company currently runs an on-premises application that usesASP.NET on Linux machines. The application is resource-intensive and serves customers directly. The company wants to modernize the application to .NET. The company wants to run the application on containers and to scale based on Amazon CloudWatch metrics. The company also wants to reduce the time spent on operational maintenance activities. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use AWS App2Container to containerize the application. Use an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
o.B: Use AWS App2Container to containerize the application. Use an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2 instances.
o.C: Use AWS App Runner to containerize the application. Use App Runner to deploy the application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
o.D: Use AWS App Runner to containerize the application. Use App Runner to deploy the application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) on Amazon EC2 instances.

e.why: AWS App2Container analyzes existing .NET or Java applications and containerizes them, producing CloudFormation templates for ECS or EKS. Deploying to ECS on Fargate removes server management, and ECS Service Auto Scaling uses CloudWatch metrics, so this has the least operational overhead.

others.B: ECS on EC2 instances means managing and patching the container hosts.
others.C: App Runner does not containerize applications and does not deploy to ECS. It runs services from code or images on its own platform.
others.D: App Runner does not containerize applications or deploy to EKS, and EKS on EC2 adds overhead.

q: A company is designing a new internal web application in the AWS Cloud. The new application must securely retrieve and store multiple employee usernames and passwords from an AWS managed service. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Store the employee credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Use AWS CloudFormation and the BatchGetSecretValue API to retrieve usernames and passwords from Parameter Store.
o.B: Store the employee credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Use AWS CloudFormation and AWS Batch with the BatchGetSecretValue API to retrieve the usernames and passwords from Secrets Manager.
o.C: Store the employee credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Use AWS CloudFormation and AWS Batch with the BatchGetSecretValue API to retrieve the usernames and passwords from Parameter Store.
o.D: Store the employee credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Use AWS CloudFormation and the BatchGetSecretValue API to retrieve the usernames and passwords from Secrets Manager.

e.why: Secrets Manager is the managed service for storing credentials securely, and its BatchGetSecretValue API retrieves several secrets in one call. Using it directly, with CloudFormation to provision the secrets, has the least overhead.

others.A: BatchGetSecretValue is a Secrets Manager API, not a Parameter Store API.
others.B: AWS Batch is a compute job scheduler and is not needed to call a Secrets Manager API.
others.C: Parameter Store does not offer BatchGetSecretValue, and AWS Batch is unnecessary.

q: A company that is in the ap-northeast-1 Region has a fleet of thousands of AWS Outposts servers. The company has deployed the servers at remote locations around the world. All the servers regularly download new software versions that consist of 100 files. There is significant latency before all servers run the new software versions. The company must reduce the deployment latency for new software versions. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create an Amazon S3 bucket in ap-northeast-1. Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution in ap-northeast-1 that includes a CachingDisabled cache policy. Configure the S3 bucket as the origin. Download the software by using signed URLs.
o.B: Create an Amazon S3 bucket in ap-northeast-1. Create a second S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. Configure replication between the buckets. Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses ap-northeast-1 as the primary origin and us-east-1 as the secondary origin. Download the software by using signed URLs.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket in ap-northeast-1. Configure Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration. Download the software by using the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint.
o.D: Create an Amazon S3 bucket in ap-northeast-1. Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the S3 bucket as the origin. Download the software by using signed URLs.

e.why: A CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket caches the 100 software files at edge locations around the world. Once the files are cached, thousands of remote servers download from a nearby edge instead of from Tokyo, which cuts deployment latency with little to manage. Signed URLs keep access restricted.

others.A: CloudFront is global, not regional, and turning caching off removes the latency benefit.
others.B: Adding a second bucket in us-east-1 with origin failover improves availability, not latency, and adds replication to manage.
others.C: Transfer Acceleration speeds up long-distance transfers but does not cache, so every server still pulls each file from the origin.

e.tip: Many clients downloading the same files means a caching CDN, so choose CloudFront.

q: A company currently runs an on-premises stock trading application by using Microsoft Windows Server. The company wants to migrate the application to the AWS Cloud. The company needs to design a highly available solution that provides low-latency access to block storage across multiple Availability Zones. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

o.A: Configure a Windows Server cluster that spans two Availability Zones on Amazon EC2 instances. Install the application on both cluster nodes. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server as shared storage between the two cluster nodes.
o.B: Configure a Windows Server cluster that spans two Availability Zones on Amazon EC2 instances. Install the application on both cluster nodes. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) General Purpose SSD (gp3) volumes as storage attached to the EC2 instances. Set up application-level replication to sync data from one EBS volume in one Availability Zone to another EBS volume in the second Availability Zone.
o.C: Deploy the application on Amazon EC2 instances in two Availability Zones. Configure one EC2 instance as active and the second EC2 instance in standby mode. Use an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP Multi-AZ file system to access the data by using Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) protocol.
o.D: Deploy the application on Amazon EC2 instances in two Availability Zones. Configure one EC2 instance as active and the second EC2 instance in standby mode. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volumes as storage attached to the EC2 instances. Set up Amazon EBS level replication to sync data from one io2 volume in one Availability Zone to another io2 volume in the second Availability Zone.

e.why: FSx for NetApp ONTAP Multi-AZ provides block storage over iSCSI, with synchronous replication and automatic failover across AZs. An active-standby pair of EC2 instances can both reach the same LUN, giving low-latency, highly available block storage without custom replication.

others.A: FSx for Windows File Server provides SMB file storage, not block storage.
others.B: Replicating EBS volumes at the application level takes considerable implementation effort.
others.D: EBS has no native replication across AZs, because volumes are tied to one AZ.

e.tip: For shared block storage across AZs, use FSx for NetApp ONTAP over iSCSI.

q: A company is designing a web application with an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company needs the ALB to receive HTTPS web traffic from the public internet. The ALB must send only HTTPS traffic to the web application servers hosted on the Amazon EC2 instances on port 443. The ALB must perform a health check of the web application servers over HTTPS on port 8443. Which combination of configurations of the security group that is associated with the ALB will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

o.A: Allow HTTPS inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 for port 443.
o.B: Allow all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 for port 443.
o.C: Allow HTTPS outbound traffic to the web application instances for port 443.
o.D: Allow HTTPS inbound traffic from the web application instances for port 443.
o.E: Allow HTTPS outbound traffic to the web application instances for the health check on port 8443.
o.F: Allow HTTPS inbound traffic from the web application instances for the health check on port 8443.

e.why: The ALB's security group needs three rules. An inbound rule allows HTTPS on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 for public clients. An outbound rule allows port 443 to the web instances for forwarded traffic. Another outbound rule allows port 8443 to the instances for health checks. Security groups are stateful, so response traffic does not need its own rules.

others.B: Allowing all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 is broader than needed, so least privilege points to the instance targets.
others.D: Inbound rules from the instances are not needed, because responses are allowed automatically by stateful tracking.
others.F: The ALB starts the health checks, so they need an outbound rule, not an inbound one.

e.tip: Security groups are stateful: allow the direction in which the connection is opened.

q: A company hosts an application on AWS. The application gives users the ability to upload photos and store the photos in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to use Amazon CloudFront and a custom domain name to upload the photo files to the S3 bucket in the eu-west-1 Region. Which solution will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a public certificate in the us-east-1 Region. Use the certificate in CloudFront.
o.B: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a public certificate in eu-west-1. Use the certificate in CloudFront.
o.C: Configure Amazon S3 to allow uploads from CloudFront. Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration.
o.D: Configure Amazon S3 to allow uploads from CloudFront origin access control (OAC).
o.E: Configure Amazon S3 to allow uploads from CloudFront. Configure an Amazon S3 website endpoint.

e.why: CloudFront accepts custom-domain certificates only from ACM in us-east-1. Origin access control signs CloudFront's requests to S3 with SigV4 and supports PUT and POST uploads, so the bucket policy can allow uploads only from the distribution through OAC.

others.B: CloudFront cannot use ACM certificates from eu-west-1.
others.C: Transfer Acceleration is a separate S3 feature and not how uploads through CloudFront are authorized.
others.E: S3 website endpoints do not support uploads or OAC, and they serve only GET requests over HTTP.

e.tip: Certificates for CloudFront must come from ACM in us-east-1.

q: A weather forecasting company collects temperature readings from various sensors on a continuous basis. An existing data ingestion process collects the readings and aggregates the readings into larger Apache Parquet files. Then the process encrypts the files by using client-side encryption with KMS managed keys (CSE-KMS). Finally, the process writes the files to an Amazon S3 bucket with separate prefixes for each calendar day. The company wants to run occasional SQL queries on the data to take sample moving averages for a specific calendar day. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure Amazon Athena to read the encrypted files. Run SQL queries on the data directly in Amazon S3.
o.B: Use Amazon S3 Select to run SQL queries on the data directly in Amazon S3.
o.C: Configure Amazon Redshift to read the encrypted files. Use Redshift Spectrum and Redshift query editor v2 to run SQL queries on the data directly in Amazon S3.
o.D: Configure Amazon EMR Serverless to read the encrypted files. Use Apache SparkSQL to run SQL queries on the data directly in Amazon S3.

e.why: Athena runs SQL directly on Parquet files in S3, supports reading CSE-KMS encrypted data when the table is configured for it, and charges only per TB scanned. The daily prefixes allow partition pruning, which makes it the cheapest choice for occasional queries.

others.B: S3 Select does not support client-side encrypted objects or moving-average queries, and it is closed to new customers.
others.C: Redshift Spectrum needs a Redshift cluster or Serverless workgroup, which costs more for occasional queries.
others.D: EMR Serverless with Spark SQL takes more setup and costs more than Athena for occasional sampling.

e.tip: For occasional SQL on S3, choose Athena.

q: A company is implementing a new application on AWS. The company will run the application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones within multiple AWS Regions. The application will be available through the internet. Users will access the application from around the world. The company wants to ensure that each user who accesses the application is sent to the EC2 instances that are closest to the user’s location. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Implement an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy. Use an internet-facing Application Load Balancer to distribute the traffic across all Availability Zones within the same Region.
o.B: Implement an Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing policy. Use an internet-facing Network Load Balancer to distribute the traffic across all Availability Zones within the same Region.
o.C: Implement an Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy. Use an internet-facing Application Load Balancer to distribute the traffic across all Availability Zones within the same Region.
o.D: Implement an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy. Use an internet-facing Network Load Balancer to distribute the traffic across all Availability Zones within the same Region.

e.why: Geoproximity routing sends users to the resource that is geographically closest to them, and you can shift that with a bias. That matches the requirement to reach the closest EC2 instances. Within each Region, an internet-facing NLB spreads traffic across the AZs.

others.A: Geolocation routing chooses a target by the user's country or continent, not the nearest Region, so users near a border can be sent farther away.
others.C: Multivalue answer routing returns random healthy records and ignores location.
others.D: Weighted routing splits traffic by fixed ratios, not by the user's location.

e.tip: Geolocation follows where the user is, for example by country. Geoproximity follows physical distance and can be biased.

q: A financial services company plans to launch a new application on AWS to handle sensitive financial transactions. The company will deploy the application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company will use Amazon RDS for MySQL as the database. The company’s security policies mandate that data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Configure encryption at rest for Amazon RDS for MySQL by using AWS KMS managed keys. Configure AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) SSL/TLS certificates for encryption in transit.
o.B: Configure encryption at rest for Amazon RDS for MySQL by using AWS KMS managed keys. Configure IPsec tunnels for encryption in transit.
o.C: Implement third-party application-level data encryption before storing data in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Configure AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) SSL/TLS certificates for encryption in transit.
o.D: Configure encryption at rest for Amazon RDS for MySQL by using AWS KMS managed keys. Configure a VPN connection to enable private connectivity to encrypt data in transit.

e.why: RDS encryption at rest with KMS is a single setting at creation time and covers storage, backups, snapshots, and replicas. For encryption in transit, TLS is used: RDS supplies server certificates, and ACM can provide TLS certificates for the application endpoints such as an ALB. Both are managed, so this has the least operational overhead.

others.B: Running IPsec tunnels between EC2 and RDS inside a VPC adds operational complexity that is not needed.
others.C: Third-party application-level encryption adds code and key management overhead.
others.D: A VPN is meant for connecting outside networks and is not needed to encrypt traffic between EC2 and RDS.

q: A company is migrating its on-premises Oracle database to an Amazon RDS for Oracle database. The company needs to retain data for 90 days to meet regulatory requirements. The company must also be able to restore the database to a specific point in time for up to 14 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create Amazon RDS automated backups. Set the retention period to 90 days.
o.B: Create an Amazon RDS manual snapshot every day. Delete manual snapshots that are older than 90 days.
o.C: Use the Amazon Aurora Clone feature for Oracle to create a point-in-time restore. Delete clones that are older than 90 days.
o.D: Create a backup plan that has a retention period of 90 days by using AWS Backup for Amazon RDS.

e.why: An AWS Backup plan can keep RDS snapshots for 90 days and can also turn on continuous backups, which give point-in-time restore for up to 35 days and so cover the 14-day need, all under one managed policy. RDS automated backups alone are capped at 35 days of retention.

others.A: RDS automated backup retention has a maximum of 35 days, so it cannot be set to 90 days.
others.B: Taking and deleting daily manual snapshots is operational work and does not give point-in-time restore.
others.C: Aurora cloning does not exist for RDS for Oracle, and a clone is not a backup.

e.tip: RDS automated backups top out at 35 days. For longer retention, use AWS Backup or manual snapshots.

q: A company is developing a new application that uses a relational database to store user data and application configurations. The company expects the application to have steady user growth. The company expects the database usage to be variable and read-heavy, with occasional writes. The company wants to cost-optimize the database solution. The company wants to use an AWS managed database solution that will provide the necessary performance. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Deploy the database on Amazon RDS. Use Provisioned IOPS SSD storage to ensure consistent performance for read and write operations.
o.B: Deploy the database on Amazon Aurora Serverless to automatically scale the database capacity based on actual usage to accommodate the workload.
o.C: Deploy the database on Amazon DynamoDB. Use on-demand capacity mode to automatically scale throughput to accommodate the workload.
o.D: Deploy the database on Amazon RDS. Use magnetic storage and use read replicas to accommodate the workload.

e.why: Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity, measured in ACUs, up and down in fine increments with actual load, so a variable, read-heavy relational workload pays only for what it uses. It is fully managed and can add readers as growth continues.

others.A: Provisioned IOPS storage is billed whether or not it is used, which is costly for variable demand.
others.C: DynamoDB is not relational, and the application needs a relational database.
others.D: Magnetic storage is previous generation with poor performance and is not recommended.

q: A company hosts its application on several Amazon EC2 instances inside a VPC. The company creates a dedicated Amazon S3 bucket for each customer to store their relevant information in Amazon S3. The company wants to ensure that the application running on EC2 instances can securely access only the S3 buckets that belong to the company’s AWS account. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 that is attached to the VPC. Update the IAM instance profile policy to provide access to only the specific buckets that the application needs.
o.B: Create a NAT gateway in a public subnet with a security group that allows access to only Amazon S3. Update the route tables to use the NAT Gateway.
o.C: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 that is attached to the VPUpdate the IAM instance profile policy with a Deny action and the following condition key:
o.D: Create a NAT Gateway in a public subnet. Update route tables to use the NAT Gateway. Assign bucket policies for all buckets with a Deny action and the following condition key:

e.why: A gateway endpoint sends S3 traffic privately at no charge. A Deny statement in the instance profile policy with the condition s3:ResourceAccount (or aws:ResourceAccount) not equal to the company's account ID blocks access to any bucket outside the account. That covers every customer bucket, including new ones, without listing each bucket.

others.A: Listing specific buckets in the policy has to be updated every time a customer bucket is added, which is more overhead.
others.B: A NAT gateway costs money, security groups cannot filter by AWS service, and nothing limits access to the company's own buckets.
others.D: A NAT gateway adds cost, and keeping deny statements in every bucket policy is more work than one identity policy.

e.tip: To limit access to your own account's buckets, use a Deny with the aws:ResourceAccount or s3:ResourceAccount condition.

q: A company is building a cloud-based application on AWS that will handle sensitive customer data. The application uses Amazon RDS for the database, Amazon S3 for object storage, and S3 Event Notifications that invoke AWS Lambda for serverless processing. The company uses AWS IAM Identity Center to manage user credentials. The development, testing, and operations teams need secure access to Amazon RDS and Amazon S3 while ensuring the confidentiality of sensitive customer data. The solution must comply with the principle of least privilege. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use IAM roles with least privilege to grant all the teams access. Assign IAM roles to each team with customized IAM policies defining specific permission for Amazon RDS and S3 object access based on team responsibilities.
o.B: Enable IAM Identity Center with an Identity Center directory. Create and configure permission sets with granular access to Amazon RDS and Amazon S3. Assign all the teams to groups that have specific access with the permission sets.
o.C: Create individual IAM users for each member in all the teams with role-based permissions. Assign the IAM roles with predefined policies for RDS and S3 access to each user based on user needs. Implement IAM Access Analyzer for periodic credential evaluation.
o.D: Use AWS Organizations to create separate accounts for each team. Implement cross-account IAM roles with least privilege. Grant specific permission for RDS and S3 access based on team roles and responsibilities.

e.why: The company already uses IAM Identity Center. Permission sets give granular, least-privilege access to RDS and S3, and assigning them to team groups provisions short-term role credentials in each account. This is central and needs the least management.

others.A: Hand-building IAM roles for each team in each account takes more effort than using permission sets.
others.C: Individual IAM users mean long-term credentials and higher management overhead.
others.D: Creating a separate account for each team with cross-account roles adds a lot of overhead.

q: A company has an Amazon S3 bucket that contains sensitive data files. The company has an application that runs on virtual machines in an on-premises data center. The company currently uses AWS IAM Identity Center. The application requires temporary access to files in the S3 bucket. The company wants to grant the application secure access to the files in the S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an S3 bucket policy that permits access to the bucket from the public IP address range of the company’s on-premises data center.
o.B: Use IAM Roles Anywhere to obtain security credentials in IAM Identity Center that grant access to the S3 bucket. Configure the virtual machines to assume the role by using the AWS CLI.
o.C: Install the AWS CLI on the virtual machine. Configure the AWS CLI with access keys from an IAM user that has access to the bucket.
o.D: Create an IAM user and policy that grants access to the bucket. Store the access key and secret key for the IAM user in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to retrieve the access key and secret key at startup.

e.why: IAM Roles Anywhere lets workloads outside AWS, such as these on-premises virtual machines, use X.509 certificates from a trusted certificate authority to get temporary credentials for an IAM role. The VMs can then reach the S3 bucket without long-lived access keys.

others.A: Allowing access by IP address alone does not authenticate the application.
others.C: IAM user access keys on the VM are long-lived credentials, which goes against the requirement for temporary access.
others.D: Keeping IAM user keys in Secrets Manager still relies on long-lived credentials.

e.tip: For workloads outside AWS that need temporary credentials, use IAM Roles Anywhere.

q: A company hosts its core network services, including directory services and DNS, in its on-premises data center. The data center is connected to the AWS Cloud using AWS Direct Connect (DX). Additional AWS accounts are planned that will require quick, cost-effective, and consistent access to these network services. What should a solutions architect implement to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

o.A: Create a DX connection in each new account. Route the network traffic to the on-premises servers.
o.B: Configure VPC endpoints in the DX VPC for all required services. Route the network traffic to the on-premises servers.
o.C: Create a VPN connection between each new account and the DX VPRoute the network traffic to the on-premises servers.
o.D: Configure AWS Transit Gateway between the accounts. Assign DX to the transit gateway and route network traffic to the on-premises servers.

e.why: A transit gateway, shared to the new accounts with AWS Resource Access Manager, connects all VPCs to one Direct Connect gateway through a transit VIF. Every account gets consistent, low-latency access to the on-premises directory and DNS services over the existing Direct Connect link.

others.A: A separate Direct Connect connection for each account is expensive and slow to provision.
others.B: VPC endpoints reach AWS services or PrivateLink services. They do not route traffic to on-premises servers.
others.C: A VPN connection for each account adds tunnels to manage and gives less consistent performance.

q: A company hosts its main public web application in one AWS Region across multiple Availability Zones. The application uses an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group and an Application Load Balancer (ALB).
