A web development team needs a cost-optimized compute solution to improve the company’s ability to serve dynamic content globally to millions of customers. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the existing ALB as the origin.
o.B: Use Amazon Route 53 to serve traffic to the ALB and EC2 instances based on the geographic location of each customer.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket with public read access enabled. Migrate the web application to the S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting.
o.D: Use AWS Direct Connect to directly serve content from the web application to the location of each customer.

e.why: CloudFront in front of the existing ALB speeds up dynamic content over the AWS global network, using persistent connections and TCP optimizations at edge locations, and caches whatever can be cached. It serves millions of users worldwide without running compute in more Regions, which keeps cost down.

others.B: Route 53 geolocation routing with only one Region does not bring content closer to users.
others.C: S3 website hosting serves only static content, not a dynamic application.
others.D: Direct Connect is a private link to on-premises networks and does not deliver content to the public.

q: A company stores user data in AWS. The data is used continuously with peak usage during business hours. Access patterns vary, with some data not being used for months at a time. A solutions architect must choose a cost-effective solution that maintains the highest level of durability while maintaining high availability. Which storage solution meets these requirements?

o.A: Amazon S3 Standard
o.B: Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering
o.C: Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive
o.D: Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)

e.why: S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves each object between access tiers automatically based on how it is used, so data left untouched for months becomes cheaper, with no retrieval fees and no performance impact. It keeps 11 nines of durability and stores data across multiple AZs.

others.A: S3 Standard charges the full rate for data that sits unused for months.
others.C: Deep Archive retrieval takes hours, which does not suit data in continuous use.
others.D: One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, which lowers availability and resilience.

e.tip: Unknown or changing access patterns point to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

q: A company is testing an application that runs on an Amazon EC2 Linux instance. A single 500 GB Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) General Purpose SSO (gp2) volume is attached to the EC2 instance. The company will deploy the application on multiple EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. All instances require access to the data that is stored in the EBS volume. The company needs a highly available and resilient solution that does not introduce significant changes to the application's code. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Provision an EC2 instance that uses NFS server software. Attach a single 500 GB gp2 EBS volume to the instance.
o.B: Provision an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Configure the file system as an SMB file store within a single Availability Zone.
o.C: Provision an EC2 instance with two 250 GB Provisioned IOPS SSD EBS volumes.
o.D: Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Configure the file system to use General Purpose performance mode.

e.why: Amazon EFS is an NFS file system that many instances in an Auto Scaling group can mount at once across AZs. It is regional, highly available, and elastic, and applications use it like a POSIX file system with minimal code changes. General Purpose performance mode suits typical workloads.

others.A: A single NFS server on EC2 is a single point of failure.
others.B: Single-AZ FSx for Windows File Server uses SMB, which is not native to Linux, and it is not highly available.
others.C: EBS volumes attach to one instance in one AZ and cannot be shared by an Auto Scaling group.

q: A company recently launched a new application for its customers. The application runs on multiple Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones. End users use TCP to communicate with the application. The application must be highly available and must automatically scale as the number of users increases. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

o.A: Add a Network Load Balancer in front of the EC2 instances.
o.B: Configure an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances.
o.C: Add an Application Load Balancer in front of the EC2 instances.
o.D: Manually add more EC2 instances for the application.
o.E: Add a Gateway Load Balancer in front of the EC2 instances.

e.why: A Network Load Balancer handles TCP traffic at layer 4 with high performance across AZs. An Auto Scaling group adds and removes instances automatically as the number of users changes. Together they provide high availability and scale automatically at low cost.

others.C: An ALB handles only HTTP and HTTPS and does not suit raw TCP clients.
others.D: Adding instances by hand is not automatic scaling.
others.E: A Gateway Load Balancer is for inline security appliances, not for application traffic.

q: A company is designing the architecture for a new mobile app that uses the AWS Cloud. The company uses organizational units (OUs) in AWS Organizations to manage its accounts. The company wants to tag Amazon EC2 instances with data sensitivity by using values of sensitive and nonsensitive. IAM identities must not be able to delete a tag or create instances without a tag. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

o.A: In Organizations, create a new tag policy that specifies the data sensitivity tag key and the required values. Enforce the tag values for the EC2 instances. Attach the tag policy to the appropriate OU.
o.B: In Organizations, create a new service control policy (SCP) that specifies the data sensitivity tag key and the required tag values. Enforce the tag values for the EC2 instances. Attach the SCP to the appropriate OU.
o.C: Create a tag policy to deny running instances when a tag key is not specified. Create another tag policy that prevents identities from deleting tags. Attach the tag policies to the appropriate OU.
o.D: Create a service control policy (SCP) to deny creating instances when a tag key is not specified. Create another SCP that prevents identities from deleting tags. Attach the SCPs to the appropriate OU.
o.E: Create an AWS Config rule to check if EC2 instances use the data sensitivity tag and the specified values. Configure an AWS Lambda function to delete the resource if a noncompliant resource is found.

e.why: An Organizations tag policy sets the allowed values, sensitive and nonsensitive, for the tag key and can enforce them for EC2 instances. SCPs block actions: one denies ec2:RunInstances when aws:RequestTag for the key is missing (a Null condition), and another denies ec2:DeleteTags.

others.B: An SCP cannot define allowed tag values in the way a tag policy does.
others.C: Tag policies cannot deny instance launches or tag deletions. They only standardize tag keys and values.
others.E: Detecting problems and deleting resources afterward is reactive, and it can delete resources by mistake.

e.tip: Tag policies standardize keys and values. SCPs deny actions such as launching untagged instances or deleting tags.

q: A company runs database workloads on AWS that are the backend for the company's customer portals. The company runs a Multi-AZ database cluster on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company needs to implement a 30-day backup retention policy. The company currently has both automated RDS backups and manual RDS backups. The company wants to maintain both types of existing RDS backups that are less than 30 days old. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure the RDS backup retention policy to 30 days for automated backups by using AWS Backup. Manually delete manual backups that are older than 30 days.
o.B: Disable RDS automated backups. Delete automated backups and manual backups that are older than 30 days. Configure the RDS backup retention policy to 30 days for automated backups.
o.C: Configure the RDS backup retention policy to 30 days for automated backups. Manually delete manual backups that are older than 30 days.
o.D: Disable RDS automated backups. Delete automated backups and manual backups that are older than 30 days automatically by using AWS CloudFormation. Configure the RDS backup retention policy to 30 days for automated backups.

e.why: Setting the automated backup retention period to 30 days keeps automated backups for the required time and removes older ones at no extra cost. Manual snapshots never expire on their own, so those older than 30 days must be deleted, which here is done manually. Existing backups younger than 30 days are kept.

others.A: Bringing in AWS Backup is not necessary, because RDS retention can be set directly.
others.B: Disabling automated backups deletes the existing automated backups, which the company wants to keep.
others.D: Disabling automated backups removes the existing ones, and CloudFormation is not a tool for deleting snapshots.

q: A company is planning to migrate a legacy application to AWS. The application currently uses NFS to communicate to an on-premises storage solution to store application data. The application cannot be modified to use any other communication protocols other than NFS for this purpose. Which storage solution should a solutions architect recommend for use after the migration?

o.A: AWS DataSync
o.B: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
o.C: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
o.D: Amazon EMR File System (Amazon EMRFS)

e.why: Amazon EFS is a fully managed, elastic file system that uses NFS v4.0 and v4.1. The legacy application can keep using NFS with no changes.

others.A: DataSync is a data transfer service, not storage.
others.B: EBS is block storage attached to one instance and does not speak NFS.
others.D: EMRFS lets EMR clusters use S3 and is not an NFS share.

q: A company uses GPS trackers to document the migration patterns of thousands of sea turtles. The trackers check every 5 minutes to see if a turtle has moved more than 100 yards (91.4 meters). If a turtle has moved, its tracker sends the new coordinates to a web application running on three Amazon EC2 instances that are in multiple Availability Zones in one AWS Region. Recently, the web application was overwhelmed while processing an unexpected volume of tracker data. Data was lost with no way to replay the events. A solutions architect must prevent this problem from happening again and needs a solution with the least operational overhead. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.A: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the data. Configure the application to scan for new data in the bucket for processing.
o.B: Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to handle transmitted location coordinates. Use an AWS Lambda function to process each item concurrently.
o.C: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to store the incoming data. Configure the application to poll for new messages for processing.
o.D: Create an Amazon DynamoDB table to store transmitted location coordinates. Configure the application to query the table for new data for processing. Use TTL to remove data that has been processed.

e.why: An SQS queue durably buffers incoming tracker data, keeping messages for up to 14 days, so bursts no longer overwhelm the EC2 application. The instances poll and process at their own pace, and messages stay in the queue until they are deleted after processing, so no data is lost. It is fully managed.

others.A: Scanning an S3 bucket for new objects is inefficient and needs custom tracking of what has been processed.
others.B: Lambda behind API Gateway could hit concurrency throttling and gives no buffer for replay, and the processing would have to be rewritten.
others.D: Polling a DynamoDB table needs custom logic to track processed items and adds overhead.

e.tip: If an application is overwhelmed or losing data, decouple it with an SQS queue.

q: A company's software development team needs an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ cluster. The RDS cluster will serve as a backend for a desktop client that is deployed on premises. The desktop client requires direct connectivity to the RDS cluster. The company must give the development team the ability to connect to the cluster by using the client when the team is in the office. Which solution provides the required connectivity MOST securely?

o.A: Create a VPC and two public subnets. Create the RDS cluster in the public subnets. Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN with a customer gateway in the company's office.
o.B: Create a VPC and two private subnets. Create the RDS cluster in the private subnets. Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN with a customer gateway in the company's office.
o.C: Create a VPC and two private subnets. Create the RDS cluster in the private subnets. Use RDS security groups to allow the company's office IP ranges to access the cluster.
o.D: Create a VPC and two public subnets. Create the RDS cluster in the public subnets. Create a cluster user for each developer. Use RDS security groups to allow the users to access the cluster.

e.why: Keeping the RDS cluster in private subnets means it has no public exposure. A Site-to-Site VPN from the office customer gateway encrypts traffic and gives the desktop client private connectivity only from the office network, which makes it the most secure option.

others.A: Public subnets expose the database without need, even with a VPN in place.
others.C: Private subnets cannot be reached from the office over the internet without a VPN or Direct Connect, so allowing office IPs in a security group is not enough.
others.D: Public subnets with only security groups and database users expose the cluster to the internet.

q: A solutions architect is creating an application that will handle batch processing of large amounts of data. The input data will be held in Amazon S3 and the output data will be stored in a different S3 bucket. For processing, the application will transfer the data over the network between multiple Amazon EC2 instances. What should the solutions architect do to reduce the overall data transfer costs?

o.A: Place all the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group.
o.B: Place all the EC2 instances in the same AWS Region.
o.C: Place all the EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone.
o.D: Place all the EC2 instances in private subnets in multiple Availability Zones.

e.why: Data moving between EC2 instances in the same AZ over private IPs costs nothing, while traffic between AZs is charged at about 0.01 USD per GB in each direction. Putting all the batch-processing instances in one AZ removes the inter-instance transfer charges. Transfer between S3 and EC2 in the same Region is also free.

others.A: An Auto Scaling group does not decide where instances are placed in a way that reduces transfer charges.
others.B: Keeping everything in one Region still incurs inter-AZ charges if instances are spread across AZs.
others.D: Spreading instances across multiple AZs is what incurs inter-AZ data transfer charges.

e.tip: For lowest cost on heavy east-west traffic, keep the instances in one AZ, accepting the trade-off in availability.

q: A company hosts a multi-tier web application that uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster for storage. The application tier is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances. The company's IT security guidelines mandate that the database credentials be encrypted and rotated every 14 days. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

o.A: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret that uses the KMS key with the appropriate credentials. Associate the secret with the Aurora DB cluster. Configure a custom rotation period of 14 days.
o.B: Create two parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: one for the user name as a string parameter and one that uses the SecureString type for the password. Select AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption for the password parameter, and load these parameters in the application tier. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password every 14 days.
o.C: Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system in all EC2 instances of the application tier. Restrict the access to the file on the file system so that the application can read the file and that only super users can modify the file. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the key in Aurora every 14 days and writes new credentials into the file.
o.D: Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon S3 bucket that the application uses to load the credentials. Download the file to the application regularly to ensure that the correct credentials are used. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the Aurora credentials every 14 days and uploads these credentials to the file in the S3 bucket.

e.why: Secrets Manager encrypts the secret with a KMS key and integrates natively with Aurora. Its managed rotation can be set to a custom schedule of every 14 days, with no custom rotation code, so it takes the least effort.

others.B: Parameter Store cannot rotate secrets, so you would have to write and maintain a custom Lambda function.
others.C: Keeping credentials in a file on EFS with a custom rotation function is fragile and requires significant operational effort.
others.D: Keeping credentials in a file in S3 with custom rotation is insecure and requires significant operational effort.

q: A streaming media company is rebuilding its infrastructure to accommodate increasing demand for video content that users consume daily. The company needs to process terabyte-sized videos to block some content in the videos. Video processing can take up to 20 minutes. The company needs a solution that will scale with demand and remain cost-effective. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use AWS Lambda functions to process videos. Store video metadata in Amazon DynamoDB. Store video content in Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
o.B: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) and AWS Fargate to implement microservices to process videos. Store video metadata in Amazon Aurora. Store video content in Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
o.C: Use Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to process videos. Store video content in Amazon S3 Standard. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for queuing and to decouple processing tasks.
o.D: Deploy a containerized video processing application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) on Amazon EC2. Store video metadata in Amazon RDS in a single Availability Zone. Store video content in Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

e.why: Processing terabyte-sized videos for up to 20 minutes goes beyond Lambda's 15-minute limit and storage limits. ECS on Fargate scales containers with demand and has no servers to manage. Aurora stores the metadata, and S3 Intelligent-Tiering keeps storage costs down for video whose access patterns vary.

others.A: Lambda's 15-minute timeout and limited ephemeral storage cannot handle 20-minute jobs on terabyte-sized videos.
others.C: An ALB in front of batch processing workers is unnecessary, and running EC2 fleets adds management work.
others.D: Glacier Deep Archive is too slow to retrieve for videos that users watch daily, and single-AZ RDS is not resilient.

q: A company runs an on-premises application on a Kubernetes cluster. The company recently added millions of new customers. The company's existing on-premises infrastructure is unable to handle the large number of new customers. The company needs to migrate the on-premises application to the AWS Cloud. The company will migrate to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The company does not want to manage the underlying compute infrastructure for the new architecture on AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use a self-managed node to supply compute capacity. Deploy the application to the new EKS cluster.
o.B: Use managed node groups to supply compute capacity. Deploy the application to the new EKS cluster.
o.C: Use AWS Fargate to supply compute capacity. Create a Fargate profile. Use the Fargate profile to deploy the application.
o.D: Use managed node groups with Karpenter to supply compute capacity. Deploy the application to the new EKS cluster.

e.why: With AWS Fargate for EKS, each pod runs on serverless compute that AWS provisions and manages. Fargate profiles choose which pods run on Fargate. There are no nodes to patch or scale, so this has the least operational overhead.

others.A: Self-managed nodes leave the company managing the EC2 compute.
others.B: Managed node groups still run EC2 instances in your account that you have to look after, such as handling AMI updates.
others.D: Karpenter improves node provisioning but still leaves the company managing EC2 nodes and the Karpenter configuration.

e.tip: If the question says not to manage compute for EKS or ECS, choose Fargate.

q: A company is launching a new application that requires a structured database to store user profiles, application settings, and transactional data. The database must be scalable with application traffic and must offer backups. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Deploy a self-managed database on Amazon EC2 instances by using open source software. Use Spot Instances for cost optimization. Configure automated backups to Amazon S3.
o.B: Use Amazon RDS. Use on-demand capacity mode for the database with General Purpose SSD storage. Configure automatic backups with a retention period of 7 days.
o.C: Use Amazon Aurora Serverless for the database. Use serverless capacity scaling. Configure automated backups to Amazon S3.
o.D: Deploy a self-managed NoSQL database on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for cost optimization. Configure automated backups directly to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.

e.why: Aurora Serverless v2 is a managed relational database that scales capacity automatically with application traffic and is billed for the capacity used. It includes continuous automated backups stored in S3. This meets the needs for structured data, scaling, and backups cost-effectively.

others.A: A self-managed database on Spot Instances risks interruption and data loss and adds operational burden.
others.B: RDS has no on-demand capacity mode, and a provisioned instance does not scale automatically with traffic.
others.D: A NoSQL database does not fit structured transactional data, and running it yourself on EC2 adds overhead.

q: A company runs its legacy web application on AWS. The web application server runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in the public subnet of a VPC. The web application server collects images from customers and stores the image files in a locally attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. The image files are uploaded every night to an Amazon S3 bucket for backup. A solutions architect discovers that the image files are being uploaded to Amazon S3 through the public endpoint. The solutions architect needs to ensure that traffic to Amazon S3 does not use the public endpoint. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for the S3 bucket that has the necessary permissions for the VPC. Configure the subnet route table to use the gateway VPC endpoint.
o.B: Move the S3 bucket inside the VPC. Configure the subnet route table to access the S3 bucket through private IP addresses.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 access point for the Amazon EC2 instance inside the VPConfigure the web application to upload by using the Amazon S3 access point.
o.D: Configure an AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPC that has the Amazon EC2 instance and Amazon S3 to provide a dedicated network path.

e.why: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 adds a route, using the S3 prefix list, to the subnet's route table. S3 traffic from the instance then stays on the AWS private network instead of going over the public internet. Gateway endpoints for S3 cost nothing.

others.B: An S3 bucket cannot be moved into a VPC.
others.C: Access points control access permissions but still use public S3 endpoints unless they are combined with a VPC endpoint.
others.D: Direct Connect connects on-premises networks to AWS. It is not a path from a VPC to S3.

q: A company is creating a prototype of an ecommerce website on AWS. The website consists of an Application Load Balancer, an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances for web servers, and an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance that runs with the Single-AZ configuration. The website is slow to respond during searches of the product catalog. The product catalog is a group of tables in the MySQL database that the company does not update frequently. A solutions architect has determined that the CPU utilization on the DB instance is high when product catalog searches occur. What should the solutions architect recommend to improve the performance of the website during searches of the product catalog?

o.A: Migrate the product catalog to an Amazon Redshift database. Use the COPY command to load the product catalog tables.
o.B: Implement an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to cache the product catalog. Use lazy loading to populate the cache.
o.C: Add an additional scaling policy to the Auto Scaling group to launch additional EC2 instances when database response is slow.
o.D: Turn on the Multi-AZ configuration for the DB instance. Configure the EC2 instances to throttle the product catalog queries that are sent to the database.

e.why: The product catalog is read-heavy and rarely updated, which makes it ideal for caching. ElastiCache for Redis with lazy loading serves repeated searches from memory, which cuts CPU on the database and makes searches much faster.

others.A: Redshift is an analytics data warehouse and is not suited to low-latency, transactional website lookups.
others.C: Adding web servers increases the load on the overloaded database.
others.D: The Multi-AZ standby does not serve reads, and throttling queries makes the user experience worse.

e.tip: For data that is read often and changes rarely, cache it in ElastiCache.

q: A company currently stores 5 TB of data in on-premises block storage systems. The company's current storage solution provides limited space for additional data. The company runs applications on premises that must be able to retrieve frequently accessed data with low latency. The company requires a cloud-based storage solution. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

o.A: Use Amazon S3 File Gateway. Integrate S3 File Gateway with the on-premises applications to store and directly retrieve files by using the SMB file system.
o.B: Use an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway with cached volumes as iSCSI targets.
o.C: Use an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway with stored volumes as iSCSI targets.
o.D: Use an AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway. Integrate Tape Gateway with the on-premises applications to store virtual tapes in Amazon S3.

e.why: The on-premises storage is block storage and is running out of space. Volume Gateway cached volumes present iSCSI block volumes, keep the full data set in S3, and cache frequently used data locally for low-latency access. That expands capacity into the cloud with little management.

others.A: S3 File Gateway provides file shares over SMB or NFS, not block storage, so applications would need to change.
others.C: Stored volumes keep the full data set on premises, which does not solve the shortage of local capacity.
others.D: Tape Gateway is for backup and archive, not low-latency application data.

e.tip: Cached volumes keep primary data in S3 with a local cache. Stored volumes keep primary data on premises with asynchronous backup to S3.

q: A company operates a food delivery service. Because of recent growth, the company's order processing system is experiencing scaling problems during peak traffic hours. The current architecture includes Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that collect orders from an application. A second group of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group fulfills the orders. The order collection process occurs quickly, but the order fulfillment process can take longer. Data must not be lost because of a scaling event. A solutions architect must ensure that the order collection process and the order fulfillment process can both scale adequately during peak traffic hours. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the CPUUtilization metric for each instance in both Auto Scaling groups. Configure each Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to meet its peak workload value.
o.B: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the CPUUtilization metric for each instance in both Auto Scaling groups. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to invoke an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to create additional Auto Scaling groups on demand.
o.C: Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use one SQS queue for order collection. Use the second SQS queue for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queues. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on notifications that the queues send.
o.D: Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use one SQS queue for order collection. Use the second SQS queue for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queues. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on the number of messages in each queue.

e.why: SQS queues decouple collection from fulfillment and hold orders durably, so nothing is lost when instances scale in or out. Scaling each Auto Scaling group on its queue depth, ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible or the backlog per instance, sizes each tier to its own workload.

others.A: Setting minimum capacity to peak wastes money, and CPU usage does not reflect backlog.
others.B: Creating new Auto Scaling groups through SNS is an anti-pattern, and there is still no durable buffer for orders.
others.C: SQS does not send scaling notifications. Scaling is based on CloudWatch queue metrics.

q: An online gaming company is transitioning user data storage to Amazon DynamoDB to support the company's growing user base. The current architecture includes DynamoDB tables that contain user profiles, achievements, and in-game transactions. The company needs to design a robust, continuously available, and resilient DynamoDB architecture to maintain a seamless gaming experience for users. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create DynamoDB tables in a single AWS Region. Use on-demand capacity mode. Use global tables to replicate data across multiple Regions.
o.B: Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache frequently accessed data. Deploy tables in a single AWS Region and enable auto scaling. Configure Cross-Region Replication manually to additional Regions.
o.C: Create DynamoDB tables in multiple AWS Regions. Use on-demand capacity mode. Use DynamoDB Streams for Cross-Region Replication between Regions.
o.D: Use DynamoDB global tables for automatic multi-Region replication. Deploy tables in multiple AWS Regions. Use provisioned capacity mode. Enable auto scaling.

e.why: DynamoDB global tables replicate active-active across Regions automatically, which gives continuous availability and resilience to a Region failure. Provisioned capacity with auto scaling is usually cheaper than on-demand for a steady, growing user base.

others.A: This option is contradictory, because global tables require replica tables in multiple Regions, and on-demand costs more for steady traffic.
others.B: DynamoDB has no manual Cross-Region Replication feature. Global tables replace it, and DAX adds cost without adding resilience.
others.C: Building your own replication with Streams duplicates what global tables already do and adds overhead.

q: A company runs its media rendering application on premises. The company wants to reduce storage costs and has moved all data to Amazon S3. The on-premises rendering application needs low-latency access to storage. The company needs to design a storage solution for the application. The storage solution must maintain the desired application performance. Which storage solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

o.A: Use Mountpoint for Amazon S3 to access the data in Amazon S3 for the on-premises application.
o.B: Configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway to provide storage for the on-premises application.
o.C: Copy the data from Amazon S3 to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Configure an Amazon FSx File Gateway to provide storage for the on-premises application.
o.D: Configure an on-premises file server. Use the Amazon S3 API to connect to S3 storage. Configure the application to access the storage from the on-premises file server.

e.why: S3 File Gateway runs on premises as a VM or appliance. It presents the S3 data over NFS or SMB with a local cache, so the rendering application gets low-latency access while the data stays in low-cost S3.

others.A: Mountpoint for S3 has no local caching gateway, so latency to S3 over the WAN would hurt rendering performance.
others.C: Copying data to FSx for Windows File Server adds storage cost and duplicates the data.
others.D: Building a custom file server on the S3 API means more development and upkeep.

q: A company hosts its enterprise resource planning (ERP) system in the us-east-1 Region. The system runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Customers use a public API that is hosted on the EC2 instances to exchange information with the ERP system. International customers report slow API response times from their data centers. Which solution will improve response times for the international customers MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection that has a public virtual interface (VIF) to provide connectivity from each customer's data center to us-east-1. Route customer API requests by using a Direct Connect gateway to the ERP system API.
o.B: Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the API. Configure the CachingOptimized managed cache policy to provide improved cache efficiency.
o.C: Set up AWS Global Accelerator. Configure listeners for the necessary ports. Configure endpoint groups for the appropriate Regions to distribute traffic. Create an endpoint in the group for the API.
o.D: Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN to establish dedicated VPN tunnels between Regions and customer networks. Route traffic to the API over the VPN connections.

e.why: Global Accelerator sends international users into the AWS global network at the nearest edge location using anycast static IPs, avoiding congested internet paths to us-east-1. This lowers API latency for dynamic, uncacheable traffic without moving the ERP system.

others.A: Direct Connect for each customer data center is very expensive and slow to set up.
others.B: The CachingOptimized policy caches responses, which is inappropriate for dynamic API exchanges and could return stale or wrong data.
others.D: VPN tunnels to every customer network add overhead and still run over the internet.

e.tip: For non-cacheable or TCP traffic from global users to a single Region, choose Global Accelerator.

q: A company tracks customer satisfaction by using surveys that the company hosts on its website. The surveys sometimes reach thousands of customers every hour. Survey results are currently sent in email messages to the company so company employees can manually review results and assess customer sentiment. The company wants to automate the customer survey process. Survey results must be available for the previous 12 months. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST scalable way?

o.A: Send the survey results data to an Amazon API Gateway endpoint that is connected to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create an AWS Lambda function to poll the SQS queue, call Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis, and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Set the TTL for all records to 365 days in the future.
o.B: Send the survey results data to an API that is running on an Amazon EC2 instance. Configure the API to store the survey results as a new record in an Amazon DynamoDB table, call Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis, and save the results in a second DynamoDB table. Set the TTL for all records to 365 days in the future.
o.C: Write the survey results data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function to read the data and call Amazon Rekognition for sentiment analysis. Store the sentiment analysis results in a second S3 bucket. Use S3 lifecycle policies on each bucket to expire objects after 365 days.
o.D: Send the survey results data to an Amazon API Gateway endpoint that is connected to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure the SQS queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function that calls Amazon Lex for sentiment analysis and saves the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Set the TTL for all records to 365 days in the future.

e.why: API Gateway feeding SQS absorbs bursts of thousands of survey responses an hour. Lambda processes them, Amazon Comprehend performs natural language sentiment analysis, and DynamoDB stores the results, with TTL deleting records after 365 days. Every part is serverless and scales automatically.

others.B: An API on a single EC2 instance does not scale and is a single point of failure.
others.C: Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video, not the sentiment of text.
others.D: Amazon Lex builds chatbots and is not a sentiment analysis service, and SQS does not push to Lambda. Lambda polls the queue.

e.tip: Comprehend handles text and sentiment, Rekognition handles images and video, and Lex builds chatbots.

q: A company uses AWS Systems Manager for routine management and patching of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an IP address type target group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). New security protocols require the company to remove EC2 instances from service during a patch. When the company attempts to follow the security protocol during the next patch, the company receives errors during the patching window. Which combination of solutions will resolve the errors? (Choose two.)

o.A: Change the target type of the target group from IP address type to instance type.
o.B: Continue to use the existing Systems Manager document without changes because it is already optimized to handle instances that are in an IP address type target group behind an ALB.
o.C: Implement the AWSEC2-PatchLoadBalanacerInstance Systems Manager Automation document to manage the patching process.
o.D: Use Systems Manager Maintenance Windows to automatically remove the instances from service to patch the instances.
o.E: Configure Systems Manager State Manager to remove the instances from service and manage the patching schedule. Use ALB health checks to re-route traffic.

e.why: The AWSEC2-PatchLoadBalancerInstance Automation runbook deregisters an instance from its load balancer target group, patches it, and registers it again. Running it through Systems Manager Maintenance Windows removes instances from service on schedule during patching, which avoids the errors.

others.A: Changing the target type would mean recreating the target group, and it does not take instances out of service during patching.
others.B: The current document is causing the errors, so leaving it unchanged does not fix anything.
others.E: State Manager keeps instances in a desired configuration. It does not coordinate deregistering instances, and health checks react only after a failure.

q: A medical company wants to perform transformations on a large amount of clinical trial data that comes from several customers. The company must extract the data from a relational database that contains the customer data. Then the company will transform the data by using a series of complex rules. The company will load the data to Amazon S3 when the transformations are complete. All data must be encrypted where it is processed before the company stores the data in Amazon S3. All data must be encrypted by using customer-specific keys. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational effort?

o.A: Create one AWS Glue job for each customer. Attach a security configuration to each job that uses server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) to encrypt the data.
o.B: Create one Amazon EMR cluster for each customer. Attach a security configuration to each cluster that uses client-side encryption with a custom client-side root key (CSE-Custom) to encrypt the data.
o.C: Create one AWS Glue job for each customer. Attach a security configuration to each job that uses client-side encryption with AWS KMS managed keys (CSE-KMS) to encrypt the data.
o.D: Create one Amazon EMR cluster for each customer. Attach a security configuration to each cluster that uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) to encrypt the data.

e.why: The data must be encrypted where it is processed, before it reaches S3, with customer-specific keys. That points to client-side encryption with a separate KMS key for each customer. Serverless Glue jobs, one per customer with its own security configuration and KMS key, avoid managing clusters, so this takes the least operational effort.

others.A: SSE-S3 is server-side encryption with keys that S3 manages, so the keys are not customer-specific and the data is not encrypted before it is stored.
others.B: A separate EMR cluster for each customer with a custom client-side root key means a lot of cluster and key management.
others.D: SSE-KMS encrypts on the server side after the data arrives in S3, and EMR clusters for each customer add overhead.

e.tip: In practice, Glue security configurations offer SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS for S3 targets, while EMR supports CSE-KMS. For the exam, client-side encryption with KMS keys per customer is the intended idea.

q: A company hosts a website analytics application on a single Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instance. The analytics application is highly resilient and is designed to run in stateless mode. The company notices that the application is showing signs of performance degradation during busy times and is presenting 5xx errors. The company needs to make the application scale seamlessly. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of the web application. Use the AMI to launch a second EC2 On-Demand Instance. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the load across the two EC2 instances.
o.B: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of the web application. Use the AMI to launch a second EC2 On-Demand Instance. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted routing to distribute the load across the two EC2 instances.
o.C: Create an AWS Lambda function to stop the EC2 instance and change the instance type. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke the Lambda function when CPU utilization is more than 75%.
o.D: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of the web application. Apply the AMI to a launch template. Create an Auto Scaling group that includes the launch template. Configure the launch template to use a Spot Fleet. Attach an Application Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.

e.why: The application is stateless and resilient, so it can tolerate Spot interruptions. An Auto Scaling group built from a launch template with the AMI, using Spot capacity, behind an ALB scales out and in automatically during busy periods at the lowest compute price.

others.A: A fixed second On-Demand instance does not scale seamlessly and costs more than Spot.
others.B: Weighted DNS routing across two fixed instances has no health-aware load balancing and does not scale automatically.
others.C: Stopping the instance to resize it causes downtime and is not seamless scaling.

e.tip: For stateless, interruption-tolerant workloads, an Auto Scaling group with Spot capacity is the most cost-effective option. In practice, use the group's mixed instances policy.

q: A company runs an environment where data is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The objects are accessed frequently throughout the day. The company has strict da ta encryption requirements for data that is stored in the S3 bucket. The company currently uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) for encryption. The company wants to optimize costs associated with encrypting S3 objects without making additional calls to AWS KMS. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).
o.B: Use an S3 Bucket Key for server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) on the new objects.
o.C: Use client-side encryption with AWS KMS customer managed keys.
o.D: Use server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C) stored in AWS KMS.

e.why: An S3 Bucket Key creates a short-lived bucket-level key from KMS and uses it to generate data keys for objects locally in S3. That cuts KMS requests and costs by up to 99% for objects accessed often, while keeping SSE-KMS encryption. It applies to new objects, or to existing ones once they are copied again.

others.A: SSE-S3 drops KMS altogether, which may break the strict encryption requirement to use KMS keys.
others.C: Client-side encryption still calls KMS for data keys and adds application complexity.
others.D: SSE-C keys are supplied with each request and are not stored or managed in KMS.

e.tip: If the goal is to reduce KMS request costs for SSE-KMS, turn on S3 Bucket Keys.

q: A company runs multiple workloads on virtual machines (VMs) in an on-premises data center. The company is expanding rapidly. The on-premises data center is not able to scale fast enough to meet business needs. The company wants to migrate the workloads to AWS. The migration is time sensitive. The company wants to use a lift-and-shift strategy for non-critical workloads. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

o.A: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to collect data about the VMs.
o.B: Use AWS Application Migration Service. Install the AWS Replication Agent on the VMs.
o.C: Complete the initial replication of the VMs. Launch test instances to perform acceptance tests on the VMs.
o.D: Stop all operations on the VMs. Launch a cutover instance.
o.E: Use AWS App2Container (A2C) to collect data about the VMs.
o.F: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the VMs.

e.why: AWS Application Migration Service is the rehost, or lift-and-shift, tool. You install the Replication Agent on each VM for continuous block-level replication. After the initial sync, you launch test instances for acceptance testing, then stop the source operations and launch cutover instances to finish the migration quickly.

others.A: The Schema Conversion Tool converts database schemas and does not collect VM data or migrate servers.
others.E: App2Container containerizes applications, which is replatforming, not lift-and-shift.
others.F: DMS migrates databases, not whole VMs.

e.tip: Lift-and-shift of servers means AWS Application Migration Service: install the agent, replicate, test, then cut over.

q: A company hosts an application in a private subnet. The company has already integrated the application with Amazon Cognito. The company uses an Amazon Cognito user pool to authenticate users. The company needs to modify the application so the application can securely store user documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Which combination of steps will securely integrate Amazon S3 with the application? (Choose two.)

o.A: Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool to generate secure Amazon S3 access tokens for users when they successfully log in.
o.B: Use the existing Amazon Cognito user pool to generate Amazon S3 access tokens for users when they successfully log in.
o.C: Create an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint in the same VPC where the company hosts the application.
o.D: Create a NAT gateway in the VPC where the company hosts the application. Assign a policy to the S3 bucket to deny any request that is not initiated from Amazon Cognito.
o.E: Attach a policy to the S3 bucket that allows access only from the users' IP addresses.

e.why: A Cognito identity pool exchanges user pool tokens for temporary IAM credentials, scoped by policy for example to each user's own prefix, so users can access S3 securely. An S3 VPC endpoint lets the application in the private subnet reach S3 privately without going over the internet.

others.B: User pools issue JWTs for authentication. They cannot give out AWS credentials for S3 without an identity pool.
others.D: A NAT gateway sends traffic over the internet and adds cost, and S3 cannot tell whether a request came from Cognito.
others.E: Restricting the bucket to user IP addresses is unworkable for users on varying networks and does not authenticate them.

e.tip: User pools handle authentication and issue JWTs. Identity pools issue temporary AWS credentials.

q: A company has a three-tier web application that processes orders from customers. The web tier consists of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The processing tier consists of EC2 instances. The company decoupled the web tier and processing tier by using Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). The storage layer uses Amazon DynamoDB. At peak times, some users report order processing delays and halls. The company has noticed that during these delays, the EC2 instances are running at 100% CPU usage, and the SQS queue fills up. The peak times are variable and unpredictable. The company needs to improve the performance of the application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Use scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale out the processing tier instances for the duration of peak usage times. Use the CPU Utilization metric to determine when to scale.
o.B: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis in front of the DynamoDB backend tier. Use target utilization as a metric to determine when to scale.
o.C: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache the responses for the web tier. Use HTTP latency as a metric to determine when to scale.
o.D: Use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling target tracking policy to scale out the processing tier instances. Use the ApproximateNumberOfMessages attribute to determine when to scale.

e.why: The peaks are unpredictable, and the processing tier is overwhelmed while the queue fills up. A target tracking policy on SQS queue depth, ideally the backlog per instance, scales the processing instances out as messages pile up and back in when the queue drains, which reduces delays.

others.A: Scheduled scaling cannot handle peaks that are variable and unpredictable.
others.B: Caching DynamoDB does not fix CPU saturation on the processing tier.
others.C: CloudFront caching for the web tier does nothing for the overloaded queue workers.

q: A company's production environment consists of Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances that run constantly between Monday and Saturday. The instances must run for only 12 hours on Sunday and cannot tolerate interruptions. The company wants to cost-optimize the production environment. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Purchase Scheduled Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run for only 12 hours on Sunday. Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run constantly between Monday and Saturday.
o.B: Purchase Convertible Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run for only 12 hours on Sunday. Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run constantly between Monday and Saturday.
o.C: Use Spot Instances for the EC2 instances that run for only 12 hours on Sunday. Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run constantly between Monday and Saturday.
o.D: Use Spot Instances for the EC2 instances that run for only 12 hours on Sunday. Purchase Convertible Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run constantly between Monday and Saturday.

e.why: The keyed answer matches capacity to usage. Scheduled Reserved Instances gave discounted, uninterruptible capacity for a recurring window such as 12 hours on Sunday, and Standard Reserved Instances give the deepest discount for instances that run constantly.

others.B: A Convertible Reserved Instance bills around the clock, so paying for it to cover only 12 hours a week is wasteful.
others.C: Spot Instances can be interrupted, and the Sunday workload cannot tolerate interruptions.
others.D: Spot Instances can be interrupted, and Convertible Reserved Instances give a smaller discount than Standard ones.

e.tip: AWS no longer sells Scheduled Reserved Instances. Today you would use On-Demand Instances, or On-Demand Capacity Reservations, for the Sunday window.

q: A digital image processing company wants to migrate its on-premises monolithic application to the AWS Cloud. The company processes thousands of images and generates large files as part of the processing workflow. The company needs a solution to manage the growing number of image processing jobs. The solution must also reduce the manual tasks in the image processing workflow. The company does not want to manage the underlying infrastructure of the solution. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to process the images. Configure Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to orchestrate the workflow. Store the processed files in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS).
o.B: Use AWS Batch jobs to process the images. Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate the workflow. Store the processed files in an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.C: Use AWS Lambda functions and Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to process the images. Store the processed files in Amazon FSx.
o.D: Deploy a group of Amazon EC2 instances to process the images. Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate the workflow. Store the processed files in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume.

e.why: AWS Batch manages compute for image processing jobs and scales it automatically. It can run on Fargate or managed compute environments, so there is no infrastructure to manage. Step Functions orchestrates the workflow steps and removes manual tasks, and S3 stores the large output files cheaply and without limits.

others.A: ECS on EC2 Spot means managing instances, SQS is a queue rather than a workflow orchestrator, and EFS costs more than S3 for outputs.
others.C: EC2 Spot Instances bring infrastructure to manage, and there is no workflow orchestration.
others.D: Self-managed EC2 instances and a single EBS volume mean operational overhead and limited scalability.

q: A company's image-hosting website gives users around the world the ability to up load, view, and download images from their mobile devices. The company currently hosts the static website in an Amazon S3 bucket. Because of the website's growing popularity, the website's performance has decreased. Users have reported latency issues when they upload and download images. The company must improve the performance of the website. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

o.A: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the S3 bucket to improve the download performance. Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration to improve the upload performance.
o.B: Configure Amazon EC2 instances of the right sizes in multiple AWS Regions. Migrate the application to the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the website traffic equally among the EC2 instances. Configure AWS Global Accelerator to address global demand with low latency.
o.C: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the S3 bucket as an origin to improve the download performance. Configure the application to use CloudFront to upload images to improve the upload performance. Create S3 buckets in multiple AWS Regions. Configure replication rules for the buckets to replicate users' data based on the users' location. Redirect downloads to the S3 bucket that is closest to each user's location.
o.D: Configure AWS Global Accelerator for the S3 bucket to improve network performance. Create an endpoint for the application to use Global Accelerator instead of the S3 bucket.

e.why: CloudFront caches images at edge locations, which speeds up downloads for users around the world. S3 Transfer Acceleration sends uploads through edge locations over the AWS backbone to the bucket. Both are configuration changes that need little implementation effort.

others.B: Moving to EC2 instances in several Regions is a major re-architecture.
others.C: Multi-Region buckets with replication and redirect logic take much more work than needed.
others.D: S3 cannot be a standard Global Accelerator endpoint for this purpose, and the option ignores caching downloads.

e.tip: For downloads, use CloudFront. For uploads to S3 over long distances, use S3 Transfer Acceleration.

q: A company runs an application in a private subnet behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in a VPC. The VPC has a NAT gateway and an internet gateway. The application calls the Amazon S3 API to store objects. According to the company's security policy, traffic from the application must not travel across the internet. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.A: Configure an S3 interface endpoint. Create a security group that allows outbound traffic to Amazon S3.
o.B: Configure an S3 gateway endpoint. Update the VPC route table to use the endpoint.
o.C: Configure an S3 bucket policy to allow traffic from the Elastic IP address that is assigned to the NAT gateway.
o.D: Create a second NAT gateway in the same subnet where the legacy application is deployed. Update the VPC route table to use the second NAT gateway.

e.why: An S3 gateway endpoint adds a route to the route table so S3 API traffic from the private subnet stays on the AWS network and bypasses the NAT gateway and internet. Gateway endpoints for S3 have no hourly or data processing charges, so this is the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Interface endpoints also keep traffic private but cost money per hour and per GB.
others.C: Traffic through a NAT gateway still goes to the public S3 endpoint, and a bucket policy does not change the path.
others.D: A second NAT gateway still sends traffic toward the internet and adds cost.

e.tip: Gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB and are free, so prefer them for cost.

q: A company has an application that runs on an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster on Amazon EC2 instances. The application has a UI that uses Amazon DynamoDB and data services that use Amazon S3 as part of the application deployment. The company must ensure that the EKS Pods for the UI can access only Amazon DynamoDB and that the EKS Pods for the data services can access only Amazon S3. The company uses AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Which solution meals these requirements?

o.A: Create separate IAM policies for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB access with the required permissions. Attach both IAM policies to the EC2 instance profile. Use role-based access control (RBAC) to control access to Amazon S3 or DynamoDB for the respective EKS Pods.
o.B: Create separate IAM policies for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB access with the required permissions. Attach the Amazon S3 IAM policy directly to the EKS Pods for the data services and the DynamoDB policy to the EKS Pods for the UI.
o.C: Create separate Kubernetes service accounts for the UI and data services to assume an IAM role. Attach the AmazonS3FullAccess policy to the data services account and the AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess policy to the UI service account.
o.D: Create separate Kubernetes service accounts for the UI and data services to assume an IAM role. Use IAM Role for Service Accounts (IRSA) to provide access to the EKS Pods for the UI to Amazon S3 and the EKS Pods for the data services to DynamoDB.

e.why: Separate Kubernetes service accounts linked to separate IAM roles through IRSA give each set of pods only its own permissions: S3 for the data services and DynamoDB for the UI. Pod credentials come from the service account's role, not from the node.

others.A: Putting both policies on the instance profile gives every pod access to both services, and Kubernetes RBAC cannot limit AWS API access.
others.B: IAM policies cannot be attached directly to pods.
others.D: This swaps the access, giving the UI S3 and the data services DynamoDB, which is the opposite of what is required.

e.tip: Full-access managed policies are broader than least privilege. A scoped custom policy is better in practice.

q: A company needs to give a globally distributed development team secure access to the company's AWS resources in a way that complies with security policies. The company currently uses an on-premises Active Directory for internal authentication. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts that support multiple projects. The company needs a solution to integrate with the existing infrastructure to provide centralized identity management and access control. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.A: Set up AWS Directory Service to create an AWS managed Microsoft Active Directory on AWS. Establish a trust relationship with the on-premises Active Directory. Use IAM rotes that are assigned to Active Directory groups to access AWS resources within the company's AWS accounts.
o.B: Create an IAM user for each developer. Manually manage permissions for each IAM user based on each user's involvement with each project. Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) as an additional layer of security.
o.C: Use AD Connector in AWS Directory Service to connect to the on-premises Active Directory. Integrate AD Connector with AWS IAM Identity Center. Configure permissions sets to give each AD group access to specific AWS accounts and resources.
o.D: Use Amazon Cognito to deploy an identity federation solution. Integrate the identity federation solution with the on-premises Active Directory. Use Amazon Cognito to provide access tokens for developers to access AWS accounts and resources.

e.why: AD Connector proxies authentication to the existing on-premises Active Directory without copying the directory. Connecting it to IAM Identity Center lets AD groups be mapped to permission sets across all accounts in the organization, which gives central identity management with the least overhead.

others.A: Running AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a trust and roles for each account adds a directory to run and more manual setup.
others.B: Individual IAM users are not centralized and create heavy management overhead.
others.D: Cognito handles identities for customer-facing applications, not workforce access to AWS accounts.

e.tip: For workforce access across Organizations with an existing AD, use IAM Identity Center with AD Connector or a trust with AWS Managed Microsoft AD.

q: A company is developing an application in the AWS Cloud. The application's HTTP API contains critical information that is published in Amazon API Gateway. The critical information must be accessible from only a limited set of trusted IP addresses that belong to the company's internal network. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.A: Set up an API Gateway private integration to restrict access to a predefined set of IP addresses.
o.B: Create a resource policy for the API that denies access to any IP address that is not specifically allowed.
o.C: Directly deploy the API in a private subnet. Create a network ACL. Set up rules to allow the traffic from specific IP addresses.
o.D: Modify the security group that is attached to API Gateway to allow inbound traffic from only the trusted IP addresses.

e.why: An API Gateway resource policy can allow or deny calls based on the source IP address, using aws:SourceIp, or on the VPC endpoint. A policy that denies any IP not on the trusted list makes the API reachable only from the company's internal network ranges.

others.A: Private integrations connect API Gateway to backends inside a VPC and do not filter client IP addresses.
others.C: API Gateway is a managed service and cannot be deployed into a private subnet with network ACLs.
others.D: API Gateway endpoints have no security groups for you to change.

e.tip: In practice, resource policies are supported only on REST APIs. For HTTP APIs, use a Lambda authorizer or WAF in front.
